body.text: yogācārabhūmau
body.translated_text: In the <s>Yogācārabhūmi</s>,

body.text: om namo buddhāya // daśeme dharmāḥ saphalasya bodhisattvamārgasya mahāyānasya saṃgrahāya saṃvartante / katame daśa / ādhāro liṅgaṃ pakṣo 'dhyāśayo vihāra upapattiḥ parigraho bhūmiścaryā pratiṣṭhā ca /
body.translated_text: <s>Oṃ</s> Homage to the <s>Buddha</s>! // These ten <s>dharmas</s> conduce to the comprehension of the fruitful path of the <s>Bodhisattva</s>, the <s>Mahāyāna</s>. Which ten? The foundation (<s>ādhāra</s>), the mark (<s>liṅga</s>), the inclination (<s>pakṣa</s>), the resolve (<s>adhyāśaya</s>), the abiding (<s>vihāra</s>), the rebirth (<s>upapattiḥ</s>), the undertaking (<s>parigraha</s>), the stage (<s>bhūmi</s>), the practice (<s>caryā</s>), and the establishment (<s>pratiṣṭhā</s>).

body.text: uddānam /
body.translated_text: Summary verse:

children.translated_text: Foundation, mark, inclination, resolve, abiding, rebirth,
undertaking, stage, practice—and establishment is the last. //

body.text: tatrādhāraḥ katamaḥ / iha bodhisattvasya svagotraṃ prathamaścittotpādaḥ sarve ca bodhipakṣyā dharmā ādhāra ityucyate / tatkasya hetoḥ / iha bodhisattvo gotraṃ niśritya pratiṣṭhāpayitavyo bhavati / pratibalo 'nuttarāṃ samyaksaṃbodhimabhisaṃboddhum / tasmāt sabhāgatayā gotramādhāra ityucyate / iha bodhisattvaḥ prathamacittotpādaṃ niśritya pratiṣṭhāya dāne 'pi prayujyate śīle kṣāntau vīryeṃ dhyāne prajñāyāmapi prayujyate iti / yadvā pāramitāsu puṇyasaṃbhāre jñānasaṃbhāre sarveṣu ca bodhipakṣyeṣu dharmeṣu prayujyate / tasmātprathamacittotpādasya bodhisattvasya caryāprayogasyādhāra ityucyate / iha bodhisattvastameva bodhisattvacaryāprayogaṃ niśritya pratiṣṭhāyānuttarāṃ samyaksaṃbodhiṃ paripūrayati / tasmātsa bodhisattvacaryāprayogastasya mahābodhiparipūrerādhāra ityucyate / agotrastha pudgalo gotre 'sati cittotpāde 'pi yatnasamāśraye satyabhavyaścānuttarāyāḥ samyaksaṃbodheḥ paripūraye / tadanena paryāyeṇa veditavyamanutpāditacittasyāpi bodhisattvasya akṛte 'pi bodhisattvacaryāprayoge gotramādhāra iti / sa cet punargotrasthaścittaṃ notpādayati bodhicaryāsu na prayujyate na kṣipraṃ bodhimārāgayati tāsvapi
body.translated_text: There, what is the foundation? Here, the <s>Bodhisattva</s>'s own lineage (<s>gotra</s>), the first generation of the mind [of awakening] (<s>cittotpāda</s>), and all the qualities conducive to awakening (<s>bodhipakṣyā dharmāḥ</s>) are called the foundation. For what reason? Here, the <s>Bodhisattva</s>, relying on the lineage, is to be established [on the path]. He is capable of fully awakening to the unsurpassed, perfect awakening (<s>anuttarā samyaksaṃbodhi</s>). Therefore, by way of homogeneity, the lineage is called the foundation. Here, the <s>Bodhisattva</s>, relying on and being established in the first generation of the mind, engages in generosity, moral conduct, patience, vigor, meditation, and also in wisdom. Or else he engages in the <s>pāramitās</s> (perfections), in the accumulation of merit (<s>puṇyasaṃbhāra</s>), in the accumulation of knowledge (<s>jñānasaṃbhāra</s>), and in all the qualities conducive to awakening. Therefore, the first generation of the mind is called the foundation of the <s>Bodhisattva</s>'s practice and endeavor. Here, the <s>Bodhisattva</s>, relying on and being established in that very practice and endeavor of the <s>Bodhisattva</s>, fulfills the unsurpassed, perfect awakening. Therefore, that practice and endeavor of the <s>Bodhisattva</s> is called the foundation for the fulfillment of his great awakening. A person established in the absence of lineage (<s>agotra</s>), even with effort and reliance on the generation of the mind in the absence of lineage, is incapable of the fulfillment of the unsurpassed, perfect awakening. By this method, it should be understood that even for the <s>Bodhisattva</s> who has not yet generated the mind and has not yet undertaken the practice of the <s>Bodhisattva</s>, the lineage is the foundation. But if one established in the lineage does not generate the mind, does not engage in the practices of awakening, one does not quickly reach awakening; but in the opposite case,

body.text: viparyayāt kṣipramārāgayatīti veditavyam / tatpunaretadgotramādhāra ityucyate / upastambho heturniśraya upaniṣatpūrvaṅgamo nilaya ityapyucyate / yathāgotramevaṃ prathamaścittotpādaḥ sarvā ca bodhisattvacaryā /
body.translated_text: one should understand that one quickly reaches it. That lineage is again called the foundation; it is also called the support (<s>upastambha</s>), the cause (<s>hetu</s>), the basis (<s>niśraya</s>), the proximate cause (<s>upaniṣat</s>), the precursor (<s>pūrvaṅgama</s>), and the abode (<s>nilaya</s>). Just as with the lineage, so with the first generation of the mind and with the entire practice of the <s>Bodhisattva</s>.

body.text: tatra gotraṃ katamat / samāsato gotraṃ dvividham / prakṛtisthaṃ samudānītañca / tatra prakṛtisthaṃ gotraṃ yadbodhisattvānāṃ ṣaḍāyatanaviśeṣaḥ / sa tādṛśaḥ paraṃparāgato 'nādikāliko dharmatāpratilabdhaḥ / tatra samudānītaṃ gotraṃ yatpūrvakuśalamūlābhyāsātpratilabdham / tadasminnarthe dvividhamapyabhipretam / tatpunargotraṃ bījamityapyucyate / dhātuḥ prakṛtirityapi / tatpunarasamudāgataphalaṃ sūkṣmaṃ vinā phalena / samudāgataphalamaudārikaṃ saha phalena /
body.translated_text: There, what is the lineage? In brief, the lineage is twofold: naturally abiding (<s>prakṛtistham</s>) and cultivated (<s>samudānītam</s>). There, the naturally abiding lineage is the distinctive nature of the six sense-bases (<s>ṣaḍāyatanaviśeṣa</s>) of the <s>Bodhisattvas</s>. That is of such a nature, handed down through succession, beginningless in time, obtained through the nature of reality (<s>dharmatāpratilabdha</s>). There, the cultivated lineage is that which is obtained through the repeated practice of previously [accumulated] roots of virtue (<s>kuśalamūla</s>). Both are intended in this context. That lineage, moreover, is also called seed (<s>bīja</s>), element (<s>dhātu</s>), and nature (<s>prakṛti</s>). That which has not yet produced its fruit is subtle, being without fruit; that which has produced its fruit is coarse, being together with fruit.

body.text: tena khalu gotreṇa samanvāgatānāṃ bodhisattvānāṃ sarvaśrāvakapratyekabuddhānatikramya prāgevānyān sattvānniruttaro viśeṣo veditavyaḥ / tatkasya hetoḥ / dve ime samāsato viśuddhī / kleśāvaraṇaviśuddhirjñeyāvaraṇaviśuddhiśca / tatra sarvaśrāvakapratyekabuddhānāṃ tadgotraṃ kleśāvaraṇaviśuddhyā viśudhyati na tu jñeyāvaraṇaviśuddhyā / bodhisattvagotraṃ punarapi kleśāvaraṇaviśuddhyā api jñeyāvaraṇaviśuddhyā viśudhyati / tasmātsarvaprativiśiṣṭaṃ niruttaramityucyate /
body.translated_text: For <s>Bodhisattvas</s> endowed with that lineage, a distinction surpassing all <s>Śrāvakas</s> and <s>Pratyekabuddhas</s>, let alone other beings, should be understood as unsurpassed. For what reason? There are, in brief, these two kinds of purification: purification from the obscuration of afflictions (<s>kleśāvaraṇaviśuddhi</s>) and purification from the obscuration of the knowable (<s>jñeyāvaraṇaviśuddhi</s>). There, the lineage of all <s>Śrāvakas</s> and <s>Pratyekabuddhas</s> is purified by purification from the obscuration of afflictions, but not by purification from the obscuration of the knowable. The lineage of the <s>Bodhisattva</s>, however, is purified both by purification from the obscuration of afflictions and by purification from the obscuration of the knowable. Therefore it is called the most distinguished of all, unsurpassed.

body.text: api ca caturbhirākārairbodhisattvasya śrāvakapratyekabuddhebhyo viśeṣo veditavyaḥ / katamaiścaturbhiḥ / indriyakṛtaḥ pratipattikṛtaḥ kauśalyakṛtaḥ phalakṛtaśca / tatrāyamindriyakṛto viśeṣaḥ / prakṛtyaiva bodhisattvastīkṣṇendriyo bhavati / pratyekabuddho madhyendriyaḥ śrāvako mṛdvindriyaḥ / tatrāyaṃ pratipattikṛto viśeṣaḥ / śrāvakapratyekabuddhaścātmahitāya pratipanno bhavati / bodhisattvaḥ apyātma hitāya api parahitāya bahujanahitāya bahujanasukhāya lokānukampāyai arthāya hitāya sukhāya devamanuṣyāṇām / tatrāyaṃ kauśalyakṛto viśeṣaḥ / śrāvakaḥ pratyekabuddhaśca skandhadhātvāyatanapratītyasamutpāda-sthānāsthānasatyakauśalyaṃ karoti bodhisattvastatra cānyeṣu ca sarvavidyāsthāneṣu / tatrāyaṃ phalakṛto viśeṣaḥ / śrāvakaḥ śrāvakabodhiphalamadhigacchati / pratyekabuddhaḥ pratyekabodhimadhigacchati / bodhisattvo 'nuttaraṃ samyaksaṃbodhiphalamadhigacchati /
body.translated_text: Furthermore, the distinction of the <s>Bodhisattva</s> from <s>Śrāvakas</s> and <s>Pratyekabuddhas</s> should be understood in four aspects. Which four? Due to faculties (<s>indriyakṛta</s>), due to practice (<s>pratipattikṛta</s>), due to skill (<s>kauśalyakṛta</s>), and due to result (<s>phalakṛta</s>). There, this is the distinction due to faculties: the <s>Bodhisattva</s> is by nature endowed with sharp faculties; the <s>Pratyekabuddha</s> has medium faculties; the <s>Śrāvaka</s> has soft faculties. There, this is the distinction due to practice: the <s>Śrāvaka</s> and <s>Pratyekabuddha</s> practice for the benefit of oneself; the <s>Bodhisattva</s> practices for the benefit of oneself, for the benefit of others, for the welfare of many, for the happiness of many, out of compassion for the world, for the sake, benefit, and happiness of gods and humans. There, this is the distinction due to skill: the <s>Śrāvaka</s> and <s>Pratyekabuddha</s> develop skill in the aggregates (<s>skandha</s>), elements (<s>dhātu</s>), sense-bases (<s>āyatana</s>), dependent origination (<s>pratītyasamutpāda</s>), the possible and impossible (<s>sthānāsthāna</s>), and the truths (<s>satya</s>); the <s>Bodhisattva</s> develops skill in those and also in all other fields of knowledge. There, this is the distinction due to result: the <s>Śrāvaka</s> attains the fruit of <s>Śrāvakabodhi</s> (disciple-awakening); the <s>Pratyekabuddha</s> attains <s>Pratyekabodhi</s> (solitary awakening); the <s>Bodhisattva</s> attains the fruit of the unsurpassed, perfect awakening.

body.text: ṣaḍimāni bodhisattvasya pāramitānāṃ gotraliṅgāni saṃpadyante / yairevaṃ pare saṃjānate bodhisattvo 'yamiti / dānapāramitāyā gotraliṅgaṃ śīlakṣāntivīryadhyānaprajñāpāramitāyā gotraliṅgam / tatredaṃ bodhisattvasya dānapāramitāyā gotraliṅgam / iha bodhisattvaḥ prakṛtyaiva dānarucirbhavati / satsu ca saṃvidyamāneṣu deyadharmeṣu satatasamitaṃ pareṣāṃ saṃvibhāgaśīlo bhavati pramuditacittaśca dadāti na vimanaskaḥ / alpādapi ca saṃvibhāgasya karttā bhavati / viśadañca dānamanuprayacchati / na hīnam / adānena ca jihreti / pareṣāñca dānasya varṇaṃ bhāṣate / dāne cainānupacchandayati / dātārañca dṛṣṭvā āttamanā bhavati sumanaskaḥ / gurubhyo vṛddhatarakebhyo dakṣiṇīyebhyaḥ satkārārhebhya utthāyāsanamanuprayacchati / pṛṣṭo 'pṛṣṭo vā teṣu teṣu sattvakṛtyeṣvanapāyamihaloke paraloke nyāyopadeśamanuprayacchati / rājacaurāmitrāṇyudakādibhayabhītānāñca sattvānāmabhayamanuprayacchati / yathāśaktyā cainān paritrāyate tasmādvicitrāt pratatādugrādbhayāt / nikṣiptañcāsya haste paradhanaṃ nābhidruhyati / ṛṇaṃ gṛhītvā parebhyo na visaṃvādayati nābhidruhyati / svadāyādaṃ na vañcayate na vipralambhayati / maṇimuktāvaidūryaśaṃkhaśilāpravālajātarūparajatāśmagarbhamusāragalvalohitikādakṣiṇāvartaprabhṛtiṣūpakaraṇajāteṣu mūḍhaṃ viparyasyacittaṃ samyaksaṃbodhayati / yathāsyānyato 'pi na vipralambhaḥ syāt / kutaḥ punaḥ svayamenaṃ vipralambhayiṣyati / prakṛtyā codārabhogādhimukto bhavati / udāreṣvasya sarvabhogaparibhogeṣu cittaṃ krāmati / udāreṣu ca karmānteṣvadhimukto bhavati na parīttāyadvāreṣu / santi cemāni loke vyasanāni / tadyathā strīvyasanam / madyavyasanam / dyūtavyasanam / naṭa-nartaka-hāsaka-lāsakādisaṃdarśanavyasanamityevaṃrūpebhyovyasanebhyo laghu ladhveva vairāgyaṃ pratilabhate / hrīvyapatrāpyaṃ prāviṣkaroti vipule 'pi ca bhogapratilambhe nādhimātralolupo bhavati prāgevālpe / itimānyevaṃ bhāgīyāni bodhisattvasya dānapāramitāyā gotraliṅgāni veditavyāni /
body.translated_text: These six signs of lineage for the <s>pāramitās</s> (perfections) of the <s>Bodhisattva</s> are accomplished, by which others recognize: 'This is a <s>Bodhisattva</s>.' The sign of lineage for the <s>Dānapāramitā</s> (perfection of generosity), the sign of lineage for the <s>Śīla</s>-, <s>Kṣānti</s>-, <s>Vīrya</s>-, <s>Dhyāna</s>-, and <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> (perfections of moral conduct, patience, vigor, meditation, and wisdom). There, this is the sign of lineage for the <s>Bodhisattva</s>'s <s>Dānapāramitā</s>: Here, the <s>Bodhisattva</s> is by nature delighted in giving; and when there are suitable things to be given, one is continually disposed to sharing with others, gives with a joyful mind, and is not dejected. One gives even from little, and gives generously, not meanly. One is ashamed of not giving, speaks praise of others' giving, and encourages them in giving. And seeing a giver, one becomes elated and glad. One offers one's seat to elders, seniors, those worthy of offerings, and those deserving of respect. Whether asked or unasked, in the various needs of beings, one provides righteous counsel that is harmless in this world and the next. And to beings frightened by the dangers of kings, thieves, enemies, floods, and so forth, one gives fearlessness and protects them as best one can from that varied, extended, and terrible danger. One does not betray the wealth of others placed in one's hand; having incurred a debt from others, one does not deceive or betray them; one does not cheat or deceive one's heirs. Regarding the categories of valuable materials—gems, pearls, <s>vaiḍūrya</s>, conch-shells, stones, corals, gold, silver, emeralds, <s>musāragalva</s>, red gems, right-spiraling [conch shells], and the like—one rightly awakens those who are confused and whose minds are mistaken, so that they may not be deceived by others; how much less would one deceive them oneself. By nature, one is inclined toward magnificent enjoyments; one's mind proceeds toward magnificent enjoyments and possessions of every kind; and one is inclined toward magnificent undertakings, not toward limited doorways. And there are these vices in the world, namely: the vice of women, the vice of intoxicants, the vice of gambling, the vice of viewing actors, dancers, comedians, and performers—from such vices, one very quickly obtains dispassion. One manifests moral shame (<s>hrī</s>) and moral dread (<s>vyapatrāpya</s>), and even when obtaining vast enjoyments, one is not excessively greedy, much less so when they are small. Thus, these should be understood as the signs of lineage belonging to the <s>Bodhisattva</s>'s <s>Dānapāramitā</s>.

body.text: tatremāni bodhisattvasya śīlapāramitāyā gotraliṅgāni / iha bodhisattvaḥ prakṛtyā mṛdunā kāyavāṅmanaskarmaṇā samanvāgato bhavatyakuśalena nātyartharaudreṇa nātyarthasattvopaghātakena / kṛtvāpi ca pāpakaṃ karma laghu ladhveva vipratisāraṃ pratilabhate / tañca jehrīyamāṇaḥ samācarati na nandījātaḥ / pāṇiloṣṭadaṇḍaśastrādibhiśca sattvānāmaviheṭhanajātīyo bhavati / prakṛtivatsalaśca bhavati sattvapriyaḥ / satkārārheṣu ca kālena kālamabhivādanavandanapratyutthānāñjalisāmīcīkarmaṇā pratyupasthito bhavati / dakṣiṇaśca bhavati / nāgarikaḥ paracittānuvartī / smitapūrvaṅgamaśca bhavatyuttānamukhavarṇavigatabhrūkuṭiḥ pūrvābhibhāṣī / upakāriṣu ca sattveṣu kṛtajño bhavati kṛtavedī / arthikeṣu ca sattveṣu ṛjutāṃ pratipadyate / na māyāśāṭhyenaitān vilobhayati / dharmeṇāsāhasena ca bhogān samudānayati nādharmeṇa / prakṛtyaiva ca puṇyakāmo bhavati / parapuṇya kriyāsvapi vyāpāraṃ gacchati prāgevātmanaḥ / parabādhayā cāttyartha bādhyate yaduta pareṣāṃ vadhabandhanacchedanatāḍanakutsanatarjanādikayā dṛṣṭvā vā śrutvā vā / dharmasamādānagurukaśca bhavati saṃparāyagurukaḥ / aṇumātre 'pyavadye bhayadarśī prāgeva prabhūte / parakṛtyeṣu ca parakaraṇīyeṣu sahāyībhāvaṃ gacchati yaduta kṛṣivaṇijyāgorakṣyarājapauruṣyalipigaṇananyasanasaṃkhyāmudrāyāṃ bhartṛprasādane kulaprasādane rājakulaprasādane mitrāmitraprasādane bhogānāmarjane rakṣaṇe sannidhau prayoge visarge āvāhavivāhābhakṣaṇasaṃbhakṣaṇeṣvevaṃbhāgīyeṣu sattvakṛtyeṣu sahāyībhāvaṃ gacchati / na kalahabhaṇḍanavigrahavivādeṣu ca paraviheṭhanakaraṇīyeṣu ye ātmanaḥ pareṣāñcānarthāyāhitāya duḥkhāya saṃvartante / akṛtyāccaitāṃ nivārayati yaduta daśabhyaḥ pāpakebhyo 'kuśalebhyaḥ / karmapathebhyaḥ / paravaśyaśca bhavati paravidheyaḥ / samānakṣāntiśīlatayā apahāya svakāryaṃ parairātmakārye yathākāmaṃ niyojyate / ārdracittaśca bhavati peśalacitto na ca ciramāghātacittatāṃ pratighacittatāmudvahati nānyatra tatkṣaṇa evāsya taccittaṃ bhadratāyāṃ parivartate / satyagurukaśca bhavati nābhūtavacanena parān visaṃvādayati / na ca pareṣāṃ mitrabhedaṃ rocayati na karoti /
body.translated_text: There, these are the signs of lineage for the <s>Bodhisattva</s>'s <s>Śīlapāramitā</s> (perfection of moral conduct): Here, the <s>Bodhisattva</s> is by nature endowed with gentle conduct of body, speech, and mind—unwholesome [conduct] that is not excessively fierce and not excessively harmful to beings. And having committed an evil deed, one very quickly obtains remorse; and one performs it with shame, not with delight. One is by nature not inclined to harming beings with hand, clod, stick, weapon, and the like. One is by nature affectionate and dear to beings. And at proper times, one is attentive to those worthy of respect with salutation, veneration, rising from one's seat, joining palms, and proper service. One is dexterous, urbane, considerate of others' minds. One is a smiler with a bright face, free from frowning, and speaks first. One is grateful and appreciative toward beings who have been helpful. Toward beings who are supplicants, one acts straightforwardly and does not entice them with deceit and fraud. One acquires wealth through righteous means, without violence, not through unrighteousness. One is by nature desirous of merit and engages in the meritorious activities of others, all the more so in one's own. One is extremely distressed by the suffering of others, namely by seeing or hearing of the beating, binding, cutting, striking, reviling, and threatening of others, and the like. One is serious about undertaking the <s>Dharma</s> and serious about the hereafter. One sees danger even in the slightest fault, much more so in a great one. One assists others in their tasks and duties, namely in agriculture, commerce, cattle-keeping, royal service, writing, calculation, and other arts, in the use of seals, in winning the favor of patrons, winning the favor of families, winning the favor of the royal court, in winning the favor of friends and adversaries, in earning, protecting, storing, employing, and distributing wealth, in marriage, wedding feasts, eating together and sharing food, and in similar matters pertaining to the needs of beings—one assists. But not in quarrels, disputes, conflict, and litigation that serve to harm others, which lead to misfortune, harm, and suffering for oneself and others. One dissuades them from evil, namely from the ten unwholesome courses of action. One is amenable and compliant to others; through being of equal patience and disposition, setting aside one's own affairs, one is employed by others in one's own tasks as they wish. One is tender-hearted and gentle-minded, and does not long maintain a mind of hostility or aversion—rather, at that very moment, one's mind turns to a state of goodness. One is serious about truthfulness and does not deceive others with false speech. One does not delight in or create discord among friends.

body.text: na cāsambaddhamapārtha nirartha sahasā pralapati / priyaṃvadaśca bhavatyaparakaṭukaḥ api svakasya dāsādiparijanasya prāgeva pareṣām guṇapriyaśca bhavati pareṣāṃ bhūtasya varṇasyāhartā / itīmānyevaṃbhāgīyāni bodhisattvasya śīlapāramitāyā gotraliṅgāni veditavyāni /
body.translated_text: One does not speak rashly that which is disconnected, purposeless, or meaningless. One is pleasant-spoken and not harsh, even toward one's own servants and attendants, much less toward others. One is fond of virtues and is a reporter of the true merits of others. Thus, these should be understood as the signs of lineage belonging to the <s>Bodhisattva</s>'s <s>Śīlapāramitā</s>.

body.text: tatremāni bodhisattvasya kṣāntipāramitāyā gotraliṅgāni / iha bodhisattvaḥ prakṛtyā pareṣāmantikādapakāraṃ labdhvā nāghātacittatāṃ prāviṣkaroti nāpyapakārāya prapadyate / saṃjñapyamānaścāśu saṃjñaptiṃ pratigṛhṇāti / na ca khilaṃ dhārayati na cirakālikaṃ vairāśayaṃ vahati / itīmānyevaṃbhāgīyāni bodhisattvasya kṣāntipāramitāyā gotraliṅgāni veditavyāni /
body.translated_text: Therein, these are the signs of the <s>Bodhisattva</s>'s lineage for the <s>kṣāntipāramitā</s> (perfection of patience): Here, a <s>Bodhisattva</s>, by nature, having received harm from others, does not manifest a mind of hostility, nor does he set forth toward retaliation. When asked for forgiveness, he quickly accepts the apology. He does not hold a grudge, nor does he carry a long-lasting disposition of enmity. These and similar [traits] are to be known as the signs of the <s>Bodhisattva</s>'s lineage for the <s>kṣāntipāramitā</s> (perfection of patience).

body.text: tatremāni bodhisattvasya vīryapāramitāyā gotraliṅgāni / iha bodhisattvaḥ prakṛtyā utthānavān bhavati / kālyotthāyī sāyaṃ nipātī na nidrāsukhaṃ śayanasukhaṃ pārśvasukhamatyarthaṃ svīkaroti / pratyupasthite ca kṛtye abhibhūyākartukāmatāmālasyaṃ pratisaṃkhyāya prayujyate tasya kṛtyasyābhiniṣpattaye / sarvakṛtyasamārambheṣu ca dṛḍhaniścayo bhavati nākṛtvā nāpariprāpya sarveṇa sarvaṃ vīryasraṃsayati antarā vā viṣādamāpadyate / udāreṣu ca parameṣvartheṣu na cetasā saṃkocamāpadyate / nāpyātmānaṃ paribhavati / śakto 'haṃ pratibalameṣāmadhigamāyetyutsāhajātaḥ / vīraśca bhavati mahāsabhāpraveśe vā paraiḥ sahābhiprayoga pratyabhiyoge vā tadanyatra vā duṣkarakarmaṇi mahāvyavasāyeṣvapi cārthopasaṃhiteṣu nātyarthaṃ khedamāpadyate prāgeva parītteṣu / itīmānyevaṃbhāgīyāni bodhisattvasya vīryapāramitāyā gotraliṅgāni veditavyāni /
body.translated_text: Therein, these are the signs of the <s>Bodhisattva</s>'s lineage for the <s>vīryapāramitā</s> (perfection of energy): Here, a <s>Bodhisattva</s> is by nature energetic. He rises early and retires late; he does not excessively indulge in the pleasure of sleep, the pleasure of reclining, or the pleasure of lying on one's side. When a task presents itself, he overcomes unwillingness and laziness by reflection and applies himself to the accomplishment of that task. In all undertakings of tasks, he is of firm resolve—he does not in any way slacken his energy without having done and accomplished everything, nor does he succumb to despair midway. Even in noble and supreme endeavors, he does not experience mental shrinking; nor does he disparage himself, [thinking:] 'I am capable, I have the strength for the attainment of these'—thus confidence arises. He is heroic, whether in entering a great assembly, in contending against others in an encounter, or in other difficult deeds; even in great exertions connected with meaningful purposes, he does not become excessively fatigued, much less in minor ones. These and similar [traits] are to be known as the signs of the <s>Bodhisattva</s>'s lineage for the <s>vīryapāramitā</s> (perfection of energy).

body.text: tatremāni bodhisattvasya dhyānapāramitāyā gotraliṅgāni / iha bodhisattvaḥ prakṛtyā dharmārthopanidhyāne avikṣepabahulo bhavati / araṇyavanaprasthānāni / ca prāntāni śayanāsanāni manuṣyarahaḥsevitāni vigatapāpakāni pratisaṃlayanasārūpyakāṇi dṛṣṭvā śrutvā sukhaṃ tannaiṣkramyaṃ prāvivekyamiti
body.translated_text: Therein, these are the signs of the <s>Bodhisattva</s>'s lineage for the <s>dhyānapāramitā</s> (perfection of meditation): Here, a <s>Bodhisattva</s> is by nature predominantly undistracted in the contemplation of the meaning of the <s>Dharma</s>. Having seen or heard of forests, woodland retreats, and secluded lodgings frequented by solitary people, free from evil, suitable for meditative seclusion—[thinking:] 'How pleasant is that renunciation, that solitude!'—

body.text: naiṣkramyaprāvivekye tīvramautsukyamutpādayati / prakṛtyā ca mandakleśo bhavati mandanivaraṇo mandadauṣṭhulyaḥ / pravivekagatasya cāsya svārthaṃ paritulayataḥ pāpakāḥ asadvitarkā nātyarthaṃ cittaṃ kṣobhayanti na paryādāya tiṣṭhanti / [saḥ] amitrapakṣe 'pi tvaritaṃ tvaritaṃ maitracittatāmupasthāpayati prāgeva mitrodāsīnapakṣe / vicitraiśca duḥkhairduḥkhitānāṃ sattvānāṃ duḥkhaṃ śrutvā vā dṛṣṭvā vā mahatkāruṇyacittamutpādayati / duḥkhāpanayāya ca teṣāṃ sattvānāṃ yathāśaktyā yathābalaṃ vyāpāraṃ gacchati / prakṛtyā ca sattveṣu hitakāmo bhavati sukhakāmaḥ / dhṛtimāṃśca bhavatyāpatsu jñātivyasane vā bhogavyasane vā vadhe vā bandhane vā pravāse vā ityevaṃbhāgīyāsvāpatsu / medhāvī ca dharmāṇāṃ grahaṇadhāraṇohanasamarthaḥ smṛtibalena ca samanvāgato bhavati / sa cirakṛtacirabhāṣitamapyanusmarttā bhavati pareṣāñcānusmārayitā / itīmānyevaṃbhāgīyāni bodhisattvasya dhyānapāramitāyā gotraliṅgāni veditavyāni /
body.translated_text: he generates intense eagerness for renunciation and solitude. By nature he has mild afflictions, mild hindrances, and mild rigidity. When he has gone into solitude and is reflecting on his own purpose, evil unwholesome thoughts do not excessively disturb his mind nor do they persist in overwhelming it. Even toward those on the enemy's side, he quickly establishes a mind of friendliness (<s>maitrī</s>), much more so toward those on the side of friends and neutral parties. Having heard of or seen beings suffering from various kinds of suffering, he generates a mind of great compassion (<s>karuṇā</s>). And for the removal of the suffering of those beings, he exerts effort according to his ability and power. By nature he is inclined toward the welfare and happiness of beings. He is steadfast in calamities—whether misfortune of relatives, loss of possessions, slaughter, imprisonment, exile, or similar calamities. He is intelligent, capable of grasping, retaining, and understanding <s>dharmas</s>, and is endowed with the power of mindfulness. He is able to remember what was done or said long ago, and to remind others [as well]. These and similar [traits] are to be known as the signs of the <s>Bodhisattva</s>'s lineage for the <s>dhyānapāramitā</s> (perfection of meditation).

body.text: tatremāni bodhisattvasya prajñāpāramitāyā gotraliṅgāni / iha bodhisattvaḥ sarvavidyāsthānajñeyapraveśāya sahajayā prajñayā samanvāgato bhavati / adhandhaśca bhavatyamandaḥ amomuhajātīyaḥ / tāsu tāsu ca pramādasthānaviratiṣu pratisaṃkhyānabaliko bhavati / itīmānyevaṃbhāgīyāni bodhisattvasya prajñāpāramitāyā gotraliṅgāni veditavyāni /
body.translated_text: Therein, these are the signs of the <s>Bodhisattva</s>'s lineage for the <s>prajñāpāramitā</s> (perfection of wisdom): Here, a <s>Bodhisattva</s> is endowed with innate wisdom for entering all fields of knowledge and knowable objects. He is neither dull nor slow, nor of a confused disposition. In various matters where heedlessness should be avoided, he has the power of discernment. These and similar [traits] are to be known as the signs of the <s>Bodhisattva</s>'s lineage for the <s>prajñāpāramitā</s> (perfection of wisdom).

body.text: tānīmāni bodhisattvasya audārikāṇyānumānikāni gotraliṅgāni veditavyāni / bhūtārthaniścaye tu buddhā eva bhagavantaḥ pratyakṣadarśinaḥ /
body.translated_text: These are to be known as the <s>Bodhisattva</s>'s coarse, inferential signs of the lineage. But in the determination of the true nature [of the lineage], only the <s>Buddhas</s>, the <s>Bhagavāns</s>, are direct perceivers.

body.text: yasmācca tadgotraṃ bodhisattvānāṃ prakṛtyaiva guṇayuktaṃ bhadraṃ kalyāṇaṃ śukladharmasamanvāgataṃ tasmāttāvad durabhisaṃbhavasya śreṣṭhasyācintyasyācalasyānuttarasya tathāgatasya padasyāvāptaye hetubhāvena yujyate 'nyathā na yujyate / tāvacca bodhisattva ebhiḥ śukladharmaiḥ prakṛtyaiva yukto bhavati yāvanna śukladharmavairodhikaiścaturbhirupakleśaiḥ sakalavikalairupakliṣṭo bhavati / yadā copakliṣṭo bhavati sa tadā eṣu ca śukleṣu dharmeṣu na saṃdṛśyate / apāyeṣu caikadā upapadyate / apāyopapattāvapi bodhisattvasya tadanyebhyaḥ apāyopapannebhyaḥ sattvebhyo
body.translated_text: And because the <s>Bodhisattva</s>'s lineage (<s>gotra</s>) is by nature endowed with qualities, auspicious, wholesome, and accompanied by virtuous <s>dharmas</s> (<s>śukladharma</s>)—therefore, it is fitting [for it] to serve as the cause for attaining the difficult-to-reach, supreme, inconceivable, unshakeable, unsurpassed state of the <s>Tathāgata</s>; otherwise it would not be fitting. And the <s>Bodhisattva</s> is by nature endowed with these virtuous <s>dharmas</s> as long as he is not defiled by the four secondary defilements (<s>upakleśa</s>) that oppose virtuous <s>dharmas</s>—in whole or in part. But when he is defiled, then these virtuous <s>dharmas</s> are not manifest in him, and he is sometimes reborn in the lower realms (<s>apāya</s>). Even when the <s>Bodhisattva</s> is reborn in the lower realms, a great distinction due to lineage is to be known compared to other beings reborn in the lower realms.

body.text: gotrakṛto mahān viśeṣo veditavyaḥ / iha bodhisattvo dīrgheṇa kālena kadācit karhicidapāyeṣūpapadyate / upapannaścāśu parimucyate apāyebhyaḥ / na ca tathā tīvrāmāpāyikīṃ duḥkhāṃ vedanāṃ vedayate tadyathā 'nye 'pāyopapannāḥ sattvāḥ / tayā ca tanvyā duḥkhayā vedanayā spṛṣṭo 'dhimātraṃ saṃvegamutpādayati / teṣu ca sattveṣu tatropapanneṣu duḥkhiteṣu kāruṇyacittaṃ pratilabhate yaduta tenaiva gotreṇa ca sattveṣu tatropapanneṣu duḥkhiteṣu kārūṇyacittaṃ pratilabhate yaduta tenaiva gotreṇa buddhamahākaruṇāhetunā codyamānaḥ / ityevaṃbhāgīyaḥ apāyopapattau bodhisattvasya tadanyebhyaḥ apāyopapannebhyaḥ sattvebhyo viśeṣo veditavyaḥ /
body.translated_text: Here, a <s>Bodhisattva</s> is reborn in the lower realms only after a long time, rarely and occasionally. Having been reborn, he is quickly freed from the lower realms. And he does not experience such intense painful feelings of the lower realms as other beings reborn in the lower realms [do]. Touched by that mild painful feeling, he generates intense spiritual urgency (<s>saṃvega</s>). And toward those beings who are reborn there and suffering, he obtains a mind of compassion—that is, being impelled by that very lineage and the cause of the <s>Buddha</s>'s great compassion. Such and similar is the distinction of the <s>Bodhisattva</s>, when reborn in the lower realms, from other beings reborn in the lower realms.

body.text: tatra katame te bodhisattvasya catvāraḥ śukladharmavairodhikā upakleśāḥ / pūrvaṃ pramattasya kleśābhyāsāttīvrakleśatā āyatakleśatā cāyaṃ prathama upakleśaḥ / mūḍhasyākuśalasya pāpamitrasaṃśrayo 'yaṃ dvitīya upakleśaḥ / gurubhartṛrājacaurapratyarthikadyabhibhūtasyāsvātantryaṃ cittavibhramaścāyaṃ tṛtīya upakleśaḥ / upakaraṇavikalasya jīvikāpekṣā ayaṃ caturtha upakleśaḥ /
body.translated_text: What then are those four secondary defilements (<s>upakleśa</s>) of the <s>Bodhisattva</s> that oppose virtuous <s>dharmas</s>? First, intense affliction and prolonged affliction due to habituation to afflictions from previous heedlessness—this is the first secondary defilement. Second, association with evil companions due to being deluded and unskillful—this is the second secondary defilement. Third, lack of freedom and mental disturbance due to being overpowered by teachers, masters, kings, thieves, adversaries, and the like—this is the third secondary defilement. Fourth, concern for livelihood due to lack of resources—this is the fourth secondary defilement.

body.text: caturbhiḥ kāraṇairevaṃ gotrasaṃpanno 'pi bodhisattvo na śaknotyanuttara samyaksaṃbodhimabhisaṃboddhum / katamaiścaturbhiḥ / iha bodhisattvaḥ ādita eva kalyāṇamitraṃ na labhate aviparītabodhimārgadaiśikaṃ buddhaṃ vā bodhisattvaṃ vā / idaṃ prathamaṃ kāraṇam / punaraparaṃ bodhisattvo labdhvāpi kalyāṇamitraṃ viparītagrāhī viparītaṃ śikṣate bodhisattvaśikṣāsu / idaṃ dvitīyaṃ kāraṇam / punaraparaṃ bodhisattvo labdhvāpi kalyāṇamitramaviparītaṃ śikṣamāṇo bodhisattvaśikṣāsu tasmin prayoga śithilaprayogo bhavati kusīdo nodagrapratatavīryasamanvāgataḥ / idaṃ tṛtīyaṃ kāraṇam / punaraparaṃ bodhisattvo labdhvā kalyāṇamitramaviparītaṃ śikṣamāṇo bodhisattvaśikṣāsu tasmiṃśca prayoge ārabdhavīryaḥ aparipakvendriyo bhavatyaparipūrṇabodhisaṃbhāraḥ dīrghakālāparijayādvodhipakṣya dharmāṇām / idañcaturtha kāraṇam / gotre satyetatkāraṇavaikalyādvodheraprāptiḥ / sānnidhyāttu prāptirbhavati / asati tu gotre sarveṇa sarva sarvathā bodharaprāptireva veditavyā /
body.translated_text: By four causes, even a <s>Bodhisattva</s> endowed with lineage is unable to fully awaken to unsurpassed perfect awakening (<s>anuttara samyaksaṃbodhi</s>). By which four? Here, a <s>Bodhisattva</s> does not obtain from the very beginning a virtuous friend (<s>kalyāṇamitra</s>) who is an unerring guide to the path of awakening—whether a <s>Buddha</s> or a <s>Bodhisattva</s>. This is the first cause. Furthermore, even having obtained a virtuous friend, the <s>Bodhisattva</s> grasps wrongly and trains incorrectly in the <s>Bodhisattva</s>-trainings. This is the second cause. Furthermore, even having obtained a virtuous friend and training correctly in the <s>Bodhisattva</s>-trainings, the <s>Bodhisattva</s> is lax in that practice, lazy, not endowed with zealous and sustained energy. This is the third cause. Furthermore, having obtained a virtuous friend, training correctly in the <s>Bodhisattva</s>-trainings, and having initiated energy in that practice, the <s>Bodhisattva</s>'s faculties are unripened and his accumulation of awakening (<s>bodhisaṃbhāra</s>) is incomplete, because of the long time needed for mastery of the factors of awakening (<s>bodhipakṣyadharma</s>). This is the fourth cause. When the lineage exists but these causes are deficient, there is non-attainment of awakening. But when they are present, attainment occurs. When there is no lineage, in every case and in every way, only non-attainment of awakening is to be understood.

body.text: bodhisattvabhūmau ādhāre yogasthāne prathamaṃ gotrapaṭalaṃ samāptam //
body.translated_text: In the <s>Bodhisattvabhūmi</s>, in the Foundation (<s>Ādhāra</s>) section of the Yoga Place, the first chapter on Lineage (<s>Gotrapaṭala</s>) is completed.

children.translated_text: Chapter on the Generation of the Mind (<s>Cittotpādapaṭala</s>)

body.text: iha bodhisattvasya prathamaścittotpādaḥ sarvabodhisattvasamyakpraṇidhānānāmādyaṃ samyakpraṇidhānaṃ tadanyasamyakpraṇidhānasaṃgrāhakam / tasmāt sa āditaḥ samyakpraṇidhānasvabhāvaḥ / sa khalu bodhisattvo bodhāya cittaṃ praṇidadhadevaṃ cittamabhisaṃskaroti vācañca bhāṣate / aho batāhamanuttarāṃ samyaksaṃbodhimabhisaṃbudhyeyaṃ sarvasattvānāñcārthakaraḥ syāmatyantaniṣṭhe nirvāṇe pratiṣṭhāpayeyaṃ tathāgatajñāne ca / sa evamātmanaśca bodhiṃ sattvārthañca prārthayamānaścittamutpādayati / tasmātsa cittotpādaḥ prārthanākāraḥ / tāṃ khalu bodhiṃ sattvārthañcālamvya sa cittotpādaḥ prārthayate nānālambya / tasmātsa cittotpādo bodhyālambanaḥ sattvārthālambanaśca / sa ca cittotpādaḥ sarvabodhipakṣyakuśalamūlasaṃgrahāya pūrvaṅgamatvātkuśalaḥ paramakauśalyaguṇayuktaḥ bhadraḥ paramabhadraḥ kalyāṇaḥ paramakalyāṇaḥ sarvasattvādhiṣṭhānakāyavāṅmanoduścaritavairodhikaḥ / yāni ca kānicittadanyāni laukikalokottareṣvartheṣu kuśalāni samyakpraṇidhānāni teṣāṃ sarveṣāmagrya metatsamyakpraṇidhānaṃ niruttaraṃ yaduta bodhisattvasya prathamaścittotpādaḥ / evamayaṃ prathamaścittotpādaḥ svabhāvato 'pi veditavyaḥ / ākārato 'pyālambanato 'pi guṇato 'pyutkarṣato 'ti pañcalakṣaṇo veditavyaḥ /
body.translated_text: Here, the <s>Bodhisattva</s>'s first generation of the mind (<s>cittotpāda</s>) is the foremost correct aspiration (<s>samyakpraṇidhāna</s>) among all <s>Bodhisattva</s> correct aspirations, encompassing all other correct aspirations. Therefore, from the very beginning, it is of the nature of correct aspiration. That <s>Bodhisattva</s>, generating the mind toward awakening (<s>bodhi</s>), forms such an intention and utters these words: 'Oh, may I fully awaken to unsurpassed perfect awakening (<s>anuttarā samyaksaṃbodhi</s>), and may I accomplish the welfare of all beings, establishing them in the ultimate <s>nirvāṇa</s> and in the knowledge of the <s>Tathāgata</s>!' Thus, aspiring for both his own awakening and the welfare of beings, he generates the mind. Therefore that generation of the mind is of the nature of aspiration. That generation of the mind aspires with awakening and the welfare of beings as its object, not without an object. Therefore that generation of the mind has awakening as its object (<s>bodhyālambana</s>) and the welfare of beings as its object (<s>sattvārthālambana</s>). And that generation of the mind is wholesome (<s>kuśala</s>), because it is the precursor to the gathering of all wholesome roots pertaining to awakening; endowed with the quality of supreme skillfulness; auspicious, supremely auspicious; wholesome, supremely wholesome; opposed to all misdeeds of body, speech, and mind that serve as the basis for all beings. And whatever other correct aspirations there may be regarding worldly and supramundane purposes—among all of these, this correct aspiration is the foremost and unsurpassed, namely, the <s>Bodhisattva</s>'s first generation of the mind. Thus this first generation of the mind is to be known with regard to its nature, and is to be known as having five characteristics: with regard to its nature, aspect, object, quality, and superiority.

body.text: tasya ca bodhicittasya sahotpādādevāvatīrṇe bhavati bodhisattvo 'nuttare bodhimahāyāne / bodhisattvo bodhisattva iti ca saṃkhyāṃ gacchati yaduta saṃketavyavahāranayena / tasmātsa cittotpādaḥ avatārasaṃgṛhītaḥ / utpādya ca bodhisattvastaccittaṃ krameṇānuttarāṃ samyaksaṃbodhimadhigacchati nānutpādya / tasmādanuttarāyāḥ samyaksaṃbodheḥ sa cittotpādo mūlam / duḥkhiteṣu ca sattveṣu sa kāruṇiko bodhisattvaḥ paritrāṇābhiprāyastaccittamutpādayati / tasmātsa cittotpādaḥ karuṇāniṣyandaḥ /
body.translated_text: And from the very moment of the arising of that <s>bodhicitta</s> (mind of awakening), the <s>Bodhisattva</s> has entered the unsurpassed great vehicle of awakening (<s>bodhimahāyāna</s>). And he comes to be reckoned as a '<s>Bodhisattva</s>'—that is, by the method of conventional designation. Therefore, that generation of the mind is encompassed by [the concept of] entry. And having generated that mind, the <s>Bodhisattva</s> gradually attains unsurpassed perfect awakening, not without having generated it. Therefore, that generation of the mind is the root of unsurpassed perfect awakening. And that compassionate <s>Bodhisattva</s>, with the intention of rescuing suffering beings, generates that mind. Therefore, that generation of the mind is the outflow of compassion (<s>karuṇā</s>).

body.text: tañca cittotpādaṃ niśritya pratiṣṭhāya bodhisattvo bodhipakṣyeṣu dharmeṣu sattvārtha kriyāyāñca bodhisattvaśikṣāyāṃ prayujyate / tasmātsa cittotpādo bodhisattvaśikṣāyāḥ sanniśrayaḥ / evamasau prathamaścittotpādaḥ saṃgrahato 'pi mūlato 'pi niṣyandato 'pi sanniśrayato 'pi veditavyaḥ /
body.translated_text: And relying on and established in that generation of the mind, the <s>Bodhisattva</s> applies himself to the factors of awakening (<s>bodhipakṣyadharma</s>) and to the accomplishment of the welfare of beings in the <s>Bodhisattva</s>-training. Therefore, that generation of the mind is the support (<s>sanniśraya</s>) of the <s>Bodhisattva</s>-training. Thus this first generation of the mind is to be known with regard to its encompassment, root, outflow, and support.

body.text: sa ca bodhisattvasya prathamacittotpādaḥ samāsena dvividhaḥ / nairyāṇikaścānairyāṇikaśca / tatra nairyāṇiko ya utpanno 'tyantamanuvartate na punarvyāvartate / anairyāṇikaḥ punarya utpanno nātyantamanuvartate punareva vyāvartate / tasya ca cittotpādasya vyāvṛttirapi dvividhā / ātyantikī cānātyantikī ca / tatrātyantikī yatsakṛdvyāvṛttaṃ cittaṃ na punarutpadyate bodhāya / anātyantikī punaḥ yadvyāvṛttaṃ cittaṃ punaḥ punarutpadyate bodhāya /
body.translated_text: And that first generation of the mind of the <s>Bodhisattva</s> is, in brief, of two kinds: definitive (<s>nairyāṇika</s>) and non-definitive (<s>anairyāṇika</s>). Therein, the definitive is that which, once arisen, continues perpetually and does not turn back. The non-definitive is that which, once arisen, does not continue perpetually and turns back again. And the turning back of that generation of the mind is also twofold: final (<s>ātyantikī</s>) and non-final (<s>anātyantikī</s>). Therein, the final is when the mind, having once turned back, does not arise again toward awakening. The non-final is when the mind, having turned back, arises again and again toward awakening.

body.text: tasya khalu cittasyotpādaḥ caturbhiḥ pratyayaiścaturbhirhetubhiścaturbhirbalairveditavyaḥ / catvāraḥ pratyayāḥ katame / iha kulaputro vā kuladruhitā vā tathāgatasya vā bodhisattvasya vā acintyamatyadbhutaṃ prātihāryaṃ prabhāvaṃ paśyati saṃpratyayitasya vā 'ntikācchṛṇoti / tasya dṛṣṭvā vā śrutvā vā evaṃ bhavati / mahānubhāvā bateyaṃ bodhiryasyāṃ sthitasya vā pratipannasya vā 'yamevarūpaḥ prabhā[vaḥ] idamevaṃrūpaṃ prātihāryaṃ dṛśyate ca śrūyate ca sa tadeva prabhāvadarśanaṃ śravaṇaṃ vādhipatiṃ kṛtvā mahābodhyadhimukto mahābodhau cittamutpādayati / ayaṃ prathamaḥ pratyayaścittasyotpattaye / sa na haiva prabhāvaṃ paśyati vā śṛṇoti vā aparitvanuttarāṃ bodhimārabhya saddharmaṃ śṛṇoti bodhisattvapiṭakaṃ deśyamānaṃ śrutvā ca punarabhiprasīdati / abhiprasannaśca saddharmaśravaṇamadhipatiṃ kṛtvā tathāgatajñānādhimuktaḥ tathāgatajñānapratilambhāya cittamutpādayati / ayaṃ dvitīyaḥ pratyayaścittasyotpattaye / sa na haiva dharma śṛṇotyapi tu bodhisattvaḥ saddharmāntardhānimāmukhāmupagatāṃ paśyati / dṛṣṭvā ca punarasyaivaṃ bhavati aprameyāṇāṃ bata sattvānāṃ duḥkhāpagamāya bodhisattvasaddharmasthitiḥ saṃvartate / yannvahaṃ bodhisattva-saddharmacirasthitaye cittamutpādayeyaṃ yaduta eṣāmeva sattvānāṃ duḥkhāpakarṣaṇāya / [sa] saddharmadhāraṇamevādhipatiṃ kṛtvā tathāgatajñānādhimuktastathāgatajñānapratilambhāya cittamutpādayati / ayaṃ
body.translated_text: The arising of that mind [of awakening] is to be understood through four conditions (<s>pratyaya</s>), four causes (<s>hetu</s>), and four powers (<s>bala</s>). What are the four conditions? Here, a son or daughter of good family sees an inconceivable, most wondrous miraculous display (<s>prātihārya</s>) and power (<s>prabhāva</s>) of a <s>Tathāgata</s> or a <s>Bodhisattva</s>, or hears about it from a trustworthy person. Having seen or heard, the thought arises in them: 'How mighty indeed is this <s>bodhi</s> (awakening), standing in which or practicing which, such power and such a miraculous display is seen and heard!' Taking that very seeing or hearing of the power as the governing condition, with faith in the great <s>bodhi</s>, one generates the mind toward the great <s>bodhi</s>. This is the first condition for the arising of the mind. [Second:] One does not [necessarily] see or hear the power; nevertheless, with regard to the supreme awakening, one hears the true <s>Dharma</s>, hears the <s>Bodhisattva Piṭaka</s> being taught, and having heard it, one develops deep faith. With deep faith, taking the hearing of the true <s>Dharma</s> as the governing condition, with conviction in the knowledge of the <s>Tathāgata</s>, one generates the mind for the attainment of the <s>Tathāgata</s>'s knowledge. This is the second condition for the arising of the mind. [Third:] One does not [necessarily] hear the <s>Dharma</s>; however, the <s>Bodhisattva</s> sees the true <s>Dharma</s> approaching the verge of disappearance. Having seen this, the thought arises: 'Alas, for the removal of suffering of immeasurable beings, the continuation of the <s>Bodhisattva</s>'s true <s>Dharma</s> is beneficial. Let me generate the mind for the long-lasting continuation of the <s>Bodhisattva</s>'s true <s>Dharma</s>, precisely for the removal of suffering of these beings.' Taking the preservation of the true <s>Dharma</s> as the governing condition, with conviction in the knowledge of the <s>Tathāgata</s>, one generates the mind for the attainment of the <s>Tathāgata</s>'s knowledge. This is the

body.text: tṛtīyaḥ pratyayaścittasyotpattaye / sa na haiva saddharmāntardhāniṃ pratyupasthitāṃ paśyati apitvantayuge 'ntakāle pratyavarāntayugikān sattvāśrayān paśyati yaduta daśabhirupakleśairupakliṣṭān / tadyathā mohabahulānāhrīkyānapatrāpyabahulānīrṣyāmātsaryabahulān duḥkhabahulān dauṣṭhulyabahulān kleśabahulān duścaritabahulān pramādabahulān kausīdyabahulān āśraddhyabahulāṃśca / dṛṣṭvā ca punarasyaivaṃ bhavati / mahān batāyaṃ kaṣāyakālaḥ pratyupasthitaḥ / asminnevamupakliṣṭe kāle na sulabho nihīnaḥ śrāvakapratyekabodhāvapi tāvaccittotpādaḥ prāgevānuttarāyāṃ samyaksaṃbodhau / yannvahamapi tāvaccittamutpādayeyam apyeva [nāma] mamānuśikṣamāṇā anye 'pyutpādayeyuriti / so 'ntakāle cittotpādadurlabhatāmadhipatiṃ kṛtvā mahābodhāvadhimukto mahābodhau cittamutpādayati / ayaṃ caturthaḥ pratyayaścittasyotpattaye /
body.translated_text: third condition for the arising of the mind. [Fourth:] One does not [necessarily] see the true <s>Dharma</s> as approaching disappearance; however, in the final age, at the end of time, one sees the conditions of beings in the degraded final age — that is, afflicted by the ten secondary defilements (<s>upakleśa</s>): namely, those abundant in delusion, those abundant in shamelessness, those abundant in lack of moral dread, those abundant in envy and miserliness, those abundant in suffering, those abundant in unwholesomeness, those abundant in afflictions, those abundant in misconduct, those abundant in heedlessness, those abundant in laziness, and those abundant in faithlessness. Having seen this, the thought arises: 'Alas, a great age of degeneration (<s>kaṣāyakāla</s>) has arrived! In such a defiled time, even an inferior arising of the mind toward <s>Śrāvaka</s>-awakening or <s>Pratyekabuddha</s>-awakening is difficult to find — how much more so toward the supreme perfect awakening! Let me at least generate the mind [toward supreme awakening], so that perhaps, following my example, others too may generate it.' Taking the difficulty of generating the mind at the end of time as the governing condition, with faith in the great <s>bodhi</s>, one generates the mind toward the great <s>bodhi</s>. This is the fourth condition for the arising of the mind.

body.text: catvāro hetavaḥ katame / gotrasaṃpadvodhisattvasya prathamo hetuścittasyotpattaye / buddhabodhisattvakalyāṇamitraparigraho dvitīyo hetuścittasyotpattaye / sattveṣu kāruṇyaṃ bodhisattvasya tṛtīyo hetuścittasyotpattaye / saṃsāraduḥkhād duṣkaracaryāduḥkhādapi dīrghakālikādvicitrāttīvrānnirantarādabhīrutā caturtho hetuścittasyotpattaye /
body.translated_text: What are the four causes? The first cause for the arising of the <s>Bodhisattva</s>'s mind is the completeness of the spiritual lineage (<s>gotrasaṃpat</s>). The second cause is being taken under the care of <s>Buddhas</s>, <s>Bodhisattvas</s>, and spiritual friends (<s>kalyāṇamitra</s>). The third cause is compassion (<s>kāruṇya</s>) toward beings. The fourth cause is fearlessness in the face of the suffering of <s>saṃsāra</s> and the suffering of difficult practices, even when long-lasting, varied, intense, and uninterrupted.

body.text: tatra gotrasaṃpadvodhisattvasya dharmatāpratilabdhaiva veditavyā /
body.translated_text: There, the completeness of the <s>Bodhisattva</s>'s spiritual lineage (<s>gotrasaṃpat</s>) is to be understood as obtained by the nature of things (<s>dharmatā</s>).

body.text: caturbhirākārairbodhisattvasya mitrasaṃpadveditavyā / iha bodhisattvasya mitramādita evājaḍaṃ bhavatyadhandhajātīyaṃ paṇḍitaṃ vilakṣaṇaṃ na ca kudṛṣṭipatitam / iyaṃ prathamā mitrasaṃpat / na cainaṃ pramāde viniyojayati / na pramādasthānamasyopasaṃharati / iyaṃ dvitīyā mitrasaṃpat / na cainaṃ duścirite viniyojayati na duścaritasthānamasyopasaṃharati / iyaṃ tṛtīyā mitrasaṃpat / na cainamutkṛṣṭatarebhyaḥ śraddhācchandasamādānavīryopāyaguṇebhyo vicchandayitvā nihīnatareṣu śraddhācchandasamādānavīryopāyaguṇeṣu samādāpayati / tadyathā mahāyānādvicchandayitvā śrāvakayāne vā pratyekabuddhayāne vā bhāvanāmayād vicchandayitvā cintāmaye cintāmayādvicchandayitvā śrutamaye śrutamayādvicchandayitvā vaiyāvṛttyakarmaṇi śīlamayād vicchandayitvā dānamaye ityevaṃbhāgīyebhya utkṛṣṭatarebhyo guṇebhyo na vicchandayitvā evaṃbhāgīyeṣu nihīnatareṣu guṇeṣu samādāpayati / iyaṃ caturthī mitrasaṃpat /
body.translated_text: The completeness of spiritual friendship for the <s>Bodhisattva</s> is to be understood through four aspects. Here, the <s>Bodhisattva</s>'s spiritual friend is, from the very beginning, not dull, not of sluggish disposition, wise, discerning, and not fallen into wrong views — this is the first completeness of spiritual friendship. [Second:] He does not engage the [<s>Bodhisattva</s>] in heedlessness, nor does he present opportunities for heedlessness to him — this is the second completeness. [Third:] He does not engage the [<s>Bodhisattva</s>] in misconduct, nor does he present opportunities for misconduct to him — this is the third completeness. [Fourth:] He does not dissuade him from superior qualities of faith, aspiration, undertaking, vigor, and skill in means, only to establish him in inferior qualities of faith, aspiration, undertaking, vigor, and skill in means. For example, he does not dissuade him from the <s>Mahāyāna</s> to establish him in the <s>Śrāvakayāna</s> or <s>Pratyekabuddhayāna</s>; does not dissuade him from the cultivation through meditation (<s>bhāvanāmaya</s>) to establish him in that arising from reflection (<s>cintāmaya</s>); does not dissuade him from that arising from reflection to establish him in that arising from hearing (<s>śrutamaya</s>); does not dissuade him from that arising from hearing to establish him in service (<s>vaiyāvṛttyakarman</s>); does not dissuade him from the moral-based to establish him in the giving-based. In this manner, he does not dissuade from superior qualities of this kind to establish in inferior qualities of this kind — this is the fourth completeness of spiritual friendship.

body.text: caturbhirākārai rbodhisattvaḥ karuṇābahulo bhavati sattveṣu / santi te lokadhātavo yeṣu duḥkhaṃ nopalabhyate daśasu dikṣvanantāparyanteṣu lokadhātuṣu / sa ca bodhisattvaḥ saduḥkhe loka dhātau pratyājāto bhavati yatra duḥkhamupalabhyate nāduḥkhe / parañcānyatamena duḥkhena spṛṣṭamupadrutamabhibhūtaṃ paśyati / ātmanā cā 'nyatamena duḥkhena spṛṣṭo bhavatyupadruto 'bhibhūtaḥ / punaśca paramātmānaṃ vā tadubhayaṃ vā dīrghakālikena vicitreṇa tīvreṇa nirantareṇa duḥkhena spṛṣṭamupadrutamabhibhūtaṃ paśyati / iti tasya bodhisattvasya svagotrasanniśrayeṇa prakṛtibhadratayā ebhiścaturbhirālambanairadhiṣṭhānaiḥ karuṇāmṛdumadhyādhimātrā pravarvate anyatrābhyāsataḥ //
body.translated_text: The <s>Bodhisattva</s> is abundant in compassion toward beings in four ways. There are world-systems where suffering is not found, among the infinite and boundless world-systems in the ten directions. Yet the <s>Bodhisattva</s> has been reborn in a world-system where suffering is found, not in one without suffering. Moreover, he sees others touched, afflicted, and overpowered by one or another form of suffering. And he himself is touched, afflicted, and overpowered by one or another form of suffering. Furthermore, he sees others, himself, or both, touched, afflicted, and overpowered by long-lasting, varied, intense, and uninterrupted suffering. Thus, for the <s>Bodhisattva</s>, depending on his own spiritual lineage (<s>gotra</s>) and through innate goodness, by these four objects and foundations, compassion arises — in mild, moderate, and intense degrees — apart from [the compassion arising through] repeated cultivation.

body.text: caturbhiḥ kāraṇairbodhisattvaḥ sattveṣu karuṇāṃ saṃpuraskṛtya saṃsāraduḥkhāddīrghakālikādvicitrāttīvrānnirantarādapi na bibheti nottrasyati prāgeva nihīnāt / prakṛtyā sāttviko bhavati dhṛtimān balavān / idaṃ prathamaṃ kāraṇam / paṇḍito bhavati samyagupanidhyānaśīlaḥ pratisaṃkhyānabalikaḥ / idaṃ dvitīyaṃ kāraṇam / anuttarāyāṃ samyaksaṃbodhāvadhimātrayā 'dhimuktyā samanvāgato bhavati / idaṃ tṛtīyaṃ kāraṇam / sattveṣu cādhimātrayā karuṇayā samanvāgato bhavati idaṃ caturtha kāraṇam /
body.translated_text: For four reasons, the <s>Bodhisattva</s>, having placed compassion toward beings at the forefront, does not fear or tremble at the suffering of <s>saṃsāra</s> — long-lasting, varied, intense, and uninterrupted — let alone at inferior [suffering]. [First:] He is by nature endowed with <s>sattva</s> (courage), possessing fortitude and strength — this is the first reason. [Second:] He is wise, habituated to proper reflection, strong in analytical discernment — this is the second reason. [Third:] He is endowed with intense conviction (<s>adhimukti</s>) in the supreme perfect awakening — this is the third reason. [Fourth:] He is endowed with intense compassion toward beings — this is the fourth reason.

body.text: catvāri balāni katamāni / adhyātmabalaṃ parabalaṃ hetubalaṃ prayogabalañca / tatra svaśaktipatitā yā ruciranuttarāyāṃ samyaksaṃbodhau idamucyate bodhisattvasyādhyātmabalaṃ cittasyotpattaye / paraśaktisamutpāditā tu ruciranuttarāyāṃ samyaksaṃbodhau bodhisattvasya parabalam ityucyate cittasyotpattaye / pūrvako bodhisattvasya mahāyānapratisaṃyuktakuśaladharmābhyāsa etarhi buddhabodhisattvasandarśana mātrakeṇa tadvarṇaśravaṇamātrakeṇa vā āśu cittasyottpattaye prāgeva saddharmaśravaṇena vā prabhāvadarśanena vā hetubalam ityucyate cittasyottpattaye / dṛṣṭadhārmiko bodhisattvasya satpuruṣasaṃsevā-saddharmaśravaṇacintādiko dirghakālikaḥ kuśaladharmābhyāsaḥ prayogabalam ityucyate cittasyotpattaye /
body.translated_text: What are the four powers? They are: the inner power (<s>adhyātmabala</s>), the power from others (<s>parabala</s>), the causal power (<s>hetubala</s>), and the power of practice (<s>prayogabala</s>). There, the inclination (<s>ruci</s>) toward the supreme perfect awakening that has arisen through one's own capacity is called the <s>Bodhisattva</s>'s inner power for the arising of the mind. The inclination toward the supreme perfect awakening that has been generated through the capacity of others is called the <s>Bodhisattva</s>'s power from others for the arising of the mind. The <s>Bodhisattva</s>'s prior cultivation of wholesome qualities connected with the <s>Mahāyāna</s> [is such that] now, through the mere sight of <s>Buddhas</s> and <s>Bodhisattvas</s>, or through the mere hearing of their praise, the mind swiftly arises [toward awakening] — how much more through hearing the true <s>Dharma</s> or seeing miraculous displays: this is called the causal power for the arising of the mind. The <s>Bodhisattva</s>'s long-lasting cultivation of wholesome qualities in this present life — such as association with good persons, hearing the true <s>Dharma</s>, reflection, and so forth — this is called the power of practice for the arising of the mind.

body.text: tatra bodhisattvasya samastavyastāṃścaturaḥ pratyayāṃścaturo hetūnāgamya sacedadhyātmabalena hetubalena ca samastābhyāṃ dvābhyāṃ balābhyāṃ taccittamutpadyate /
body.translated_text: There, when the <s>Bodhisattva</s>'s mind arises based on all four conditions and four causes collectively and individually, and through the two powers combined — the inner power and the causal power —

body.text: evantad dṛḍhaṃñca sārañca niścalaṃ cotpadyate / parabalaprayogabalābhyāṃ tu taccittamadṛḍhodayaṃ veditavyam /
body.translated_text: then that [mind] arises firm, essential, and unshakable. But when [it arises] through the power from others and the power of practice, that mind is to be understood as arising without firmness.

body.text: catvāri bodhisattvasya cittavyāvṛttikāraṇāni / katamāni catvāri / na gotrasaṃpanno bhavati / pāpamitraparigṛhīto bhavati / sattveṣu mandakaruṇo bhavati / saṃsāraduḥkhācca dīrghakālikādvicitrāttīvrānnirantarād bhīrurbhavati atyartha bibhetyuttasyati saṃtrāsamāpadyate / caturṇāṃ cittotpattihetūnāṃ viparyayeṇa catvāryetāni cittavyāvṛttikāraṇāni vistareṇa pūrvavadveditavyāni /
body.translated_text: There are four causes for the reversal (<s>vyāvṛtti</s>) of the <s>Bodhisattva</s>'s mind. What are the four? [First:] One is not endowed with the [proper] spiritual lineage (<s>gotra</s>). [Second:] One is under the influence of evil friends (<s>pāpamitra</s>). [Third:] One has feeble compassion toward beings. [Fourth:] One is afraid of the suffering of <s>saṃsāra</s> — long-lasting, varied, intense, and uninterrupted — one fears exceedingly, trembles, and falls into dread. These four causes for the reversal of the mind are to be understood in detail as the opposites of the four causes for the arising of the mind, as previously [described].

body.text: dvāvimau dṛḍhaprathamacittotpādikasya bodhisattvasya lokāsādhāraṇāvāścaryādbhūtau dharmau / katamau dvau / sarvasattvāṃśca kaḍatrabhāvena parigṛhṇāti / na ca punaḥ kaḍatraparigrahadoṣeṇa lipyate / tatrāyaṃ kaḍatraparigrahadoṣaḥ / kaḍatrasyānugrahopaghātābhyāṃ kliṣṭānurodhavirodhau / tau ca bodhisattvasya na vidyete / dvāvimau dṛḍhaprathamacittotpādikasya bodhisattvasya sattveṣu kalyāṇādhyāśayau pravartete / hitādhyāśayaśca sukhādhyāśayaśca / tatra hitādhyāśayo yā akuśalāt sthānād vyutthāpya kuśale sthāne pratiṣṭhāpanakāmatā sukhādhyāśayo yā vighātināmanāthānāmapratiśaraṇānāṃ sattvānāṃ kliṣṭavarjitānugrāhakavastūṣasaṃharaṇakāmatā /
body.translated_text: There are two extraordinary qualities, uncommon to the world, wondrous and marvelous, belonging to the <s>Bodhisattva</s> who has firmly generated the first mind [of awakening]. What are the two? He embraces all beings as his kin, and yet is not defiled by the fault of kinship-attachment. There, the fault of kinship-attachment is this: afflicted attachment and aversion arising from the benefit or harm of one's kin. These do not exist in the <s>Bodhisattva</s>. Two wholesome dispositions toward beings operate in the <s>Bodhisattva</s> who has firmly generated the first mind: the disposition toward benefit (<s>hitādhyāśaya</s>) and the disposition toward happiness (<s>sukhādhyāśaya</s>). There, the disposition toward benefit is the desire to remove [beings] from unwholesome states and establish them in wholesome states. The disposition toward happiness is the desire to gather for distressed, helpless, and unprotected beings the means of assistance that are free from affliction.

body.text: dvāvimau dṛḍhaprathamacittotpādikasya bodhisattvasya prayogau / adhyāśayaprayogaḥ pratipattiprayogaśca / tatrādhyāśayaprayogo yā tasyaiva hitasukhādhyāśayasya pratidivasamanubṛṃhaṇā / pratipattiprayogaḥ pratidivasamātmanaśca buddhadharmaparipākaprayogaḥ sattvānāñca yathāśakti yathāvalamadhyāśayaprayogameva niśritya hitasukhopasaṃhāraprayogaḥ /
body.translated_text: There are two forms of practice for the <s>Bodhisattva</s> who has firmly generated the first mind: the practice of disposition (<s>adhyāśayaprayoga</s>) and the practice of conduct (<s>pratipattiprayoga</s>). There, the practice of disposition is the daily strengthening of that very disposition toward benefit and happiness. The practice of conduct is the daily effort toward the ripening of <s>Buddha</s>-qualities for oneself and, as much as one is able and capable, the effort to bring about benefit and happiness for beings, relying precisely on the practice of disposition.

body.text: dve ime dṛḍhaprathamacittotpādikasya bodhisattvasya mahatī kuśaladharmāyadvāre / svārthaprayogaścānuttarāyāḥ samyaksaṃbodheḥ samudāgamāya / parārthaprayogaśca sarvasattvānāṃ sarvaduḥkhanirmokṣāya / yathā dve āyadvāre evaṃ dvau mahāntau kuśaladharmasannicayau dvāvaprameyau kuśaladharmaskandhau / peyālam /
body.translated_text: There are two great gateways of wholesome qualities for the <s>Bodhisattva</s> who has firmly generated the first mind: the effort for one's own welfare, for the accomplishment of the supreme perfect awakening; and the effort for the welfare of others, for the complete liberation of all beings from all suffering. Just as there are two gateways of gain, so there are two great accumulations of wholesome qualities, two immeasurable aggregates of wholesome qualities. Abbreviation [follows].

body.text: dve ime prathamacittotpādikasya bodhisattvasya prathamaṃ cittotpādamupādāya
body.translated_text: There are two [distinguishing features] for the <s>Bodhisattva</s> who has generated the first mind: from the first generation of the mind onward,

body.text: bodhāya kuśalaparigrahavaiśeṣye tadanyaṃ kuśalaparigrahamupanidhāya / hetuvaiśeṣyaṃ phalavaiśeṣyañca / sa khalu bodhisattvasya kuśalaparigraho 'nuttanurāyāḥ samyaksaṃbodherhetuḥ sā ca tasya phalam / na tadanyaḥ sarvaśrāvakapratyekabuddhakuśalaparigrahaḥ prāgeva tadanyeṣāṃ sattvānām / tasmādvodhisattvānāṃ kuśalaparigrahastadanyasmātsarvakuśalaparigrahāddhetubhāvataḥ phalataśca prativiśiṣṭaḥ /
body.translated_text: the distinction in the acquisition of wholesome [qualities] directed toward awakening, compared with other acquisitions of wholesome [qualities], [consists of] the distinction of cause and the distinction of fruit. The <s>Bodhisattva</s>'s acquisition of wholesome [qualities] is the cause of the supreme perfect awakening, and that [awakening] is its fruit. No acquisition of wholesome [qualities] by all <s>Śrāvakas</s> and <s>Pratyekabuddhas</s> [can equal it] — how much less that of other beings. Therefore, the <s>Bodhisattvas</s>' acquisition of wholesome [qualities] is superior to all other acquisitions of wholesome [qualities], both in terms of cause and in terms of fruit.

body.text: dvāvimau dṛḍhaprathamacittotpādikasya bodhisattvasya cittotpādānuśaṃsau / sahacittotpādācca sarvasattvānāṃ dakṣiṇīyabhūto bhavati gurubhūtaḥ puṇyakṣetraṃ pitṛkalpaḥ prajānāmavyābādhyasya ca puṇyasya parigrahaṃ karoti / tatredamavyābādhyaṃ puṇyam / yena samanvāgato bodhisattvaścakravarti-dviguṇonārakṣeṇārakṣito bhavati / yasminnārakṣe sadā pratyupasthite na śaknuvanti suptamattapramattasyāpi vyāḍā vā yakṣā vā amanuṣyā vā naivāsikā vā viheṭhāṃ kartum / parivṛttajanmā punarayaṃ bodhisattvastena puṇyaparigraheṇālpābādho bhavatyarogajātīyaḥ / na ca dīrgheṇa khareṇa vā ābādhena spṛśyate / sattvārtheṣu ca sattvakaraṇīyeṣvasya vyāyacchamānasya kāyena vācā dharmañca deśayataḥ nātyarthaṃ kāyaḥ krāmyati na smṛtiḥ pramuṣyate na cittamupahanyate / prakṛtyaiva tāvadgotrastho bodhisattvo mandadauṣṭhulyo bhavati / utpādita cittastu bhūyasyā mātrayā mandatara dauṣṭhulyo bhavati yaduta kāyadauṣṭhulyena cittadauṣṭhulyena ca / asiddhānyapi ca tadanya hastagatāni sattvānāmītyupadravopasargasaṃśamakāni mantrapadāni vidyāpadāni taddhastagatāni sidhyanti / kaḥ punarvādaḥ siddhāni / adhikena ca kṣāntisauratyena samanvāgato bhavati / parata-upatāpasahaḥ aparopatāpī ca / pareṇāpi ca paramupatāpyamānamupalabhyātyartha bādhyate / krodherṣyāśāṭhyamrakṣādayaścāsyopakleśāhatavegā mandāyamānāḥ kadācitsamudācarantyāśu ca vigacchanti / yatra ca grāmakṣetre prativasati tasmin bhayabhairavadurbhikṣadoṣā amanuṣyakṛtāścopadravā anutpannāśca notpadyante utpannāśca vyupaśāmyanti / sa cetpunaḥ sa prathamacittotpādiko bodhisattvaḥ ekadā
body.translated_text: These are two benefits of the generation of the mind for the <s>Bodhisattva</s> who has firmly generated the first mind [of awakening]. Immediately upon generating the mind, he becomes worthy of offerings for all beings, becomes venerable, a field of merit, like a father to creatures, and he acquires inviolable merit. There, this is that inviolable merit: the <s>Bodhisattva</s> endowed with it is protected by a guard twice as great as that of a <s>Cakravartin</s> (universal monarch). When that guard is always at hand, wild beasts, <s>Yakṣas</s>, non-human beings, or <s>Naivāsikas</s> are unable to harm him even when asleep, intoxicated, or heedless. Moreover, this <s>Bodhisattva</s>, reborn [in another life], through that acquisition of merit becomes one of little illness, belonging to the class of the healthy. And he is not touched by prolonged or severe illness. And when exerting himself in matters for the benefit of beings and in duties toward beings, teaching the <s>Dharma</s> with body and speech, his body does not become excessively fatigued, his mindfulness is not lost, and his mind is not impaired. Already by nature, the <s>Bodhisattva</s> established in the lineage has mild heaviness (<s>dauṣṭhulya</s>). But having generated the mind, he becomes to a greater degree milder in heaviness—namely, in bodily heaviness and mental heaviness. Moreover, <s>mantra</s>-formulas and <s>vidyā</s>-formulas for pacifying the calamities and afflictions of beings, which are ineffective in the hands of others, become effective in his hands. How much more so those already effective! And he becomes endowed with superior patience and gentleness. He is able to endure being caused distress by others, and he does not cause distress to others. And upon perceiving another being greatly distressed by yet another, he is greatly pained. And his secondary afflictions—anger, envy, deceit, concealment, and the like—have their force impaired, grow weak, arise only occasionally, and quickly disappear. And in whatever village or region he dwells, the faults of fear, terror, and famine, and calamities caused by non-human beings—those that have not arisen do not arise, and those that have arisen subside. And if that <s>Bodhisattva</s> of the first generation of the mind at some time

body.text: narakeṣvapāyabhūmāvupapadyate sa bhūyasyā mātrayā āśutaraṃ ca mucyate narakebhyaḥ / tanutarāñca duḥkhāṃ vedanāṃ vedayate bhṛśatarañca saṃvegamutpādayati teṣāñca sattvānāmantike karuṇācittatāmavyābādhya puṇyaparigrahahetoḥ / ityevaṃbhāgīyān bahūnanuśaṃsānavyābādhya puṇyaparigrahātprathamacittotpādiko bodhisattvaḥ pratyanubhavati / bodhisattvabhūmāvādhāre yogasthāne dvitīyaṃ cittotpādapaṭalaṃ [samāptam*] //
body.translated_text: is reborn in the hells, in the realms of misfortune, he is released from the hells to a greater degree and more quickly. He experiences a thinner painful feeling and generates a more intense sense of urgency, and toward those beings nearby [he develops] a compassionate mind, on account of [his] acquisition of inviolable merit. Thus, the <s>Bodhisattva</s> of the first generation of the mind experiences many such benefits from the acquisition of inviolable merit. In the <s>Bodhisattvabhūmi</s>, in the Foundation of the Yoga-section, the second chapter, the <s>Cittotpāda-paṭala</s> (Chapter on the Generation of the Mind) [is completed]. //

children.translated_text: <s>Svaparārtha-paṭala</s> (Chapter on One's Own and Others' Benefit)

body.text: evamutpāditacittānāṃ bodhisattvānāṃ bodhisattvacaryā katamā / samāsato bodhisattvā yatra śikṣante yathā ca śikṣante yacca śikṣante tat sarvamaikadhyamabhisaṃkṣipya bodhisattvacaryetyucyate /
body.translated_text: What is the <s>Bodhisattva</s>-practice of <s>Bodhisattvas</s> who have thus generated the mind? In brief, wherever <s>Bodhisattvas</s> train, however they train, and whatever they train in—all of that, gathered together, is called <s>Bodhisattva</s>-practice.

body.text: kutra punarbodhisattvāḥ śikṣante / saptasu sthāneṣu śikṣante / sapta sthānāni katamāni / svārthaḥ parārthaḥ tattvārthaḥ prabhāvaḥ sattvaparipākaḥ ātmano buddhadharmaparipākaḥ anuttarā ca samyaksaṃbodhiḥ saptamaṃ sthānam /
body.translated_text: Where then do <s>Bodhisattvas</s> train? They train in seven areas. What are the seven areas? One's own benefit (<s>svārtha</s>), others' benefit (<s>parārtha</s>), the meaning of reality (<s>tattvārtha</s>), power (<s>prabhāva</s>), maturation of beings (<s>sattvaparipāka</s>), maturation of one's own <s>Buddha</s>-qualities (<s>buddhadharmaparipāka</s>), and the unsurpassed perfect awakening (<s>anuttarā samyaksaṃbodhi</s>) is the seventh area.

body.text: uddānam /
body.translated_text: Summary verse (<s>uddāna</s>):

children.translated_text: One's own and others' benefit, the meaning of reality, power, the maturation
of beings and of one's own <s>Buddha</s>-qualities, and supreme awakening is the seventh. //

body.text: svaparārthaḥ katamaḥ samāsato daśavidhaḥ svaparārtho veditavyaḥ / kevalaṃ parasambaddhaḥ hitānvayaḥ sukhānvayaḥ hetusaṃgṛhītaḥ phalasaṃgṛhītaḥ ehikaḥ āmutrikaḥ ātyantikaḥ anātyantikaśca /
body.translated_text: What is one's own and others' benefit? In brief, one's own and others' benefit should be understood as tenfold: exclusive (<s>kevala</s>), connected with others (<s>parasambaddha</s>), conducive to welfare (<s>hitānvaya</s>), conducive to happiness (<s>sukhānvaya</s>), comprised in causes (<s>hetusaṃgṛhīta</s>), comprised in results (<s>phalasaṃgṛhīta</s>), pertaining to this life (<s>aihika</s>), pertaining to the next life (<s>āmutrika</s>), ultimate (<s>ātyantika</s>), and non-ultimate (<s>anātyantika</s>).

body.text: tatra kevalaḥ svārthaḥ parārthaśca bodhisattvena parijñāya prahātavyaḥ bodhisattvavidheḥ samatikrāntatvādananurūpatvācca / pariśiṣṭe ca śikṣitavyaḥ / tatrāyaṃ kevalaḥ svārtho bodhisattvasya yo 'nena parijñāya prahātavyo bhavati / ātmanaḥ sukhakāmasya bhogānāṃ paryeṣaṇā upabhogaśca / dharmamatsariṇo vā punaḥ sato dharmāṇāṃ buddhabodhisattvabhāṣitānāṃ paryeṃṣaṇā dhāraṇā ca / svargakāmasya svargārtha śīlaṃ vīryārambhaṃ dhyānaṃ prajñāṃ samādāya vartanā / lokāmiṣaphalābhilāṣiṇo vā punaḥ lokāmiṣanimittaṃ tathāgatacaityapūjā / lābhakāmasya vā lābhanimittaṃ lābhanirvartakaṃ mamārthaṃ pareṣāmutplāvakaṃ vicitrābhūtaguṇākhyānam / ātmanaḥ paricaryāsvīkaraṇakāmasya paricaryāsvīkaraṇārthamadharmeṇa gaṇasaṃgraho na dharmeṇa / parato dāsabhūtān sattvān dāsabhāvāddhi pramokṣayati yāvadevātmano dāsabhāvāya /
body.translated_text: There, exclusive self-interest and [exclusive] interest in others are to be comprehended and abandoned by the <s>Bodhisattva</s>, because they transcend and are unfitting for the <s>Bodhisattva</s>'s method. And one should train in the remainder. There, this is the exclusive self-interest of the <s>Bodhisattva</s> which is to be comprehended and abandoned by him: the search for and enjoyment of possessions by one who desires happiness for oneself alone; or, being one who is miserly with the <s>Dharma</s>, the search for and retention of the <s>dharmas</s> spoken by <s>Buddhas</s> and <s>Bodhisattvas</s>; the practice of undertaking moral conduct, vigor, meditation, and wisdom for the sake of heaven by one who desires heaven; or the worship of <s>Tathāgata</s> shrines for the sake of worldly rewards by one who desires worldly gains; or, by one desiring gain, the narration of varied and extraordinary qualities for the purpose of gain, producing gain for oneself and cheating others; or, by one desiring personal service, gathering a following through unrighteousness rather than righteousness for the purpose of receiving personal service. He liberates beings who are in a state of servitude to others from their servitude only for the purpose of making them his own slaves.

body.text: bandhanabaddhān sattvān bandhanādvimokṣya svayameva badhnāti yāvadevātmanaḥ kṛtyaniṣpattaye / daṇḍādibhayabhītāṃśca sattvān parato daṇḍādibhayādvipramokṣayati yāvadeva svayameva bhayagrahaṇārtham / dṛṣṭadharmasukhavihāraśca bodhisattvasya sattvārthanidhyānavirahitaḥ kevalaḥ svārtho veditavyaḥ / ityevaṃbhāgīyo bodhisattvasya kevalaḥ svārtho vedivtayo yo bodhisattvena parijñāya prahātavyaḥ /
body.translated_text: He liberates beings bound in bonds from their bonds only to bind them himself, just for the accomplishment of his own purposes. And he frees beings frightened by the fear of punishment and the like from others' threat of punishment only for the purpose of seizing [them through] fear for himself. And the pleasant abiding in this very life of the <s>Bodhisattva</s>, devoid of reflection on the benefit of beings, should be understood as exclusive self-interest. Thus, such is the exclusive self-interest of the <s>Bodhisattva</s> that is to be comprehended and abandoned by the <s>Bodhisattva</s>.

body.text: dānaṃ punaḥ bodhisattvasya kṣāntiśca kāruṇyapūrvakaṃ vā bodhipariṇataṃ vā svarganimittaṃ vā nityakālaṃ parasambaddha eva svārtho veditavyaḥ /
body.translated_text: Moreover, the <s>Bodhisattva</s>'s generosity (<s>dāna</s>) and patience (<s>kṣānti</s>)—whether preceded by compassion, dedicated to awakening, or for the sake of heaven—should always be understood as self-interest connected with others (<s>parasambaddha svārtha</s>).

body.text: ityetān yathānirdiṣṭānākārān sthāpayitvā tadanya etadviparyayātsvārtho bodhisattvānāṃ sarva eva parārthasambaddho veditavyaḥ /
body.translated_text: Thus, setting aside these aspects as described, all other self-interest of <s>Bodhisattvas</s>, by the opposite [of what was described], should be understood as connected with others' benefit.

body.text: tatrāyaṃ bodhisattvasya kevalaḥ parārtho bodhisattvena parijñāya prahātavyaḥ / vipanna dṛṣṭerdānam anāgamadṛṣṭeraphaladarśinaḥ bhraṣṭaśīlasya pratipattivirahitasya pareṣāṃ dharmadeśanā / adhobhūmisamatikrāntasyādhobhūmikaśukladharmopasaṃhāro dhyānavyāvartanakuśalasya ca bodhisattvasya / tathāhi sa dhyānairvihṛtya dhyānaṃ vyāvarttya praṇidhāya yatra kāmaṃ tatra kāmadhātāvupapadyate / vaśitāprāptasya ca bodhisattvasya daśasu nikṣu vicitrairnirmāṇaiḥ vicitrāṇāṃ sattvānāmarthakriyā / ca svakṛtārthasya munestathāgatasya balavaiśāradyādisarvāveṇikabuddhadharmasaṃniśrayeṇāpramāṇeṣu sattveṣvapramāṇārthakriyā / so 'pi parārthaḥ kevalo veditavyaḥ / tatra pūrvako dvividhaḥ parārthaḥ kevalo yathā nirdiṣṭo bodhisattvena parijñāya prahātavyaḥ / tadanyatra ca kevale parārthe bhūyasyā mātrayā śikṣitavyam / ityetānākārān sthāpayitvā etadviparyayācca bodhisattvānāṃ sarvaḥ parārthaḥ svārthaḥ sambaddhaḥ / tatrāpi bodhisattvena śikṣitavyam /
body.translated_text: There, this is the exclusive interest in others of the <s>Bodhisattva</s> that is to be comprehended and abandoned by the <s>Bodhisattva</s>: the giving of one with wrong views; the teaching of <s>Dharma</s> to others by one who holds the view of no [karmic] consequence, who sees no fruit, who has fallen from moral conduct, and who is devoid of practice; the bringing about of wholesome qualities of a lower stage by one who has transcended a lower stage, and by the <s>Bodhisattva</s> who is skilled in turning away from <s>dhyāna</s>—for indeed, having dwelt in the <s>dhyānas</s>, turning away from <s>dhyāna</s>, and having made a resolve, he is reborn wherever he wishes in the desire-realm (<s>Kāmadhātu</s>); and the activity for the benefit of various beings through various emanations in the ten directions by the <s>Bodhisattva</s> who has attained mastery (<s>vaśitā</s>); and the immeasurable activity for the benefit of immeasurable beings by the <s>Muni</s>, the <s>Tathāgata</s> who has accomplished his own purpose, through reliance on the powers (<s>bala</s>), fearlessnesses (<s>vaiśāradya</s>), and all the exclusive <s>Buddha</s>-qualities. That too should be understood as exclusive interest in others. There, the former twofold exclusive interest in others, as described, is to be comprehended and abandoned by the <s>Bodhisattva</s>. And in the other [kinds of] exclusive interest in others, one should train to a greater degree. Thus, setting aside these aspects, and by the opposite [of what was described], all interest in others of <s>Bodhisattvas</s> is connected with self-interest. In that too, the <s>Bodhisattva</s> should train.

body.text: hitānvayaḥ svaparārtho bodhisattvasya katamaḥ / samāsataḥ pañcākāro veditavyaḥ / anavadyalakṣaṇaḥ anugrāhakalakṣaṇaḥ aihikaḥ āmutrikaḥ aupaśamikaśca / tatra yatkiṃcid bodhisattvaḥ ātmanā vā parīttaṃ prabhūtaṃ vā kuśalaparigrahaṃ kuśalopacayaṃ karoti paraṃ vā parītte prabhūte vā kuśalaparigrahe kuśalopacaye samādāpayati vinayati
body.translated_text: What is the <s>Bodhisattva</s>'s own and others' benefit that is conducive to welfare (<s>hitānvaya</s>)? In brief, it should be understood as fivefold: characterized by blamelessness (<s>anavadya</s>), characterized by assistance (<s>anugrāhaka</s>), pertaining to this life (<s>aihika</s>), pertaining to the next life (<s>āmutrika</s>), and pertaining to pacification (<s>aupaśamika</s>). There, whatever wholesome accumulation and increase—whether small or great—the <s>Bodhisattva</s> undertakes himself, or whatever he causes others to undertake, trains,

body.text: niveśayati pratiṣṭhāpayati / ayamanavadyalakṣaṇo bodhisattvasya hitānvayaḥ svaparārtho veditavyaḥ / yatkiṃcidvodhisattvaḥ ātmano vā parasya vā kliṣṭa varjitaṃ sukhamupasaṃharati upakaraṇasukhaṃ vā dhyānasukhaṃ vā ayaṃ bodhisattvasyānugrāhakalakṣaṇo hitānvayaḥ svaparārtho veditavyaḥ / asti bodhisattvasya svaparārtha iha-hito nāmutra / astyamutra neha / astyamutra caiha ca / asti naivāmutra neha-hitaḥ / sa punareṣa caturvidhaḥ svaparārthaḥ caturṣu dharmasamādaneṣvanupūrva yathāyogaṃ dṛṣṭavyaḥ / catvāri dharmasamādānāni katamāni / asti dharmasamādānaṃ pratyutpanna-sukhāmāyatyāṃ duḥkhavipākam / asti pratyutpannaduḥkhamāyatyāṃ sukhavipākam / asti pratyutpannasukhamāyatyāṃ sukhavipākam / asti pratyutpannaduḥkhamāyatyāṃ duḥkhavipākam / vibhaṅgā eṣāṃ yathāsūtrameva veditavyāḥ / tatra nirvāṇaṃ nirvāṇaṃsaṃprāpakaśca nirvāṇapakṣyā laukikalokottarā dharmā ityeṣa samāsato bodhisattvasya hitānvaya aupaśamikaḥ svaparārthaḥ sarvaprativiśiṣṭo niruttaro veditavyaḥ /
body.translated_text: establishes, and firmly grounds them in—this should be understood as the <s>Bodhisattva</s>'s own and others' benefit conducive to welfare, characterized by blamelessness. Whatever happiness the <s>Bodhisattva</s> brings about for himself or another that is free from affliction—whether the happiness of material provisions, or the happiness of <s>dhyāna</s> (meditation)—this should be understood as the <s>Bodhisattva</s>'s own and others' benefit conducive to welfare, characterized by assistance. There is the <s>Bodhisattva</s>'s own and others' benefit that is beneficial here but not hereafter; that is beneficial hereafter but not here; that is beneficial both here and hereafter; and that is beneficial neither here nor hereafter. This fourfold own and others' benefit should be seen in order, as appropriate, in the four undertakings of <s>dharma</s> (<s>dharmasamādāna</s>). What are the four undertakings of <s>dharma</s>? There is an undertaking of <s>dharma</s> that is pleasant in the present but ripens as suffering in the future; one that is suffering in the present but ripens as happiness in the future; one that is pleasant in the present and ripens as happiness in the future; and one that is suffering in the present and ripens as suffering in the future. Their detailed analysis should be understood as in the <s>sūtra</s>. There, <s>Nirvāṇa</s>, the <s>dharmas</s> conducive to <s>Nirvāṇa</s>—both mundane and supramundane—that lead to the attainment of <s>Nirvāṇa</s>: this, in brief, should be understood as the <s>Bodhisattva</s>'s own and others' benefit conducive to welfare pertaining to pacification—the most distinguished of all, unsurpassed.
