body.text: kathaṃ punardurgṛhītā bhavati śūnyatā / yaḥ kaści] cchramaṇo vā brāhmaṇo vā tacca necchati yena śūnyam / tadapi necchati yat śūnyam / iyamevaṃrūpā durgṛhītā śūnyatetyucyate / taktasya hetoḥ / yena hi śūnyaṃ tadasadbhāvāt / yacca śūnyaṃ tatsadbhāvācchūnyatā yujyeta / sarvābhāvācca kutra kiṃ kena śūnyaṃ bhaviṣyati / na ca tena tasyaiva śūnyatā yujyate / tasmādevaṃ durgṛhītā śūnyatā bhavati /
body.translated_text: How then is emptiness (<s>śūnyatā</s>) wrongly grasped? When any <s>śramaṇa</s> (ascetic) or <s>brāhmaṇa</s> neither accepts that by which [something] is empty, nor accepts that which is empty — such a form of wrongly grasped emptiness is declared. For what reason? Because that by which [something] is empty does not [truly] exist, and that which is empty does exist — [only then] would emptiness be appropriate. But if absolutely nothing exists, then where, what, and by what would anything be empty? And it is not appropriate that anything be empty of itself. Therefore, emptiness is wrongly grasped in this way.

body.text: kathañca punaḥ sugṛhītā śūnyatā bhavati / yataśca yad yatra na bhavati tat tena śūnyamiti samanupaśyati / yatpunaratrāvaśiṣṭaṃ bhavati tatsadihāstīti yathābhūtaṃ prajānāti / iyamucyate śūnyatāvakrāntiryathābhūtā aviparītā / tadyathā rūpādisaṃjñake yathā nirdiṣṭe vastuni rūpamityevamādiprajñaptivādātmako dharmo nāsti / atastadrūpādisaṃjñakaṃ vastu tena rūpamityevamādiprajñaptivādātmanā śūnyam / kiṃ punastatra rūpādisaṃjñake vastunayavaśiṣṭam / yaduta tadeva rūpamityevamādiprajñaptivādāśrayaḥ / taccobhayaṃ yathābhūtaṃ prajānāti yaduta vastamātrañca vidyamānaṃ vastamātre ca prajñaptimātraṃ ca cāsadbhūtaṃ samāropayati / na bhūtamapavadate nādhikaṃ karoti na nyūnīkaroti notkṣipati na pratikṣipati / yathābhūtañca tathatāṃ nirabhilāpyasvabhāvatāṃ yathābhūtaṃ prajānāti / iyamucyate sugṛhītā śūnyatā samyak prajñayā supratividdheti / iyaṃ tāvadupapattisādhanayuktirānulomikī yayā nirabhilāpyasvabhāvatā sarvadharmāṇāṃ pratyavagantavyā /
body.translated_text: And how is emptiness correctly grasped? Since whatever is not present somewhere — one sees that [place] as empty of that; and whatever remains here as present — one knows that as 'this truly exists here.' This is called the entry into emptiness, as it truly is, without distortion. For instance, in the object designated as form and so forth, as described, the <s>dharma</s> whose nature consists of the designative statement 'form' and such — that does not exist. Therefore, the object designated as form and so forth is empty of the nature consisting of the designative statement 'form' and such. What then remains in the object designated as form and so forth? Namely, that very foundation of the designative statements 'form' and such. And one knows both aspects as they truly are: namely, the mere object as existent, and in the mere object, the mere designation as unreal — one does not superimpose the unreal, does not deny the real, does not add anything, does not diminish, does not cast away, and does not reject. And one knows <s>tathatā</s> (suchness), the inexpressible own-nature, as it truly is. This is called 'correctly grasped emptiness, well penetrated by correct wisdom.' This, then, is the conforming rational proof (<s>upapattisādhanayukti</s>) by which the inexpressible own-nature of all <s>dharmas</s> is to be comprehended.

body.text: āptāgamato 'pi nirabhilāpyasvabhāvāḥ sarvadharmā veditavyāḥ / yathoktaṃ bhagavatā evamevārthaṃ gāthābhigītena paridīpayatā bhavasaṃkrāntisūtre /
body.translated_text: From authoritative scripture (<s>āptāgama</s>) too, all <s>dharmas</s> are to be understood as having an inexpressible own-nature. As the <s>Bhagavān</s> has said, illuminating this very meaning through a verse spoken in the <s>Bhavasaṃkrāntisūtra</s>:

body.text:
yena yena hi nāmnā vai yo yo dharmo 'bhilapyate /
na sa saṃvidyate tatra dharmāṇāṃ sā hi dharmatā // iti /
body.translated_text:
By whatever name any <s>dharma</s> is expressed,
that [name-nature] is not found therein — such indeed is the <s>dharmatā</s> (true nature) of <s>dharmas</s>.

body.text: kathañca punariyaṃ gāthā etamevārthaṃ paridīpayati / rūpādisaṃjñakasya dharmasya yadrūpamityevamādi nāma / yena rūpamityevamādinā nāmnā te rūpādisaṃjñakā dharmā abhilapyante 'nuvyavahriyante rūpamiti vā vedaneti vā vistareṇa yāvannirvāṇamiti vā / tatra na ca rūpādisaṃjñakā dharmāḥ svayaṃ rūpādyātmakāḥ / na ca teṣu tadanyo rūpādyātmako dharmo vidyate / yā punasteṣāṃ rūpādisaṃjñakānāṃ dharmāṇāṃ nirabhilāpyenārthena vidyamānatā saiṣā paramārthataḥ svabhāvadharmatā veditavyā / uktañca bhagavatā arthavargīyeṣu /
body.translated_text: And how does this verse illuminate this very meaning? For a <s>dharma</s> designated as form and so forth, the name is 'form' and such. By such names as 'form' and so forth, those <s>dharmas</s> designated as form and so forth are expressed, conventionally used — 'form,' or 'feeling,' in detail up to '<s>nirvāṇa</s>.' There, the <s>dharmas</s> designated as form and so forth are not in themselves of the nature of form and so forth. Nor is there any other <s>dharma</s> of the nature of form and so forth found in them. But the existence of the <s>dharmas</s> designated as form and so forth through their inexpressible referent — that is to be understood as their ultimate own-nature <s>dharmatā</s>. And the <s>Bhagavān</s> has said in the <s>Arthavargīya</s> [verses]:

body.text:
yāḥ kāñcana saṃvṛtayo hi loke sarvā hi tā munirno upaiti /
anupago hyasau kena upādadīta dṛṣṭaśrute kāntimasaṃprakurvan /
body.translated_text:
Whatever conventions there are in the world — the Sage does not enter into any of them.
For one who is unattached, how would one grasp? — not producing attachment to what is seen and heard.

body.text: kathamiyaṃ gāthā etamevārthaṃ paridīpayati / rūpādisaṃjñake vastuni yā rūpamityevamādyāḥ prajñaptayaḥ / tāḥ saṃvṛtaya ityucyante / tābhiḥ prajñaptibhistasya vastunastādātmyamityevaṃ nopaiti tāḥ saṃvṛtīḥ / tatkasya hetoḥ / samāropāpavādikā dṛṣṭirasya nāsti / ato 'sau tasyā viparyāsapratyupasthānāyā dṛṣṭerabhāvādanupaga ityucyate / sa evamanapagaḥ san kenopādadīta / tayā dṛṣṭyā vinā tadvastusamāropato vāpavādato vā anupādadānaḥ samyagdarśī bhavati jñeye tadasya dṛṣṭam / yastasyaiva jñeyasyābhilāpānuśravastadasya śrutam / tasmin dṛṣṭaśrute tṛṣṇāṃ notpādayati na vivardhayati / nānyatra tenāvalambanena prajahātyupekṣakaśca viharati / evaṃ kāntiṃ karoti / panaścoktaṃ bhagavatā saṃthakātyāyanamārabhya-iha saṃtha bhikṣurna pṛthivīṃ niśritya dhyāyati / nāpaḥ / na tejaḥ / na vāyum /
body.translated_text: How does this verse illuminate this very meaning? The designations such as 'form' and so forth applied to the object designated as form and so forth — these are called 'conventions' (<s>saṃvṛti</s>). [The Sage] does not enter into those conventions, [thinking:] 'The object is identical with those designations.' For what reason? Because he does not have the view of superimposition or denial. Therefore, due to the absence of that distorted view that would present [itself], he is called 'unattached' (<s>anupaga</s>). Being thus unattached, how would he grasp? Without that [distorted] view, neither superimposing upon the object nor denying it, not grasping, he has correct vision regarding the knowable — that is his 'seeing.' The hearing of the verbal description of that very knowable — that is his 'hearing.' In that which is seen and heard, he does not generate or increase craving (<s>tṛṣṇā</s>). He does not abandon [it] through some other object of support, but dwells in equanimity. This is how he 'does not produce attachment.' Furthermore, the <s>Bhagavān</s> has said with reference to <s>Saṃthakātyāyana</s>: 'Here, <s>Saṃtha</s>, a <s>bhikṣu</s> does not meditate depending on earth, nor on water, nor on fire, nor on wind.

body.text: nākāśavijñānākiñcanyanaivasaṃjñānāsaṃjñāyatanaṃ nemaṃ lokaṃ na paraṃ lokaṃ nobhau sūryācandramasau na dṛṣṭaśrutamatavijñātaṃ prāptaṃ paryeṣitaṃ manasānuvitarkitamanuvicāritam / tatsarvaṃ na niśritya dhyāyati / kathaṃ dhyāyī / pṛthivīṃ na niśritya dhyāyati vistareṇa yāvat sarvaṃ na niśritya dhyāyati / iha saṃtha bhikṣoryā pṛthivyāṃ pṛthivīsaṃjñā sā vibhūtā bhavati / apsu apsaṃjñā vistareṇa yāvat sarvatra yā saṃjñā sā vibhūtā bhavati / evaṃdhyāyī bhikṣurna pṛthivīṃ niśritya dhyāyati vistareṇa yāvanna sarvaṃ sarvamiti niśritya dhyāyati / evaṃ dhyāyinaṃ bhikṣuṃ sendrā devāḥ seśānāḥ saprajāpataya ārānnamaṣyanti /
body.translated_text: not the sphere of space (<s>ākāśa</s>), not the sphere of consciousness (<s>vijñāna</s>), not the sphere of nothingness (<s>ākiñcanya</s>), not the sphere of neither-perception-nor-non-perception (<s>naivasaṃjñānāsaṃjñāyatana</s>), not this world, not the other world, not both sun and moon, not what is seen, heard, thought, cognized, attained, sought, or mentally reflected and deliberated upon—relying on none of all that does he meditate. How does one who meditates [meditate]? Not relying on the earth does he meditate, and in detail, not relying on anything at all does he meditate. Here, O <s>Saṃtha</s>, when a monk has the perception of earth in the earth, that has been destroyed. When he has the perception of water in water, and in detail, wherever there is perception, that has been destroyed. A monk meditating thus does not meditate relying on the earth, and in detail, does not meditate relying on anything at all, [thinking] 'this is everything.' The gods, together with <s>Indra</s>, together with <s>Īśāna</s>, together with <s>Prajāpati</s>, will bow to such a meditating monk from afar:

body.text:
namaste puruṣājanya namaste puruṣottama /
yasya te nābhijānīmaḥ kiṃ tvaṃ niśritya dhyāyasi // iti /
body.translated_text:
'Homage to you, O noble among men! Homage to you, O supreme among men!
We do not know—relying on what do you meditate?' //

body.text: kathañca punaretatsūtrapadametamevārthaṃ paridīpayati pṛthivyādisaṃjñake vastuni yā pṛthivītyevamādikā nāmasaṃketaprajñaptiḥ sā pṛthivyādisaṃjñetyucyate / sā punaḥ saṃjñā pṛthivyādisaṃjñake vastuni samāropikā cāpavādikā ca / tanmayasvabhāvavastugrāhikā samāropikā / vastumātraparamārthanāśagrāhikā cāpavādikā saṃjñetyucyate / sā ca saṃjñāsya vibhūtā bhavati / vibhava ucyate prahāṇaṃ tyāgaḥ / tasmādāgamato 'pi tathāgatāt paramāptāgamādveditavyaṃ nirabhilāpyasvabhāvāḥ sarvadharmā iti / evaṃ nirabhilāpyasvabhāveṣu sarvadharmeṣu kasmādabhilāpaḥ prayujyate tathā hi vinābhilāpena sā nirabhilāpyadharmatā pareṣāṃ vakta mapi na śakyate śrotumapi / vacane śravaṇe cāsati sā nirabhilāpyasvabhāvatā jñātumapi na śakyate / tasmādabhilāpaḥ prayujyate śravaṇajñānāya /
body.translated_text: And how does this <s>sūtra</s>-passage illuminate this very meaning? In an object designated as 'earth' and so forth, the conventional designation (<s>nāmasaṃketaprajñapti</s>) such as 'earth' and the like is what is called 'the perception of earth and so forth.' That perception, moreover, in an object designated as 'earth' and so forth, is both superimposing (<s>samāropikā</s>) and denying (<s>apavādikā</s>). That which grasps the object as being of that intrinsic nature is called superimposing perception. That which grasps the mere object as destroyed in its ultimate reality is called denying perception. And that perception of his has been destroyed (<s>vibhūtā</s>). Destruction (<s>vibhava</s>) means abandonment, relinquishment. Therefore, even from the authoritative tradition (<s>āgama</s>)—from the <s>Tathāgata</s>, who is the supremely reliable authority—it should be understood that all <s>dharmas</s> are of inexpressible nature (<s>nirabhilāpyasvabhāva</s>). If all <s>dharmas</s> are of inexpressible nature, why then is verbal expression employed? Because without verbal expression, that very inexpressible nature of <s>dharmas</s> can neither be spoken about to others nor heard. And in the absence of speaking and hearing, that inexpressible nature cannot even be known. Therefore, verbal expression is employed for the sake of knowledge through hearing.

body.text: tasyā eva tathatāyā evamaparijñātatvādvālānāṃ tannidāno 'ṣṭavidho vikalpaḥ pravartate trivastujanakaḥ / sarvasattvabhājanalokānāṃ nirvartakaḥ / tadyathā svabhāva vikalpo viśeṣavikalpaḥ piṇḍagrāhavikalpaḥ ahamiti vikalpaḥ mameti vikalpaḥ priyavikalpaḥ apriyavikalpaḥ tadubhayaviparītaśca vikalpaḥ / sa punarayamaṣṭavidho vikalpaḥ katameṣāṃ trayāṇāṃ vastūnāṃ janako bhavati / yaśca
body.translated_text: Because that very <s>tathatā</s> (suchness) has not been fully comprehended in this way, an eightfold conceptualization (<s>vikalpa</s>) arises in the childish, conditioned by that [non-comprehension], which produces three [kinds of] objects and brings about the existence of all beings and the world-vessel. Namely: conceptualization of intrinsic nature (<s>svabhāvavikalpa</s>), conceptualization of distinction (<s>viśeṣavikalpa</s>), conceptualization of aggregate-grasping (<s>piṇḍagrāhavikalpa</s>), conceptualization of 'I' (<s>ahamiti vikalpa</s>), conceptualization of 'mine' (<s>mameti vikalpa</s>), conceptualization of the agreeable (<s>priyavikalpa</s>), conceptualization of the disagreeable (<s>apriyavikalpa</s>), and conceptualization contrary to both of those. That eightfold conceptualization—of which three objects does it become the producer?

body.text: svabhāvavikalpo yaśca viśeṣavikalpo yaśca piṇḍagrāhavikalpa itīme trayo vikalpā vikalpaprapañcādhiṣṭhānaṃ vikalpaprapañcālambanaṃ vastu janayanti rūpādisaṃjñakam / yadvastvadhiṣṭhāya sa nāmasaṃjñābhilāpaparigṛhīto nāmasaṃjñābhilāpaparibhāvito vikalpaḥ prapañcayan tasminneva vastuni vicaratyanekavidho bahunānāprakāraḥ / tatra yañcāhamiti vikalpo yaśca mameti vikalpaḥ itīmau dvau vikalpau satkāyadṛṣṭiśca tadanyasarvadṛṣṭi[-mūlaṃ māna-]mūlamasmimānañca tadanyasarvamānamūlaṃ janayataḥ / tatra priyavikalpo 'priyavikalpastadubhayaviparītaśca vikalpo yathāyogaṃ rāgadveṣamohān janayanti / evamayamaṣṭavidho vikalpaḥ asya trividhasya vastunaḥ prādurbhāvāya saṃvartate yaduta vikalpādhiṣṭhānasya prapañcavastunaḥ dṛṣṭyasmimānasya rāgadveṣamohānāñca / tatra vikalpaprapañcavastvāśrayā satkāyadṛṣṭirasmimānaśca / satkāyadṛṣṭyasmimānāśritā rāgadveṣamohāḥ / ebhiśca tribhirvastubhiḥ sarvalokānāṃ pravṛttipakṣo niravaśeṣaḥ paridīpito bhavati /
body.translated_text: The conceptualization of intrinsic nature, the conceptualization of distinction, and the conceptualization of aggregate-grasping—these three conceptualizations produce the object designated as 'form' and the like, which is the basis and referent of conceptual proliferation (<s>vikalpaprapañca</s>). Relying on that object, conceptualization—grasped by name, designation, and verbal expression, conditioned and permeated by name, designation, and verbal expression—proliferates and operates in that very object in multiple and manifold ways. There, the conceptualization of 'I' and the conceptualization of 'mine'—these two conceptualizations produce the view of the person-aggregate (<s>satkāyadṛṣṭi</s>) and the root of all other views, and the conceit 'I am' (<s>asmimāna</s>) and the root of all other conceits. There, the conceptualization of the agreeable, the conceptualization of the disagreeable, and the conceptualization contrary to both—these, respectively, produce passion (<s>rāga</s>), aversion (<s>dveṣa</s>), and delusion (<s>moha</s>). Thus, this eightfold conceptualization conduces to the manifestation of three kinds of objects: namely, the object that is the basis and referent of conceptual proliferation, the view of the person-aggregate and the conceit 'I am,' and passion, aversion, and delusion. There, the view of the person-aggregate and the conceit 'I am' are based on the object of conceptual proliferation. Passion, aversion, and delusion are based on the view of the person-aggregate and the conceit 'I am.' And through these three objects, the entire side of the arising of all worlds is illuminated without remainder.

body.text: tatra svabhāvavikalpaḥ katamaḥ / rūpādisaṃjñake vastuni rūpamityevamādiryo vikalpaḥ / ayamucyate svabhāvavikalpaḥ /
body.translated_text: There, what is the conceptualization of intrinsic nature? In an object designated as 'form' and the like, the conceptualization such as 'this is form' and so forth—this is called the conceptualization of intrinsic nature.

body.text: viśeṣavikalpaḥ katamaḥ / tasminneva rūpādisaṃjñake vastuni ayaṃ rūpī ayamarūpī ayaṃ sanidarśano 'yamanidarśana evaṃ sapratigho 'pratighaḥ / sāsravo 'nāsravaḥ saṃskṛto 'saṃskṛtaḥ kuśalo 'kuśalo vyākṛto 'vyākṛtaḥ atīto 'nāgataḥ pratyutpanna ityevaṃbhāgīyenāpramāṇena prabhedanayena yā svabhāvavikalpādhiṣṭhānā tadviśiṣṭārthavikalpanā / ayamucyate viśeṣavikalpaḥ /
body.translated_text: What is the conceptualization of distinction? In that very object designated as 'form' and the like, [the conceptualization:] 'this has form, this is formless; this is visible, this is invisible; likewise, this is resistant, non-resistant; defiled, undefiled; conditioned, unconditioned; wholesome, unwholesome; determined, undetermined; past, future, present'—this kind of conceptualization of distinct meanings based on the conceptualization of intrinsic nature, following an immeasurable manner of differentiation—this is called the conceptualization of distinction.

body.text: piṇḍagrāhavikalpaḥ katamaḥ / yastasminneva rūpādisaṃjñake vastuni ātmasattva jīvajantusaṃjñāsaṃketopasaṃhitaḥ piṇḍiteṣu bahuṣu dharmeṣu piṇḍagrāhahetukaḥ pravartate gṛhasenāvanādiṣu bhojanapānayānavastrādiṣu ca tatsaṃjñāsaṃketopasaṃhitaḥ / ayamucyate piṇḍagrāhavikalpaḥ /
body.translated_text: What is the conceptualization of aggregate-grasping? That which, in that very object designated as 'form' and the like, operating through the conventional designations of self, being, soul, creature, and proceeding by grasping aggregated collections of many <s>dharmas</s> as wholes—in houses, armies, forests, and the like, in food, drink, vehicles, garments, and the like—accompanied by such conventional designations—this is called the conceptualization of aggregate-grasping.

body.text: ahamiti mameti ca vikalpaḥ katamaḥ / yadvastu sāsravaṃ sopādānīyaṃ dīrghakālamātmato vā ātmīyato vā saṃstutamabhiniviṣṭaṃ paricitaṃ tasmādasaṃgrāha-saṃstavāt svaṃ dṛṣṭisthānīyaṃ vastu pratītyotpadyate vitatho viakalpaḥ / ayamucyate ahamiti mameti ca vikalpaḥ /
body.translated_text: What is the conceptualization of 'I' and 'mine'? That object which is defiled, with clinging, and which, having been long intimately associated with, fixated upon, and familiarized as self or as belonging to self—from that habitual intimacy, depending on one's own object, which stands in the place of a view, there arises a false conceptualization—this is called the conceptualization of 'I' and 'mine.'

body.text: priyavikalpaḥ katamaḥ / yaḥ śubha-manāpa-vastvālambano vikalpaḥ /
body.translated_text: What is the conceptualization of the agreeable? That conceptualization which takes as its object a pleasant, attractive thing.

body.text: apriyavikalpaḥ katamaḥ / yo 'śubhāmanāpa-vastvālambano vikalpaḥ /
body.translated_text: What is the conceptualization of the disagreeable? That conceptualization which takes as its object an unpleasant, unattractive thing.

body.text: priyāpriyobhayaviparīto vikalpaḥ katamaḥ / yaḥ śubhāśubha-manāpāmanāpatadubhayavivarjitavastvālambano vikalpaḥ / taccaitad dvayaṃ bhavati samāsataḥ vikalpaśca vikalpādhiṣṭhānaṃ vikalpālambanañca vastu / taccaitadubhayamanādikālikaṃ cānyonyahetukañca veditavyam / pūrvako vikalpaḥ pratyutpannasya vikalpālambanasya vastunaḥ prādurbhāvāya pratyutpannaṃ punarvikalpālambanaṃ vastu prādurbhūtaṃ pratyutpannasya tadālambanasya [vikalpasya] prādurbhāvāya hetuḥ / tatraitarhi vikalpasyāparijñānamāyatyāṃ tadālambanasya vastunaḥ prādurbhāvāya / tatsaṃbhāvācca punarniyataṃ tadadhiṣṭhānasyāpi tadāśritasya vikalpasya prādurbhāvo bhavati /
body.translated_text: What is the conceptualization contrary to both agreeable and disagreeable? That conceptualization which takes as its object a thing that is free from both pleasant and unpleasant, attractive and unattractive [qualities]. That [whole scheme] constitutes, in brief, two things: conceptualization, and the object that is the basis and referent of conceptualization. And both of these should be understood as beginningless in time and as mutually causal. A prior conceptualization [serves] for the manifestation of a present object that is the referent of conceptualization; and again, a present manifest object that is the referent of conceptualization [serves] as the cause for the manifestation of a present conceptualization that takes it as its referent. Then, the non-comprehension of conceptualization at that time [serves] for the future manifestation of the object that is its referent. And from the occurrence of that, there is certainly again the manifestation of the conceptualization based on and dependent on that [object].

body.text: kathañca punarasya vikalpasya parijñānaṃ bhavati / catasṛbhiḥ paryeṣaṇābhiḥ caturvidhena ca yathābhūtaparijñānena /
body.translated_text: And how does the full comprehension of this conceptualization take place? Through four investigations (<s>paryeṣaṇā</s>) and through a fourfold correct knowledge as it truly is (<s>yathābhūtaparijñāna</s>).

body.text: catasraḥ paryeṣaṇāḥ katamāḥ / nāmaparyeṣaṇā / vastuparyeṣaṇā / svabhāvaprajñaptiparyeṣaṇā ca / viśeṣaprajñaptiparyeṣaṇā ca /
body.translated_text: What are the four investigations? Investigation of name (<s>nāmaparyeṣaṇā</s>), investigation of object (<s>vastuparyeṣaṇā</s>), investigation of the designation of intrinsic nature (<s>svabhāvaprajñaptiparyeṣaṇā</s>), and investigation of the designation of distinction (<s>viśeṣaprajñaptiparyeṣaṇā</s>).

body.text: tatra nāmaparyeṣaṇā yadvodhisattvo nāmni nāmamātraṃ paśyati / evaṃ vastuni vastumātradarśanaṃ [vastu]paryeṣaṇā / svabhāvaprajñaptau svabhāvaprajñaptimātradarśanaṃ svabhāvaprajñaptiparyeṣaṇā / viśeṣaprajñaptau viśeṣaprajñaptimātradarśanaṃ viśeṣaprajñaptiparyeṣaṇā / sa nāmavastuno bhinnañca lakṣaṇaṃ paśyatyanuśliṣṭañca / nāmavastvanuśleṣasanniśritāṃ ca svabhāvaprajñapti viśeṣaprajñaptiñca [prati]vidhyati /
body.translated_text: There, the investigation of name is when the <s>Bodhisattva</s> sees in a name merely the name. Likewise, seeing in an object merely the object is the investigation of object. Seeing in the designation of intrinsic nature merely the designation is the investigation of the designation of intrinsic nature. Seeing in the designation of distinction merely the designation is the investigation of the designation of distinction. He sees the characteristic of name and object as both distinct and connected. And he penetrates the designation of intrinsic nature and the designation of distinction as dependent on the connection of name and object.

body.text: catvāri yathābhūtaparijñānāni katamāni / nāmaiṣaṇāgataṃ yathābhūtaparijñānaṃ vastveṣaṇāgataṃ svabhāvaprajñaptyeṣaṇāgataṃ viśeṣaprajñaptyeṣaṇāgatañca yathābhūtaparijñānam /
body.translated_text: What are the four kinds of correct knowledge as it truly is? The correct knowledge arrived at through the investigation of name, the correct knowledge arrived at through the investigation of object, the correct knowledge arrived at through the investigation of the designation of intrinsic nature, and the correct knowledge arrived at through the investigation of the designation of distinction.

body.text: nāmaiṣaṇāgataṃ yathābhūtaparijñānaṃ katamat / sa khalu bodhisattvo nāmni nāmamātratāṃ paryeṣya tannāmaivaṃ yathābhūtaṃ parijānāti itīdaṃ nāma ityarthaṃ vastuni vyavasthāpyate yāvadeva saṃjñārtha dṛṣṭyarthamupacārārtham / yadi rūpādisaṃjñake vastuni rūpamiti nāma na vyavasthāpyeta na kañcittadvastu rūpamitmevaṃ saṃjānīyāt /
body.translated_text: What is the correct knowledge arrived at through the investigation of name? That <s>Bodhisattva</s>, having investigated the mere name-ness in the name, correctly knows that name as it truly is: 'This name is established in the object for the sake of meaning, merely for the sake of designation, the sake of seeing, and the sake of conventional usage. If the name "form" were not established for the object designated as "form" and the like, no one would cognize that object as "form."'

body.text:
asaṃjānan samāropato nābhiniveśeta / anabhiniveśaṃ nābhilapet / iti yadevaṃ yathābhūtaṃ prajānāti / idamucyate nāmaiṣaṇāgataṃ yathābhūtaparijñānam /
vastveṣaṇāgataṃ yathābhūtaparijñānaṃ katamat / yataśca bodhisattvo [vastuni] vastumātratāṃ paryeṣya sarvābhilāpaviśliṣṭaṃ nirabhilāpyaṃ tadrūpādisaṃjñakaṃ vastu paśyati / idaṃ dvitīyaṃ yathābhūtaparijñānaṃ vastveṣaṇāgatam /
body.translated_text: Not cognizing, one would not superimpose [through fixation]. Not superimposing, one would not verbally express [it]. Thus, when one correctly knows [this] as it truly is—this is called the correct knowledge arrived at through the investigation of name. What is the correct knowledge arrived at through the investigation of object? When the <s>Bodhisattva</s>, having investigated the mere object-ness in the object, sees that object designated as 'form' and the like as completely disconnected from all verbal expression, inexpressible—this is the second correct knowledge as it truly is, arrived at through the investigation of object.

body.text: svabhāvaprajñaptyeṣaṇāgataṃ yathābhūtaparijñānaṃ katamat yataśca bodhisattvaḥ rūpādisaṃjñake vastuni svabhāvaprajñaptau prajñaptimātratāṃ paryeṣya tathā svabhāvaprajñaptyā atatsvabhāvasya vastunaḥ tatsvabhāvābhāsatāṃ yathābhūtaṃ pratividhyati prajānāti / tasya nirmāṇapratibimbapratiśrutkā-pratibhāsodakacandrasvapnamāyopamaṃ tatsvabhāvaṃ paśyataḥ tadābhāsamatanmayam idṃ tṛtīyaṃ yathābhūtaṃ parijñānaṃ sugambhīrārthagocaram /
body.translated_text: What is the correct knowledge arrived at through the investigation of the designation of intrinsic nature? When the <s>Bodhisattva</s>, having investigated the mere designation-ness in the designation of intrinsic nature in an object designated as 'form' and the like, penetrates and knows as it truly is the appearance of that object as having that intrinsic nature through the designation of intrinsic nature, [though] the object is not of that intrinsic nature. For one who sees that intrinsic nature as like a magical creation, a reflection, an echo, a mirage, the moon in water, a dream, or an illusion—an appearance, not made of that [nature]—this is the third correct knowledge as it truly is, having a profoundly deep meaning as its domain.

body.text: viśeṣaprajñaptyeṣaṇāgataṃ yathābhūtaparijñānaṃ katamat / yataśca bodhisattvo viśeṣaprajñaptau prajñaptimātratāṃ paryeṣya tasmin rūpādisaṃjñake vastuni viśeṣaprajñaptimadvayārthena paśyati / na tadvastu bhāvo nābhāvaḥ / abhilāpyenātmanā 'pariniṣpannatvānna bhāvaḥ / na punarabhāvo nirabhilāpyenātmanā vyavasthitatvāt / evaṃ na rūpī paramārthasatyatayā / nārūpī saṃvṛtisatyena tatra rūpopacāratayā / yathā bhāvaścābhāvaśca rūpī cārūpī ca / tathā sanidarśanānidarśanādayo viśeṣaprajñaptiparyāyāḥ sarve 'nena nayenaivaṃ veditavyāḥ / iti yadetāṃ viśeṣaprajñaptimevamadvayārthena yathābhūtaṃ prajānāti / idamucyate viśeṣaprajñaptyeṣaṇāgataṃ yathābhūtaparijñānam /
body.translated_text: What is the correct knowledge arrived at through the investigation of the designation of distinction? When the <s>Bodhisattva</s>, having investigated the mere designation-ness in the designation of distinction, sees the designation of distinction in that object designated as 'form' and the like by the meaning of non-duality (<s>advaya</s>). That object is neither existent (<s>bhāva</s>) nor non-existent (<s>abhāva</s>). It is not existent because it is not fully accomplished (<s>apariniṣpanna</s>) by its expressible nature. Yet it is not non-existent because it subsists by its inexpressible nature. Thus, it is neither 'having form' in the sense of ultimate truth, nor 'formless,' because in conventional truth, form is ascribed there. Just as [the analysis applies to] existent and non-existent, having form and formless, so the categories of designation of distinction such as visible and invisible and the rest should all be understood by this same method. Thus, when one correctly knows this designation of distinction by the meaning of non-duality as it truly is—this is called the correct knowledge arrived at through the investigation of the designation of distinction.

body.text: tatra yo 'sāvaṣṭavidho mithyāvikalpo bālānāṃ trivastujanako lokanirvartakaḥ so 'sya caturvidhasya yathābhūtaparijñānasya vaikalyādasamavadhānātpravartate / tasmācca punarmithyāvikalpātsaṃkleśaḥ / saṃkleśātsaṃsārasaṃsṛtiḥ saṃsārasaṃsṛteḥ saṃsārānugataṃ jātijarāvyādhimaraṇādikaṃ duḥkhaṃ pravartate / yadā ca bodhisattvena caturvidhaṃ yathābhūtaparijñānaṃ niśritya so 'ṣṭavidho vikalpaḥ parijñāto bhavati dṛṣṭe dharme tasya samyak parijñānādāyatyāṃ tadadhiṣṭhānasya tadālambanasya prapañcapatitasya
body.translated_text: There, that eightfold false conceptualization of the childish, which produces the three [kinds of] objects and brings about the world, arises from the incompleteness and non-attention to this fourfold correct knowledge as it truly is. And from that false conceptualization arises defilement (<s>saṃkleśa</s>); from defilement, the cycle of <s>saṃsāra</s>; from the cycle of <s>saṃsāra</s>, the suffering of birth, old age, disease, death, and so forth that accompanies <s>saṃsāra</s> arises. But when the <s>Bodhisattva</s>, relying on the fourfold correct knowledge as it truly is, has fully comprehended that eightfold conceptualization—through its correct full comprehension in this present life, in the future the object of conceptual proliferation that is the basis and referent [of conceptualization],

body.text: vastunaḥ prādurbhāvo na bhavati / tasyānudayādaprādurbhāvāttadālambanasyāpi vikalpasyāyatyāṃ prādurbhāvo na bhavati / evaṃ tasya savastukasya vikalpasya nirodho yaḥ sa sarvaprapañcanirodho veditavyaḥ / evañca prapañcanirodho bodhisattvasya mahāyānaparinirvāṇamiti veditavyam / dṛṣṭe ca dharme tasya śreṣṭhatattvārtha gocarajñānasya viśuddhatvāt sarvatra vaśitāprāpti labhate sa bodhisattvaḥ / yaduta nirmāṇe 'pi vicitre nairmāṇikyā ṛddhyā / pariṇāme ca vicitre pāriṇāmikyā ṛddhyā / sarvajñeyasya ca jñāne yāvadabhipretaṃ cāvasthāne / kāmakārataśca vinopakramaṃ cyutau /
body.translated_text: the arising of the object does not occur. Since it does not arise and does not appear, the arising of conceptual discrimination having that as its object also does not occur in the future. Thus, the cessation of that conceptual discrimination which has a [real] object—this should be understood as the cessation of all conceptual elaboration (<s>prapañca</s>). And the cessation of conceptual elaboration should be understood as the <s>Bodhisattva</s>'s <s>Mahāyāna</s>-<s>parinirvāṇa</s>. And in this very life, because of the purity of that supreme knowledge whose domain is the meaning of reality (<s>tattvārtha</s>), that <s>Bodhisattva</s> attains mastery (<s>vaśitā</s>) everywhere—namely, mastery through varied emanation (<s>nirmāṇa</s>) by means of the creative magical power (<s>nairmāṇikī ṛddhi</s>); mastery through varied transformation by means of the transformative magical power (<s>pāriṇāmikī ṛddhi</s>); mastery in the knowledge of all that is knowable; mastery in abiding as long as intended; and mastery in voluntary passing away without any impairment.

body.text: sa evaṃ vaśitāprāptaḥ sarvasattvaśreṣṭho bhavati niruttaraḥ / evañca sarvatra vaśinastasya bodhisattvasya uttamāḥ pañcānuśaṃsā veditavyāḥ / paramāṃ cittaśāntimanuprāpto bhavati vihārapraśāntatayā na kleśapraśāntatayā / sarvavidyāsthāneṣu cāsyāvyāhataṃ pariśuddhaṃ paryavadātaṃ jñānadarśanaṃ pravartate / akhinnaśca bhavati sattvānāmarthe saṃsārasaṃsṛtyā / tathāgatānāñca sarvasandhāyavacanānyanupraviśati / na ca mahāyānādhimukteḥ saṃhāryo bhavatyaparapratyayatayā /
body.translated_text: Having thus attained mastery, he becomes the foremost of all beings, unsurpassed. And for this <s>Bodhisattva</s> who has mastery everywhere, five supreme benefits should be understood: He attains supreme mental peace through the peace of abiding, not through the peace of afflictions. In all fields of knowledge, his knowledge and vision operates unobstructed, purified, and cleansed. He is unwearied in the welfare of beings through his wandering in <s>saṃsāra</s>. He penetrates all the intentional teachings (<s>sandhāyavacana</s>) of the <s>Tathāgatas</s>. And he cannot be shaken from his devotion to the <s>Mahāyāna</s> by being dependent on others.

body.text: asya khalu pañcavidhasyānuśaṃsasya pañcavidhameva karma veditavyam / paramo dṛṣṭadharmasukhavihāro bodhisattvasya bodhāya prayoganiryātasya kāyikacaitasikasya vyāyāmaklamasya nāśāya cittaśānteranuśaṃsasyaitatkarma veditavyam / sarvabuddhadharmāṇāṃ paripāko bodhisattvasya sarvavidyāsthāneṣvavyāhatajñānatāyā anuśaṃsasyai tatkarma veditavyam / sattvaparipāko bodhisattvasya saṃsārākheditāyā anuśaṃsasyaitatkarma veditavyam / vineyānāmut pannotpannānāṃ saṃśayānāṃ prativinodanaṃ dharmanetryāśca dīrghakālaṃ parikarṣaṇaṃ sandhāraṇaṃ saddharmapratirūpakāṇāṃ śāsanāntardhāyakānāṃ parijñānaprakāśanāpakarṣaṇatayā sarvasandhāyavacanapraveśānuśaṃsasyaitatkarma veditavyam / sarvaparapravādinigraho dṛḍhavīryatā ca prāṇidhānāccācyutiḥ asaṃhāryatā 'parapratyayatvānuśaṃsasyaitatkarma veditavyam /
body.translated_text: For this fivefold benefit, a fivefold function should be understood. The supreme pleasant abiding in this present life of the <s>Bodhisattva</s> who has set out in endeavor toward awakening, for the destruction of bodily and mental fatigue from exertion—this should be understood as the function of the benefit of mental peace. The maturation of all <s>Buddha</s>-qualities of the <s>Bodhisattva</s>—this should be understood as the function of the benefit of unobstructed knowledge in all fields of knowledge. The maturation of beings by the <s>Bodhisattva</s>—this should be understood as the function of the benefit of unweariness in <s>saṃsāra</s>. The dispelling of doubts that arise again and again in those to be trained, the long-term drawing out and preservation of the guide of the <s>Dharma</s>, and the illumination and removal of counterfeit teachings that cause the disappearance of the true teaching—this should be understood as the function of the benefit of penetrating all intentional teachings. The overcoming of all rival doctrines, firm vigor, non-falling from one's vow (<s>praṇidhāna</s>), and being unshakeable—this should be understood as the function of the benefit of not being dependent on others.

body.text: evaṃ hi bodhisattvasya yāvat kiñcidbodhisattvakaraṇīyaṃ tatsarvamebhiḥ pañcabhiranuśaṃsakarmabhiḥ parigṛhītaṃ bhavati / tatpunaḥ karaṇīyaṃ katamat / asaṃkliṣṭañca ātmasukhaṃ buddhadharmaparipākaḥ sattvaparipākaḥ saddharmasya dhāraṇam acalapraṇidhānasyottaptavīryasya paravādavinigrahaśca /
body.translated_text: Thus, whatever is the entire duty of the <s>Bodhisattva</s>—all of that is comprised by these five benefit-functions. And what is that duty? Undefiled personal happiness, the maturation of <s>Buddha</s>-qualities, the maturation of beings, the preservation of the true <s>Dharma</s>, and the overcoming of rival doctrines through unflinching vigor and unwavering vow.

body.text: tatra caturṇā tattvārthānāṃ prathamau dvau hīnau / tṛtīyo madhyamaḥ / caturtha uttamo veditavyaḥ /
body.translated_text: There, of the four [kinds of] meaning of reality, the first two are inferior. The third is middling. The fourth should be understood as supreme.

body.text: bodhisattvabhūmāvādhāre yogasthāne caturthaṃ tattvārthapaṭalam //
body.translated_text: In the <s>Bodhisattvabhūmi</s>, in the Foundation Section of Yoga, the fourth chapter, the <s>Tattvārtha-paṭala</s> (Chapter on the Meaning of Reality), is completed. //

body.text: tatra prabhāvo bodhisattvānāṃ katamaḥ / samāsataḥ samādhivaśitāprāptasya samādhivaśitāsanniśrayeṇocchāmātrāt sarvārthasamṛddhiḥ karmaṇyacittasya suparibhāvitacittasyāryaḥ prabhāva ityucyate / dharmāṇāñca yā mahāphalatā mahānuśaṃsatā sā teṣāṃ prabhāva ityucyate / pūrvaṃ mahāpuṇyasaṃbhāropacayād buddhānāṃ bodhisattvānāṃ ca sahajā āścaryādbhutadharmatā / ayamapi teṣāṃ sahajo 'paraḥ prabhāvo veditavyaḥ /
body.translated_text: There, what is the power (<s>prabhāva</s>) of <s>Bodhisattvas</s>? In brief, for one who has attained mastery of <s>samādhi</s> (concentration), depending on that mastery of <s>samādhi</s>, the accomplishment of all purposes from a mere wish, of one whose mind is workable and well-cultivated—this is called the noble power (<s>ārya prabhāva</s>). And the great fruitfulness and great benefit of <s>dharmas</s>—that is called the power of those [<s>dharmas</s>]. The innate wondrous and marvelous nature of <s>Buddhas</s> and <s>Bodhisattvas</s>, arising from the prior accumulation of great merit—this too should be understood as another, innate power of theirs.

body.text: sa khalveṣa prakārabhedena buddhabodhisattvānāṃ pañcavidho bhavati / abhijñāprabhāvo dharmaprabhāvaḥ sahajaśca prabhāvaḥ sādhāraṇaśca śrāvaka pratyekabudvairasādhāraṇaśca taiḥ /
body.translated_text: That [power], by differentiation of types, is fivefold for <s>Buddhas</s> and <s>Bodhisattvas</s>: the power of higher knowledges (<s>abhijñā-prabhāva</s>), the power of <s>dharmas</s> (<s>dharma-prabhāva</s>), innate power (<s>sahaja prabhāva</s>), that which is shared with <s>Śrāvakas</s> and <s>Pratyekabuddhas</s>, and that which is unshared with them.

body.text: tatra ṣaḍbhijñāḥ - ṛddhiviṣayo divyaṃ śrotraṃcetasaḥ paryāyaḥ pūrvanivāsānusmṛtiścyutyupapādadarśanamāsravakṣayajñānasākṣātkriyā ca abhijñāprabhāva ityucyate / tatra ṣaṭpāramitāḥ-dānaṃ śīlaṃ kṣāntirvīryaṃ dhyānaṃ prajñā ca dharmā ityucyante / teṣāṃ dharmāṇāṃ yo 'nubhāvaḥ sa dharmaprabhāva ityucyate /
body.translated_text: There, the six higher knowledges (<s>abhijñā</s>)—the domain of magical power (<s>ṛddhiviṣaya</s>), the divine ear (<s>divyaśrotra</s>), the reading of others' minds (<s>cetaḥparyāya</s>), the recollection of former lives (<s>pūrvanivāsānusmṛti</s>), the knowledge of the death and rebirth [of beings] (<s>cyutyupapādadarśana</s>), and the direct realization of the knowledge of the destruction of outflows (<s>āsravakṣayajñānasākṣātkriyā</s>)—are called the power of higher knowledges. There, the six <s>pāramitās</s>—generosity (<s>dāna</s>), moral conduct (<s>śīla</s>), patience (<s>kṣānti</s>), vigor (<s>vīrya</s>), meditation (<s>dhyāna</s>), and wisdom (<s>prajñā</s>)—are called <s>dharmas</s>. The influence of those <s>dharmas</s> is called the power of <s>dharmas</s>.

body.text: tatra ṛddhiḥ katamā / samāsato dvividhā / pāriṇāmikī nairmāṇikī ca / sā punardvidhāpyanekavidhā prakārabhedataḥ /
body.translated_text: There, what is magical power (<s>ṛddhi</s>)? In brief, it is twofold: transformative (<s>pāriṇāmikī</s>) and creative (<s>nairmāṇikī</s>). That [twofold power], moreover, is also manifold by differentiation of types.

body.text: tatra pāriṇāmikyā ṛddheḥ prakāraprabhedaḥ katamaḥ / tadyathā kampanaṃ jvalanaṃ spharaṇaṃ vidarśanamanyathībhāvakaraṇaṃ gamanāgamanaṃ saṃkṣepaḥ prathanaṃ sarvarūpakāyapraveśanaṃ sabhāgatopasaṃkrāntirāvirbhāvastirobhāvaḥ vaśitvakaraṇaṃ pararddhayabhibhavanaṃ pratibhānadānaṃ
body.translated_text: There, what is the differentiation of types of transformative magical power (<s>pāriṇāmikī ṛddhi</s>)? They are: causing trembling (<s>kampana</s>), blazing (<s>jvalana</s>), pervading (<s>spharaṇa</s>), displaying (<s>vidarśana</s>), transformation of nature (<s>anyathībhāvakaraṇa</s>), going and coming (<s>gamanāgamana</s>), contraction (<s>saṃkṣepa</s>), expansion (<s>prathana</s>), entering all form-bodies (<s>sarvarūpakāyapraveśana</s>), becoming equal to an assembly (<s>sabhāgatopasaṃkrānti</s>), appearing and disappearing (<s>āvirbhāva-tirobhāva</s>), bringing under control (<s>vaśitvakaraṇa</s>), overpowering others' magical powers (<s>pararddhyabhibhavana</s>), bestowing eloquence (<s>pratibhānadāna</s>),

body.text: smṛtidānaṃ sukhadānaṃ raśmipramokṣaśca ityevaṃbhāgīyā ṛddhi pāriṇāmikītyucyate /
body.translated_text: bestowing mindfulness (<s>smṛtidāna</s>), bestowing happiness (<s>sukhadāna</s>), and the emission of rays of light (<s>raśmipramokṣa</s>)—such types of magical power are called transformative (<s>pāriṇāmikī</s>).

body.text: tatra kampanam / iha tathāgataḥ samādhivaśitāprāpto vā karmaṇyacitto vā bodhisattvo vihāramapi kampayati / gṛhamapi grāmanagarakṣetramapi narakalokamapi tiryaglokamapi pretalokamapi manuṣyalokamapi devalokamapi cāturdvīpakamapi sāhasrikamapi lokadhātuṃ dvisāhasrikamapi trisāhasramahāsāhasramapi lokadhātuṃ trisāhasraśatamapi sahasramapi śatasahasramapi yāvadaprameyānasaṃkhyeyān trisāhasramahāsāhasrān lokadhātūn kampayati /
body.translated_text: There, causing trembling (<s>kampana</s>): Here, a <s>Tathāgata</s> who has attained mastery of <s>samādhi</s>, or a <s>Bodhisattva</s> whose mind is workable, causes a dwelling to tremble. He also causes a house to tremble, a village, a city, a region, the hell-world, the animal-world, the world of hungry ghosts, the human world, the world of gods, a four-continent [world-system], a thousandfold world-system, a two-thousandfold world-system, a three-thousandfold great-thousandfold world-system, a hundred three-thousandfold systems, a thousand, a hundred thousand, up to immeasurable and innumerable three-thousandfold great-thousandfold world-systems to tremble.

body.text: tatra jvalanam / ūrdhva kāyāt prajvalati / adhaḥkāyācchītalā vāridhārāḥ syandante / adhaḥkāyāt prajvalati / uparimāt kāyācchītalā vāridhārāḥ syandante / tejodhātumapi samāpadyate / sarvakāyena prajvalati / sarvakāyena prajvalitasya vividhā arciṣaḥ kāyānnirgacchanti nīlapītalohitāvadātamāñjiṣṭhāḥ sphaṭikavarṇāḥ /
body.translated_text: There, blazing (<s>jvalana</s>): From the upper body he blazes forth; from the lower body cool streams of water flow. From the lower body he blazes forth; from the upper body cool streams of water flow. He also enters the fire element; with his entire body he blazes. When his entire body blazes, various flames emerge from his body—blue, yellow, red, white, crimson, and crystal-colored.

body.text: tatra spharaṇam / yathāpi tadgṛhamapyābhayā spharati vihāramapi pūrvavadyāvadaprameyānasaṃkhyām lokadhātūnābhayā spharati pūrvavattadyathā kampane /
body.translated_text: There, pervading (<s>spharaṇa</s>): Just as he pervades a house with radiance, so he pervades a dwelling—and as before, up to immeasurable and innumerable world-systems he pervades with radiance, just as in the case of causing trembling.

body.text: tatra vidarśanam / yathā sukhopaniṣaṇṇādyāgatāyāḥ śramaṇabrāhmaṇaśrāvakabodhisattvadevanāgayakṣagandharvāsuragaruḍakinnaramahoragāyāḥ pariṣadaḥ tathāgato vā bodhisattvo vā apāyānapi vidarśayatyadhaḥ / devamanuṣyānapi vidarśayatyūrdhvam / tadanyāni ca buddhakṣetrāṇi vidarśayati / teṣu ca buddhabodhisattvān yāvadgaṅgānadībālukāsamānyapi buddhakṣetrāṇyatikramya yena nāmnā saṃśabditaṃ bhavati buddhakṣetraṃ tatra ca buddhakṣetre yannāmako bhavati tathāgataḥ tacca buddhakṣetraṃ darśayati tañca tathāgatam / tacca nāma vyapadiśati tasya buddhakṣetrasya tathāgatasya ca / tato 'pyarvāgvidarśaṃyati vyapadiśati tato 'pi pareṇa yatkāmaṃ yāvatkāmam /
body.translated_text: There, displaying (<s>vidarśana</s>): To an assembly that has comfortably assembled—consisting of <s>śramaṇas</s>, <s>brāhmaṇas</s>, <s>Śrāvakas</s>, <s>Bodhisattvas</s>, gods, <s>Nāgas</s>, <s>Yakṣas</s>, <s>Gandharvas</s>, <s>Asuras</s>, <s>Garuḍas</s>, <s>Kinnaras</s>, and <s>Mahoragas</s>—a <s>Tathāgata</s> or a <s>Bodhisattva</s> displays the lower realms below, displays gods and humans above, and displays other <s>Buddha</s>-fields as well. And in those [fields], he displays <s>Buddhas</s> and <s>Bodhisattvas</s>—even crossing over <s>Buddha</s>-fields as numerous as the sands of the river <s>Gaṅgā</s>—whatever the name by which a <s>Buddha</s>-field is designated, and whatever the name of the <s>Tathāgata</s> in that <s>Buddha</s>-field, he displays that <s>Buddha</s>-field and that <s>Tathāgata</s>, and declares the name of that <s>Buddha</s>-field and of that <s>Tathāgata</s>. He also displays and declares [fields] nearer than that and beyond that, as many as he wishes and as far as he wishes.

body.text: tatrānyathībhāvakaraṇam / sa cet pṛthivīmapo 'dhimucyate tattathaiva bhavati nānyathā / tejo vāyumadhimucyate tadapi tathaiva bhavati nānyathā / sa cedapaḥ pṛthivīmadhimucyate / sa cettejaḥ pṛthivīmadhimucyate / apo vāyumadhimucyate / sa cedvāyu pṛthivīmadhimucyate / apastejo 'dhimucyate / sarvaṃ tattathaiva bhavati nānyathā / yathā mahābhūteṣvanyonyapariṇāme nānyathībhāvakriyā evaṃ rūpagandharasaspraṣṭavyeṣu veditavyam / sa cettṛṇaparṇagomayamṛttikādīni dravyāṇi bhojanapānayānavastrālaṅkārabhāṇḍopaskaragandhamālyavilopanamadhimucyate / pāṣāṇaśarkarakapālādīni ca maṇimuktāvaidūryaśaṅkhaśilāpravāḍamadhimucyate / himavantaṃ vā parvatarājamādiṃ kṛtvā sarvaparvatān suvarṇaṃmadhimucyate / tadapi sarvaṃ tathaiva bhavati nānyathā / tathā suvarṇānāṃ sattvānāṃ durvarṇatāmadhimucyate / durvarṇānāṃ suvarṇatām / tadubhayavivarjitānāṃ suvarṇatāṃ vā durvarṇatāṃ vā tadubhayaṃ vā / yathā suvarṇadurvarṇatāmevaṃ vyaṅgāvyaṅgatāṃ kṛśa sthūlatāmityevamādi yatkiñcidanyathā satsvalakṣaṇataḥ śakyarūpañcā [nyathā] 'dhimucyate / tatsarvaṃ tathā bhavati yathā 'dhimucyate /
body.translated_text: There, transformation of nature (<s>anyathībhāvakaraṇa</s>): If he resolves upon earth as water, it becomes exactly so and not otherwise. If he resolves upon fire or wind, that too becomes exactly so. If he resolves upon water as earth, upon fire as earth, upon water as wind, upon wind as earth, upon water as fire—all becomes exactly so and not otherwise. Just as with the mutual transformation of the great elements, so it should be understood with form, smell, taste, and tangibles. If he resolves upon substances such as grass, leaves, cow-dung, and clay as food, drink, vehicles, clothing, ornaments, furnishings, vessels, utensils, perfumes, garlands, and ointments—and upon stones, gravel, and potsherds as gems, pearls, <s>vaiḍūrya</s>, conch-shells, stones, and corals—and upon <s>Himavat</s>, the king of mountains, beginning with all mountains, as gold—all of that too becomes exactly so and not otherwise. Likewise, he resolves upon well-complexioned beings as ill-complexioned, upon ill-complexioned as well-complexioned, upon those lacking both as either well-complexioned or ill-complexioned or both. Just as with complexion, so with being disfigured or undisfigured, thin or stout, and so forth—whatever can be transformed from its own characteristic into something otherwise, he resolves upon it, and it all becomes so, just as he resolves.

body.text: tatra gamanāgamanam / tiraḥ kuḍyaṃ tiraḥ śailaṃ tiraḥ prākāramasajyamānena kāyena gacchati vistareṇa yāvadbrahmalokamupasaṃkrāmati pratyāgacchati ca yāvadakaniṣṭhādūrdhvaṃ tiryagvā punaryāvadaprameyānasaṃkhyeyāṃstrisāhasramahāsāhasrān lokadhātūn gacchati āgacchati ca kāyena vā audārikeṇa cāturmahābhautikena / dūraṃ cāsannamadhimucya manaḥsadṛśena vā javena gacchati cāgacchati ca /
body.translated_text: There, going and coming (<s>gamanāgamana</s>): He passes through walls, through mountains, through ramparts with an unobstructed body; in detail, he approaches up to the <s>Brahma</s>-world and returns—up above from <s>Akaniṣṭha</s>, or sideways, up to immeasurable and innumerable three-thousandfold great-thousandfold world-systems—he goes and comes, either with the coarse physical body made of the four great elements, or by resolving that what is distant is near, he goes and comes with a speed like that of the mind.

body.text: tatra saṃkṣepaprathanam / himavantamapi parvatarājaṃ paramāṇumātramabhisaṃkṣipati / paramāṇumapi hima vantaṃ parvatarājaṃ pratānayati /
body.translated_text: There, contraction and expansion (<s>saṃkṣepa-prathana</s>): He contracts even <s>Himavat</s>, the king of mountains, to the size of an atom. He expands even an atom to the size of <s>Himavat</s>, the king of mountains.

body.text: tatra sarvarūpakāyapraveśanam / mahatyā vicitrāyāḥ pariṣadaḥ purastāt sa grāmanigamatṛṇavana[-bhūmi-]parvataṃ rūpakāyamātmakāye praveśayati / sā ca sarvā pariṣattasminneva kāye praviṣṭamātmānaṃ saṃjānīte /
body.translated_text: There, entering all form-bodies (<s>sarvarūpakāyapraveśana</s>): Before a great and varied assembly, he causes the form-body of a village, town, grassland, forest, land, or mountain to enter his own body. And that entire assembly perceives itself as having entered that very body.

body.text: tatra sabhāgatopasaṃkrāntiḥ / kṣatriyapariṣada mupasaṃkrāmati / upasaṃkrāntasya yādṛśī teṣāṃ varṇapuṣkalatā bhavati tādṛśī tasya / yādṛśa ārohapariṇāhastādṛśastasya bhavati / yādṛśī svaraguptisteṣāṃ tādṛśī tasya bhavati / yañca te 'rthaṃ mantrayante tamasāvarthaṃ mantrayate / yamapi te 'rthaṃ na mantrayante tamapi so 'rthaṃ na mantrayate / uttaraṃ caitānānudhārmyā kathayā saṃdarśayitvā samādāpayitvā samuttejayitvā saṃpraharṣayitvā 'ntarddhīyate / antarhitañcainaṃ na prajānanti ko 'nveṣo 'ntarhito devo vā manuṣyo veti / yathā kṣatriyapariṣadamevaṃ brāhmaṇagṛhapatiśramaṇapariṣadaṃ cāturmahārājakāyikān devān trayastriṃśān yāmāṃstuṣitānnirmāṇaratīnparanirmitavaśavartino devānevaṃ brahmakāyikān brahmapurohitānmahābrahmaṇaḥ parīttābhānapramāṇābhānābhāsvarān parīttaśubhānapramāṇaśubhān śubhakṛssnān anabhrakān puṇyaprasavān bṛhatphalānasaṃjñisattvān abṛhān atapān sudṛśān sudarśanānakaniṣṭhān /
body.translated_text: There, becoming equal to an assembly (<s>sabhāgatopasaṃkrānti</s>): He approaches an assembly of <s>Kṣatriyas</s>. Having approached, his complexion becomes like theirs. His height and girth become like theirs. His tone of voice and manner become like theirs. Whatever matter they deliberate upon, that very matter he deliberates upon. Whatever matter they do not deliberate upon, that too he does not deliberate upon. Furthermore, having instructed, encouraged, inspired, and gladdened them with a discourse in accordance with the <s>Dharma</s>, he disappears. And once he has disappeared, they do not recognize [him], wondering, 'Who indeed was this who has disappeared—a god or a human?' Just as with the assembly of <s>Kṣatriyas</s>, so too with the assemblies of <s>Brāhmaṇas</s>, householders, and <s>śramaṇas</s>; the <s>Cāturmahārājikā</s> gods, the <s>Trāyastriṃśa</s>, <s>Yāma</s>, <s>Tuṣita</s>, <s>Nirmāṇarati</s>, and <s>Paranirmitavaśavartin</s> gods; likewise the <s>Brahmakāyika</s>, <s>Brahmapurohita</s>, <s>Mahābrahmā</s>, <s>Parīttābha</s>, <s>Apramāṇābha</s>, <s>Ābhāsvara</s>, <s>Parīttaśubha</s>, <s>Apramāṇaśubha</s>, <s>Śubhakṛtsna</s>, <s>Anabhraka</s>, <s>Puṇyaprasava</s>, <s>Bṛhatphala</s>, <s>Asaṃjñisattva</s>, <s>Abṛha</s>, <s>Atapa</s>, <s>Sudṛśa</s>, <s>Sudarśana</s>, and <s>Akaniṣṭha</s> [gods].

body.text: tatrāvirbhāvatirobhāvaḥ / mahatyā pariṣadaḥ purastācchatakṛtvaḥ sahasrakṛtvaḥ ato vā pareṇāntardhīyate / punaśca tathaivātmabhāva mupadarśayatyāviṣkaroti /
body.translated_text: There, appearing and disappearing (<s>āvirbhāvatirobhāva</s>): Before a great assembly, a hundred times, a thousand times, or more, one disappears. And again, one displays and manifests one's own form in the same way.

body.text: tatra vaśitvakaraṇam / yāvān kaścit sattvadhātuḥ taṃ sarva gamanāgamanasthānādyāsu kriyāsu saṃvartayati / sa cedasyai vaṃ bhavati gacchatu gacchati / tiṣṭhatu tiṣṭhati / āgacchatvāgacchati / bhāṣatāṃ bhāṣate /
body.translated_text: There, [the power of] mastery (<s>vaśitvakaraṇa</s>): Whatever being there may be in the entire realm of beings, one directs them all in activities such as going, coming, standing, and so forth. If his [intention] is thus: 'Let him go'—he goes; 'Let him stand'—he stands; 'Let him come'—he comes; 'Let him speak'—he speaks.

body.text: tatra pararddhyabhibhavaḥ / tathāgatastadanyeṣāṃ sarvarddhimatāmṛdhyabhisaṃskāramabhibhūya yathākāmaṃ sarvaṃ saṃpādayati / niṣṭhāgato bodhisattva ekajātipratibaddhaśca caramabhaviko vā tathāgataṃ sthāpayitvā tulyajātīyañca bodhisattvaṃ tadanyeṣāṃ
body.translated_text: There, the overpowering of others' supernatural powers (<s>pararddhyabhibhava</s>): The <s>Tathāgata</s>, overpowering the supernatural exertion of all other possessors of supernatural power, accomplishes everything as he wishes. A <s>Bodhisattva</s> who has reached culmination, who is bound by one more birth or who is in his last existence, apart from the <s>Tathāgata</s> and a <s>Bodhisattva</s> of equal rank, of all others

body.text: sarveṣāmṛddhyabhisaṃskāramabhibhavati / tadanye bodhisattvā utkṛṣṭatarabhūmipraviṣṭāṃstulyajātīyāṃśca bodhisattvān sthāpayitvā tadanyeṣāṃ sarvarddhimatāmṛddhyabhisaṃskāramabhibhavanti /
body.translated_text: overpowers the supernatural exertion of all. Other <s>Bodhisattvas</s>, apart from those who have entered a higher stage and those of equal rank, overpower the supernatural exertion of all [other] possessors of supernatural power.

body.text: tatra pratibhānadānam / pratibhā[na]dāne paryādatte pratibhānamupasaṃharati /
body.translated_text: There, the gift of eloquence (<s>pratibhānadāna</s>): When [a being's] eloquence has been exhausted, one restores their eloquence.

body.text: tatra smṛtidānam / dharmeṣu smṛtau pramuṣitāyāṃ smṛtimupasaṃharati /
body.translated_text: There, the gift of mindfulness (<s>smṛtidāna</s>): When mindfulness regarding <s>dharmas</s> has been lost, one restores mindfulness.

body.text: tatra sukhadānam / ye 'sya bhāṣamāṇasya dharmaṃ śṛṇvanti teṣāṃ tādṛśaṃ kāyikaṃ caitasikamanugrahamupasaṃharati pratiprasrabdhi sukham / yena te vigatanivaraṇā dharmaṃ śrṛṇvanti / tacca tāvatkālikayogena na tvatyantam dhātuvaiṣamikāṃścaupakramikānamanuṣyābhisṛṣṭāṃścopasargān vyupaśamayati /
body.translated_text: There, the gift of happiness (<s>sukhadāna</s>): For those who hear the <s>Dharma</s> while he is speaking, one bestows such physical and mental benefit—the happiness of tranquility (<s>pratiprasrabdhisukha</s>)—by which they hear the <s>Dharma</s> free from the hindrances (<s>nīvaraṇa</s>). And that is by a temporary application, not permanently. One allays afflictions arising from elemental imbalance (<s>dhātuvaiṣamika</s>), from external treatment (<s>aupakramika</s>), and from non-human attack (<s>amanuṣyābhisṛṣṭa</s>).

body.text: tatra raśmipramokṣaḥ bodhisattvo vā tathāgato vā ṛddhyātadrūpān raśmīn kāyatpramuñcati ya ekatyā daśasu dikṣvaprameyāsaṃkhyeyeṣu lokadhātuṣu gatvā nārakāṇāṃ sattvānāṃ nārakāṇi duḥkhāni pratiprasrambhayati / ekatyā devalokasthānudārān devanāgayakṣagandharvāsuragaruḍakinnaramahoragān svabhavanasthān gatvā ihāgamanāya saṃcodayati / tathā tadanyalokadhātusthitān bodhisattvānihāgamanāya saṃcodayati daśasu dikṣvaprameyāsaṃkhyeyeṣu lokadhātuṣu / samāsatasthāgataḥ aprameyairasaṃkhyeyairnānāprakārai raśmibhirapramāṇānāṃ sattvānāṃ vicitramaprameyamasaṃkhyeyamarthaṃ karoti / te punarete sarve pāriṇāmikyā ṛddhyāḥ prakārā ekaikaśaḥ prabhidyamānā aprameyā asaṃkhyeyā veditavyāḥ / anyathā prakṛtyā vidyamānasya vastunastadanyathāvikārāpādanatā pariṇāma ityucyate / tasmādeṣā pāriṇāmikī ṛddhirityucyate /
body.translated_text: There, the emission of light rays (<s>raśmipramokṣa</s>): A <s>Bodhisattva</s> or a <s>Tathāgata</s>, by supernatural power, releases rays of various forms from the body. Some of these, going to immeasurable and innumerable world-systems in the ten directions, alleviate the hellish sufferings of beings in the hells. Some, going to the noble gods, <s>nāgas</s>, <s>yakṣas</s>, <s>gandharvas</s>, <s>asuras</s>, <s>garuḍas</s>, <s>kinnaras</s>, and <s>mahoragas</s> dwelling in their own abodes in the heavenly realms, summon them to come here. Likewise, one summons <s>Bodhisattvas</s> abiding in other world-systems to come here, in immeasurable and innumerable world-systems in the ten directions. In brief, the <s>Tathāgata</s>, by immeasurable, innumerable, and manifold rays, accomplishes various, immeasurable, and innumerable purposes for immeasurable beings. All these varieties of transformative supernatural power (<s>pāriṇāmikī ṛddhi</s>), when analyzed one by one, should be understood as immeasurable and innumerable. The bringing about of a change to a different state of a thing that naturally exists otherwise—this is called transformation (<s>pariṇāma</s>). Therefore, this is called transformative supernatural power.

body.text: tatra nairmāṇikī ṛddhiḥ katamā / samāsato nirvastukaṃ nirmāṇam / nirmāṇacittena yathākāmamabhisaṃskṛtaṃ smṛddhyatīyaṃ nairmāṇikī ṛddhirityucyate / sā cānekavidhā / kāyanirmāṇaṃ vāḍnirmāṇaṃ viṣayanirmāṇañca / tatpunaḥ kāyanirmāṇamātmano vā sadṛśaṃ visadṛśaṃ vā parasya vā sadṛśaṃ visadṛśaṃ vā nirmimīte / tatpunaḥ kāyanirmāṇamātmanastu pareṣāñca sadṛśāsadṛśam / indriyasabhāgamindriyādhiṣṭhānaṃ nirmimīte na tvindriyam / viṣayasadṛśamapi nirmāṇaṃ
body.translated_text: There, what is the creative supernatural power (<s>nairmāṇikī ṛddhi</s>)? In brief, it is creation without substance (<s>nirvastukanirmāṇa</s>). That which is fashioned at will by the mind of creation and which succeeds supernaturally—this is called creative supernatural power. And it is manifold: creation of body (<s>kāyanirmāṇa</s>), creation of speech (<s>vāṅnirmāṇa</s>), and creation of objects (<s>viṣayanirmāṇa</s>). There, the creation of body creates either a likeness of oneself or unlike oneself, or a likeness of another or unlike another. The creation of body, whether a likeness or unlike, of oneself or others, creates something similar in sense-faculties and their bases (<s>indriyādhiṣṭhāna</s>), but does not [actually] create the sense-faculties themselves. Even the creation resembling objects

body.text: nirmimīte / tadyathā bhojanapānādi maṇimuktāvaidūryādi ca yatkiñcidrūpagandharasaspraṣṭavyasaṃgṛhītaṃ bāhyamupakaraṇaṃ tatsadṛśaṃ tadvinirmuktaṃ sarvaṃ yathākāmaṃ nirmimīte / tatpunarātmasabhāgamanekavidhaṃ bahu nānāprakāraṃ devanāga[yakṣā]suragaruḍakinnaramahoragavarṇa manuṣyavarṇa tiryakpretanārakavarṇaṃ śrāvakavarṇaṃ pratyekabuddhavarṇaṃ bodhisattvavarṇaṃ tathāgatavarṇam / sa yadi tādṛśa eva bodhisattvo bhavati tādṛśameva nirmimīte / ātmasabhāgamasya tannirmāṇaṃ bhavati / anyathā tu visabhāgaṃ bhavati nirmāṇamātmanaḥ / sa cetparaṃ devabhūtaṃ tatsādṛśyena nirmimīte parasadṛśamasya tannirmāṇaṃ bhavati / sacedvaisādṛśyena nirmimīte paravisabhāgaṃ bhavati / yathā devabhūtamevaṃ yāvattathāgatabhūtaṃ veditavyam /
body.translated_text: one creates. That is, food and drink and so forth, gems, pearls, <s>vaiḍūrya</s>, and so forth—whatever external requisites included among form, smell, taste, and tangibles—one creates everything resembling those and distinct from those, as one wishes. And the creation resembling oneself is manifold, abundant, and of various kinds: forms of gods, <s>nāgas</s>, <s>yakṣas</s>, <s>asuras</s>, <s>garuḍas</s>, <s>kinnaras</s>, <s>mahoragas</s>, human forms, animal forms, hungry ghost forms, hell-being forms, <s>Śrāvaka</s> forms, <s>Pratyekabuddha</s> forms, <s>Bodhisattva</s> forms, and <s>Tathāgata</s> forms. If the <s>Bodhisattva</s> is of such a kind and creates a form of that very kind, then that creation is a likeness of himself. But if otherwise, the creation is unlike himself. If one creates a likeness of another who is a god, that creation is a likeness of the other. If one creates something dissimilar, it is unlike the other. Just as with a god-being, so it should be understood up to a <s>Tathāgata</s>-being.

body.text: tatra prabhūtakāyanirmāṇaṃ katamat / iha tathāgato vā bodhisattvo vā daśasu dikṣvaprameyāsaṃkhyeyeṣu lokadhātuṣu sakṛdaprameyāsaṃkhyeyānāṃ sattvānām arthaṃ karoti tairvicitravarṇanirmitaiḥ / kiñcicca nirmāṇamadhitiṣṭhati yaduparate 'pi bodhisattve tathāgete vā 'nuvartata eva / kiñcinnirmāṇaṃ buddhabodhisattvānāṃ kevalaṃ sattvānāṃ vidarśanāya māyopamaṃ bhavati / kiñcitpunarbhūtaṃ bhojanapānayānavastrādimaṇimuktāvaidūryaśaṃkhaśīlāpravāḍādi ca nirmitaṃ bhavati / tathaiva nānyathā / yena vittopakaraṇonaiva vittopakaraṇakāryaṃ kriyate / idantāvat kāyanirmāṇaṃ viṣayanirmāṇaṃ ca /
body.translated_text: There, what is the creation of abundant bodies (<s>prabhūtakāyanirmāṇa</s>)? Here, a <s>Tathāgata</s> or <s>Bodhisattva</s>, in immeasurable and innumerable world-systems in the ten directions, at once accomplishes the purpose of immeasurable and innumerable beings through those various created forms. Some creations are sustained, so that even when the <s>Bodhisattva</s> or <s>Tathāgata</s> has passed, they continue to operate. Some creations of <s>Buddhas</s> and <s>Bodhisattvas</s> are merely for the viewing of beings, like illusions. But some creations are real—food, drink, vehicles, clothing, gems, pearls, <s>vaiḍūrya</s>, conch-shells, crystal, coral, and so forth—created just as they are, not otherwise, so that with the created resources of wealth, the functions of wealth-resources are indeed carried out. So much for the creation of body and the creation of objects.

body.text: vāṅnirmāṇaṃ punarasti susvaratāyuktam / asti viśadasvarānvitaṃ svasambaddhaṃ parasambaddhamasambaddhaṃ dharmadeśanāsaṃgṛhītaṃ pramattasaṃcodanā-saṃgṛhītañca /
body.translated_text: The creation of speech (<s>vāṅnirmāṇa</s>), moreover, is of [several kinds]: that endowed with beautiful voice, that accompanied by clear voice, self-connected, other-connected, unconnected, that included in <s>Dharma</s>-teaching, and that included in the admonishment of the heedless.

body.text: tatra susvaratā / buddhabodhisattvānāṃ nirmito vāgvyāhāro gambhīro bhavati megharavaḥ kalaviṅkamanojñasvarasadṛśo hṛdayaṃgamaḥ gremaṇīyaḥ / paurī ca sā vāṅnirmitā bhavati valguvispaṣṭā vijñeyā śravaṇīyā apratikūlā aniśritā aparyantā /
body.translated_text: There, beautiful voice (<s>susvaratā</s>): The created verbal utterance of <s>Buddhas</s> and <s>Bodhisattvas</s> is deep, like the sound of thunder, resembling the pleasant voice of the <s>kalaviṅka</s> bird, touching the heart, and delightful. And that created speech is polished, elegant, clear, intelligible, pleasing to hear, inoffensive, unbiased, and boundless.

body.text: tatra viśadasvaratā / ākāṃkṣamāṇaḥ tathāgato vā bodhisattvo vā vicitrāṃ devanāgayakṣāsura garuḍakinnaramahoragaśrāvakabodhisattvapariṣadaṃ
body.translated_text: There, clear voice (<s>viśadasvaratā</s>): When wishing, a <s>Tathāgata</s> or <s>Bodhisattva</s>, [addressing] the varied assembly of gods, <s>nāgas</s>, <s>yakṣas</s>, <s>asuras</s>, <s>garuḍas</s>, <s>kinnaras</s>, <s>mahoragas</s>, <s>Śrāvakas</s>, and <s>Bodhisattvas</s>

body.text: sanniṣaṇṇāṃ sannipatitāṃ yāvadyojanaśatapariṣanmaṇḍalaparyantāṃ sarvāṃ svareṇa suparipūrṇena vijñāpayati ye 'pi dūre ya 'pyantike niṣaṇṇāḥ / ākāṃkṣamāṇaḥ sāhasrikacūḍikalokadhātun svareṇa vijñāpayati / dvisāhasraṃ vā trisāhasraṃ vā yāvaddaśasu dikṣvaprameyāsaṃkhyeyān lokadhātūn svareṇa vijñāpayati / tasmācca ghoṣādanekaprakārā sattvānāṃ dharmadeśanā niścarati / yā sattvānāmarthāya saṃvartate /
body.translated_text: seated and gathered, extending to the boundary of the assembly circle of a hundred <s>yojanas</s>, one makes known to all with a perfectly full voice, whether they are seated far or near. When wishing, one makes known with one's voice the thousandfold summit world-system (<s>sāhasrikacūḍikalokadhātu</s>), or the twofold-thousandfold, or the threefold-thousandfold, up to immeasurable and innumerable world-systems in the ten directions. And from that sound issues forth <s>Dharma</s>-teaching of many kinds for beings, which conduces to their benefit.

body.text: tatra svasambaddhaṃ vāṅnirmāṇaṃ yatsvayameva nirmitayā vācā dharmaṃ vā deśayati pramattaṃ vā saṃcodayati /
body.translated_text: There, self-connected speech creation (<s>svasambaddha vāṅnirmāṇa</s>) is when one personally teaches the <s>Dharma</s> or admonishes the heedless through one's own created speech.

body.text: parasaṃbaddhaṃ punaryat paranirmitayā vācā dharmaṃ vā deśayati pramattaṃ vā saṃcodayati /
body.translated_text: Other-connected [speech creation], however, is when one teaches the <s>Dharma</s> or admonishes the heedless through the created speech of another.

body.text: tatrāsambaddhaṃ vāṅnirmāṇaṃ yadākāśāt vāṅniścarati nirmitādvā na sattvasantānāt /
body.translated_text: There, unconnected speech creation (<s>asambaddha vāṅnirmāṇa</s>) is when speech issues forth from space or from a creation, not from the continuum of a sentient being.

body.text: tatra dharmadeśanānirmāṇaṃ yat tatra tatra sammūḍhānāṃ yuktisaṃdarśanārtham /
body.translated_text: There, the creation of <s>Dharma</s>-teaching (<s>dharmadeśanānirmāṇa</s>) is for the purpose of showing what is reasonable to those who are confused in various ways.

body.text: tatra codanānirmāṇaṃ yadasammūḍhānāṃ pratilabdhaprasādānāṃ pramattānāṃ pramāde hrīsaṃjananāya apramāde ca samādāpanāya /
body.translated_text: There, the creation of admonishment (<s>codanānirmāṇa</s>) is for the purpose of generating shame (<s>hrī</s>) regarding heedlessness and inducing diligence in those who are not confused, who have gained faith, but who are heedless.

body.text: tadetadanekavidhaṃ nirmāṇam / samāsataḥ kāyanirmāṇaṃ vāṅnirmāṇaṃ viṣaya nirmāṇañca veditavyam / itīyaṃ nairmāṇikī ṛddhiḥ / eṣāpi caikaikaprakārabhedenāprameyā cāsaṃkhyeyā ca veditavyā /
body.translated_text: This creation is of many kinds. In brief, it should be understood as creation of body (<s>kāyanirmāṇa</s>), creation of speech (<s>vāṅnirmāṇa</s>), and creation of objects (<s>viṣayanirmāṇa</s>). This is the creative supernatural power (<s>nairmāṇikī ṛddhi</s>). And this too, by the divisions of each individual type, should be understood as immeasurable and innumerable.

body.text: sā punareṣā dvividhāpi ṛddhirbuddhabodhisattvānāṃ samāsato dve kārye niṣpādayati / āvarjayitvā vā ṛddhiprātihāryeṇa sattvān buddhaśāsane 'vatārayati anugrahaṃ vā anekavidhaṃ bahu nānāprakāraṃ duḥkhitānāṃ sattvānāmupasaṃharati /
body.translated_text: This twofold supernatural power of <s>Buddhas</s> and <s>Bodhisattvas</s>, in brief, accomplishes two purposes: having attracted beings through the miracle of supernatural power (<s>ṛddhiprātihārya</s>), one introduces them into the <s>Buddha</s>'s teaching; or one bestows manifold, abundant, and various kinds of assistance upon suffering beings.

body.text: tatra pūrvenivāsajñānaṃ buddhabodhisattvānāṃ katamat / iha tathāgato vā bodhisattvo vā ātmanaivātmanastāvatpūrvanivāsaṃ samanusmarati amukā nāma te sattvā yatrāhamabhūvamevannāmeti vistareṇa yathāsūtraṃ sattvakāyadikaṃ sarvamanusmarati / yathā cātmanātmanaḥ samanusmarati tathā pareṣāmapi anusmārayati / svayameva ca pareṣāmanusmarati / ye 'pi te sattvakāyāḥ pūrvānte yannivāsāstānapyātmanā
body.translated_text: There, what is the knowledge of former abodes (<s>pūrvanivāsajñāna</s>) of <s>Buddhas</s> and <s>Bodhisattvas</s>? Here, a <s>Tathāgata</s> or <s>Bodhisattva</s> first recollects his own former abodes: 'Those beings named thus [were where] I was, with such a name'—and so on in detail as in the <s>sūtra</s>, recollecting everything beginning with the groups of beings. Just as one recollects one's own [former abodes], so one also causes others to recollect. One personally recollects others' [former lives]. And whatever groups of beings existed in the past, and whatever abodes they had—these too one

body.text: smarati pareṣāṃ smārayati amukā nāma te sattvā yatrāhamabhūvamevaṃnāmeti vistareṇa / teṣāmapi sattvānāṃ tathaiva sarvaṃ pūrvenivāsamanusmarati yathaivātmano dṛṣṭadharme / sūkṣmamapi samanusmarati yatkiñcidalpaṃ vā prabhūtaṃ vā pūrvaceṣṭitaṃ pūrvameva cetayitvā apramuṣitam / nirantaramapi samanusmarati / kṣaṇaṃ nairantaryayogenāvicchinnaṃ yayaivānupūrvyā kṛtamitamapyanusmarati / yasya kalpagaṇanāyogena śakyā saṃkhyāṃ kartum aprameyāsaṃkhyeyamapyanusmarati / yasya kalpagaṇanāyogenāśakyā saṃkhyāṃ kartum avyāhatamasya samāsataḥ pūrvenivāsajñānaṃ pravartate yatreṣṭaṃ yatheṣṭaṃ yāvadiṣṭam / evaṃrūpo bodhisattvasya tathāgatasya ca pūrvenivāsasaṃgṛhītaḥ prabhāvaḥ / sa tena pūrvenivāsānusmṛtijñānena jātakān pūrvān bodhisattvacaryāṃ sattvānāṃ buddhe bhagavati prasādajananārthaṃ gauravotpādanārthaṃ ca vicitrānanekaprakārān prakāśayati itivṛttakāṃśca pūrvayogapratisaṃyuktān sattvānāṃ karmaphalavipākamārabhya / śāśvatadṛṣṭikānāṃ ca sattvānāṃ śāśvatadṛṣṭiṃ nāśayati tadyathā pūrvāntakalpakānāṃ śāśvatavādināmekatya-śāśvatikānāṃ vā /
body.translated_text: recollects personally and causes others to recollect: 'Those beings named thus [were where] I was, with such a name'—and so on in detail. Of those beings too, one recollects all their former abodes just as one's own in the present life. One recollects even what is subtle—whatever little or much was previously done, having previously intended it, without forgetting. One recollects without interruption, moment by moment in continuous succession, in the very order in which things were done. One recollects even what is immeasurable and innumerable, whose calculation can be made by the method of counting <s>kalpas</s>. One's knowledge of former abodes operates unobstructed even regarding what cannot be calculated by the method of counting <s>kalpas</s>—in brief, wherever desired, however desired, and as far as desired. Such is the power of the <s>Bodhisattva</s> and the <s>Tathāgata</s> included under the knowledge of former abodes. With that knowledge of the recollection of former abodes, one reveals former <s>jātaka</s> tales and the previous <s>Bodhisattva</s> conduct in various and manifold ways, for the purpose of generating faith and respect in beings toward the <s>Buddha Bhagavān</s>. And one reveals narratives (<s>itivṛttaka</s>) connected with former associations regarding the ripening of the fruits of beings' actions. And one destroys the eternalist view (<s>śāśvatadṛṣṭi</s>) of beings who hold eternalist views, such as those who speculate about the prior limit (<s>pūrvāntakalpaka</s>), eternalists (<s>śāśvatavādin</s>), or partial eternalists.

body.text: divyaṃ śrotrajñānaṃ buddhabodhisattvānāṃ katamat / iha tathāgato vā bodhisattvo vā divyena śrotreṇa divyān mānuṣyakān śabdānāryānapyanāryānapi ghanānapyaṇukānapi vyaktānapyavktānapi nirmitānapyanirmitānapi dūrāntikasthān śṛṇoti /
body.translated_text: What is the knowledge of the divine ear (<s>divyaśrotrajñāna</s>) of <s>Buddhas</s> and <s>Bodhisattvas</s>? Here, a <s>Tathāgata</s> or <s>Bodhisattva</s>, with the divine ear, hears divine and human sounds, noble and ignoble, gross and subtle, distinct and indistinct, created and uncreated, situated far and near.

body.text: tatra divyāḥ śabdāḥ ūrdhvaṃ yāvadakaniṣṭhabhavanopapannānāṃ sattvānām / sa cetpareṇābhogaṃ na karoti atha karoti tato 'pi pareṇānyeṣūrdhvaṃ lokadhātuṣu śṛṇoti /
body.translated_text: There, divine sounds are those of beings born upward as far as the <s>Akaniṣṭha</s> heaven. And if one applies effort beyond that, then one hears also in the world-systems further above.

body.text: tatra mānuṣyakāḥ śabdāḥ / tiryak sarvacāturdvīpakopapannānāṃ sattvānām /
body.translated_text: There, human sounds are those of beings born in the entire four continents, laterally.

body.text: tatrāryāḥ śabdāḥ / ye buddhānāṃ buddhaśrāvakānāṃ ca bodhisattvānāṃ pratyekabuddhānāñca / teṣāṃ vā 'ntikācchrutvānuśrāvayatāṃ tadanyeṣāṃ sattvānām / tadyathā saṃdarśayatāṃ samādāpayatāṃ vā samuttejayatāṃ saṃpraharṣayatāṃ kuśalasamādānamārabhyākuśalatyāgañca /
body.translated_text: There, noble sounds are those of <s>Buddhas</s>, <s>Buddha</s>-disciples, <s>Bodhisattvas</s>, and <s>Pratyekabuddhas</s>; and of other beings who, having heard from them, announce [their teachings]—namely, those who instruct, encourage, inspire, and gladden, beginning with the undertaking of the wholesome and the abandonment of the unwholesome.

body.text: tathā 'saṃkliṣṭacittānāmuddeśaḥ svādhyāyo viniścayaḥ samyak codanā smāraṇāvavādānuśāsanī iti yadvā punaranyadapi kiñcit subhāṣitaṃ sulapitamarthopasaṃhitam / amī ucyante āryāḥ śabdāḥ /
body.translated_text: Also, for those with undefiled minds: instruction (<s>uddeśa</s>), recitation (<s>svādhyāya</s>), elucidation (<s>viniścaya</s>), proper admonishment (<s>codanā</s>), reminding (<s>smāraṇā</s>), advice (<s>avvadā</s>), and guidance (<s>anuśāsanī</s>)—and whatever other speech that is well-spoken, well-uttered, and connected with meaning. These are called noble sounds.

body.text: tatrānāryāḥ śabdāḥ / ye sattvānāṃ mṛṣāvādapaiśunyapārūṣyasaṃbhinnapralāpaśabdā adho vā 'pāyopapannānāmūrdhvaṃ vā devopapannānāṃ tiryagvā manuṣyeṣūpapannānām /
body.translated_text: There, ignoble sounds are: the sounds of beings' false speech, slander, harsh speech, and frivolous talk — whether of those reborn below in the lower realms, above among the gods, or laterally among humans.

body.text: tatra dhanāḥ śabdāḥ / ye mahāsattvasaṃghaśabdā vā vividhairvā kāraṇaiḥ kāryamāṇānāmārttasvaraṃ kandamānānāṃ vikrośatāṃ vā meghastanitaśabdā vā śaṃkhabherīpaṭahaśabdā vā /
body.translated_text: There, loud sounds are: the sounds of great assemblies of beings, or the cries of distress, the wailing and screaming of those being tortured for various reasons, or the sounds of thunder-clouds, or the sounds of conch-shells, kettledrums, and war-drums.

body.text: aṇukāḥ śabdāḥ / antato yāvat karṇajāpaśabdāḥ /
body.translated_text: Minute sounds are: sounds down to and including the sound of whispering in the ear.

body.text: vyaktāḥ śabdāḥ / yeṣāmartho vijñāyate /
body.translated_text: Distinct sounds are: those whose meaning is understood.

body.text: avyaktāḥ śabdāḥ / yeṣāmartho na vijñāyate / tadyathā drāmiḍānāṃmantrāṇāṃ vāyuvanaspatiśukasārikākokilajīvaṃjīvakādīnām /
body.translated_text: Indistinct sounds are: those whose meaning is not understood — such as [the sounds] of <s>Drāmiḍa</s> [languages], of mantras, of wind, trees, parrots, mynahs, cuckoos, <s>jīvaṃjīvaka</s> birds, and the like.

body.text: tatra nirmitāḥ śabdāḥ / ye ṛddhimadbhiścetovaśiprāptairvā ṛddhyabhisaṃskṛtāḥ /
body.translated_text: There, created sounds are: those produced through supernatural power by those possessing supernatural abilities or those who have attained mastery of mind.

body.text: dūrāḥ śabdāḥ / yatra grāme kṣetre vihāre vā tathāgato vā bodhisattvo vā viharati tatra ye śabdā niścaranti tān sthāpayitvā tadanyatra yāvadaprameyāsaṃkhyeyeṣu lokadhātuṣu /
body.translated_text: Distant sounds are: apart from whatever sounds issue forth where a <s>Tathāgata</s> or <s>Bodhisattva</s> dwells — whether in a village, a region, or a monastery — all other [sounds] extending throughout immeasurable and countless world-systems.

body.text: cyutyupapattijñānaṃ buddhabodhisattvānāṃ katamat / iha tathāgato vā bodhisattvo vā divyena cakṣuṣā viśuddhenātikrāntamānuṣyakeṇa sattvān paśyati cyutikāle 'pi cyutānapi suvarṇadurvarṇān hīnapraṇītānaparānte ca jātān / vṛddheścānvayādindriyāṇāṃ paripākādvicitre kāyaceṣṭite kuśalākuśalāvyākṛteṣu pravartamānān / tathāvabhāsamapi paśyati jānīte sūkṣmamapi paśyati / yadrūpaṃ nirmitaṃ yacca divyamacchaṃ rūpamadho yāvadavīcimūrdhvaṃ yāvadakaniṣṭhabhavanam / sa cedadha ūrdhvaṃ vānyeṣu lokadhātuṣu rūpadarśanamārabhyābhogaṃ karoti tiryagyāvadaprameyeṣvasaṃkhyeyeṣu lokadhātuṣu sarvaṃ rūpagataṃ paśyati / antatasteṣu teṣu buddhakṣetreṣu
body.translated_text: What is the knowledge of death and rebirth (<s>cyutyupapattijñāna</s>) of <s>Buddhas</s> and <s>Bodhisattvas</s>? Here, a <s>Tathāgata</s> or <s>Bodhisattva</s>, with the divine eye — purified, surpassing human [vision] — sees beings at the time of death and having died, of good or bad complexion, of low or exalted [station], and reborn in their subsequent [destination]. And through the maturation of the faculties of growth, lineage, and so forth, engaged in various bodily activities — wholesome, unwholesome, and indeterminate. He sees and knows even the [subtle] appearance as it is; he sees even what is subtle. Whatever form is created, and whatever divine, translucent form [there is], downward as far as <s>Avīci</s>, upward as far as the <s>Akaniṣṭha</s> abode — if he directs his attention to seeing form below, above, or in other world-systems, extending laterally throughout immeasurable and countless world-systems, he sees all that pertains to form. Even in those various <s>Buddha</s>-fields,

body.text: tāṃstāṃstathāgatān vicitreṣu mahatsu parṣanmaṇḍaleṣu niṣaṇṇān dharma deśayataḥ paśyati / tatra divyena cakṣuṣā tathāgato vā bodhisattvo vā daśasu dikṣu kāyaceṣṭitaṃ śubhāśubhaṃ dṛṣṭvā yathāyogaṃ yathārha teṣu sattveṣu pratipadyate / divyena ca śrotreṇa vākceṣṭitaṃ śubhāśubhaṃ śrutvā teṣu sattveṣu yathāyogaṃ yathārhaṃ pratipadyate / evaṃ divyena cakṣuṣā divyena śrotreṇa bodhisattvastathāgato vā samāsena karma karoti /
body.translated_text: he sees those <s>Tathāgatas</s> seated in various great assembly-circles, teaching the <s>Dharma</s>. There, with the divine eye, a <s>Tathāgata</s> or <s>Bodhisattva</s>, having seen the wholesome and unwholesome bodily activities of [beings] in the ten directions, acts accordingly and appropriately toward those beings. And with the divine ear, having heard the wholesome and unwholesome verbal activities, he acts accordingly and appropriately toward those beings. Thus, in summary, the <s>Bodhisattva</s> or <s>Tathāgata</s> performs his work through the divine eye and the divine ear.

body.text: tatra cetaḥparyāyajñānaṃ buddhabodhisattvānāṃ katamat / iha bodhisattvo vā tathāgato vā pareṣāṃ daśasu dikṣvaprameyāsaṃkhyeyeṣu lokadhātuṣu sattvānāṃ kleśaparyavasthitamapi cittaṃ jānāti / vigatakleśaparyavasthānamapi kleśasānubandhaṃ sānuśayamapi kleśaniranubandhaṃ niranuśayamapi mithyāpraṇihitamapi cittaṃ jānāti / tadyathā tīrthikacittaṃ sāmiṣābhiprāyasya kliṣṭamapi cittaṃ samyak praṇihitamapi cittaṃ jānāti / etadviparyayeṇa hīnamapi cittaṃ jānāti / tadyathā kāmadhātūpapannānāṃ sarvasattvānāmantato mṛgapakṣiṇāmapi / madhyamacittaṃ jānāti tadyathā sarveṣāṃ rūpadhātūpapannānāṃ sattvānām / praṇītamapi cittaṃ jānāti tadyathā sarveṣāmārūpyopapannāṃ sattvānām / sukhaprasaṃyuktamapi duḥkhaprasaṃyuktamapyaduḥkhāsukhavedanāsaṃprayuktamapi cittaṃ jānāti / ekena paracittajñānenaikasya sattvasya yasya yadyathā yādṛśaṃ yāvaccitaṃ pratyupasthitaṃ bhavati tatsakṛdyathābhūtaṃ prajānāti / ekenaiva paracittajñānena prabhūtānāmapi sattvānāṃ yeṣāṃ yadyathā yādṛśaṃ yāvaccittaṃ pratyupasthitaṃ bhavati tadapi sakṛdyathābhūtaṃ prajānāti / sā punariyamabhijñā buddhasya bodhisattvānāmindriyaparāparajñānāya sattvānāṃ nānādhimuktijñānāya nānādhātucaritajñānāya yathāyogañca pratipatsu citrāsu nirvāṇapuraḥsarīṣu samyaksanniyogāya / idamasyāḥ karma veditavyam /
body.translated_text: There, what is the knowledge of the minds of others (<s>cetaḥparyāyajñāna</s>) of <s>Buddhas</s> and <s>Bodhisattvas</s>? Here, a <s>Bodhisattva</s> or <s>Tathāgata</s> knows the minds of other beings in the ten directions, in immeasurable and countless world-systems: a mind afflicted by the obsessive hold of defilements, a mind free from the obsessive hold of defilements, a mind with the underlying tendency of defilements, a mind without the underlying tendency of defilements, a wrongly directed mind — such as the mind of a <s>tīrthika</s> (non-Buddhist ascetic) whose intention involves worldly attachment — he knows a defiled mind, a rightly directed mind. Conversely, he knows an inferior mind — such as that of all beings reborn in the desire realm, down to even animals and birds. He knows a middling mind — such as that of all beings reborn in the form realm. He knows a superior mind — such as that of all beings reborn in the formless [realm]. He knows a mind associated with pleasure, a mind associated with suffering, and a mind associated with neither-suffering-nor-pleasure. With a single [exercise of the] knowledge of others' minds, whatever mind of a single being — of whatever kind, whatever manner, whatever extent — is present, he knows it at once as it truly is.
