With that same single knowledge of others' minds, even of numerous beings — whatever mind of whatever kind, whatever manner, whatever extent is present — he knows that too at once as it truly is. This <s>abhijñā</s> (supernatural knowledge) of the <s>Buddhas</s> and <s>Bodhisattvas</s> serves for knowing the superiority and inferiority of beings' faculties, for knowing their diverse dispositions, for knowing the diverse temperaments and conducts of their elements, and for the correct application in various practices leading to <s>nirvāṇa</s> as appropriate. This is to be understood as its function.

body.text: tatrāsravakṣayajñānaṃ buddhabodhisattvānāṃ katamat / iha tathāgato vā bodhisattvo vā kleśānāṃ kṣayaprāptiṃ yathābhūtaṃ prajānāti / prāpto mayā parairvā āsravakṣayo na veti / āsravakṣayaprāptyupāyamapyātmanaḥ pareṣāñca yathābhūtaṃ prajānāti /
body.translated_text: There, what is the knowledge of the destruction of outflows (<s>āsravakṣayajñāna</s>) of <s>Buddhas</s> and <s>Bodhisattvas</s>? Here, a <s>Tathāgata</s> or <s>Bodhisattva</s> knows as it truly is the attainment of the destruction of defilements: 'The destruction of outflows has been attained by me or by others, or has not [been attained].' He knows as it truly is the means for the attainment of the destruction of outflows, for himself and for others.

body.text: yathā upāyamevamanupāyamapi yathābhūtaṃ prajānāti / āsravakṣayaprāptāvabhimānaṃ pareṣāṃ yathābhūtaṃ prajānāti / nirabhimānamapi yathābhūtaṃ prajānāti / bodhisattvaḥ punaḥ sarvaṃ caitat prajānātyāsravakṣayañca svayaṃ na sākṣātkaroti / ataḥ sāsravañca svayaṃ na sākṣātkaroti / ataḥ sāsravāñca vastu bodhisattvaḥ sahasravairna vijahāti / tatra ca vicarati sāsrave vastuni / na ca saṃkliśyata iti so 'sya sarvaprabhāvāṇāṃ mahattamaḥ prabhāvo veditavyaḥ / tena khalvāsravakṣayajñānena buddhabodhisattvāḥ svayaṃ na kliśyante / pareṣāñca vyapadiśantya bhimānañca nāśayanti / idamasya karma veditavyam /
body.translated_text: Just as he knows the [correct] means, so too he knows the non-means as it truly is. He knows as it truly is the conceit regarding the attainment of the destruction of outflows in others. He knows the absence of conceit as it truly is. The <s>Bodhisattva</s>, moreover, knows all of this and yet does not himself directly realize the destruction of outflows. Therefore, a <s>Bodhisattva</s> does not abandon the things that are accompanied by outflows, even in a thousand lifetimes. And he moves among those things accompanied by outflows, yet is not defiled — this is to be understood as the greatest of all his powers. Through that knowledge of the destruction of outflows, <s>Buddhas</s> and <s>Bodhisattvas</s> themselves are not defiled, and they point out to others [their] conceit and destroy it. This is to be understood as its function.

body.text: tatra dharmaprabhāvaḥ katamaḥ / dānaprabhāvaḥ śīlakṣāntivīryadhyānaprajñāprabhāvaśca / sa punareṣa dānādīnāṃ dharmāṇāṃ prabhāvaḥ samāsataścaturbhirākārairveditavyaḥ / vipakṣaprahāṇataḥ saṃbhāraparipākataḥ svaparānugrahataḥ āyatyāṃ phaladānataśca /
body.translated_text: There, what is the efficacy of <s>dharmas</s> (<s>dharmaprabhāva</s>)? It is the efficacy of generosity (<s>dāna</s>), moral conduct (<s>śīla</s>), patience (<s>kṣānti</s>), vigor (<s>vīrya</s>), meditation (<s>dhyāna</s>), and wisdom (<s>prajñā</s>). This efficacy of <s>dharmas</s> such as generosity and the rest is to be understood, in brief, through four aspects: the abandonment of the opposing [factor], the ripening of the accumulation [of merit], the benefiting of self and others, and the giving of fruit in the future.

body.text: dānaṃ dadad bodhisattvo dānavipakṣaṃ mātsaryaṃ prajahāti / ātmano bodhisaṃbhārabhūtañca bhavati tadasya dānam / dānena ca saṃgrahavastunā sattvān paripācayati / pūrvaṃ dānāt sumanā dadaccittaṃ prasādayati / dattvā cāvipratisārī / triṣu kāleṣu pramuditacittatayā ātmānamanugṛhaṇāti / pareṣāṃ ca jighatsāpipāsāśotoṣṇavyādhīcchāvighātabhayaduḥkhāpanayanāt paramanugṛhṇāti / paratra ca yatra yatra pratyājāyate āḍhyo bhavati mahābhogo mahāpakṣo mahāparivāra ityeṣa caturākāro dānasya prabhāvo nāta uttari nāto bhūyaḥ /
body.translated_text: The <s>Bodhisattva</s>, while giving gifts (<s>dāna</s>), abandons miserliness (<s>mātsarya</s>), the opposing factor of generosity. And that giving becomes part of his accumulation for awakening (<s>bodhisaṃbhāra</s>). Through generosity as a means of gathering [beings] (<s>saṃgrahavastu</s>), he matures beings. Before giving, being well-disposed, the giver purifies the mind. Having given, being free from regret, at the three times [before, during, and after] with a joyful mind, he benefits himself. And by removing the suffering of others' hunger, thirst, cold, heat, illness, [unfulfilled] desire, affliction, and fear, he benefits others. And wherever he is reborn in the future, he becomes wealthy, of great possessions, with a great following and great retinue. This is the fourfold efficacy of generosity — there is nothing beyond this, nothing more.

body.text: kāyavāksaṃvaraśīlaṃ samādadāno bodhisattvaḥ śīlavipakṣaṃ dauḥśīlyaṃ prajahāti / bodheśca saṃbhārabhūtaṃ bhavati tadasya śīlasamādānam / samānārthatayā ca saṃgrahavastunā sattvān paripācayati / dauḥśīlyapratyayaṃ bhayamavadyaṃ vairaṃ prajahadātmānamanugṛhaṇāti sukhaṃ svapan sukhaṃ pratibudhyamānaḥ / tathā śīlavato 'vipratisāraḥ prāmodyaṃ yāvaccittasamādhiḥ / ityevamātmānamanugṛhṇāti / sarvasattvānāñca sarvaprakārairaviheṭhanatayā abhayamanuprayacchati / evaṃ paramapyanugṛhṇāti /
body.translated_text: The <s>Bodhisattva</s>, undertaking the moral conduct (<s>śīla</s>) of restraint of body and speech, abandons immorality (<s>dauḥśīlya</s>), the opposing factor of moral conduct. And that undertaking of moral conduct becomes part of his accumulation for awakening. Through being of equal purpose as a means of gathering [beings], he matures beings. Abandoning the fear, blame, and hostility that are conditions of immorality, he benefits himself — sleeping happily and waking happily. Likewise, for the morally virtuous one there is freedom from regret, gladness, up to mental concentration (<s>cittasamādhi</s>) — thus he benefits himself. And by not harming all beings in any way, he gives fearlessness to them — thus he benefits others.

body.text: tannidānañca kāyasya bhedātsugatau svargaloke deveṣūpapadyate / ityayaṃ caturākāraḥ prabhāvaḥ śīlasya / nāta uttari nāto bhūyaḥ /
body.translated_text: And because of that, at the breaking up of the body, he is reborn in a good destination, in the heavenly world, among the gods. This is the fourfold efficacy of moral conduct — there is nothing beyond this, nothing more.

body.text: kṣamo bodhisattvaḥ kṣāntivipakṣamakṣānti prajahāti / bodheśca saṃbhārabhūtā sāsya kṣānti rbhavati / samānārthatayaiva ca sattvān paripācayati / ātmānañca parañca mahato bhayātparitrāyamāṇastayā kṣyāntyā ātmānañca paraṃścānugṛhṇāti / tato nidānañca bodhisattva āyatyāmavairabahulo bhavatyabhedabahulaścāduḥkhadaurmanasyabahulaḥ / dṛṣṭe ca dharme 'vipratisārī kālaṃ karoti / kāyasya ca bhedātsugatau svargaloke deveṣūpapadyate / ityayañcaturākāraḥ kṣānteḥ prabhāvo nāta uttari nāto bhūyaḥ /
body.translated_text: The <s>Bodhisattva</s>, being patient (<s>kṣama</s>), abandons impatience (<s>akṣānti</s>), the opposing factor of patience. And that patience of his becomes part of the accumulation for awakening. Through being of equal purpose, he matures beings. Protecting both himself and others from great danger through that patience, he benefits both himself and others. And because of that, the <s>Bodhisattva</s> in the future will have little enmity, much harmony, and little suffering and displeasure. And in this present life, being free from regret, he dies [peacefully]. At the breaking up of the body, he is reborn in a good destination, in the heavenly world, among the gods. This is the fourfold efficacy of patience — there is nothing beyond this, nothing more.

body.text: ārabdhavīryo bodhisattvo viharan vīryavipakṣaṃ kausīdyaṃ prajahāti / bodheśca saṃbhārabhūtaṃ bhavati sanniśrayaśca tadvīryam / samānārthatayaiva ca sattvān paripācayati / ārabdhavīryaśca sukhaṃ sparśaṃ viharannavyavakīrṇaḥ pāpakairakuśalairdharmaḥ pūrveṇāparaṃ viśeṣādhigamaṃ paśyan prītiprāmodyenātmānamanugṛhṇāti / kuśalapakṣābhiyuktaśca paraṃ na kāyena vācā vā viheṭhayati / pareṣāṃ cārabdhavīryatāyāṃ chandaṃ janayati / evaṃ paramapyanugṛhṇāti / hetubalikaśca bhavati āyatyāṃ puruṣakārābhirataśca / ityayaṃ caturākāro vīryaprabhāvaḥ / nāta uttari nāto bhūyaḥ /
body.translated_text: The <s>Bodhisattva</s>, dwelling with initiated vigor (<s>vīrya</s>), abandons laziness (<s>kausīdya</s>), the opposing factor of vigor. And that vigor becomes part of his accumulation for awakening and its support. Through being of equal purpose, he matures beings. With vigor initiated, dwelling happily in [spiritual] attainment, uncontaminated by evil unwholesome <s>dharmas</s>, seeing progressive attainment from the earlier to the later, through joy and gladness he benefits himself. Devoted to the side of wholesome [qualities], he does not harm others by body or speech. And he generates desire for initiated vigor in others — thus he benefits others. And he becomes strong in causal [merit] and delights in human effort in the future. This is the fourfold efficacy of vigor — there is nothing beyond this, nothing more.

body.text: dhyānaṃ samāpadyamāno bodhisattvo dhyānavipakṣaṃ kleśaṃ kāma vitarkaprītisukharūpasaṃjñādīṃścopakleśān prajahāti / bodheśca saṃbhārabhūtaṃ sanniśrayabhūtaṃ bhavati tadasya dhyānam / samānārthatayaiva ca sattvān paripācayati / dṛṣṭadharmasukhavihāratayātmānamanugṛhṇāti / śāntapraśāntavītarāgacittatayā sattveṣvavyābādhyo bhavannavikopyaḥ paramapyanugṛhṇāti / jñānaviśuddhirabhijñānirhāraviśuddhirdevopapattiścāyatyāṃ dhyānaphalam / ityeṣa caturākāro dhyānaprabhāvo nāta uttari nāto bhūyaḥ /
body.translated_text: The <s>Bodhisattva</s>, entering into meditation (<s>dhyāna</s>), abandons the opposing factors of meditation — namely, the defilements of sense-desire, discursive thought, joy, pleasure, perception of form, and the secondary defilements. And that meditation of his becomes part of and the support for his accumulation for awakening. Through being of equal purpose, he matures beings. Through the pleasant abiding in the present life, he benefits himself. Through the tranquil, peaceful, and dispassionate state of mind, being non-harmful and imperturbable toward beings, he benefits others. The fruit of meditation in the future is: purification of knowledge, the production of supernatural knowledge (<s>abhijñā</s>), and rebirth among the gods. This is the fourfold efficacy of meditation — there is nothing beyond this, nothing more.

body.text: prajñāvān bodhisattvaḥ prajñāvipakṣamavidyāṃ prajahāti / bodheśca saṃbhārabhūtā bhavatyasya sā prajñā / dānenāpi priyavāditayāpyarthacaryayāpi samānārthatayāpi
body.translated_text: The wise <s>Bodhisattva</s>, endowed with wisdom (<s>prajñā</s>), abandons ignorance (<s>avidyā</s>), the opposing factor of wisdom. And that wisdom of his becomes part of his accumulation for awakening. Through generosity, through pleasant speech, through acting for others' benefit, and through being of equal purpose,

body.text: ca sattvān paripācayati / jñeyavastu-yathārtha-pratyavagamopasaṃhitenodāreṇa prītiprāmodyenātmānamanugṛhṇāti / sarvatra nyāyopadeśena dṛṣṭe dharme saṃparāye ca hitasukhābhyāṃ sattvānapyanugṛhṇāti / sarvakuśalamūlaparigrahañca tayā samyakkaroti / āyatyāñca dvividhamapyāvaraṇavisaṃyogaṃ sākṣātkaroti kleśāvaraṇavisaṃyogaṃ jñeyāvaraṇavisaṃyogañca / ityayaṃ caturākāraḥ prajñāyāḥ prabhāvaḥ / nāta uttari nāto bhūyaḥ / ayamucyate dharmaprabhāvaḥ /
body.translated_text: he matures beings. Through the magnificent joy and gladness accompanied by the correct comprehension of knowable objects as they truly are, he benefits himself. Through righteous instruction everywhere, bringing benefit and happiness to beings in this present life and the hereafter, he benefits others. And through that [wisdom], he correctly gathers all roots of virtue. In the future, he directly realizes both kinds of freedom from obscuration: freedom from the obscuration of afflictions (<s>kleśāvaraṇavisaṃyoga</s>) and freedom from the obscuration of the knowable (<s>jñeyāvaraṇavisaṃyoga</s>). This is the fourfold efficacy of wisdom — there is nothing beyond this, nothing more. This is called the efficacy of <s>dharmas</s>.

body.text: sahajaḥ prabhāvo buddhabodhisattvānāṃ katamaḥ / prakṛtijātismaratā / sattvānāmarthe apratisaṃkhyāya dīrghakālikavicitra-tīvranirantaraduḥkhasahiṣṇutā / sattvānāmevārthe sattvārthasaṃpādakena duḥkhena modanā / tuṣiteṣu copapannasya yāvadāyustuṣiteṣvavasthānam / tribhiśca sthānaistuṣitopapannānāṃ tadanyeṣāṃ deva putrāṇāmabhibhavaḥ divyenāyuṣā divyena varṇena divyena yaśasā / upapadyamānasya ca mātuḥ kukṣāvudāreṇāvabhāsena lokadhātuspharaṇaṃ saṃprajānataśca mātuḥ kukṣipraveśaḥ sthānaṃ nirgamo janma ca / jātamātrasya ca pṛthivyāṃ saptapadagamanamaparigṛhītasyākenacit / vācaśca bhāṣaṇā jātasya codāradevanāgayakṣāsuragaruḍakinnaramahoragairdivyaimālyairvādyairdhūpaiścelavikṣepaiśchatradhva-japatākādibhirvarapravarābhiḥ pūjākarma / niruttaraiśca dvātriṃśatā mahāpuruṣalakṣaṇaiḥ sulakṣitagātratā / carame ca bhave paścime janmani sarvapratyarthikairmārānīkairapi sarvopakramaiścābādhyatā / bodhimaṇḍe ca niṣaṇṇasya maitryā sarvamārabalaparājayaḥ / sarvaparvasu caikaikasminnārāyaṇa balasanniviṣṭatā / dahrasyaiva kumārakasya svayameva kauśalakṛtāvinaḥ / sarvalaukikaśilpasthānānāṃ tvaritatvaritamanupraveśaḥ / svayañcānācārya kamekākina eva ca trisāhasramahāsāhasre mahābodherabhisaṃbodhaḥ / brahmaṇā ca sahāṃpatinā svayamupasaṃkramya loke saddharmadeśanāyai adhyeṣaṇā / mahāmegharavāpratisaṃvedanā / avyutthānatayā ca samāpatteḥ śāntatā / bodhisattve ca mṛgapakṣiṇāmapyantataḥ kṣudramṛgāṇāmapi paramā viśvāsyatā / sarvakālamupasaṃkramaṇaṃ tasya cāntike yathākāmavihāritā /
body.translated_text: What is the innate power (<s>sahaja prabhāva</s>) of <s>Buddhas</s> and <s>Bodhisattvas</s>? Natural remembrance of [past] births. Endurance of long-lasting, varied, intense, and uninterrupted suffering for the welfare of beings, without deliberation. Rejoicing in suffering that accomplishes the welfare of beings, precisely for the sake of beings. When reborn among the <s>Tuṣita</s> [gods], remaining in <s>Tuṣita</s> for the duration of life. And surpassing the other sons of the gods reborn in <s>Tuṣita</s> in three respects: divine lifespan, divine complexion, and divine renown. When being conceived, pervading the world-systems with a magnificent radiance from the mother's womb; and entering the mother's womb, abiding, emerging, and being born with full awareness. The moment he is born, walking seven steps on the earth, unsupported by anyone. And the utterance of speech. And upon birth, worship by the exalted gods, <s>Nāgas</s>, <s>Yakṣas</s>, <s>Asuras</s>, <s>Garuḍas</s>, <s>Kinnaras</s>, and <s>Mahoragas</s> with divine garlands, music, incense, cloth-tossing, parasols, banners, flags, and supreme offerings. And a body well-marked with the unsurpassed thirty-two marks of a great person. And in the final existence, the last birth, invulnerability by all hostile forces of <s>Māra</s> and all their assaults. And while seated on the <s>bodhimaṇḍa</s> (seat of awakening), the defeat of all the forces of <s>Māra</s> through loving-kindness (<s>maitrī</s>). And the strength of <s>Nārāyaṇa</s> established in each and every limb. Even as a young boy, rapid entry into all worldly arts and crafts through one's own innate skill. And the fully awakening to the great awakening in the trichiliocosm, alone, without a teacher, by oneself. And the request by <s>Brahmā Sahāṃpati</s>, approaching of his own accord, for the teaching of the true <s>Dharma</s> in the world. The awareness of the sound of great thunderclouds. And the tranquility of meditative attainment through non-disturbance. And the supreme trust of even animals and birds, even small creatures, in the <s>Bodhisattva</s>: approaching him at all times and abiding near him as they wish.

body.text: tiraścāmantikāttathāgatasya pūjā tadyathā markaṭo madhvaneḍakaṃ tathāgatāyānupradattavān / pratigṛhīte ca tasmin bhagavatā sa markaṭo hṛṣṭamānasaḥ pratyavasṛṣṭaḥ sa nṛtyamānaḥ / bhagavantamevoddiśya tathāgataḥ snāsyati taṃ snāpayiṣyāmīti meghapratīkṣaṇā / vṛkṣamūle ca bodhisattvasya tathāgatasya vā santiṣṭhatastasya sarvavṛkṣāṇāṃ prācīnanimnāsu chāyāsu tasya vṛkṣasya chāyayā kāyāvijahanatā / ṣaḍbhirvarṣairabhisaṃbuddhabodhestathāgatasyāvatāragaveṣiṇo 'pi mārasyālabdhāvatāratā / sārūpya sahagatāyāśca smṛteḥ satatasamitaṃ pratyupasthānatā / smṛtasya ca pratisaṃviditānāṃ vedanānāṃ saṃjñānāṃ vitarkāṇāmutpādaḥ sthānaṃ nirodhaśca /
body.translated_text: And the worship of the <s>Tathāgata</s> from animals—as when the monkey offered a honeycomb to the <s>Tathāgata</s>; and when the <s>Bhagavān</s> accepted it, that monkey, with a delighted mind, leapt away dancing. Watching the clouds, [thinking:] 'The <s>Tathāgata</s> will bathe; I shall bathe him.' And when the <s>Bodhisattva</s> or <s>Tathāgata</s> stands at the foot of a tree, while the shadows of all other trees incline to the east, the shadow of his tree does not leave his body. And though <s>Māra</s> sought an opportunity against the <s>Tathāgata</s> for six years after his awakening, he found no opportunity. And the constant presence of mindfulness accompanied by conformity [to the <s>Dharma</s>]. And for one who is mindful, the arising, abiding, and cessation of known feelings, perceptions, and thoughts.

body.text: tathā darśanānugrahakaraḥ sahajaḥ prabhāvo buddhānāmāryacāravihārasaṃgṛhītaśca /
body.translated_text: Likewise, the innate power of the <s>Buddhas</s> that grants benefit through sight and is included in noble conduct and abiding.

body.text: tatra darśanānugrahakaraḥ / tadyathā unmattāḥ kṣiptacittāḥ tathāgataṃ dṛṣṭvā svacittaṃ pratilabhante / vilomagarbhāḥ striyaḥ anulomagarbhā bhavanti / andhāścakṣūṃṣi pratilabhante badhirāḥ śrotrāṇi / raktānāṃ rāgaparyavasthānāṃ vigacchati dviṣṭānāṃ dveṣaparyavasthānaṃ mūḍhānāṃ mohaparyavasthānam / ityayamevaṃbhāgīyo darśanānugrahakaraḥ sahajaḥ prabhāvo veditavyaḥ /
body.translated_text: There, the [power] that grants benefit through sight: for example, the insane and those with disturbed minds, upon seeing the <s>Tathāgata</s>, regain their own mind. Women with breech births have normal births. The blind gain sight, the deaf gain hearing. For those afflicted by passion, the obsession of passion departs; for those afflicted by hatred, the obsession of hatred; for those afflicted by delusion, the obsession of delusion. Such and similar should be understood as the innate power that grants benefit through sight.

body.text: tatrāryacāravihārasaṃgṛhītaḥ sahajaḥ prabhāvaḥ / tadyathā dakṣiṇena pārśvena siṃhaśayyāṃ kalpayati / sa cāsya tṛṇaparṇasaṃstara ekapārśvādhiśayito bhavati / avikopitastathāgatārhatsamyaksaṃbuddhaḥ śayānaḥ / na cāsya vāyuḥ kāyāccīvaramapakarṣati / siṃhagatimapi gacchati / ṛṣabhagatimapi gacchati / dakṣiṇaṃ pādaṃ tatprathamata uddharati / tato vāmena pādenānugacchati / gacchataścāsya uccā bhūmipradeśā nīcā bhavanti / nīcā ścoccāḥ / samāḥ pāṇitalajātāḥ / apagatapāṣāṇaśarkarakapālāḥ / vivekanimnena ca cittena grāmaṃ praviśati / praviśataścāsya nīcāni dvārāṇi uccāni bhavanti / āhāramāharato naikaudanapulākamapyatibhinnaṃ praviśati / na cāvaśiṣṭaṃ bhavati yāvad dvitīyamālopaṃ
body.translated_text: There, the innate power included in noble conduct and abiding: for example, he composes his lion-couch on his right side. And his bed of grass and leaves, though laid on one side, remains undisturbed as the <s>Tathāgata</s>, the <s>Arhat</s>, the Perfectly Awakened One, lies sleeping. And the wind does not blow his robe from his body. He also walks with the gait of a lion and the gait of a bull. He lifts his right foot first, then follows with the left. And as he walks, high places become low and low places become high; [the ground becomes] even, like the palm of a hand, free from stones, pebbles, and potsherds. And he enters the village with a mind inclined to seclusion. And as he enters, low doorways become high. When he takes food, not even a single grain of rice enters unevenly, nor is any left over until he places the second morsel.

body.text: prakṣipati / ityayamevaṃbhāgīya āryacāravihārasaṃgṛhītaḥ prabhāvo veditavyaḥ / parinirvāṇasamaye ca mahāpṛthivīcāla ulkāpātā diśo dāhā antarikṣe devadundubhīnāmabhinadanam / so 'pi sahaja eva tathāgatānāṃ prabhāvo nābhijñāsaṃskṛtaḥ / ayaṃ buddhabodhisattvānāṃ sahajaḥ prabhāva ityucyate /
body.translated_text: Such and similar should be understood as the power included in noble conduct and abiding. And at the time of <s>parinirvāṇa</s>, there is a great earthquake, falling of meteors, burning of the directions, and the resounding of divine drums in the sky. That too is an innate power of the <s>Tathāgatas</s>, not produced by superknowledge (<s>abhijñā</s>). This is called the innate power of <s>Buddhas</s> and <s>Bodhisattvas</s>.

body.text: tatra katamo buddhabodhisattvānāṃ śrāvakapratyekabuddhairasādhāraṇaḥ prabhāvaḥ / katamaśca sādhāraṇaḥ / asādhāraṇatā samāsatastribhirākārairveditavyā / sūkṣmataḥ prakārato dhātutaśca / iha tathāgato bodhisattvo vā 'prameyāsaṃkhyeyānāṃ sattvānāmaprameyāsaṃkhyena prabhāvopāyena yathā 'rthakriyā bhavati tadyathābhūtaṃ prajānāti / evaṃ sūkṣmataḥ / sarvaprakāreṇa cābhijñāprabhāveṇa dharmaprabhāveṇa sahajena prabhāveṇa samanvāgato bhavati / evaṃ prakārataḥ / sarvalokadhātavaḥ sarvasattvadhātavaścāsya prabhāvaviṣayañca bhavati / evaṃ dhātutaḥ / śrāvakasya tu saha sattvadhātunā dvisāhasro lokadhāturabhijñāviṣayaḥ / pratyekabuddhasya sarva eva trisāhasro 'bhijñāviṣayaḥ / tatkasya hetoḥ / tathā hi te ekasyaivātmano damāya pratipannāḥ / no tu sarvasattvānām / tasmātteṣāmeka eva dhātuḥ paramaprabhāvaviṣayo bhavati / etānākārān sthāpayitvā buddhabodhisattvānāṃ tadanyaḥ prabhāvaḥ śrāvakapratyekabuddhaiḥ sādhāraṇo veditavyaḥ / tadevaṃ sati śrāvakapratyekabuddhā eva tāvadbuddhabodhisattvaiḥ saha na tulyābhijñā bhavanti / kutaḥ punaḥ sarve devamanuṣyāstīrthyāḥ pṛthagjanāśca /
body.translated_text: There, which power of <s>Buddhas</s> and <s>Bodhisattvas</s> is uncommon with <s>Śrāvakas</s> and <s>Pratyekabuddhas</s>, and which is common? The uncommon nature should be understood in brief through three aspects: in subtlety, in variety, and in scope of element. Here, the <s>Tathāgata</s> or <s>Bodhisattva</s> correctly knows, as it truly is, the purpose-accomplishing activity for immeasurable and incalculable beings through immeasurable and incalculable means of supernatural power. Thus, in subtlety. And one is endowed with the power of superknowledge in all its varieties, the power of <s>Dharma</s>, and innate power. Thus, in variety. And all world-systems and all realms of beings are within the scope of one's power. Thus, in scope of element. But for the <s>Śrāvaka</s>, the scope of superknowledge, together with the realm of beings, is a two-thousandfold world-system. For the <s>Pratyekabuddha</s>, the entire three-thousandfold world-system is the scope of superknowledge. For what reason? For they have entered the path for the disciplining of one self alone, not of all beings. Therefore, for them, a single element alone is the scope of their supreme power. Setting aside these aspects, the remaining power of <s>Buddhas</s> and <s>Bodhisattvas</s> should be understood as common with <s>Śrāvakas</s> and <s>Pratyekabuddhas</s>. This being so, <s>Śrāvakas</s> and <s>Pratyekabuddhas</s> are already not equal in superknowledge to <s>Buddhas</s> and <s>Bodhisattvas</s>—how much less all gods, humans, non-Buddhist teachers, and ordinary persons.

body.text: yaścāpi prātihāryaprabhāvo buddhabodhisattvānāmṛddhyādeśanānuśāsti-saṃgṛhītaḥ so 'pyabhijñāprabhāva eva yathāyogaṃ praviṣṭo veditavyaḥ ṛddhiviṣayacetasaḥ paryāyāsravakṣayajñānābhijñāprabhāveṣu / bodhisattvabhūmāvādhāre yogasthāne pañcamaṃ prabhāvapaṭalam // 5 //
body.translated_text: And the power of miracles (<s>prātihārya</s>) of <s>Buddhas</s> and <s>Bodhisattvas</s>, included in supernatural display (<s>ṛddhi</s>), mind-reading (<s>ādeśanā</s>), and instruction (<s>anuśāsti</s>)—that too should be understood as included in the power of superknowledge, respectively, in the domains of supernatural display, knowledge of others' minds, and knowledge of the destruction of defilements. In the <s>Bodhisattvabhūmi</s>, in the Foundation section of the Yoga Place, the fifth chapter on Supernatural Power (<s>Prabhāvapaṭala</s>) is completed. // 5 //

body.text: tatra paripākaḥ katamaḥ / paripākaḥ samāsataḥ ṣaḍbhirākārairveditavyaḥ / svabhāvato 'pi paripācya pudgalato 'pi paripākaprakārabhedato 'pi paripākopāyato 'pi paripācakapudgalato 'pi paripakvapudgala-lakṣaṇato 'pi ca /
body.translated_text: There, what is maturation (<s>paripāka</s>)? Maturation should be understood in brief through six aspects: from the standpoint of intrinsic nature, the person to be matured, the differentiation of types of maturation, the means of maturation, the person who matures, and the characteristics of a matured person.

body.text: tatrāyaṃ paripākasvabhāvaḥ / kuśaladharmavīje sati kuśalānāṃ dharmāṇāmāsevanānvayād yā kleśajñeyāvaraṇaprahāṇaviśuddhyanukūlā kāyacittakarmaṇyatā kalyatā samyak prayoganiṣṭhā yatra sthitāḥ śāstāraṃ vā āgamyānāgamya vā śāstāraṃ bhavyo bhavati pratibalo 'nantaraṃ kleśāvaraṇaprahāṇaṃ vā sākṣātkartuṃ jñeyāvaraṇaprahāṇaṃ vā / tadyathā vraṇo yadā paripāṭanāya niṣṭhāgato bhavatyanantaraṃ pāṭanārhaḥ / saḥ paripakva ityucyate / ghaṭaghaṭīśarāvādi ca mṛnmayaṃ bhāṇḍaṃ yadā paribhogāya niṣṭhāgataṃ bhavati anantaraṃ paribhogārha tadā parikvamityucyate / phalāni vā āmrapanasādīni yadā paribhogāya niṣṭhāgatāni bhavantyanantaraṃ paribhogārhāṇi tadā paripakvānītyucyante / evameva kuśalānāṃ dharmāṇāmāsevanānvayād asau samyak prayoganiṣṭhā anantaraṃ viśuddhye saṃvartate / sa paripākasvabhāvaḥ /
body.translated_text: There, this is the intrinsic nature of maturation: when there is a seed of wholesome <s>dharmas</s>, through the sequential cultivation of wholesome <s>dharmas</s>, there arises a workability and fitness of body and mind that is conducive to the purification through abandonment of the obscurations of affliction and the knowable—a correct culmination of practice, established in which, whether one approaches a teacher or without approaching a teacher, one becomes capable and able to directly realize the abandonment of the obscuration of afflictions or the abandonment of the obscuration of the knowable. Just as a boil, when it has reached the culmination for bursting, is immediately ready to be lanced—that is called 'matured.' And a clay vessel such as a pot, pitcher, or bowl, when it has reached the culmination for use, is immediately fit for use—that is called 'matured.' And fruits such as mangoes, jackfruits, and the like, when they have reached the culmination for consumption, are immediately fit for consumption—those are called 'matured.' Even so, through the sequential cultivation of wholesome <s>dharmas</s>, that correct culmination of practice conduces immediately to purification. This is the intrinsic nature of maturation.

body.text: tatra paripācyāḥ pudgalāḥ samāsataścatvāraḥ / śrāvakagotraḥ śrāvakayāne / pratyekabuddhagotraḥ pratyekabuddhayāne / buddhagotro mahāyāne paripācayitavyaḥ / agotrastho 'pi pudgalaḥ sugatigamanāya paripācayitavyo bhavati / bodhisattvānāṃ buddhānāñca bhagavatām ityete catvāraḥ pudgalāḥ eṣu caturṣu vastuṣu paripācayitavyāḥ / evaṃ paripācyapudgalataḥ paripāko veditavyaḥ /
body.translated_text: There, the persons to be matured are in brief four: one of <s>Śrāvaka</s> lineage is to be matured in the <s>Śrāvakayāna</s>; one of <s>Pratyekabuddha</s> lineage in the <s>Pratyekabuddhayāna</s>; one of <s>Buddha</s> lineage is to be matured in the <s>Mahāyāna</s>. Even a person without lineage (<s>agotra</s>) is to be matured for rebirth in the good destinies. These four persons of the <s>Bodhisattvas</s> and the <s>Buddhas</s>, the <s>Bhagavāns</s>, are to be matured in these four domains. Thus, maturation should be understood from the standpoint of persons to be matured.

body.text: tatra paripākaprabhedaḥ katamaḥ / samāsataḥ ṣaḍvidhaḥ paripākaḥ / indriyaparipākaḥ kuśalamūlaparipākaḥ jñānaparipākaśca mṛdumadhyādhimātraśca paripākaḥ /
body.translated_text: There, what is the differentiation of maturation? In brief, maturation is sixfold: maturation of faculties (<s>indriyaparipāka</s>), maturation of roots of virtue (<s>kuśalamūlaparipāka</s>), maturation of knowledge (<s>jñānaparipāka</s>), and maturation that is mild, medium, and intense.

body.text: tatrendriyaparipākaḥ / yā āryurvarṇakulaiśvaryasampadādeyavacanatā maheśākhyatāmanuṣyatvaṃ
body.translated_text: There, the maturation of faculties: that which is the excellence of lifespan, complexion, family, sovereignty, having one's words heeded, great renown, manhood,

body.text: mahotsāhatā yāmāśrayaparipākaphalasaṃpadamāgamya bhavyo bhavatyātaptānuprayogāyāparikhinnamānasaśca bhavati sarvavidyāsthānasamudāgamābhiyogeṣu /
body.translated_text: and great energy—upon attaining the excellent result of the maturation of the basis, one becomes capable of unflagging application and has an unwearied mind in the endeavors for mastering all fields of knowledge.

body.text: kuśalamūlaparipākaḥ katamaḥ / yā prakṛtyā mandarajaskatāyāmāgamya prakṛtyaivāsya pāpakeṣvakuśaleṣu dharmeṣu / cittaṃ na krāmati mandanivaraṇaśca bhavati mandavitarka ṛjupradakṣiṇagrāhī /
body.translated_text: What is the maturation of roots of virtue? That which, upon attaining one's natural state of having mild defilements, by one's very nature, one's mind does not proceed toward evil, unwholesome <s>dharmas</s>; and one has mild hindrances, mild discursive thought, and is straightforward and receptive.

body.text: jñānaparipākaḥ katamaḥ / smṛtimān bhavati meghāvī pratibalaśca bhavati subhāṣitadurbhāṣitānāṃ dharmāṇāmarthasya ājñānāyodgrahaṇāya dhāraṇāya prativedhāya / sahajayā prajñayā samanvāgato bhavati yāṃ prajñāmāgamya bhavyo bhavati pratibalaḥ sarvato 'tyantaṃ sarvakleśāccittaṃ vimocayitum / tatrendriyaparipākena vipākāvaraṇādvimukto bhavati / kuśalamūlaparipākena karmāvaraṇādvimukto bhavati / jñānaparipākena kleśāvaṇādvimukto bhavati /
body.translated_text: What is the maturation of knowledge? One becomes mindful, intelligent, and capable of comprehending, grasping, retaining, and penetrating the meaning of <s>dharmas</s> both well-spoken and ill-spoken. One is endowed with innate wisdom (<s>sahajā prajñā</s>), upon attaining which one becomes capable and able to completely and ultimately liberate the mind from all afflictions. There, through the maturation of faculties, one is freed from the obscuration of ripening (<s>vipākāvaraṇa</s>). Through the maturation of roots of virtue, one is freed from the obscuration of action (<s>karmāvaraṇa</s>). Through the maturation of knowledge, one is freed from the obscuration of afflictions (<s>kleśāvaraṇa</s>).

body.text: mṛduparipākaḥ katamaḥ / dvābhyāṃ kāraṇābhyāṃ mṛduḥ paripāko bhavati / adīrghakālābhyāsataścendriyakuśalamūlajñānaparipākahetoḥ aparipuṣṭanihīnahetvabhyāsataśca / madhyaḥ paripāko 'nayoreva dvayoḥ kāraṇayoranyataravaikalyādanyatarasānnidhyācca veditavyaḥ / adhimātraḥ punaḥ paripāka ubhayoranayoḥ kāraṇayoravaikalyādveditavyaḥ /
body.translated_text: What is mild maturation? Mild maturation occurs for two reasons: due to non-long-lasting practice of the causes of maturation of faculties, roots of virtue, and knowledge; and due to the practice of unnourished and inferior causes. Medium maturation should be understood as arising from the deficiency of one of these two reasons and the presence of the other. Intense maturation, moreover, should be understood as arising from the non-deficiency of both these reasons.

body.text: tatra paripākopāyaḥ katamaḥ / sa saptaviṃśatividho veditavyaḥ / dhātupuṣṭayā vartaṃmānapratyayopasaṃhārataḥ avatārato ratigrahaṇataḥ ādiprasthānataḥ anādiprasthānataḥ śuddhidūrataḥ śuddhyāsannataḥ prayogataḥ āśayataḥ āmiṣopasaṃhārataḥ dharmopasaṃhārataḥ ṛddhyāvarjanatayā dharmadeśanayā guhyadharmākhyānataḥ vivṛtadharmākhyānataḥ mṛduprayogato madhyaprayogataḥ adhimātraprayogataḥ śravaṇataḥ cintanato bhāvanataḥ saṃgrahaṇato nigrahaṇataḥ svayaṃkṛtataḥ parādhyeṣaṇataḥ tadubhayataśca /
body.translated_text: What then is the method of ripening (<s>paripākopāya</s>)? It is to be known as twenty-seven-fold: through the nourishment of the element (<s>dhātu</s>), through the provision of present conditions, through entry, through the grasping of delight, through initial setting forth, through non-initial setting forth, through being far from purity, through being near to purity, through application, through intention, through the provision of material gifts, through the provision of <s>Dharma</s>, through attracting by supernatural power, through <s>Dharma</s>-teaching, through the exposition of hidden <s>Dharma</s>, through the exposition of revealed <s>Dharma</s>, through mild application, through moderate application, through intense application, through hearing, through reflection, through cultivation, through gathering, through restraining, through one's own action, through requesting others, and through both of those.

body.text: tatra dhātupuṣṭiḥ katamā / yā prakṛtyā kuśaladharmabījasaṃpadaṃ niśritya pūrvakuśaladharmābhyāsāduttarottarāṇāṃ kuśaladharmabījānāṃ paripuṣṭatarā paripuṣṭatamā utpattiḥ sthitiḥ / iyamucyate dhātupuṣṭiḥ /
body.translated_text: What therein is the nourishment of the element? That which, relying on the natural endowment of seeds of wholesome <s>dharmas</s>, through the previous habituation to wholesome <s>dharmas</s>, is the progressively more and most nourished arising and stability of seeds of wholesome <s>dharmas</s>—this is called the nourishment of the element.

body.text: tatra vartamānapratyayopasaṃhāraḥ katamaḥ / dṛṣṭe dharme aviparītā dharmadeśanā / tatra cāviparītagrāhitā / yathāvaddharmānudharmapratipattiśca / tatra dhātupuṣṭeḥ pūrvakeṇa hetunā vartamānaḥ paripāko nivartate / vartamānapratyayopasaṃhārato vartamāna evaṃ heturvartamānaḥ paripāko veditavyaḥ /
body.translated_text: What therein is the provision of present conditions? Unerring <s>Dharma</s>-teaching in the present life; unerring grasping therein; and practice in conformity with the <s>Dharma</s> as it truly is. There, through the prior cause of the nourishment of the element, the present ripening proceeds. Through the provision of present conditions, the present cause and present ripening are to be understood.

body.text: tatrāvatāraḥ katamaḥ / śraddhāpratilambhamadhipatiṃ kṛtvā āgārikasya duścaritavivekaśikṣāpadasamādānam / anāgārikāṃ vā pravrajataḥ kāmavivekaśikṣāpadasamādānam /
body.translated_text: What therein is entry? With the attainment of faith as the governing factor, for a householder it is the undertaking of the training rules for abstaining from misconduct; or for one going forth into homelessness, it is the undertaking of the training rules for abstaining from sensual pleasures.

body.text: ratigrāhaḥ katamaḥ / yā sarvaduḥkha-nairyāṇikīñca pratipadaṃ kāmasukhātmaklamathānta-vivarjitāñca sukhāṃ pratipadamāgamya svākhyāte dharmavinaye śāsanābhiratiḥ
body.translated_text: What is the grasping of delight? That delight in the teaching within the well-proclaimed <s>Dharma</s> and <s>Vinaya</s>, having arrived at the practice leading to the escape from all suffering, the pleasant practice free from the two extremes of sensual pleasure and self-mortification.

body.text: tatrādiprasthānaṃ katamat / ya eva tatprathamataḥ saṃvejanīyeṣu dharmeṣu saṃvegamāgamya nyāyārthapratipādane cānuśaṃsāṃ viditvā 'vatāraḥ / idamevādiprasthānamityucyate /
body.translated_text: What therein is initial setting forth? That very entry which occurs first, having arrived at spiritual urgency (<s>saṃvega</s>) regarding <s>dharmas</s> that inspire urgency and having known the benefit of establishing the meaning of truth—this itself is called the initial setting forth.

body.text: anādiprasthānaṃ katamat / yā avatīrṇasya pudgalasya paripācyamānatāyāṃ vartamānasya bodhisattvebhyo buddhebhyaścānadhyupekṣāmāgamya vivṛtānāñca sthānānāṃ bhūyo bhūyaḥ uttānakriyāmāgamya uttarottaraparipākagamanatā /
body.translated_text: What is non-initial setting forth? That progressive advance in ripening of a person who has already entered and is in the process of being ripened, having arrived at non-indifference from <s>Bodhisattvas</s> and <s>Buddhas</s>, and having arrived at further and further clarification of matters that have been revealed.

body.text: tatra viśuddhidūratā katamā / yat kausīdyaṃ vā āgamya pratyayavaidhuryaṃ vā mahatā dīrgheṇa kālena prabhūtairjanmāntarāparivartaiḥ kalpaparivartairvā bhavyo bhavati viśuddhaye / etadviparyayeṇa viśuddhyāsannatā veditavyā /
body.translated_text: What therein is being far from purity? That which, due to laziness or due to deficiency of conditions, over a great, long period of time, through many turns of lifetimes or turns of <s>kalpas</s> (eons), one becomes fit for purification. Being near to purity is to be understood as the opposite of this.

body.text: tatra prayogaḥ katamaḥ / yā svārthaprāptau tīvracchandatāmāgamya vinipātabhayaṃ vā 'mutra dṛṣṭe vā dharme parato 'yaśobhayamāgamya śikṣāpadeṣvanupālanā sātatyakāritā satkṛtyakāritā ca /
body.translated_text: What therein is application? That which, having arrived at intense desire for the attainment of one's own purpose, and having arrived at fear of downfall in the next life or fear of disgrace from others in the present life, is the observance of the training rules, practiced with continuity and practiced with earnestness.

body.text: tatrāśayaḥ katamaḥ / dharmeṣu ca yā samyak santīraṇā-kṣāntimāgamyāsmāddharmavinayādasaṃhāryatāyai pareṣāñcādhigame 'bhisaṃpratyaya guṇasaṃbhāvanāmāgamya yā triṣu ratneṣu svārthaprāptau cāvicalā śraddhadhānatā /
body.translated_text: What therein is intention? Having arrived at correct investigation and acceptance regarding <s>dharmas</s>, for the sake of being unshakeable from this <s>Dharma</s> and <s>Vinaya</s>, and having arrived at conviction in the attainment of others and esteem for their qualities—that unwavering faith-holding in the Three Jewels and in the attainment of one's own purpose.

body.text: ābhiṣopasaṃhāraḥ katamaḥ / yaḥ sarveṇa ca sarvaṃ bhojanapānādivikalānāṃ bhojanapānādyupasaṃhāraḥ / anukūlapānabhojanādivikālānāñcānukūlapānabhojanādyupasaṃhāraḥ /
body.translated_text: What is the provision of material gifts? That which is the provision of food, drink, and so forth to those lacking food, drink, and so forth in every way; and the provision of suitable drink, food, and so forth to those lacking suitable drink, food, and so forth.

body.text: tatra dharmopasaṃhāraḥ katamaḥ / yaduddeśato vā dharmāṇāmanupradānaṃ samyagarthavivaraṇato vā /
body.translated_text: What therein is the provision of <s>Dharma</s>? The giving of <s>dharmas</s> such as <s>sūtras</s> and so forth, whether through recitation or through correct explanation of their meaning.

body.text: ṛddhyāvarjanatā katamā / yā ṛddhimata ṛddhiprātihāryavidarśanā sattvānukampayā sattvānāmāśayaviśuddhiṃ vādhipatiṃ kṛtvā prayogaviśuddhiṃ vā ete sattvāḥ prātihāryaṃ dṛṣṭvā śrutvā vā āśayaśuddhiṃ vā śāsane pratilapsyante prayokṣyante samyagiti / te ca tena prātihāryeṇāvarjitamānasā āśayaśuddhiṃ vā pratilabhante prayujyante vā samyak /
body.translated_text: What is attracting by supernatural power? That display of miraculous wonder (<s>ṛddhiprātihārya</s>) by one possessing supernatural power, out of compassion for beings—having made either the purification of the beings' intention or the purification of their practice the governing factor, [thinking:] 'These beings, having seen or heard the miraculous display, or [through] purification of intention, will attain purification in the teaching and will rightly engage.' And those, with their minds attracted by that miraculous display, attain purification of intention or rightly engage.

body.text: tatra deśanā katamā / svayaṃ svārthaprāptāvaśaktasya saddharmadeśanā samyak pratipattisahāyabhūtā / śaktasyāpi ca kṣiprābhijñatāyai anukūlā saddharmadeśanā /
body.translated_text: What therein is teaching? The teaching of the true <s>Dharma</s>, which serves as an aid to correct practice, for one who is himself unable in the attainment of his own purpose; and for one who is able, the teaching of the true <s>Dharma</s> that is conducive to swift direct knowledge.

body.text: tatra guhyadharmākhyānaṃ katamat / yā bālaprajñānāṃ sattvānāmatyudāragambhīrārthadharmapraticchādanatā uttānasupraveśasukhopāyāvatāradharmadeśanatā /
body.translated_text: What therein is the exposition of hidden <s>Dharma</s>? The concealing of exceedingly noble and profound <s>dharmas</s> from beings of weak wisdom, and the teaching of <s>Dharma</s> through accessible, easily entered, easy methods of approach.

body.text: vivṛtadharmākhyānaṃ katamat / yā pṛthuprajñānāṃ sattvānāṃ sukhapraviṣṭabuddhaśāsanānayānāmatyudāragambhīrasthānavivaraṇatā /
body.translated_text: What is the exposition of revealed <s>Dharma</s>? The revealing of exceedingly noble and profound matters to beings of extensive wisdom who have easily entered the methods of the <s>Buddha</s>'s teaching.

body.text: tatra mṛduḥ prayogaḥ katamaḥ / yaḥ sātatyaprayogavivarjitaḥ satkṛtyaprayogavivarjitaśca /
body.translated_text: What therein is mild application? That which is devoid of application with continuity and devoid of application with earnestness.

body.text: madhyaḥ prayogaḥ katamaḥ / yaḥ sātatyaprayogavivarjito vā satkṛtyaprayogavivarjito vā / ityanayordvayoḥ prayogayoranyataravivarjitaḥ /
body.translated_text: What is moderate application? That which is devoid of either application with continuity or application with earnestness—devoid of one of these two applications.

body.text: adhimātraḥ prayogaḥ katamaḥ / yastadubhayaprayogasaṃyuktaḥ sātatyaprayogasaṃyuktaḥ satkṛtyaprayogasaṃyuktaśca /
body.translated_text: What is intense application? That which is conjoined with both applications—conjoined with application with continuity and conjoined with application with earnestness.

body.text: tatra śrutaṃ katamat / yo bauddhapravacanādhimuktasya sūtrādīnāṃ dharmāṇāṃ śravaṇodgrahaṇa-dhāraṇasvādhyāyābhiyogaḥ /
body.translated_text: What therein is hearing? The effort of hearing, grasping, retaining, and reciting <s>dharmas</s> such as <s>sūtras</s> and so forth, for one who has conviction in the word of the <s>Buddha</s>.

body.text: cintā katamā / praviveke dharmanidhyānābhiratasya arthābhyūhanāsaṃlakṣaṇāniścayaḥ /
body.translated_text: What is reflection? The determination of meaning—the investigation, observation, and ascertainment—for one who delights in the contemplation of <s>dharmas</s> in solitude.

body.text: bhāvanā katamā / śamathapragrahopekṣānimitteṣu samyagupalakṣaṇāpūrvikā śamathavipaśyanopekṣā 'bhyāsaratiḥ /
body.translated_text: What is cultivation? The practice of and delight in the repeated cultivation of <s>śamatha</s> (calm), <s>vipaśyanā</s> (insight), and equanimity, preceded by correct observation of the signs of tranquility, exertion, and equanimity.

body.text: saṃgrahaḥ katamaḥ / samyag nirāmiṣacittasya niśrayadānamācāryopādhyāyanyāyena / pṛthagvidhā ca paricaryā tadyathā glānopasthānaparicaryā dharmyacīvarapiṇḍapātaśayanāsanaglānapratyayabhaiṣajyaparicaryā śokakaukṛtyaprativinodanaparicaryā kleśaprativinodanaparicaryā / ityevaṃbhāgīyāḥ pṛthagvidhā paricaryāṃ veditavyāḥ /
body.translated_text: What is gathering? The providing of support with a pure, non-material mind, in the manner of a teacher or preceptor; and various forms of service, such as: service in attending the sick, service in providing lawful robes, alms-food, lodging, and medicine for the sick, service in dispelling sorrow and remorse, and service in dispelling afflictions. Such and similar various forms of service are to be understood.

body.text: nigrahaḥ katamaḥ / ātmagatāṃ saṃkleśārakṣāṃ saṃvidhāya skhalitacodanā mṛdau vyatikrame / madhye vyatikrame 'vasādanā / adhimātre vyatikrame pravāsanā / tatra yā ca codanā yā cāvasādanā sā teṣāmeva hitasukhārthaṃ tadanyeṣāñca / yā punaḥ pravāsanā punaḥ pratisaṃharaṇāya sāpi teṣāṃ cānyeṣāṃ ca hitasukhāya / yā punarapratisaṃhāryā pravāsanā sā pareṣāmeva hitasukhāya / tathāhi pareṣāṃ pravāsanāṃ vyatikramanidānam / pareṣūpalabhyāvyatikramāya cetayate /
body.translated_text: What is restraining? Having arranged for the guarding against one's own defilement: admonishment for a mild transgression; censure for a moderate transgression; expulsion for a serious transgression. Therein, both the admonishment and the censure are for the welfare and happiness of those very persons and of others. And the expulsion that leads to readmission is also for the welfare and happiness of both those persons and others. But the expulsion that is irrevocable is for the welfare and happiness of others alone. For others, seeing the cause of expulsion in the transgression, resolve to avoid transgression themselves.

body.text: kathaṃ svayaṃ paripācayati / ānulomikañca dharmaṃ deśayati akuśalāt sthānādyutthāpya kuśale sthāne pratiṣṭhāpanāya / yathāvādī ca bhavati tathākārī / dharmānudharmapratipannastatsvabhāvānuvartī / yenainaṃ pare naivamāha / tvameva tāvat svayaṃ nākuśalātsthānādyutthitaḥ kuśale ca sthāne pratiṣṭhitaḥ kasmāttvaṃ tatra paraṃ samādāpayitavyaṃ codayitavyaṃ smārayitavyaṃ manyase / tvameva tāvat paraiścodayitavyaḥ smārayitavyaḥ samādāpayitavyaḥ /
body.translated_text: How does one ripen [beings] by oneself? One teaches the <s>Dharma</s> in accordance [with the goal], for the purpose of raising them from unwholesome states and establishing them in wholesome states. And one is a doer as one says—practicing in conformity with the <s>Dharma</s>, following its nature—so that others do not say to him: 'You yourself have not yet risen from unwholesome states and are not established in wholesome states; why then do you think you should exhort, urge, and remind others? You yourself should first be exhorted, reminded, and urged by others.'

body.text: kathaṃ paramadhyeṣate / yasyāntike sattvānāmadhimātraśca premagauravaṃ niviṣṭaṃ bhavati / yaścopāyajño bhavati dharmadeśanāyāṃ suśikṣitaḥ / stamadhyeṣate vyāpārayati paripākāya /
body.translated_text: How does one request others? One who has the deepest affection and respect of beings established toward them, and who is skilled in methods and well-trained in <s>Dharma</s>-teaching—one requests and engages such a person for the ripening [of beings].

body.text: ubhābhyāmābhyāṃ samastābhyāṃ svaparādhyeṣaṇākṛtaḥ paripāko veditavyaḥ /
body.translated_text: The ripening accomplished by both of these together—by one's own action and by requesting others—is to be understood.

body.text: ityanena saptaviṃśatividhena paripākopāyena sā ṣaḍvidhā paripākaprabheda saṃpadveditavyā / indriyaparipākasya kuśalamūlaparipākasya jñānaparipākasya mṛdumadhyādhimātrasya ca paripākasya /
body.translated_text: Thus, through this twenty-seven-fold method of ripening, that sixfold excellence of the types of ripening is to be understood: the ripening of faculties, the ripening of wholesome roots, the ripening of knowledge, and the ripening of mild, moderate, and intense [degrees].

body.text: tatra paripācakāḥ pudgalāḥ katame / samāsataḥ ṣaṭ bodhisattvāḥ ṣaṭasu bodhisattvabhūmiṣu vyavasthitāḥ sattvān paripācayanti / adhimukticaryābhūmisthito
body.translated_text: What therein are the persons who ripen [others]? In brief, six [types of] <s>Bodhisattvas</s>, established on the six <s>Bodhisattva</s>-stages, ripen beings. The <s>Bodhisattva</s> established on the stage of conduct through aspiration (<s>adhimukticaryābhūmi</s>)—

body.text: bodhisattvo 'dhimukticārī / śuddhādhyāśayabhūmisthito bodhisattvaḥ śuddhādhyāśayaḥ / caryāpratipattibhūmisthito bodhisattvaścaryāpratipannaḥ / niyata bhūmisthito bodhisattvo niyata-patitaḥ / niyatacaryā-pratipattibhūmisthito bodhisattvo niyatacaryāpratipannaḥ / niṣṭhāgamanabhūmisthito bodhisattvo niṣṭhāgataḥ / tatrāgotrasthānāṃ pudgalānāṃ sugatigamanāya paripākaḥ punaḥ punaḥ pratyāvartyo bhavati punaḥ punaḥ karaṇīyaḥ / gotrasthānāṃ punaḥ paripāko na pratyāvartyo bhavati na punaḥ punaḥ karaṇīyaḥ /
body.translated_text: is a <s>Bodhisattva</s> of aspiring conduct. The <s>Bodhisattva</s> established on the stage of pure superior intention (<s>śuddhādhyāśayabhūmi</s>) has pure superior intention. The <s>Bodhisattva</s> established on the stage of practice and engagement (<s>caryāpratipattibhūmi</s>) is engaged in practice. The <s>Bodhisattva</s> established on the stage of certainty (<s>niyatabhūmi</s>) has attained certainty. The <s>Bodhisattva</s> established on the stage of certain practice and engagement (<s>niyatacaryāpratipattibhūmi</s>) is engaged in certain practice. The <s>Bodhisattva</s> established on the stage of reaching the culmination (<s>niṣṭhāgamanabhūmi</s>) has reached the culmination. Therein, for persons without lineage (<s>agotra</s>), the ripening for going to happy destinies must be done again and again, repeatedly. But for persons with lineage (<s>gotra</s>), the ripening does not revert and does not need to be done again and again.

body.text: tatra paripakvapudgalalakṣaṇaṃ katamat / śrāvakaḥ pūrvakuśalābhyāsād yadāmṛdupākavyavasthito bhavati sa mṛducchando bhavati mṛduprayogaścāpāyānapi gacchati na ca dṛṣṭe dharme śrāmaṇyaphalamadhigacchati na ca dṛṣṭe dharme parinirvāti / yadā tu madhyapākavyavasthito bhavati sa madhyacchandaśca bhavati madhyaprayogo na cāpāyān gacchati / dṛṣṭe ca dharme śrāmaṇyaphalaṃ prāpnoti / no tu dṛṣṭe dharme parinirvāti / adhimātre paripāke sthitaḥ adhimātracchando bhavati adhimātraprayogaśca na cāpāyān gacchati / dṛṣṭe ca dharme śrāmaṇyaphalaṃ prāpnoti / dṛṣṭa eva ca dharme parinirvāti /
body.translated_text: What therein is the characteristic of a ripened person? When a <s>Śrāvaka</s>, through previous habituation to wholesome [qualities], is established in mild ripening, he has mild desire and mild application, may even go to the lower realms, does not attain the fruit of the ascetic life (<s>śrāmaṇyaphala</s>) in this very life, and does not attain <s>parinirvāṇa</s> in this very life. But when he is established in moderate ripening, he has moderate desire and moderate application, does not go to the lower realms, attains the fruit of the ascetic life in this very life, but does not attain <s>parinirvāṇa</s> in this very life. When established in intense ripening, he has intense desire and intense application, does not go to the lower realms, attains the fruit of the ascetic life in this very life, and attains <s>parinirvāṇa</s> in this very life.

body.text: pratyekabuddhastathaiva veditavyaḥ yathā śrāvakaḥ / tatkasya hetoḥ / tulyajātīyo 'sya mārgaḥ śrāvakaiḥ / ayantu śrāvakebhyaḥ pratyekabuddhasya viśeṣaḥ / paścime bhave paścime ātmabhāvapratilambhe 'nācāyakaṃ pūrvābhyāsavaśāt saptatriṃśadvodhipakṣyān dharmān bhāvayitvā sarvakleśaprahāṇādarhattvaṃ sākṣātkaroti / tasmātpratyekabuddha ityucyate /
body.translated_text: The <s>Pratyekabuddha</s> is to be understood in the same way as the <s>Śrāvaka</s>. For what reason? Because his path is of the same type as that of the <s>Śrāvakas</s>. But this is the distinction of the <s>Pratyekabuddha</s> from the <s>Śrāvakas</s>: in his last existence, in his last attainment of a personal body, without a teacher, through the force of previous habituation, having cultivated the thirty-seven factors conducive to awakening (<s>bodhipakṣyadharma</s>), he directly realizes <s>arhatship</s> through the abandonment of all afflictions. Therefore he is called a <s>Pratyekabuddha</s> (solitary awakened one).

body.text: bodhisattvaḥ punaradhimukticaryābhūmisthito muduparipāko veditavyaḥ / adhyāśayaśuddho caryāpratipattibhūmau ca madhyaparipākaḥ / niyāto niṣṭhitaścādhimātraparipākaḥ / tatra mṛdupākavyavasthito bodhisattvo mṛducchando bhavati mṛduprayogaḥ apāyāṃśca gacchati / prathamakalpāsaṃkhyeyaparyantataśca sa veditavyaḥ / uttaptairacalaiḥ suviśuddhaiśca bodhipakṣyaiḥ kuśalaidharmaiḥ sarvaireva visaṃyukto bhavati / madhyapāko bodhisattvo madhyacchando bhavati madhyaprayogaḥ / na cāpāyān gacchati dvitīyakalpāsaṃkhyeyaparyantataśca bhavati / uttaptairacalaiśca bodhipakṣyaiḥ kuśalairdharmaiḥ
body.translated_text: The <s>Bodhisattva</s>, however, when established on the stage of conduct through aspiration, is to be understood as having mild ripening. On the stages of pure superior intention and practice-engagement, moderate ripening. On the stages of certainty and culmination, intense ripening. Therein, the <s>Bodhisattva</s> established in mild ripening has mild desire and mild application, and may go to the lower realms. He is to be understood as being within the limit of the first incalculable <s>kalpa</s> (eon). He is completely dissociated from all wholesome <s>dharmas</s> of the factors of awakening that are heated, immovable, and thoroughly purified. The <s>Bodhisattva</s> of moderate ripening has moderate desire and moderate application, does not go to the lower realms, and is within the limit of the second incalculable <s>kalpa</s>. With heated and immovable wholesome <s>dharmas</s> of the factors of awakening—

body.text: saṃyukto bhavati / suviśuddhairvisaṃyuktaḥ / adhimātrapākasthito bodhisattvaḥ adhimātracchando bhavatyadhimātraprayogaśca / na cāpāyān gacchati / tṛtīyakalpāsaṃkhyeyaparyantataśca bhavati / uttaptairacalaiḥ suviśuddhairbodhipakṣyaiḥ kuśalairdharmaiḥ samanvāgato bhavati / tatra prakṛtyā ghanatvādujjvalatvādadhimātramahāphalatvānmahānuśaṃsatvāccottaptā ityucyante / apratyāvartyatvādaparihāṇīyatvādviśeṣagāmitvādacalā ityucyante / bodhisattvabhūmau niruttaratvātsuviśuddhā ityucyante /
body.translated_text: is conjoined [with impure factors] and not conjoined with the thoroughly pure ones. The <s>Bodhisattva</s> established in the stage of intense maturation has intense aspiration and intense practice. He does not go to the lower realms. And it extends to the limit of the third incalculable aeon (<s>kalpāsaṃkhyeya</s>). He is endowed with thoroughly heated, immovable, thoroughly purified, wholesome factors conducive to awakening (<s>bodhipakṣya</s>). There, they are called 'thoroughly heated' (<s>uttapta</s>) because of being by nature dense, radiant, of intensely great fruit, and of great benefit. They are called 'immovable' (<s>acala</s>) because of being irreversible, non-declining, and progressive. They are called 'thoroughly purified' (<s>suviśuddha</s>) because of being unsurpassed on the <s>Bodhisattva</s>-stages.

body.text: tatra yaścāmiṣakṛtaḥ paripāko yaśca ṛddhyāvarjanajo yaśca guhyadharmākhyānajo yaśca mṛduprāyogiko yaśca śrutamātrakṛtaḥ paripāka ityeṣa pañcavidhaḥ paripākaḥ dīrghakālābhyāsādapyeṣāṃ dharmāṇāṃ mṛduka eva bhavati prāgevettakakālābhyāsāt / tadanyaistu sarvaiḥ paripākasya kāraṇaiḥ paripākasya triprakāranayo veditavyaḥ / mṛdukenābhyāsena mṛduko madhyena madhyaḥ adhimātreṇādhimātraḥ paripāko veditavyaḥ / tasya ca mṛdumadhyādhimātrasya paripākasyaikaikasya triprakāranayo veditavyaḥ / mṛdukasya [mṛdu-]mṛduko mṛdumadhyo mṛdvadhimātraḥ / madhyasya ca madhyamṛduko madhyamadhyo madhyādhimātraḥ / adhimātrasyādhimātramṛduradhimātramadhyo 'dhimātrādhimātraḥ / ityevaṃ bhāgīyottarottaraprabhedanayenāpramāṇaḥ paripākaprabhedaḥ sattvānāṃ buddhabodhisattvakṛto veditavyaḥ /
body.translated_text: There, the maturation that is brought about by material gifts, the maturation arising from attraction through supernatural power, the maturation arising from the exposition of secret <s>dharmas</s>, the maturation through gentle practice, and the maturation brought about merely from hearing — this fivefold maturation, even through long-term cultivation of these <s>dharmas</s>, remains only mild, let alone through cultivation for a shorter time. Through all other causes of maturation, however, the threefold method of maturation is to be understood: through mild cultivation, mild maturation; through middling, middling; through intense, intense maturation is to be understood. And of each of these mild, middling, and intense levels of maturation, a threefold method is to be understood: of the mild — mild-mild, mild-middling, mild-intense; of the middling — middling-mild, middling-middling, middling-intense; of the intense — intense-mild, intense-middling, intense-intense. Thus, by the method of progressively further differentiation, the differentiation of maturation of beings accomplished by <s>Buddhas</s> and <s>Bodhisattvas</s> is to be understood as immeasurable.

body.text: tatra bodhisattvaḥ ebhiḥ paripākakāraṇairyathānirdiṣṭairātmanaśca buddhadharmaparipākāyendriyaparipākaṃ kuśalamūlaparipākaṃ jñānaparipākañca mṛdumadhyādhimātrañca samudānayati parasattvānāñca parapudgalānāṃ yānatrayaniryāṇāya /
body.translated_text: There, the <s>Bodhisattva</s>, through these causes of maturation as described, brings about — for the ripening of his own <s>Buddha</s>-qualities — the maturation of faculties, the maturation of roots of virtue, and the maturation of knowledge, in mild, middling, and intense degrees; and [likewise] for the deliverance of other beings and other persons through the three vehicles.

body.text: iti bodhisattvabhūmāvādhāre yogasthāne ṣaṣṭhaṃ paripākapaṭalam //
body.translated_text: Thus, in the <s>Bodhisattvabhūmi</s>, in the Foundation Section of Yoga, the sixth chapter, the <s>Paripāka-paṭala</s> (Chapter on Maturation), is completed. //

body.text: tatra bodhiḥ katamā / samāsato dvividhañca prahāṇaṃ dvividhañca jñānaṃ bodhirityucyate /
body.translated_text: There, what is <s>bodhi</s> (awakening)? In brief, twofold abandonment and twofold knowledge are called <s>bodhi</s>.

body.text: tatra dvividhaṃ prahāṇaṃ-kleśāvaraṇaprahāṇaṃ jñeyāvaraṇaprahāṇañca / dvividhaṃ punarjñānaṃ yat kleśāvaraṇaprahāṇācca nirmalaṃ sarvakleśaniranubandhajñānam / jñeyāvaraṇaprahāṇācca yatsarvasmin jñeye 'pratihatamanāvaraṇaṃ jñānam /
body.translated_text: There, the twofold abandonment is: the abandonment of the obscuration of afflictions (<s>kleśāvaraṇaprahāṇa</s>) and the abandonment of the obscuration of the knowable (<s>jñeyāvaraṇaprahāṇa</s>). The twofold knowledge is: the stainless knowledge of all defilements that results from the abandonment of the obscuration of afflictions — the knowledge unaccompanied by any defilement; and the knowledge that is unimpeded and unobstructed regarding all that is knowable, resulting from the abandonment of the obscuration of the knowable.

body.text: aparaḥ paryāyaḥ / śuddhajñānaṃ sarvajñānamasaṅgajñānañca / sarvakleśavāsanāsamuddhātaścākliṣṭāyāścāvidyāyāḥ niḥśeṣaprahāṇamanuttarā samyaksaṃbodhirityucyate / tatra savāsanānāṃ sarvakleśānāṃ sarvataścātyantañca prahāṇādyad jñānaṃ tacchuddhamityucyate / sarvadhātuṣu sarvavastuṣu sarvaprakāreṣu sarvakāleṣu yadjñānamavyāhataṃ pravartate tatsarvajñānamityucyate / tatra dvau vā dhātū / lokadhātuḥ sattvadhātuśca / tatra dvividhaṃ vastu / saṃskṛtamasaṃskṛtañca / tasyaiva ca saṃkṛtāsaṃskṛtasya vastuno 'pramāṇaḥ prakārabhedaḥ svalakṣaṇottarajātiprabhedena sāmānyalakṣaṇaprabhedena hetuphalaprabhedena dhātugatikuśalākuśalāvyākṛtādiprabhedena / tatra kālastrividhaḥ / atīto 'nāgataḥ pratyutpannaśca / ityetatsarvadhātukaṃ sarvavastukaṃ sarvaprakāraṃ sarvakālaṃ jñānaṃ sarvajñānamityucyate / tatrāsaṅgajñānaṃ yadābhogamātrādeva sarvatrādhiṣṭhitaṃ tvaritamasaktaṃ jñānaṃ pravartate / na punaḥ punarābhogaṃ kurvato nānyatraikābhogapratibaddhameva tajjñānaṃ bhavati /
body.translated_text: Another method [of describing awakening]: Pure knowledge, omniscient knowledge, and unobstructed knowledge. The complete uprooting of the residual impressions (<s>vāsanā</s>) of all defilements, together with the complete abandonment of non-afflictive ignorance (<s>akliṣṭā avidyā</s>) — this is called the unsurpassed perfect awakening (<s>anuttarā samyaksaṃbodhi</s>). There, the knowledge that arises from the complete and thorough abandonment in every way of all defilements together with their residual impressions is called 'pure' (<s>śuddha</s>). The knowledge that operates unimpeded regarding all elements, all objects, all aspects, and all times is called 'omniscient' (<s>sarvajñāna</s>). There, 'two elements' are: the world of [physical] realms (<s>lokadhātu</s>) and the world of beings (<s>sattvadhātu</s>). 'Two objects' are: the conditioned (<s>saṃskṛta</s>) and the unconditioned (<s>asaṃskṛta</s>). And the differentiation of aspects of that conditioned and unconditioned object is immeasurable — through differentiation of individual characteristics, higher genera, and types; through differentiation of general characteristics; through differentiation of cause and effect; through differentiation of elements, destinies, wholesome, unwholesome, indeterminate, and so forth. 'Three times' are: past, future, and present. Thus, this knowledge pertaining to all elements, all objects, all aspects, and all times is called 'omniscient knowledge.' There, 'unobstructed knowledge' (<s>asaṅgajñāna</s>) is that knowledge which, through mere application of attention, operates everywhere as established, swiftly, and without attachment — not requiring repeated application of attention, not being bound to a single application of attention to the exclusion of another.

body.text: aparaḥ paryāyaḥ / catvāriṃśaduttaramāveṇikaṃ buddhadharmaśataṃ yā ca tathāgatasyāraṇā praṇidhijñānaṃ pratisaṃvidaśca / iyamanuttarā samyaksaṃbodhirucyate /
body.translated_text: Another method: One hundred and forty unique <s>Buddha</s>-qualities (<s>āveṇika buddhadharma</s>), together with the <s>Tathāgata</s>'s freedom from conflict (<s>araṇā</s>), the knowledge born of aspiration (<s>praṇidhijñāna</s>), and the analytical knowledges (<s>pratisaṃvid</s>) — this is called the unsurpassed perfect awakening.

body.text: tatredaṃ catvāriṃśaduttaramāveṇikaṃ buddhadharmaśatam / dvātriṃśanmahāpuruṣalakṣaṇānyaśītyanuvyañjanāni catasraḥ sarvākārāḥ pariśuddhayaḥ daśa balāni catvāri vaiśāradyāni trīṃṇi smṛtyupasthānāni trīṇyarakṣyāṇi mahākaruṇā 'sammoṣadharmatā
body.translated_text: Here are the one hundred and forty unique <s>Buddha</s>-qualities: Thirty-two marks of a great being (<s>mahāpuruṣalakṣaṇa</s>), eighty minor marks (<s>anuvyañjana</s>), four kinds of complete purity (<s>sarvākārapariśuddhi</s>), ten powers (<s>bala</s>), four fearlessnesses (<s>vaiśāradya</s>), three foundations of mindfulness (<s>smṛtyupasthāna</s>), three things not requiring guarding (<s>arakṣya</s>), great compassion (<s>mahākaruṇā</s>), the quality of non-forgetting (<s>asammoṣadharmatā</s>),

body.text: vāsanāsamudghātaḥ sarvākāravarajñānañca / eṣāñca buddhadharmāṇāṃ vibhāgaḥ pratiṣṭhāpaṭale bhaviṣyati /
body.translated_text: the uprooting of residual impressions (<s>vāsanāsamudghāta</s>), and the knowledge of all aspects of the supreme (<s>sarvākāravarajñāna</s>). The differentiation of these <s>Buddha</s>-qualities will be [explained] in the <s>Pratiṣṭhā-paṭala</s> (Chapter on Establishment).

body.text: tatreyaṃ paramā bodhiḥ saptabhiḥ paramatābhiryuktā yeneyaṃ sarvabodhīnāṃ parametyucyate /
body.translated_text: There, this supreme awakening (<s>paramā bodhi</s>) is endowed with seven supremacies, by which it is called the supreme of all awakenings.

body.text: sapta paramatāḥ katamāḥ āśrayaparamatā pratipattiparamatā sampattiparamatā jñānaparamatā prabhāvaparamatā prahāṇaparamatā vihāraparamatā ca / yattathāgato dvātriṃśatā mahāpuruṣalakṣaṇaiḥ sulakṣitagātraḥ / iyamasyāśrayaparamatetyucyate / yattathāgata ātmahitāya parahitāya bahujanahitāya [bahujanasukhāya] lokānukampāyai arthāya hitāya sukhāya devamanuṣyāṇāṃ pratipannaḥ / iyamasya pratipattiparamatetyucyate / yattathāgato niruttarābhirapratisamābhiścatasṛbhiḥ saṃpattibhiḥ samanvāgataḥ śīlasaṃpattyā dṛṣṭisaṃpattyā ācārasaṃpattyā ājīvasaṃpattyā [pratipannaḥ] / iayamasya sampattiparamatetyucyate / yattathāgato niruttarābhirapratisamābhiścatasṛbhiḥ pratisaṃvidbhiḥ samanvāgataḥ dharmapratisaṃvidā 'rthapratisaṃvidā niruktipratisaṃvidapratibhānapratisaṃvidā ca / iyamasya jñānaparamatetyucyate / yattathāgato niruttarābhirapratisamābhiḥ ṣaḍbhirabhijñābhiḥ samanvāgataḥ yathā pūrvanirdiṣṭābhiḥ / iyaṃ tathāgatasya prabhāvaparamatetyucyate / yattathāgataḥ savāsanasarvakleśaprahāṇena niruttareṇāpratisamena jñeyāvaraṇa prahāṇena ca samanvāgataḥ / iyamasya prahāṇaparamatetyucyate / yattathāgatastribhirniruttarairapratisamairvihāraistabdahula vihārī āryeṇa vihāreṇa divyena brāhmeṇa / iyamasya vihāraparamatetyucyate / tatra śūnyatānimittāpraṇihitavihārā nirodhasamāpattivihāraścāryo vihāra ityucyate / catvāri dhyānānyārūpyasamāpattayaśca divyo vihāra ityucyate / catvāryapramāṇāni brāhmo vihāra ityucyate / tasmātpunastrividhādvihārāścatvāraḥ paramavihārā yaistathāgatāstadvahulavihāriṇo bhavanti / āryādvihārācchūnyatā vihāro nirodhasamāpattivihāraśca / divyādvihārādāniṃjyacaturthadhyānavihāraḥ / brāhmādvihārātkaruṇāvihāro yena tathāgatastriskṛto rātrau triskṛtvo divase ṣaṭkṛtvo rātriṃdivena buddhacakṣaṣā lokaṃ vyavalokayati ko hīyate
body.translated_text: What are the seven supremacies? Supremacy of basis (<s>āśrayaparamatā</s>), supremacy of practice (<s>pratipattiparamatā</s>), supremacy of attainment (<s>sampattiparamatā</s>), supremacy of knowledge (<s>jñānaparamatā</s>), supremacy of power (<s>prabhāvaparamatā</s>), supremacy of abandonment (<s>prahāṇaparamatā</s>), and supremacy of abiding (<s>vihāraparamatā</s>). That the <s>Tathāgata</s>'s body is well-marked with the thirty-two marks of a great being — this is called his supremacy of basis. That the <s>Tathāgata</s> has practiced for his own benefit, for the benefit of others, for the benefit of many, [for the happiness of many,] out of compassion for the world, for the sake, benefit, and happiness of gods and humans — this is called his supremacy of practice. That the <s>Tathāgata</s> is endowed with four unsurpassed, unequaled attainments — attainment of moral conduct (<s>śīlasaṃpatti</s>), attainment of view (<s>dṛṣṭisaṃpatti</s>), attainment of conduct (<s>ācārasaṃpatti</s>), and attainment of livelihood (<s>ājīvasaṃpatti</s>) — this is called his supremacy of attainment. That the <s>Tathāgata</s> is endowed with four unsurpassed, unequaled analytical knowledges — analytical knowledge of <s>dharmas</s> (<s>dharmapratisaṃvid</s>), of meaning (<s>arthapratisaṃvid</s>), of etymology (<s>niruktipratisaṃvid</s>), and of eloquence (<s>pratibhānapratisaṃvid</s>) — this is called his supremacy of knowledge. That the <s>Tathāgata</s> is endowed with six unsurpassed, unequaled supernatural knowledges (<s>abhijñā</s>) as previously described — this is called the <s>Tathāgata</s>'s supremacy of power. That the <s>Tathāgata</s> is endowed with the unsurpassed, unequaled abandonment of all defilements together with their residual impressions and the abandonment of the obscuration of the knowable — this is called his supremacy of abandonment. That the <s>Tathāgata</s> predominantly abides in three unsurpassed, unequaled modes of abiding — the noble abiding (<s>ārya vihāra</s>), the divine abiding (<s>divya vihāra</s>), and the <s>Brahma</s>-abiding (<s>brāhma vihāra</s>) — this is called his supremacy of abiding. There, the abidings in emptiness (<s>śūnyatā</s>), signlessness (<s>ānimitta</s>), and wishlessness (<s>apraṇihita</s>), and the abiding in the attainment of cessation (<s>nirodhasamāpatti</s>) — these are called the noble abiding. The four <s>dhyānas</s> (meditations) and the formless attainments — these are called the divine abiding. The four immeasurables (<s>apramāṇa</s>) — these are called the <s>Brahma</s>-abiding. Therefore, from these three modes of abiding, four supreme abidings arise in which the <s>Tathāgatas</s> predominantly dwell: From the noble abiding — the emptiness-abiding and the cessation-attainment-abiding. From the divine abiding — the abiding in the imperturbable fourth <s>dhyāna</s>. From the <s>Brahma</s>-abiding — the compassion-abiding, by which the <s>Tathāgata</s>, three times during the night and three times during the day — six times in a day and night — surveys the world with the <s>Buddha</s>-eye: 'Who is declining?

body.text: ko vardhate kasyānutpannāni kuśalamūlānyavaropayāmi kvaṃ yāvadvistareṇāgraphale 'rhattve pratiṣṭhāpayāmīti /
body.translated_text: Who is progressing? In whom shall I plant unarisen roots of virtue? Whom shall I establish in the supreme fruit, in <s>Arhatship</s>?' — and so on in detail.

body.text: tatrāśrayaparamatayā tathāgatā mahāpuruṣā ityucyante / pratipattiparamatayā mahākāruṇikā ityucyante / saṃpattiparamatayā mahāśīlamahādharmāṇa ityucyante / jñānaparamatayā mahāprajñā ityucyante / prabhāvaparamatayā mahābhijñā ityucyante / prahāṇaparamatayā mahāvimuktaya ityucyante / vihāraparamatayā mahāvihāratad bahulavihāriṇa ityucyante /
body.translated_text: There, by the supremacy of basis, <s>Tathāgatas</s> are called 'great beings.' By the supremacy of practice, they are called 'greatly compassionate.' By the supremacy of attainment, they are called 'of great moral conduct and great <s>dharmas</s>.' By the supremacy of knowledge, they are called 'of great wisdom.' By the supremacy of power, they are called 'of great supernatural knowledge.' By the supremacy of abandonment, they are called 'of great liberation.' By the supremacy of abiding, they are called 'ones who predominantly dwell in the great abidings.'

body.text: teṣāñca punastathāgatānāṃ daśabhirākārairguṇābhidhānañca bhavati guṇānusmaraṇatā ca / katamairdaśabhiḥ / ityapi sa bhagavāṃstathāgato 'rhansamyaksaṃbuddho vidyācaraṇasaṃpannaḥ sugato lokavidanuttaraḥ puruṣadamyasārathiḥ śāstā devamanuṣyāṇāṃ buddho bhagavāniti / tatrāvitathavacanāttathāgataḥ / sarvaprāptayārthaprāptatvāt anuttarapuṇyakṣetratvāt pūjārhatvāccārhan / yathāvatparamārthena dharmānubodhātsamyaksaṃbuddhaḥ / tisṛbhirvidyābhiryathāsūtroktena ca caraṇena vipaśyanāśamathapakṣobhayasusampannatvādvidyācaraṇasampannaḥ / paramotkarṣagamanādapunaḥ pratyāgamanācca sugataḥ / sattvadhātulokadhātvoḥ sarvākāreṇa kleśavyavadānajñānāllokavit / paramacittadamopāyajñatayā ekasyaiva loke puruṣabhūtasya ca prādurbhāvāt anuttaraḥ puruṣadamyasārathiḥ / cakṣurbhūtatvājjñānārthadharmatattva bhūtatvād vyaktasyārthasya nirṇetṛtvāt sarvārthapratisaraṇatvādavyutpannasyārthasya vyutpādakatvā dutpannasya saṃśayasyocchedakatvāt gambhīrāṇāṃ sthānānāṃ vivaraṇāt paryavadāpakatvāttanmūlatvāt sarvadharmāṇāṃ tannetṛkatvāttatpratisaraṇatvāt sarvaduḥkhasya niḥsaraṇaṃ śāsti vyapadiśati samyagdevamanuṣyāṇām / tasmācchāstā devamanuṣyāṇāmityucyate / arthopasaṃhitasya dharmarāśeranarthopasaṃhitasya dharmarāśernnaivārthopasaṃhitasya nānārthopasaṃhitasya dharmarāśeḥ sakalasarvākārābhisaṃbodhād buddha ityucyate / sarvamārabalamahāsaṃgrāmāvabhaṅgādbhagavān /
body.translated_text: And the qualities of those <s>Tathāgatas</s> are designated and recollected through ten aspects. Through which ten? 'Thus indeed is that <s>Bhagavān</s> — a <s>Tathāgata</s>, an <s>Arhat</s>, a <s>Samyaksaṃbuddha</s> (Perfectly Awakened One), endowed with knowledge and conduct (<s>vidyācaraṇasaṃpanna</s>), a <s>Sugata</s> (Well-gone One), a Knower of the World (<s>lokavid</s>), Unsurpassed (<s>anuttara</s>), Tamer of Men (<s>puruṣadamyasārathi</s>), Teacher of Gods and Humans (<s>śāstā devamanuṣyāṇām</s>), a <s>Buddha</s>, a <s>Bhagavān</s>.' There: Because of speaking without falsehood — '<s>Tathāgata</s>' (Thus-gone). Because of having attained all attainments, because of being an unsurpassed field of merit, and because of being worthy of worship — '<s>Arhat</s>.' Because of awakening to <s>dharmas</s> correctly as they truly are in the ultimate sense — '<s>Samyaksaṃbuddha</s>.' Because of being well-endowed on both sides — insight (<s>vipaśyanā</s>) and tranquility (<s>śamatha</s>) — through the three knowledges (<s>vidyā</s>) and the conduct as stated in the <s>sūtras</s> — 'Endowed with knowledge and conduct.' Because of having gone to the supreme height and not returning — '<s>Sugata</s>.' Because of knowing in every way the world of beings and the world of [physical] realms, through the knowledge of defilement and purification — 'Knower of the World.' Because of being supreme in the skill of the means for taming the minds [of beings], and because of manifesting as one who is a 'man' (<s>puruṣa</s>) uniquely in the world — 'Unsurpassed Tamer of Men.' Because of being an eye [of wisdom], because of being the reality of knowledge, meaning, and <s>dharma</s>, because of being the arbiter of manifest meaning, because of being the refuge for all purposes, because of explaining the unexplained, because of cutting off doubt that has arisen, because of illuminating profound matters, because of purifying, because all <s>dharmas</s> are rooted in him, because of being their guide and refuge — he instructs and proclaims the way out of all suffering correctly to gods and humans. Therefore he is called 'Teacher of Gods and Humans.' Because of complete awakening in all aspects to the mass of <s>dharmas</s> connected with benefit, the mass of <s>dharmas</s> connected with non-benefit, and the mass of <s>dharmas</s> connected with neither benefit nor non-benefit — he is called '<s>Buddha</s>.' Because of breaking apart the great army and power of all <s>Māras</s> — '<s>Bhagavān</s>.'

body.text: tatra prabhūtairapi kalpairekasyāpi buddhasya prādurbhāvo na bhavati / ekasminneva ca kalpe prabhūtānāṃ buddhānāmutpādo bhavati / teṣu teṣu ca daśasu dikṣvaprameyāsaṃkhyeyeṣu lokadhātuṣvaprameyāṇāmeva buddhānāmutpādo veditavyaḥ / tatkasya hetoḥ / santi daśasu dikṣvaprameyāsaṃkhyeyā bodhisattvā ye tulyakālakṛtapraṇidhānāstulyasaṃbhārasamudāgatāśca / yasminneva divase pakṣe māse saṃvatsare ekena bodhisattvena bodhau cittaṃ praṇihitaṃ tasminneva divase pakṣe māse saṃvatsare sarvaiḥ / yathā caika utsahito ghaṭito vyāyacchitaśca tathā sarve / tathāhi dṛśyante 'sminneva lokadhātāvanekāni bodhisattvaśatāni yāni tulyakālapraṇidhānāni tulyatyāgāni tulyakṣāntikāni tulyavīryāṇi tulyadhyānāni tulyaprajñānāni / prāgeva daśasu dikṣvanantāparyanteṣu lokadhātuṣu / buddhakṣetrāṇyapi trisāhasramahāsāhasrāṇyaprameyāsaṃkhyeyāni daśasu dikṣu saṃvidyante / na ca tulyasaṃbhārasamudāgatayordvayostāvadbodhisattvayorekasmin lokadhātau buddhakṣetre yugapadutpattyavakāśo 'sti prāgevāprameyāsaṃkhyeyānām / na ca punastulyasaṃbhārāṇāṃ krameṇānuparipāṭikayā utpādoyujyate / nāpi sarveṇa sarvamanutpāda eva yujyate / tasmāddaśasu dikṣvaprameyāsaṃkhyeyeṣu lokadhātuṣu yathā pariśodhiteṣu tathāgataśūnyeṣu te tulyasaṃbhārā bodhisattvā anyonyeṣu buddhakṣetreṣūtpadyanta iti veditavyam / tadanena paryāyeṇa bahuṣu lokadhātuṣu buddhabāhulyameva yujyate / na caikasmin buddhakṣetre dvayostathāgatayoryugapadutpādo bhavati / tatkasya hetoḥ / dīrgharātraṃ khalu bodhisattvenaivaṃ praṇidhānamanubṛṃhitaṃ bhavati / yathāhameko 'pariṇāyake loke pariṇāyakaḥ syāṃ sattvānāṃ vinetā sarvaduḥkhebhyo vimocayitā parinirvāpayiteti / yasyaivaṃ dīrgharātraṃ praṇidhānamanubṛṃhayataḥ samyak pratipattiparigṛhītamṛdhyatyeva tat / punaśca śakta ekastathāgatastrisāhasramahāsāhasre ekasmin buddhakṣetre sarvabuddhakārya kartum / ato dvitīyasya tathāgatasya vyartha evotpādaḥ syāt / bhūyaścaikasya tathāgatasya loke utpādātsattvānām evārthakaraṇaprasiddhiḥ pracuratarā bhavati pradakṣiṇatarā / tatkasya hetoḥ / teṣāmevaṃ bhavatyayameva kṛtsne jagatyekastathāgato na dvitīyaḥ / asmiñjanapadacārikāṃ vā viprakānte parinirvṛte vā nāsti sa kaścid dvitīyaḥ /
body.translated_text: There, even in many <s>kalpas</s> (cosmic ages), the appearance of even a single <s>Buddha</s> may not occur. And in a single <s>kalpa</s>, the arising of many <s>Buddhas</s> occurs. In the various immeasurable and innumerable world-systems in the ten directions, the arising of immeasurable <s>Buddhas</s> should be understood. For what reason? There exist in the ten directions immeasurable and innumerable <s>Bodhisattvas</s> who have made their vows at the same time and have accumulated equal provisions. On the very day, fortnight, month, and year in which one <s>Bodhisattva</s> directed his mind toward awakening, on that very day, fortnight, month, and year, all [others did likewise]. Just as one was enthusiastic, diligent, and exerted himself, so too were all. For indeed, in this very world-system, many hundreds of <s>Bodhisattvas</s> are seen who have equal vows, equal renunciation, equal patience, equal vigor, equal meditation, and equal wisdom—how much more so in the infinite and boundless world-systems in the ten directions! <s>Buddha</s>-fields that are three-thousandfold great-thousandfold [world-systems] exist in immeasurable and innumerable numbers in the ten directions. There is no occasion for even two <s>Bodhisattvas</s> of equally accumulated provisions to arise simultaneously in a single world-system or <s>Buddha</s>-field—much less for immeasurable and innumerable ones. Nor is it fitting for those of equal provisions to arise in sequence one after another. Nor is it fitting for there to be no arising at all. Therefore, it should be understood that those <s>Bodhisattvas</s> of equal provisions arise in each other's <s>Buddha</s>-fields in the immeasurable and innumerable world-systems in the ten directions that have been purified accordingly and are empty of a <s>Tathāgata</s>. By this method, the abundance of <s>Buddhas</s> in many world-systems is indeed fitting, yet the simultaneous arising of two <s>Tathāgatas</s> in a single <s>Buddha</s>-field does not occur. For what reason? For a long time, the <s>Bodhisattva</s>'s vow has been nurtured thus: 'May I alone be the guide in a world without a guide, the trainer of beings, the liberator from all suffering, the one who leads them to <s>parinirvāṇa</s>.' For one who has thus nurtured the vow for a long time, that vow, embraced by correct practice, is indeed fulfilled. Furthermore, a single <s>Tathāgata</s> is capable of accomplishing all <s>Buddha</s>-activities in a single <s>Buddha</s>-field of a three-thousandfold great-thousandfold [world-system]. Therefore, the arising of a second <s>Tathāgata</s> would be purposeless. Moreover, from the arising of a single <s>Tathāgata</s> in the world, the accomplishment of the welfare of beings becomes more abundant and more auspicious. For what reason? For them the thought arises thus: 'This <s>Tathāgata</s> alone is the one in the entire world, there is no second. When he is traveling in the countryside or has passed into <s>parinirvāṇa</s>, there is no second

body.text: yasyāsmābhirantike brahmacaryaṃ caritavyaṃ syāt dharmo vā śrotavya iti viditvā 'titvarante ghanatareṇa chandavyāyāmena brahmacaryavāsāya saddharmaśravaṇāya ca / buddhabahutvaṃtu te upalabhya nātitvareran / evameṣāmekasya buddhasyotpādātsvārthe karaṇaprasiddhiḥ pracuratarā ca bhavati pradakṣiṇatarā ca /
body.translated_text: in whose presence we might practice the holy life or hear the <s>Dharma</s>'—knowing this, they hasten with denser zeal and exertion toward dwelling in the holy life and hearing the true <s>Dharma</s>. But if they perceived many <s>Buddhas</s>, they would not hasten so. Thus, from the arising of a single <s>Buddha</s>, the accomplishment of their own welfare becomes more abundant and more auspicious.
