body.text: tatra sarvabuddhānāṃ sarvaṃ samasamaṃ bhavati nirviśiṣṭaṃ sthāpayitvā catvāri sthānāni-āyurnāma kulaṃ kāyañca / ityeṣāñcaturṇāṃ dharmāṇāṃ hrāsavṛddhyā vilakṣaṇatā buddhānām / na tvanyena kenacit / na ca strī anuttarāṃ samyaksaṃbodhimasaṃbudhyate / tatkasya hetoḥ / tathā hi bodhisattvaḥ prathamasyaiva kalpāsaṃkhyeyasyātyayāt / strībhāvaṃ vijahāti / bodhimaṇḍaniṣadanamupādāya na punarjātu strī bhavati / prakṛtyā ca bahukleśo duṣprajñaśca bhavati sarvo mātṛgrāmaḥ / na ca prakṛtyā bahukleśasantānena duṣprajñasantānena ca śakyamanuttarāṃ samyaksaṃbodhimabhisaṃboddhum /
body.translated_text: There, everything is equal and undifferentiated for all <s>Buddhas</s>, except for four matters—lifespan (<s>āyus</s>), name (<s>nāma</s>), family (<s>kula</s>), and body (<s>kāya</s>). By the decrease and increase of these four <s>dharmas</s>, there is variation among <s>Buddhas</s>, but not by anything else. And a woman does not fully awaken to the unsurpassed, perfect awakening (<s>anuttarā samyaksaṃbodhi</s>). For what reason? For indeed, the <s>Bodhisattva</s>, after the passing of the first incalculable <s>kalpa</s> (<s>kalpāsaṃkhyeya</s>), abandons the female state. From sitting on the seat of awakening (<s>bodhimaṇḍa</s>) onward, one never again becomes a woman. And by nature, the entire female sex is afflicted with many defilements and of poor wisdom. And it is not possible for one whose mind-stream is by nature afflicted with many defilements and of poor wisdom to fully awaken to the unsurpassed, perfect awakening.

body.text: evamiyamanuttarā samyaksaṃbodhiḥ svabhāvato 'pi yathānirdiṣṭā yathābhūtaṃ veditavyā / paramato 'pi guṇanirdeśānusmaraṇato 'pi saṃbhavato 'pi viśeṣato 'pi yathānirdiṣṭā yathābhūtaṃ veditavyā / api tvacintyaiva sarvatarkamārgasamatikrāntatvādaprameyāsaṃkhyeyaguṇasamuditatvādanuttaraiva ca samyaksaṃbodhiḥ sarvaśrāvaka-pratyekabuddhatathāgatānābhi nirvṛttaye bhavati / tasmādeṣaiva bodhiragryā śreṣṭhā varā praṇīteti /
body.translated_text: Thus, this unsurpassed, perfect awakening should be understood as it truly is, as described, both in terms of its own nature, in terms of its supreme [status], in terms of the recollection of its description of qualities, in terms of its arising, and in terms of its distinctive features. Moreover, it is inconceivable, because it transcends all paths of reasoning, because it is endowed with immeasurable and innumerable qualities, and because the unsurpassed, perfect awakening alone exists for the final liberation of all <s>Śrāvakas</s>, <s>Pratyekabuddhas</s>, and <s>Tathāgatas</s>. Therefore, this awakening alone is the highest, most excellent, supreme, and exalted.

body.text: iti bodhisattvabhūmāvādhāre yogasthāne saptamaṃ bodhipaṭalam /
body.translated_text: Thus, in the <s>Bodhisattvabhūmi</s>, in the Foundation Section of Yoga, the seventh chapter, the <s>Bodhi-paṭala</s> (Chapter on Awakening), [is completed].

body.text: nirdiṣṭaṃ tāvadyatra bodhisattvena śikṣitavyam / yathā punaḥ śikṣitavyaṃ tadvakṣyāmi /
body.translated_text: Thus far, that in which the <s>Bodhisattva</s> should train has been described. Now I shall explain how one should train.

body.text: uddānam /
body.translated_text: Summary verse (<s>uddāna</s>):

body.text:
adhimukterbahulatā dharmaparyeṣṭideśanā /
pratipattistathā samyagavavādānuśāsanam /
upāyasahitaṃ kāyavāṅmanaḥkarma paścimam /
body.translated_text: Abundance of devotion, seeking the <s>Dharma</s>, teaching, practice likewise, correct instruction and guidance, and lastly, action of body, speech, and mind accompanied by skillful means.

body.text: ihādita eva bodhisattvena bodhisattvaśikṣāsu śikṣitukāmenādhimuktibahulena bhavitavyaṃ dharmeparyeṣakeṇa dharmadeśakena dharmānudharmapratipannena samyagavavādānuśāsakena samyagavavādānuśāsanyāñca sthitena upāyaparigṛhītakāyavāṅmanaḥkarmaṇā ca bhavitavyam /
body.translated_text: Here, from the very beginning, the <s>Bodhisattva</s> who desires to train in the <s>Bodhisattva</s>-trainings should be one of abundant devotion (<s>adhimukti</s>), a seeker of the <s>Dharma</s>, a teacher of the <s>Dharma</s>, one who practices in accordance with the <s>Dharma</s> (<s>dharmānudharmapratianna</s>), one who correctly instructs and guides, one who abides in correct instruction and guidance, and one whose actions of body, speech, and mind are embraced by skillful means (<s>upāya</s>).

body.text: kathañca bodhisattvo 'dhimuktibahulo bhavati / iha bodhisattvo 'ṣṭavidhe 'dhimuktyadhiṣṭhāne śraddhāprasādapūrvaṃkeṇa niścayena rucyā samanvāgato bhavati / triṣu ratneṣu buddhadharmaṃsaṃghaguṇeṣu buddhabodhisattvaprabhāve ca yathānirdiṣṭe tattvārthe ca yathānirdiṣṭe hetau ca phale ca vicitre yathāyogapatite aviparīte prāptavye cārthe samartho 'haṃ prāptumiti / yathā prāptavye arthe evaṃ prāptyupāye astyayaṃ prāptyupāyaḥ prāptavyasyārthasyeti / tatra prāptavyo 'yathā bodhiranuttarā / prāptyupāyaḥ punaḥ sarve bodhisattvaśikṣāmārgāḥ / tathā subhāṣite sulapite supravyāhṛte 'dhimuktistadyathā sūtraṃ geyaṃ vyākaraṇādiṣu dharmeṣu /
body.translated_text: And how does the <s>Bodhisattva</s> become one of abundant devotion? Here, the <s>Bodhisattva</s> is endowed with certainty preceded by faith and serene confidence (<s>śraddhāprasāda</s>) and delight in eight bases of devotion (<s>adhimuktyādhiṣṭhāna</s>): in the Three Jewels—the qualities of the <s>Buddha</s>, the <s>Dharma</s>, and the <s>Saṃgha</s>; in the power of <s>Buddhas</s> and <s>Bodhisattvas</s>; in the meaning of reality as described; in cause and result—variously, as appropriately pertaining, and without error; in the goal to be attained, [thinking:] 'I am capable of attaining it'; and just as in the goal to be attained, so in the means of attainment, [thinking:] 'This means of attainment of the goal to be attained exists.' There, the goal to be attained is the unsurpassed awakening (<s>bodhi</s>). The means of attainment, moreover, are all the paths of the <s>Bodhisattva</s>-trainings. Likewise, devotion to what is well-spoken, well-set-forth, and well-proclaimed—namely, in <s>dharmas</s> such as <s>sūtras</s>, <s>geyas</s>, <s>vyākaraṇas</s>, and so forth.

body.text: tatrāsminnaṣṭavidhe 'dhimuktyādhiṣṭhāne bodhisattvasya dvābhyāṃ kāraṇābhyāmadhimuktibahulatā veditavyā / adhimuktyabhyāsabahulīkārataśca tīvrakṣāntisanniveśataśca /
body.translated_text: There, in these eight bases of devotion, the <s>Bodhisattva</s>'s abundance of devotion should be understood by two reasons: by the repeated cultivation and abundance of devotion, and by the implanting of intense patience (<s>tīvrakṣānti</s>).

body.text: tatra dharmaṃ bodhisattvaḥ paryeṣamāṇaḥ kiṃ paryeṣate / kathaṃ paryeṣate / kimarthaṃ
body.translated_text: There, what does the <s>Bodhisattva</s> seek when seeking the <s>Dharma</s>? How does he seek? For what purpose

body.text: paryeṣate / samāsato bodhisattvo bodhisattvapiṭakañca paryeṣate śrāvakapiṭakañca / vāhyakāni ca śāstrāṇi laukikāni ca śilpakarmapasthānāni paryeṣate /
body.translated_text: does he seek? In brief, the <s>Bodhisattva</s> seeks both the <s>Bodhisattvapiṭaka</s> (collection of <s>Bodhisattva</s> [scriptures]) and the <s>Śrāvakapiṭaka</s> (collection of disciple [scriptures]). He also seeks the external treatises (<s>bāhyaśāstra</s>) and the mundane arts and crafts (<s>śilpakarmasthāna</s>).

body.text: tatra dvādaśāṅgādvacogatādyadvaipulyaṃ tadvodhisattvapiṭakam / avaśiṣṭaṃ śrāvakapiṭakaṃ veditavyam / bāhyakāni punaḥ śāstrāṇi samāsatastrīṇi / hetuśāstraṃ śabdaśāstraṃ cikitsaka śāstrañca / tatra laukikāni śilpakarmasthānānyanekavidhāni bahunānāprakārāṇi / suvarṇakārāyaskāramaṇikārakarmajñānaprabhṛtīni / tānyetāni sarvavidyāsthānaparigṛhītāni pañcavidyāsthānāni bhavanti / adhyātmavidyā hetuvidyā śabdavidyā vyādhicikitsāvidyā śilpakarmasthānavidyā ca / itīmāni pañca vidyāsthānāni yāni bodhisattvaḥ paryeṣate / evamanena sarvavidyāsthānāni paryeṣitāni bhavanti /
body.translated_text: There, from the twelvefold word of the <s>Buddha</s>, the <s>Vaipulya</s> (extensive teachings) is the <s>Bodhisattvapiṭaka</s>. The remainder should be understood as the <s>Śrāvakapiṭaka</s>. The external treatises, moreover, are in brief threefold: the science of reasoning (<s>hetuśāstra</s>), the science of grammar (<s>śabdaśāstra</s>), and the science of medicine (<s>cikitsāśāstra</s>). There, the mundane arts and crafts are of many and various kinds—knowledge of goldsmithery, ironworking, gem-cutting, and the like. All these are comprised in the five fields of knowledge (<s>pañca vidyāsthāna</s>): the inner science (<s>adhyātmavidyā</s>), the science of reasoning (<s>hetuvidyā</s>), the science of grammar (<s>śabdavidyā</s>), the science of medicine (<s>cikitsāvidyā</s>), and the science of arts and crafts (<s>śilpakarmasthānavidyā</s>). These are the five fields of knowledge that the <s>Bodhisattva</s> seeks. Thus, all fields of knowledge have been sought by him.

body.text:
tatra buddhavacanamadhyātmaśāstramityucyate / tatpunaḥ katyākāraṃ pravartate / evaṃ yāvallaukikāni śilpakarmasthānāni katyākārāṇi pravartante / buddhavacanaṃ samāsato dvyākāraṃ pravartate / samyaghetuphalaparidīpanākāraṃ kṛtāviprahāṇā kṛtānabhyāgamaparidīpanākārañca / hetuśāstramapi dvyākāram / paropāraṃbhakathānuśaṃsaparidīpanākāraṃ parataścetivādavipramokṣānuśaṃsaparidīpanākārañca / śabdaśāstramapi dvyā kāram / dhāturūpasādhanavyavasthānaparidīpanākāraṃ vāksaṃskārānuśaṃsaparidīpanākārañca / cikitsāśāstrañcaturākāraṃ pravartate / āvādhakośalaparidīpanākaram / āvādhasamutthānakauśalaparidīpanākāram / utpannasyāvādhasya prahāṇakauśalaparidīpanākāram / prahāṇasya cāvādhasyāyatyāmanutpādakauśalaparidīpanākāram / laukikāni śilpakarmasthānajñānāni
svakasvakaśilpakarmasthānānuṣṭhānakāryapariniṣpattiparidīpanākārāṇi /
body.translated_text: There, the word of the <s>Buddha</s> is called the inner science (<s>adhyātmaśāstra</s>). In how many aspects does it operate? Likewise, in how many aspects do the mundane arts and crafts operate? The word of the <s>Buddha</s>, in brief, operates in two aspects: in the aspect of the correct illumination of cause and result, and in the aspect of illuminating the non-loss of what has been done and the non-arrival of what has not been done. The science of reasoning also operates in two aspects: in the aspect of illuminating the benefit of countering others' arguments, and in the aspect of illuminating the benefit of liberating oneself from others' opposing doctrines. The science of grammar also operates in two aspects: in the aspect of illuminating the establishment of roots, forms, and derivations, and in the aspect of illuminating the benefit of the refinement of speech. The science of medicine operates in four aspects: in the aspect of illuminating skill in diseases; in the aspect of illuminating skill in the origin of diseases; in the aspect of illuminating skill in the elimination of diseases that have arisen; and in the aspect of illuminating skill in the non-arising in the future of diseases that have been eliminated. The mundane arts and crafts operate in the aspect of illuminating the accomplishment of the purpose of practicing each respective art and craft.

body.text: kathañca buddhavacanamaviparītaṃ hetuphalaṃ paridīpayati / daśeme hetavaḥ aviparītaṃ hetuvyavasthānaṃ sarvahetusaṃgrahe veditavyāḥ saṃkleśāya vā vyavadānāya vā laukināmapi ca teṣāṃ sasyādīnāmavyākṛtānāṃ pravṛttaye / daśa hetavaḥ
body.translated_text: And how does the word of the <s>Buddha</s> illuminate cause and result without error? These ten causes should be understood as the correct establishment of causes, comprising all causes, whether for defilement or purification of worldly beings, and also for the operation of neutral [phenomena] such as crops and the like. The ten causes

body.text: katame / anuvyavahārahetuḥ / apekṣāhetuḥ / ākṣepahetuḥ / parigrahahetuḥ / abhinirvṛttihetuḥ / āvāhakahetuḥ pratiniyamahetuḥ / sahakārihetuḥ virodhahetuḥ / avirodhahetuśca /
body.translated_text: are: the conventional-usage cause (<s>anuvyavahārahetu</s>), the dependence cause (<s>apekṣāhetu</s>), the projecting cause (<s>ākṣepahetu</s>), the encompassing cause (<s>parigrahahetu</s>), the producing cause (<s>abhinirvṛttihetu</s>), the bringing-about cause (<s>āvāhakahetu</s>), the determining cause (<s>pratiniyamahetu</s>), the co-operating cause (<s>sahakārihetu</s>), the opposing cause (<s>virodhahetu</s>), and the non-opposing cause (<s>avirodhahetu</s>).

body.text: tatra sarvadharmāṇāṃ yannāma nāmapūrvikā ca saṃjñā saṃjñāpūrvakaścābhilāpaḥ / ayamucyate teṣāṃ dharmāṇāmanuvyavahārahetuḥ / tatra yadapekṣaṃ yaddhetukaṃ yasmin vastunyarthitvamupādānañca bhavatyayamasyocyate 'pekṣāhetuḥ / tadyathā hastāpekṣaṃ hastahetukamādānakarma / pādāpekṣaṃ pādahetukamabhikramapratikramakarma / parvāpekṣaṃ parvahetukaṃ samiñjitaprasāritakarma / jighatsāpipāsāpekṣaṃ jighatsāpipāsāhetukaṃ bhojanapānādānaṃ paryeṣaṇatā ca / ityevaṃbhāgīyo 'pramāṇa-nayānugataḥ apekṣāheturveditavyaḥ / tatra bījamāvasānikasya svaphalasyākṣepahetuḥ / bījanirmuktaḥ tadanyaḥ pratyayaḥ parigrahahetuḥ / tadeva bījaṃ svaphalasya nirvṛttihetuḥ / tatpunarbījanirvṛttaṃ phalamuttarasya bījākṣiptasya phalasyāvāhakahetuḥ nānāvijātīya-vibhinnakāraṇatvaṃ pratiniyamahetuḥ / yaścāpekṣāhetuḥ yaścākṣepahetuḥ yaśca parigrahaheturyaśca nirvṛttiheturyaścāvāhakaheturyaśca pratiniyamaheturityetān sarvān hetūn ekadhyamabhisaṃkṣipya sahakāriheturityucyate / utpattāvāntarāyiko hetuvirodhahetuḥ / antarāyavaikalyamavirodhahetuḥ /
body.translated_text: There, the conventional-usage cause of all <s>dharmas</s> is their name, the designation preceded by name, and the verbal expression preceded by designation. This is called the conventional-usage cause of those <s>dharmas</s>. There, the dependence cause is that in dependence on which, caused by which, and with respect to which thing there is desire and grasping. For example: the action of taking is dependent on and caused by the hand; the action of walking forward and backward is dependent on and caused by the feet; the action of bending and stretching is dependent on and caused by the joints; the seeking and taking of food and drink is dependent on and caused by hunger and thirst. Such, following an immeasurable method, should be understood as the dependence cause. There, the seed is the projecting cause of its own ultimate fruit. The other conditions apart from the seed are the encompassing cause. That very seed is the producing cause of its own fruit. That fruit produced from the seed, moreover, is the bringing-about cause of the subsequent fruit projected by the seed. The differentiation of cause by different species is the determining cause. The projecting cause, the dependence cause, the encompassing cause, the producing cause, the bringing-about cause, and the determining cause—gathering all these causes together into one is called the co-operating cause. The cause that obstructs arising is the opposing cause. The absence of obstruction is the non-opposing cause.

body.text: tatra virodhaḥ samāsataḥ ṣaḍvidhaḥ / vāgvirodhaḥ / tadyathā śāsrāṇi pūrvāparaviruddhāni bhavanti tadekatyānāṃ śramaṇabrāhmaṇānām yuktivirodhaḥ / sādhyasya jñeyasyārthasya sādhanāyopapattisādhanayuktirayujyamānā bhavati / utpativirodhaḥ / tadyathā utpatti pratyayavaikalpādutpattyāntarāyikadharmasānnidhyāccopattirna bhavati / sahavasthāna virodhaḥ / tadyathā ālokatamaso rāgadveṣayoḥ sukhaduḥkhayoḥ / vipratyanīkavirodhaḥ / tadyathā ahinakulayormārjāramūṣikayoranyonyapratyarthikayośca pratyamitrayoḥ / vipakṣaprātipakṣikaśca virodhaḥ / tadyathā 'śubhabhāvanā-kāmarāgayoḥ maitrībhāvanā-vyāpādayoḥ karuṇābhāvanāvihiṃsayoḥ bodhyaṅgāryāṣṭāṅgamārgabhāvanāyāḥ sarvakleśānāñca traidhātukāvacarāṇām asmiṃstvarthe utpattivirodha evābhipretaḥ /
body.translated_text: Therein, contradiction (<s>virodha</s>) is, in brief, sixfold. Verbal contradiction—for example, when the teachings of certain ascetics and brahmins are mutually contradictory. Logical contradiction—when the reasoning and proof for establishing the knowable object to be proven is unfitting. Origination-contradiction—for example, when origination does not occur due to deficiency of the conditions of origination or due to the presence of factors obstructing origination. Co-existence contradiction—for example, between light and darkness, between desire and hatred, between pleasure and pain. Antagonistic contradiction—for example, between a snake and a mongoose, between a cat and a mouse, and between mutual adversaries and enemies. And the contradiction of the opposing and its antidote—for example, between the cultivation of the unattractive (<s>aśubhabhāvanā</s>) and sensual desire, between the cultivation of loving-kindness (<s>maitrībhāvanā</s>) and malice, between the cultivation of compassion (<s>karuṇābhāvanā</s>) and harmfulness, between the cultivation of the factors of awakening (<s>bodhyaṅga</s>) and the noble eightfold path and all afflictions pertaining to the three realms. In this [last] case, origination-contradiction is what is intended.

body.text: punaḥ sarveṣāmeṣāṃ hetūnāṃ dvābhyāṃ hetubhyāṃ saṃgrahaḥ / janakena ca hetunā
body.translated_text: Furthermore, all these causes are encompassed by two causes: the generative cause (<s>janakahetu</s>)—

body.text: upāyahetunā ca / yadākṣepakaṃ nirvartakañca bījaṃ tajjanako hetuḥ / avaśiṣṭā hetava upāyaheturveditavyaḥ /
body.translated_text: and the instrumental cause (<s>upāyahetu</s>). That seed which attracts and produces is the generative cause. The remaining causes are to be known as the instrumental cause.

body.text: catvāraḥ pratyayāḥ hetupratyayaḥ samanantarapratyayaḥ ālambanapratyayaḥ adhipatipratyayaśca / tatra yo janako hetuḥ saḥ hetupratyayaḥ / yaḥ punarupāyahetuḥ so 'dhipatipratyayo veditavyaḥ / samanantarapratyayaścālambanapratyayaśca cittacaitasikānāmeva dharmāṇām / tathā hi cittacaitasikā dharmāḥ prāgutpannāvakāśadānaparigṛhītā ālambanaparigṛhītāśca prādurbhavanti pravartante ca / tasmātsamanantarapratyaya ālambanapratyayaśca parigrahahetunā saṃgṛhītau veditavyau /
body.translated_text: There are four conditions (<s>pratyaya</s>): the cause-condition (<s>hetupratyaya</s>), the immediately preceding condition (<s>samanantarapratyaya</s>), the object-condition (<s>ālambanapratyaya</s>), and the dominant condition (<s>adhipatipratyaya</s>). Therein, the generative cause is the cause-condition. The instrumental cause is to be known as the dominant condition. The immediately preceding condition and the object-condition pertain only to mental (<s>citta</s>) and mental-associate (<s>caitasika</s>) <s>dharmas</s>. For mental and mental-associate <s>dharmas</s> arise and operate having been encompassed by the giving of opportunity by previously arisen [mental states] and having been encompassed by an object. Therefore, the immediately preceding condition and the object-condition are to be known as encompassed by the supporting cause (<s>parigrahahetu</s>).

body.text: tatra kathamebhirdaśabhirhetubhiḥ sarvalaukikā bhāvāḥpravartante / kathañca saṃkleśo bhavati / kathañca vyavadānam / yānīmāni vividhāni sasyāni dhānyasaṃkhyātāni loke yairayaṃ loko jīvikāṃ kalpayati teṣāṃ tāvadyadidaṃ nāma saṃjñā vyāgvyāhāro vividhastad yathā yavaśāligodhūmatilamudgamāṣakulatthādikaḥ / ayameṣāmanuvyavahārahetuḥ yavā ānīyantāṃ dīyantāṃ piṣyantāṃ sthāpyantāmityevamādikasya vyavahārasya yathā yavā evamavaśiṣṭheṣvapi veditavyam jighatsāpipāsādaurbalyaṃ kāyasthityapekṣaṃ kavaḍīkārāhārāsvādāpekṣañca / teṣvarthitvaṃ paryeṣaṇā upanādānamupabhogaśca bhavati / ayameṣāmapekṣāhetuḥ / yato yataḥ svabījād yasya [yasya] sasyasya prādurbhāvo bhavati tadbījaṃ tasyākṣepahetuḥ / pṛthivīvṛṣṭyādikaḥ pratyayo 'ḍkuraprādurbhāvāya parigrahahetuḥ tadbījaṃ tasyāṅkurasyābhinirvṛttihetuḥ / sa khalvaṅkurakāṇḍa patraparaṃparāsantānastasyāḥ sasyaniṣpatteḥ sasyaparipākagyāvāhakahetuḥ / yavabījācca yavāṅkurasya yavasasyasya ca prādurbhāvo bhavati nānyasya / evaṃ pariśiṣṭebhyo veditavyam / ayameṣāṃ pratiniyamahetuḥ / sarve caite apekṣāhetumupādāya pratiniyamahetvantāheta vaḥ sasyasyābhiniṣpattaye sahakārihetuḥ / na hi taddhānyamanyatamahetuvaikalyānniṣpadyate / tasmātsarvā sā sāmagrī sahakāriheturityucyate / aśani-sasyaroganipātādayo 'ntarāyā virodhahetuḥ / tadvaikalyaṃ nānantarāyaḥ avirodhahetuḥ / evamete daśa hetavastadanyeṣvapi laukikeṣu bhāveṣu yathāyogaṃ veditavyāḥ / tadyathā dhānyaparigrahe /
body.translated_text: How then do all worldly entities operate through these ten causes? And how does defilement (<s>saṃkleśa</s>) occur? And how does purification (<s>vyavadāna</s>)? Consider first the various crops counted as grains in the world, by which this world sustains its livelihood—their names, designations, and verbal expressions being various, such as barley, rice, wheat, sesame, mung bean, black gram, horse gram, and so forth. This is their conventional-usage cause (<s>anuvyavahārahetu</s>)—of such conventional usage as 'Let barley be brought, given, ground, stored,' and so on; and similarly for the rest. [There is also] the concern arising from hunger, thirst, and weakness, regarding the maintenance of the body and regarding the enjoyment of food. The seeking, pursuit, acquisition, and consumption of these occurs. This is their dependence-cause (<s>apekṣāhetu</s>). From whatever seed of its own kind a particular crop arises, that seed is its attraction-cause (<s>ākṣepahetu</s>). Conditions such as earth, rain, and so forth for the arising of the sprout constitute the supporting cause (<s>parigrahahetu</s>). That seed is the production-cause (<s>abhinirvṛttihetu</s>) of that sprout. And that sprout, through the succession of stalk, leaves, and so forth, is the conveying-cause (<s>āvāhakahetu</s>) leading to the production and ripening of the crop. From a barley seed, a barley sprout and barley crop arise, not another. Similarly for the rest. This is their determinative cause (<s>pratiniyamahetu</s>). All these causes, beginning with the dependence-cause and ending with the determinative cause, are the cooperative cause (<s>sahakārihetu</s>) for the production of the crop. For that grain does not come to completion with the deficiency of any single cause. Therefore, that entire assemblage is called the cooperative cause. Lightning, crop diseases, and such calamities are the contradiction-cause (<s>virodhahetu</s>). Their absence is the non-contradiction cause (<s>avirodhahetu</s>). Thus these ten causes are to be understood, as appropriate, in other worldly entities as well—just as in the case of grain cultivation.

body.text: tatra sarvasya pratītyasamutpādasya yadidaṃ nāmasaṃjñā-vāgvyāhāraḥ tadyathā avidyā saṃskārā vijñānaṃ nāmarūpaṃvistareṇa yāvajjarāmaraṇaśokaparidevaduḥkhadaurmanasyopāyāsāḥ / ityayantāvat saṃkleśasyānuvyavahārahetuḥ / avidyāpratyayāḥ saṃskārā yāvajjātipratyayaṃ jarāmaraṇamityevamādikasya anuvyavahārasya viṣayāsvādāpekṣā caiṣu bhavāṅgeṣu pravṛtiḥ / ayamasya saṃkleśasyāpekṣāhetuḥ / avidyādīnāṃ dharmāṇāṃ dṛṣṭe dharme yāni bījāni jātasya bhūtasyeha tānyanyajānmikasya jātijarāmaraṇasyākṣepahetuḥ / asatpuruṣasaṃsevā 'saddharmaśravaṇamayoniśomanaskāraḥ pūrvābhyāsāvedhaścāvidyādīnāmutpattaye parigrahahetuḥ / svakasvakaṃ bījamavidyādīnāṃ nirvṛṃttihetuḥ / te punaravidyādayo bhavaparyavasānā uttarottarāvāhanapāraṃparyeṇa tasyānyajānmikasya jātijarāmaraṇasyāvāhakahetuḥ / anye saha svavīryairavidyādayo bhavaparyavasānā narakopapattaye saṃvartante / anye tiryakpretamanuṣyadevopapattaye / ityeyaṃ saṃkleśasya pratiniyamahetuḥ / apekṣāhetumādiṃ kṛtvā sarva ete hetavaḥ pratiniyamahetuparyavasānāḥ sahakāriheturityucyate / tasya punaḥ saṃkleśasya virodhahetuḥ gotrasaṃpad buddhānāmutpādaḥ saddharmasya deśanā satpuruṣasaṃsevā saddharmaśravaṇaṃ yoniśo manaskāro dharmānudharmapratipattiḥ sarve ca bodhipakṣyā dharmāḥ / avirodhahetureṣāmeva yathoddiṣṭānāṃ dharmāṇāṃ vaikalyaṃ virahitatvam / evamebhirdaśabhirhetubhiḥ sarvaḥ saṃkleśaḥ sarvasattvānāṃ veditavyaḥ / tatra yaḥ sarveṣu vyavadānapakṣyeṣu dharmeṃṣu nirodhe ca nirvāṇe nāmasaṃjñāvāgvyāhāraḥ / ayaṃ vyavadānasyānuvyavahārahetuḥ / itīmāni smṛtyupasthānāni samyak prahāṇāni yāvadāryāṣṭāṅgo mārgaṃḥ / avidyānirodhācca saṃskāranirodho vistareṇa yāvajjātinirodhājjarāmaraṇanirodha ityasyaivaṃbhāgīyasyānuvyavahārasya / tatra yā saṃskārādīnavāpekṣā vyavadānaparyeṣaṇā vyavadānaparigraho vyavadānapariniṣpattiḥ ayamasyāpekṣāhetuḥ / yā gotrasthasya pudgalasya gotrasaṃpat sopadhiśeṣa [nirūpadhiśeṣa] nirvāṇādhigamāya pūrvaṅgamāya / [ayaṃ] vyavadānasyākṣepahetuḥ / satpuruṣasaṃsevā saddharmaśravaṇaṃ yoniśomanaskāraḥ pūrvakṛtaścendriyaparipākaḥ parigrahahetuḥ / tāni gotrasaṃgṛhītānyanāsravabodhipakṣyadharmabījāni teṣāṃ bodhipakṣyāṇāṃ dharmāṇāmabhinirvṛttihetuḥ te punaḥ svabījānnirvṛttā bodhipakṣyā dharmāḥ sopadhiśeṣa-nirupadhiśeṣanirvāṇadhātvoḥ krameṇāvāhakahetuḥ /
body.translated_text: Therein, the names, designations, and verbal expressions of the entire dependent origination (<s>pratītyasamutpāda</s>)—such as ignorance (<s>avidyā</s>), formations (<s>saṃskāra</s>), consciousness (<s>vijñāna</s>), name-and-form (<s>nāmarūpa</s>), in detail up to old age, death, sorrow, lamentation, suffering, mental distress, and anguish—this is the conventional-usage cause of defilement. 'Conditioned by ignorance, formations arise,' up to 'conditioned by birth, old age and death'—the concern with the enjoyment of objects in these links of existence and the engagement therein: this is the dependence-cause of defilement. The seeds in this present life of <s>dharmas</s> beginning with ignorance—those, of a being already born and existing here, are the attraction-cause of birth, old age, and death in another life. Association with bad persons, hearing wrong <s>Dharma</s>, improper mental attention, and the impress of previous habituation are the supporting cause for the arising of ignorance and the rest. The respective seed of each is the production-cause of ignorance and the rest. And these, from ignorance through to the culmination in existence, through the succession of progressive conveying, are the conveying-cause of that birth, old age, and death in another life. Some, together with their own force, from ignorance through to the culmination in existence, conduce to rebirth in the hells; others to rebirth among animals, hungry ghosts, humans, or gods. This is the determinative cause of defilement. Beginning with the dependence-cause, all these causes through to the determinative cause are called the cooperative cause. And the contradiction-cause of that defilement is: the endowment with lineage (<s>gotrasaṃpad</s>), the arising of <s>Buddhas</s>, the teaching of the true <s>Dharma</s>, association with good persons, hearing the true <s>Dharma</s>, proper mental attention, practice in conformity with the <s>Dharma</s>, and all factors conducive to awakening (<s>bodhipakṣyadharma</s>). The non-contradiction cause is the deficiency and absence of these very factors as enumerated. Thus, through these ten causes, all defilement of all beings is to be understood. Therein, the names, designations, and verbal expressions pertaining to all <s>dharmas</s> on the side of purification and to the cessation that is <s>nirvāṇa</s>—this is the conventional-usage cause of purification. [Such as:] 'These are the foundations of mindfulness, the right exertions, up to the noble eightfold path'; and 'from the cessation of ignorance comes the cessation of formations, in detail up to from the cessation of birth comes the cessation of old age and death'—for such conventional usage. Therein, the concern with formations and so forth, the search for purification, the acquisition of purification, and the completion of purification—this is the dependence-cause. The endowment with lineage of a person possessing lineage, which serves as the precursor to the attainment of <s>nirvāṇa</s> with and without remainder—this is the attraction-cause of purification. Association with good persons, hearing the true <s>Dharma</s>, proper mental attention, and the previously accomplished ripening of faculties are the supporting cause. Those seeds of the undefiled factors conducive to awakening, encompassed by the lineage, are the production-cause of those factors conducive to awakening. And those factors conducive to awakening, produced from their own seeds, are progressively the conveying-cause of the <s>nirvāṇa</s>-element with remainder and without remainder.

body.text: tatra yacchrāvakagotraṃ śrāvakayānena parinirvāṇāya saṃvartate pratyekabuddhagotraṃ pratyekabuddhayānena parinirvāṇāya saṃvartate mahāyānagotraṃ mahāyānena parinirvāṇāya saṃvartate ayaṃ vyavadānasya pratiniyamahetuḥ / yaścāpekṣāheturvyavadānapakṣyo yaśca yāvat pratiniyamaheturayamasya sahakāriheturityucyate / gotrāsampannatā buddhānāmanutpādaḥ akṣaṇepapattirasatpuruṣasaṃsevā 'saddharmaśravaṇamayoniśomanaskāro mithyāpratipattiḥ virodhahetuḥ / asyaiva virodhahetoryadvaikalyavirahitatvamayamucyate 'virodhahetuḥ / tatra yaḥ saṃkleśapakṣyo virodhahetuḥ sa vyavadānaheturdraṣṭavyaḥ / yo vyavadānapakṣyo virodhahetuḥ sa saṃkleśaheturdraṣṭavyaḥ / evaṃ ebhirdaśabhirhetubhiḥ saṃkleśo daśabhireva vyavadānaṃ bhavatyatīte 'pyadhvanyabhūdanāgate 'pyadhvani bhaviṣyati saṃkleśāya vā vyavadānāya vā na ebhya uttari na ebhyo bhūyānanyo heturvidyate /
body.translated_text: Therein, the <s>Śrāvaka</s>-lineage conduces to <s>parinirvāṇa</s> through the <s>Śrāvaka</s>-vehicle; the <s>Pratyekabuddha</s>-lineage conduces to <s>parinirvāṇa</s> through the <s>Pratyekabuddha</s>-vehicle; the <s>Mahāyāna</s>-lineage conduces to <s>parinirvāṇa</s> through the <s>Mahāyāna</s>. This is the determinative cause of purification. The dependence-cause and the rest up to the determinative cause on the side of purification—this is called the cooperative cause. The absence of lineage-endowment, the non-arising of <s>Buddhas</s>, rebirth in inopportune circumstances, association with bad persons, hearing wrong <s>Dharma</s>, improper mental attention, and wrong practice—this is the contradiction-cause. The deficiency and absence of this very contradiction-cause is called the non-contradiction cause. Therein, the contradiction-cause on the side of defilement is to be seen as the cause of purification. The contradiction-cause on the side of purification is to be seen as the cause of defilement. Thus, through these ten causes, defilement [arises] and through these very ten, purification [arises]—this was so in the past and will be so in the future, whether for defilement or for purification; no other cause beyond or additional to these exists.

body.text: tatra phalaṃ katamat / samāsataḥ pañca phalāni / vipākaphalaṃ niṣyandaphalaṃ visaṃyogaphalaṃ puruṣakāraphalamadhipatiphalañca /
body.translated_text: What therein is the result (<s>phala</s>)? In brief, there are five results: the maturation result (<s>vipākaphala</s>), the outflow result (<s>niṣyandaphala</s>), the separation result (<s>visaṃyogaphala</s>), the human-effort result (<s>puruṣakāraphala</s>), and the dominant result (<s>adhipatiphala</s>).

body.text: akuśalānāṃ dharmāṇāmapāyeṣu vipāko vipacyate / kuśalasāsravāṇāṃ sugatau / tadvipākaphalam / yatpunarakuśalābhyāsādakuśalārāmatā saṃtiṣṭhate akuśalabahulatā kuśalābhyāsātkuśalārāmatā kuśalabahulatā pūrvakarmasādṛśyena vā paścātphalānuvartanatā tanniṣyandaphalam / āryāṣṭāṅgasya mārgasya kleśanirodho visaṃyogaphalam / yaḥ punalaukikena mārgeṇa kleśanirodhaḥ sa nātyantamanuvartate pṛthagjanānām / tasmāttanna visaṃyogaphalam / yatpunarekatyadṛṣṭe dharme 'nyatamānyatamena śilpakarmasthānasanniśritena puruṣakāreṇa yadi vā kṛṣyā yadi vā vaṇijyayā yadi vā rājapauruṣṭeṇa lipi-gaṇana-nyasana-saṃkhyā-mudrayā sasyādikaṃ lābhādikañca phalamabhinirvartayati idamucyate puruṣakāraphalam / cakṣuvijñānañcukṣurindriyasyādhipatiphalam / evaṃ yāvanmanovijñānaṃ manaindriyasya / tathā prāṇairaviyogo jīvitendriyasya / iti sarveṣāmindriyasya / iti sarveṣāmindriyāṇāṃ dvāviṃśatīnāṃ svena svenādhipatyena yatphalaṃ nirvartate tadadhipatiphalaṃ veditavyam / taccādhipatyaṃ dvāviṃśatīnāmindriyāṇāṃ veditavyam / tadyathā vastu saṃgrahaṇyām /
body.translated_text: The maturation of unwholesome <s>dharmas</s> ripens in the lower realms; that of wholesome defiled [<s>dharmas</s>] ripens in happy destinies. That is the maturation result. Furthermore, from the habituation to unwholesome [<s>dharmas</s>], delight in the unwholesome persists and unwholesomeness predominates; from the habituation to wholesome [<s>dharmas</s>], delight in the wholesome and predominance of wholesomeness [persists]; or the subsequent result follows in conformity with previous action—that is the outflow result. The cessation of afflictions through the noble eightfold path is the separation result. The cessation of afflictions through the mundane path, however, does not persist finally for ordinary persons; therefore that is not the separation result. Furthermore, when someone in this present life, through some human effort based on a craft or occupation, whether through agriculture, commerce, royal service, writing, calculation, bookkeeping, accounting, or seal-making, produces a result such as crops, gains, and so forth—this is called the human-effort result. Eye-consciousness is the dominant result of the eye-faculty. Similarly, up to mind-consciousness being that of the mind-faculty. Likewise, non-separation from the vital functions is [the dominant result] of the life-faculty. Thus, whatever result is produced by the respective dominance of all twenty-two faculties—that is to be known as the dominant result. And that dominance of the twenty-two faculties is to be understood as in the <s>Vastusaṃgrahaṇī</s>.

body.text: evaṃ hi bodhisattvo buddhavacanaṃ samyaghetuphalaparidīpanākāraṃ viditvā sthānāsthānajñānabalagotramāsevanānvayāt krameṇa viśodhayati vivardhayati ca /
body.translated_text: Thus the <s>Bodhisattva</s>, having understood the word of the <s>Buddha</s> as it correctly illuminates cause and result, progressively purifies and develops the lineage of the power of knowledge of what is possible and impossible (<s>sthānāsthānajñānabala</s>) through its cultivation.

body.text: na cākṛtamanyakṛtaṃ vā kasyacidvipacyate / na ca svayaṃ kṛtānāṃ karmaṇāṃ kalpaśatairapi praṇāśo bhavati phaladānaṃ prati / evamakṛtānabhyāgamakṛtāvipraṇāśaṃ buddhavacanaṃ paridīpitaṃ bodhisattvo yathābhūtaṃ jñātvā karma-svakatā-jñānabalagotraṃ krameṇa viśodhayati vivardhayati ca /
body.translated_text: No [result] ripens for anyone from what is not done or from what is done by another; nor is there destruction, even in hundreds of <s>kalpas</s> (eons), of self-made actions with respect to the giving of fruit. Thus, having truly known the word of the <s>Buddha</s> that illuminates [the principle of] 'what is not done does not come' and 'what is done does not perish,' the <s>Bodhisattva</s> progressively purifies and develops the lineage of the power of knowledge of the ownership of actions (<s>karmasvakatājñānabala</s>).

body.text: tatra kathaṃ bodhisattvaḥ śrutaṃ paryeṣate / iha bodhisattvastīvraṃ gauravamupasthāpya subhāṣite sulapite dharma paryeṣate / evaṃrūpaścāsya samāsena subhāṣitagauravaṃ pratyupasthitaṃ bhavati / yadasau bodhisattva ekasubhāṣitaśravaṇahetorapi taptāṃ jvalitāmapyayomayīṃ bhūmiṃ pareṇa prāmodyenādareṇa praviśedyadyanyathā subhāṣitaśravaṇaṃ na labheta prāgeva prabhūtasya subhāṣitasyārthe / yacca bodhisattvasya sve ātmabhāve samucchraye premagauravaṃ prāgevānyeṣu sarvakāyapariṣkāreṣu bhojanapānādiṣu / yacca subhāṣitaśravaṇe pūrvakaṃ premagauravaṃ paścimaṃ premagauravamupanidhāya śatatamīmapi kalāṃ nopaiti sahasratamīmapi saṃkhyāmapi kalāmapi gaṇanāmapyupaniṣadamapi nopaiti sa tathā subhāṣite gauravajātaḥ subhāṣitaṃ śṛṇvannakhinnaśca bhavattyatṛptaśca / śrāddhaśca bhavati prasādabahalaścārdrasantāna ṛjukadṛṣṭiḥ / saguṇa kāmatayā dharmakāmatayā dharmabhāṇakamupasaṃkrāmati nopārambhābhiprāyeṇa sagauravatayā na mānastambhena kiṃkuśalagaveṣaṇatayā na ātmodbhāvanārtham ātmānañca parāṃśca kuśalamūle saṃniyojayiṣyāmīti na lābhasatkārahetoḥ /
body.translated_text: There, how does the <s>Bodhisattva</s> seek learning? Here, the <s>Bodhisattva</s>, having established intense reverence for the well-spoken and well-expressed, seeks the <s>Dharma</s>. And such, in brief, is the reverence for the well-spoken that is present in him: that <s>Bodhisattva</s>, even for the sake of hearing a single well-spoken [word], would enter even a heated, blazing, iron ground with supreme delight and care, if he could not otherwise obtain the hearing of the well-spoken—how much more for the sake of abundant well-spoken [teaching]. And the loving reverence that the <s>Bodhisattva</s> has for his own person and bodily growth, let alone for all bodily adornments, food, drink, and so forth—compared to the loving reverence for hearing the well-spoken, the former does not reach even a hundredth part, a thousandth, a numerical fraction, a calculable portion, or a comparable measure. Having developed such reverence for the well-spoken, he is unwearied and insatiable when hearing the well-spoken. And he is faithful, abundant in serene confidence, of tender disposition, and of correct views. With desire for qualities and desire for the <s>Dharma</s>, he approaches the <s>Dharma</s>-reciter, not with the intention of finding fault, but with reverence, not with the pride of conceit; seeking what is wholesome, not for the purpose of self-aggrandizement, [thinking:] 'I shall establish both myself and others in roots of virtue'—not for the sake of gain and honor.

body.text: sa evamupasaṃkramaṇasaṃpannaḥ asaṃkliṣṭaśca dharma śṛṇotyavikṣiptaśca /
body.translated_text: Endowed thus with proper approach, he hears the <s>Dharma</s> without defilement and without distraction.

body.text: kathamasaṃkliṣṭaḥ śṛṇoti / stambhasaṃkleśavigato 'vamanyanāsaṃkleśavigataḥ laya-saṃkleśavigataśca /
body.translated_text: How does he hear without defilement? Free from the defilement of rigidity (<s>stambha</s>), free from the defilement of contempt (<s>avamanyanā</s>), and free from the defilement of depression (<s>laya</s>).

body.text: tatra ṣaḍbhirākāraiḥ stambhasaṃkleśavigato bhavati / caturbhirākārairavamanyāsaṃkleśavigato bhavati / ekenākāreṇa layasaṃkleśavigato bhavati / kālena śṛṇoti satkṛtya śuśrūṣamāṇo nāsūyannanuvidhīyamāno 'nupārambhaprekṣī / ebhiḥ ṣaḍbhirākāraiḥ stambhasaṃkleśavigataḥ /
body.translated_text: There, one is free from the defilement of rigidity in six aspects; free from the defilement of contempt in four aspects; free from the defilement of depression in one aspect. One hears at the proper time, with respect, with willingness to listen, without resentment, in conformity, and looking without fault-finding. Through these six aspects one is free from the defilement of rigidity.

body.text: dharme gauravamupasthāpya dharmabhāṇake pudgale gauravamupasthāpya dharmamaparibhavan dharmabhāṇakaṃ pudgalamaparibhavan ebhiścaturbhirākārairavamanyanāsaṃkleśavigataḥ śṛṇoti /
body.translated_text: Having established reverence for the <s>Dharma</s>, having established reverence for the person who recites the <s>Dharma</s>, not despising the <s>Dharma</s>, not despising the person who recites the <s>Dharma</s>—through these four aspects one hears free from the defilement of contempt.

body.text: ātmānamaparibhavan śṛṇoti / anenaikenākāreṇa layasaṃkleśavigataḥ śṛṇoti / evaṃ hi bodhisattvaḥ asaṃkliṣṭo dharma śṛṇoti /
body.translated_text: Not despising oneself, one hears. Through this one aspect, one hears free from the defilement of depression. Thus indeed does the <s>Bodhisattva</s> hear the <s>Dharma</s> without defilement.

body.text: tatra kathaṃ bodhisattvaḥ avikṣipto dharmaṃ śṛṇoti / pañcabhirākāraiḥ / ājñācitta ekāgracittaḥ avihitaśrotraḥ samāvarjitamānasaḥ sarvacetasā samanvāhṛtya dharmaṃ śṛṇoti / evaṃ hi bodhisattvaḥ śrutaṃ paryeṣate /
body.translated_text: There, how does the <s>Bodhisattva</s> hear the <s>Dharma</s> without distraction? In five aspects: with a mind of understanding, with a one-pointed mind, with undiverted ear, with engaged mind, and gathering [the teaching] with one's entire consciousness, one hears the <s>Dharma</s>. Thus indeed does the <s>Bodhisattva</s> seek learning.

body.text: tatra kimarthaṃ bodhisattvaḥ śrutaṃ paryeṣate / buddhavacanaṃ tāvad bodhisattvaḥ paryeṣate / samyagdharmāpratipatti saṃpādanārthaṃ pareṣāñca vistareṇasaṃprakāśanārtham / hetuvidyāṃ bodhisattvaḥ paryeṣate tasyaiva śāstrasya durbhāṣitadurlapitatāyā yathābhūta parijñānārthaṃ paravādanigrahārthaṃ cāprasannānāmasmiṃcchāsane prasādāya prasannānāñca bhūyobhāvāya / śabdavidyāṃ bodhisattvaḥ paryeṣate / saṃskṛtalapitādhimuktānātmani saṃpratyayotpādanārthaṃ saniruktapadavyañjananirūpaṇatayā ekasya cārthasya nānāprakāraniruttyanuvyavahārānupraveśārtham / cikitsāśāstraṃ bodhisattvaḥ paryeṣate sattvānāṃ nānāprakāravyādhivyupaśamanārthaṃ mahājanakāyasyānugrahārtham / laukikāni śilpakarmasthānāni bodhisattvaḥ paryeṣate 'lpakṛcchreṇa bhogasaṃharaṇārthaṃ sattvānāmarthāya sattvānāñca bahumānotpādanārthaṃ śilpajñānasaṃvibhāgena cānugrahasaṃgrahārtham / sarvāṇi ca etāni pañcavidyāsthānāni bodhisattvaḥ paryeṣate 'nuttarāyāḥ samyaksaṃbodhermahājñānasambhāraparipūṇārtham / na hi sarvatraivamaśikṣamāṇaḥ krameṇa sarvajñajñānamanāvaraṇaṃ pratilabhate / yattāvadvodhisattvaḥ paryeṣate yathā ca paryeṣate yadarthañca paryeṣate tannirdiṣṭam /
body.translated_text: There, for what purpose does the <s>Bodhisattva</s> seek learning? First, the <s>Bodhisattva</s> seeks the word of the <s>Buddha</s> for the purpose of accomplishing the correct practice of the <s>Dharma</s> and for extensively illuminating it to others. The <s>Bodhisattva</s> seeks the science of logic (<s>hetuvidyā</s>) for the purpose of knowing as it truly is the ill-spoken and ill-expressed quality of that [opposing] treatise, and for the purpose of refuting opposing doctrines, for generating faith in those without faith in this teaching, and for the increase [of faith] in those already faithful. The <s>Bodhisattva</s> seeks the science of grammar and language (<s>śabdavidyā</s>) for the purpose of generating confidence in oneself among those inclined toward refined speech, through the exposition of words, terms, and syllables with their etymology, and for entering into the various modes of expression and usage for a single meaning. The <s>Bodhisattva</s> seeks the science of medicine (<s>cikitsāśāstra</s>) for the purpose of pacifying the various diseases of beings and for benefiting a great multitude of people. The <s>Bodhisattva</s> seeks worldly arts and crafts for the purpose of easily accumulating resources for the welfare of beings and for generating esteem in beings, and for the purpose of benefiting and gathering [beings] through the sharing of craft-knowledge. And the <s>Bodhisattva</s> seeks all these five fields of knowledge (<s>pañcavidyāsthāna</s>) for the purpose of fulfilling the great accumulation of knowledge for unsurpassed perfect awakening. For without training thus in all these, one does not gradually obtain unobstructed omniscient knowledge. What the <s>Bodhisattva</s> seeks, how he seeks, and for what purpose he seeks—that has been stated.

body.text: tatra kiṃ bodhisattvaḥ pareṣāṃ deśayati / kathañca deśayati / kimarthañca deśayati / tatra yadeva paryeṣate tadeva deśayati / yadarthañca paryeṣate tadarthameva pareṣāṃ deśayati / dvābhyāṃ punarākārābhyāṃ deśayati / anulomāṃ ca kathāṃ kathayati pariśuddhāṃ ca / tatra
body.translated_text: There, what does the <s>Bodhisattva</s> teach to others? And how does he teach? And for what purpose does he teach? There, he teaches the very thing he seeks; and for the very purpose for which he seeks, for that very purpose he teaches to others. And he teaches in two aspects: he gives discourse that is conforming (<s>anulomā</s>) and discourse that is pure (<s>pariśuddhā</s>). There,

body.text: kathamanulomāṃ kathāṃ kathayati / anurūpeṇeryāpithena sthitāya deśayati nāpratirūpeṇa / na uccatarake āsane niṣaṇṇāyāglānāya nodgunṭhikākṛtāya na purato gacchate vistareṇa yathāsūtraṃ veditavyam / tatkasya hetoḥ / dharmaguravo hi buddhabodhisattvāḥ / dharme hi tatkriyamāṇe pareṣāmadhimātraṃ dharmagauravamutpadyate / śravaṇe cādarajātā bhavanti nāvajñājātāḥ / sarveṣāṃ ca deśayati / nirantaraṃ sarvaṃ ca deśayati / dharmamātsaryamakurvannācāryamuṣṭiṃ dharmeṣu karoti / yathākramaṃ padavyaṃjanamuddiśati / yathākramoddiṣṭaṃ ca padavyaṃjanaṃ yathākramamevārthato vibhajati / arthopasaṃhitaṃ ca dharmamarthaṃ coddiśati nānarthopasaṃhitam / saṃdarśayitavyāṃ saṃdarśayati samādāpayitavyāṃ samādāpayati samuttejayitavyāṃ samuttejayati saṃpraharṣayitavyāṃ saṃpraharṣayati / pratyakṣānumānāptāgamayuktāṃ ca kathāṃ karoti nāpramāṇayuktām / sugatigamanānukūlāmapi avyākulāmapi supraveśāṃna gahanāṃ caturāryasatyapratisaṃyuktāmapi sarvāsāñca pariṣadāṃ yā pariṣad yā kathā yathārhati tāṃ tathāsyai kathaṃ karoti / ebhistāvatpañcadaśabhirākārairbodhisattvānāṃ sattveṣvanulomā sarvaparārtheṣu kathā veditavyā /
body.translated_text: how does he give conforming discourse? He teaches to one standing with appropriate deportment, not with inappropriate [deportment]; not to one seated on a higher seat, not to one who is not sick [yet reclines], not to one whose head is covered, not to one who walks ahead—and in detail, this is to be understood as in the <s>sūtra</s>. For what reason? Because the <s>Buddhas</s> and <s>Bodhisattvas</s> are teachers of the <s>Dharma</s>. For when that is done with respect to the <s>Dharma</s>, intense reverence for the <s>Dharma</s> arises in others. And they become attentive in hearing, not disdainful. And he teaches to all; he teaches everything continuously. Not being miserly with the <s>Dharma</s>, he does not keep a teacher's closed fist regarding the <s>dharmas</s>. He expounds the words and syllables in their proper order. And having expounded the words and syllables in order, he explains their meaning in that very order. He expounds the <s>Dharma</s> that is connected with meaning and purpose, not that which is unconnected with meaning. To those who are to be shown, he shows; to those who are to be induced, he induces; to those who are to be encouraged, he encourages; to those who are to be delighted, he delights. And he gives discourse that is supported by direct perception, inference, and authoritative tradition (<s>āptāgama</s>), not unsupported by valid means of knowledge. [Discourse] that conduces to rebirth in good destinies, that is orderly, that is easily accessible and not obscure, that is connected with the Four Noble Truths, and for each of the assemblies, he gives the appropriate discourse to each assembly as is fitting. Through these fifteen aspects, the conforming discourse of the <s>Bodhisattvas</s> toward beings in all matters for the benefit of others should be understood.

body.text: punaśca bodhisattvaḥ apakāriṣu [sattveṣu] maitracittatāmupasthāpya kathāṃ karoti / duścaritacāriṣu sattveṣu hitacittatāmupasthāpya kathāṃ kathayati / sukhitaduḥkhiteṣu sattveṣu pramatteṣu dīneṣu hitasukhānukampācittatāmupasthāpya kathāṃ karoti / na cerṣyāparyavasthānamadhipatiṃ kṛtvā ātmānamutkarṣayati / na parān paṃsayati / nirāmiṣeṇa ca cittenāpratikāṃkṣamāṇo lābhasatkāraślokaṃ pareṣāṃ dharmān deśayati /
body.translated_text: Furthermore, the <s>Bodhisattva</s>, having established a mind of friendliness (<s>maitrī</s>) toward beings who have done harm, gives discourse. Toward beings engaged in misconduct, having established a mind of beneficence, he gives discourse. Toward beings who are happy, suffering, heedless, or wretched, having established a mind of benefit, happiness, and compassion, he gives discourse. And he does not exalt himself under the dominion of the obsession of envy. He does not disparage others. And with a mind free from worldly gain, not seeking gain, honor, or fame, he teaches the <s>Dharma</s> to others.

body.text: ebhiḥ pañcabhirākārairbodhisattvaḥ pariśuddhāṃ kathāṃ kathayati / ta ete samāsato viṃśatirākārā bhavanti / kālena satkṛtyānupūrvamanusandhyanusahitaṃ harṣayatā roca[yatā] toṣayatā utsāhayatā anavasādayatā yuktā sahitā 'vyavakīrṇānudhārmikī yathā pariṣat maitracittena hitacittenānukampācittenāniśritena lābhasatkāraśloke ātmānamanutkarṣayatā parāṃścāpaṃsayatā / evaṃ bodhisattvaḥ pareṣāṃ dharmaṃ deśayati /
body.translated_text: Through these five aspects, the <s>Bodhisattva</s> gives pure discourse. These are, in summary, twenty aspects: at the proper time, with respect, in sequence, with continuity, in a connected manner, gladdening, inspiring delight, satisfying, encouraging, not disheartening, well-reasoned, coherent, unscattered, in accordance with the <s>Dharma</s>, appropriate to the assembly, with a mind of friendliness, with a mind of beneficence, with a mind of compassion, without attachment to gain and honor, not exalting oneself, and not disparaging others. Thus does the <s>Bodhisattva</s> teach the <s>Dharma</s> to others.

body.text: tatra
body.translated_text: There, what is the <s>Bodhisattva</s>'s practice in conformity with the <s>Dharma</s> (<s>dharmānudharmapratipattiḥ</s>)? In brief, it should be understood as fivefold: the conforming practice through body, speech, and mind with regard to those very <s>dharmas</s> as sought and as grasped, and correct reflection (<s>cintanā</s>) and cultivation (<s>bhāvanā</s>).

body.text: katamā bodhisattvasya dharmānudharmapratipattiḥ / samāsataḥ pañcavidhā veditavyā / teṣāmeva [yathā] paryeṣitānāṃ yathodgṛhītānāṃ dharmāṇāṃ kāyena vācā manasā cānuvartanā samyak cintanā bhāvanā ca /

yeṣāṃ dharmāṇāṃ bhagavatā kāyena vācā manasā kriyā niṣiddhā yeṣāñcābhyanujñātā kāyena vācā manasā kriyā tasya kāyavāṅmanaskarmaṇastathaiva parivarjanaṃ pratiniṣevaṇā samudānayatā ca / kāyena vācā manasā cānuvartanā dharmānudharmapratipattirityucyate /
body.translated_text: Those <s>dharmas</s> whose performance through body, speech, and mind has been prohibited by the <s>Bhagavān</s>, and those whose performance through body, speech, and mind has been permitted—the avoidance, observance, and accomplishment of those actions of body, speech, and mind accordingly: the conforming practice through body, speech, and mind is called the practice in conformity with the <s>Dharma</s>.

body.text: tatra samyak cintanā bodhisattvasya katamā / iha bodhisattva ekākī rahogato yathāśrutāṃ dharmāṃścintayitukāmastulayitukāma upaparīkṣitukāma ādita evācintyāni sthānāni vivarjayitvā dharmāṃścintayitumārabhate pratatañca cintayati / sātasya satkṛtya prayogeṇa na ślatham / kiñcicca bodhisattvaścintāprayukto yuktyā vicārayatyanupraviśati / kiñcidadhimucyata eva / arthapratisaraṇaśca bhavati cintayanna vyañjanapratisaraṇaḥ / kālānadeśamahāpadeśāṃśca yathābhūtaṃ prajānāti / ādipraveśena na cintāṃ praviśati / praviṣṭaśca punaḥ punarmanasikārataḥ sāratāmupanayati / aciṃntyaṃ varjayan bodhisattvaḥ sammohaṃ ciṃttāvikṣepaṃ nādhigacchati / pratataṃ sātatya-satkṛtya-prayuktaścintayannavijñātapūrvañcārtha vijānāti labhate vijñātañca / pratilabdhamarthaṃ na vināśayati na saṃpramoṣayati / yuktyā punaḥ kiñcit pravi[cinvan] praviśayan vicārayan na parapratyayo bhavati / teṣu yuktiparīkṣiteṣu dharmeṣu kiñcitpunaradhimucyamāno ye 'pyasya dharmeṣu gambhīreṣu buddhirnāvagāhate tathāgatagocarā ete dharmā nāsmadbuddhigocarā ityevamapratikṣipaṃstān dharmānātmānamakṣatañcānupahatañca pariharatyanavadyam / arthaṃ pratisaran bodhisattvo na vyañjanaṃ buddhānaṃ bhagavatāṃ sarvasandhyāya-vacanānyanupraviśati / kālāpadeśamahāpadeśakuśalo bodhisattvaḥ tattvārthānna vicalayituṃ na vikampayituṃ kenacit kathaṃcicchakyate / āditaścintāmanupraviśan bodhisattvaḥ apratilabdhapūrvāṃ kṣāntiṃ pratilabhate / tāmeva punaḥ pratilabdhāṃ
body.translated_text: There, what is the correct reflection of the <s>Bodhisattva</s>? Here, the <s>Bodhisattva</s>, alone, in seclusion, wishing to reflect upon, weigh, and examine the <s>dharmas</s> as heard, first setting aside the inconceivable matters, begins to reflect upon the <s>dharmas</s> and reflects extensively. With sustained, diligent effort, not lax. And the <s>Bodhisattva</s>, engaged in reflection, investigates some things by reasoning and enters into them; some things he accepts on conviction. He takes meaning as the refuge when reflecting, not the letter. And he correctly knows the occasions, references, and great references of time. He enters into reflection by the gateway of the beginning. And having entered, through repeated attention, he brings it to the essence. Avoiding the inconceivable, the <s>Bodhisattva</s> does not fall into confusion or scattering of reflection. Reflecting with sustained, continuous, and diligent effort, he comes to know meanings not previously known, and he obtains [understanding of] what was previously known. He does not destroy or lose the meaning already obtained. And investigating some things through reasoning, examining and deliberating, he does not depend on others [for understanding]. Among those <s>dharmas</s> examined by reasoning, accepting some things on conviction, even those profound <s>dharmas</s> into which his understanding does not penetrate—[thinking:] 'These <s>dharmas</s> are within the domain of the <s>Tathāgata</s>, not within the domain of my understanding'—thus not rejecting those <s>dharmas</s>, he maintains himself unharmed and unimpaired, blamelessly. Taking meaning as the refuge, not the letter, the <s>Bodhisattva</s> penetrates all the intentional statements (<s>sandhyāyavacana</s>) of the <s>Buddhas</s>, the <s>Bhagavāns</s>. Being skillful in the references and great references of time, the <s>Bodhisattva</s> cannot be shaken or caused to waver by anyone in any way from the true meaning. Entering into reflection from the beginning, the <s>Bodhisattva</s> obtains a patience (<s>kṣānti</s>) not previously obtained. Then, bringing that obtained

body.text: kṣāntiṃ sāratāmupanayan bodhisattvaḥ bhāvanāma nupraviśati / ebhiraṣṭābhirākārairbodhisattvaścintāsaṃgṛhītāṃ dharmānudharmapratipatti pratipanno bhavati /
body.translated_text: patience to its essence, the <s>Bodhisattva</s> enters into cultivation (<s>bhāvanā</s>). Through these eight aspects, the <s>Bodhisattva</s> is established in the practice in conformity with the <s>Dharma</s> that is included in reflection.

body.text: bhāvanā katamā / samāsataścaturvidhā veditavyā / śamatho vipaśyanā śamathavipaśyanābhyāsaḥ śamathavipaśyanābhiratiśca /
body.translated_text: What is cultivation (<s>bhāvanā</s>)? In brief, it should be understood as fourfold: calm abiding (<s>śamatha</s>), insight (<s>vipaśyanā</s>), the combined practice of calm abiding and insight, and delight in calm abiding and insight.

body.text: tatra śamathaḥ katamaḥ / yathāpi tadvodhisattvaḥ aṣṭākārāyāśvintāyāḥ susamāptatvānnirabhilāpye vastumātre 'rthamātre ālambane cittamupanibadhya sarvaprapañcāpagatena sarvacittapariplavāpagatena saṃjñā-manasikāreṇa sarvālambanānyadhimucyamānaḥ adhyātmasamādhinirmitteṣu cittaṃ saṃsthāpayati avasthāpayati vistareṇa yāvadekotīkaroti samādhatte / ayamucyate śamathaḥ /
body.translated_text: There, what is calm abiding (<s>śamatha</s>)? The <s>Bodhisattva</s>, having well-completed the eightfold reflection, fixing the mind on the inexpressible, on the mere object, on the mere meaning as the referent, with a perception and mental engagement free from all conceptual proliferation and free from all mental agitation, applying conviction to all referents, establishes, places, and in detail, up to unifying and concentrating the mind on the inner meditative signs (<s>samādhinimitta</s>). This is called calm abiding (<s>śamatha</s>).

body.text: vipaśyanā katamā tenaiva punaḥ śamathaparibhāvitena manaskāreṇa yathā cintitānāṃ dharmāṇāṃ nimittamanasikriyā vicayaḥ pravicayo dharmapravicayaḥ vistareṇa yāvatpāṇḍityaṃ prajñācāraḥ / iyamucyate vipaśyanā /
body.translated_text: What is insight (<s>vipaśyanā</s>)? With that very attention cultivated by calm (<s>śamatha</s>), the attending to the signs of <s>dharmas</s> as contemplated—investigation, thorough investigation, investigation of <s>dharmas</s>, in detail up to learned wisdom and the practice of wisdom (<s>prajñācāra</s>)—this is called insight.

body.text: śamathavipaśyanābhyāsaḥ katamaḥ / yaḥ śamathavipaśyanāyāñca sātatyaprayogaḥ satkṛtyaprayogaśca /
body.translated_text: What is the practice of calm and insight (<s>śamathavipaśyanābhyāsa</s>)? The continuous application and earnest application in calm and insight.

body.text: śamathavipaśyanābhiratiḥ katamā / teṣveva śamathavipaśyanā-nimitteṣu yaccittasyācalanaṃ svarasenaivābhisaṃskāravāhitāsthānaṃ saṃgraho 'visaraṇā / iyamucyate śamathavipaśyanābhiratiḥ
body.translated_text: What is delight in calm and insight (<s>śamathavipaśyanābhirati</s>)? The non-wavering of the mind with regard to those very signs of calm and insight, its spontaneous resting carried by mental formations, its collection and non-dispersal—this is called delight in calm and insight.

body.text: tatra bodhisattvo yathā yathā śamathavipaśyanābhyāsaṃ karoti tathā tathā śamathavipaśyanābhiratiḥ saṃtiṣṭhate / yathā yathā śamathavipaśyanābhiratiḥ saṃtiṣṭhate tathā tathā śamatho vipaśyanā ca pariśudhyataḥ / yathā yathā śamatho viśudhyati tathā tathā kāyaprasrabdhiścittaprasrabdhiḥ pṛthuvṛddhivaipulyatāṃ gacchati / yathā yathā vipaśyanā viśudhyati tathā tathā jñānadarśanaṃ pṛthuvṛddhivaipulyatāṃ gacchati / etāvacca bhāvanāyāḥ karaṇīyam / yadutāśrayagatañca dauṣṭhulyamanapanetavyaṃ sarvatra ca jñeye jñānadarśanaṃ viśodhayitavyaṃ ca / caitatsarvaṃ bhāvanākarmānayā caturākārayā bhāvanayā bodhisattvasya saṃpadyate /
body.translated_text: There, to the extent that the <s>Bodhisattva</s> practices calm and insight, to that extent delight in calm and insight becomes established. To the extent that delight in calm and insight becomes established, to that extent calm and insight become purified. To the extent that calm becomes purified, to that extent physical tranquility (<s>kāyaprasrabdhi</s>) and mental tranquility (<s>cittaprasrabdhi</s>) increase, grow, and expand. To the extent that insight becomes purified, to that extent knowledge-vision (<s>jñānadarśana</s>) increases, grows, and expands. And this much is the task of cultivation: namely, the rigidity (<s>dauṣṭhulya</s>) rooted in the basis must be removed, and knowledge-vision must be purified with regard to all that is knowable. And all this is accomplished for the <s>Bodhisattva</s> through this fourfold cultivation, the activity of cultivation.

body.text: avavādaḥ katamaḥ / samāsato 'ṣṭavidho veditavyaḥ / yathāpi tadvodhisattvaḥ samādhisanniśrayeṇa vā saṃvāsānvayādvā yeṣāmavavaditukāmo bhavati yo vā punaranyo bodhisattvo 'smai avavadati tathāgato vā sa ādita eva cittaṃ paryeṣate jānāti / cittaṃ paryeṣya indriya paryeṣate jānāti / indriyaṃ paryeṣya āśrayaṃ paryeṣate jānāti / āśayaṃ paryeṣyānuśayaṃ paryeṣate jānāti / anuśayaṃ paryeṣya yathāyogaṃ yathārhameva vicitreṣvavatāramukheṣvavatārayati / yadi vā 'śubhayā yadi vā maitryā yadi vā idaṃpratyayatā-pratītyasamutpādena yadi vā dhātubhedena yadi vā ānāpānasmṛtyā yathāyogaṃ yathārhamavaratāramukheṣvavatārya śāśvatāntāsadgrāha pratipakṣeṇa madhyamāṃ pratipadaṃ deśayati / ucchedāntāsadgrāha pratipakṣeṇa madhyamāṃ pratipadaṃ deśayati / akṛte ca kṛtābhimānaṃ tyājayati / aprāpte asparśite asākṣātkṛte sākṣātkṛtābhimānaṃ tyājayati /
body.translated_text: What is instruction (<s>avavāda</s>)? In brief, it should be understood as eightfold. When a <s>Bodhisattva</s>, relying on meditative concentration (<s>samādhi</s>) or through living together, wishes to instruct those [beings], or when another <s>Bodhisattva</s> or a <s>Tathāgata</s> instructs him—one first examines and knows the mind; having examined the mind, one examines and knows the faculties (<s>indriya</s>); having examined the faculties, one examines and knows the disposition (<s>āśaya</s>); having examined the disposition, one examines and knows the latent tendencies (<s>anuśaya</s>); having examined the latent tendencies, one introduces them appropriately into various gateways of entry as is fitting—whether through contemplation of the impure (<s>aśubhā</s>), loving-kindness (<s>maitrī</s>), conditionality and dependent origination (<s>pratītyasamutpāda</s>), analysis of elements (<s>dhātubheda</s>), or mindfulness of breathing (<s>ānāpānasmṛti</s>). Having introduced them appropriately into the gateways of entry, one teaches the middle path (<s>madhyamā pratipad</s>) as the antidote to the wrong grasping of the extreme of eternalism. One teaches the middle path as the antidote to the wrong grasping of the extreme of annihilationism. And one removes the conceit of having accomplished what is unaccomplished. One removes the conceit of having directly realized what is not attained, not touched, and not directly realized.

body.text: so 'yamaṣṭavidho 'vavādaḥ punaḥ samāsatastribhiḥ sthānaiḥ saṃgṛhīto veditavyaḥ / trīṇi sthānāni katamāni / asthitasya cittasyādito 'vasthitaye samyagālambanopanibandhaḥ / sthitacittasya ca svārthaprāptaye samyagupāyamārgadeśanā / aniṣṭhitasvakāryasya cāntarādhiṣṭhānaparityāgaḥ / tatra cittendriyāśayānuśayajñānena yathāyogamavatāramukhāvatāraṇatayā ca cittasthitaye samyagālambanopanibandho veditavyaḥ / tatra śāśvatocchedāntāsadgrāhapratipakṣeṇa madhyamayā pratipadā sthitacittasya svārthaprāptaye samyagupāyamārgadeśanā veditavyā / tatrākṛte yāvadasākṣātkṛte sākṣātkṛtābhimānatyājanatayā aniṣṭhitasvakāryasyāntarādhiṣṭhānaparityāgo veditavyaḥ / evamebhistribhiḥ sthānairaṣṭavidho 'vavādaḥ saṃgṛhīto veditavyaḥ /
body.translated_text: This eightfold instruction, moreover, should be understood as comprised in three bases, in brief. What are the three bases? First, for the mind that is not yet established, the proper binding to the correct object for its establishment. Second, for the established mind, the teaching of the correct method-path for attaining its purpose. Third, for one whose task is not yet completed, the non-abandonment of intermediate support. There, through the knowledge of mind, faculties, disposition, and latent tendencies, and through the introduction into the appropriate gateways of entry, the proper binding to the correct object for the establishment of the mind should be understood. There, through the middle path as antidote to the wrong grasping of the extremes of eternalism and annihilationism, the teaching of the correct method-path for the attainment of the purpose of the established mind should be understood. There, through the removal of the conceit of having directly realized what is not accomplished up to what is not directly realized, the non-abandonment of intermediate support for one whose task is not yet completed should be understood. Thus, the eightfold instruction should be understood as comprised in these three bases.

body.text: eva mevāvavādaṃ parato vā labhamāno bodhisattvaḥ pareṣāṃ vānuprayacchannaṣṭānāṃ balānāṃ gotraṃ krameṇa viśodhayati vivardhayati dhyānavimokṣasamādhisamāpattijñānabalasyendriyaparāparajñānabalasya nānādhimuktijñānabalasya nānādhātujñānabalasya sarvatra gāminī pratipaj jñānabalasya pūrvenivāsānusmṛtijñānabalasya cyutyupapattijñānabalasya ca /
body.translated_text: In this way, the <s>Bodhisattva</s>, receiving instruction from others or giving it to others, gradually purifies and develops the lineage of the eight powers (<s>bala</s>): the power of knowledge of <s>dhyāna</s>, liberations, concentrations, and attainments; the power of knowledge of the superior and inferior faculties; the power of knowledge of various aspirations; the power of knowledge of various elements; the power of knowledge of the path leading everywhere; the power of knowledge of the recollection of former abodes; and the power of knowledge of the passing away and rebirth [of beings].

body.text: tatrānuśāsanaṃ katamat / tatpañcavidhaṃ veditavyam / sāvadyasamudācārapratiṣedhaḥ anavadyasamudācārābhyanujñā pratiṣiddhābhyanujñāteṣu dharmeṣu skhalitasamācāra-saṃcodanā punaḥ punaranādarajātasya skhalataḥ avasādanayā smṛtikaraṇānupradānamakaluṣeṇāvipariṇatena snigdhenāśayena / samyak pratipannasya ca pratiṣiddhābhyanujñāteṣu dharmeṣu bhūtaguṇapriyākhyānatayā saṃpraharṣaṇā / itīdaṃ samāsataḥ pañcākāraṃ bodhisattvānāmanuśāsanaṃ veditavyam / yaduta pratiṣedho 'bhyanujñā codanā 'vasādanā saṃpraharṣaṇā ca /
body.translated_text: There, what is guidance (<s>anuśāsana</s>)? It should be understood as fivefold: prohibition of blameworthy conduct; permission of blameless conduct; admonishment for stumbling in the practice of prohibited and permitted <s>dharmas</s>; for one who is repeatedly negligent and stumbling, the bestowal of reminders that humble, with a disposition that is untroubled, unchanged, and affectionate; and rejoicing the one who is correctly practicing in the prohibited and permitted <s>dharmas</s> by truthfully proclaiming their genuine qualities. Thus, in brief, this fivefold guidance of <s>Bodhisattvas</s> should be understood: namely, prohibition, permission, admonishment, humbling, and rejoicing.

body.text: tatropāyasaṃgṛhītaṃ bodhisattvānāṃ kāyavāṅmanaskarma katamat / samāsato bodhisattvānāṃ catvāri saṃgrahavastūnyupāya ityucyante / yathoktaṃ bhagavatā catuḥsaṃgrahavastusaṃgṛhītenopāyena samanvāgato bodhisattvo bodhisattva ityucyata iti / kena punaḥ kāraṇena catvāri saṃgrahavastūnyupāya ityucyante / samāsataścaturvidha upāyaḥ sattvānāṃ vinayāya saṃgrahāya / nāstyata ūttari nāstyato bhūyaḥ / tadyathā 'nugrāhako grāhakaḥ avatārako 'nuvartakaśca / tatra dānaṃ bodhisattvasyānugrāhakaṃ upāyaḥ / tathā hi vicitreṇāmiṣadānenānugṛhyamāṇāḥ sattvāḥ śrotavyaṃ kartavyaṃ vacanaṃ manyate / tadanantaraṃ bodhisattvaḥ priyavāditayā tatra tatra sammūḍhānāṃ tatsammohāśeṣāpanayāya yuktiṃ grāhayati sandarśayati / evamasya priyavāditā grāhaka upāyo bhavati / tathā ca yuktyā grāhitān sandarśitānsattvān akuśalātsthānād vyutthāpya kuśale sthāne samādāpayati vinayati niveśayati pratiṣṭhāpayati / sāsyārthacaryā bhavatyavatāraka upāyaḥ / evañca bodhisattvaḥ tānsarvānavatārya tatsabhāgavṛttasamācāreṇānuvartate yenāsya na bhavanti vineyā vaktāraḥ / tvaṃ tāvadātmanā na śraddhāsampannaḥ śīlasampannastyāgasampannaḥ prajñāsampannaḥ kasmādbhavān parānatra samādāpayati / tena ca codayati smārayatīti tasmātsamānarthatā bodhisattvasya caturtho 'nuvartaka upāyo veditavyaḥ /
body.translated_text: There, what is the body, speech, and mental action of <s>Bodhisattvas</s> that is comprised in skillful means (<s>upāya</s>)? In brief, the four means of attraction (<s>saṃgrahavastu</s>) of <s>Bodhisattvas</s> are called skillful means. As the <s>Bhagavān</s> stated: 'A <s>Bodhisattva</s> endowed with skillful means comprised in the four means of attraction is called a <s>Bodhisattva</s>.' And for what reason are the four means of attraction called skillful means? In brief, the fourfold skillful means is for the training and attraction of beings. There is nothing beyond this, nothing more than this. Namely: benefiting, convincing, introducing, and exemplifying. There, giving (<s>dāna</s>) is the <s>Bodhisattva</s>'s benefiting means. For beings who are gratified by various material gifts consider his word worthy of being heard and followed. Thereupon, the <s>Bodhisattva</s>, through kind speech (<s>priyavāditā</s>), causes those who are confused in various ways to grasp and see what is reasonable for the complete removal of their confusion. Thus, his kind speech is the convincing means. And having caused beings to grasp and see through reasoning, one raises them from unwholesome states and establishes, trains, settles, and firmly grounds them in wholesome states. This beneficial conduct (<s>arthacaryā</s>) is the introducing means. And thus the <s>Bodhisattva</s>, having introduced all of them, follows the same conduct and practice as them, so that those to be trained do not say of him: 'You yourself are not endowed with faith, moral conduct, generosity, or wisdom—why then do you establish others in these?' And through this one admonishes and reminds them. Therefore, consistency of practice (<s>samānārthatā</s>) should be understood as the <s>Bodhisattva</s>'s fourth, exemplifying means.

body.text: ityebhiścaturbhirupāyaryatparigṛhītaṃ samastairvyastairvā bodhisattvasya kāyakarma vākkarma manaskarma / tadupāyaparigrahaṇāmityucyate sattvānāṃ samyaksaṃgrahāya vinayāya paripācanāya /
body.translated_text: The body, speech, and mental action of the <s>Bodhisattva</s> that is encompassed by these four means, whether together or separately, is called the application of skillful means, for the correct attraction, training, and maturation of beings.

body.text: iti bodhisattvabhūmāvādhāre yogasthāne aṣṭamaṃ balagotrapaṭalam /
body.translated_text: Thus, in the <s>Bodhisattvabhūmi</s>, in the Foundation Section of Yoga (<s>Ādhārayogasthāna</s>), the eighth chapter on the Lineage of Powers (<s>Balagotrapaṭala</s>).

body.text: uddānaṃ /
body.translated_text: Summary verse (<s>uddāna</s>):

children.translated_text: that which accords with the good person, and all-aspected likewise,
that which accords with overcoming adversity, pleasure here and hereafter,
and pure—this is the ninefold giving, in brief. //

body.text: iha bodhisattvaḥ krameṇa ṣaṭpāramitāṃ paripūryānuttarāṃ samyaksaṃbodhimabhisaṃbudhyate / dānapāramitāṃ śīlakṣāntivīryadhyānaprajñāpāramitāñca /
body.translated_text: Here, the <s>Bodhisattva</s>, gradually fulfilling the six <s>pāramitās</s>, fully awakens to the unsurpassed, perfect awakening (<s>anuttarā samyaksaṃbodhi</s>): the perfection of generosity (<s>dānapāramitā</s>), the perfection of moral conduct (<s>śīlapāramitā</s>), the perfection of patience (<s>kṣāntipāramitā</s>), the perfection of vigor (<s>vīryapāramitā</s>), the perfection of meditation (<s>dhyānapāramitā</s>), and the perfection of wisdom (<s>prajñāpāramitā</s>).

body.text: tatra katamā bodhisattvasya dānapāramitā / navākāraṃ dānaṃ bodhisattvasya dānapāramitetyucyate / svabhāvadānaṃ sarvadānaṃ duṣkaradānaṃ sarvatomukhaṃ dānaṃ satpuruṣadānaṃ sarvākāradānaṃ vighātārthikadānamihāmutrasukhaṃ dānaṃ viśuddhadānaṃ ca /
body.translated_text: There, what is the <s>Bodhisattva</s>'s perfection of generosity (<s>dānapāramitā</s>)? The ninefold giving of the <s>Bodhisattva</s> is called the perfection of generosity: giving by nature (<s>svabhāvadāna</s>), all-giving (<s>sarvadāna</s>), difficult giving (<s>duṣkaradāna</s>), all-directional giving (<s>sarvatomukhadāna</s>), giving of a good person (<s>satpuruṣadāna</s>), all-aspected giving (<s>sarvākāradāna</s>), giving for overcoming adversity (<s>vighātārthikadāna</s>), giving that is pleasant here and hereafter (<s>ihāmutrasukhadāna</s>), and pure giving (<s>viśuddhadāna</s>).

body.text: kaśca dānasya svabhāvaḥ / yā cetanā sarvapariṣkāra-svadehanirapekṣasya bodhisattvasya kevalādhyātmikavastuparityāgāya kāyavākkarmānavadyaśca sarvadeyavastuparityāgaḥ / saṃvarasthāyinaḥ āgamadṛṣṭeḥ phaladarśino yo yenārthī tasya ca tadvastupratipādanā bodhisattvasya dānasvabhāvo veditavyaḥ /
body.translated_text: And what is the nature of giving (<s>dānasvabhāva</s>)? The intention (<s>cetanā</s>) of a <s>Bodhisattva</s> who is indifferent to all possessions and his own body, for the relinquishing of purely internal things; the blameless physical and verbal action of relinquishing all things to be given; of one who abides in the precepts, who has the view based on scripture, and who sees the fruit—the bestowal of whatever thing to whichever being is in need of it—this should be understood as the <s>Bodhisattva</s>'s nature of giving.

body.text: tatra sarvadānaṃ katamat / sarvamucyate samāsato dvividhaṃ deyavastu / ādhyātmikaṃ bāhyañca / tatra ā majjñaḥ svadehaparityāgo bodhisattvasya kevalādhyātmikavastuparityāga ityucyate / yatpunarbodhisattvo vāntāśināṃ sattvānāmarthe bhuktvā bhuktvā 'nnapānaṃ vamati / tatsaṃsṛṣṭamādhyātmikabāhyavastudānaṃ bodhisattvasyetyucyate / etadyathoktaṃ sthāpayitvā pariśiṣṭadeyavastuparityāgo bāhyadeyavastuparityāgaḥ evocyate / tatra bodhisattvaḥ pareṣāṃ dehārthināṃ samāsato dvābhyāmākārābhyāṃ svadehamanuprayacchati / yathākāmakaraṇīyaṃ vā paravaśyaṃ paravidheyamātmānaṃ pareṣāmanuprayacchati / tadyathāpi nāma kaścit pareṣāṃ
body.translated_text: There, what is all-giving (<s>sarvadāna</s>)? 'All' is said to refer to, in brief, a twofold category of things to be given: internal (<s>ādhyātmika</s>) and external (<s>bāhya</s>). There, the relinquishing of one's own body down to the marrow is called the <s>Bodhisattva</s>'s relinquishing of purely internal things. And when a <s>Bodhisattva</s>, for the sake of beings who eat vomited food, eats food and drink and then vomits it—that is called the <s>Bodhisattva</s>'s giving of things mixed as both internal and external. Setting aside what has been described, the relinquishing of remaining things to be given is called the relinquishing of external things to be given. There, the <s>Bodhisattva</s>, for those who desire his body, gives his own body in two ways, in brief: one gives oneself to others as subject to their will, obedient, to be used as they wish—just as, for example, someone

body.text: bhaktācchādanahetordāsabhāvamupagacchet / evameva nirāmiṣacitto bodhisattvaḥ paramabodhikāmaḥ parahitasukhakāmo dānapāramittāṃ paripūrayitukāmo yathākaraṇīyaṃ pareṣāṃ vaśyaṃ paravidheyamātmānaṃ pareṣāmanuprayacchati / karacaraṇanayanaśiro 'ṅgapratyaṅgārthināṃ māṃsarudhirasnāyvarthināṃ yāvanmajjāyināṃ yāvanmajjānamanuprayacchati / dvābhyāmeva kāraṇābhyāṃ bodhisattvo bāhyaṃ vastu sattvebhyaḥ parityajati / yathāsukhaparibhogāya vā yācitakamanuprayacchati / tadvaśitvāya vā sarveṇa sarva nirmuktena cittenānuprayacchati / na ca punarbodhisattvaḥ sarvamādhyātmikabāhyaṃ vastvaviśeṣeṇaiva sarvathā ca sattvānāṃ dadāti / kiñca bodhisattvo dvividhādasmādādhyātmikabāhyādvastunaḥ sattvānāṃ dadāti / kathaṃ na dadāti / yadasmādādhyātmikabāhyādvastunaḥ sattvānāṃ dānaṃ sukhāyaiva syānna tu hitāya naiva vāsukhāya nāpi hitāya tadbodhisattvaḥ pareṣāṃ na dadāti / yatpunarhitāya syānnāvaśyaṃ sukhāyā-sukhāya vā punarhitāya ca tadvodhisattvaḥ pareṣāṃ dānaṃ dadāti / ityayaṃ tāvaddānasya cādānasya ca samāsanirdeśaḥ /
body.translated_text: enters into servitude for the sake of food and clothing for others. Even so, the <s>Bodhisattva</s>, with a mind free from material attachment, desiring supreme awakening, desiring the benefit and happiness of others, desiring to fulfill the perfection of generosity, gives himself to others as subject to their will, obedient, to be used as they wish. To those who desire hands, feet, eyes, head, limbs, and minor limbs, to those who desire flesh, blood, and sinews, down to those who desire marrow—one gives up to the marrow. It is for two reasons alone that the <s>Bodhisattva</s> relinquishes external things to beings: one gives what is requested for comfortable enjoyment, or one gives everything whatsoever with a completely released mind for the purpose of mastery over it. But the <s>Bodhisattva</s> does not give all internal and external things indiscriminately to beings in every way. Rather, the <s>Bodhisattva</s> gives from these internal and external things to beings in a twofold way. How does one not give? When giving from these internal and external things to beings would be for their pleasure only but not for their benefit, or would be neither for their pleasure nor for their benefit—that the <s>Bodhisattva</s> does not give to others. But when it would be for their benefit, whether or not necessarily for their pleasure, or even when unpleasant but for their benefit—that the <s>Bodhisattva</s> gives to others. Thus, this is the summary instruction on giving and not-giving.

body.text: ataḥ paraṃ vistaravibhāgo veditavyaḥ / iha bodhisattvaḥ parotpīḍanāya [paravadhāya] paravañcanāya cāyogavihitena copanimantritamātmānaṃ paravaśyaṃ paravidheyaṃ na dadāti / apyeva nāma bodhisattvaḥ śatakṛtvaḥ sahasrakṛtvaḥ svajīvitaparityāgamapi pareṣāmantikādabhyupagacchet / natveva rājñayā parārādhanārthaṃ parotpīḍanāṃ paravadhaṃ paravañcanāṃ vā kuryāt / yadi ca bodhisattvaḥ śuddhāśayo bhavati dānamārabhya so 'pi sattvakārye prabhūte karaṇīye pratyupasthite svadehāṅgapratyaṅgayācanake ca pratyupasthite na svadehāṅgapratyaṅgānyanuprayacchati / tatkasya hetoḥ / na hyasya bodhisattvasya dānamārabhya śuddhāśayasya punaḥ kenacitparyāyeṇedaṃ dātavyamasmai dātanyamiti bhavati cetasaḥ saṃkocaḥ / tasmādasau bodhisattvo yadāśayaśuddhyarthaṃ pratyupasthitaṃ sattvakāryamadhyupekṣya dadyāt so 'syāśayaḥ śuddha iti na
body.translated_text: Hereafter, the detailed differentiation is to be understood. Here, a <s>Bodhisattva</s> does not give himself over to be controlled and directed by others for the purpose of harming others, [killing others,] or deceiving others, even when solicited by one who has no rightful claim. Indeed, a <s>Bodhisattva</s> would accept the giving up of his own life a hundred times, a thousand times, at the request of others — but he would never, by royal command or for the sake of pleasing another, harm, kill, or deceive others. And even if the <s>Bodhisattva</s> is of pure intention regarding giving, when there is abundant work for beings to be done that has arisen and [simultaneously] supplicants requesting his bodily limbs and members have come forward, he does not give his bodily limbs and members. For what reason? Because for this <s>Bodhisattva</s> of pure intention regarding giving, there is no mental shrinking whatsoever regarding what should be given or to whom it should be given. Therefore, that <s>Bodhisattva</s> — because if he were to give, neglecting the work for beings that has arisen, for the sake of purifying his intention, his intention [would not actually be] pure —

body.text: pratyupasthitaṃ sattvakāryamadhyupekṣya dadāti / na ca mārakāyikeṣu deveṣu yācanakeṣu viheṭhābhiprāyeṣu pratyupasthiteṣu svadehamaṅgavibhāgaśo dadāti / mā haiva teṣāmadhimātrā kṣatiścopahatiśca bhaviṣyatīti yathā mārakāyikeṣu deveṣu / eva tadādiṣṭeṣu sattveṣu veditavyam / nāpi conmattakṣiptacitteṣu bodhisattvaḥ svadehamaṅgavibhāgaśo 'nuprayacchati / na hi te svacitte 'vasthitāḥ / nārthino mṛgayante / nānyatra vipralāpaḥ / sa teṣāmasvatantratvāccetasaḥ tasmānna dadāti / etānākārān sthāpayitvā etadviparyayāt svadehaṃ tāvadbodhisattvaḥ paravidheyatayā vā 'ṅgapratyaṅgavibhāgaśo vārthibhyaḥ parityajati / evantāvadbodhisattvasyādhyātmikasya vastuno dānañcādānañca veditavyam /
body.translated_text: does not give while neglecting the work for beings that has arisen. Nor does he give his body limb by limb when <s>Mārakāyika</s> gods have come as supplicants with the intention of causing harm — [thinking:] 'Let there not be excessive injury and damage to them.' Just as with the <s>Mārakāyika</s> gods, so it is to be understood with beings instigated [by Māra]. Nor does the <s>Bodhisattva</s> give his body limb by limb to those who are mad or disturbed in mind. For they are not established in their own minds; they do not truly seek what they request; and it is nothing but incoherent speech. Because of their lack of self-control of mind, he does not give to them. Setting aside these [exceptional] cases, in the opposite circumstances, the <s>Bodhisattva</s> indeed gives up his own body — either as one submitting to another's direction, or limb by limb to those who request it. Thus, the giving and non-giving of the <s>Bodhisattva</s>'s internal possessions is to be understood.
