body.text: bāhyātpunarvastuno bodhisattvo yāni viṣāgniśastramadyāni sattvānāmupaghātāya tāni nānuprayacchatyarthibhyaḥ ātmopaghātāya vā yācitānyarthināṃ paropaghātāya [vā] / yāni punarviṣāgniśasramadyānyanugrahāya sattvānāṃ tāni bodhisattvo dadātyarthibhya ātmano vā 'nugrahāya yācitānyarthināṃ parānugrahāya vā / punarna ca bodhisattvaḥ parakīyaṃ draviṇamaviśvāsyaṃ parebhyo 'nuprayacchati / na ca bodhisattvaḥ sāñcaritreṇa paradāramupasaṃhṛtya pareṣāmanuprayacchati / na ca saprāṇakaṃ pānabhojanamanuprayacchati / yadapi [rati]krīḍopasaṃhitamanarthopasaṃhitaṃ sattvānāṃ bodhisattvasya deyaṃ vastu tadapi bodhisattvo 'rthibhyo na dadāti / tatkasya hetoḥ / yadyapi tadvastu teṣāṃ cittaprasādamātrakamutpādayed bodhisattvasyāntike / apitu vipulataramasya taddānamanarthaṃ kuryādyaddhetorasau madaṃ pramādaṃ duścaritamadhyāpadyamānaḥ kāyasya bhedādapāyeṣūpapadyate / sa cetpunastadratikrīḍādikaṃ va tu nāpāyagamanāya bhavennāpi cākuśalamūlopacayāya kāmaṃ tadbodhisattvastādṛśaṃ ratikrīḍādikaṃ vasta cittaprasādahetoranupracchedarthibhyastenāpi vastunā saṃgrahāya paripākāya / kīdṛśaṃ punā ratikrīḍāvastu bodhisattvo na dadātyarthibhyaḥ /
body.translated_text: Regarding external possessions: the <s>Bodhisattva</s> does not give poisons, fire, weapons, or intoxicants to supplicants for the purpose of harming beings — whether requested for self-harm or for harming others. But poisons, fire, weapons, and intoxicants that serve for the welfare of beings — these the <s>Bodhisattva</s> does give to supplicants, whether requested for one's own welfare or for the welfare of others. Furthermore, the <s>Bodhisattva</s> does not give away the property of others that has not been entrusted to him. Nor does the <s>Bodhisattva</s>, having seduced another's wife through deceit, give her to others. Nor does he give food and drink that contain living creatures. Whatever objects of entertainment and amusement that are connected with non-benefit for beings — the <s>Bodhisattva</s> does not give those to supplicants either. For what reason? Even though that object might produce a momentary satisfaction of mind toward the <s>Bodhisattva</s>, nevertheless, that giving would produce more extensive non-benefit for the [recipient], since engaging in intoxication, heedlessness, and misconduct because of it, at the breaking up of the body he would be reborn in the lower realms. But if that object of entertainment and amusement would not lead to rebirth in the lower realms, nor to the accumulation of unwholesome roots, then the <s>Bodhisattva</s> may freely give such objects of entertainment and amusement as produce mental satisfaction, for the purpose of gathering and maturing supplicants through that very object. What kind of entertainment does the <s>Bodhisattva</s> not give to supplicants?

body.text: kidṛśaṃ dadāti / tadyathā mṛgavadhaśikṣāṃ bodhisattvo na dadāti / kṣudrayajñeṣu ca mahārambheṣu yeṣu bahavaḥ prāṇinaḥ saṃghātamāpadya jīvitādvyaparopyante / tadrūpān yajñānna svayaṃ yajati na parairyājayati / nāpi ca devakuleṣu paśuvadhamanuprayacchati / na ca prabhūtaprāṇyāśritān [deśān] jalajairvā [sthalajairvā] prāṇibhiradhyuṣitāṃsteṣāṃ prāṇināmuparodhāya yācito 'nuprayacchati /
body.translated_text: What kind does he give? For example, the <s>Bodhisattva</s> does not give instruction in hunting animals. And in great sacrifices of great violence, where many living beings are brought together and killed — he himself does not perform such sacrifices, nor does he have others perform them. Nor does he give slaughter of animals at temples. Nor, when requested, does he give away lands inhabited by many living creatures — [regions] teeming with aquatic or terrestrial beings — for the destruction of those creatures.

body.text: na jālāni na yantrāṇi na jālayantraśikṣāṃ prāṇināmuparodhāya yācito 'nuprayacchati / nāpyākrośāya vadhāya bandhāya daṇḍanāya kāraṇāya śatrūṇāṃ śatrumanuprayacchati / samāsato bodhisattvo yatkiñcit parasattvotpīḍayā parasattvabādhāya sattvānāṃ ratikrīḍāvastu tatsarvaṃbodhisattvo na dadātyarthibhyaḥ / yāni punarimāni vicitrāṇi hastyaśvarathayānavāhanāni vastrālaṅkārāṇi praṇītāni ca pānabhojanāni nṛttagītavāditaśikṣā nṛttagītavāditabhājanāni ca gandhamālyavilepanaṃ vicitraśca bhāṇḍopaskara udyānāni ca gṛhāṇi striyaśca paricaryāyai vividheṣu ca śilpakarmasthāneṣu śikṣā ityevaṃrūpaṃ ratikrīḍāvastu bodhisattvaścittaprasādahetorarthibhyo 'nuprayacchati / na ca bodhisattvaḥ amātrayā 'pathyaṃ vā glānāyārthine 'pi pānabhojanamanuprayacchati / na tṛpteṣu lolupajātīyeṣu sattveṣu praṇītaṃ pānabhojanamanuprayacchati / nāpi ca śokārtānāṃ sattvānāmātmodbandhanāya vā tāḍnāya vā viṣabhakṣaṇāya vā prapātapatanāya vā kāmakāraṃ dadāti / na ca bodhisattvo mātāpitaraṃ sarveṇa sarvaṃmarthibhyo 'nuprayacchati / tathāhi bodhisattvasya mātāpitaraṃ paramaguru-sthānīyamāpāyakaṃ poṣakaṃ saṃvardhakaṃ tadbodhisattvena dīrgharātraṃ śirasodvahatā na khedamāpattavyam / tayoścādhamanabandhaka sthāpanavikraye ātmā vaśyo vidheyo dātavyaḥ / tatkathaṃ bodhisattvaḥ parebhyo 'nupradātumutsaheta kutaḥ punaḥ pradadyāt / nāpi bodhisattvo rājā mūrdhābhiṣiktaḥ prabhuḥ sve pṛthivīmaṇḍale sattvānāṃ saparigrahāṇāṃ parakīyaṃ putradāraṃ pareṣāmantikādācchidya pareṣāmanuprayacchati / nānyatra kṛtsnaṃ grāmaṃ vā grāmapradeśaṃ vā janapadapradeśaṃ vā bhogamanuprayacchet / yathā mamābhūttathā te bhavatviti / na ca bodhisattvaḥ svaṃ putradāraṃ dāsīdāsakarmakarapauruṣeyaparigrahaṃ samyagasaṃjñaptamakāmakaṃ vimanaskaṃ pareṣāmarthināmanuprayacchati / samyak saṃjñaptamapi ca sumanaskaṃ chandajātaṃ nāmitreṣu na yakṣarākṣaseṣu na raudrakarmasu pratipādayati / nāpi ca dāsabhāvāya pratipādayati putradāraṃ sukumāraṃ kulaputraṃ janam / na ca bodhisattvo 'dhimātraparapīḍāpravṛtteṣu raudrakarmasu yācanakeṣu rājyapradānaṃ dadāti / rājyādapi ca tāṃstathāvidhān pudgalāṃścyāvayati sa cet pratibalo bhavati cyāvayitum / na ca bodhisattvo mātāpitrorantikādbhogānācchidya yācanakebhyaḥ prayacchati / yathā mātāpitrorevaṃ putradāradāsīdāsakarmakarapauruṣeyebhyaḥ / nāpi ca
body.translated_text: Nor does he give nets or traps or instruction in nets and traps when asked, for the destruction of living creatures. Nor does he give over enemies to [their] enemies for the purpose of reviling, killing, binding, punishing, or torturing. In summary, the <s>Bodhisattva</s> does not give to supplicants any object of entertainment whatsoever that involves the oppression or injury of other beings. But these various things — elephants, horses, chariots, vehicles, conveyances, garments, ornaments, fine food and drink, instruction in dance, song, and music, and the instruments for dance, song, and music, perfumes, garlands, ointments, various household goods, gardens, houses, women for attendance, and instruction in various arts and crafts — such objects of entertainment the <s>Bodhisattva</s> gives to supplicants as a cause for their mental satisfaction. The <s>Bodhisattva</s> does not give immoderate or unwholesome food and drink to a sick supplicant. He does not give fine food and drink to satiated, greedy-natured beings. Nor does he freely give [the means] for self-hanging, self-striking, poison-eating, or falling from a precipice to beings afflicted with grief. The <s>Bodhisattva</s> does not under any circumstances give his parents to supplicants. For indeed, the <s>Bodhisattva</s>'s parents hold the position of supreme teacher — they are nourishers, sustainers, and rearers; the <s>Bodhisattva</s>, even carrying them on his head for a long time, should not become weary. And rather than placing them in a degrading, enslaving, depositing, or selling [situation], he should give himself as one to be controlled and directed [instead]. How then could the <s>Bodhisattva</s> dare to give [his parents] to others, let alone actually give them? Nor does the <s>Bodhisattva</s>, being a consecrated king with sovereignty over his own domain, seize the wives and children of [his subjects who are] beings with dependents from others and give them to others. Nor does he give away an entire village, or part of a village, or part of a region, or possessions otherwise [than rightfully] — [saying:] 'As it was mine, so let it be yours.' Nor does the <s>Bodhisattva</s> give his own wife, children, servants, workers, or dependents to supplicants when they have not been properly informed, are unwilling, and are displeased. And even when properly informed, willing, and consenting, he does not hand them over to enemies, to <s>Yakṣas</s> and <s>Rākṣasas</s>, or to those engaged in cruel deeds. Nor does he hand over to slavery his wife, children, or persons of gentle birth. The <s>Bodhisattva</s> does not give sovereignty to supplicants who engage in excessively harmful and cruel deeds. He even removes such persons from sovereignty, if he has the power to do so. Nor does the <s>Bodhisattva</s>, having seized possessions from his parents, give them to supplicants. As with parents, so also with his wife, children, servants, workers, and dependents. Nor

body.text: mātāpitaraṃ bādhitvā vistareṇa yāvatkarmakarapauruṣeyaṃ bādhitvā parebhyo yācanakebhyo deyavastu parityajati / dharmaṇa cāsāhasena bodhisattvo bhogān saṃhṛtya dānaṃ dadāti nādharmeṇa sāhasena / na paramutpīḍyopahatya na ca buddhānāṃ bhagavatāṃ śāsane bodhisattvo vyavasthitaḥ śikṣāṃ vyatikramya kathañcit dānaṃ dadāti / dānañca dadad bodhisattvaḥ sarvasattveṣu samacitto dadāti dakṣiṇīyabuddhimupasthāpya mitrāmitrodāsīneṣu guṇavatsu doṣasatsu hīneṣu tulyeṣu viśiṣṭeṣu sukhiteṣu duḥkhiteṣu ca / na ca bodhisattvo yathoktādyathāpratijñātādyācanakāya nyūnaṃ dāna dadāti / nānyatra sama vā adhikaṃ vā / na ca bodhisattvaḥ praṇītaṃ vastu pratijñāya lūhaṃ pratyavaraṃ dadāti / nānyatralūhaṃ pratyavaraṃ pratijñāya praṇītaṃ dadāti saṃvidyamāne praṇīte / na ca bodhisattvo vimanasko na kruddhaḥ kṣubhitamānaso dānaṃ dadāti / nāpi ca dānaṃ dattvā nindayati punaḥ punaḥ parikīrtanatayā evaṃ caivañca tvaṃ mayā dānenānugṛhītaḥ savardhito 'bhyuddhṛto veti / na ca bodhisattvo nihīnapuruṣasyāpi dānaṃ dadadapaviddhamasatkṛtyānuprayacchati prāgeva guṇavataḥ /
body.translated_text: does he abandon material objects intended for supplicants by oppressing his parents, and in detail, up to his workers and dependents. The <s>Bodhisattva</s> gives gifts having gathered possessions righteously and without violence — not through unrighteousness or violence. Not by oppressing or injuring others. And the <s>Bodhisattva</s>, established in the teaching of the <s>Buddhas</s>, the <s>Bhagavāns</s>, does not in any way give gifts by transgressing the training. And while giving, the <s>Bodhisattva</s> gives with an equal mind toward all beings, establishing the attitude that [all recipients are] fields worthy of offerings — whether toward friends, enemies, or neutral persons; toward those with qualities or those with faults; toward the low, the equal, or the distinguished; toward those in happiness or those in suffering. The <s>Bodhisattva</s> does not give less than what was promised or committed to the supplicant. Nor [does he give] to another [instead], whether equal or more. The <s>Bodhisattva</s> does not give a coarse, inferior thing having promised a fine one. Nor elsewhere, having promised a coarse, inferior thing, does he give a fine one when a fine one is available. The <s>Bodhisattva</s> does not give with a displeased mind, nor angry, nor with an agitated mind. Nor, having given, does he repeatedly reproach [the recipient] by publicizing: 'In such and such ways you have been benefited by me with gifts, sustained, and uplifted.' The <s>Bodhisattva</s> does not give even to an inferior person dismissively and without respect — how much less to one endowed with virtues.

body.text: na ca bodhisattvo vividhavipratipattisthitānāmuddhatānāmasaṃvṛtātmanāṃ
body.translated_text: Nor does the <s>Bodhisattva</s>, toward supplicants who are in various states of transgression, who are agitated, unrestrained,

body.text: yācanakānāmākrośakānāṃ roṣakāṇāṃ paribhāṣakāṇāṃ vipratipattyā khinnamānaso dānaṃ dadāti / nānyatra teṣāmevāntike bodhisattvo bhūyasyā mātrayā kleśāveśaprakṛtitāmavagamyānukampācittamupasthāpya dānaṃ dadāti / na cāsaddṛṣṭyā parāmṛṣṭaṃ [dānaṃ] dadāti / tadyathā mahāraudrayajñeṣu na hiṃsādānena dharmaṃ pratyeti / nāpi kautakamaṅgalapratisaṃyuktaṃ dānaṃ dadāti / nāpi suviśuddhenāpi sarvākāreṇa dānamātrakeṇa laukikalokottarāṃ vairāgyaviśuddhiṃ pratyeti nānyatra / saṃbhāramātrakatayā viśuddherdānaṃ dhārayati / na ca phaladarśī dadāti / sarvañca dānamanuttarāyāṃ samyak sambodhau pariṇāmayati / sarvaprakārasya dānasya sarvaṃ prakāraṃ yathābhūtaṃ phalaṃ vipāke 'bhisaṃpratyayajāto bodhisattvo 'parapratyayo 'nanyaneyo dānaṃ dadāti tadyathā 'nnado balavān bhavati / vastrado varṇavān yānadaḥ sukhitaḥ cakṣuṣmān pradīpada ityevamādi vistareṇa veditavyam / na ca bodhisattvo dāridryabhayabhīto dānaṃ dadāti / nānyatra kāruṇyābhiprāya eva / na ca bodhisattvo yācanakānāmapratirūpaṃ dānaṃ dadāti / tadyathā yatīnāmucchiṣṭaṃ vā pānabhojanamuccāraprasrāvakheṭaśiṃghāṇakavāntaviriktapūyarudhiṃrasaṃsṛṣṭaṃ
body.translated_text: who revile, are angry, or reproach him — becoming mentally vexed by their transgressions — give with [such vexation]. Rather, all the more, understanding the natural proclivity to affliction of those very [supplicants], generating a mind of compassion toward them, the <s>Bodhisattva</s> gives. He does not give gifts that are tainted by wrong views — for example, he does not approach the <s>Dharma</s> through gifts of harm at great and cruel sacrifices. Nor does he give gifts connected with superstitious rites and omens. Nor, even through giving that is thoroughly pure in every way, does he approach worldly or supramundane purification through dispassion by mere giving alone — and nothing else. He maintains giving only as a part of the accumulation [of merit], understanding that purification [comes] from the [full] accumulation. He does not give with an eye to the fruit. He dedicates all giving to the unsurpassed perfect awakening. Having arrived at conviction — independently, not led by others — regarding the true fruit and ripening of giving in all its aspects, the <s>Bodhisattva</s> gives. For example: the giver of food becomes powerful; the giver of clothing becomes beautiful; the giver of vehicles becomes happy; the giver of eyes becomes clear-sighted; the giver of lamps [becomes similarly] — and so on, to be understood in detail. The <s>Bodhisattva</s> does not give out of fear of poverty — but only out of the intention of compassion. The <s>Bodhisattva</s> does not give unsuitable gifts to supplicants — for example, to ascetics, leftover or contaminated food mixed with urine, feces, phlegm, snot, vomit, purgatives, pus, or blood,

body.text: vā abhidūṣitaṃ vā / anākhyātamapratisaṃveditamodanakulmāṣamutsarjanadharmī / tathā
body.translated_text: or spoiled [food]. [Nor does he give] unannounced, unnotified [food of] cakes and porridge that are to be discarded. Likewise,

body.text: apalāṇḍubhakṣāṇāṃ palāṇḍusaṃmiśraṃ palāṇḍusaṃsṛṣṭam / evamamāṃsabhakṣāṇām / amadyapānāṃ madyamiśraṃ madyasaṃsṛṣṭaṃ vā / tathā 'pratirūpe karmaṇi viniyojya bodhisattvo na pareṣāṃ dānaṃ dadāti / ityevaṃbhāgīyamapratirūpaṃ dānaṃ na dadāti / na ca punarbodhisattvo yācanakaṃ punaḥ punaryācanatayā gatapratyāgatikatayā sevāvṛttasaṃvidhānena parikliśya dānaṃ dadāti / nānyatra yācitamātra eva / na ca bodhisattvaḥ kīrtiśabdaślokamiśritaṃ dānaṃ dadāti / na [ca] parataḥ pratikārasanniśritaṃ na śakratvamāratvacakravartitvaiśvaryasanniśritaṃ [dadāti] / na ca pareṣāṃ kuhanārthaṃ dānaṃ dadāti / kaccinmāṃ pare rājāno vā rājamahāmātyā vā naigamajanapadā brāhmaṇagṛhapatayo dhaninaḥ śreṣṭhinaḥ sārthavāhā dātāraṃ dānapatiṃ viditvā satkuryurgurūkuryurmānayeyuḥ pūjayeyuriti / na ca kārpaṇyadānaṃ dadāti / alpādapi viśadaṃ dadāti prāgeva prabhūtāt / na ca pareṣāṃ vipralambhāya dānaṃ dadāti /
body.translated_text: To those who do not eat onions, [one should not give food] mixed or combined with onions. Likewise for those who do not eat meat. To those who do not drink liquor, [one should not give drink] mixed or combined with liquor. Similarly, a <s>Bodhisattva</s> does not give gifts to others by employing them in improper activity. Thus, he does not give such kinds of improper gifts. Moreover, a <s>Bodhisattva</s> does not give gifts to a supplicant by afflicting him through repeatedly asking, through coming and going, or through arrangements of service and attendance—[he gives] only upon the mere request. A <s>Bodhisattva</s> does not give gifts mixed with [desire for] fame, reputation, and praise. He does not give relying on reciprocation from others, nor relying on [attaining] the sovereignty of <s>Śakra</s>, <s>Māra</s>, or a <s>Cakravartin</s>. He does not give gifts for the purpose of deceiving others, [thinking:] 'Perhaps others—kings, royal ministers, townspeople, countryfolk, <s>Brāhmaṇas</s>, householders, the wealthy, guild-masters, and caravan-leaders—knowing me as a giver and lord of giving, would honor me, revere me, respect me, and worship me.' He does not give miserly gifts; even from little he gives generously—how much more so from abundance. He does not give gifts for the purpose of deceiving others,

body.text: anena dānena vilobhya viśrambhayitvā paścādenaṃ vipravādayiṣyāmīti / na ca vibhedāya parataḥ pareṣāṃ dānaṃ dadāti / tadyathā dānena grāmaṃ vā grāmapradeśaṃ vā janapadaṃ vā janapadapradeśaṃ vā vibhedya svāmināmantikādācchetsyāmyākramiṣyāmīti / dakṣaśca bodhisattvo bhavatyanalasaśca utthānasampannaḥ svayaṃ ca sannaddhaḥ parikare pūrvaṅgamo deyavastu parityāge svayañca dadāti paraiśca dāpayati na svayaṃ kausīdyaṃ prāviṣkṛtya parānājñāpayati dānāya / mahāntamapi gaṇasannipātamarthināṃ śīlavadduḥśīlānāṃ sanniṣaṇṇaṃ saṃnipatitaṃ viditvā vṛddhāntamupādāya yāvannavakāntaṃ tatsarvaṃ deyavastu gatapratyāgatikatayā punaḥ punaranukrameṇa pratipādayati na ca bodhisattvaḥ prabhūteṣu vipuleṣu vistīrṇeṣu bhogeṣu saṃvidyamāneṣu mitaṃ dānaṃ dadāti / na ca paraviheṭhanāya pareṣāṃ dānaṃ dadāti / ākrośanāya vā roṣaṇatāḍanatarjanakutsanakabandhanacchedanarodhanapravāsanāya vā dānaṃ dadāti / pūrvameva ca dānād bodhisattvaḥ sumanā bhavati dadaccittaṃ prasādayati / dattvā cāvipratisārī bhavati / na ca śāṭhyāddānaṃ dadāti maṇimuktāśaṅkhaśilāvaidūryapravāḍādipratirūpakāṇi tadāśāvatāṃ sattvānām / na ca bodhisattvena kiñcidalpaṃ [vā prabhūtaṃ vā] deyavastu yanna prāgeva cetasā sarvasattvānāṃ
body.translated_text: [thinking:] 'Having lured and gained the confidence of this person through this gift, I shall afterward cheat him.' Nor does the <s>Bodhisattva</s> give gifts to others for the purpose of causing division, such as [thinking:] 'By means of this gift, having divided a village, a district of a village, a country, or a district of a country, I shall seize it and take it from its masters.' The <s>Bodhisattva</s> is skillful, diligent, and energetic in the relinquishment of things to be given; he gives by himself and causes others to give, being armed himself and leading his retinue in the foregoing—he does not make himself manifest laziness and command others to give. When he knows that a great assembly of supplicants—whether virtuous or of poor conduct—has gathered and assembled, from the most senior down to the most junior, he distributes all the things to be given to them in order, going and coming [among them] again and again. The <s>Bodhisattva</s> does not give limited gifts when abundant, vast, and extensive possessions are available. Nor does he give gifts to others for the purpose of harming them—for the purpose of abuse, angering, striking, threatening, reviling, binding, cutting, imprisoning, or banishing. Already before giving, the <s>Bodhisattva</s> is well-disposed; while giving, he makes the mind serene; and after giving, he is without regret. He does not give gifts through fraud—such as imitation gems, pearls, conch-shells, stones, <s>vaiḍūrya</s>, and corals—to beings who desire such things. And there is no thing to be given by the <s>Bodhisattva</s>, whether small or large, that has not first been mentally released for the sake of all beings.

body.text: nirmuktaṃ bhavati / paścādyācakaḥ svakamiva dhanaṃ yācitakānupradattaṃ bodhisattvādyācate / kālena ca bodhisattvo dānaṃ dadāti nākālena / kalpikamātmanaḥ parasya ca nākalpikam / ācāreṇa nānācāreṇa / avikṣiptena ca cetasā na vikṣiptena / na ca bodhisattvo yācanakamavahasati nāvaspaṇḍayati / ma maṅkubhāvamasyopasaṃharati / na bhṛkuṭīkṛto bhavati / uttānamukhavarṇaḥ smitapūrvaṃṅgamaḥ pūrvābhibhāṣī bhavati / na ca vilambitaṃ tvaritaṃ tvaritaṃ dānaṃ dadāti / ayācito 'pi bodhisattvaḥ svayaṃ pravārayitvā parān yo yenārthī bhavati tasya taddadāti / svayaṃ gṛhītaṃ caiṣāmabhyanujānāti / na ca bodhisattvo dauṣprajñadānaṃ dadāti / dadat prājñadānameva dadāti /
body.translated_text: Afterward, the supplicant asks the <s>Bodhisattva</s> for what has [already] been requested and given, as though it were one's own wealth. The <s>Bodhisattva</s> gives gifts at the proper time, not at an improper time; what is fitting for himself and others, not what is unfitting; with proper conduct, not with improper conduct; with an undistracted mind, not a distracted one. The <s>Bodhisattva</s> does not ridicule or mock the supplicant, nor does he bring about humiliation for him. He is not frowning, but has an open and bright countenance, preceded by a smile, and speaks first. He does not give gifts in a delayed or hurried manner. Even unasked, the <s>Bodhisattva</s>, having himself made the invitation, gives to others whatever each one needs. He also approves of what they themselves have taken. The <s>Bodhisattva</s> does not give gifts unwisely; when giving, he gives only wisely.

body.text: prājñadānaṃ bodhisattvasya katamat / iha bodhisattvaḥ satsu saṃvidyamāneṣu deyadharmeṣu pūrvameva yācanakābhyāgamanādevaṃ cittamabhisaṃskaroti / sa cenme dvau yācanakāvāgacchetāṃ sukhitaścākṛpaṇo 'varākaḥ sanāthaḥ sapratisaraṇaḥ duḥkhitaśca kṛpaṇo varākaḥ anāthaḥ apratisaraṇaḥ / tena mayā sacenme bhogānāṃ dvayorapi santarpaṇāyecchāparipūraye tadā saṃbhavo 'sti ubhau santarpayitavyau / dvayorapīcchā paripūriḥ karaṇīyā / sa cenna tāvadbhogasaṃbhavaḥ syādahaṃ dvayoḥ santarpayeyaṃ yadicchāparipūriñca kuryāṃ sukhitamapahāya duḥkhitāya dānaṃ deyam / akṛpaṇamavarākaṃ sanāthaṃ sapratisaraṇamapahāya kṛpaṇāya varākāya anāthāyāpratisaraṇāya dānaṃ deyamiti / sa evaṃ cittamabhisaṃskṛtya yathābhisaṃskārameva karmaṇā saṃpādayati / sa cetpunaḥ sukhitasya yācanakasyecchāṃ na śaknoti paripūrayituṃ sa tameva pūrvakaṃ svacittābhisaṃskārakalpamupādāya taṃ yācakamevaṃ saṃjñapya preṣayati / asya mayā duḥkhitasya pūrvanisṛṣṭaṃ pūrvapratijñātametaddeyavastu ato mayā 'syaiva pratipāditam / na ca me tvayyadātukāmamanā asti / ato na bhadramukhenāsmākamantike praṇayavimukhatā karaṇīyeti / punaraparaṃ bodhisattvaḥ satsu saṃvidyamāneṣu deyadharmeṣu yāni tāni matsarikulāni bhavanti paramamatsarikulānyāgṛhītapariṣkārāṇi kuṭakuñcakāni yeṣu na jātu śramaṇabrāhmaṇeṣu deyadharme prajāyate tāni bodhisattvaḥ kulānyupasaṃkramya pratisaṃmodya praṇayañca saṃvidhāyaivamāha / aṅga tāvatte bhavantaḥ akośakṣayeṇa mahatā upakāreṇa pratyavasthitā bhavantu / mama gṛhe vipulā bhogā vipulā deyadharmāḥ
body.translated_text: What is the wise giving (<s>prājñadāna</s>) of the <s>Bodhisattva</s>? Here, when things to be given are available, the <s>Bodhisattva</s>, even before the supplicant arrives, prepares his mind thus: 'If two supplicants were to come to me—one happy, not wretched, not destitute, with a protector, with a refuge; and one suffering, wretched, destitute, without a protector, without a refuge—then if my possessions allow the satisfaction of both and the fulfillment of their wishes, both should be satisfied and the wishes of both should be fulfilled. But if the possessions are not sufficient for me to satisfy both and fulfill their wishes, then, setting aside the happy one, the gift should be given to the one who is suffering; setting aside one who is not wretched, not destitute, who has a protector and a refuge, the gift should be given to the wretched, destitute, unprotected one without refuge.' Having thus prepared his mind, he carries out his action just as he has prepared it. If, moreover, he is unable to fulfill the wish of the happy supplicant, he takes up the very resolve he had previously made in his mind and sends that supplicant away, informing him thus: 'This thing to be given was previously released and previously promised by me for this suffering person; therefore I have given it to him. I do not have an unwilling mind toward you. Therefore, with a kind face, do not turn away from us in displeasure.' Furthermore, when things to be given are available, the <s>Bodhisattva</s> approaches those households that are miserly—supremely miserly households with tightly guarded possessions, close-fisted, in which nothing whatsoever to be given to <s>śramaṇas</s> and <s>brāhmaṇas</s> ever arises—and having greeted them and established friendly relations, he speaks thus: 'Come now, good sirs, be established in great benefit without the depletion of your treasury. In my house there are abundant possessions and abundant things to give.

body.text: saṃvidyante / so 'haṃ dānapāramitāparipūraye yācanakenārthī / sa cedyūyaṃ yācanakamārāgayatha mā nirākṛtya visarjayiṣyatha madīyaṃ dhanaṃ deyadharmamādāya tebhyo vā visṛjata yathāsukhameva / athavā taṃ yācanakamasmākamupasaṃharatha dīyamānañca mayā dānamanumodatha / te ca tasya pratiśrutyākośakṣayeṇa priyeṇāyaṃ kulaputro 'smākamārādhitacitto bhavatīti tathā kurvanti / evaṃ hi tena bodhisattvena yeṣāmāyatyāṃ mātsaryamalavinayāya bījamavaropitaṃ bhavati / krameṇa ca tenābhyāsena tena prajñāpūrvakeṇopāyakauśalyena svakamapi parīttaṃ parebhyo dhanamanuprayacchanti / mṛdukamalobhaṃ niśritya madhyaṃ pratilabhante / madhyaṃ niśrityādhimātraṃ pratilabhante / punaraparaṃ bodhisattvo ye 'sya bhavantyācāryopādhyāyāḥ sārdhavihāryantevāsinaḥ sabrahmacāriṇaśca lobhaprakṛtayo lubdhajātīyā ye ca na lubdhajātīyā api tu deyadharmavaikalyādicchāvighātavantastatra bodhisattvo buddhāvaropitaṃ vā dharmā[varopitaṃ vā] saṃghāvaropitaṃ vā dānamayaṃ puṇyakriyāvastu kartukāmasteṣāmevotsṛjati / tān deya dharmāṃstaiḥ kārayati na svayaṃ karoti / evaṃ tena bodhisattvena svayañca bahutaraṃ puṇyaṃ prasūtaṃ bhavati / tadekatyānāñca sabrahmacāriṇāṃ kleśavinayaḥ kṛto bhavati / tadekatyānāṃ dharmecchāparipūriḥ kṛtā bhavati / sattvasaṃgrahaḥ sattvaparipākaśca kṛto bhavati / punaraparaṃ bodhisattvaḥ satsu saṃvidyamāneṣu deyadharmeṣu yācanakamākūṭananimittamātrakeṇaiva jñātvā yathākāmaṃ deyadharmaiḥ pratipādayati / yo 'pi cainamupasaṃkrānto bhavati kūṭavāṇijyanaivaṃ vyaṃsayiṣyāmīti / tasyāpi bhāvamājñāya tadduścaritamanyeṣāmapi tāvacchādayati prāgeva tasyaiva / icchāñcāsya paripūrayati yenāsāvamaṅkurudagro viśāradaḥ saumanasyajāto viprakrāmati / yenāpi ca bodhisattvaḥ kūṭa-kapaṭena vañcito bhavati na cānena sā vañcanā pūrvaṃ pratividdhā bhavati paścācca pratividhyati / pratividhya na ca tena vastunā punastaṃ vyaṃsakaṃ pudgalañcodayati smārayati / sarvañca tacchalakṛta madattādānamasmai bhāvenābhyanumodate / ityevaṃbhāgīyaṃ tāvadbodhisattvasya satsu saṃvidyamāneṣu prājñadānaṃ veditavyam / punaraparaṃ bodhisattvaḥ asatsu asaṃvidyamāneṣu deyadharmeṣu kṛtāvī bodhisattvasteṣu teṣu śilpakarmasthāneṣu sa tadrūpaṃ śilpakarmasthānamāmukhīkaroti /
body.translated_text: I, for the fulfillment of the perfection of generosity (<s>dānapāramitā</s>), am in need of supplicants. If you encounter a supplicant, do not turn him away; take my own wealth—the things to be given—and give them to him as you wish. Or else bring that supplicant to me, and rejoice in the gift I give.' They, having promised, [thinking:] 'This son of good family is pleased with us through benefit without depletion of our treasury,' do accordingly. In this way, by that <s>Bodhisattva</s>, a seed has been sown for the future disciplining of their defilement of miserliness. And gradually, through that practice, through that skillful means preceded by wisdom, they give even their own small [amount of] wealth to others. Depending on mild non-greed, they attain the moderate [level]; depending on the moderate, they attain the intense [level]. Furthermore, the <s>Bodhisattva</s> [considers]: those who are his teachers, preceptors, co-residents, pupils, and fellow practitioners of the holy life who are by nature greedy and of a greedy disposition, and also those who are not of a greedy disposition but whose wish [to give] is obstructed by the lack of things to be given—in those cases, the <s>Bodhisattva</s>, wishing to create meritorious formations (<s>puṇyakriyāvastu</s>) dedicated to the <s>Buddha</s>, the <s>Dharma</s>, or the <s>Saṃgha</s>, releases [the goods] to them; he has them perform [the giving] of those things to be given, and does not do it himself. In this way, by that <s>Bodhisattva</s>, more abundant merit is produced by himself; for some of his fellow practitioners, the disciplining of their defilements is accomplished; for some, the fulfillment of their wish for the <s>Dharma</s> is accomplished; and the gathering and maturation of beings is accomplished. Furthermore, when things to be given are available, the <s>Bodhisattva</s>, upon recognizing a supplicant by a mere gesture or sign, provides him with things to be given as he wishes. And even one who has approached him through deceitful commerce, [thinking:] 'I shall cheat him in this way'—knowing his disposition, the <s>Bodhisattva</s> conceals that person's wrongdoing from others, and all the more so from that person himself. He fulfills his wish, so that the person departs without humiliation, confident, and joyful. And even when the <s>Bodhisattva</s> has been deceived by trickery and fraud—if he did not previously detect the deception but discovers it later—even upon discovering it, he does not on that account accuse or remind that deceitful person. And he wholeheartedly approves of all that was taken from him through trickery as though it had been freely given. Such should be understood as the wise giving of the <s>Bodhisattva</s> when things to be given are available. Furthermore, when the <s>Bodhisattva</s> has no things to give and they are not available, the <s>Bodhisattva</s>, being accomplished in the various arts and crafts, takes up the appropriate art or craft.

body.text: yenālpakṛcchreṇa mahāntaṃ dhanaskandhamabhinirjityādhyāvasati / pareṣāñcitrakatho madhurakathaḥ kalyāṇapratibhāno bodhisattvāstathā dharmadeśanāṃ pravartayati yathā daridrāṇāmapi sattvānāṃ dātukāmatā santiṣṭhate prāgevāḍhyānām / matsariṇāmapi prāgeva tyāgaśīlānām / yāni vā punastāni śrāddhakulāni yeṣvaharahaḥ pravṛtā eva deyadharmā vistīrṇabhogatayā teṣu kuleṣu āgatāgatān yācanakānupasaṃharati / svayameva vā gatvā dāneṣu dīyamāneṣu puṇyeṣu kriyamāṇeṣu dakṣo 'nalasa utthānasampannaścittamabhiprasādya kāyena vācā yathāśaktyā yathābalaṃ vyāpāraṃ gacchati / supratipāditañca taddānaṃ yācanakeṣu karoti / evaṃ hi taddānam / yadupasthāpaka-vaiguṇyād duṣpratipāditaṃ syāt pakṣapatitaṃ vā anādarato vā smṛtisaṃpramoṣato vā tanna bhavati / evaṃ hi bodhisattvaḥ asatsvasaṃvidyamāneṣu bhogeṣu prājñadānasya dātā bhavati yāvadāśayaśuddhi nādhigacchati / śuddhāśayastu bodhisattvo yathaivāpāsamatikramaṃ pratilabhate tathaivākṣayabhogatāṃ janmani pratilabhate / punaraparaṃ bodhisattvo na tīrthikāya randhraprekṣiṇe dharmaṃ mukhoddeśato vā pustakagataṃ vā dadāti / nāpi lobhaprakṛtaye pustakaṃ vikretukāmāya sannidhiṃ vā kartukāmāya / na tu tena jñānenānarthine [jñānenārthine vā] / punaḥ sa cetkṛtārthaḥ pustakena bhavati svayaṃ dadātyasmai yathāsukhameva / sa cedakṛtārtho bhavati yasyārthe tena tatpustakamanvāvartitam / evamasau bodhisattvaḥ ādarśamanyaṃ dṛṣṭvā lekhayitvā vānyaddadāti / sa cennaivādarśaṃ paśyati nāpi lekhayituṃ śaknoti tenādita evaṃ svacittaṃ pratyavekṣitavyam / mā haiva me dharmamātsaryamalaparyavasthitaṃ cittam / mā haivāhamāśayata eva na dātukāmo 'bhilikhitaṃ dharmam / sa cetsa evaṃ pratyavekṣamāṇo jānīyādasti me dharmamātsaryamalasamudācāro 'pi tena bodhisattvenaivaṃ cittamabhisaṃskṛtya dātavyam / evaṃ dharmadānaṃ syāt / yadyahamanena dharmadānena mūka evaṃ syāṃ dṛṣṭe dharme tathāpi mayā 'nadhivāsya kleśaṃ dātavyameva syāddharmadānam / prāgeva jñānasaṃbhāravikalaḥ / sa cetpunaḥ pratyavekṣamāṇo jānīyānnāsti me [dharma] mātsaryamalasamudācāro 'pi tena bodhisattvenaivaṃ pratisaṃśikṣitavyam / aham [ātmanaḥ] kleśanirghātanārthaṃ vā etaddharmadānaṃ dadyāṃ jñānasaṃbhāraparipūraṇārthaṃ vā sattva
body.translated_text: by which, with little effort, he gains and acquires a great mass of wealth. Speaking to others in varied, sweet, and felicitous words, the <s>Bodhisattva</s> delivers <s>Dharma</s>-teachings such that even in poor beings the desire to give arises, how much more so in the wealthy; even in the miserly, how much more in those naturally generous. Or again, in those faithful families where gifts of <s>Dharma</s> are regularly offered day after day due to their abundant possessions—he brings the various supplicants who come to those families. Or going himself, when gifts are being given and merit is being made, he is diligent, not lazy, endowed with initiative, and having inspired their minds, he engages with body and speech according to his ability and power. And he ensures that the gift is well-bestowed upon the supplicants. For in this way that gift—which through the attendant's deficiency might be poorly bestowed, or biased, or careless, or made through lapse of mindfulness—does not [become so]. Thus the <s>Bodhisattva</s>, when possessions are not present or available, becomes a giver of wise giving (<s>prājñadāna</s>) until he attains purification of intention. But the <s>Bodhisattva</s> of purified intention, just as he overcomes misfortune, so too in [each] birth he obtains inexhaustible wealth. Furthermore, the <s>Bodhisattva</s> does not give <s>Dharma</s>—whether by oral instruction or in written form—to a heretic (<s>tīrthika</s>) who is looking for vulnerabilities. Nor to one of greedy nature who wishes to sell the manuscript or to hoard it. Nor [does he give] through that knowledge to one who has no need [or to one who does have need]. Again, if he himself has accomplished his purpose with the manuscript, he gives it to him freely. If he has not accomplished his purpose—the purpose for which that manuscript was being used by him—then the <s>Bodhisattva</s>, having seen or having caused another copy to be written, gives the other. If he neither sees another copy nor is able to have one written, then he should first examine his own mind thus: 'May my mind not be beset by the stain of stinginess regarding <s>Dharma</s>! May I not, from intention alone, be unwilling to give the written <s>Dharma</s>!' If, examining thus, he knows: 'There is in me the occurrence of the stain of <s>Dharma</s>-stinginess'—then that <s>Bodhisattva</s>, having resolved his mind thus, should give. The <s>Dharma</s>-gift would be thus: 'Even if through this gift of <s>Dharma</s> I were to become mute in this present life, still I should give the gift of <s>Dharma</s> without acquiescing to the affliction.' How much more so [should he give] when he would merely be deficient in the accumulation of knowledge. If, examining again, he knows: 'There is no occurrence of the stain of <s>Dharma</s>-stinginess in me'—then that <s>Bodhisattva</s> should train himself thus: 'Would I give this gift of <s>Dharma</s> for the sake of eliminating my own afflictions, or for the sake of completing the accumulation of knowledge, or for the welfare of beings—

body.text: priyatāyaiva vā / so 'haṃ kleśaṃ tāvanna paśyāmi / jñānasaṃbhāramapi dṛṣṭadharmasāmparāyikaṃ prabhūtataramananupradānāt paśyāmi / na padānāt / sāmparāyikameva pratanukaṃ dharmalābhapracuratāyai / ananuprayacchaṃścāhaṃ sarvasattvānāṃ hitasukhāya jñānaṃ samudānaya tasya ca sattvasya tadanyeṣāñca sarvasattvānāṃ priyakārī bhavāmi / anupracchannasyaivaikasya sattvasya priyakārī iti viditvā yathābhūtaṃ sa cedbodhisattvo na dadātyanavadyo bhavatyavipratisārī / asamatikrāntaśca bhavati bodhisattvavṛttam /
body.translated_text: or simply for dearness?' 'I do not see any affliction [in not giving]. But I see that the accumulation of knowledge, both in this life and in future lives, would be more abundant through not giving than through giving. Only the future [accumulation] would be slightly [less], for the sake of abundance of <s>Dharma</s>-acquisition. And by not giving, I gather knowledge for the welfare and happiness of all beings, and I become a doer of what is dear to that being and to all other beings—rather than being a doer of what is dear to only one being in a concealed manner.' Having understood thus, if the <s>Bodhisattva</s> does not give, he is blameless and without remorse, and he has not transgressed the <s>Bodhisattva</s>'s conduct.

body.text: kathañca punarna dadāti / na khalu punarbodhisattvaḥ utsahate yācanakaṃ niṣṭhurayā vācā pratikṣeptum / na te dāsyāmītyapi upāyakauśalyanainaṃ saṃjñapyānupreṣayati / tatredamupāyakauśalyam / prāgeva bodhisattvena sarvapariṣkārāḥ sarvadeyadharmā daśasu dikṣu viśaddhenāśayena buddhabodhisattvānāṃ visṛṣṭā bhavanti vikalpitāstadyathāpi nāma bhikṣurācāryāya vā upādhyāyāya vā cīvaraṃ vikalpayet / sa evaṃ vikalpahetoḥ sarvavicitrodārapariṣkāradeyadharmasannidhiprāpto 'pyāryavaṃśavihārī bodhisattva ityucyate / aprameyapuṇyaprasotā ca bhavati / tañca puṇyamasya nityakālaṃ tadbahulamanaskārasya sarvakālānugatamabhivardhate / sa tān deyadharmān buddhabodhisattvanikṣiptāniva dhārayati / yadi yācanakaṃ paśyati yuktarūpaścāsmin yathepsitaṃ deyadharmapratipādanaṃ paśyati / sa nāsti tat kiñcid buddhabodhisattvānāṃ yatsattveṣu aparityaktamiti viditvā yācanakasyecchāṃ paripūrayati / no cedyuktarūpaṃ samanupaśyati sa tameva kalpamupādāya parakīyametad bhadramukha na caitadyuṣmākamanujñātaṃ dātumiti ślakṣnena vacasā saṃjñapyainaṃ preṣayati / anyadvā tad dviguṇaṃ triguṇaṃ dānamānasatkāraṃ kṛtvānupreṣayati / yenāsau jānīte nāyaṃ bodhisattvo lobhātmakatayā 'smākaṃ na dātukāmaḥ / api tu nūnamasvatantra evaṃ tasmin pustakadharmadāne yena na dadātīti / idamapi bodhisattvasya dharmadānamārabhya prājñadānaṃ veditavyam / punaraparaṃ bodhisattvaḥ sarvadānāni dharmāmiṣābhaya[dānā]ni praryāyato 'pi lakṣaṇato 'pi nirvacanato 'pi hetuphalaprabhedato 'pi yathābhūtaṃ prajānannanuprayacchati / idamapi bodhisattvasya prājñadānaṃ veditavyam / punaraparaṃ bodhisattvaḥ apakāriṣu sattveṣu maitryāśayo dānaṃ dadāti / duḥkhiteṣu karuṇāśayaḥ / guṇavatsu muditāśayaḥ /
body.translated_text: And how does he not give [without transgression]? The <s>Bodhisattva</s> does not venture to reject a supplicant with harsh words—not even saying 'I will not give to you.' Rather, through skillful means, he makes [the supplicant] understand and sends him away. Herein is the skillful means: the <s>Bodhisattva</s> has previously, with purified intention, relinquished and dedicated all his possessions and all gifts of <s>Dharma</s> to the <s>Buddhas</s> and <s>Bodhisattvas</s> in the ten directions—just as a monk would dedicate a robe to his teacher or preceptor. Because of this dedication, even though he is in possession of various noble and excellent possessions and gifts of <s>Dharma</s>, the <s>Bodhisattva</s> is said to be one who dwells in the noble lineage (<s>āryavaṃśavihārī</s>). And he becomes a source of immeasurable merit. And that merit, through his constant mental attention to it at all times, continually increases. He holds those gifts of <s>Dharma</s> as if entrusted by the <s>Buddhas</s> and <s>Bodhisattvas</s>. If he sees a supplicant and it is fitting, he sees the proper occasion for bestowing the desired gift of <s>Dharma</s>. Knowing that 'there is nothing that the <s>Buddhas</s> and <s>Bodhisattvas</s> have not relinquished for beings,' he fulfills the wish of the supplicant. If he does not see it as fitting, he employs that very dedication and says: 'O good sir, this is not mine; it has not been authorized for me to give'—and with gentle words makes him understand and sends him away. Or he renders twice or three times the gift of honor and respect and sends him away. So that the supplicant knows: 'This <s>Bodhisattva</s> is not unwilling to give to us out of greediness; rather, he is simply not autonomous regarding that gift of <s>Dharma</s> in a manuscript, which is why he does not give.' This too is to be known as the <s>Bodhisattva</s>'s wise giving with respect to the gift of <s>Dharma</s>. Furthermore, the <s>Bodhisattva</s>, truly knowing all gifts—gifts of <s>Dharma</s>, material gifts, and gifts of fearlessness—by their synonyms, characteristics, etymologies, and classification of causes and results, gives accordingly. This too is to be known as the <s>Bodhisattva</s>'s wise giving. Furthermore, the <s>Bodhisattva</s> gives to beings who have done him harm with an intention of friendliness (<s>maitrī</s>); to those who are suffering, with an intention of compassion (<s>karuṇā</s>); to those endowed with qualities, with an intention of sympathetic joy (<s>muditā</s>)—

body.text: upakāriṣu mitreṣu suhṛtsūpekṣāśayaḥ / idamapi bodhisattvasya prājñadānaṃ veditavyam /
body.translated_text: and to benefactors, friends, and well-wishers, with an intention of equanimity (<s>upekṣā</s>). This too is to be known as the <s>Bodhisattva</s>'s wise giving.

body.text: punaraparaṃ bodhisattvo dānavibandhanamapi dānavibandhapratipakṣamapi yathābhūtaṃ prajānāti / tatra catvāro dānavibandhāḥ / pūrvako 'nabhyāsaḥ / deyadharmaparīttatāvaikalyam / agre manorame ca vastuni gṛddhiḥ āyatyāñca bhogasampatti phaladarśanābhinandanatā / yataśca bodhisattvasya deyadharmeṣu saṃvidyamāneṣu yācanake ca samyagupasthite dāne cittaṃ na krāmati / so 'nabhyāsakṛto me 'yaṃ doṣa iti laghu ladhveva prajñayā pratisidhyati / evañca punaḥ pratividhyati / nūnaṃ mayā pūrvaṃ dānaṃ na dattaṃ yena me etarhi samyak saṃvidyamāneṣu bhogeṣu samyak pratyupasthite ca yācanake dāne cittaṃ na krāmati / sa cedetarhina pratisaṃkhyāya dāsyāmi punarapi me āyatyāṃ dānavidveṣo bhaviṣyati / sa eva pratibidhya dānapratibandhapratipakṣa niśṛtya pratisaṃkhyāya dadāti / nābhyāsakṛtadoṣānusārī bhavati na tadvaśagaḥ / punaraparaṃ bodhisattvasya sa cedyad yācanake samyak pratyupasthite parīttabhogatayā dāne cittaṃ na krāmati sa ta vighātakṛta dānavipratibandhahetuṃ laghu-laghveva prajñayā pratividhya tadvighātakṛtaṃ duḥkhamadhivāsayan pratisaṃkhyāya kāruṇyāddānaṃ dadāti / tasyaivaṃ bhavati / pūrvakarmadoṣeṇa vā paravineyatayā vā mayā bahūni pragāḍhāni kṣut pipāsādikāni duḥkhānyanubhūtāni bhave vinā parānugraham / yadi ca me maraṇāya kālakriyāyai savarteta etaddānakṛta parānugrahahetuka dṛṣṭe dharme duḥkha tathāpi me dānameva śreyo na tu yācanakanirākaraṇam / prāgeva yaḥ kaścidyena kenacicchākapatreṇa jīvati ityevaṃ bodhisattvastadvighātakṛtaṃ dukhamadhivāsya dāna dadāti / panarapara bodhisattvasya samyag yācake pratyupasthite sa cedadhimātramanāpatvādagryatvāddeyavastuno dāne citta na krāmati ta bodhisattvo gardhakṛt doṣa laghu-laghveva pratijñayā pratividhya duḥkhe me eṣa sukhasaṃjñāviparyāsaḥ āyatyāṃ duḥkhajanaka iti viparyāsaparijñānāttañca prahāya prati saṃkhyāya tadvastu dadāti / punaraparaṃ bodhisattvasya sa ceddānaṃ dattvā dānaphale
body.translated_text: Furthermore, the <s>Bodhisattva</s> truly understands both the obstacles to giving (<s>dānavibandha</s>) and the antidotes to those obstacles. Therein, there are four obstacles to giving. First, previous non-habituation. Second, deficiency due to scarcity of things to be given. Third, greed for a pleasing and excellent object. Fourth, delight in seeing the result of future abundance of possessions. When, despite having things to give and a proper supplicant being present, the mind does not incline toward giving—[the <s>Bodhisattva</s> thinks:] 'This fault of mine is caused by non-habituation,' and with wisdom he swiftly counteracts it. And he further counteracts it thus: 'Surely I did not give previously; that is why now, when possessions are properly available and a supplicant is properly present, my mind does not incline toward giving. If I do not give now after reflection, my aversion to giving will arise again in the future.' Having thus counteracted it and relying on the antidote to the obstacle to giving, he gives after reflection. He does not follow the fault of non-habituation nor does he come under its power. Furthermore, if the <s>Bodhisattva</s>'s mind does not incline toward giving due to scarcity of possessions when a proper supplicant is present, he swiftly counteracts with wisdom the cause of this obstacle to giving caused by scarcity. Enduring the suffering caused by that scarcity, he gives out of compassion after reflection. His thought is thus: 'Through the fault of past <s>karma</s> or through having to be trained by others, I have endured many intense sufferings of hunger, thirst, and the like in existence without benefiting others. Even if this giving-caused suffering of benefiting others in this present life were to lead to my death—still, giving would be better for me than rejecting the supplicant.' How much more so for one who sustains life on whatever leaf of greens. Thus the <s>Bodhisattva</s>, enduring the suffering caused by scarcity, gives. Furthermore, if the <s>Bodhisattva</s>'s mind does not incline toward giving due to the excessive disliking and excellency of the object to be given when a proper supplicant is present, he swiftly counteracts with wisdom the fault caused by greed—

body.text: mahābhogatāyāmanuśaṃsadarśanamutpadyate nānuttarāyāṃ samyaksaṃbodhau taṃ bodhisattvo mithyāphaladṛṣṭikṛtaṃ doṣaṃ laghu-laghveva prajñayā pratividhya sarvasaṃskārāṇāmasāratāṃ yathābhūtaṃ pratyavekṣate / sarvasaṃskārāḥ kṣaṇabhaṅgurāḥ phalopabhogaparikṣayabhaṅgurā viprayogabhaṅgurāśca / sa evaṃ pratyavekṣamāṇaḥ phaladarśanaṃ prahāya yatkiñciddānaṃ dadāti sarvaṃ tanmahābodhi-pariṇāmitameva dadāti /
body.translated_text: [thinking:] 'This is my inversion of perceiving happiness in what is suffering, which will generate suffering in the future.' Through this understanding of the inversion, and abandoning it, he gives that object after reflection. Furthermore, if after giving, the perception of benefit in the result of giving arises with regard to great wealth rather than toward unsurpassed perfect awakening, the <s>Bodhisattva</s>, swiftly counteracting with wisdom the fault caused by the wrong view of result, contemplates as it truly is the essencelessness of all conditioned formations: 'All conditioned formations are momentarily destructible, destructible through the exhaustion of enjoyment of results, and destructible through separation.' Examining thus, abandoning the perception of result, whatever gift he gives, he gives it all dedicated to great awakening (<s>mahābodhi</s>).

body.text: tadidaṃ bodhisattvasya caturvidhasya dānavibandhasya caturvidhaṃ dānaprativandhapratipakṣajñānaṃ veditavyam / prativedho duḥkhādivāsanā viparyāsaparijñānaṃ saṃskārāsāratvadarśanañca / tatra trividhena bodhisattvaḥ pratipakṣajñānena pūrvakeṇa niyataṃ samyak ca dānaṃ dadāti / ekena paścimena pratipakṣajñānena samyak puṇyaphalaparigrahaṃ karoti / idamapi bodhisattvasya prājñadānaṃ veditavyam /
body.translated_text: This is to be known as the <s>Bodhisattva</s>'s fourfold knowledge of the antidotes to the four obstacles to giving: counteraction, endurance of suffering and such, understanding of inversions, and seeing the essencelessness of conditioned formations. Therein, through the first three antidote-knowledges, the <s>Bodhisattva</s> gives certainly and correctly. Through the last antidote-knowledge, he correctly gathers the result of merit. This too is to be known as the <s>Bodhisattva</s>'s wise giving.

body.text: punaraparaṃ bodhisattvaḥ adhyātmyaṃ rahogataḥ śuddhenāśayena ghanarasena prasādena saṃkalpairvicitrānudārānaprameyān deyadharmānadhimucya sattveṣu dānāya pratipāditāyābhilaṣati yena bodhisattvaḥ alpakṛcchreṇāprameyaṃ puṇyaṃ prasūyate / idamapi bodhisattvasya prājñadānaṃ veditavyam / tadidaṃ bodhisattvasya prājñasya [mahā]prājñadānam / evaṃ samāsataḥ saṃvidyamāneṣvasaṃvimādeṣu cāmiṣadānasaṃgṛhīteṣu deyadharmeṣu tathā dharmadānamupādāya pratisaṃvidamupādāyādhyāśayadānamupādāya dānavipratibandhapratipakṣajñānamupādāyāśayādhimuktidānañcopādāya bodhisattvasyaivāveṇikaṃ veditavyam / evaṃ hi bodhisattvasyādhyātmika-bāhyasarvavastudānaprabhedo vistareṇa veditavyaḥ /
body.translated_text: Furthermore, the <s>Bodhisattva</s>, inwardly, in solitude, with purified intention, with dense essence of faith, through mental resolutions, having imagined various, noble, and immeasurable things to be given, aspires to bestow them as gifts to beings—whereby the <s>Bodhisattva</s>, with little effort, produces immeasurable merit. This too is to be known as the <s>Bodhisattva</s>'s wise giving. This is the <s>Bodhisattva</s>'s [great] wise giving of one who is wise. Thus, in brief, when there exist things to be given encompassed by material gifts—whether available or not—and taking up the gift of <s>Dharma</s>, taking up the analytical knowledges (<s>pratisaṃvid</s>), taking up the gift of superior intention, taking up the knowledge of antidotes to obstacles to giving, and taking up the gift of aspiration and conviction—this is to be known as exclusively that of the <s>Bodhisattva</s>. Thus the classification of the <s>Bodhisattva</s>'s giving of all internal and external objects is to be understood in detail.

body.text: ata ūrdhvamasmādeva sarvadānaprabhedāttadanyaḥ sarvo duṣkarādidānaprabhedo veditavyaḥ /
body.translated_text: Henceforth, from this very classification of all giving, the classification of all other types of giving beginning with 'difficult giving' (<s>duṣkaradāna</s>) and so forth is to be understood.

body.text: tatra katamadbodhisattvasya duṣkaradānam / yadbodhisattvaḥ parīttaṃ deyavastu saṃvidyamānamātmānaṃ bādhitvā duḥkhamadhivāsya pareṣāmanuprayacchati / idaṃ bodhisattvasya prathamaṃ duṣkaradānam / yadbodhisattvaḥ iṣṭañca vastu prakṛtisnehādvā dīrghakāla saṃstavādvā 'dhimātropakārādvā 'gryañca pravaraṃ deyavastugardhaṃ prativinodya parebhyo 'nuprayacchati /
body.translated_text: There, what is the <s>Bodhisattva</s>'s difficult generosity (<s>duṣkaradāna</s>)? When the <s>Bodhisattva</s>, having only little to give, afflicts himself and endures suffering to give to others—this is the <s>Bodhisattva</s>'s first difficult generosity. When the <s>Bodhisattva</s> gives to others a cherished object—whether from natural affection, long intimacy, or supreme usefulness—that is foremost and excellent, dispelling attachment to the gift,

body.text: idaṃ bodhisattvasya dvitīyaṃ duṣkaradānaṃ yadbodhisattvaḥ kṛcchatārjitān deyadharmān parebhyo 'nuprayacchati / idaṃ tṛtīyaṃ bodhisattvasya duṣkaradānam /
body.translated_text: this is the <s>Bodhisattva</s>'s second difficult generosity. When the <s>Bodhisattva</s> gives to others things to be given that were acquired with hardship—this is the <s>Bodhisattva</s>'s third difficult generosity.

body.text: tatra katamadbodhisattvasya sarvatomukhaṃ dānam / yadbodhisattvaḥ svakaṃ vā paraṃ vā samādāpya deyavastu svabhṛtyeṣu vā mātāpitṛputradāradāsīdāsakarmakarapauruṣeyamitrāmātyajñātisālohiteṣvanuprayacchati / pareṣu vā 'rthiṣu / etatsarvatomukhaṃ dānamityucyate /
body.translated_text: There, what is the <s>Bodhisattva</s>'s all-embracing generosity (<s>sarvatomukhaṃ dānam</s>)? When the <s>Bodhisattva</s>, either himself or having induced another, gives things to be given to his own dependents—mother, father, son, wife, female and male servants, workers, retainers, friends, ministers, relatives, and kinsmen—or to other supplicants. This is called all-embracing generosity.

body.text: samāsato bodhisattvasya caturākāraṃ satpuruṣasya satpuruṣadānam /
body.translated_text: In brief, the <s>Bodhisattva</s>'s generosity of a good person is fourfold.

body.text: tava katamad bodhisattvasya satpuruṣasya satpuruṣadānam / yadbodhisattvaḥ śraddhayā dānaṃ dadāti satkṛtya svahastena kālena parānanupahatya idaṃ bodhisattvasya satpuruṣasya satpuruṣadānamityucyate /
body.translated_text: There, what is the <s>Bodhisattva</s>'s generosity of a good person? When the <s>Bodhisattva</s> gives with faith, with respect, with his own hand, at the proper time, and without harming others—this is called the <s>Bodhisattva</s>'s generosity of a good person.

body.text: tatra katamadbodhisattvasya sarvākāraṃ dānam / aniścitadānatā / viśadadānatā / pramuditadānatā / abhīkṣṇadānatā / pātradānatā / apātradānatā sarvadānatā / sarvatradānatā / sarvakāladānatā / anavadyadānatā sarvavastudānatā / deśavastudānatā / dhanadhānyavastudānatā / itīda trayodaśākāraṃ dānaṃ bodhisattvasya sarvākāramityucyate /
body.translated_text: There, what is the <s>Bodhisattva</s>'s generosity in all its aspects (<s>sarvākāraṃ dānam</s>)? Giving without partiality, generous giving, joyful giving, frequent giving, giving to worthy recipients, giving to unworthy recipients, giving to all, giving everywhere, giving at all times, blameless giving, giving of all things, giving of local goods, giving of wealth and grain. Thus, this thirteen-fold generosity is called the <s>Bodhisattva</s>'s generosity in all its aspects.

body.text: tatra katamadbodhisattvasya vighātārthika dānam / iha bodhisattvo bhojanena pānena vighātiṣvarthikeṣu bhojanapānaṃ dadāti / yānārthikeṣu yānaṃ vastrārthikeṣu vastramalaṅkārārthikeṣu alaṃkāraṃ vicitrabhāṇḍopaskārārthikeṣu vicitrabhāṇḍopaskāraṃ dadāti / gandhamālyavilepanārthikeṣu gandhamālyavilepanam / pratiśrayārthikeṣu pratiśrayam / ālokavighātārthikeṣvālokaṃ dadāti / idamaṣṭākāra bodhisattvasya vighātārthikadānaṃ veditavyam /
body.translated_text: There, what is the <s>Bodhisattva</s>'s giving to those in distress (<s>vighātārthikadānam</s>)? Here, the <s>Bodhisattva</s> gives food and drink to those in distress who need food and drink; vehicles to those who need vehicles; garments to those who need garments; ornaments to those who need ornaments; various utensils and furnishings to those who need them; incense, garlands, and ointments to those who need them; shelter to those who need shelter; light to those in distress who need light. This eightfold [giving] should be understood as the <s>Bodhisattva</s>'s giving to those in distress.

body.text: tatra katamadbodhisattvasyehāmutrasukhaṃ dānam / āmiṣadānaṃ dharmadānamabhayadānañca samāsataḥ ihāmutrasukhaṃ bodhisattvānāṃ dānaṃ veditavyam / tatpunarāmiṣadānaṃ praṇītaṃ śucikalpikam / vinīya mātsaryamalaṃ sannidhimalañca dadāti / tatra mātsaryamalavinayaścittāgrahaparityāgāt sannidhimalavinayo bhogāgrahaparityāgādveditavyaḥ / abhayadānaṃ siṃhavyādhragrāharājacaurodakādibhayaparitrāṇatayā veditavyam / dharmadānamaviparītadharmadeśanā nyāyopadeśaḥ śikṣāpadasamādāpanā
body.translated_text: There, what is the <s>Bodhisattva</s>'s giving that brings happiness in this world and the next (<s>ihāmutrasukhaṃ dānam</s>)? In brief, material giving (<s>āmiṣadāna</s>), <s>Dharma</s>-giving (<s>dharmadāna</s>), and the giving of fearlessness (<s>abhayadāna</s>) should be understood as the <s>Bodhisattva</s>'s giving that brings happiness here and hereafter. Moreover, material giving is excellent, pure, and proper. One gives having removed the stain of miserliness and the stain of hoarding. There, the removal of the stain of miserliness should be understood as the relinquishment of mental grasping; the removal of the stain of hoarding should be understood as the relinquishment of grasping at possessions. The giving of fearlessness should be understood as the protection from fear of lions, tigers, crocodiles, kings, thieves, floods, and the like. <s>Dharma</s>-giving is the non-erroneous teaching of the <s>Dharma</s>, righteous counsel, and inducing others to undertake the precepts of training.

body.text: ca / tadetatsarvamabhisamasya navākāraṃ bodhisattvasya dānaṃ sattvānābhihāmutrasukhaṃ bhavati / tatrāmiṣābhayadānaṃ saprabhedabhihasukham dharmadānaṃ punaḥ saprabhedamamutrasukham /
body.translated_text: Considering all of this together, the <s>Bodhisattva</s>'s nine-fold giving brings happiness for beings here and hereafter. There, the giving of material things and fearlessness, with their subdivisions, brings happiness in this life; the giving of <s>Dharma</s>, with its subdivisions, brings happiness in the next.

body.text: tatra katamadbodhisattvasya viśuddhaṃ dānam / taddaśākaraṃ veditavyam / asaktamaparāmṛṣṭamasaṃbhṛtamanunnatamaniśritamalīnamadīnamavimukhaṃ pratīkārānapekṣaṃ vipākānapekṣañca /
body.translated_text: There, what is the <s>Bodhisattva</s>'s pure generosity (<s>viśuddhaṃ dānam</s>)? It should be understood as tenfold: without attachment, without grasping [wrong views], without accumulation, without pride, without dependence, without depression, without dejection, without aversion, without expectation of reciprocation, and without expectation of karmic result.

body.text: tatrāsaktaṃ dānaṃ katamat / iha bodhisattvo yācanake samyak pratyupasthite tvaritamavilambitaṃ dadāti / na yācanakasya tathā lābhamāramya tvarā bhavati yathā bodhisattvasya dānamārabhya /
body.translated_text: There, what is giving without attachment? Here, the <s>Bodhisattva</s>, when a supplicant has properly presented himself, gives quickly and without delay. For the supplicant does not have such eagerness upon obtaining the gift as the <s>Bodhisattva</s> has in undertaking the act of giving.

body.text: aparāmṛṣṭaṃ dānaṃ katamat / na hi bodhisattvo dṛṣṭyā evaṃ dānaṃ parāmṛśati / nāsti vā 'sya dānasya phalam / hiṃsādānena vā punardharmo bhavatīti / susampannena vā punardānamātrakeṇa laukikalokottarā viśuddhirbhavatīti /
body.translated_text: What is giving without grasping [wrong views]? The <s>Bodhisattva</s> does not grasp at giving with [wrong] views such as: 'There is no fruit of this giving,' or 'Violence constitutes <s>dharma</s> through giving,' or 'Through the mere act of giving, thoroughly accomplished, mundane and supramundane purification occurs.'

body.text: asaṃbhṛtaṃ dānaṃ katamat / na khalu bodhisattvaḥ saṃbhṛtya dīrghakālikaṃ deyadharmasannicarya kṛtvā paścāt sakṛddānaṃ dadāti / tatkasya hetoḥ / na hi bodhisattvaḥ saṃvidyamāneṣu deyadharmeṣu samyak pratyupasthitasya yācanakasya nirākaraṇamutsahate nāpi pratirūpaṃ paśyati yena tannirākaroti / kutaḥ punaḥ sannicayaṃ kariṣyati / na ca saṃbhṛtadānena bodhisattvaḥ puṇyasyāyadvāramadhikaṃ paśyati / samaṃ deyavastu tulyeṣu vyastasamasteṣu yācanakeṣu krameṇa vā sakṛdvā dīyamānaṃ kena kāraṇena puṇyaviśeṣatāṃ parigṛhṇīyāditi sampaśyannapi ca bodhisattvaḥ sāvadyameva saṃbhṛtadānaṃ paśyati / niravadyaṃ paśyati yathotpannaṃ bhogadānam / tatkasya hetoḥ / tathāhi saṃbhṛtadātā 'rthito yācanakairyācanakaśatāni pūrvaṃ nirākṛtya teṣāmāghātamakṣamapratyayaṃ janayitvā paścādanarthito 'pi tadekatyānāṃ saṃbhṛtadānaṃ dadāti / tasmādbodhisattvaḥ sambhṛtadānaṃ na dadāti /
body.translated_text: What is giving without accumulation? The <s>Bodhisattva</s> certainly does not accumulate and hoard things to be given over a long time and then give a single [large] gift afterward. For what reason? For the <s>Bodhisattva</s> does not endure rejecting a supplicant who has properly presented himself when there are things to give, nor does he see it as appropriate to reject him—how then would he accumulate? And the <s>Bodhisattva</s> does not see a greater gateway of merit in accumulated giving. For when equal things to be given are distributed to equal supplicants, whether separately or collectively, whether gradually or all at once—by what reason would it acquire a superiority of merit? Seeing this, the <s>Bodhisattva</s> sees accumulated giving as actually blameworthy, and sees giving [of things] as they arise as blameless. For what reason? For one who gives in an accumulated manner, having been asked by hundreds of supplicants, first refuses them and creates in them frustration, impatience, and distrust, and later gives that accumulated gift to only some of them, even unasked. Therefore the <s>Bodhisattva</s> does not give in an accumulated manner.

body.text: anunnatadānaṃ katamat / yācanakāya nīcacitto bodhisattvo dānaṃ dadāti / na ca paraspardhayā dadāti / na ca dānaṃ dattvā tena dānena manyate ahamasmi dātā dānapatiranye ca na tatheti /
body.translated_text: What is giving without pride? The <s>Bodhisattva</s> gives with a humble mind toward the supplicant. He does not give out of rivalry with others. And having given, he does not become conceited about that giving, [thinking:] 'I am a giver, a lord of giving, and others are not like me.'

body.text: aniścitadānaṃ katamat / na hi bodhisattvaḥ kīrtiśabdaghoṣaślokaṃ niśritya dānaṃ dadāti / vikalpākṣarasaṃbhūtāṃ ghoṣamātrapratibaddhāṃ vṛṣamatropamāṃ kīrtiṃ manyamānaḥ /
body.translated_text: What is giving without partiality? The <s>Bodhisattva</s> does not give relying on fame, reputation, renown, or praise—regarding fame as mere sound produced by conceptual syllables, bound to mere utterance, comparable to a [passing] bull's [bellow].

body.text: alīnaṃ dānaṃ katamat / iha bodhisattvaḥ pūrvameva dānāt sumanā bhavati / dadaccittaṃ prasādayati / dattvā cāvipratisārī bhavati / vipulāni ca paramodārāṇi bodhisattvānāṃ dānāni śrutvā nātmānaṃ paribhavan saṃkocamāpadyate /
body.translated_text: What is giving without depression? Here, the <s>Bodhisattva</s> is glad of mind even before giving. While giving, he purifies the mind. And having given, he is without regret. And having heard of the vast and supremely magnificent gifts of the <s>Bodhisattvas</s>, he does not fall into timidity by belittling himself.

body.text: adīnaṃ dānaṃ katamat / vicintya vicintya bodhisattvo yatnena deyadharmebhyo yānyagrāṇi pravarāṇi bhojanapānayānavastrādīni tānyanuprayacchati /
body.translated_text: What is giving without dejection? The <s>Bodhisattva</s>, having carefully considered, deliberately gives the foremost and most excellent things to be given—food, drink, vehicles, garments, and the like.

body.text: avimukhaṃ dānaṃ katamat / samacitto bodhisattvaḥ apakṣapatito mitrāmitrodāsīneṣu samakāruṇyo dānaṃ dadāti /
body.translated_text: What is giving without aversion? The <s>Bodhisattva</s>, with an equal mind, impartial, gives with equal compassion toward friends, enemies, and those who are neutral.

body.text: pratīkārānapekṣaṃ dānaṃ katamat / kāruṇyacitto 'nukampācitto bodhisattvo dānaṃ dadanna parataḥ pratyupakāraṃ pratyāśaṃsate / sukhakāmāṃ tṛṣṇādāhena dahyamānāmapratibalāṃ prakṛtiduḥkhitāṃ janatāṃ saṃpaśyan /
body.translated_text: What is giving without expectation of reciprocation? The <s>Bodhisattva</s>, with a compassionate and sympathetic mind, gives without expecting a return favor from others, seeing the people as desiring happiness, burning with the fire of craving, unable [to help themselves], and by nature suffering.

body.text: vipākānapekṣaṃ dānaṃ katamat / na bodhisattvo dānaṃ dattvā dānasyāyatyāṃ bhogasampadaṃ vā ātmabhāvasampadaṃ vā phalavipākaṃ pratyāśaṃsate / sarvasaṃskāreṣu phalgudarśī paramabodhāvanuśaṃsadarśī /
body.translated_text: What is giving without expectation of karmic result? The <s>Bodhisattva</s>, having given, does not expect the ripening result of that giving in the future—whether excellence of possessions or excellence of bodily form. Seeing all conditioned things as trifling, he sees the benefit [only] in supreme awakening.

body.text: ebhirdaśabhirākārairbodhisattvānāṃ viśuddhaṃ suviśuddhaṃ dānaṃ bhavati /
body.translated_text: Through these ten aspects, the giving of the <s>Bodhisattvas</s> becomes pure and well-purified.

body.text: evaṃ hi bodhisattva etannavākāraṃ dānaṃ niśritya dānapāramitāṃ paripūrayitvā 'nuttarāṃ samyaksaṃbodhimabhisaṃbudhyate /
body.translated_text: Thus indeed, the <s>Bodhisattva</s>, relying on this nine-fold giving, having fulfilled the <s>Dānapāramitā</s> (perfection of generosity), fully awakens to unsurpassed perfect awakening.

body.text: iti bodhisattvabhūmāvādhāre yogasthāne navamaṃ dānapaṭalam /
body.translated_text: Thus, in the <s>Bodhisattvabhūmi</s>, in the Foundation section of the Yoga Place, the ninth chapter on Generosity (<s>Dānapaṭala</s>) is completed.

body.text: uddānam /
body.translated_text: Summary verse:

children.translated_text: that of a good person, and in all aspects likewise, //
that for those in distress, happiness here and hereafter,
and pure—this is the ninefold [treatment of] moral conduct, in summary. //

body.text: tatra śīlaṃ bodhisattvānāṃ katamat / tadapi navavidhaṃ veditavyam / svabhāva śīlaṃ sarvaśīlaṃ duṣkaraśīlaṃ sarvatomukhaṃ śīlaṃ satpuruṣaśīlaṃ sarvākāraśīlaṃ vighātārthikaśīlaṃ ihāmutrasukhaṃ śīlaṃ viśuddhaśīlañca /
body.translated_text: There, what is the moral conduct (<s>śīla</s>) of the <s>Bodhisattvas</s>? It too should be understood as ninefold: intrinsic-nature moral conduct, all moral conduct, difficult moral conduct, all-embracing moral conduct, moral conduct of a good person, moral conduct in all aspects, moral conduct for those in distress, moral conduct that brings happiness here and hereafter, and pure moral conduct.

body.text: tatra svabhāvaśīlaṃ katamat / caturbhirguṇairyuktaṃ samāsato bodhisattvānāṃ svabhāvaśīlaṃ veditavyam / katamaiścaturbhiḥ / parataḥ samyaksamādānataḥ suviśuddhāśayatayā vyatikrāntaiḥ pratyāpattyā 'vyatikramāya cādarajātasyopasthitasmṛtitayā / tatra parataḥ śīlasamādānādbodhisattvasya paramupanidhāya śikṣāvyatikrame vyapatrāpyamutpadyate / suviśuddhāśayatayā śīleṣu bodhisattvasyātmānamupanidhāya śikṣāvyatikrame hīrutpadyate / śikṣāpadānāṃ vyatikrama-pratyāpattyā ādarajātasya cādita evāvyatikramādbodhisattvo dvābhyāmākārābhyāṃ niṣkaukṛtyo bhavati / evamayaṃ bodhisattvaḥ samādanamāśayaviśuddhiñca niśritya hrīvyapatrāpyamutpādayati / hrīvyapatrāpyāt śīlaṃ samāttaṃ rakṣati / rakṣamāṇo niṣkaukṛtyo bhavati / tatra yacca parataḥ samādānaṃ yaśca viśuddho 'dhyāśayaḥ itīmau dvau dhamauṃ yā ca vyatikramapratyāpattiryaścādaraḥ avyatikrame 'nayordvayordharmayorāvāhakau / tatra yacca parataḥ samādānaṃ yaśca suviśuddho 'dhyāśayaḥ yaścāvyatikramāyādarajāta ityebhistribhirdharmairavipattirbodhisattvaśīlasya veditavyā / vyatikramapratyāpattyā punaśchidritasya pratyānayanavyutthānaṃ veditavyam / tatpunaretaccaturbhiguṇairyuktaṃ svabhāvaśīlaṃ bodhisattvānāṃ
body.translated_text: There, what is intrinsic-nature moral conduct? In brief, the intrinsic-nature moral conduct of <s>Bodhisattvas</s> should be understood as endowed with four qualities. Which four? From undertaking [the precepts] from another, from purity of intention, from restoration after transgression, and from the presence of mindfulness arising from respect for non-transgression. There, from undertaking moral conduct from another, there arises in the <s>Bodhisattva</s> moral dread (<s>vyapatrāpya</s>) regarding transgression of the trainings, with reference to others. From purity of intention, there arises in the <s>Bodhisattva</s> moral shame (<s>hrī</s>) regarding transgression of the trainings, with reference to oneself. Through restoration after transgression of the precepts, and from respect for non-transgression from the very beginning, the <s>Bodhisattva</s> is free from remorse in two aspects. Thus this <s>Bodhisattva</s>, relying on the undertaking [of precepts] and the purity of intention, generates moral shame and moral dread. From moral shame and moral dread, he guards the moral conduct that has been undertaken. Guarding it, he becomes free from remorse. There, the undertaking from another and the pure intention—these two <s>dharmas</s>; and the restoration after transgression and the respect for non-transgression—these bring about the two <s>dharmas</s>. There, the undertaking from another, the well-purified intention, and the respect arising for non-transgression—through these three <s>dharmas</s>, the non-failure of the <s>Bodhisattva</s>'s moral conduct should be understood. Through restoration after transgression, moreover, the recovery and reformation of what has been broken should be understood. That intrinsic-nature moral conduct of the <s>Bodhisattvas</s>, endowed with these four qualities,

body.text: kalyāṇaṃ veditavyamātmahitāya parahitāya bahujanahitāya bahujanasukhāya lokānukampāyai cārthāya hitāya sukhāya devamanuṣyāṇāṃ samādānato 'nuśikṣaṇataśca / aprameyaṃ veditavyamaprameyabodhisattvaśikṣāparigṛhītatayā / sattvānugrāhakaṃ veditavyaṃ sarvasattvahitasukhapratyupasthānatayā / mahāphalānuśaṃsaṃ veditavyam anuttarasamyak saṃbodhiphalaparigrahānupradānatayā /
body.translated_text: should be understood as auspicious—for one's own benefit, for the benefit of others, for the welfare of many, for the happiness of many, out of compassion for the world, for the sake, benefit, and happiness of gods and humans—through both undertaking and subsequent training. It should be understood as immeasurable, because it is embraced by the immeasurable trainings of the <s>Bodhisattva</s>. It should be understood as benefiting beings, because of the presence of benefit and happiness for all beings. It should be understood as bearing great fruit and benefit, because of the embracing and bestowing of the fruit of unsurpassed perfect awakening.

body.text: tatra katamad bodhisattvasya sarvaśīlam / samāsato bodhisattvasya gṛhipakṣagataṃ pravrajitapakṣagatañca śīlaṃ sarvaśīlamityucyate /
body.translated_text: There, what is the all [encompassing] moral conduct of the <s>Bodhisattva</s>? In brief, the moral conduct of the <s>Bodhisattva</s> pertaining to the household life and pertaining to the renunciant life—[both together] are called 'all moral conduct.'

body.text: tatpunargṛhipakṣāśritaṃ pravrajitapakṣāśritañca śīlaṃ samāsatastrividham / saṃvaraśīlaṃ kuśaladharmasaṃgrāhakaśīlaṃ sattvārthakriyāśīlañca /
body.translated_text: That moral conduct, based on the household side and based on the renunciant side, is in brief threefold: the moral conduct of restraint (<s>saṃvaraśīla</s>), the moral conduct of gathering wholesome <s>dharmas</s> (<s>kuśaladharmasaṃgrāhakaśīla</s>), and the moral conduct of acting for the welfare of beings (<s>sattvārthakriyāśīla</s>).

body.text: tatra saṃvaraśīlaṃ bodhisattvasya katamat / yatsaptanairṇāyikaṃ prātimokṣasaṃvarasamādānaṃ bhikṣubhikṣuṇī-śikṣamāṇā-śrāmaṇera-śramaṇeryyupāsakopāsikāśīlam / tadetad gṛhipravrajitapakṣe yathāyogaṃ veditavyam /
body.translated_text: There, what is the moral conduct of restraint of the <s>Bodhisattva</s>? The undertaking of the <s>prātimokṣa</s>-restraint of seven types: the moral conduct of <s>bhikṣu</s>, <s>bhikṣuṇī</s>, <s>śikṣamāṇā</s>, <s>śrāmaṇera</s>, <s>śrāmaṇerī</s>, <s>upāsaka</s>, and <s>upāsikā</s>. This should be understood as applying, respectively, to the household and renunciant sides.

body.text: tatra kuśaladharmasaṃgrāhakaṃ śīlaṃ yatkiñcidbodhisattvaḥ śīlasaṃvarasamādānādūrdhvaṃ mahābodhāya kuśalamācinoti kāyena vācā manasā sarvaṃ tatsamāsataḥ kuśaladharmasaṃgrāhakaṃ śīlamityucyate / tatpunaḥ katamat / iha bodhisattvaḥ śīlaṃ niśritya śīlaṃ pratiṣṭhāya śrute yogaṃ karoti cintāyāṃ śamathavipaśyanābhāvanāyāmekārāmatāyām / tathā gurūṇāmabhivādana-vandana pratyutthānāñjalikarmaṇaḥ kālena kālaṃ kartā bhavati / tathā kālena kālaṃ teṣāmeva gurūṇāṃ gauraveṇopasthānasya kartā bhavati / glānānāṃ satkṛtya kāruṇyena glānopasthānasya kartā bhavati tathā subhāṣite sādhukārasya dātā bhavati / guṇavatāṃ pudgalānāṃ bhūtasya varṇasyāhartā bhavati / tathā sarvasattvānāṃ daśasu dikṣu sarvapuṇyasyāśayena prasannacittamutpādya vācaṃ bhāṣāmāṇo 'numoditā bhavati / tathā sarvaṃ vyatikramaṃ pratisaṃkhyāya pareṣāṃ kṣamitā bhavati / tathā sarvaṃ kāyena vācā manasā kṛtaṃ kuśalamanuttarāyāṃ samyaksaṃbodhau pariṇāmayitā bhavati / kālena ca kālaṃ vicitrāṇāṃ samyak praṇidhānānāṃ triratnapūjāyāśca sarvākārāyā udārāyāḥ kartā
body.translated_text: There, what is the moral conduct that collects wholesome <s>dharmas</s> (<s>kuśaladharmasaṃgrāhaka śīla</s>)? Whatever wholesome [actions] the <s>Bodhisattva</s> accumulates by body, speech, and mind for the sake of great awakening after undertaking the moral restraint—all that, in brief, is called moral conduct that collects wholesome <s>dharmas</s>. And what is that? Here, the <s>Bodhisattva</s>, relying on and established in moral conduct, engages in the practice of learning (<s>śruta</s>), reflection (<s>cintā</s>), the cultivation of calm and insight (<s>śamathavipaśyanābhāvanā</s>), and delight in solitude (<s>ekārāmatā</s>). Likewise, from time to time one performs salutation, veneration, rising from one's seat, and the gesture of joined palms toward teachers. Likewise, from time to time one performs respectful attendance upon those very teachers. One attends to the sick with earnestness and compassion. Likewise, one gives applause to what is well-spoken. One proclaims the true merits of persons endowed with virtues. Likewise, generating a mind of serene faith with the intention toward all merit of all beings in the ten directions, one speaks words of rejoicing. Likewise, having reflected on all transgressions, one practices forbearance toward others. Likewise, one dedicates all wholesome [actions] done by body, speech, and mind to the unsurpassed, perfect awakening. And from time to time one performs various proper aspirations (<s>praṇidhāna</s>) and magnificent worship of the Three Jewels (<s>Triratna</s>) in all its forms

body.text: bhavati / abhiyuktaśca bhavatyārabdhavīryaḥ satatasamitaṃ kuśalapakṣe / apramādavihārī kāyena vācā / śikṣāpadānāṃ smṛtisaṃprajanyacārikayā cārakṣakaḥ / indriyaiśca guptadvāro bhojane mātrajñaḥ pūrvarātrāpararātraṃ jāgarikānuyuktaḥ satpuruṣasevī kalyāṇamitrasanniśritaḥ ātmaskhalitānāñca parijñātā bhavati doṣadarśī / parijñāya ca doṣaṃ dṛṣṭvā pratisaṃhartā bhavati / skhalitaśca buddhabodhisattvānāṃ sahadhārmikāṇāṃ cāntike 'tyayadeśako bhavati / evaṃbhāgīyānāṃ kuśalānāṃ dharmāṇāmarjanarakṣaṇavivardhanāya yacchīlaṃ [tad] bodhisattvasya kuśaladharmasaṃgrāhakaṃ śīlamityucyate /
body.translated_text: One is diligent, with vigor aroused, constantly and continuously on the side of the wholesome. One dwells in heedfulness (<s>apramāda</s>) in body and speech. One guards the rules of training through the practice of mindfulness and clear comprehension (<s>smṛtisaṃprajanya</s>). One is guarded at the doors of the sense-faculties, moderate in eating, devoted to wakefulness in the first and last watches of the night, attending upon good persons, relying on virtuous friends (<s>kalyāṇamitra</s>). One fully knows one's own stumblings and faults and sees the danger in them. Having fully known and seen the danger, one withdraws [from them]. And when one has stumbled, one confesses transgressions in the presence of <s>Buddhas</s>, <s>Bodhisattvas</s>, and fellow practitioners of the <s>Dharma</s>. The moral conduct for the acquisition, protection, and increase of such wholesome <s>dharmas</s>—that is called the <s>Bodhisattva</s>'s moral conduct that collects wholesome <s>dharmas</s>.

body.text: tatra katamad bodhisattvasya sattvānugrāhakaṃ śīlam / tatsamāsata ekādaśākāraṃ veditavyam / ekādaśākārāḥ katame / sattvakṛtyeṣvarthopasaṃhiteṣu [vicitreṣu] sahāyībhāvaḥ / sattvānāmutpannotpanneṣu vyādhyādiduḥkheṣu glānopasthānādikaḥ sahāyībhāvaḥ / tathā laukikalokottareṣvartheṣu dharmadeśanāpūrvaka upāyopadeśapūrvakaśca nyāyopadeśaḥ / upakāriṣu ca sattveṣu kṛtajñatāmanurakṣato 'nurūpa[pratyupakāra-]pratyupasthānam / vivighebhyaśca siṃhavyāghrarājacaurodakāgnyādikebhyo vicitrebhyo bhayasthānebhyaḥ sattvānāmārakṣā / bhogajñātivyasaneṣu śokavinodanā / upakaraṇavighātiṣu sattveṣu sarvopakaraṇopasaṃhāraḥ / nyāyapatitaḥ samyaṅniśrayadānato dharmeṇa gaṇaparikarṣaṇā / ālapanasaṃlapanapratisammodanaiḥ kālenopasaṃkramaṇatayā parato bhojanapānādi [prati]grahato laukikārthānuvyavahārataḥ āhūtasyāgamanagamanataḥ samāsataḥ sarvānarthopasaṃhitāmanāpasamudācāraparivarjanaiścittānuvartanatā / bhūtaiśca guṇaiḥ saṃpraharṣaṇatā / rahaḥ prakāśaṃ vodbhāvanatāmupādāya / snigdhena hitādhyāśayānugatenāntargatamānasena nigrahakriyā avasādanā vā daṇḍakarmānupradānaṃ va pravāsanā vā yāvadevākuśalāsthānāt vyutthāpya kuśale sthāne sanniyojanārtham / ṛddhibalena ca narakādigatipratyakṣaṃ sandarśanatayā 'kuśalādudvejanā buddhaśāsanāvatārāya cāvarjanā toṣaṇā vismāpanā /
body.translated_text: There, what is the <s>Bodhisattva</s>'s moral conduct that benefits beings (<s>sattvānugrāhaka śīla</s>)? In brief, it should be understood as having eleven aspects. What are the eleven aspects? Being a companion in the various meaningful tasks of beings; being a companion through tending the sick and so forth when various afflictions such as illness arise for beings; likewise, teaching the <s>Dharma</s> preceded by instruction in means and preceded by proper guidance regarding worldly and supramundane matters; for beings who have been helpful, maintaining gratitude and the appropriate offering of reciprocal service; protecting beings from various frightening dangers such as lions, tigers, kings, thieves, floods, fire, and the like; consoling grief when there are misfortunes of wealth, relatives, and calamity; providing all necessities for beings deprived of their requisites; leading a community rightfully through providing proper support; social engagement through greeting, conversing, exchanging pleasantries, visiting at appropriate times, accepting food and drink from others, conducting worldly affairs, and coming and going when summoned—in brief, conforming to the minds [of beings] while avoiding all conduct that is unpleasant and connected with harm; encouraging with genuine qualities; and, adopting a disposition that is affectionate, with a beneficial superior intention, and with a sincere heart—whether in private or in public—corrective discipline, humbling, the bestowal of punishment, or banishment, for the sole purpose of raising [beings] from unwholesome states and establishing them in wholesome states; and through the power of supernatural ability (<s>ṛddhibala</s>), by directly showing the realms of hell and other destinies, generating revulsion from the unwholesome, and attracting, pleasing, and amazing [beings] for their entry into the <s>Buddha</s>'s teaching.

body.text: kathañca bodhisattvaḥ saṃvaraśīle sthitaḥ kuśaladharmasaṃgrāhake śīle sthitaḥ sattvārthakriyāśīle ca sthitaḥ susaṃvṛtaśīlī ca bhavati susaṃgṛhītakuśalaśīlī ca
body.translated_text: And how does the <s>Bodhisattva</s>, established in the moral conduct of restraint, established in the moral conduct that collects wholesome <s>dharmas</s>, and established in the moral conduct of acting for the welfare of beings, become one of well-restrained morality, one of well-collected wholesome morality, and

body.text: sarvākārasattvārthakriyāśīlī ca / iha bodhisattvaḥ prātimokṣasaṃvaravyavasthitaḥ sa ceccakravartirājyamapyutsṛjya pravrajito bhavati sa tasmiṃścakravartirājye evaṃ nirapekṣo bhavati tadyathā tṛṇe vā 'medhye vā / nihīnapuruṣasya jīvikābhiprāyasya pravrajitasya pratyavarān kāmānapahāya na tathā teṣu pratyavareṣu kāmeṣu nirapekṣatā bhavati yathā bodhisattvasyāśayaviśuddhatāmupādāya pravrajitasya sarvamānuṣyakakāmapravareṣu cakravartikāmeṣu / anāgateṣvapi mārabhavanaparyāpanneṣvapi kāmeṣu bodhisattvo nābhinandī bhavati nāpi ca teṣāmarthāya praṇidhāya brahmacaryaṃ carati mahāvicitrapratibhayagahanapraveśamiva tān kāmān yathābhūtaṃ saṃpaśyan prāgeva tadanyeṣu divyeṣu / vartamāne 'pyadhvani pravrajito bodhisattva udārebhyaḥ sattvebhya udāramapi lābhasatkāraṃ vāntāśanamiva samyak prajñayā paśyan nāsvādayati prāgeva pratyavarebhyaḥ [sattvebhyaḥ] pratyavaram / pravivekābhirataśca bhavati ekākī saṃvamadhye vā sarvakālaṃ cittavyapakṛṣṭavihārī / sa na śīlasaṃvaramātrakeṇa tuṣṭho bhavati / api tu śīlaṃ niśritya śīlaṃ pratiṣṭhāya ye te 'prameyā bodhisattvasamādhayasteṣāmabhinirhārāya vaśitāprāptaye vyāyacchate / saḥ saṃsargato 'pyaṇukām apyasatsaṃkathā masadvācaṃ nādhivāsayati pravivekagataścāṇukamapyasadvitarkam / pramuṣitayā ca smṛtyā tatsamudācārahetoḥ kālena kālaṃ tīvraṃ vipratisāramādīnavadarśanamutpādayati / yamābhīkṣṇakaṃ
