vipratisāramādīnavadarśanamāgamyotpannamātrāyāmasatsaṃkathāyāmasadvitarke ca tvaritatvaritaṃ sā smṛtirupatiṣṭhate / akaraṇacittañca pratilabhate / yena pratisaṃharati / pratisaṃharaṇābhyāsataśca krameṇa tadyathā pūrvaṃ tatsamudācāra-ratirabhūt tathā etaharyasamudācāra-ratiḥ santiṣṭhate samudācāraprātikūlyañca / sarvabodhisattvaśikṣāpadāni cāsya mahābhūmipraviṣṭānāṃ bodhisattvānāṃ śrutvā udārāṇyaprameyāṇyacintyāni dīrghakālikāni paramaduśkarāṇi na bhavati cetasa uttāso vā layaḥ saṃkoco vā nānyatrāsyaivaṃ bhavati / te 'pi manuṣyabhūtāḥ krameṇa śikṣamāṇāḥ bodhisattvaśikṣāṣvaprameyācintyakāyavāksaṃvarasamanvāgatāḥ saṃvṛttāḥ / vayamapi manuṣyabhūtāḥ krameṇa ca śikṣamāṇāḥ asaṃśayamanuprāpsyāmastāṃ kāyavāksaṃvarasampattimiti / ātmadoṣāntaraskhalitagaveṣī ca bodhisattvo bhavati śīlasaṃvare vyavasthito na paradoṣāntaraskhalitagaveṣī / sarvaraudraduḥśīlānāñca
body.translated_text: one of all-aspected moral conduct of acting for the welfare of beings? Here, the <s>Bodhisattva</s> is established in the <s>prātimokṣa</s> restraint. If one has gone forth having even renounced the sovereignty of a <s>cakravartin</s> (universal monarch), one is as indifferent to that <s>cakravartin</s> sovereignty as to grass or filth. For a person of low character who has gone forth with the intention of [merely securing] a livelihood, having abandoned inferior sensual pleasures, there is not such indifference to those inferior pleasures as there is for the <s>Bodhisattva</s>, who has gone forth with purity of intention, toward the supreme human pleasures of a <s>cakravartin</s>. Even toward future pleasures belonging to the realms of <s>Māra</s>, the <s>Bodhisattva</s> has no delight, nor does one practice the holy life with aspiration for their sake, seeing those pleasures as they truly are—as if entering a great, varied, terrifying thicket—much less toward other divine pleasures. Even in the present life, the <s>Bodhisattva</s> who has gone forth, receiving even generous gains and honors from noble beings, does not savor them, seeing them correctly with wisdom as vomited food—much less inferior [gains] from inferior [beings]. One delights in seclusion, dwelling alone or in company, at all times with a mind withdrawn. One is not content with mere moral restraint; rather, relying on and established in morality, one strives for the realization and mastery of those immeasurable <s>Bodhisattva samādhis</s>. Even from association, one does not tolerate even the slightest improper conversation or speech; and when in seclusion, one does not tolerate even the slightest improper thought. And when mindfulness is lost, which is the cause of such [improper] conduct, from time to time one generates intense remorse and perception of danger. Through that frequently arising remorse and perception of danger, when improper conversation or improper thought has just arisen, mindfulness is quickly established, and one obtains the mind of non-doing, by which one withdraws. And through the habit of withdrawing, gradually, just as previously there was delight in such conduct, so now delight in non-conduct becomes established, along with aversion to [improper] conduct. And upon hearing the magnificent, immeasurable, inconceivable, long-term, and supremely difficult training rules of <s>Bodhisattvas</s> who have entered the great stages, there arises in one's mind no alarm, sinking, or contraction. Rather, one thinks: 'They too, being human, training gradually in the <s>Bodhisattva</s> trainings, came to possess the immeasurable and inconceivable restraint of body and speech. We too, being human and training gradually, shall undoubtedly attain that perfection of bodily and verbal restraint.' And the <s>Bodhisattva</s> established in the moral restraint is one who searches for faults and stumblings in oneself, not one who searches for faults and stumblings in others. Even toward all fierce and immoral

body.text: sattvānāmantike nāghātacitto bhavati na pratighacittaḥ / dharmamahākaruṇatāmupādāyādhimātrameva teṣāmantike bodhisattvānāmanukampācittañca kartukāmatācittañca pratyupasthitaṃ bhavati / saṃvaraśīlavyasthitaśca bodhisattvaḥ pāṇiloṣṭadaṇḍaśastrasaṃsparśairapi pareṣāmantike cittamapi na pradūṣayati / kutaḥ punaḥ pāpikāṃ vācaṃ niścārayiṣyati pratihaniṣyati vā prāgeva punaḥ ākrośaroṣaṇaparibhāṣaṇaistanukaduḥkhasparśajairapakāraiḥ / saṃvaraśīlavyavasthitaśca bodhisattvaḥ pañcāṅgaparigṛhītenāpramādena samanvāgato bhavati pūrvāntasahagatenāparāntasahagatena madhyāntasahagatena pūrvakālakaraṇīyena sahānucareṇa ca / bodhisattvaśikṣāsu śikṣamāṇo bodhisattvaḥ atītamadhvānamupādāya yāmāpattimāpannaḥ sā 'nena yathādharmaṃ pratikṛtā bhavati / ayamasya pūrvāntasahagato 'pramādaḥ / anāgate 'pyadhvani yāmāpattimāpatsyate tāmapi yathādharmaṃ pratikariṣyati / ayamasyāparāntasahagato 'pramādaḥ / pratyutpanne 'pyadhvani yāmāpattimāpadyate tāmapi yathādharmaṃ pratikaroti / ayamasya madhyāntasahagato 'pramādaḥ / pūrvameva cāpatterbodhisattvastīvramautsukyamāpadyate / kaccidahaṃ tathā tathā careyaṃ yathā yathā caran yathā yathā viharan āpattiṃ nāpadyeyam / ayaṃ bodhisattvasya pūrvakālakaraṇīyo 'pramādaḥ / sa pūrvakālakaraṇīyamevāpramādaṃ niśritya tathā tathā carati tathā tathā viharati yathā yathāsya carato viharato vā āpattirnottiṣṭhate / ayamasya sahānucaro 'pramādaḥ / saṃvaraśīla-vyavasthito bodhisattvaḥ praticchannakalyāṇo bhavati vivṛtapāpaḥ alpecchaḥ santuṣṭaḥ duḥkhasahiṣṇuraparitasanajātīyaḥ anuddhataśca acapalaśca praśānteryāpathaḥ kuhanādisarvamithyājīvakarakadharmavivarjitaḥ / ebhirdaśabhiraṅgaiḥ samanvāgato bodhisattvaḥ saṃvaraśīlavyavasthitaḥ susaṃvṛtaśīlī bhavati / yadutātīteṣu kāmeṣu nirapekṣatayā anāgateṣvanabhinandanatayā pratyutpa-nneṣvanadhyavasānatayā pravivekavāsābhiratyā vāgvitarkapariśodhanatayā ātmano 'paribhavanatayā sauratyena kṣāntyā 'pramādena ācārājīvaviśuddhyā ceti /
body.translated_text: beings, one does not have a mind of hostility or aversion. Rather, by virtue of great compassion for the <s>Dharma</s>, an intense mind of sympathy and a mind of desire to act [for their welfare] is present in the <s>Bodhisattvas</s> toward them. And the <s>Bodhisattva</s> established in the moral conduct of restraint does not corrupt even the mind toward others through contact with fist, clod, stick, or weapon. How much less would one utter evil speech or strike back—much less [engage in] harm through abuse, irritation, or reproach, or through slight painful contacts. And the <s>Bodhisattva</s> established in the moral conduct of restraint is endowed with diligence (<s>apramāda</s>) possessed of five factors: associated with the past, associated with the future, associated with the present, the prior-action [factor], and the accompanying [factor]. The <s>Bodhisattva</s> training in the <s>Bodhisattva</s> trainings—whatever offense one has committed in the past, that has been properly remedied according to the <s>Dharma</s>. This is one's diligence associated with the past. Whatever offense one will commit in the future, that too one will properly remedy according to the <s>Dharma</s>. This is one's diligence associated with the future. Whatever offense one commits in the present, that too one properly remedies according to the <s>Dharma</s>. This is one's diligence associated with the present. And even before an offense, the <s>Bodhisattva</s> develops intense eagerness: 'May I conduct myself in such a way that, while so conducting and so abiding, I do not fall into an offense!' This is the <s>Bodhisattva</s>'s diligence of prior action. Relying on that very diligence of prior action, one so conducts oneself and so abides that no offense arises. This is one's accompanying diligence. The <s>Bodhisattva</s> established in the moral conduct of restraint is one who conceals virtues and reveals faults, is of few desires, content, patient of hardship, not given to panic, calm and composed, free from hypocrisy and all forms of wrong livelihood. Endowed with these ten factors, the <s>Bodhisattva</s> established in the moral conduct of restraint becomes one of well-restrained morality—namely, through indifference to past pleasures, non-delight in future pleasures, non-attachment to present pleasures, delight in secluded dwelling, purification of speech and thought, non-self-deprecation, gentleness, patience, diligence, and purity of conduct and livelihood.

body.text: punarbodhisattvaḥ kuśala[dharma]saṃgrāhakaśīle vyavasthitaḥ uttpannāṃ kāyabhogāpekṣāṃ svalpāmapi nādhivāsayati prāgeva prabhūtām / sarvadauḥśīlyanidānabhūtāṃśca
body.translated_text: Furthermore, the <s>Bodhisattva</s> established in the moral conduct that collects wholesome <s>dharmas</s> does not tolerate even the slightest arising of desire for bodily pleasures, much less abundant [desire]. And all the sources that constitute the cause of immorality

body.text: kleśopakleśān krodhopanāhādīnutpannān nādhivāsayati / utpannāṃ pareṣāmantike āghātapratighavairacittatāṃ nādhivāsayati / utpannamālasyakausīdyaṃ nādhivāsayati / utpannaṃ samāpatyāsvādaṃ samāpattikleśaṃ nādhivāsayati / pañca ca sthānāni yathābhūtaṃ prajānāti / kuśalaphalānuśaṃsaṃ yathābhūtaṃ prajānāti / kuśalahetuṃ kuśalahetuphale viparyāsamaviparyāsañca kuśalasaṃgrahāya cāntarāyaṃ yathābhūtaṃ prajānāti / kuśalaphale bodhisattvaḥ anuśaṃsadarśī kuśalahetuṃ paryeṣate / kuśalasaṃgrahāya viparyāsañcāviparyāsañca yathābhūtaṃ prajānan bodhisattvaḥ prāpya kuśalaphalaṃ nānitye nityadarśī bhavati / na duḥkhe sukhadarśī / nāśucau śacidarśī / nānātmanyātmadarśī / antarāyañca prajānan kuśalasaṃgrahāya parivarjayati / tasyaibhirdaśabhirākāraiḥ kuśaladharmasaṃgrāhakaśīlavyavasthitasya kṣiprameva kuśalasaṃgraho bhavati sarvākāra[saṃgraha]śca yaduta dānopaniṣadāśīlopaniṣadā kṣāntyupaniṣadā vīryopaniṣadā dhyānopaniṣadā pañcākārayā ca [pra]jñayā /
body.translated_text: he does not tolerate the arisen afflictions and secondary afflictions such as anger, resentment, and the like. He does not tolerate the arisen states of hostility, aversion, and enmity-minded attitudes toward others. He does not tolerate arisen laziness and indolence. He does not tolerate the arisen relishing of attainments and defilements of attainments. And he knows five topics as they truly are: he knows as it truly is the benefit of the fruit of wholesome [actions]; he knows as it truly is the cause of the wholesome, the distortion and non-distortion regarding the cause and fruit of the wholesome, and the obstacles to the gathering of the wholesome. The <s>Bodhisattva</s>, seeing the benefit in the fruit of the wholesome, seeks out the cause of the wholesome. Knowing as it truly is the distortion and non-distortion regarding the gathering of the wholesome, the <s>Bodhisattva</s>, having obtained the fruit of the wholesome, does not see permanence in the impermanent, does not see happiness in suffering, does not see purity in the impure, does not see self in the non-self. And knowing the obstacles to the gathering of the wholesome, he avoids them. For this <s>Bodhisattva</s> established in the moral conduct that gathers wholesome <s>dharmas</s> through these ten aspects, the gathering of the wholesome comes about swiftly and in all its aspects — namely, through the proximate cause of generosity (<s>dāna</s>), the proximate cause of moral conduct (<s>śīla</s>), the proximate cause of patience (<s>kṣānti</s>), the proximate cause of vigor (<s>vīrya</s>), the proximate cause of meditation (<s>dhyāna</s>), and through wisdom (<s>prajñā</s>) in its five aspects.

body.text: punarbodhisattvaḥ ekādaśabhirākāraiḥ sarvākāre sattvārthakriyāśīle vyavasthitaḥ / ekaikena sarvākāreṇākāreṇa samanvāgato bhavati / iha bodhisattvaḥ sattvānāṃ teṣu teṣu kṛtyeṣu sahāyībhāvaṃ gacchan kṛtyacintāyāṃ kṛtyasamarthane sahāyībhāvaṃ gacchati adhvagamanāgamane samyakkarmāntaprayoge bhogānāmārakṣaṇe vibhinnānyo 'nyapratisandhāne utsave puṇyakriyāyāñca duḥkheṣu vā / punarbodhisattvaḥ sahāyībhāvaṃ gacchan vyādhitān sattvān paricarati / andhān praṇayati panthānaṃ vyapadiśati / badhirān hastasavācikayārthaṃ grāhayati saṃjñānimittavyapadeśena / vyaṅgān śirasā vā yānena vā vahati / kāmacchandaparyavasthānaduḥkhitānāṃ sattvānāṃ kāmacchandaparyavasthānaduḥkhaṃ prativinodayati / vyāpādastyānamiddhauddhatyakaukṛtyavicikitsāparyavasthānaduḥkhitānāṃ sattvānāṃ yāvadvicikitsāparyavasthānaduḥkhaṃ prativinodayati / kāmavitarkaparyavasthānena duḥkhitānāṃ sattvānāṃ kāmavitarkaṃ prativinodayati / yathākāmavitarkam evaṃ vyāpādahiṃsājñātijanapadāpara vitarkāvamanyanāpratisaṃyuktaḥ kulodaya pratisaṃyuktaśca vitarko veditavyaḥ pariparibhavaparājayaduḥkhena duḥkhitānāṃ sattvānāṃ paraparibhavaparājayaduḥkhaṃ
body.translated_text: Furthermore, the <s>Bodhisattva</s> is established in the moral conduct of serving the welfare of beings in all its aspects through eleven modes. He is endowed with each and every aspect. Here, the <s>Bodhisattva</s>, acting as a companion to beings in their various tasks, assists in the deliberation about tasks, in the accomplishment of tasks, in coming and going on journeys, in the proper application to work, in the protection of wealth, in the reconciliation of those who have fallen apart, in festivals, in the making of merit, and in [times of] suffering. Furthermore, the <s>Bodhisattva</s>, acting as a companion, attends the sick; leads the blind; points out the way; makes the deaf understand through hand gestures and sign-language; carries the disabled on his head or by vehicle. He dispels the suffering of beings afflicted by the obsessive hold of sensual desire. He dispels the suffering of beings afflicted by the obsessive hold of ill-will, sloth-and-torpor, restlessness-and-remorse, and doubt. He dispels the [suffering of] sensual thoughts in beings afflicted by the obsessive hold of sensual thoughts. Just as with sensual thoughts, so with thoughts of ill-will, harm, relatives, homeland, and others — discontent-connected and family-connected thoughts are to be understood. He dispels the suffering of humiliation and defeat in beings suffering from humiliation and defeat by others.

body.text: prativinodayati / adhvapariśrāntānāṃ sthānāsanadānenāṅgaprapīḍanena śramaklamaduḥkhaṃ prativinodayati / punarbodhisattvaḥ sattvānāṃ nyāyaṃ vyapadiśan duścaritacāriṇāṃ sattvānāṃ duścaritaprahāṇāya dharmaṃ deśayati yuktaiḥ padavyañjanaiḥ sahitairānulomikairānucchavikairaupayikaiḥ pratirūpaiḥ pradakṣiṇaiḥ nipakasyāṅgasaṃbhāraiḥ / upāyakauśalyaṃ vā punarvyapadiśati yathā duścaritacāriṇāṃ sattvānāṃ duścaritaprahāṇāya evaṃ matsāriṇāṃ [sattvānāṃ] mātsaryaprahāṇāya dṛṣṭe vā dharme samyagalpakṛcchreṇa bhogānāmarjanāya rakṣaṇāya ca śāsane 'smin pratihatānāṃ śraddhāpratilambhāya darśanapratilambhāya / darśanaviśuddhyā 'pāyasamatikramāya sarvasaṃyojanaparyādānāt sarvaduḥkhasamatikramāya punarbodhisattva upakāriṇāṃ sattvānāṃ kṛtajñatāṃ prāviṣkurvan dṛṣṭvā satkṛtyālapati [saṃlapati] pratisammodayati-ehi svāgatavāditayā / āsanasthānānupradānena ca saṃpratīcchati / tulyādhikena cāsya pratilābhasatkāreṇa pratyupasthito bhavati na nyūnena / sa kṛtyeṣvasyāyācito 'pi sahāyībhāvaṃ gacchati prāgeva yācitaḥ / yathā kṛtyeṣu evaṃ duḥkheṣu nayopadeśe bhayaparitrāṇe vyasanasthaśokaprativinodane upakaraṇopasaṃhāre sanniśrayadāne cittānuvartane bhūtairguṇaiḥ saṃpraharṣaṇe snigdhena cāntarbhāvena vinigrahe ṛddhyā cottāsanāvarjaneneti / peyālam / punarbodhisattvo bhītānāṃ sattvānāṃ bhayesvārakṣakaḥ / kṣudramṛgabhayādapi sattvān rakṣati mitrāmātyajñātisālohitamaraṇepyācāryopādhyāyagurūsthānīyamaraṇe 'pi śokaṃ prativinodayati / bhoga vyasanaṃ vā punarārabhya sa cedbhogā rājñā vā pareṣāmapahṛtā bhavanti / tatra śokaṃ prativinodayati / caurairvā 'pahṛtā bhavanti / agninā vā dagdhā udakena vā apahṛtāḥ kunihitā vā nidhayaḥ pranaṣṭā bhavanti / kuprayuktā vā karmāntāḥ pralugnā bhavanti / apriyairvā dāyādairadhigatā bhavanti / kule vā kulāṃgāra
body.translated_text: He dispels the suffering of fatigue in those weary from travel through the giving of a seat or place to sit and through massage. Furthermore, the <s>Bodhisattva</s>, pointing out what is right to beings, teaches the <s>Dharma</s> for the abandonment of misconduct to beings who engage in misconduct — with appropriate words and phrases that are well-connected, conforming, suitable, fitting, proper, and auspicious, with the components of a wise person's [speech]. Or he points out skillful means for the abandonment of misconduct by beings who engage in misconduct. Just as for the abandonment of misconduct, so for the abandonment of miserliness by the miserly; for the acquisition and protection of wealth in this very life with little effort by those properly [disposed]; for the gaining of faith by those who have lost faith in this teaching; for the gaining of [right] view; for transcending the lower realms through the purification of view; and for the transcendence of all suffering through the complete exhaustion of all fetters. Furthermore, the <s>Bodhisattva</s>, manifesting gratitude toward beings who have been helpful, having seen [them], speaks respectfully and converses, greets them warmly — saying 'Welcome!' — and receives them by offering a seat or place. He repays them with honor and gifts equal to or greater [than what was received], not less. He acts as a companion in their tasks even without being asked, let alone when asked. As in tasks, so in [times of] suffering, in giving counsel, in protection from danger, in consoling the grief-stricken, in providing requisites, in giving shelter, in following the minds [of beings], in delighting [them] by truthfully [praising] their genuine qualities, in correction through an inner disposition that is affectionate, and in attracting and inspiring through supernatural power. Abbreviation [follows]. Furthermore, the <s>Bodhisattva</s> is a protector of frightened beings in their fears. He protects beings even from the fear of wild animals, from the fear of whirlpools and crocodiles, from the fear of kings, from the fear of thieves, from the fear of adversaries, from the fear of masters and overlords, from the fear of loss of livelihood, from the fear of disrepute, from the fear of embarrassment in assemblies, from the fear of non-human beings and ghosts. Furthermore, the <s>Bodhisattva</s> consoles the grief of beings in distress: beginning with calamities involving relatives, he consoles grief even at the death of parents; at the death of wife and children; at the death of servants, workers, and dependents; at the death of friends, ministers, relatives, and kinsmen; at the death of teachers, preceptors, and those in the position of elders. Furthermore, beginning with calamities involving wealth: if possessions have been seized by the king or by others, he consoles their grief. [Likewise] if seized by thieves; if burnt by fire or carried away by water; if hidden treasures are lost; if enterprises poorly managed have gone to ruin; if [wealth has been] obtained by disliked heirs; or if in the family a prodigal

body.text: utpanno bhavati / yena te bhogā anayena vyasanamāpāditā bhavanti / tannidānamapi śokamutpannaṃ mṛdumadhyādhimātraṃ sattvānāṃ bodhisattvaḥ samyak prativinodayati / punarupakaraṇārthinām upakaraṇopasaṃhāraṃ kurvan bodhisattvo bhojanaṃ bhojanārthibhyo dadāti / pānaṃ pānārthibhyaḥ / yānaṃ yānārthibhyaḥ / vastraṃ vastrārthibhyaḥ / alaṅkāramalaṅkārārthibhyaḥ / bhāṇḍopaskaraṃ bhāṇḍopaskarārthibhyaḥ / gandhamālyavilepanaṃ gandhamālyavilepanārthibhyaḥ / pratiśrayaṃ pratiśrayārthibhyaḥ / ālokamālokārthibhyo dadāti / punaḥ parigrahaśīlena bodhisattvaḥ sattvānāṃ gaṇaparikarṣaṇayogena parigrahaṃ kurvan pūrvantāvat niśrayaṃ dadāti nirāmiṣeṇa cittenānukampācittenānukampācittameva [saṃ]puraṣkṛtya / tato dharmeṇa cīvarapiṇḍapātaśayanāsanaglānapratyayabhaiṣajyapariṣkārāneṣāmarthe śrāddhānāṃ brāhmaṇagṛhapatīnāmantikātparyeṣate / dhārmikaiśca dharmalabdhaiḥ svaiścīvarapiṇḍapātaśayānāsanaglāna pratyayabhaiṣajyapariṣkāraiḥ sādhāraṇaparibhogī ca bhavatyapratiguptabhojī / aṣṭākārañcānulomikamavavādaṃ kālena kālamanuprayacchati / pañcākārayā cānuśāsanyā samyaksamanuśāsti / tadyathokte 'nuśāsanī-balagotrapaṭale tathehāpi veditavyā / punarbodhisattvaścittānuvartanaśīlena sattvānāṃ cittamanuvartamānaḥ ādita evaṃ sattvānāṃ bhāvaṃ ca jānāti prakṛtiñca / bhāvañca jñātvā prakṛtiñca yathā yaiḥ sattvaiḥ sārdhaṃ saṃvastavyaṃ bhavati tathā [taiḥ] saṃvasati / yathā yeṣu sattveṣu pratipattavyaṃ bhavati tathā teṣu pratipadyate / yasya ca sattvasya bodhisattvaścittamanuvartitukāmo bhavati tasya ca cetpaśyatyevaṃrūpeṇāsya vastusamudācāreṇa kāyikavācikena duḥkhadaurmasyamutpatsyete / taccaduḥkhadaurmanasyamasya nākuśalāt sthānād vyutthānāya kuśale ca sthāne pratiṣṭhāpanāya saṃvartiṣyate / pratisaṃkhyāya bodhisattvastaṃ kāyikavācikaṃ vastasamudācāraṃ yatnataḥ pariharati na samudācarati / sa cetpunastad duḥkhadaurmanasyamasyākuśalāt sthānād vyutthāpya
body.translated_text: has arisen, through whom those possessions have been brought to ruin and calamity — the <s>Bodhisattva</s> properly consoles the grief that has arisen in beings, whether mild, middling, or intense, born from such causes. Furthermore, the <s>Bodhisattva</s>, providing requisites to those who need them, gives food to those who need food, drink to those who need drink, a vehicle to those who need a vehicle, clothing to those who need clothing, ornaments to those who need ornaments, household goods to those who need household goods, perfumes, garlands, and ointments to those who need them, shelter to those who need shelter, and light to those who need light. Furthermore, with the moral conduct of embracing [beings], the <s>Bodhisattva</s>, drawing [them] in by the method of assembling a group, first gives shelter with a mind free from material [motivation], with a mind of compassion, placing compassion itself at the forefront. Then, righteously, he seeks robes, alms-food, lodging, and medicine for the sick — the requisites for their needs — from faithful householders and <s>brāhmaṇas</s>. And with his own requisites — robes, alms-food, lodging, and medicine — obtained righteously through the <s>Dharma</s>, he shares communally, eating without concealment. And from time to time, he gives conforming admonition in eight aspects. And with fivefold guidance, he correctly guides [them]. Namely, the guidance as stated in the <s>Balagotra-paṭala</s> (Chapter on the Power of Lineage) — so too here it is to be understood. Furthermore, the <s>Bodhisattva</s>, with the moral conduct of following the minds [of beings], adapting to the minds of beings, first knows the disposition and nature of beings. Having known their disposition and nature, he dwells with those beings with whom he should associate, in the manner appropriate. He acts toward those beings toward whom he should act, in the manner appropriate. And when the <s>Bodhisattva</s> wishes to follow the mind of a being, if he sees that through such and such a physical or verbal conduct, suffering and displeasure would arise in that [being], and that suffering and displeasure would not serve to remove them from an unwholesome state and establish them in a wholesome state — then the <s>Bodhisattva</s>, having reflected, carefully avoids that physical and verbal conduct and does not engage in it. But if that suffering and displeasure would serve to remove them from an unwholesome state and establish them in a wholesome state,

body.text: kuśale sthāne pratiṣṭhāpanāya paśyati nānuvartate / pratisaṃkhyāya bodhisattvaḥ paracittaṃ yaduta parānukampāmevopādāya yena ca pareṣāṃ vastusamudācāreṇa kāyikavācikenānyeṣāmutpadyate duḥkhadaurmanasyam tacca pareṣāṃ tadanyeṣāmakuśalāt sthānād vyutthānāya kuśale sthāne pratiṣṭhā[pa]nāya [na] saṃvartate pratisaṃkhyāya pratisaṃharati bodhisattvastatkāyavāk [karma]samudācāraṃ tadanyeṣāṃ cittānurakṣayā / sa cetpunaḥ paśyati pareṣāṃ tadanyeṣāṃ vā tadubhayorvā akuśalāt sthānād vyutthāpya kuśale sthāne pratiṣṭhāpanāya pratisaṃkhyāya samudācarati bodhisattvastaṃ kāyavāksamudācāram / nānuvartate teṣāṃ sattvānāṃ cittamanukampācittamevopasthāpya / yena ca bodhisattva ātmano vastusamudācāreṇa kāyikavācikena pareṣāṃ duḥkhadaurmanasyamutpadyamānaṃ samanupaśyati sa ca kāyavāksamudācāro na śikṣāpadaparigṛhīto bhavati na puṇyajñānasambhārānugataḥ tacca duḥkhadaurmanasyaṃ pareṣāṃ nākuśalāt sthānāditi pūrvavadveditavyam / pratisaṃharati bodhisattvastaṃ kāyavāksamudācāraṃ paracittānurakṣayā / [tad] viparyayātsamudācāraḥ pūrvavadveditavyaḥ / yathā duḥkhadaurmanasyamevaṃ sukhasaumanasyaṃ yathāyogaṃ vistareṇa veditavyam / na ca paracittānuvartī bodhisattvaḥ parasya krodhaparyavasthānena paryavasthitasya sammukhamavigate krodhaparyavasthāne varṇamapi bhāṣate prāgevāvarṇam / nāpi saṃjñāptimanuprayacchati / punaḥ paracittānuvartī bodhisattvaḥ paramanālapantamapyālapati [prati]sammodayati prāgevālapantaṃ pratisammodayantam / [na ca] paracittānuvartī bodhisattvaḥ pareṣāṃ kṣubhyati nānyatrāvasādayitukāmaḥ / teṣāmevānukampayā praśāntairindriyairavasādayati / na ca paricittānuvartī bodhisattvaḥ paramavahasati nāvaspaṇḍayati na maḍkubhāvamasyopasaṃharati nāpyasparśavihārāya kaukṛtyamupasaṃharati / nigṛhītasyāpi parājitasya na nigrahasthānena saṃcodayati / nīcaiḥ prapannasya na cocchritamātmānaṃ vikhyāpayati / na ca paracittānuvartī bodhisattvaḥ pareṣāmasevī bhavati nāpyatisevī nāpyakālasevī nāpi teṣāṃ purastātpriyavigarhako bhavati nāpyapriyapraśaṃsakaḥ / nāpyasaṃstutaviśvāsī bhavati / nābhīkṣṇayācakaḥ / pratigrahe 'pi ca mātrāṃ jānāti / pratigraheṇa ca bhojanapānādikenopanimantrito na nirākaroti / dhārmiko vā nyāyasaṃjñaptimanuprayacchati /
body.translated_text: he sees [that it leads] to establishing them in a wholesome state, he does not follow [their wishes]. Having reflected upon the minds of others—taking up compassion for others—and when, through the bodily and verbal conduct of others, suffering and displeasure arise in yet others, and that [suffering] does not conduce to raising those others from an unwholesome state and establishing them in a wholesome state, the <s>Bodhisattva</s>, having reflected, restrains that bodily and verbal conduct, out of safeguarding the minds of those others. But if he sees that it [does conduce] to raising those others or those very persons or both from an unwholesome state and establishing them in a wholesome state, the <s>Bodhisattva</s>, having reflected, engages in that bodily and verbal conduct; he does not follow the minds of those beings, but presents only a compassionate mind. And when the <s>Bodhisattva</s> observes that through his own bodily and verbal conduct, suffering and displeasure arise in others, and that bodily and verbal conduct is not embraced by the training-rules, nor accompanied by the accumulations of merit and knowledge, and that suffering and displeasure of others [does not conduce] to removing them from an unwholesome state—this should be understood as before: the <s>Bodhisattva</s> restrains that bodily and verbal conduct, out of safeguarding others' minds. In the opposite case, the conduct should be understood as before. Just as with suffering and displeasure, so with pleasure and gladness, it should be understood in detail as appropriate. The <s>Bodhisattva</s> who follows others' minds does not speak praise—much less blame—to the face of one who is overpowered by the envelopment of anger, while that envelopment has not subsided. Nor does he offer admonition. Again, the <s>Bodhisattva</s> who follows others' minds greets and exchanges pleasantries even with one who does not greet him—how much more so with one who greets and exchanges pleasantries. The <s>Bodhisattva</s> who follows others' minds does not become agitated toward others, nor does he wish to put them down elsewhere; he puts them down only through compassion for them, with tranquil faculties. The <s>Bodhisattva</s> who follows others' minds does not mock another, does not ridicule him, does not bring about humiliation for him, nor does he cause remorse for the sake of an unpleasant dwelling. Even toward one who has been censured and defeated, he does not rebuke with the grounds of censure. And toward one who has humbled himself, he does not display himself as exalted. The <s>Bodhisattva</s> who follows others' minds does not frequent others excessively, nor is he overly attendant, nor does he attend at the wrong time; he is not one who openly praises what is pleasing and censures what is displeasing; he is not one who has untested confidence; he is not a constant asker. In receiving gifts too, he knows the measure. When invited with an offering of food, drink, and the like, he does not refuse. Or else he offers righteous and proper admonition.

punarbodhisattvo bhūtaguṇasaṃharṣaṇaśīlena sattvān saṃpraharṣayan śraddhāguṇasampannān śraddhāguṇasaṃkathayā saṃpraharṣayati śīlaguṇasampannān śīlaguṇasaṃkathayā śrutaguṇasaṃpannān śrutaguṇasaṅkathayā tyāgaguṇasampannāṃstyāgaguṇasaṅkathayā prajñāguṇasampannān prajñāguṇasaṃkathayā saṃpraharṣayati / punarbodhisattvaḥ nigrahaśīlena sattvānnigṛhṇan mṛdvaparādhaṃ mṛduvyatikramaṃ snigdhenāntarbhāvenāvipannena mṛdvyā 'vasādanikayā avasādayati / madhyāparādhaṃ madhyavyatikramaṃ madhyayā ['vasādanikayā] adhimātrāparādhamadhimātrabyatikramamadhimātrayā 'vasādanikayā 'vasādayati / yathā cāvasādanikā tathā daṇḍakarma veditavyam / mṛdumadhyāparādhaṃ mṛdumadhyavyatikramaṃ bodhisattvastāvatkālikayogena punarādānāya pravāsayati teṣāmeva cānyeṣāñca samanuśāsanārthamanukampācittatayā adhimātrāparādhaṃ [adhimātravyatikramaṃ] punarasaṃvāsāyāsaṃbhogāya yāvajjīvenāpyapunaḥpratigrahaṇāya pravāsayati teṣāmeva cānukampayā / mā te bahutaramasmin śāsane 'puṇyaparigrahaṃ kariṣyantīti / pareṣāñca hitakāmatayā samanuśāsanārtham / punarbodhisattvaḥ ṛddhibalena sattvānuttrāsāyitukāmaḥ āvarjayitukāmo vā duścaritacāriṇāṃ sattvānāṃ duścaritavipākaphalamapāyānnarakānmahānarakān śītalanarakān pratyekanarakānupanīyopanīya darśayati / paśyantu bhavanto duścaritasya [kṛtopacitasya] manuṣyabhūtairidamīdṛśaṃ raudraṃ paramakaṭukamaniṣṭaṃ phalavipākaṃ pratyanubhūyamānamiti / te ca taṃ dṛṣṭvā uttrasyanti saṃvegamāpadyante duścaritātprativiramanti / tadekatyāṃśca sattvān bodhisattvasya mahatyāṃ pariṣadi sannisannasya praśnasaṃpādenānādeyaṃ vacanaṃ kartukāmān bodhisattvo vajrapāṇiṃ vā 'nyatamaṃ vā udāravarṇamahākāyaṃ [mahābalaṃ] yakṣamabhinirmimīya bhīṣayatyuttrāsayati / tannidānaṃ saṃpratyayajātasya bahumānajātasya samyageva praśnaprativyākaraṇārtham / tasya ca mahājanakāyasya tena praśnavyākaraṇena vinayanārtham / vicitreṇa vā punaḥ ṛdvyabhisaṃskāreṇa tadyathā eko bhūtvā bahudhā bhavan bahudhā bhūtvā eko bhavan tiraḥ kuḍayaṃ tiraḥ
śailaṃ tiraḥ prākāramasajjamānena kāyena gacchanvistareṇa yāvadbrahmalokaṃ kāyena vaśe vartayan yamakānyapi prātihāryāṇi vidarśayastejodhātumapi samāpadyamānaḥ śrāvakāsādhāraṇaṃ vā punarṛddhimupadarśayannāvarjayan toṣayitvā saṃpraharṣya aśraddhaṃ
body.translated_text: Furthermore, the <s>Bodhisattva</s>, who by nature delights in praising genuine qualities, when gladdening beings: he gladdens those endowed with the quality of faith through talk of the quality of faith; those endowed with the quality of moral conduct through talk of the quality of moral conduct; those endowed with the quality of learning through talk of the quality of learning; those endowed with the quality of generosity through talk of the quality of generosity; and those endowed with the quality of wisdom through talk of the quality of wisdom. Furthermore, the <s>Bodhisattva</s>, who by nature disciplines beings: for a mild offense and mild transgression, he reprimands with a mild rebuke, with an affectionate inner disposition that is unimpaired. For a moderate offense and moderate transgression, with a moderate rebuke. For a great offense and great transgression, with a great rebuke he reprimands. Just as with the rebuke, so the penalty (<s>daṇḍakarma</s>) should be understood. For one of mild or moderate offense and transgression, the <s>Bodhisattva</s>, through a temporary expulsion for the purpose of readmission, banishes [him]—out of compassion for those very persons and for the instruction of others. For one of great offense and great transgression, he banishes through non-cohabitation, non-association, and even lifelong non-readmission—out of compassion for those very persons, [thinking:] 'May they not accumulate more demerit in this teaching'—and for the instruction of others, out of desire for their welfare. Furthermore, the <s>Bodhisattva</s>, wishing to terrify beings through the power of magical ability (<s>ṛddhibala</s>), or wishing to attract beings who conduct themselves wrongly, by supernatural power leads them and shows them the fruits of wrongdoing's ripening—the lower realms, the hells, the great hells, the cold hells, and the isolated hells—[saying:] 'Let the worthy ones behold this terrible, extremely bitter, and unwelcome ripening of fruit being experienced by those who, while human, performed and accumulated wrongdoing.' They, having seen it, become terrified, obtain a sense of urgency, and desist from wrongdoing. And certain beings, seated in the <s>Bodhisattva</s>'s great assembly, wishing to render his words unworthy of acceptance through the provocation of questions—the <s>Bodhisattva</s> creates an apparition of <s>Vajrapāṇi</s> or some other <s>Yakṣa</s> of magnificent appearance, great body, and great strength, and thereby frightens and terrifies them—for the purpose of answering those questions correctly, once they have been led to trust and reverence, and for the purpose of disciplining that great assembly of people through that question-and-answer. Or else, through various kinds of magical transformation—such as being one, becoming many; being many, becoming one; passing through walls, through mountains, through ramparts with an unobstructed body, in detail up to controlling the body as far as the <s>Brahma</s>-world; displaying even the twin miracle (<s>yamaka prātihārya</s>); entering even the fire element; or displaying the magical power unshared with <s>Śrāvakas</s>—attracting, pleasing, and gladdening them, he establishes one lacking faith

body.text: śraddhāsaṃpadi niveśayati / duḥśīlaṃ śīlasaṃpadi alpaśrutaṃ śrutasaṃpadi matsariṇaṃ tyāgasaṃpadi duṣprajñaṃ prajñāsaṃpadi niveśayati / evaṃ hi bodhisattvaḥ sarvākāreṇa sattvārthakriyāśīlena samanvāgato bhavati /
body.translated_text: in the accomplishment of faith; one of poor conduct in the accomplishment of moral conduct; one of little learning in the accomplishment of learning; one who is miserly in the accomplishment of generosity; and one of poor wisdom in the accomplishment of wisdom. Thus, the <s>Bodhisattva</s> is endowed in every way with a nature that works for the welfare of beings.

body.text: ta ete bhavanti trayo bodhisattvasya śīlaskandhāḥ aprameyāḥ puṇyaskandhāḥ / saṃvaraśīlasaṃgṛhītaḥ kuśala dharmasaṃgrāhaka[śīla]saṃgṛhītaḥ sattvārthakriyāśīlasaṃgrahītaśca śīlaskandhaḥ /
body.translated_text: These, then, are the three aggregates of moral conduct (<s>śīlaskandha</s>) of the <s>Bodhisattva</s>, immeasurable aggregates of merit: the aggregate of moral conduct comprised in restraint (<s>saṃvaraśīla</s>), the aggregate of moral conduct comprised in the collection of wholesome <s>dharmas</s> (<s>kuśaladharmasaṃgrāhakaśīla</s>), and the aggregate of moral conduct comprised in working for the welfare of beings (<s>sattvārthakriyāśīla</s>).

body.text: tatra bodhisattvenāsmin trividhe 'pi śīlaskandhe bodhisattvaśikṣāyāṃ śikṣitukāmena gṛhiṇā vā pravrajitena vā 'nuttarāyāṃ samyaksaṃbodhau kṛtapraṇidhānena sahadhārmikasya bodhisattvasya kṛtapraṇidhānasya vijñasya pratibalasya vāgvijñaptyarthagrahaṇāvabodhāya ityevaṃrūpasya bodhisattvasya pūrvaṃ pādayornipatyādhyeṣaṇāṃ kṛtvā yathā tavāhaṃ kulaputrāntikādbodhisattvaśīlasaṃvarasamādānamākāṃkṣāmyādātuṃ tadarhasyanuparodhena muhūrtamasmākamanukampayā dātuṃ śrotuñca / ityevaṃ samyagadhyeṣyaikāṃsamuttarāsaṅgaṃ kṛtvā buddhānāṃ bhagavatāmatītānāgatapratyutpannānāṃ daśamu dikṣu mahābhūmipraviṣṭānāñca mahājñānaprabhāvaprāptānāṃ bodhisattvānāṃ sāmīcīṃ kṛtvā guṇāṃśca teṣāṃmāmukhīkṛtya ghanarasaṃ prasādaṃ cetasaḥ sañjanayya parīttaṃ vā yasya [vā] yācati śaktirhetubalañca / sa vijño bodhisattvo nīcairjānu-maṇḍalanipatitena vā utkuṭu[ka]sthitena vā tathāgatapratimāṃ purataḥ sthāpayitvā saṃpūraskṛtyaivaṃ syādvacanīyaḥ / anuprayaccha me kulaputrāyuṣman bhadanteti vā bodhisattvaśīlasaṃvarasamādānam / ityuktvā ekāgrāṃ smṛtimupasthāpya cittapraśādamevānupabṛṃhayatā na cirasyedānīṃ me 'kṣayasyāprameyasya niruttarasya mahāpuṇyanidhānasya prāptirbhaviṣyatīti etamevārthamanucintayatā tūṣṇīṃ bhavitavyam / tena punarvijñena bodhisattvena sa tathā pratipanno bodhisattvaḥ avikṣiptena cetasā sthitena vā niṣaṇṇena vā āsane idaṃ syādvacanīyaḥ / śruṇu evaṃnāman kulaputra dharmabhrātariti vā bodhisattvo 'si bodhau ca kṛtapraṇidhānaḥ / tena omiti [prati]jñātavyam / sa punaruttari idaṃ syādvacanīyaḥ / pratīcchasi tvamevaṃnāman
body.translated_text: There, the <s>Bodhisattva</s> who wishes to train in these three aggregates of moral conduct in the <s>Bodhisattva</s>-training—whether a householder or one gone forth—having made the vow for the unsurpassed, perfect awakening, should first fall at the feet of a fellow <s>Bodhisattva</s> who has [also] made the vow, who is learned, capable, and able to grasp the meaning of verbal communication—a <s>Bodhisattva</s> of such a kind—and, having made the request: 'May it please you, O son of good family, that I desire to receive from you the undertaking of the <s>Bodhisattva</s> moral discipline (<s>śīlasaṃvara</s>); please, without objection, grant it and hear us, out of compassion, for a moment'—having thus properly made the request, with the upper robe arranged over one shoulder, having performed the proper salutation to the <s>Buddhas</s>, the <s>Bhagavāns</s> of past, future, and present, and to the <s>Bodhisattvas</s> in the ten directions who have entered the great stages and attained the power of great knowledge, and having brought to mind their qualities, generating a dense and rich serene confidence in the mind—whether modest or whatever one's capacity and causal power—that learned <s>Bodhisattva</s>, [the preceptor,] with the one kneeling on the ground or standing in a squatting position, having placed an image of the <s>Tathāgata</s> before him and facing it, should say the following: 'Please, O son of good family, or venerable sir, grant me the undertaking of the <s>Bodhisattva</s> moral discipline.' Having said this, with one-pointed mindfulness established, nurturing only mental serenity, [thinking:] 'Soon now I shall obtain the attainment of an inexhaustible, immeasurable, unsurpassed great storehouse of merit'—reflecting on this very meaning, one should remain silent. Then that learned <s>Bodhisattva</s> [preceptor], to the <s>Bodhisattva</s> who has thus practiced, standing or seated with undistracted mind, should say the following: 'Listen, O son of good family named so-and-so, or brother in the <s>Dharma</s>: you are a <s>Bodhisattva</s> and have made the vow for awakening.' To this, one should assent by saying 'Yes.' Then [the preceptor] should further say the following: 'Do you accept, O [son of good family] named so-and-so,

body.text: kulaputra mamāntikāt sarvāṇi bodhisattvaśikṣāpadāni sarvañca bodhisattvaśīlaṃ saṃvaraśīlaṃ kuśaladharmasaṃgrāhakaśīlaṃ sattvārthakriyāśīlañca / yāni śikṣāpadāni yacchīlamatītānāṃ sarvabodhisattvānāmabhūt / yāni śikṣāpadāni yacchīlamanāgatānāṃ sarvabodhisattvānāṃ bhaviṣyati / yāni śikṣāpadāni yacchīlametarhi daśasu dikṣu pratyutpannānāṃ sarvabodhisattvānāṃ bhavati / yeṣu śikṣāpadeṣu yacchīle 'tītāḥ sarvabodhisattvāḥ śikṣitavantaḥ / anāgatāḥ sarvabodhisattvāḥ śikṣiṣyante / pratyutpannāḥ sarvabodhisattvāḥ śikṣante / tena pratigṛhṇāmīti pratijñātavyam / evaṃ dvirapi trirapi tena ca vijñena bodhisattvena vaktavyam / tena ca mamādāyakena bodhisattvena yāvat trirapi pratijñātavyaṃ pṛṣṭena / evaṃ hi tena vijñena bodhisattvena tasya pratigrāhakasya bodhisattvasya yāvat trirapi bodhisattvaśīlasaṃvarasamādāna dattvā pratijñāñca pratigṛhyāvyutthita eva tasmin pratigrāhake bodhisattve tasyā eva tathāgatapratimāyāḥ purato daśasu dikṣu sarvabuddhabodhisattvānāṃ tiṣṭhatāṃ dhriyatāṃ yāpayatāṃ pādayornipatya sāmīcīṃ kṛtvā evamārocayitavyam / pratigṛhītamanena evanāmnā bodhisattvena mama evaṃnāmno bodhisattvasyāntikādyāvat trirapi bodhisattvaśīlasaṃvarasamādānam / so 'hamevanāmātmānaṃ sākṣibhūtamasyaitannāmno bodhisattvasya paramāryāṇāṃ viparokṣāṇāmapi sarvatra sarvasattvāviparokṣabuddhīnāṃ daśasu dikṣvanantāparyanteṣu lokadhātuṣvārocayāmyasmin bodhisattvaśīlasaṃvarasamādanam / eva dvirapyevaṃ trirapi vaktavyam / evañca punaḥ śīlasaṃvarasamādānakarmaparisamāptyanantaraṃ dharmatā khalveṣā yadvā daśasu dikṣvanantāparnyateṣu lokadhātuṣu tathāgatānāṃ mahābhūmipraviṣṭānāñca bodhisattvānāñca tiṣṭhatāṃ dhriyatāṃ tadrūpaṃ nimittaṃ pradurbhāvati / yena teṣāmevaṃ bhavati / bodhisattvena bodhisattvaśīlasaṃvarasamādānaṃ samāptamiti / teṣāñcānantaraṃ samanvāharastasya bodhisattvasyāntike bhavati / samanvāharatāñca jñānadarśanaṃ pravartate / te tena jñānadarśanena yathābhūtamevaṃ pratisaṃvedayanti / yathā evaṃnānmā bodhisattvena amuṣmin lokadhātāvevaṃnāmno bodhisattvasyāntikāt samyagbodhisattvaśīla saṃbarasamādānaṃ gṛhītamiti / te cāsya sarve putrasyaiva bhrāturivakalyāṇairmanobhiḥ pratyanukampante / evaṃ kalyāṇamanaḥpratyanukampitasya [tasya] bodhisattvasya
body.translated_text: 'O son of good family, [receive] from me all the precepts of the <s>Bodhisattva</s> and all the moral conduct of the <s>Bodhisattva</s>—the moral conduct of restraint, the moral conduct of gathering wholesome <s>dharmas</s>, and the moral conduct of acting for the welfare of beings. Those precepts and that moral conduct which all past <s>Bodhisattvas</s> had, those precepts and that moral conduct which all future <s>Bodhisattvas</s> will have, those precepts and that moral conduct which all present <s>Bodhisattvas</s> in the ten directions now have—those precepts and that moral conduct in which all past <s>Bodhisattvas</s> have trained, all future <s>Bodhisattvas</s> will train, and all present <s>Bodhisattvas</s> are training—accept them [saying:] "I accept."' This is to be declared. Thus [the formula is to be spoken] twice and three times by that learned <s>Bodhisattva</s> [who confers the vow]. And by that receiving <s>Bodhisattva</s>, when asked, it is to be declared up to three times. Thus indeed, that learned <s>Bodhisattva</s>, having given the undertaking of the <s>Bodhisattva</s>-moral-conduct-restraint up to three times to that receiving <s>Bodhisattva</s>, and having accepted the declaration—while that receiving <s>Bodhisattva</s> remains standing, before that very image of the <s>Tathāgata</s>, prostrating at the feet of all <s>Buddhas</s> and <s>Bodhisattvas</s> abiding, dwelling, and living in the ten directions, and performing respectful salutation, should announce thus: 'This <s>Bodhisattva</s> of such-and-such name has received from me, the <s>Bodhisattva</s> of such-and-such name, up to three times, the undertaking of the <s>Bodhisattva</s>-moral-conduct-restraint. I, of such-and-such name, announce myself as witness of this <s>Bodhisattva</s> of such-and-such name, before the supreme noble ones who are beyond sight yet whose knowledge is not beyond the sight of all beings everywhere, in the infinite and boundless world-systems in the ten directions, regarding this undertaking of the <s>Bodhisattva</s>-moral-conduct-restraint.' Thus it is to be spoken twice, and thus three times. And furthermore, immediately after the completion of the ceremony of the moral-conduct-restraint-undertaking, it is indeed the nature of reality that in the infinite and boundless world-systems in the ten directions, such a sign appears before the <s>Tathāgatas</s> who abide and dwell there, and before the <s>Bodhisattvas</s> who have entered the great stages, whereby they know: 'A <s>Bodhisattva</s> has completed the undertaking of the <s>Bodhisattva</s>-moral-conduct-restraint.' And immediately there is their attention toward that <s>Bodhisattva</s>. And as they attend, knowledge-vision operates. Through that knowledge-vision, they know as it truly is thus: 'The <s>Bodhisattva</s> of such-and-such name, in such-and-such a world-system, has correctly received from the <s>Bodhisattva</s> of such-and-such name the <s>Bodhisattva</s>-moral-conduct-restraint-undertaking.' And they all look upon him with benevolent minds, as upon a son or a brother. Thus, for that <s>Bodhisattva</s> upon whom they look with benevolent minds,

body.text: bhūyasyā mātrayā vṛddhiḥ pratikāṃkṣitavyā kuśalānāṃ dharmāṇāṃ na hāniḥ / pratigṛhītañca tacchīlasaṃvarasamādānārocanaṃ tairveditavyam / parisamāptau ca tasmin bodhisattvaśīlasaṃvarasamādānakarmaṇyubhābhyāṃ tābhyāṃ bodhisattvābhyāṃ daśasu dikṣu teṣāmanantāparyantalokadhātugatānāṃ buddhabodhisattvānāṃ sāmīcīṃ kṛtvā pādayornipatyotthātavyam / idaṃ tasya bodhisattvasya śīlasaṃvarasamādānaṃ sarvaśīla-saṃvarasamādānaprativiśiṣṭaṃ bhavati niruttaramaprameyapuṇyaskandhasamanvāgataṃ paramakalyāṇacittāśayasamutthāpitaṃ sarvasattveṣu sarvākāraduścaritapratipakṣabhūtam / yasya śīlasaṃvarasamādānasya sarvaprātimokṣasaṃvarasamādānāni śatatamīmapi kalāṃ nopayanti sahasratamīmapi saṃkhyāmapi kalāmapi gaṇanāmapyupamāmapyupaniṣadamapi nopayanti yaduta puṇyaparigrahamupādāya / tena punarbodhisattvenaivaṃ bodhisattvaśīlasaṃvarasamādānavyavasthitena svayaṃ cābhyuhyābhyuhyedaṃ bodhisattvasya pratirūpaṃ kartum idamapratirūpaṃ kartumiti tathaiva tata ūrdhvaṃ karmaṇā saṃpādayitavyaṃ śikṣā karaṇīyā / bodhisattvasūtrapiṭakādvā yatnataḥ śrutvā 'smābodhisattvasūtrapiṭakamātṛkānibandhāt śrutvā tathaiva śikṣā karaṇīyā / na ca punaḥ sarveṣāṃ bodhisattvānāmantikādvijñānāmapyetacchīlasaṃvarasamādānamādātavyam / bodhisattvena nāśrāddhasyāntikāt pragrahītavyam / yastatprathamata etadevaṃvidhaṃ śīlasaṃvarasamādānaṃ nādhimucyeta nāvatarennāvakalpayennalubdhasya na lobhābhibhūtasya mahecchasyāsantuṣṭasya na śīlavipannasya śikṣāsvanādarakāriṇaḥ śaithilikasya na krodhanasyopanāhinaḥ akṣāntibahulasya parato vyatikramāsahiṣṇoḥ nālasasya kusīdasya yadbhūyasā rātrindivaṃ nidrāsukhaṃ pārśvasukhaṃ śayanasukhañca svīkurvataḥ saṅgaṇikayā cātināmayataḥ / na vikṣiptacittasyāntato godohanamātramapi kuśalacittaikāgratābhāvanā 'samarthasya / na mandasya na momuhajātīyasyātyarthaṃ saṃlīnacittasya bodhisattvasūtrapiṭakaṃ bodhisattvapiṭakamātṛkāmapavadamānasya / na ca punaretat saṃvarasamādānavidhānaṃ bodhisattvenodgṛhya paryavāpyāpi bodhisattvapiṭaka pratihatānāmaśrāddhānāṃ sattvānāṃ sahasaivārocayitavya pravedayitavyam / tatkasya hetoḥ / tathāhi śrutvā '[na]dhimucyamānā mahatājñānāvaraṇenāvṛtā
body.translated_text: growth and not decline of wholesome <s>dharmas</s> should be expected to an even greater extent. And the announcement of the received moral-conduct-restraint-undertaking should be understood by them [the <s>Buddhas</s> and <s>Bodhisattvas</s>]. And upon the completion of that ceremony of the <s>Bodhisattva</s>-moral-conduct-restraint-undertaking, both those <s>Bodhisattvas</s> should rise, having prostrated at the feet of and performed respectful salutation to those <s>Buddhas</s> and <s>Bodhisattvas</s> in the infinite and boundless world-systems in the ten directions. This moral-conduct-restraint-undertaking of the <s>Bodhisattva</s> is the most distinguished among all moral-conduct-restraint-undertakings, endowed with an immeasurable aggregate of merit, arisen from the supremely auspicious intention, serving as the antidote to all forms of misconduct toward all beings. Compared to this moral-conduct-restraint-undertaking, all <s>prātimokṣa</s>-restraint-undertakings do not reach even a hundredth part, a thousandth, a numerical fraction, a calculable portion, a comparison, or a comparable measure—that is, in terms of the embrace of merit. Furthermore, that <s>Bodhisattva</s>, thus established in the <s>Bodhisattva</s>-moral-conduct-restraint-undertaking, should himself investigate and determine: 'This is proper for the <s>Bodhisattva</s> to do, and this is improper to do,' and accordingly, from then on, he should accomplish it in action and undertake the training. Or having diligently heard from this <s>Bodhisattva</s>-sūtra-piṭaka, or having heard from this treatise on the <s>Bodhisattva</s>-sūtra-piṭaka matrix, he should likewise undertake the training. But this moral-conduct-restraint-undertaking is not to be received from all <s>Bodhisattvas</s>—not even from learned ones. A <s>Bodhisattva</s> should not receive it from one who lacks faith. One who initially does not accept, does not believe in, does not approve of, and does not aspire to this kind of moral-conduct-restraint-undertaking—not from one who is greedy, overpowered by greed, of great desires, and dissatisfied; not from one who is morally deficient, careless in the trainings, and lax; not from one who is irascible, vindictive, abundantly impatient, and unable to endure transgressions from others; not from one who is lazy, indolent, who for the most part day and night indulges in the pleasure of sleep, the pleasure of lying on one's side, and the pleasure of reclining, and who wastes time in socializing; not from one of distracted mind, incapable of even so much as the time to milk a cow in the cultivation of one-pointed wholesome mental concentration; not from one who is dull, of a confused disposition, with an excessively contracted mind, one who rejects the <s>Bodhisattva</s>-sūtra-piṭaka and the <s>Bodhisattva</s>-piṭaka matrix. Furthermore, a <s>Bodhisattva</s> should not suddenly announce or proclaim this procedure of the restraint-undertaking, having studied and mastered it, to beings who are hostile and faithless toward the <s>Bodhisattva</s>-piṭaka. For what reason? For having heard it, those who do not accept it, covered by a great obscuration of ignorance,

body.text: apavaderan / yaścainamapavadate sa yāvadapramāṇena puṇyaskandhena samanvāgataḥ saṃvarasthāyī bodhisattvo bhavati tāvadapramāṇenaiva so 'puṇyaskandhenānuṣakto bhavati yāvattāṃ pāpikāṃ vācaṃ pāpikāṃ dṛṣṭiṃ pāpakān sakalpān sarveṇa sarva notsṛjati /
body.translated_text: would disparage it. And whoever disparages it incurs an aggregate of demerit equal in measure to the immeasurable aggregate of merit possessed by the <s>Bodhisattva</s> who abides in the restraint, and remains burdened by it until he completely abandons that evil speech, evil view, and evil intention.

body.text: śīlasaṃvarasamādānañca kartukāmasya bodhisattvasya purato 'syāṃ bodhisattvasūtrapiṭakamātṛkāyāṃ yāni bodhisattvasya śikṣāpadānyāpattisthānāni cākhyātāni tānyanuśrāvayitavyāni / ca cedāśayato vicārayitvā prajñayā pratisaṃkhyāyotsahate / na parasamādāpanikayā nāpi paraspardhayā [sa]dhīro bodhisattvo veditavyaḥ / tena ca pratigṛhītavyaṃ tasya ca dātavyametena vidhinā etacchīlasaṃvarasamādānam /
body.translated_text: And to the <s>Bodhisattva</s> who wishes to undertake the moral-conduct-restraint, the precepts and grounds of offense of the <s>Bodhisattva</s> that are described in this treatise on the <s>Bodhisattva</s>-sūtra-piṭaka matrix should first be recited before him. And if, having examined his intention and deliberated with wisdom, he is willing—not through being induced by another or through rivalry—that <s>Bodhisattva</s> should be understood as firm. He should receive it, and it should be given to him through this procedure—this moral-conduct-restraint-undertaking.

body.text: evañca śīlasaṃvaravyavasthitasya bodhisattvasya catvāraḥ pārājayikasthānīyadharmā bhavanti / katame catvāraḥ / lābhasatkārādhyavasitasyātmotkarṣaṇā parapaṃsanā bodhisattvasya pārājāyikasthānīyo dharmaḥ / satsu saṃvidyamāneṣu bhogeṣu lobhaprakṛtitvāt duḥkhiteṣu kṛpaṇeṣvanātheṣvapratiśaraṇeṣvasamyagayācakeṣu pratyupasthiteṣu nairvṛṇyādāmiṣāvisargaḥ dharmamātsaryāccārthināṃ samyakpratyupasthitānāṃ dharmāṇāmasaṃvibhāgakriyā bodhisattvasya pārājayikasthānīyo dharmaḥ / yadapi bodhisattvastadrūpaṃ krodhaparyavasthānamanuvṛṃhayati yena tato na vākpāruṣyaniścāraṇamātrakeṇa nivartate / krodhābhibhūtaḥ pāṇinā vā loṣṭena vā daṇḍena vā śastreṇa sattvāṃstāḍayati vihiṃsayati viheṭhayati / krodhāśayameva ca tīvramantarākṛtvā pareṣāmantikādvyatikramasajñapti na pratigṛhaṇāti na kṣamate nāśayaṃ vimuñcati / ayamapi bodhisattvasya pārājayikasthānīyo dharmaḥ / bodhisattvapiṭakāpavādaḥ saddharmapratirūpakāṇāñca rocanā dīpanā vyavasthāpanā / svayaṃ vā saddharmapratirūpakādhimuktasya pareṣāṃ cā 'nuvṛttyā bodhisattvasya pārājayikasthānīyo dharmaḥ / itīme catvāraḥ pārājayikasthānīyā dharmāḥ / yeṣāṃ bodhisattvo 'nyatamānyatamaṃ dharmamadhyāpadya prāgeva sarvānabhavyo bhavati dṛṣṭe dharme vipulasya bodhisattvasaṃbhārasyopacayāya parigrahāya / abhavyo bhavati ca dṛṣṭe
body.translated_text: And for the <s>Bodhisattva</s> thus established in the <s>Bodhisattva</s>-moral-conduct-restraint, there are four <s>pārājika</s>-class <s>dharmas</s> (grounds for defeat). Which four? For the <s>Bodhisattva</s> who is intent on gain and honor, self-aggrandizement and disparagement of others is a <s>pārājika</s>-class <s>dharma</s>. When possessions exist and are available, due to having a greedy nature, the non-distribution of material gifts to those who are suffering, wretched, without protector, without refuge, and who have not properly asked—out of stinginess; and due to miserliness regarding the <s>Dharma</s>, the non-sharing of <s>dharmas</s> with those who properly present themselves seeking them—this is a <s>pārājika</s>-class <s>dharma</s> of the <s>Bodhisattva</s>. And when the <s>Bodhisattva</s> nourishes such an obsession of anger that he does not desist from mere utterance of harsh speech—overcome by anger, he strikes, harms, and injures beings with hand, clod, stick, or weapon; and harboring an intense intention of anger, he does not accept the acknowledgment of transgression from others, does not forgive, and does not release resentment—this too is a <s>pārājika</s>-class <s>dharma</s> of the <s>Bodhisattva</s>. Disparagement of the <s>Bodhisattva</s>-piṭaka and the advocacy, illumination, and establishment of counterfeit <s>dharmas</s>—whether one is oneself devoted to counterfeit <s>dharmas</s> or follows others [in doing so]—this is a <s>pārājika</s>-class <s>dharma</s> of the <s>Bodhisattva</s>. These are the four <s>pārājika</s>-class <s>dharmas</s>. A <s>Bodhisattva</s> who commits any one of them, let alone all, becomes incapable, in this very life, of the accumulation and acquisition of the vast <s>Bodhisattva</s>-provisions. He becomes incapable, in this very life, of purification of intention.

body.text: dharme āśayaviśuddheḥ / [sa] bodhisattvapratirūpakaśca bhavati / no tu bhūto bodhisattvaḥ /
body.translated_text: And he becomes a counterfeit <s>Bodhisattva</s>, not a true <s>Bodhisattva</s>.

body.text: mṛdumadhyaparyavasthāna[ta]śca bodhisattvaḥ ebhiścaturbhiḥ pārājayikasthānīyadharmasamudācārādbodhisattvaśīlasaṃvarasamādānaṃ [na] vijahāti / adhimātraparyavasthānatastu vijahāti / yataśca bodhisattvaḥ eṣāṃ caturṇāṃ pārājayikasthānīyānāṃ dharmāṇāmabhīkṣṇa-samudācārāt parīttamapi hrībyapatrāpyaṃ notpādayati / tena ca prīyate / tena ca ramate / tatraiva guṇadarśī bhavati / iyamadhimātratā paryavasthānasya veditavyā / na tu bodhisattvaḥ sakṛdeva pārājayikasthānīyadharmasamudācārāt bodhisattvaśīlasaṃvarasamādānaṃ vijahāti / tadyathā pārājayirkaidharmairbhikṣuḥprātimokṣasaṃvaram / parityaktasamādāno 'pi ca bodhisattvo dṛṣṭe dharme bhavyaḥ punarādānāya bodhisattvaśīlasaṃvarasamādānasya bhavati nābhavya eva tadyathā pārājayikādhyāpannaḥ prātimokṣasaṃvarastho bhikṣuḥ / samāsataśca dvābhyāmeva kāraṇābhyāṃ bodhisattvaśīlasaṃvarasamādānasya tyāgo bhavati / anuttarāyāṃ samyaksaṃbodhau praṇidhānaparityāgataśca pārājayikasthānīyadharmādhimātraparyavasthānasamucārataśca / na ca parivṛttajanmāpi bodhisattvaḥ bodhisattvaśīlasaṃvarasamādānaṃ vijahāti / adha urdhvaṃ tiryaksarvatropapadyamāno yena bodhisattvena praṇidhānaṃ na tyaktaṃ bhavati / nāpi ca pārājayikasthānīyānāṃ dharmāṇāmadhimātraṃ paryavasthānaṃ samudācaritaṃ bhavati / muṣitasmṛtistu parivṛttajanmā bodhisattvaḥ kalyāṇamitrasamparkamāgamya smṛtyudbodhanārthaṃ punaḥ punarādānaṃ karoti / na tvabhinavasamādānam /
body.translated_text: And with mild or moderate obsession, the <s>Bodhisattva</s> does not lose the <s>Bodhisattva</s>-moral-conduct-restraint-undertaking through the commission of these four <s>pārājika</s>-class <s>dharmas</s>. But with intense obsession, he does lose it. And when the <s>Bodhisattva</s>, through the frequent commission of these four <s>pārājika</s>-class <s>dharmas</s>, does not generate even a small amount of moral shame and moral dread; and he takes pleasure in it, delights in it, and sees it as meritorious—this should be understood as the intense degree of obsession. But the <s>Bodhisattva</s> does not lose the <s>Bodhisattva</s>-moral-conduct-restraint-undertaking merely from a single commission of a <s>pārājika</s>-class <s>dharma</s>—as a <s>bhikṣu</s> [loses] the <s>prātimokṣa</s>-restraint through <s>pārājika</s> offenses. And even a <s>Bodhisattva</s> who has abandoned the undertaking is capable, in this very life, of re-undertaking the <s>Bodhisattva</s>-moral-conduct-restraint-undertaking—he is not permanently incapable, as is a <s>bhikṣu</s> who has committed a <s>pārājika</s> offense while established in the <s>prātimokṣa</s>-restraint. And in brief, the abandonment of the <s>Bodhisattva</s>-moral-conduct-restraint-undertaking occurs for only two reasons: from the abandonment of the aspiration for unsurpassed perfect awakening, and from the commission of a <s>pārājika</s>-class <s>dharma</s> with intense obsession. And even a <s>Bodhisattva</s> who has been reborn [in another life] does not lose the <s>Bodhisattva</s>-moral-conduct-restraint-undertaking. Whether being reborn below, above, or transversely—everywhere—that <s>Bodhisattva</s> who has not abandoned the aspiration, and who has not committed the <s>pārājika</s>-class <s>dharmas</s> with intense obsession [retains the vow]. But a <s>Bodhisattva</s> who is reborn and whose mindfulness has been lost, upon encountering a virtuous friend (<s>kalyāṇamitra</s>), re-undertakes [the vow] for the purpose of awakening mindfulness, again and again. But it is not a fresh undertaking.

body.text:
evaṃ bodhisattvaśīlasaṃvarasthitasya bodhisattvasyāpattirapi veditavyā / anāpattirapi kliṣṭāpyakliṣṭāpi mṛdvī madhyā 'dhimātrā api /
evaṃ bodhisattvaśīlasaṃvarasthito bodhisattvaḥ pratidivasaṃ tathāgatasya vā tathāgatamuddiśya caitye dharmasya vā dharmamuddiśya pustakagate 'pi bodhisattvasūtrapiṭake
body.translated_text: And for the <s>Bodhisattva</s> thus established in the <s>Bodhisattva</s>-moral-conduct-restraint, offenses and non-offenses, both afflicted and non-afflicted, and of mild, medium, and intense [degrees] should be understood. And the <s>Bodhisattva</s> thus established in the <s>Bodhisattva</s>-moral-conduct-restraint, every day, before the <s>Tathāgata</s> or a <s>stūpa</s> dedicated to the <s>Tathāgata</s>, or before the <s>Dharma</s>, or a manuscript of the <s>Bodhisattva</s>-sūtra-piṭaka dedicated to the <s>Dharma</s>,

body.text: [bodhisattvasūtrapiṭaka]mātṛkāyāṃ vā saṃghasya vā yo 'sau daśasu dikṣu mahābhūmipraviṣṭānāṃ bodhisattvānāṃ saṃghaḥ kiñcidevālpaṃ vā prabhūtaṃ vā pūjādhikārikamakṛtvā 'ntata ekapraṇāmamapi kāyena antato guṇānārabhya buddhadharmasaṃghānāmekacatuṣpadāyā api gāthāyāḥ pravyāhāraṃ vācā antata ekaprasādamapi buddhadharmasaṃghaguṇānusmaraṇapūrvakañcetasā rātriṃdivamatināmayati sāpattiko bhavati sātisāraḥ / sa cedagauravādālasyakausīdyādāpadyate kliṣṭāmāpattimāpanno bhavati / sa cet smṛtisaṃpramoṣādāpadyate akliṣṭāmāpattimāpanno bhavati / anāpattiḥ kṣiptacetasaḥ / anāpattiḥ śuddhāśayabhūmipraviṣṭasya / tathāhi śuddhāśayo bodhisattvaḥ tadyathā avetyaprasādalābhī bhikṣarnityakālameva dharmatayā śāstāraṃ paricarati paramayā ca pūjayā pūjayati dharmasaṃghañca /
body.translated_text: in the <s>Bodhisattva Sūtra-piṭaka Mātṛkā</s>, or of the <s>Saṃgha</s>—which is the community of <s>Bodhisattvas</s> who have entered the great stages in the ten directions—without performing even a small or large act of worship, [that is:] even one prostration with the body, or even the utterance of one four-line verse of praise regarding the qualities of the <s>Buddha</s>, <s>Dharma</s>, and <s>Saṃgha</s> with speech, or even one moment of faith preceded by the recollection of the qualities of the <s>Buddha</s>, <s>Dharma</s>, and <s>Saṃgha</s> with the mind—if he passes a day and night [without doing so], he commits a transgression (<s>āpatti</s>) with a fault. If he falls into this through lack of reverence, laziness, or sloth, he incurs an afflicted transgression. If he falls into this through lapse of mindfulness, he incurs a non-afflicted transgression. There is no transgression for one whose mind is disturbed. There is no transgression for one who has entered the stage of pure superior intention. For the <s>Bodhisattva</s> of pure superior intention—just as a monk who has attained unwavering confidence—naturally at all times attends to the Teacher and honors with supreme worship the <s>Dharma</s> and the <s>Saṃgha</s>.

body.text: bodhisattvo mahecchatāmasantuṣṭiṃ lābhasatkāragardhamutpannamadhivāsayati sāpattiko bhavati sātisāraḥ kliṣṭāmāpattimāpadyate / anāpattistatprahāṇāya cchandajātasya vīryamārabhata statpratipakṣaparigraheṇa tatpratibandhāvasthitasya prakṛtyā tīvrakleśatayābhibhūya punaḥ punaḥ samudācārāṇāt /
body.translated_text: If the <s>Bodhisattva</s> tolerates the arising of great desire, discontent, and pride in gain and honor, he commits a transgression with a fault and incurs an afflicted transgression. There is no transgression for one who, having generated the desire for its abandonment, has initiated energy and, through the embrace of its antidote, remains in a state of counteraction, but is overpowered by the natural intensity of affliction and [the fault] arises again and again.

body.text: bodhisattvo vṛddhatarakaṃ guṇavantaṃ satkārārhaṃ sahadhārmikaṃ dṛṣṭvā mānābhinigrahītaḥ āghātacittaḥ pratighacitto vā utthāyāsanaṃ nānuprayacchati / paraiścālapyamānaḥ pratisammodyamānaḥ paripṛṣṭaśca na yuktarūpeṇa vāk pratyudāhāreṇa pratyupatiṣṭhate mānābhinigṛhīta eva āghātacittaḥ pratighacitto vā sāpattiko bhavati sātisāraḥ kliṣṭāmāpattimāpadyate / no cenmānābhinigṛhīto nāghātacittaḥ pratighacitto vā api tvālasyakausīdyādavyākṛtacitto vā smṛtisaṃpramoṣād [vā] sāpattika eva bhavati sātisāro no tu kliṣṭāmāpattimāpadyate / anāpattirvāḍhaglānaḥ syāt kṣiptacitto vā / anāpattiḥ [suptaḥ] syādayañca prativibuddhasaṃjñī upaśliṣyed ālapet saṃlapet pratisammodayet paripṛcchet / anāpattiḥ pareṣāṃ dharmadeśanāyāṃ prayuktasya sāṃkathyaviniścaye vā / anāpattistadanyeṣāṃ pratisaṃmodayataḥ / anāpattiḥ pareṣāṃ dharmaṃ deśayatāmavahitaśrotrasya śṛṇvataḥ sāṃkathyaṃviniścayaṃ vā / anāpattirdharmasaṃkathāvirasatāṃ dhārmakathikacittañcānurakṣataḥ /
body.translated_text: If the <s>Bodhisattva</s>, seeing an elder, virtuous, worthy-of-honor co-practitioner, suppressed by pride, with a mind of hostility or aversion, does not offer his seat; and when addressed by others in greeting and asked questions, does not respond with a proper verbal reply—suppressed by pride, with a mind of hostility or aversion, he commits a transgression with a fault and incurs an afflicted transgression. If he is not suppressed by pride, nor has a mind of hostility or aversion, but [acts so] from laziness, sloth, with an indeterminate mind, or through lapse of mindfulness, he still commits a transgression with a fault, but does not incur an afflicted transgression. There is no transgression if he is seriously ill or has a disturbed mind. There is no transgression [if he is] asleep—and upon awakening, he should approach, address, converse with, greet, and inquire. There is no transgression if he is engaged in teaching <s>Dharma</s> to others or in discussion for ascertaining [meaning]. There is no transgression if he is greeting others [at the time]. There is no transgression if he is listening attentively to others teaching <s>Dharma</s> or [engaged in] discussion and ascertainment. There is no transgression if he is guarding against the weariness of <s>Dharma</s>-discussion and protecting the mind of the <s>Dharma</s>-speaker.

body.text: anāpattistenopāyena teṣāṃ sattvānāṃ damayato vinayataḥ akuśalātsthānādvyutthāpya kuśale sthānepratiṣṭhāpayataḥ / [anāpattiḥ] sāṃdhikakriyākāramanurakṣataḥ anāpattiḥ pareṣāṃ prabhūtatarāṇāṃ cittamanurakṣataḥ /
body.translated_text: There is no transgression if by that means he is taming and disciplining those beings, raising them from unwholesome states and establishing them in wholesome states. There is no transgression if he is preserving the protocol of the <s>Saṃgha</s>. There is no transgression if he is protecting the minds of those who are more numerous among others.

body.text: bodhisattvaḥ parairupanimantryamāṇo gṛhe vā vihārāntare vā gṛhāntare vā bhojanapānavastrādibhiḥ pariṣkāraiḥ mānābhinigṛhītaḥ āghātacittaḥ pratighacitto vā na gacchati / na nimantraṇāṃ svīkaroti / sāpattiko bhavati sātisāraḥ kliṣṭāmāpattimāpadyate / ālasyakausīdyānna gacchati akliṣṭāmāpattimāpadyate / anāpattirglānaḥ syādapratibalaḥ kṣiptacitto va / anāpattirviprakṛṣṭo deśaḥ syāt mārgaśca sapratibhayaḥ / anāpattistenopāyenāsya damayitukāmaḥ syāt vinetukāmo 'kuśalātsthānād vyutthāpya kuśale sthāne pratiṣṭhāpayitukāmaḥ / anāpattiranyasya pūrvataraṃ pratijñānaṃ bhavet / anāpattirnirantarakuśalapakṣa-[prayuktasya kuśalapakṣa-]cchidrīkārānurakṣārthamagacchataḥ anāpattirapūrvasyārthopasaṃhitasya dharmārthaśravaṇasya parihāṇihetoḥ / yathā dharmārthaśravaṇasya evaṃ sāṃkathyaviniścayasyāpi veditavyam / anāpattirviheṭhanābhiprāyeṇa nimantritaḥ syāt / anāpattiḥ pareṣāṃ prabhūtatarakāṇāmāghatacittamanurakṣataḥ / anāpattiḥ sāṃdhikaṃ kriyākāramanurakṣataḥ /
body.translated_text: If the <s>Bodhisattva</s>, when invited by others to a household, another monastery, or another residence for food, drink, garments, and other provisions, suppressed by pride, with a mind of hostility or aversion, does not go and does not accept the invitation—he commits a transgression with a fault and incurs an afflicted transgression. If he does not go through laziness and sloth—he incurs a non-afflicted transgression. There is no transgression if he is ill, incapable, or has a disturbed mind. There is no transgression if the place is distant and the road is dangerous. There is no transgression if by that means he wishes to tame and discipline [the inviter], raising them from unwholesome states and establishing them in wholesome states. There is no transgression if he has a prior engagement with another. There is no transgression if he does not go in order to guard against a break in his continuous engagement with the wholesome. There is no transgression if [going would cause] the loss of unprecedented, purposeful hearing of <s>Dharma</s>. As with hearing <s>Dharma</s>, so too with discussion for ascertaining [meaning]. There is no transgression if he has been invited with the intention of harassment. There is no transgression if he is guarding the hostile minds of others who are more numerous. There is no transgression if he is preserving the protocol of the <s>Saṃgha</s>.

body.text: bodhisattvaḥ pareṣāmantikājajātarūpajatamaṇimuktāvaidūryādikāni ca dhanajātāni vicitrāṇi prabhūtāni pravarāṇi labhamāno 'nudadhyamānaḥ āghātacittaḥ pratighacitto na pratigṛhṇāti pratikṣipati / sāpattiko bhavati sātisāraḥ kliṣṭāmāpattimāpadyate sattvopekṣayā / ālasyakausīdyānna pratigṛhṇāti / sāpattiko bhavati sātisāro no tu kliṣṭāmāpattimāpadyate / anāpattiḥ kṣiptacittasya / anāpattistasmin pratigrahe ratiṃ cetasaḥ paśyataḥ / [anāpattirvipratisāramasya paścāt saṃbhāvayavaḥ /] anāpattirdānavibhramasya saṃbhāvayataḥ / anāpattirvinirmuktāgrahasya dānapaterdāridrayaṃ vighātaṃ tannidānaṃ saṃbhāvayataḥ / anāpattiḥ sāṃdhikaṃ staupikaṃ saṃbhāvayataḥ / anāpattiḥ parāhṛtamanena saṃbhāvayataḥ yato nidānamasyotpadyeta vadho vā bandho vā daṇḍo vā jyā-nirgarhaṇā vā /
body.translated_text: If the <s>Bodhisattva</s>, when receiving from others abundant, various, and excellent wealth such as gold, silver, gems, pearls, <s>vaiḍūrya</s>, and so forth being offered to him—with a mind of hostility or aversion does not accept and rejects [them]—he commits a transgression with a fault and incurs an afflicted transgression through neglect of beings. If he does not accept through laziness and sloth—he commits a transgression with a fault but does not incur an afflicted transgression. There is no transgression for one with a disturbed mind. There is no transgression if he perceives that his mind would take delight in that acceptance. There is no transgression if he anticipates remorse afterward. There is no transgression if he anticipates that the donor might become confused [about the gift]. There is no transgression if he anticipates that the donor, having given beyond his means, might suffer poverty or loss as a result. There is no transgression if he anticipates [the gift is] communal or belongs to a <s>stūpa</s>. There is no transgression if he anticipates that it has been taken from another, which might result in the owner's killing, imprisonment, punishment, fine, or public censure.

body.text: bodhisattvaḥ pareṣāṃ dharmārthināmāghātacittaḥ pratighacittaḥ īrṣyāviprakṛto vā dharmaṃ nānuprayacchati / sāpattiko bhavati sātisāraḥ kliṣṭāmāpattimāpadyate / ālasyakausīdyānna dadāti sāpattiko bhavati sātisāro na kliṣṭāmāpattimāpadyate / anāpattistīrthikaḥ syāt randhraprekṣī / anāpattirbāḍhaglānaḥ syāt kṣiptacitto vā / anāpattistenopāyena damayitukāmaḥ syādvinetukāmaḥ akuśalāt sthānād vyutthāpya kuśale sthāne pratiṣṭhāpayitukāmaḥ / anāpattirdharme na pravṛttaḥ syāt / anāpattiryadyagauravo 'pratīśo durīryāpathaḥ pratigṛhṇīyāt / anāpattirmṛdvindriyasyodārayā dharmadeśanayā dharmaparyāptyā uttrāsaṃ mithyādarśanaṃ mithyābhiniveśaṃ kṣatiñcopahatiñca saṃbhāvayet / anāpattistaddhastagatasya parebhyaḥ abhājanabhūtebhyo visāraṃ dharmasya saṃbhāvayet /
body.translated_text: If the <s>Bodhisattva</s>, with a mind of hostility, aversion, or corrupted by jealousy, does not give <s>Dharma</s> to those who seek it—he commits a transgression with a fault and incurs an afflicted transgression. If he does not give through laziness and sloth—he commits a transgression with a fault but does not incur an afflicted transgression. There is no transgression if [the seeker] is a heretic (<s>tīrthika</s>) looking for vulnerabilities. There is no transgression if he is seriously ill or has a disturbed mind. There is no transgression if by that means he wishes to tame and discipline [the person], raising them from unwholesome states and establishing them in wholesome states. There is no transgression if [the person] is not engaged in the <s>Dharma</s>. There is no transgression if [the person], being disrespectful, irreverent, and of poor conduct, would accept [improperly]. There is no transgression if he anticipates that a person of mild faculties might become frightened, develop wrong views, wrong attachment, harm, or damage through a noble <s>Dharma</s>-teaching or <s>Dharma</s>-text. There is no transgression if he anticipates that the <s>Dharma</s>, having fallen into [that person's] hands, might be disseminated to others who are unworthy vessels.

body.text: bodhisattvo raudreṣu duḥśīleṣu ca sattveṣvāghātacittaḥ pratighacittaḥ upekṣate viceṣṭate vā raudratāṃ duḥśīlatāmeva ca pratyayaṃ kṛtvā / sāpattiko bhavati sātisāraḥ kliṣṭāmāpattimāpadyate / ālasyakausīdyādupekṣate smṛtisaṃpramoṣācca viceṣṭate / sāpattiko bhavati sātisāro no tu kliṣṭāmāpattimāpadyate / tatkasya hetoḥ / na hi bodhisattvasya śīlavataḥ śānteḥ kāyavāṅmanaskarmapracāre tathānukampācittañca kartukāmatā ca pratyupasthitā bhavati yathā raudreṣu duḥśīleṣu sattveṣu duḥkhahetau vartamāneṣu / anāpattiḥ kṣiptacittasya / anāpattistenopāyenāsya damayitukāmaḥ syādvistareṇa pūrvavat / anāpattiḥ pareṣāṃ prabhūtānāñcittānurakṣiṇaḥ / anāpattiḥ saṃghakriyākārānurakṣiṇaḥ /
body.translated_text: If the <s>Bodhisattva</s>, with a mind of hostility or aversion, neglects or acts against violent and immoral beings, taking their violence and immorality itself as the reason—he commits a transgression with a fault and incurs an afflicted transgression. If he neglects through laziness and sloth, or acts against through lapse of mindfulness—he commits a transgression with a fault but does not incur an afflicted transgression. For what reason? For a <s>Bodhisattva</s> who is virtuous and peaceful in the conduct of body, speech, and mind, compassionate mind and the desire to act [beneficially] are present most urgently with respect to violent and immoral beings who are engaged in the cause of suffering. There is no transgression for one with a disturbed mind. There is no transgression if by that means he wishes to tame [them], and so on in detail as before. There is no transgression if he is protecting the minds of others who are more numerous. There is no transgression if he is preserving the protocol of the <s>Saṃgha</s>.

body.text: bodhisattvo yadbhagavatā prātimokṣe vinaye pratikṣepaṇa-sāvadyaṃ vyavasthāpitaṃ paracittānurakṣāmupādāyāprasannānāṃ sattvānāṃ prasādāya prasannānāñca bhūyobhāvāya / tatra tulyāṃ śrāvakaiḥ śikṣāṃ karoti nirnirākaraṇam / tatkasya hetoḥ / śrāvakāstāvadātmārthaparamāḥ / te tāvanna paraniranurakṣā aprasannānāṃ prasādāya prasannānāñca bhūyobhāvāya śikṣāsu śikṣante / prāgeva bodhisattvāḥ parārthaparamāḥ /
body.translated_text: Whatever the <s>Bhagavān</s> has established in the <s>Prātimokṣa Vinaya</s> as blameworthy through rejection—for the sake of protecting the minds of others, for generating faith in those without faith, and for the increase of those with faith—in these matters, the <s>Bodhisattva</s> trains equally with the <s>Śrāvakas</s>, without exception. For what reason? The <s>Śrāvakas</s> are primarily concerned with their own welfare. Yet even they train in the precepts for protecting others' [minds], for generating faith in those without faith, and for the increase of those with faith. How much more so the <s>Bodhisattvas</s>, who are primarily concerned with the welfare of others.

body.text: yatpunaḥ pratikṣepaṇasāvadyamalpārthatāmalpakṛtyatāmalpotsukavihāratāmārabhya śrāvakāṇāṃ bhagavatā vyavasthāpitāṃ tatra bodhisattvo na tulyāṃ śikṣāṃ śrāvakaiḥ karoti / tatkasya hetoḥ / śobhate śrāvakaḥ svārthaparamaḥ parārthanirapekṣaḥ parārthamārabhyālpārthaḥ alpakṛtyaścālpotsukavihārī ca / na tu bodhisattvaḥ parārthaparamaḥ śobhate parārthamārabhyālpārtho 'lpakṛtyaścālpotsukavihārī ca tathāhi bodhisattvena pareṣāmarthe cīvaraśatāni sahastrāṇyajñātikānāṃ brāhmaṇagṛhapatīnāmantikātparyeṣitavyāni pravāritena / teṣāṃ ca sattvānāṃ balābalaṃ saṃlakṣya yāvadartha pratigṛhītavyāni / yathā cīvarakāṇyevaṃ pātrāṇi / yathā paryeṣitavyānyevaṃ svayaṃ yācitena sūtreṇājñātibhistantuvāyairvāryayitavyāni / pareṣāñcārthāya kauśeyasaṃstaraṇaśatāni niṣadanasaṃstaraṇaśatānyūpasthāpayitavyāni / jātarūparajataśatasahasrakoḍhyagrāṇyapi svīkartavyāni / evamādike 'lpārthatāmalpakṛtyatāmalpotsukavihāratāmārabhya śrāvakāṇāṃ pratikṣepaṇasāvadyena samānaśikṣo bhavati / bodhisattvo bodhisattvaśīlasaṃvarasthaḥ sattvārthamārabhya āghātacittaḥ pratighacittaḥ alpārtho bhavati alpakṛtyaḥ alpotsukavihārī / sāpattiko bhavati sātisāraḥ kliṣṭāmāpattimāpadyate / ālasyakausīdyādalpārtho bhavatyalpakṛtyaḥ alpotsukavihārī / sāpattiko bhavati sātisāro 'kliṣṭāmāpattimāpadyate /
body.translated_text: However, whatever the <s>Bhagavān</s> has established as blameworthy through rejection for the <s>Śrāvakas</s> in terms of having few possessions, few activities, and dwelling with little concern—in these matters the <s>Bodhisattva</s> does not train equally with the <s>Śrāvakas</s>. For what reason? A <s>Śrāvaka</s> who is primarily concerned with his own welfare and disregards the welfare of others looks well having few possessions, few activities, and dwelling with little concern with respect to others' welfare. But a <s>Bodhisattva</s> who is primarily concerned with the welfare of others does not look well having few possessions, few activities, and dwelling with little concern with respect to others' welfare. For the <s>Bodhisattva</s> must seek hundreds and thousands of robes for the welfare of others from householders and brahmins who are not relatives, even when previously invited [not to]; and having assessed the strength and weakness of those beings, he should accept as much as needed. As with robes, so with bowls. As [things] are to be sought, so too he should personally commission thread to be woven by non-relative weavers. For the welfare of others, he should prepare hundreds of silk and sitting-cloth spreads. He should accept even hundreds of thousands of <s>koṭis</s> of gold and silver. In such matters regarding few possessions, few activities, and dwelling with little concern, whatever is established as blameworthy through rejection for <s>Śrāvakas</s>—the <s>Bodhisattva</s> established in the <s>Bodhisattva</s>'s moral discipline, if he has few possessions, few activities, and dwells with little concern with respect to the welfare of beings, with a mind of hostility or aversion—commits a transgression with a fault and incurs an afflicted transgression. If he has few possessions, few activities, and dwells with little concern through laziness and sloth—he commits a transgression with a fault but incurs a non-afflicted transgression.

body.text: asti kiñcitprakṛtisāvadyamapi [yad] bodhisattvastadrūpeṇopāyakauśalyena samudācarati yenānāpattikaśca bhavati bahu ca puṇyaṃ prasūyate / yathāpi tadbodhisattvaścauraṃ taskaraṃ prabhūtānāṃ prāṇiśatānāṃ mahātmanāṃ śrāvakapratyekabuddhabodhisattvānāṃ vadhāyodyatamāmiṣakiñcitkahetoḥ prabhūtānantaryakarmakriyāprayuktaṃ paśyati / dṛṣṭvā ca punarevaṃ cetasā cittamabhisaṃskaroti / yadyapyahamenaṃ prāṇinaṃ jīvitādvyaparopya narakeṣūpapadyeyaṃ kāmaṃ bhavatu me narakopapattiḥ / eṣa ca sattva ānantaryakarma kṛtvā mā bhūnnarakaparāyaṇa iti / evamāśayo bodhisattvastaṃ prāṇinaṃ kuśalacitto 'vyākṛtacitto vā viditvā ṛtīyamānaḥ
body.translated_text: There is something that is blameworthy by nature, yet which the <s>Bodhisattva</s> may enact through such skillful means—whereby he is without transgression and produces great merit. For example, a <s>Bodhisattva</s> sees a robber or thief who is about to kill hundreds of living beings—great beings such as <s>Śrāvakas</s>, <s>Pratyekabuddhas</s>, and <s>Bodhisattvas</s>—for the sake of a trifling material gain, engaged in committing an action of immediate retribution (<s>ānantaryakarma</s>). Having seen this, he forms the following thought: 'Even if I, by depriving this living being of life, were to be reborn in the hells, let there be a hell-rebirth for me! But may this being, having committed an action of immediate retribution, not be destined for the hells.' With such an intention, the <s>Bodhisattva</s>, with a wholesome or indeterminate mind, knowing [the situation] and feeling reluctance—

body.text: anukampācittamevāyatyāmupādāya jīvitādvyaparopayati / anāpattiko bhavati bahu ca puṇyaṃ prasūyate /
body.translated_text: taking up only a compassionate mind for the future, deprives [that person] of life. He is without transgression and produces great merit.

body.text: yathāpi tad bodhisattvo ye sattvā rājāno vā bhavanti rājamahāmātrā vā adhimātraraudrāḥ sattveṣu nirdayā ekāntaparapīḍāpravṛttāḥ / tāṃ satyāṃ śaktau tasmādrājyaiśvaryādhipatyāccyāvayati yatra sthitāste tannidānaṃ bahvapuṇyaṃ prasavanti anukampācitto hitasukhāśayaḥ /
body.translated_text: Just as when a <s>Bodhisattva</s> [encounters] beings who are kings or chief ministers who are excessively cruel, merciless toward beings, and solely engaged in harming others — when the power exists, he deposes them from that sovereignty, lordship, and dominion, where, being established, they produce much demerit — [doing so] with a mind of compassion and an intention of benefit and happiness.
