body.text: ye ca paradravyāpahāriṇaścaurāstaskarāḥ sāṃdhikaṃ staupikañca prabhūtaṃ dravyaṃ hṛtvā svīkṛtyopabhoktukāmāsteṣāmantikāttad dravyaṃ bodhisattva ācchinatti / mā haiva teṣāṃ sa dravyaparibhogo dīrgharātramanarthāyāhitāya bhaviṣyati iti / evameva pratyayaṃ kṛtvā ācchidya sādhikaṃ saṃdhe niryātayati staipikaṃ stūpe / ye ca vaiyāvṛtyakarā vā ārāmikā vā sāṃdhikaṃ staupikañca prabhūtaṃ dravyaṃ vipratipādayantyanayena / svayaṃ [ca] paudgalikaṃ paribhuñjate / tān bodhisattvaḥ pratisaṃkhyāya mā haiva tatkarma / sa ca mithyāparibhogasteṣāṃ bhaviṣyati dīrgharātramanartāyāhitāyaiti / tasmādādhipatyāccyāvayati / tadanena paryāyeṇa bodhisattvaḥ adattamādadāno 'pyanāpattiko bhavati / bahu ca puṇyaṃ prasūyate /
body.translated_text: And when thieves and robbers who steal the property of others have seized and appropriated much property belonging to the <s>Saṅgha</s> or to <s>stūpas</s>, intending to enjoy it themselves, the <s>Bodhisattva</s> seizes that property from them — [thinking:] 'Let not their enjoyment of that property be for their long-term non-benefit and non-welfare.' Having thus reflected and seized it, he restores what belongs to the <s>Saṅgha</s> to the <s>Saṅgha</s>, and what belongs to the <s>stūpa</s> to the <s>stūpa</s>. And when attendants or monastery servants misappropriate much property belonging to the <s>Saṅgha</s> or to <s>stūpas</s> through mismanagement, and personally enjoy it as private [property], the <s>Bodhisattva</s>, having reflected — 'Let not that deed and that wrongful enjoyment be for their long-term non-benefit and non-welfare' — deposes them from their authority. In this manner, the <s>Bodhisattva</s>, even though taking what is not given, incurs no offense. And much merit is produced.

body.text: yathāpi tadgṛhī bodhisattvaḥ abrahmacaryeṣaṇārtaṃ tatpratibaddhacittamaparaparigṛhītaṃ mātṛgrāmaṃ maithunena dharmeṇa niṣevate / mā haivāghātacittatāṃ pratilabhya bahvapuṇyaṃ prasoṣyati / yathepsitakuśalamūlasanniyoge ca vaśyā bhaviṣyatyakuśala[mūla]parityāge cetyanukampācittamevopasthāpya abrahmacaryaṃ maithunaṃ [dharmaṃ] pratiṣevamāno 'pyanāpattiko bhavati / bahu ca puṇyaṃ prasūyate / pravrajitasya punarbodhisattvasya śrāvakaśāsanabhedamanurakṣamāṇasya sarvathā na kalpate 'brahmacaryaniṣevaṇam /
body.translated_text: Just as when a lay <s>Bodhisattva</s> associates with a woman who is tormented by the desire for unchaste conduct, whose mind is set upon it, and who belongs to no other [man], through the rightful means of conjugal relations — [thinking:] 'Let her not, having developed a hostile disposition, produce much demerit; and she will become amenable to being yoked to wholesome roots as desired, and to the abandonment of unwholesome [roots]' — thus, having generated a mind of compassion, even engaging in unchaste conduct and conjugal relations, he incurs no offense. And much merit is produced. But for a renunciant <s>Bodhisattva</s> who protects against the splitting of the <s>Śrāvaka</s>'s teaching, the practice of unchaste conduct is in no way permissible.

body.text: yathāpi tad bodhisattvo bahūnāṃ sattvānāṃ jīvita-vipramokṣārthaṃ bandhanavipramokṣārthaṃ hastapādanāsākarṇaccheda-cakṣurvikalībhāva-paritrāṇārthaṃ yāṃ bodhisattva
body.translated_text: Just as when a <s>Bodhisattva</s>, for the sake of liberating many beings from death, for liberating them from bondage, for saving them from the cutting off of hands, feet, nose, and ears, and from the blinding of eyes — the <s>Bodhisattva</s>

body.text: svajīvitahetorapi samprajānan mṛṣāvācaṃ na bhāṣeta / tāṃ teṣāṃ sattvānāmarthāya pratisaṃkhyāya bhāṣate / iti samāsato yena yena bodhisattvaḥ sattvānāmarthameva paśyati / nānarthaṃ paśyati / svayaṃ ca nirāmiṣacitto bhavati / kevala-sattvahitakāmatānidānaṃ ca vinidhāya saṃjñāṃ samprajānan anyathā-vācaṃ bhāṣate / bhāṣamāṇaḥ anāpattiko bhavati / bahu ca puṇyaṃ prasūyate /
body.translated_text: would not speak a false word even for the sake of his own life — yet for the sake of those beings, having reflected, he speaks it. Thus, in summary, whenever the <s>Bodhisattva</s> sees only the welfare of beings and not their non-welfare, and he himself is of a mind free from material [motivation], and solely through the cause of desiring the welfare of beings, having set aside [ordinary] perception, he speaks a word that is otherwise [than true] while fully aware �� even while speaking it, he incurs no offense. And much merit is produced.

body.text: yathāpi tad bodhisattvo ye sattvā akalyāṇamitra parigṛhītā bhavanti teṣāṃ tebhyaḥ akalyāṇamitrebhyo yathāśakti yathābalaṃ byagrakaraṇīṃ vācaṃ bhāṣate / vyagrārāmaśca bhavati tena prīyamāṇaḥ / anukampācittamevopādāya mā bhūdeṣāṃ sattvānāṃ pāpamitrasaṃsargo dīrgharātramanarthāyāhitāyeti / anena paryāyeṇa mitrabhedamapi kurvan bodhisattvo 'nāpattiko bhavati / bahu ca puṇyaṃ prasūyate /
body.translated_text: Just as when a <s>Bodhisattva</s> [encounters] beings who are under the influence of bad friends — to the extent of his ability and power, he speaks words that create division between them and those bad friends, and he delights in the division, being pleased by it — [thinking,] with a mind of compassion: 'Let not the association of these beings with bad friends be for their long-term non-benefit and non-welfare.' In this manner, even causing the breaking of friendships, the <s>Bodhisattva</s> incurs no offense. And much merit is produced.

body.text: yathāpi tad bodhisattvaḥ utpathacāriṇo 'nyāyacāriṇaḥ sattvān paruṣayā vācā tīkṣṇayāvasādayati yāvadeva tenopāyenākuśalāt sthānād vyutthāpya kuśale sthāne pratiṣṭhāpanārtham / evaṃ pārūṣiko bodhisattvo 'nāpattiko bhavati / bahu ca puṇyaṃ prasūyate /
body.translated_text: Just as when a <s>Bodhisattva</s> admonishes beings who engage in wrong conduct and unjust conduct with harsh and sharp words — solely by that means, for the purpose of removing them from unwholesome states and establishing them in wholesome states. Being harsh in this way, the <s>Bodhisattva</s> incurs no offense. And much merit is produced.

body.text: yathāpi tad bodhisattvo nṛttagītavāditādhimuktānāṃ sattvānāṃ rājacaurānnapāna-veśyā-vīthī-kathādyadhimuktānāṃ ca sattvānāṃ nṛttagītavāditena vicitrābhiśca sambhinnapralāpa-pratisaṃyuktābhiḥ saṃkathābhiranukampāśayena toṣayitvāvarjya vaśyatāṃ vidheyatāṃ copanīyākuśalāt sthānād vyutthāpya kṛśale sthāne pratiṣṭhāpayati / evaṃ sambhinnapralāpī api bodhisattvo 'nāpattiko bhavati / bahu ca puṇyaṃ prasūyate /
body.translated_text: Just as when a <s>Bodhisattva</s>, toward beings who delight in dance, song, and music, and toward beings who delight in tales of kings, thieves, food and drink, courtesans, and marketplace — having first delighted and attracted them through dance, song, music, and various conversations connected with frivolous talk, with an intention of compassion, and having brought them under influence and amenability, removes them from unwholesome states and establishes them in wholesome states. Even engaging in frivolous talk in this way, the <s>Bodhisattva</s> incurs no offense. And much merit is produced.

body.text: bodhisattvaḥ utpannāṃ kuhanāṃ lapanāṃ naimittikatāṃ naiṣpeṣikatāṃ lābhena lābhaṃ niścikīrṣutāṃ mithyājīvakarāṃ dharmānadhivāsayati / na tai ritīyate / na vinodayati / sāpattiko bhavati sātisāraḥ kliṣṭāmāpattimāpadyate / anāpattistatprativinodanāya cchandajātasya yatnamārabhamāṇasya kleśapracuratayā cittamabhibhūya samudācaraṇāt /
body.translated_text: When the <s>Bodhisattva</s> tolerates arisen hypocrisy, flattery, hinting, belittling, and the desire to obtain gain through gain — [dharmas] that constitute wrong livelihood (<s>mithyājīva</s>) — he does not dislike them, does not dispel them — he incurs an offense, with a transgression, and commits a defiled offense. But there is no offense for one who has generated the desire to dispel them and undertakes the effort, [if] due to the abundance of afflictions, the mind is overpowered and [the wrong livelihood still] occurs.

body.text: bodhisattvaḥ auddhatyābhinigṛhītena cetasā 'vyupaśāntaḥ avyayupaśamārāmaḥ uccaiḥ saṃñcagdhati saṃkrīḍate saṃkilikilāyate auddhatyaṃ dravaṃ prāviṣkaroti
body.translated_text: When the <s>Bodhisattva</s>, with a mind seized by restlessness, without inner peace, not delighting in inner peace, loudly laughs, plays, and makes merry, displaying restlessness and agitation,

body.text: pareṣāṃ hāsayitukāmo ramayitukāmaḥ / evameva ca pratyayaṃ kṛtvā sāpattiko bhavati sātisāraḥ kliṣṭāmāpattimāpadyate smṛtisaṃpramoṣādakliṣṭāmāpattimāpadyate / anāpattistadvinodanāya cchandajātasya pūrvavat / anāpattiḥ pareṣāmutpannamāghātaṃ tenopāyena prativinodayitukāmaḥ syāt / anāpattiḥ pareṣāmutpannaṃ śokamapahāpayitukāmaḥ syāt / anāpattiḥ pareṣāṃ tatprakṛtikānāṃtadārāmāṇāṃ saṃgrahāya vā praṇayānusaṃrakṣaṇāya vā tadanuvartanārtham / anāpattiḥ pareṣāṃ bodhisattve manyusambhāvanājātānāmāghātavaimukhyasaṃbhāvanājātānāṃ saumukhyāntarbhāvaśuddhyupadarśanārtham /
body.translated_text: wishing to make others laugh and entertain them — having acted thus for this reason, he incurs an offense, with a transgression, and commits a defiled offense. If through loss of mindfulness, he commits an undefiled offense. There is no offense for one who has generated the desire to dispel it, as before. There is no offense if he wishes to dispel arisen hostility in others through that means. There is no offense if he wishes to remove arisen grief in others. There is no offense if [it is done] for the gathering of or maintaining affection with those who are by nature [inclined to that] and who delight in it, or for accommodating them. There is no offense if, toward those in whom anger, distrust, and the thought of aversion and hostility have arisen toward the <s>Bodhisattva</s>, [it is done] for the purpose of demonstrating friendliness, inner purity, and favorable disposition.

body.text: yaḥ
body.translated_text: But if a <s>Bodhisattva</s> should hold such a view and declare: 'A <s>Bodhisattva</s> should not abide delighting in <s>nirvāṇa</s>; rather, he should abide turned away from <s>nirvāṇa</s>. He should not fear afflictions and secondary afflictions, nor should he in any way separate his mind from them. For a <s>Bodhisattva</s>, wandering in <s>saṃsāra</s> for three incalculable aeons, must accomplish awakening' — he incurs an offense, with a transgression, and commits a defiled offense. For what reason? Just as a <s>Śrāvaka</s> must cultivate delight in <s>nirvāṇa</s> and must generate aversion of mind toward afflictions and secondary afflictions, a hundred thousand million times more so must the <s>Bodhisattva</s> cultivate delight in <s>nirvāṇa</s> and develop aversion of mind toward afflictions and secondary afflictions. For the <s>Śrāvaka</s> is engaged in the welfare of himself alone, while the <s>Bodhisattva</s> is engaged in the welfare of all beings. Therefore, he must cultivate such non-defilement of mind that, even being an <s>Arhat</s>, surpassing [even]

body.text: punarbodhisattva evaṃdṛṣṭiḥ syādevaṃvādī na bodhisattvena nirvāṇārāmeṇa vihartavyam / api tu nirvāṇavimukhena vihartavyam / na ca kleśopakleśebhyo bhetavyam na caikāntena tebhyaścittaṃ vivecayitavyam / tathā hi bodhisattvena trīṇi kalpāsaṃkhyeyāni saṃsāre saṃsaratā bodhiḥ samudānetavyeti / sāpattiko bhavati sātisāraḥ kliṣṭāmāpattimāpadyate / tatkasya hetoḥ / yathā khalu śrāvakeṇa nirvāṇābhiratirāsevitavyā kleśopakleśebhyaśca cittamudvejayitavyaṃ tataḥ śatasahasrakoṭiguṇena bodhisattvena nirvāṇābhiratirāsevitavyā kleśopakleśebhyaśca cetasa udvego bhāvayitavyaḥ / tathā hi śrāvako 'syātmano 'rthāya prayukto bodhisattvaḥ sarvasattvānāmarthāya prayuktaḥ / tena tathā cittāsaṃkleśābhyāsaḥ samudānetavyo yathāyamanarhannapi tatprativiśiṣṭenāsaṃkleśena samanvāgataḥ sāstrave vastuni anuvicaret /
body.translated_text: that non-defilement, he moves among things accompanied by outflows.

body.text: bodhisattvo 'nādeyavacanakaramapaśabdamātmanaḥ ayaśo 'kīrti na rakṣati na pariharati bhūtavastukām / sāpattiko bhavati sātisāraḥ kliṣṭāmāpattimāpadyate / abhūtavastukāṃ na pariharati / sāpattiko bhavati sātisāraḥ akliṣṭāmāpattimāpadyate / anāpattistīrthikaḥ paraḥ syāt / iti yo vā punaranyo 'pyabhiniviṣṭaḥ / anāpattiḥ pravrajyā-bhikṣācaryā-kuśalacaryā-nidāno 'paśabdo niścaret / anāpattiḥ krodhābhibhūto viparyastacitto niścārayet /
body.translated_text: When the <s>Bodhisattva</s> does not protect and ward off false reports, disrepute, and ill-fame concerning himself — [reports] that are untrue — based on [others'] words being unacceptable: he incurs an offense, with a transgression, and commits a defiled offense. If he does not ward off [reports] based on untrue matters: he incurs an offense, with a transgression, and commits an undefiled offense. There is no offense if [the accuser] is a <s>tīrthika</s> (non-Buddhist ascetic) or some other deeply attached person. There is no offense if the ill-fame arises on account of renunciation, begging for alms, virtuous conduct, or [such activities]. There is no offense if one [fails to ward it off because one is] overpowered by anger and with a distorted mind.

body.text: bodhisattvo yena kaṭukaprayogeṇa tīkṣṇaprayogeṇa sattvānāmarthaṃ paśyati taṃ prayogaṃ daurmanasyārakṣayā na samudācarati / sāpattiko bhavati [sātisāraḥ]
body.translated_text: When the <s>Bodhisattva</s> sees that a sharp, harsh course of action would benefit beings, but does not carry it out, protecting against displeasure — he incurs an offense, [with a transgression,]

body.text: akliṣṭāmāpattimāpadyate / anāpattiryat parīttamarthaṃ dṛṣṭadhārmikaṃ paśyet prabhūtaśca tannidānaṃ daurmanasyam /
body.translated_text: and commits an undefiled offense. There is no offense if one sees only a minor, present-life benefit, and the displeasure arising from it would be great.

body.text: bodhisattvaḥ parairākruṣṭaḥ pratyākrośati / roṣitaḥ pratiroṣayati / tāḍitaḥ pratitāḍayati / bhaṇḍitaḥ pratibhaṇḍayati / sāpattiko bhavati sātisāraṃ kliṣṭāmāpattibhāpadyate /
body.translated_text: When the <s>Bodhisattva</s>, reviled by others, reviles in return; angered, retaliates in anger; struck, strikes back; quarreled with, quarrels back — he incurs an offense, with a transgression, and commits a defiled offense.

body.text: bodhisattvaḥ pareṣāṃ vyatikramaṃ kṛtvā vyatikrameṇa vā sambhāvitaḥ āghātacitto mānābhinigṛhītaḥ saṃjñaptimanurūpāṃ nānuprayacchatyupekṣate / sāpattiko bhavati sātisāraḥ kliṣṭāmāpattimāpadyate / ālasyakausīdyāt pramādādvā na saṃjñaptimanuprayacchati / sāpattiko bhavati sātisāraḥ akliṣṭāmāpattimāpadyate / anāpattistenopāyena damayitukāmaḥ syādvinetukāmaḥ akuśalāt sthānādvyutthāpya kuśale sthāne pratiṣṭhāpayitukāmaḥ / anāpattistīrthikaḥ syāt / anāpattirakalpikena sāvadyasamudācāreṇa saṃjñaptipratigrahaṇamākāṃkṣet / anāpattiḥ sa cet prakṛtyā kalahakārakaḥ syādādhikaraṇikaḥ / saṃjñapyamānaśva bhūyasyā mātrayā kupyet adhyārohet / anāpattiḥ paraṃ kṣamaṇaśīlamanā-ghātaśīlaṃ ca saṃbhāvayet parato vyatikramamārabhya saṃjñaptilābhenātyarthaṃ ritīyamānam /
body.translated_text: When the <s>Bodhisattva</s>, having committed a transgression against others or being suspected of a transgression, with a hostile mind, seized by pride, does not offer a proper apology and ignores [the matter] — he incurs an offense, with a transgression, and commits a defiled offense. If out of laziness, indolence, or heedlessness he does not offer an apology — he incurs an offense, with a transgression, and commits an undefiled offense. There is no offense if he wishes by that means to discipline, train, remove from unwholesome states and establish in wholesome states. There is no offense if [the other] is a <s>tīrthika</s>. There is no offense if [the other] would wish to receive an apology involving improper, blameworthy conduct. There is no offense if that [person] is by nature quarrelsome and litigious, and being apologized to, would become even more angry and overbearing. There is no offense if he considers the other to be of a patient and non-hostile nature, who would be excessively distressed by receiving an apology regarding a transgression.

body.text: bodhisattvaḥ pareṣāṃ kasmiṃścidadhikaraṇe nisṛtānāṃ dharmeṇa samena saṃjñaptimanuprayacchatāmāghātacittaḥ paraviheṭhanābhiprāyaḥ saṃjñaptiṃ na pratigṛhṇāti / sāpattiko bhavati sātisāraḥ kliṣṭāmāpattimāpadyate / no cedāghātacitaḥ api tvakṣamaṇaśīlatayā na pratigṛhṇāti / kliṣṭāmāpatti māpadyate / anāpattistenopāyena paraṃ damayitukāmaḥ syāt pūrvavat sarvaṃ veditavyam / anāpattiradharmeṇāsamena saṃjñaptimanuprayacchet /
body.translated_text: When the <s>Bodhisattva</s>, in some dispute involving others who have come forward, offers an apology righteously and fairly — [if] with a hostile mind and an intention of harming the other, he does not accept [their] apology — he incurs an offense, with a transgression, and commits a defiled offense. If not with a hostile mind but through being of an unforgiving nature he does not accept — he commits a defiled offense. There is no offense if he wishes by that means to discipline the other, as before — all is to be understood [as stated earlier]. There is no offense if [the apology] is offered unrighteously and unfairly.

body.text: bodhisattvaḥ pareṣāṃ krodhāśayaṃ vahati dhārayatyutpannamadhivāsayati / sāpattiko bhavati sātisāraḥ kliṣṭāmāpattimāpadyate / anāpattistatprahāṇāya cchandajātasya pūrvavat /
body.translated_text: When the <s>Bodhisattva</s> carries, maintains, and tolerates an arisen disposition of anger toward others — he incurs an offense, with a transgression, and commits a defiled offense. There is no offense for one who has generated the desire for its abandonment, as before.

body.text: bodhisattva upasthānaparicaryāparigardhamadhipatiṃ kṛtvā sāmiṣeṇa cittena gaṇaṃ parikarṣati / sāpattiko bhavati sātisāraḥ kliṣṭāmāpattimāpadyate / anāpattirnirāmiṣacittasyopasthānaparicaryāṃ svīkurvataḥ /
body.translated_text: When the <s>Bodhisattva</s>, placing desire for attendance and personal service at the forefront, with a mind of material [motivation], attracts a following �� he incurs an offense, with a transgression, and commits a defiled offense. There is no offense for one whose mind is free from material [motivation] and who accepts attendance and service.

body.text: bodhisattva utpannamālasyakausīdyaṃ nidrāsukhaṃ śayanasukhaṃ pārśvasukhañcākāle amātrayā svīkaroti / sāpattiko bhavati sātisāraḥ kliṣṭāmāpattimāpadyate / anāpatti[rvāḍha]glānaḥ syādapratibalaḥ / anāpattiradhvapariśrāntasya / anāpattistatprahāṇāya cchandajātasya pūrvavadveditavyam /
body.translated_text: When the <s>Bodhisattva</s> accepts arisen laziness and indolence, the pleasure of sleep, the pleasure of lying down, and the pleasure of reclining at improper times and in improper measure — he incurs an offense, with a transgression, and commits a defiled offense. There is no offense if he is seriously ill and without strength. There is no offense for one weary from travel. There is no offense for one who has generated the desire for its abandonment, as before — this is to be understood.

body.text: bodhisattvaḥ saṃraktacittaḥ saṃgaṇikayā kālamatināmayati / sāpattiko bhavati sātisāraḥ kliṣṭāmāpattimāpadyate / muṣitayā ssṛtyā 'tināmayati / akliṣṭāmāpattimāpadyate / anāpattiḥ para udāharet / sa ca parānuvṛttyā muhūrtamupasthitasmṛtiḥ śṛṇuyāt / anāpattiḥ kautukajātasya paripraśnamātre pṛṣṭasya ca pratyudāhāramātre /
body.translated_text: When the <s>Bodhisattva</s>, with an attached mind, whiles away time in social gathering — he incurs an offense, with a transgression, and commits a defiled offense. If through confused mindfulness he whiles away time — he commits an undefiled offense. There is no offense if another initiates [the conversation] and he, accommodating the other, listens attentively for a moment. There is no offense if he is merely curious and asks a single question, and merely replies when asked.

body.text: bodhisattvaścittasthitimārabhyaṃ citaṃ samādhātukāma āghātacitto mānabhinigṛhīto nopasaṃkramyāvavādaṃ yācate / sāpattiko bhavati sātisāraḥ kliṣṭāmāpattimāpadyate / ālasyakausīdyākliṣṭamāpattimāpadyate / anāpattiglānaḥ syādapratibalaḥ / anāpattiḥ viparītamavavādaṃ saṃbhāṣayet / anāpattiḥ svayaṃ bahaśrutaḥ syātpratibalaścittaṃ samādhātum / kṛtaṃ cānenāvavādakaraṇīyaṃ syāt /
body.translated_text: A <s>Bodhisattva</s>, wishing to compose the mind beginning with mental stability, if out of a hostile mind, suppressed by pride, does not approach and request instruction—one commits an offense (<s>sāpatti</s>) with transgression; one incurs an afflicted offense (<s>kliṣṭā āpatti</s>). If through laziness and indolence—one incurs a non-afflicted offense. No offense if one is ill and incapable. No offense if [the instructor] would give perverted instruction. No offense if one is personally learned and capable of composing the mind. No offense if one has already accomplished what instruction requires.

body.text: bodhisattva utpannaṃ kāmacchandanivaraṇamadhivasayati na vinodayati / sāpattiko bhavati sātisāraḥ kliṣṭamāpattimāpadyate / anāpattistatprahāṇāya cchandajātasya vyāyacchata stīvrakleśatayā cittamabhibhūya samudācaraṇāt / yathā kāmacchanda evaṃ vyāpādaḥ styānamiddhamauddhatyaṃ kaukṛtyaṃ vicikitsā ca veditavyā /
body.translated_text: A <s>Bodhisattva</s> who tolerates the arisen hindrance of sensual desire (<s>kāmacchandanīvaraṇa</s>) and does not dispel it—one commits an offense with transgression; one incurs an afflicted offense. No offense if, for one who has generated the desire for its abandonment and is striving, due to the intensity of the affliction, [the hindrance] arises overpowering the mind. Just as with sensual desire, so it should be understood with ill-will (<s>vyāpāda</s>), sloth and torpor (<s>styānamiddha</s>), restlessness (<s>auddhatya</s>), remorse (<s>kaukṛtya</s>), and doubt (<s>vicikitsā</s>).

body.text: bodhisattvo dhyānamāsvādayati / dhyānāsvāde ca guṇadarśī bhavati / sāpattiko bhavati sātisāraḥ kliṣṭāmāpattimādte / anāpattistatprahāṇāya cchandajātasya pūrvavat /
body.translated_text: A <s>Bodhisattva</s> who savors meditative absorption (<s>dhyāna</s>) and sees merit in that savoring—one commits an offense with transgression; one incurs an afflicted offense. No offense if, for one who has generated the desire for its abandonment, [it arises] as before.

body.text: yaḥ punarbodhisattvaḥ evaṃdṛṣṭi syādevaṃvādī na bodhisattvena śrāvakayānapratisaṃyukto dharmaḥ śrotavyo nodgrahītavyo na tatra śikṣā karaṇīyā / kiṃ bodhisattvasya śrāvakapratisaṃyuktena dharmeṇa śrutenodgṛhītena / kiṃ tatra śikṣayā prayojanamiti / sāpattiko bhavati sātisāraḥ kliṣṭāmāpattimāpadyate / tathā hi bodhisattvena tīrthikaśāstreṣvapi tāvadyogaḥ karaṇīyaḥ prāgeva buddhavacane / anāpattiḥ aikāntikasya tatparasya vicchandanārtham /
body.translated_text: If a <s>Bodhisattva</s> holds such a view and speaks thus: 'A <s>Bodhisattva</s> should not listen to, take up, or train in <s>dharmas</s> connected with the <s>Śrāvaka</s> vehicle. What use has a <s>Bodhisattva</s> for hearing and taking up <s>dharmas</s> connected with the <s>Śrāvakas</s>? What purpose is there in training in them?'—one commits an offense with transgression; one incurs an afflicted offense. For indeed, the <s>Bodhisattva</s> should engage in study even of the treatises of <s>tīrthikas</s>, much more so of the word of the <s>Buddha</s>. No offense if it is for the purpose of dissuading one who is exclusively and entirely devoted to that [Śrāvaka piṭaka].

body.text: bodhisattvo bodhisattvapiṭake sati bodhisattvapiṭake akṛtayogyaḥ sarveṇa sarvaṃ bodhisattvapiṭakamadhyupekṣya śrāvakapiṭake yogyāṃ karoti / sāpattiko bhavati sātisāraḥ kliṣṭāmāpattimāpadyate / bodhisattvo buddhavacane sati buddhavacane akṛtayogyastīrthikaśāstreṣu bahiḥśāstreṣu yogyāṃ karoti / sāpattiko bhavati sātisāraḥ kliṣṭāmāpattimāpadyate / anāpattiradhimātramedhasaḥ āśūdgrahaṇa-samarthasya cireṇāpyavismaraṇa-samarthasya arthacintanāprativedhasamarthasya buddhavacane yuktyupaparīkṣāsahagatayā 'vicalayā buddhyā samanvāgatasya taddviguṇena pratyahaṃ buddhavacane yogyāṃ kurvataḥ /
body.translated_text: A <s>Bodhisattva</s> who, when the <s>Bodhisattva Piṭaka</s> is available, without having practiced in the <s>Bodhisattva Piṭaka</s>, completely neglects the <s>Bodhisattva Piṭaka</s> in its entirety and practices in the <s>Śrāvaka Piṭaka</s>—one commits an offense with transgression; one incurs an afflicted offense. A <s>Bodhisattva</s> who, when the word of the <s>Buddha</s> is available, without having practiced in the word of the <s>Buddha</s>, practices in the treatises of <s>tīrthikas</s> and external texts—one commits an offense with transgression; one incurs an afflicted offense. No offense for one of superior intelligence, capable of swift comprehension, capable of not forgetting even after a long time, capable of penetrating the meaning through reflection, endowed with unwavering understanding accompanied by rational examination of the word of the <s>Buddha</s>, and who devotes double that [time] each day to practice in the word of the <s>Buddha</s>.

body.text: evamapi ca bodhisattvo vidhimanatikramya tīrthikaśāstreṣu bahiḥśāstreṣu kauśalaṃ kurvannabhiratarūpastatra karauti tena ca ramate na tu kaṭubhaiṣajyamiva niṣevamāṇaḥkaroti / sāpattiko bhavati sātisāraḥ kliṣṭāmāpattimāpadyate /
body.translated_text: Moreover, if a <s>Bodhisattva</s>, transgressing the proper method, while developing skill in the treatises of <s>tīrthikas</s> and external texts, appears delighted in them and takes pleasure in them, rather than [studying them] as one consuming bitter medicine—one commits an offense with transgression; one incurs an afflicted offense.

body.text: bodhisattvo bodhisattvapiṭake gambhīrāṇi sthānāni śrutvā paramagaṃbhīrāṇi tattvārthaṃ vārabhya buddhabodhisattvaprabhāvaṃ vā 'nadhimucyamāno 'pavadate / naite arthopasaṃhitā na dharmopasaṃhitā na tathāgatabhāṣitā na hitasukhāya sattvānāmiti / sāpattiko bhavati sātisāraḥ kliṣṭāmāpattimāpadyate / svena vā 'yoniśomanaskāreṇa parānuvṛtyā vā 'pavadamānaḥ /
body.translated_text: A <s>Bodhisattva</s> who, upon hearing the profound and supremely profound passages in the <s>Bodhisattva Piṭaka</s>—concerning the meaning of reality or the power of <s>Buddhas</s> and <s>Bodhisattvas</s>—having no faith, rejects them [saying]: 'These are not connected with meaning, not connected with <s>Dharma</s>, not spoken by the <s>Tathāgata</s>, not for the welfare and happiness of beings'—one commits an offense with transgression; one incurs an afflicted offense—whether rejecting through one's own improper attention or through following others.

body.text: bhavati khalu bodhisattvasya gambhīrāṇi paramagaṃbhīrāṇi sthānāni śrutvā cetaso 'nadhimokṣaḥ / tatra śrāddhenāśaṭhena bodhisattvenedaṃ pratisaṃśikṣitavyam / na me pratirūpaṃ syādandhasyācakṣuṣmatastathāgatacakṣuṣaivānuvyavaharatastathāgatasandhāya bhāṣitaṃ pratikṣeptum / iti [evaṃ] sa bodhisattva ātmānañcājñaṃ vyavasthāpayati
body.translated_text: It may happen that a <s>Bodhisattva</s>, upon hearing profound and supremely profound passages, has no faith in the mind. In that case, a faithful and honest <s>Bodhisattva</s> should train thus: 'It would not be proper for me, being blind and without eyes, to reject what the <s>Tathāgata</s> has spoken, seeing [only] with the <s>Tathāgata</s>'s eye and speaking with reference to the <s>Tathāgata</s>.' Thus that <s>Bodhisattva</s> establishes himself as ignorant

body.text: tathāgatameva ca teṣu buddhadharmeṣvaparokṣatāyāṃ samanupaśyati / evaṃ samyak pratipanno bhavati / anāpattiranadhimucyamānasyāpratikṣipataḥ /
body.translated_text: and regards the <s>Tathāgata</s> alone as having direct knowledge of those <s>Buddha</s>-<s>dharmas</s>. Thus one is correctly practicing. No offense for one who, without having faith, does not reject [the teaching].

body.text: bodhisattvaḥ sāmiṣacittaḥ pratighacittaḥ pareṣāmantike ātmānamutkarṣayati parān paṃsayati / sāpattiko bhavati sātisāraḥ kliṣṭāmāpattimāpadyate / anāpattistīrthikānabhibhavitukāmasya śāsanasthitikāmasya / anāpattistenopāyena tameva pudgalaṃ damayitukāmasya vistareṇa pūrvavat / anāpattiraprasannānāṃ prasādāya prasannānāñca bhūyobhāvāya /
body.translated_text: A <s>Bodhisattva</s> who, with a mind of material attachment or a mind of hostility, exalts himself and denigrates others in the presence of others—one commits an offense with transgression; one incurs an afflicted offense. No offense if one wishes to overpower <s>tīrthikas</s> and establish the teaching. No offense if one wishes to tame that very person by that means—as described in detail before. No offense if it is for generating faith in those without faith and for increasing [faith] in those who have faith.

body.text: bodhisattvo dharmaśravaṇa-dharmasāṃkathyaviniścayaṃ vā mānābhinigṛhītaḥ āghātacittaḥ pratighacitto nopasaṃkrāmati / sāpattiko bhavati sātisāraḥ kliṣṭāmāpattimāpadyate / ālasyakausīdyānnopasaṃkrāmati / akliṣṭāmāpattimāpadyate / anāpattirapratisaṃvedayataḥ / anāpattirglānaḥ syādapratibalaḥ anāpattirviparītāṃ deśanāṃ saṃbhāvayet / anāpattirdhārmakathikacitattānurakṣiṇaḥ anāpattiḥ punaḥ punaḥ [anu]śrutāmavadhṛtāṃ vijñātārthāṃ kathāṃ saṃjānataḥ / anāpattirbahuśrutaḥ syācchrutādhāraḥ śrutasannicayaḥ / anāpattirnirantaramālamba nacittasthiteḥ bodhisattvasamādhyabhinirhārābhiyuktasya / anāpattiradhimātradhandhaprajñasya dhandhaṃ dharmamudgṛhṇataḥ dhandhaṃ dhārayataḥ dhandhamālambane cittaṃ samādadhataḥ /
body.translated_text: A <s>Bodhisattva</s> who, suppressed by pride, with a hostile or averse mind, does not approach [to attend] <s>Dharma</s>-hearing, <s>Dharma</s>-discussion, or elucidation—one commits an offense with transgression; one incurs an afflicted offense. If through laziness and indolence one does not approach—one incurs a non-afflicted offense. No offense if one does not perceive [any teaching available]. No offense if one is ill and incapable. No offense if one would encounter perverted teaching. No offense if one wishes to protect the mind of the <s>Dharma</s>-teacher. No offense if one recognizes a teaching one has repeatedly heard, retained, and understood in meaning. No offense if one is learned, a retainer of what is heard, and a storehouse of what is heard. No offense if one is continuously engaged in the realization of <s>Bodhisattva samādhis</s> with the mind focused without interruption on the object. No offense for one of extremely slow wisdom who is slow to take up the <s>Dharma</s>, slow to retain it, and slow to compose the mind on the object.

body.text: bodhisattvo dharmabhāṇakaṃ pudgalaṃ saṃcintyāvamānayatyasatkarotyavahasatyavaspaṇṅyati vyañjanapratisaraṇaśca bhavati nārthapratisaraṇaḥ / sāpattiko bhavati sātisāraḥ kliṣṭāmāpattimāpadyate /
body.translated_text: A <s>Bodhisattva</s> who deliberately disdains, disrespects, mocks, or ridicules a <s>Dharma</s>-teacher, and who takes refuge in the letter rather than the meaning—one commits an offense with transgression; one incurs an afflicted offense.

body.text: saṃvarastho bodhisattvaḥ sattvakutyeṣvāghātacittaḥ pratighacittaḥ sahāyībhāvaṃ na gacchati yacca tatkutyasamarthe vā adhvagamanāgamane vā samyakkarmānta prayoge vā bhogarakṣaṇe vā bhinnapratisandhāne vā utsave vā puṇyakriyāyāṃ vā / sāpattiko bhavati sātisāraḥ kliṣṭāmāpattimāpadyate / ālasyakausīdyānna
body.translated_text: A <s>Bodhisattva</s> established in the restraint who, with a hostile or averse mind, does not act as a companion in the tasks of beings—whether in tasks that are important, in travel by road, in the engagement of proper livelihood, in the protection of wealth, in the reconciliation of the estranged, in festivals, or in meritorious activities—one commits an offense with transgression; one incurs an afflicted offense. If through laziness and indolence one does not

body.text: sahāyībhāvaṃ gacchati / akliṣṭāmāpattimāpadyate / anāpattirglānaḥ syādapratibalaḥ / anāpattiḥ svayaṃ kartumasamarthaḥ syāt sapratisaraṇaśca yācakaḥ / anāpattiranarthopasaṃhitamadharmopasaṃhitaṃ kṛtyaṃ syāt / anāpattistenopāyena damayitukāmaḥ syādvistareṇa pūrvavat / anāpattiranyasya pūrvataramabhyupagataṃ syāt / anāpattiranyamadhyeṣataḥ pratibalam / anāpattiḥ kuśalapakṣe nairantaryeṇa samyak prayuktaḥ syāt / anāpattiḥ prakṛtyā dhandhaḥ sthāddhandhamuddiśetpūrvavat / anāpattirbahutarakāṇāmanyeṣāñcittamanurakṣitukāmasya / anāpattiḥ sāṃdhikaṃ kriyākāramanurakṣitukāmasya /
body.translated_text: act as a companion—one incurs a non-afflicted offense. No offense if one is ill and incapable. No offense if one is personally unable to act but the requester has other recourse. No offense if the task is connected with harm and not connected with <s>Dharma</s>. No offense if one wishes to tame [the person] by that means—as described in detail before. No offense if another has already undertaken [the task] first. No offense if one requests another who is capable. No offense if one is correctly and continuously engaged in the wholesome. No offense for one who by nature is slow—as described before regarding slowness. No offense if one wishes to protect the minds of many others. No offense if one wishes to preserve the proper manner of a particular occasion.

body.text: bodhisattvo glānaṃ vyādhitaṃ sattvamāsādya nopasthānaparicaryāṃ karoti āghātacittaḥ pratighacittaḥ / sāpattiko bhavati sātisāraḥ kliṣṭāmāpattimāpadyate / ālasyakausīdyānna karoti / akliṣṭāmāpattimāpadyate / anāpattiḥ svayameva glānaḥ syādapratibalaḥ / anāpattiḥ paraṃ pratibalamadhyeṣato 'nukūlam / anāpattirglānaḥ sanāthaḥ syātsapratisaraṇaḥ / anāpattiryāpyena dīrgharogeṇa spṛṣṭaḥ syāt / anāpattirūdāranirantarakuśalapakṣābhiyuktasya kuśalapakṣacchidrānurakṣaṇārtham / anāpattiradhimātradhandhaprajñasya dhandhaṃ dharmamuddiśato dhandhaṃ dhārayato dhandhamālambane cittaṃ samādadhataḥ / anāpattiranyasya pūrvataramabhyupagataṃ syād / yathā glānasyopasthānam / evaṃ duḥkhitasya duḥkhāpanayāya sāhāyyaṃ veditavyam /
body.translated_text: A <s>Bodhisattva</s> who, encountering a sick and ailing being, does not perform attendance and care out of a hostile or averse mind—one commits an offense with transgression; one incurs an afflicted offense. If through laziness and indolence one does not do so—one incurs a non-afflicted offense. No offense if one is oneself ill and incapable. No offense if one requests another who is capable and willing. No offense if the sick person has a protector and recourse. No offense if one has been afflicted by a chronic, debilitating illness. No offense for one who is engaged in noble and continuous wholesome practices, for the purpose of preserving continuity in the wholesome. No offense for one of extremely slow wisdom who is slow to take up the <s>Dharma</s>, slow to retain it, and slow to compose the mind on the object. No offense if another has already undertaken [the care] first. Just as with attendance on the sick, so should assistance in removing the suffering of one who is in distress be understood.

body.text: bodhisattvo dṛṣṭadhārmike sāṃparāyike cārthe anayaprayuktān [sattvān] dṛṣṭvā āghātacittaḥ pratighacitto nyāyaṃ nayaṃ na vyapadiśati / sāpattiko bhavati sātisāraḥ kliṣṭāmāpattimāpadyate / ālasyakausīdyānna vyapadiśati / akliṣṭāmāpattimāpadyate / anāpattiḥ svayamajñaḥ syādapratibalaḥ / anāpattiḥ paraṃ pratibalamadhyeṣeta / anāpattiḥ sa eva svayaṃ pratibalaḥ syāt / anāpattiranyena kalyāṇamitreṇa parigṛhītaḥ syāt / anāpattistenopāyena damayitukāmaḥ syādvistareṇa pūrvavat / anāpattiryasya nyāyopadeśaḥ karaṇīyaḥ sa āghātacittaḥsyāddurvaco viparītagrāhī vigatapremagauravaḥ khaṭuṅkajātīyaḥ /
body.translated_text: A <s>Bodhisattva</s> who, seeing beings engaged in improper courses regarding matters of this life and the next, with a hostile or averse mind does not point out the proper course and guidance—one commits an offense with transgression; one incurs an afflicted offense. If through laziness and indolence one does not point it out—one incurs a non-afflicted offense. No offense if one is personally ignorant and incapable. No offense if one requests another who is capable. No offense if that [person] is personally capable. No offense if [the person] has been taken under the care of another virtuous friend. No offense if one wishes to tame [the person] by that means—as described in detail before. No offense if the one to whom proper guidance should be given is hostile, difficult to speak to, grasps perversely, is devoid of affection and respect, and is of a stubborn nature.

body.text: bodhisattva upakāriṇāṃ sattvānāmakṛtajño bhavatyakṛtavedī āghātacitto na pratyupakāreṇānurūpeṇa pratyupatiṣṭhate / sāpattiko bhavati sātisāraḥ kliṣṭāmāpattimāpadyate / ālasyakausīdyānna pratyupatiṣṭhate / akliṣṭāmāpattimāpadyate / anāpattiryatnavataḥ aśaktasyāpratibalasya / anāpattistenopāyena damayitukāmaḥ syāt pūrvavat / anāpattiḥ sa eva na saṃpratīcchetpratyupakāram /
body.translated_text: A <s>Bodhisattva</s> who is ungrateful and unappreciative toward beings who have helped, and with a hostile mind does not reciprocate with appropriate service—one commits an offense with transgression; one incurs an afflicted offense. If through laziness and indolence one does not reciprocate—one incurs a non-afflicted offense. No offense for one who is making effort but is unable and incapable. No offense if one wishes to tame [the person] by that means—as before. No offense if that [person] does not accept reciprocal service.

body.text: bodhisattvo jñātibhogavyasanasthānāṃ sattvānāmāghātacittaḥ utpannaṃśokaṃ na vinodayati / sāpattiko bhavati sātisāraḥ kliṣṭāmāpattimāpadyate / ālasyakausīdyānna prativinodayati / akliṣṭāmāpattimāpadyate / pūrvavadanāpattirveditavyā tadyathā kṛtyeṣvasahāyībhāvamārabhya /
body.translated_text: A <s>Bodhisattva</s> who, with a hostile mind, does not console the arisen grief of beings who are experiencing misfortunes of relatives, possessions, and calamity—one commits an offense with transgression; one incurs an afflicted offense. If through laziness and indolence one does not console—one incurs a non-afflicted offense. Exceptions should be understood as before, as stated beginning with 'not acting as a companion in tasks.'

body.text: bodhisattvo bhojanapānādinyupakaraṇajātāni bhojanapānādikārthibhyaḥ samyagyācito na prayacchatyāghātacittaḥ pratighacittaḥ / sāpattiko bhavati sātisāraḥ kliṣṭāmāttimāpadyate / ālasyakausīdyātpramādānnānuprayacchati / akliṣṭāmāpattimāpadyate / anāpattirasatsvasaṃvidyamāneṣu bhogeṣu / anāpattirakalpikamapathyaṃ vastu yācitaḥ / anāpattistenopāyena damayitukāmaḥ syādvinetukāmaḥ pūrvavat / anāpattī rājāpathyamanurakṣataḥ anāpattiḥ sāṃdhikaṃ kriyākāramanurakṣataḥ /
body.translated_text: A <s>Bodhisattva</s> who, when properly asked, does not give food, drink, and such requisites to those who desire food, drink, and the like, out of a hostile or averse mind—one commits an offense with transgression; one incurs an afflicted offense. If through laziness, indolence, or heedlessness one does not give—one incurs a non-afflicted offense. No offense if the possessions do not exist. No offense if what is requested is improper or unwholesome. No offense if one wishes to tame or train [the person] by that means—as before. No offense if one is protecting the king's interests. No offense if one wishes to preserve the proper manner of a particular occasion.

body.text: bodhisattvaḥ pariṣadamupasthāpya na kālena kālaṃ sabhyagavavadati samyaksamanuśāsti / na ca teṣāmarthavighātināṃ śrāddhānāṃ brāhmaṇagṛhapatīnāmantikāddharmeṇa cīvarapiṇḍapātaśayanāsana[glāna]pratyayamaiṣajyapariṣkārān paryeṣate āghātacittaḥ / sāpattiko bhavati sātisāraḥ kliṣṭāmāpattimāpadyate / [ālasyakausīdyāt pramādādvā nāvavadati na samanuśāsti na paryeṣate akliṣṭāmāpattimāpadyate /] anāpattistenopāyena damayitukāmaḥ syādvinetukāmaḥ pūrvavat / anāpattiḥ sāṃdhikaṃ kriyākāramanurakṣataḥ / anāpattirglānaḥ syāt aprayogakṣamaḥ / anāpattiranyaṃ pratibalamadhyeṣate / anāpattiḥ pariṣajjātamahāpuṇyā syāt / svayaṃ pratibalo vā cīvarādīnāṃ paryeṣaṇāya / kṛtaṃ caiṣā syāt avavādānuśāsanyām avavādānuśāsanīkaraṇīyam / anāpattistīrthikapūrvī dharmasteyena praviṣṭaḥ syāt / sa ca syādabhavyarupo vinayāya /
body.translated_text: When a <s>Bodhisattva</s>, having established an assembly, does not from time to time correctly instruct and correctly guide them, and does not seek robes, alms-food, bedding, and medicines and provisions for the sick from faithful <s>Brāhmaṇas</s> and householders who do not obstruct the purpose through the <s>Dharma</s>—if [he fails to do this] with an angry mind, he commits an offense, a transgression; he incurs a defiled offense. [If through laziness, sloth, or heedlessness he does not instruct, does not guide, does not seek—he incurs an undefiled offense.] There is no offense if he wishes to discipline and train by that skillful means, as before. There is no offense if he is safeguarding the procedural conduct of the <s>Saṃgha</s>. There is no offense if he is ill and incapable of exertion. There is no offense if he requests another capable person. There is no offense if the assembly has already generated great merit, or if they themselves are capable of seeking robes and the like, or if the work of instruction and guidance that should be done has already been done. There is no offense if one was formerly a non-Buddhist who entered through theft of the <s>Dharma</s>, and such a person would be of incapable character for being trained.

body.text: bodhisattvaḥ āghātacittaḥ pareṣāṃ cittaṃ nānuvartate / sāpattiko bhavati sātisāraḥ kliṣṭāmāpattimāpadyate / ālasyakausīdyāt pramādānnānuvartaṃte akliṣṭāmāpattimāpadyate / anāpattiḥ pareṣāṃ yadabhipretaṃ tadapathyaṃ syāt / anāpattirglānaḥ syādaprayogakṣamaḥ / anāpattiḥ sāṃdhikaṃ kriyākāramanurakṣataḥ / anāpattistasyābhipretaṃ pathyañca syāt pareṣāṃ prabhūtatarakāṇāmanabhipretamapathyañca syāt / anāpattistīrthiko nirgrāhyaḥ syāt / anāpattistenopāyena damayitukāmaḥ syādvinetukāmaḥ pūrvavat /
body.translated_text: When a <s>Bodhisattva</s>, with an angry mind, does not follow the minds of others, he commits an offense, a transgression; he incurs a defiled offense. When through laziness, sloth, or heedlessness he does not follow [their minds], he incurs an undefiled offense. There is no offense if what the other desires would be unwholesome for him. There is no offense if he is ill and incapable of exertion. There is no offense if he is safeguarding the procedural conduct of the <s>Saṃgha</s>. There is no offense if what is desired and wholesome for that person would be undesired and unwholesome for others who are more numerous. There is no offense if the non-Buddhist is to be censured. There is no offense if he wishes to discipline and train by that skillful means, as before.

body.text: bodhisattvaḥ āghātacittaḥ pareṣāṃ bhūtān guṇān nodbhāvayati bhūtaṃ varṇaṃ na bhāṣate subhāṣite sādhukāraṃ na dadāti / sāpattiko bhavati sātisāraḥ / kliṣṭāmāpattimāpadyate / ālasyāt kausīdyāt pramādādvā na bhāṣate akliṣṭāmāpattimāpadyate / anāpattiḥ prakṛtyā 'lpecchatāṃ saṃbhāvayatastadanurakṣayaiva / anāpattirglānaḥ syādapratibalaḥ / anāpattistenopāyena damayitukāmaḥ syādvinetukāmaḥ pūrvavat / anāpattiḥ sāṃghikaṃ kriyākāramanurakṣataḥ / anāpattistato nidānaṃ saṃkleśaṃ madamunnatimanarthāya saṃbhāvayataḥ tasya ca parihārārtham / anāpattirguṇaṃpratirūpakā guṇāḥ syurna bhūtāḥ / subhāṣitapratirūpakañca subhāṣitaṃ syānna bhūtam / anāpattistīrthikaḥ syānnirgrāhyaḥ / anāpattiḥ kathāparyavasānakālamāgamayataḥ /
body.translated_text: When a <s>Bodhisattva</s>, with an angry mind, does not bring forth the genuine qualities of others, does not speak genuine praise, does not give approval to what is well-spoken—he commits an offense, a transgression; he incurs a defiled offense. When through laziness, sloth, or heedlessness he does not speak, he incurs an undefiled offense. There is no offense if he is by nature cultivating fewness of desires and safeguarding that very quality. There is no offense if he is ill and incapable. There is no offense if he wishes to discipline and train by that skillful means, as before. There is no offense if he is safeguarding the procedural conduct of the <s>Saṃgha</s>. There is no offense if on that account he anticipates defilement, pride, conceit, or disadvantage for that person, and [withholds praise] for the purpose of preventing that. There is no offense if the qualities are counterfeit and not genuine, and the well-spoken is counterfeit and not genuine. There is no offense if the person is a non-Buddhist who should be censured. There is no offense if he is awaiting the appropriate time at the end of a discourse.

body.text: bodhisattvo 'vasādanārhān sattvān daṇḍakarmārhān [pravāsanārhān] kliṣṭacitto nāvasādayati / avasādayati vā na ca daṇḍakarmaṇā samanuśāsti / samanuśāsti vā na pravāsayati / sāpattiko bhavati sātisāraḥ / kliṣṭāmāpattimāpadyate / ālasyakausīdyāt pramādādvā nāvasādāyati yāvanna pravāsayati akliṣṭāmāttimāpadyate / anāpattirasādhyarūpamakathyaṃ durvacasamāghātabahulamadhyupekṣataḥ / anāpattiḥ kālāpekṣiṇaḥ / anāpattistato nidānaṃ kalahabhaṇḍanavigrahavivādaprekṣiṇaḥ / anāpattiḥ saṃvaraṇavibhedaprekṣiṇaḥ / anāpattiste sattvā aśaṭhā bhaveyustrīvreṇa hrīvyapatrāpyena samanvāgatā laghu laghveva pratyāpadyeran /
body.translated_text: When a <s>Bodhisattva</s>, with a defiled mind, does not reprimand beings who deserve reprimand, does not penalize those who deserve penalty, does not banish those who deserve banishment—or reprimands but does not discipline with penalty, or disciplines but does not banish—he commits an offense, a transgression; he incurs a defiled offense. When through laziness, sloth, or heedlessness he does not reprimand, up to does not banish, he incurs an undefiled offense. There is no offense if he observes [the person to be] of incurable character, unteachable, obstinate, and prone to hostility, and disregards him. There is no offense if he is waiting for the right time. There is no offense if he anticipates quarrels, disputes, conflict, and litigation on that account. There is no offense if he anticipates a breach in the [<s>Saṃgha</s>'s] harmony. There is no offense if those beings are without deceit and are endowed with intense moral shame and moral dread, and will quickly make amends on their own.

body.text: bodhisattvo vicitrarddhivikurvitaprabhāvasamanvāgataḥ uttrāsanārhāṇāṃ sattvānāmuttrāsanāya āvarjanārhāṇāñca sattvānāmāvarjanāya śraddhādeyaparihārāya [ṛddhyā]
body.translated_text: When a <s>Bodhisattva</s> who is endowed with the power of various magical transformations and displays, does not terrify beings who deserve to be terrified, and does not attract beings who deserve to be attracted, for the sake of safeguarding their faith and goodness, through supernatural power—

body.text: nottrāsayati nāvarjayati / sāpattiko bhavati sātisāraḥ akliṣṭāmāpattimāpadyate / anāpattiryatra sattvā yadbhūyasā pratiniviṣṭā bhaveyustīrthikā āryāpavādikayā mithyādṛṣṭ samanvāgatāḥ / sarvatra cānāpattiradhikacittakṣepato duḥkhavedanābhinna syāsamāttasaṃvarasya veditavyā /
body.translated_text: he does not terrify and does not attract—he commits an offense, a transgression; he incurs an undefiled offense. There is no offense where beings are for the most part deeply committed non-Buddhists (<s>tīrthikas</s>) who hold wrong views that disparage the noble ones. And in all cases, there is no offense for one who has taken the discipline when the mind is greatly disturbed due to painful feelings—this should be understood.

body.text: itīmānyutpannavastukāni bodhisattvānāṃ śikṣāpadāni teṣu teṣu sūtrānteṣu vyagrāṇi bhagavatā ākhyātāni saṃvaraśīlaṃ kuśalasaṃgrāhakaṃ śīlaṃ sattvārthakriyāśīlañcārabhya / tānyasyāṃ bodhisattvapiṭakamātṛkāyāṃ samagrāṇyākhyātāni yeṣu bodhisattvenāradajātena paramagauravamupasthāpya śikṣā karaṇīyā / parataḥ saṃvarasamādanaṃ kṛtvā suviśuddhena śikṣitukāmāśayena bodhyāśayena sattvārthāśayena ādita eva cāvyatikramāyādarajātena bhavitavyam / vyatikrāntena ca yathādharmapratikaraṇatayā pratyāpattiḥ karaṇīyā / sarvā ceyamāpattirbodhisattvasya duṣkṛtyataḥ saṃgṛhītā veditavyā / yasya kasyacicchrāvakayānīyasya vā mahāyānīyasya vā 'ntike deśayitavyā yastāṃ vāgvijñaptiṃ pratibalaḥ syādavaboddhaṃ pratigrahītum / sa cedbodhisattvaḥ pārājayikasthānīyaṃ dharmamadhyāpanno bhavatyadhimātreṇa paryavasthānena tena tyaktaḥ saṃvaraḥ / dvirapi punarādātavyaḥ / sa cenmadhyena paryavasthānenāpanno bhavati tena trayāṇāṃ pudgalānāmantike tato vā uttari duṣkṛtā deśayitavyā / pūrva vastu parikīrtayitvā parato niṣadyedaṃ syādvacanīyam / samanvāharatvāyupmannahamevaṃnāmā bodhisattva-vinayātisāriṇīṃ yathā parikīrtite vastuni dṛṣkṛtāmāpattimāpannaḥ / śiṣṭaṃ yathā bhikṣorduṣkṛtān deśayatastathaiva vaktavyam / pārājayikasthānīyasya ca dharmasya mṛdunā paryavasthānena tadanyāsāñcāpattīnāmekasyaiva purato deśanā veditavyā / asati cānukūle pudgale yasya purato deśyetāśayato bodhisattvena punaranadhyācārāya cittamutpādayitavyam / āyatyāñca saṃvaraḥ karaṇīyaḥ / evamasau vyutthito vaktavyastasyāḥ āpatteḥ /
body.translated_text: These are the training-rules of <s>Bodhisattvas</s> arising from actual situations, proclaimed by the <s>Bhagavān</s> in scattered form throughout the various <s>sūtras</s>, with reference to the moral conduct of restraint, the moral conduct of collecting wholesome <s>dharmas</s>, and the moral conduct of working for the welfare of beings. They have been proclaimed in their entirety in this <s>Bodhisattvapiṭaka Mātṛkā</s> (matrix of the <s>Bodhisattva</s> collection), in which the <s>Bodhisattva</s>, having aroused the utmost respect, should train. Having undertaken the discipline from another, with a thoroughly pure intention to train, an intention toward awakening, and an intention toward the welfare of beings, one should from the very beginning be devoted to non-transgression. And having transgressed, one should make restoration through proper remedy according to the <s>Dharma</s>. All this offense of the <s>Bodhisattva</s> should be understood as comprised in the category of wrongdoing (<s>duṣkṛta</s>). It should be confessed before any <s>Śrāvakayāna</s> or <s>Mahāyāna</s> follower who is capable of receiving and understanding the verbal communication. If a <s>Bodhisattva</s> commits an act that constitutes a <s>pārājika</s> (defeat) offense with an intense degree of mental obsession, the discipline is thereby lost. It should be taken again a second time. If one commits an offense with a moderate degree of obsession, the wrongdoing should be confessed before three persons or more. Having first recounted the situation, one should then sit before the other and say the following: 'May the venerable one attend to me, [son of good family] named so-and-so, a <s>Bodhisattva</s>: I have incurred a wrongdoing offense that is a transgression of the <s>Bodhisattva</s>-<s>vinaya</s>, in the situation as recounted.' The remainder is to be spoken just as for a <s>bhikṣu</s> confessing a wrongdoing. For a <s>pārājika</s>-level offense committed with mild obsession, and for other offenses, confession should be understood as being before a single person. If there is no suitable person before whom to confess, the <s>Bodhisattva</s> should, in intention, generate the mind toward non-repetition. And the discipline should be maintained for the future. Thus, one who has risen [from the offense] should be told regarding that offense.

body.text: etadapi bodhisattvasaṃvarasamādānam / yadi tairguṇairyuṃktaḥ puṅgalo na sannihitaḥsyāttato bodhisattvena tathāgatapratimāyāḥ purataḥ svayameva bodhisattvaśīlasaṃvarasamādānaṃ karaṇīyam / evañca punaḥ karaṇīyam / ekāṃsamuttarāsaṃgaṃ kṛtvā
body.translated_text: This too is the undertaking of the <s>Bodhisattva</s>-discipline: If a person endowed with those qualities is not available, then the <s>Bodhisattva</s> should undertake the <s>Bodhisattva</s> moral discipline on his own, before an image of the <s>Tathāgata</s>. And it should be done as follows: Having arranged the upper robe over one shoulder,

body.text: dakṣiṇaṃ jānumaṇḍalaṃ pṛthivyāṃ pratiṣṭhāpya purato vā utkuṭukasthitena idaṃ syādvacanīyam / ahamevaṃnāmā daśasu dikṣu sarvāstathāgatān mahābhūmipraviṣṭāṃśca bodhisattvān vijñāpayāmi / teṣāñca purataḥ sarvāṇi bodhisattvaśikṣāpadāni sarvaṃ bodhisattvaśīlaṃ samādade saṃvaraśīlaṃ kuśaladharmaṃsaṃgrāhakaṃ sattvārthakriyāśīlañca yatrātītāḥ sarvabodhisattvāḥ śikṣitavantaḥ anāgatāḥ sarvabodhisattvāḥ śikṣiṣyante pratyutpannā daśasu dikṣu sarvabodhisattvā etarhi śikṣante / dvirapi trirapyevaṃ vaktavyam / uktvā utthātavyam / śiṣṭaṃ tu sarvaṃ pūrvavadveditavyam /
body.translated_text: placing the right knee on the ground, or standing in a squatting position before [the image], one should say the following: 'I, named so-and-so, inform all the <s>Tathāgatas</s> in the ten directions and the <s>Bodhisattvas</s> who have entered the great stages and attained the power of great knowledge, and before them I undertake all the training-rules of the <s>Bodhisattva</s>, the entire moral conduct of the <s>Bodhisattva</s>—the moral conduct of restraint, the moral conduct of collecting wholesome <s>dharmas</s>, and the moral conduct of working for the welfare of beings—in which all <s>Bodhisattvas</s> of the past have trained, all <s>Bodhisattvas</s> of the future will train, and all <s>Bodhisattvas</s> of the present in the ten directions are now training.' This should be said twice and a third time. Having said it, one should rise. The remainder should be understood as before.

body.text: nāsti ca bodhisattvasyāpattimārge niravaśeṣā āpattiḥ / yadapi coktaṃ bhagavatā yadbhūyasā bodhisattvasya dveṣasamutthitā āpattirjñātavyā na rāgasamutthiteti tatrāyamabhiprāyo draṣṭavyaḥ / bodhisattvaḥ sattvānunayaṃ sattvapremādhipatiṃ kṛtvā yatkiñcicceṣṭate sarvaṃ tadbodhisattvakṛtyam / nākṛtyaṃ na ca kṛtyaṃ kurvataḥ āpattiryujyate / sattveṣu tu dviṣṭo bodhisattvo nātmano na pareṣāṃ hitamācarati / na caitadbodhisattvakṛtyam / evamakṛtyaṃ kurvataḥ āpattiryujyate /
body.translated_text: There is no offense for the <s>Bodhisattva</s> that is without remainder on the path of offense. And as the <s>Bhagavān</s> said: 'For the most part, the offense of the <s>Bodhisattva</s> should be known as arising from aversion, not from desire'—the intent therein should be understood as follows: The <s>Bodhisattva</s>, taking the affection for beings and the love of beings as predominant, whatever he does—all that is a <s>Bodhisattva</s>-duty; it is not a non-duty. And for one performing a duty, no offense is fitting. But a <s>Bodhisattva</s> who hates beings acts for neither his own welfare nor that of others. And this is not a <s>Bodhisattva</s>-duty. Thus, for one performing a non-duty, an offense is fitting.

body.text: mṛdumadhyādhimātratā ca bodhisattvasyāpattīnāṃ veditavyā / tadyathā vastusaṃgrahaṇyām /
body.translated_text: The mild, moderate, and intense degrees of the <s>Bodhisattva</s>'s offenses should be understood as in the <s>Vastusaṃgrahaṇī</s> (Compendium of Bases).

body.text: evañca punaḥ svavinaye śikṣāprayukto bodhisattvastisṛbhiḥ saṃpattibhiḥ samanvāgataḥ sukhaṃ sparśaṃ viharati prayogasampattyā āśayasampattyā pūrvahetusampattyā ca /
body.translated_text: Thus, the <s>Bodhisattva</s> who is engaged in training in his own discipline, endowed with three accomplishments, abides in comfort: accomplishment of practice (<s>prayogasampatti</s>), accomplishment of intention (<s>āśayasampatti</s>), and accomplishment of prior causes (<s>pūrvahetusampatti</s>).

body.text: tatra prayogasampat katamā / yathāpi tadbodhisattvaḥ śīleṣvakhaṇḍacārī bhavati pariśuddhakāyavāṅmanaḥsamudācāro nābhīkṣṇāpattiko vivṛtapāpaśca bhavati / iyamucyate prayogasampat /
body.translated_text: There, what is the accomplishment of practice? The <s>Bodhisattva</s> is one whose conduct in the moral precepts is unbroken, whose bodily, verbal, and mental conduct is purified, who does not commit offenses frequently, and who is open about his faults. This is called the accomplishment of practice.

body.text: āśayasampat katamā / dharmābhiprāyaḥ pravrajito bhavati na jīvikābhiprāyaḥ / arthī bhavati mahābodhyā nānarthī / arthī śrāmaṇyena nirvāṇena nānarthī / sa evamarthī na kusīdo viharati [na] hīnavīryo [nāvīryo] na vyavakīrṇa pāpakairakuśalairdharmaiḥ sāṃkleśikaiḥ paunarbhavikaiḥ sajvarairduḥkhavipākairāyatyāṃ jātijarāmaraṇīyaiḥ / itīyamucyate āśayasampat /
body.translated_text: What is the accomplishment of intention? He has gone forth with an intention toward the <s>Dharma</s>, not with an intention toward livelihood. He is desirous of great awakening, not indifferent to it. He is desirous of the ascetic life and <s>Nirvāṇa</s>, not indifferent. Being thus desirous, he does not abide in laziness, with weak or no vigor, nor is he involved with evil, unwholesome <s>dharmas</s> that are defiling, conducive to rebirth, feverish, ripening in suffering, and leading to future birth, aging, and death. This is called the accomplishment of intention.

body.text: pūrvahetusaṃpat katamā / yathāpi tadbodhisattvaḥ pūrvamanyāsu jātiṣu kṛtapuṇyo bhavati kṛtakuśalamūlo yenaitarhi svayañca na vihanyate covarapiṇḍapātaśayanāsanaglānapratyayabhaiṣajyapariṣkāraiḥ / anyeṣāmapi pratibalo bhavati saṃvibhāgakriyāyaiḥ / itīyaṃ bodhisattvasya pūrvahetusampadveditavyā /
body.translated_text: What is the accomplishment of prior causes? The <s>Bodhisattva</s> has performed merit and accumulated roots of virtue in former births, by virtue of which he himself is not now obstructed with respect to robes, alms-food, bedding, and medicines and provisions for the sick; and he is capable of sharing with others. This should be understood as the <s>Bodhisattva</s>'s accomplishment of prior causes.

body.text: ābhistisṛbhiḥ saṃpattibhiḥ samanvāgato vinaye śikṣāprayukto bodhisattvaḥ sukhaṃ sparśaṃ viharati / etadviparyayāttisṛbhirvipattibhiḥ samanvāgato duḥkhaṃ saṃsparśaṃ viharatīti veditavyam /
body.translated_text: Endowed with these three accomplishments, the <s>Bodhisattva</s> engaged in training in his discipline abides in comfort. In the opposite case, endowed with three deficiencies, he should be understood as abiding in discomfort.

body.text: idaṃ tāvadbodhisattvasya samāsavyāsataḥ sarvaśīlamityucyate gṛhipakṣagataṃ pravrajitapakṣagatañca / asyaiva ca sarvaśīlasya pravibhāgastadanyānyapi duṣkaraśīlādīni veditavyāni /
body.translated_text: This is called the entire moral conduct of the <s>Bodhisattva</s>, in brief and in detail, pertaining to both the householder side and the renunciant side. The sub-divisions of this very entire moral conduct—namely, the difficult moral conduct and the rest—should also be understood.

body.text: tatra katamadbodhisattvasya duṣkaraśīlam / tat trividhaṃ draṣṭavyam /
body.translated_text: There, what is the difficult moral conduct (<s>duṣkaraśīla</s>) of the <s>Bodhisattva</s>? It should be seen as threefold.

body.text: mahābhogasya bodhisattvasya mahatyaiśvaryādhipatye vartamānasya prahāya bhogān prahāya mahadaiśvaryādhipatyaṃ śīlasaṃvarasamādānaṃ bodhisattvasya duṣkaraśīlamityucyate /
body.translated_text: For a <s>Bodhisattva</s> of great possessions, living in great sovereignty and dominion, the undertaking of the moral discipline after abandoning possessions and abandoning great sovereignty and dominion—this is called the <s>Bodhisattva</s>'s difficult moral conduct.

body.text: kṛcchrāpanno 'pi ca bodhisattvaḥ samāttaśīlaḥ āprāṇairvipadyamānastacchīlasaṃvarasamādānaṃ na chidrīkaroti / kutaḥ punarvipādayiṣyati / idaṃ bodhisattvasya dvitīya duṣkaraśīlamityucyate /
body.translated_text: Even when fallen into difficulty, the <s>Bodhisattva</s> who has undertaken the moral conduct, even while being destroyed up to [the loss of] his life, does not create a breach in that undertaking of moral discipline. How then would he violate it? This is called the <s>Bodhisattva</s>'s second difficult moral conduct.

body.text: tathā tathā bodhisattvaḥ sarvācāravihāramanasikāreṣūpasthitasmṛtirapramatto bhavati / yathā yāvajjīvena [api] pratanukāmapyāpatiṃ nāpadyate na śīle ca skhalati kutaḥ punargurvīm / idaṃ bodhisattvasya tṛtīyaṃ duṣkaraśīlamityucyate /
body.translated_text: In such a way the <s>Bodhisattva</s>, with mindfulness established and heedfulness in all conduct, abiding, and mental engagement, throughout his entire life does not incur even the slightest offense and does not stumble in moral conduct—how much less a grave one. This is called the <s>Bodhisattva</s>'s third difficult moral conduct.

body.text: tatra katamadbodhisattvasya sarvatomukha śīlam / taccaturvidhaṃ draṣṭavyam / samāttaṃ prakṛtiśīlamabhyastamupāyayuktañca /
body.translated_text: What therein is the <s>Bodhisattva</s>'s all-encompassing moral discipline (<s>sarvatomukha śīla</s>)? It is to be seen as fourfold: undertaken, natural, habituated, and conjoined with skillful means.

body.text: tatra samāttaṃ śīlaṃ yena trividhamapi bodhisattvaśīlasaṃvarasamādānaṃ kṛtaṃ bhavati saṃvaraśīlasya kuśalasaṃgrāhaka[śīlasya] sattvārthakriyāśīlasya ca /
body.translated_text: Therein, the undertaken moral discipline is that by which the threefold undertaking of the <s>Bodhisattva</s>'s moral restraint has been performed: the moral discipline of restraint (<s>saṃvaraśīla</s>), the moral discipline of gathering wholesome <s>dharmas</s> (<s>kuśalasaṃgrāhakaśīla</s>), and the moral discipline of acting for the welfare of beings (<s>sattvārthakriyāśīla</s>).

body.text: tatra prakṛtiśīlaṃ yadgotrasthasyaiva bodhisattvasya prakṛtibhadratayaiva santānasya pariśuddhaṃ kāyavākkarma pravartate /
body.translated_text: Therein, the natural moral discipline is that of a <s>Bodhisattva</s> possessing the lineage, in whose continuum pure conduct of body and speech operates simply by virtue of his natural goodness.

body.text: tatrābhyastaṃ śīlaṃ yena bodhisattvena pūrvamanyāsu jātiṣu trividhamapi yathānirdiṣṭaṃ śīlamabhyastaṃ bhavati / sa tena pūrvahetubalādhānena [na] sarveṇa sarvaṃ pāpasamacāreṇa ramate / pāpādudvijate / kuśalasamācāre ramate / kuśalasamācāramevābhilaṣati /
body.translated_text: Therein, the habituated moral discipline is that of a <s>Bodhisattva</s> who has previously habituated the threefold moral discipline as described in other births. Through the force of that previous causal endowment, he does not in any way delight in sinful conduct; he recoils from evil; he delights in wholesome conduct; he aspires only to wholesome conduct.

body.text: tatredamupāyayuktaṃ śīlaṃ yaccatvāri saṃgrahavastūni niśritya bodhisattvasya sattveṣu kuśalaṃ kāyavakkarma pravartate /
body.translated_text: Therein, this is the moral discipline conjoined with skillful means: that by which, relying on the four means of gathering [beings] (<s>saṃgrahavastu</s>), the <s>Bodhisattva</s>'s wholesome conduct of body and speech operates among beings.

body.text: tatra katamadbodhisattvasya satpuruṣaśīlam / tatpañcavidhaṃ veditavyam / iha bodhisattvaḥ svayañca śīlavān bhavati / parāṃśca śīle samādāpayati / śīlasya / ca varṇaṃ bhāṣate / sahadhārmikañca dṛṣṭvā sumanā bhavati / āpattiṃ cāpanno yathādharma pratikaroti /
body.translated_text: What therein is the <s>Bodhisattva</s>'s moral discipline of a good person (<s>satpuruṣaśīla</s>)? It is to be known as fivefold. Here, the <s>Bodhisattva</s> is himself virtuous; he causes others to undertake moral discipline; he speaks the praise of moral discipline; seeing a co-practitioner [who is virtuous], he is pleased; and having committed a transgression, he makes amends according to the <s>Dharma</s>.

body.text: tatra katamadbodhisattvasya sarvākāraṃ śīlam / tat ṣaḍvidhaṃ saptavidhaṃ caikadhyamabhisaṃkṣipya trayodaśavidhaṃ veditavyam / mahābodhau pariṇamitam / vistīrṇaśikṣāpadaparigṛhītattvād viśadam / kāmasukhallikātmaklamathāntadvayavivarjitattvādanavadyapramodasthānīyam / yāvajjīvenāpi śikṣāpratyākhyānāt sātatyam / sarvalābhasatkāraparapravādikleśopakleśairanabhibhavanīyatvādahāryatvād dṛḍham / śīlālaṅkārasaṃyuktaṃ ca / śīlālaṅkāro veditavyastadyathā śrāvakabhūmau prāṇātipātādiviratyā / nivṛttiśīlam / kuśalasaṃgrahāt sattvārthakaraṇācca pravṛttiśīlam / pravṛttinivṛttiśīlānurakṣaṇādārakṣakaṃ śīlam / mahāpuruṣalakṣaṇavaipākyaṃ śīlam / adhicittavaipākyam / iṣṭa gativaipākyam / sattvārthakriyā vaipākyaṃ ceti /
body.translated_text: What therein is the <s>Bodhisattva</s>'s moral discipline of all aspects (<s>sarvākāra śīla</s>)? Combining six kinds and seven kinds together, it is to be known as thirteenfold. Dedicated to great awakening (<s>mahābodhi</s>). Clear, due to being encompassed by extensive training rules. A ground for blamelessness and delight, due to being free from the two extremes of sensual indulgence and self-mortification. Continuous, due to not renouncing the training even for the duration of one's life. Firm, due to being unconquerable and unshakeable by all gains, honors, others' criticism, afflictions, and secondary defilements. And conjoined with the ornament of moral discipline. The ornament of moral discipline is to be understood as follows: moral discipline of abstention—abstaining from killing and so forth, as in the <s>Śrāvakabhūmi</s>; moral discipline of engagement—through gathering wholesome [<s>dharmas</s>] and working for the welfare of beings; moral discipline of guarding—through protecting the moral disciplines of engagement and abstention; moral discipline ripening as the marks of a great being (<s>mahāpuruṣalakṣaṇa</s>); ripening as higher mind; ripening as a desired rebirth destiny; and ripening as the accomplishment of beings' welfare.

body.text: tatra katamadbodhisattvasya vighātārthikaśīlam / tadaṣṭavidhaṃ veditavyam / iha bodhisattvaḥ svayamevaivamanucintayati / yathāhamarthī [jīvitena] na me kaścijjīvatād vyaparopayet / adattamādadyāt kāmeṣu mithyācaret mṛṣāvācaṃ bhāṣeta paiśunyaṃ pāruṣyaṃ sabhinnapralāpaṃ kuryāt pāṇiloṣṭatāḍana saṃsparśaiścāniṣṭairvihiṃsāsaṃsparśaiḥ samudācarediti / tasya me evamarthinaḥ sa cet pare viparyayeṇa samudācareyuḥ tena me syādvidhātastanme syādamanāpam / paro 'pyarthino yathā 'smākaṃ pare na jīvitadvyaparopayeyurvistareṇa yāvanna vihiṃsāsasparśai samudācareyuriti /
body.translated_text: What therein is the <s>Bodhisattva</s>'s moral discipline aimed at avoiding harm (<s>vighātārthika śīla</s>)? It is to be known as eightfold. Here, the <s>Bodhisattva</s> himself reflects thus: 'Just as I desire [life] and no one should deprive me of life, take what is not given, engage in sexual misconduct, speak falsehood, engage in slander, harsh speech, or idle talk, or harm me with unwanted contacts of fists, clods, and so forth—and if others were to act contrary [to my wish], that would be destructive to me, and that would be unpleasant to me. Others too are desirous—that no one should deprive them of life, and so on in detail, nor harm them with injurious contacts.'

body.text: teṣāmapyevamarthināṃ sa cedahaṃ viparyayeṇa samudācareyaṃ tena te syurvighātinastatteṣāṃ syādamanāpam / iti yanmama pareṣāñcāmanāpaṃ so 'haṃ kiṃ tena parān samudācariṣyāmi / iti pratisaṃkhyāya bodhisattvo jīvitahetorapi parānaṣṭavidhenāmanāpena na samudācarati / idaṃ bodhisattvasyāṣṭākāraṃ vighātārthikaśīlamityucyate /
body.translated_text: 'If I were to act contrary toward those who are similarly desirous, that would be destructive to them, and that would be unpleasant to them. Thus, that which is unpleasant to me and to others—why would I act toward others in that way?' Having thus reflected, the <s>Bodhisattva</s>, even for the sake of [preserving his own] life, does not act toward others in the eightfold unpleasant manner. This is called the <s>Bodhisattva</s>'s eightfold moral discipline aimed at avoiding harm.

body.text: tatra katamadbodhisattvasyehāmutra sukhaṃ śīlam / tannavavidhaṃ draṣṭavyam / iha bodhisattvaḥ sattvānāṃ pratiśeddhavyāni sthānāni pratiṣedhayati / abhyanujñeyāni sthānānyabhyanujānāti / saṃgrahītavyān sattvān saṃgṛhṇāti / nigṛhītavyān sattvān nigṛhṇāti / tatra bodhisattva ya yatkāyavākkarmapariśuddhaṃ pravartate / idaṃ tāvaccaturvidhaṃ śīlam / punaranyaddānasahagataṃ śīlaṃ kṣāntisahagataṃ [vīryasahagataṃ] dhyānasahagataṃ prajñāsahagatañca pañcavidham / tadetadaikadhyamabhisaṃkṣipya navākāraṃ śīlaṃ bhavati / tasya ca bodhisattvasya pareṣāñca dṛṣṭadharmasaṃparāyasukhāya saṃvartate / tasmādihāmutra sukhamityucyate /
body.translated_text: What therein is the <s>Bodhisattva</s>'s moral discipline [producing] happiness in this world and the next (<s>ihāmutra sukha śīla</s>)? It is to be seen as ninefold. Here, the <s>Bodhisattva</s> restrains beings from what is to be restrained; he approves of what is to be approved; he gathers the beings who should be gathered; he disciplines the beings who should be disciplined. In these [activities], whatever pure conduct of body and speech the <s>Bodhisattva</s> exercises—this is the first fourfold moral discipline. Furthermore, there is moral discipline accompanied by giving, accompanied by patience, [accompanied by energy,] accompanied by meditation, and accompanied by wisdom—fivefold. Combining these together, the moral discipline becomes ninefold. It conduces to the happiness of the <s>Bodhisattva</s> himself and of others, both in this life and in future lives. Therefore it is called '[producing] happiness in this world and the next.'

body.text: tatra viśuddhaṃ śīlaṃ bodhisattvasya katamat / taddaśavidhaṃ veditavyam / ādita eva sugṛhīta bhavati śrāmaṇyasabodhikāmatayā na jīvikānimittam / nātilīnaṃ bhavati vyatikrame mandakaukṛtyāpagatatvāt / nātisṛtaṃ bhavatyasthānakaukṛtyāpagatatvāt / kausīdyāpagataṃ bhavati nidrāsukhapārśvasukhaśayanasukhāsvīkaraṇatayā rātriṃdivaṃ kuśalapakṣābhiyogācca / apramādaparigṛhītaṃ bhavati / pūrvavat pañcāṅgāpramādapratiniṣevaṇatayā / samyakpraṇihitaṃ bhavati lābhasatkāragardhavigamāt devatvāya praṇidhāya brahmacaryāvāsānābhyupagamācca / ācārasapattyā parigṛhītamīryāpathetikaraṇīyakuśalapakṣaprayogeṣu susampannapratirūpakāyavāk samudācāratayā / ājīvasampattyā parigṛhītaṃ kuhanādisarvamithyājīvakarakadoṣavivarjitatayā / antadvayavivarjita kāmasukhallikātmakaklamathānuyogavivarjitatvāt / nairyāṇika sarvatīrthikadṛṣṭivivarjitatayā / samādānāparibhraṣṭaṃ śīlaṃ bodhisattvānāmachidrīkaraṇāvipādanatayā / ityetaddaśākāra śīlaṃ bodhisattvānāṃ viśuddhamityucyate /
body.translated_text: What therein is the <s>Bodhisattva</s>'s pure moral discipline (<s>viśuddha śīla</s>)? It is to be known as tenfold. It is well-grasped from the very beginning, out of desire for the ascetic life and awakening, not for the sake of livelihood. It is not too withdrawn, due to being free from mild remorse in case of transgression. It is not too lax, due to being free from remorse in inappropriate situations. It is free from sloth, due to not indulging in the pleasure of sleep, the pleasure of lying on one's side, and the pleasure of reclining, and through continuous application to the wholesome both day and night. It is encompassed by heedfulness, through the practice of the five limbs of heedfulness as before. It is correctly directed, through the absence of pride in gain and honor and through not undertaking the celibate life aspiring for divine rebirth. It is encompassed by excellence of conduct, through well-accomplished and proper conduct of body and speech in deportment and in all duties and wholesome endeavors. It is encompassed by excellence of livelihood, through being free from all faults of wrong livelihood such as scheming and the like. It is free from the two extremes, due to being free from the pursuit of sensual indulgence and self-mortification. It is leading to liberation (<s>nairyāṇika</s>), through being free from all views of heretics. It is unbroken through undertaking, through the non-disruption and non-destruction of the moral discipline of <s>Bodhisattvas</s>. This tenfold moral discipline of <s>Bodhisattvas</s> is called 'pure.'

body.text: ityeṣa bodhisattvasya mahān śīlaskandho mahābodhiphalodayo yamāśritya
body.translated_text: This is the <s>Bodhisattva</s>'s great aggregate of moral discipline, yielding the fruit of great awakening, relying on which—

body.text: bodhisattvaḥ śīlapāramitāṃ paripūrayitvā anuttarāṃ samyaksaṃbodhimabhisambudhyate / yāvacca nābhisabudhyate tāvadayamasminnaprameye bodhisattvaśīlaskandhe śikṣamāṇaḥ pañcānuśaṃsān pratilabhate / buddhaiḥ samanvāhriyate / mahāprāmodyasthitaḥ kālaṃ karoti / kāyasya ca bhedāttatropapadyate yatrāsya samānādhikaśīlā bodhisattvāḥ sabhāgāḥ sahadhārmikāḥ kalyāṇamitrabhūtā bhavanti / aparimāṇena puṇyaskandhena śīlapāramitāparipūrakeṇa samanvāgato bhavati / dṛṣṭe dharme samparāye 'pi prakṛtiśīlatāṃ śīlatanmayatāṃ pratilabhate /
body.translated_text: the <s>Bodhisattva</s>, having fulfilled the <s>śīlapāramitā</s> (perfection of moral discipline), fully awakens to unsurpassed perfect awakening. And as long as he has not fully awakened, training in this immeasurable aggregate of <s>Bodhisattva</s> moral discipline, he obtains five benefits: he is attended to by the <s>Buddhas</s>; he dies in a state of great joy; after the dissolution of the body, he is reborn where there are <s>Bodhisattvas</s> of equal or superior moral discipline who are his companions, co-practitioners, and virtuous friends; he becomes endowed with an immeasurable aggregate of merit that fulfills the <s>śīlapāramitā</s>; and in this life and in future lives, he attains natural moral virtue and thorough permeation by moral discipline.

body.text: sarvañcaitacchīlaṃ yathānirdiṣṭaṃ svabhāvaśīlādikaṃ navākāraṃ trividhena śīlena saṃgṛhītaṃ veditavyam / saṃvaraśīlena kuśaladharmamaṃgrāhakeṇa sattvārthakriyāśīlena ca / tatpunastrividhaṃ śīlaṃ samāsato bodhisattvasya trīṇi kāryāṇi karoti / saṃvaraśīlaṃ cittasthitaye saṃvartate / kuśaladharmasaṃgrāhakamātmano buddhadharmaṃparipākāya saṃvartate / sattvārthakriyāśīlaṃ sattvaparipākāya saṃvartate / etāvacca bodhisattvasya sarvaṃ karaṇīyaṃ bhavati / yaduta dṛṣṭadharmasukhavihārāya cittasthitiḥ / aklāntakāyacittasya ca buddhadharmaparipākaḥ sattvaparipākaśca / etāvadbodhisattvaśīlam / etāvān bodhisattvaśīlānuśaṃsaḥ / etāvat bodhisattvaśīlakāryaṃ nāta uttari nāto bhūyaḥ / yatrātītā bodhisattvā mahābodhikāmāḥ śikṣitavantaḥ / anāgatā api śikṣiṣyante / vartamānā api daśasu dikṣvanantāparyantesu / lokadhātuṣu śikṣante
body.translated_text: All this moral discipline as described, the ninefold beginning with natural moral discipline and so forth, is to be known as encompassed by the threefold moral discipline: the moral discipline of restraint, that of gathering wholesome <s>dharmas</s>, and that of acting for the welfare of beings. Furthermore, that threefold moral discipline, in brief, accomplishes three tasks for the <s>Bodhisattva</s>: the moral discipline of restraint conduces to mental stability; the moral discipline of gathering wholesome <s>dharmas</s> conduces to the ripening of <s>Buddha</s>-qualities for oneself; the moral discipline of acting for the welfare of beings conduces to the ripening of beings. And this is the entirety of the <s>Bodhisattva</s>'s duty: namely, mental stability for pleasant abiding in this present life, and the ripening of <s>Buddha</s>-qualities and the ripening of beings with unfatigued body and mind. This is the full extent of <s>Bodhisattva</s> moral discipline; this is the full extent of its benefits; this is the full extent of its function—nothing beyond, nothing more. In this, <s>Bodhisattvas</s> of the past who desired great awakening have trained; those of the future will also train; and those of the present also train in the infinite and boundless world-realms in the ten directions.

body.text: iti bodhisattvabhūmāvādhāre yogasthāne daśamaṃ śīlapaṭalam /
body.translated_text: Thus [ends] the tenth chapter, the Moral Discipline Chapter (<s>Śīlapaṭala</s>), in the Foundation section of the Yoga Place in the <s>Bodhisattvabhūmi</s>.

body.text: uddānaṃ pūrvadveditavyaṃ tadyathā śīlapaṭale /
body.translated_text: The summary is to be understood as before, as in the Moral Discipline Chapter.

body.text: tatra katamā bodhisattvasya svabhāvakṣāntiḥ / yā pratisaṃkhyānabalasanniśrayeṇa vā prakṛtyā vā parāpakārasya marṣaṇā sarveṣāñca marṣaṇā sarvasya ca marṣaṇā nirāmiṣeṇa ca cittena kevalayā karuṇayā [marṣaṇā] / ayaṃ samāsato bodhisattvasya kṣāntisvabhāvo veditavyaḥ /
body.translated_text: What therein is the <s>Bodhisattva</s>'s natural patience (<s>svabhāvakṣānti</s>)? That which, relying on the power of reflection or by nature, is the forbearance of harm from others—the forbearance of all [harms], the forbearance of everything, with a selfless mind and with pure compassion alone. This, in brief, is to be known as the nature of the <s>Bodhisattva</s>'s patience.

body.text: tatra katamā bodhisattvasya sarvā kṣāntiḥ / yā dvividhā draṣṭavyā / gṛhipakṣāśritā pravrajitapakṣāśritā ca / sā punarubhayapakṣāśritāpi trividhā veditavyā / parāpakāramarpaṇā-kṣāntiḥ / duḥkhādhivāsanā-kṣāntiḥ / dharmanidhyānādhimokṣa kṣāntiñca /
body.translated_text: What therein is the <s>Bodhisattva</s>'s complete patience? It is to be seen as twofold: based on the householder's side and based on the renunciant's side. And based on both sides, it is further to be known as threefold: the patience of forbearing harm from others (<s>parāpakāramarṣaṇākṣānti</s>), the patience of enduring suffering (<s>duḥkhādhivāsanākṣānti</s>), and the patience of conviction in the contemplation of <s>dharmas</s> (<s>dharmanidhyānādhimokṣakṣānti</s>).

body.text: tatra kathaṃ bodhisattvaḥ parāpakāraṃ marṣayati kṣamate / iha bodhisattvastīvre nirantare citre dīrghakālikea 'pi parāpakāraje duḥkhe sammukhībhūte idaṃ pratisaṃśikṣate / svakarmāparādha eṣa me / yenāhaṃ svayaṃkṛtasyāśubhasya karmaṇo duḥkhamīdṛśaṃ phalaṃ pratyanubhavāmi / duḥkhena cāhamanarthī / iyañcākṣāntirāyatyāṃ puranapi me duḥkhahetusthānīyā / so 'hametadduḥkhahetubhūtaṃ dharmaṃ samādāya varteyam / yaddhā yanmamaivāniṣṭaṃ tenāhamātmanaivātmānaṃ sayojayeyam / ata ātmana eva me 'pakṛtaṃ syāt / na tathā pareṣām / svabhāvataśca duḥkhaprakṛtikā eveme sarvasaṃskārāḥ svaparasāntānikāḥ / tatpare tāvadajñāḥ ye asmākaṃ prakṛtiduḥkhitānāṃ bhūyo duḥkhamupasaṃharanti / asmākaṃ tu vijñānāṃ satāṃ na pratirūpaṃ syādyadvayamapi pareṣāṃ prakṛtiduḥkhitānāṃ bhūyo duḥkhamupasaṃharemaḥ / bhūyo 'pi cātmārthe tāvatprayuktānāṃ śrāvakāṇāmakṣāntirna yuktarūpā syāt svapareṣāṃ duḥkhajanikā / prāgevāsmākaṃ tu parārthaprayuktānām / idaṃ pratisaṃkhyāya sa
body.translated_text: How then does the <s>Bodhisattva</s> forbear and endure harm from others? Here, when intense, incessant, varied, and long-lasting suffering born from the harm of others confronts him, the <s>Bodhisattva</s> trains himself thus: 'This is the fault of my own <s>karma</s>, by which I experience this very suffering as the fruit of unwholesome <s>karma</s> done by myself. And I do not desire suffering. And this impatience would be a cause of suffering for me again in the future. If I were to take up this <s>dharma</s> that is the cause of suffering, I would be yoking myself to what is undesirable by my own doing. Thus the harm would be done to me by myself rather than by others. And by nature, all these conditioned formations—whether in one's own or others' continua—are of the nature of suffering. Those others are ignorant who heap further suffering upon us who are already naturally suffering. But for us who are wise, it would not be fitting to heap further suffering upon others who are likewise naturally suffering. Moreover, impatience would not be fitting even for <s>Śrāvakas</s> who are engaged in their own welfare, since it produces suffering for both oneself and others; how much less for us who are engaged in the welfare of others.' Having thus reflected—

body.text: bodhisattvaḥ pañcākārāṃ saṃjñāṃ bhāvayan mitrāmitrodāsīnebhyaḥ hīnatulyaviśiṣṭebhyaḥ sukhitaduḥkhitebhyo guṇadoṣayuktebhyaśca sattvebhyaḥ sarvāpakārāṃstitikṣate /
