body.translated_text: the <s>Bodhisattva</s>, cultivating the fivefold perception, endures all harms from beings—whether friends, enemies, or neutral; whether inferior, equal, or superior; whether happy or suffering; whether endowed with qualities or faults.

body.text: pañca saṃjñāḥ katamāḥ / pūrvajanmasuhṛtsaṃjñā / dharmamātrānusāriṇīsaṃjñā [anityasaṃjñā] duḥkhasaṃjñā / parigrahasaṃjñā ceti /
body.translated_text: What are the five perceptions? The perception of [the harmer as] a friend from a previous birth; the perception of [all as] merely following <s>dharmas</s>; [the perception of impermanence;] the perception of suffering; and the perception of [them as] one's charge.

body.text: kathañca bodhisattvo 'pakāriṣu sattveṣu suhṛtsaṃjñāṃ bhāvayati / iha bodhisattva idaṃ pratisaṃśikṣate / nāsau sattvaḥ sulabharūpo yo me na dīrghasyādhvano 'tyayāt pūrvamanyāsu jātiṣu mātā vābhūt pitā vā bhrātā vā bhaginī vā ācāryo vā upādhyāyo vā gururvā gurusthānīyo vā / tasyaivaṃ yoniśo manasikurvataḥ pratyarthikasaṃjñā apakāriṣu sattveṣu antardhīyate suhṛtsaṃjñā ca saṃtiṣṭhate / sa tāṃ suhṛtsaṃjñāṃ niśrityāpakārān marṣayati kṣamate /
body.translated_text: How does the <s>Bodhisattva</s> cultivate the perception of friendship toward beings who have done harm? Here, the <s>Bodhisattva</s> trains himself thus: 'It is not easy to find a being who, in the course of the long past, in other births, has not been my mother, father, brother, sister, teacher, preceptor, guru, or one worthy of a guru's place.' When he attends wisely in this way, the perception of enmity toward beings who have done harm disappears and the perception of friendship arises. Relying on that perception of friendship, he forbears and endures the harms.

body.text: kathañca bodhisattvaḥ apakāriṣu sattveṣu dharmamātrānusāriṇīṃ saṃjñāṃ bhāvayati / iha bodhisattva idaṃ pratiṣaṃśikṣate / pratyayādhīnamidaṃ saṃskāramātraṃ dharmamātram / nāstyatra kaścidātmā vā sattvo vā jīvo vā janturvāya ākrośedroṣayettāḍayed bhaṇḍayet paribhāṣeta vā yo vā punarākruśyeta vā roṣyeta vā tāḍayeta vā bhaṇḍayeta vā paribhāṣyeta vā / tasyaivaṃ yoniśo manasikurvataḥ sattvasaṃjñā cāntardhīyate / dharmamātrasaṃjñā ca saṃtiṣṭhate / sa tāṃ dharmamātrasaṃjñāniścitya pratiṣṭhāpya parataḥ sarvāpakārān marṣayati kṣamate /

kathañca bodhisattvo 'pakāriṣu sattveṣu anityasaṃjñāṃ bhāvayati / iha bodhisattva idaṃ pratisaṃśikṣate / ye kecit sattvā jātā bhūtāḥ sarve te anityā maraṇadharmāṇaḥ / eṣa ca paramaḥ pratyatakāro yaduta jīvitādvayaparopaṇam / evañca prakṛttyā maraṇadharmakeṣvanityeṣu sattveṣu na pratirūpaṃ syādvijñapuruṣasya kaluṣamapi tāvaccittamutpādayituṃ prāgeva pāṇinā vā prahartuṃ loṣṭena vā daṇḍena vā prāgeva sarveṇa sarvaṃ jīvitādvyaparopayitum / tasyaivaṃ yoniśo manasi kurvataḥ nityasārasajñā ca prahīyate / anityāsārasaṃjñā ca saṃtiṣṭhate / sa tāmapi anityāsārasaṃjñāṃ niśritya sarvāpakārān marṣayati kṣamate /
kathañca bodhisattvaḥ apakāriṣu sattveṣu duḥkhasaṃjñāṃ bhāvayati / iha bodhisattvo ye tāvat sattvā mahatyāmapi sampadi vartante tānapi tisṛbhiḥ

duḥkhatābhiranuṣaktān paśyati- saṃskāraduḥkhatayā vipariṇāmaduḥkhatayā duḥkhaduḥkhatayā ca prāgeva vipattisthitān / sa evaṃ paśyannidaṃ pratisaṃśikṣate / evaṃ sadā duḥkhānugatānāṃ sattvānāṃ duḥkhāpakarṣaṇāyāsmābhirvyāyacchitavyaṃ na duḥkhopasaṃhārāya / tasyaivaṃ yoniśo manasi kurvataḥ sukhasaṃjñā prahīyate duḥkhasaṃjñā cotpadyate / sa tāṃ duḥkhasaṃjñāṃ niśritya pareṣāṃ sarvāpakārān marṣayati kṣamate /

kathañca bodhisattvo 'pakāriṣu sattveṣu parigrahasaṃjñāṃ bhāvayati / iha bodhisattva idaṃ pratisaṃśikṣate / mayā khalu sarvasattvā bodhāya cittamutpādayatā kaḍatrabhāvena parigṛhītāḥ / sarvasattvānāṃ mayārthaḥ karaṇīya iti / tanna me pratirūpaṃ syādyadahamevaṃ sarvasattvānupādāyaiṣāmarthaṃ kariṣyāmītyanarthameva kuryāmapakāramamarṣayan / tasyaiva yāniśo manasi kurvataḥ apakāriṣu sattveṣu parasaṃjñā prahīyate / parigrahasaṃjñā ca saṃtiṣṭhate / sa tāṃ parigrahasajñāṃ niśritya pareṣāṃ sarvāpakārān marṣayati kṣamate /
kṣāntiḥ katamā / yanna kupyati na pratyapakāraṃ karoti / nāpyanuśayaṃ vahati / iyamucyate kṣāntiḥ /

tatra bodhisattvasya duḥkhādhivāsanākṣāntiḥ katamā / iha bodhisattva idaṃ pratisaṃśikṣate / mayā khalu pūrva kāmacaryāsu vartamānena kāmānparyeṣatā pratisaṃkhyāya duḥkhahetutayā duḥkhātmakānāṃ kāmānāmarthe prabhūtāni tīvrāṇi duḥkhāni abhyupagatāni adhivāsitānyanubhūtāni kṛṣivaṇijyā rājapauruṣyaprayuktena / evaṃ tadvayarthaṃ duḥkhasyaivārthe mayā mahad duḥkhamabhyupagataṃ pratisaṃkhyāyājñānadoṣeṇa / sāṃprataṃ tu mama sukhāhārake kuśale prayuktasya [pratisaṃkhyāya] tataḥ koṭīśatasahasraguṇasya duḥkhasyādhivāsanābhyupagamaḥ pratirūpaḥ syāt / prāgeva tato nyūnasya / evaṃ yoniśo manasi kurvan bodhāya prayukto bodhisattvaḥ sarvavastukaṃ duḥkhamadhivāsayati /

sarvavastukaṃ duḥkhaṃ katamat / tatsamāsataḥ aṣṭākāraṃ veditavyam / sanniśrayādhiṣṭhānaṃ lokadharmādhiṣṭhānam īryāpathādhiṣṭhānaṃ dharmaparigrahādhiṣṭhāna bhikṣākavṛttādhiṣṭhānam abhiyogaklamādhiṣṭhānaṃ sattvārthakriyādhiṣṭhānam itikaraṇīyādhiṣṭhānañceti /

catvāraḥ sanniśrayāḥ / yānāśritya svākhyāte dharmavinaye pravrajyā-upasampadbhikṣubhāvaḥ / tadyathā cīvaraṃ piṇḍapātaḥ śayanāsanaṃ glānapratyayabhaiṣajyapariṣkārāśca / tairbodhisattvo lūhaiḥ stokairasatkṛtya dhandhañca labdhairnotkaṇṭhyate na paritrasyati nāpi tato nidānaṃ vīryaṃ sraṃsayati / evaṃ sanniśrityādhiṣṭhānaṃ duḥkhamadhivāsayati /

nava lokadharmāḥ / alābhaḥ ayaśo nindā duḥkhaṃnāśadharmakasya nāśaḥ kṣayadharmakasya kṣayaḥ jarādharmakasya jarā vyādhidharmakasya vyādhiḥ maraṇadharmakasya maraṇam / eṣāṃ lokadharmāṇāṃ samastavyastānām āpatanāt sammukhībhāvāt yadduḥkhamutpadyate tallokadharmādhiṣṭhānamityucyate / tenāpi spṛṣṭo bodhisattvo na tannidānaṃ vīryaṃ sraṃsayati pratisaṃkhyāyodvahate adhivāsayati /

catvāra īryāpathāḥ / caṃkramaḥ sthānaṃ niṣadyā śayyā ca / tatra bodhisattvaḥ caṃkramaniṣadyābhyāṃ divārātrau vā āvaraṇīyebhyo dharmebhyaścittaṃ pariśodhayaṃstana nidānaṃ pariśramajaṃ duḥkhamadhivāsayati / na tvakāle pārśvamanuprayacchati mañce vā pīṭhe vā tṛṇasaṃstare vā parṇasaṃstare vā /

saptavidho dharmaparigrahaḥ / ratnatrayapūjopasthānaṃ gurupūjopasthānaṃ dharmāṇāmudgrahaṇamudgṛhītānāṃ pareṣāṃ vistareṇa deśanā vistareṇa svareṇa svādhyāyakriyā ekākino rahogatasya samyak cintanā tulanā upaparīkṣaṇā yogamanasikārasaṃgṛhītā śamathavipaśyanā bhāvanā ca / asmin saptākāre dharmaparigrahe bodhisattvasya vyāyacchamānasya yad duḥkhamutpadyate tadapyasāvadhivāsayati / na ca tannidānaṃ vīryaṃ straṃsayati /

bhikṣākavṛttamapi saptākāraṃ veditavyam / vairūpyābhyupagamaḥ śirastuṇḍamuṇḍanādibhirapahṛtagṛhivyañjanatayā / vaivarṇyābhyupagamo vikṛtavivarṇavastradhāraṇatayā / ākalpāntarakriyā sarvalaukikapracāreṣu tantritavihāratayā / parapratibaddhājīvikā kṛṣyādikarmāntavivarjitasya paralabdhena yātrākalpanatayā / yāvajjīvaṃ parataścīvarādiparyeṣaṇā labdhānāṃ sannidhikārāparibhogatayā / yāvajjīvaṃ

mānuṣyakebhyaḥ kāmebhya āvaraṇakriyā abrahmacaryamaithunadharmaprativivaraṇatayā / yāvajjīvaṃ mānuṣyakebhyo ratikrīḍābhya āvaraṇakiyā naṭanartanakahāsakalāsakādisaṃdarśanaprativiramaṇatayā / mitrasuhṛdvayasyaiśca saha hasitakrīḍitaramitaparicārita-prativiramaṇatayā / ityevaṃ rūpaṃ kṛcchrasaṃbādhaṃ bhikṣākavṛttamāgamya yadduḥkhamutpadyate tadapi bodhisattvo 'dhivāsayati / na ca tannidānaṃ vīyu sraṃsayati /
kuśalapakṣābhiyuktasyāpi ca bodhisattvasya [ye] pariśramanidānā utpadyante kāyikāḥ klamāḥ caitasikāḥ apyupāyāsā na bodhisattvastannidānaṃ vīryaṃ saṃstrayati /
sattvārthakarma tvekādaśaprakāraṃ pūrvavadveditavyamu / tannidānamapi bodhisattvo duḥkhasamutpannamadhivāsayati / na ca tannidānaṃ vīryaṃ straṃsayati /

itikaraṇīyaṃ pravrajitasya cīvarapātrakarmādi / gṛhiṇaḥ punaḥ samyakkṛṣivaṇijyā-rājapauruṣyādi / tannidānamapi bodhisattvo duḥkhamadhivāsayati / no tu tannidānaṃ vīryaṃ sraṃsayati / yatpunarbodhisattvaḥ spṛṣṭaḥ sannanyatamena duḥkhena prayujyata evānuttarāyai samyaksaṃbodhaye / na [na] prayujyate / prayuktaśca na vivartaṃte / avimanaskaścāsaṃkliṣṭacittaḥ prayujyate / iyamasyocyate duḥkhādhivāsanākṣāntiḥ /

tatra katamā bodhisattvasya dharmanidhyānādhimuktikṣāntiḥ / iha bodhisattvasya samyagdharmapravicayasuvicāritayā buddhyā aṣṭavidhe adhimuktyadhiṣṭhāne adhimuktiḥ susanniviṣṭā bhavati ratnaguṇeṣu tattvārthe buddhabodhisattvānāṃ mahāprabhāve hetau phale prāptavye 'rthe ātmanastatprāptyupāye jñeyagocare ca / sā punaradhimuktirdvābhyāṃ kāraṇābhyāṃ susanniviṣṭā bhavati / dīrghakālābhyāsataśca suviśuddhajñānasamudāgamataśca / itīyaṃ bodhisattvānāṃ sarvakṣāntiḥ pakṣadvayamāśritā / yāmāśritya duṣkarakṣāntyādivistaravibhāgo bodhisattvānāṃ veditavyaḥ /

tatra katamā bodhisattvasya duṣkarakṣāntiḥ / sā trividhā draṣṭavyā / iha bodhisattvo durbalānāṃ sattvānāmantikādapakāraṃ kṣamate / iyaṃ prathamā duṣkarakṣāntiḥ / prabhurbhūtvā svayaṃ kṣamate / iyaṃ dvitīyā duṣkarakṣāntiḥ / jātigotranīcatarāṇāñca sattvānāmantikādutkṛṣṭamadhimātramapakāraṃ kṣamate / iyaṃ tṛtīyā duṣkarakṣāntiḥ /
tatra katamā bodhisattvasya sarvatomukhī kṣāntiḥ / sā caturvidhā draṣṭavyā / iha bodhisattvo mitrādapyapakāraṃ kṣamate 'mitrādapyudāsīnādapi / tebhyaśca tribhyo hīnatulyādhikebhyaḥ kṣamate /

tatra katamā bodhisattvasya satpuruṣakṣāntiḥ / sā pañcavidhā draṣṭavyā / iha bodhisattvaḥ ādita eva kṣāntāvanuśaṃsadarśī bhavati / kṣamaḥ pudgalaḥ āyattyāmavairabahulo bhavati / abhedabahulo bhavati / sukhasaumanasyabahulo bhavati / avipratisārī kālaṃ karoti / kāyasya ca bhedātsugatau svargaloke deveṣūpapadyate / iti sa evamanuśaṃsadarśī / svayañca kṣamo bhavati / parañca kṣāntau samādāpayati / kṣamāyāśca varṇaṃ bhāṣate / kṣamiṇañca pudgalaṃ dṛṣṭvā sumanasko bhavatyānandījātaḥ /

tatra katamā bodhisattvasya sarvākārakṣāntiḥ / sā ṣaḍvidhā saptavidhā caikadhyamabhisaṃkṣipya trayodaśavidhā veditavyā / iha bodhisattvo 'niṣṭavipākamakṣāntiṃ viditvā bhayādapi kṣamate / sattveṣu ca dayācittaḥ kāruṇyacitta [snigdhacittaḥ] snehādapi kṣamate / anuttarāyāṃ samyaksaṃbodhau tīvracchandaḥ kṣāntipāramitāṃ paripūrayitukāmaḥ kāraṇahetorapi kṣamate / kṣāntibalāśca pravrajitā uktā bhagavatā / tadanenāpi paryāyeṇa na yuktarūpā samāttaśīlasya pravrajitasyākṣāntiriti dharmasamādānato 'pi kṣamate / gotrasampadi pūrvake ca kṣāntyabhyāse vartamāno 'vasthitaḥ prakṛtyāpi kṣamate / [niḥ]sattvāṃśca sarvadharmān viditvā nirabhilāpyadharmamātradarśī dharmanidhyānato 'pi kṣamate / sarvañcāpakāraṃ kṣamate / sarvataśca kṣamate / sarvatra ca deśe kṣamate / rahasi vā mahājanasamakṣaṃ vā sarvakālañca kṣamate / pūrvāhne 'pi madhyāhne 'pi sāyāhne 'pi rātrau ca divā vā 'tī tamapyanāgatamapi pratyutpannamapi glāno 'pi svastho 'pi patito 'pyutthito 'pi / kāyenāpi kṣamate 'praharaṇatayā / vācāpi kṣamate 'manāpavacanāniścāraṇatayā / manasāpi kṣamate 'kopyatayā kaluṣāśayādhāraṇatayā ca /
body.translated_text: There, what is the <s>Bodhisattva</s>'s all-aspect patience (<s>sarvākārakṣānti</s>)? It should be understood as thirteen-fold, combining six and seven types into one. Here, the <s>Bodhisattva</s>, knowing the undesirable ripening of impatience, practices patience even out of fear. And being compassionate-minded and sympathetic-minded toward beings, he practices patience even out of affection. Being intensely desirous of unsurpassed perfect awakening and wishing to fulfill the <s>Kṣāntipāramitā</s> (perfection of patience), he practices patience even for the sake of a cause. And the <s>Bhagavān</s> has declared that renunciants are powerful in patience. By this consideration too, it is not fitting for a renunciant who has undertaken the precepts to be impatient—thus he practices patience even from the undertaking of the <s>Dharma</s>. And abiding in the excellence of lineage (<s>gotra</s>) and in the prior practice of patience, being established [therein], he practices patience even by nature. And knowing all <s>dharmas</s> as devoid of a being-aspect, seeing them as merely inexpressible dharma-nature, he practices patience even from reflection on the <s>Dharma</s>. And he endures all harm. And he endures from all [sources]. And he endures in all places—whether in private or before a great assembly. And he endures at all times—in the forenoon, at midday, in the afternoon, at night and by day; regarding the past, the future, and the present; whether ill or well; whether fallen or risen. And he endures with the body—by not striking back. And he endures with speech—by not uttering disagreeable words. And he endures with the mind—by not becoming angry and by not harboring a turbid disposition.

body.text: tatra katamā bodhisattvasya vighātārthikakṣāntiḥ / sā 'ṣṭavidhā draṣṭavyā / duḥkhitānāṃ yācakānāmantikādyāñcoparodhanakṣāntiḥ / raudreṣvadhimātrapāpakarmasu sattveṣu dharmamahākaruṇāṃ niśrityāghātākaraṇa-kṣāntiḥ / duḥśīleṣu pravrajiteṣu
body.translated_text: There, what is the <s>Bodhisattva</s>'s patience for those in distress (<s>vighātārthikakṣānti</s>)? It should be understood as eightfold: the patience of enduring obstruction from supplicants who are suffering and in need;

body.text: dharmamahākaruṇāṃ niśrityāghātākaraṇa-kṣāntiḥ / pañcākārā ca vyavasāyasahiṣṇutākṣāntiḥ / duḥkhitānāṃ sattvānāṃ duḥkhāpanayanāya vyāyacchataḥ dharmān paryeṣataḥ dharmasyānudharme pratipadyabhānasya tāneva dharmān pareṣāṃ vistareṇa saṃprakāśayataḥ sattvakṛtyeṣu [sattvakaraṇīyeṣu] ca samyaksahāyībhāvaṃ gacchato yā vyavasāyasahiṣṇutā / itīyamaṣṭākārā vighātārthikakṣāntirityucyate / yena ca sattvā vidhātinaḥ syuḥ tasya ca kṣāntyā parivarjanāt / yena cārthinastasyopasaṃhārāt /
body.translated_text: the patience of not retaliating against beings who engage in cruel and exceedingly evil deeds, relying on the great compassion of the <s>Dharma</s>; the patience of not retaliating against immoral renunciants, relying on the great compassion of the <s>Dharma</s>; and the fivefold patience of perseverance—the perseverance when exerting oneself to remove the suffering of beings who are suffering, when seeking the <s>Dharma</s>, when practicing in conformity with the <s>Dharma</s> and teaching it, when expounding those very <s>dharmas</s> in detail to others, and when becoming a proper companion in the tasks [and duties] of beings. This eightfold [patience] is called the patience for those in distress—because of the avoidance through patience of that by which beings would be harmed, and because of the provision of that which they seek.

body.text: tatra katamā bodhisattvasya ihāmutrasukhā kṣāntiḥ / sā navavidhā dṛṣṭavyā / iha bodhisattvaḥ apramatto viharan kuśaleṣu dharmeṣu kṣamo bhavati / śītasyoṣṇasya jighatsāpipāsayoḥ daṃśasaṃsparśānāṃ [maśakasaṃsparśānāṃ vātātapayoḥ sarīsṛpasaṃsparśānāṃ] kṣamo bhavati / pariśramajanyakāyacittaklamopāyāsasya kṣamo bhavati / saṃsārapatitajarāvyādhimaraṇādikānāṃ duḥkhānāṃ sattvānukampāmeva puraskṛtā ityevaṃ kṣamo bodhisattva ātmanā ca dṛṣṭe ca dharme sukhasaṃsparśaṃ viharatyavyavakīrṇaḥ pāpakairakuśalairdharmaiḥ / sāṃparāyikañca sukhahetuṃ samādāya vartate / [pareṣāmapi ca sukhahetuṃ samādāya vartate /] pareṣāmapi ca dṛṣṭe dharme saṃparāya sukhāya pratipanno bhavati / tasmādiyamihāmutrasukhā kṣāntirityucyate /
body.translated_text: There, what is the <s>Bodhisattva</s>'s patience that brings happiness here and hereafter (<s>ihāmutrasukhā kṣānti</s>)? It should be understood as ninefold. Here, the <s>Bodhisattva</s>, dwelling diligently in wholesome <s>dharmas</s>, is patient. He is patient with cold and heat, with hunger and thirst, with the contact of gadflies [and mosquitoes, wind, sun, and creeping creatures]. He is patient with the weariness of body and mind born of fatigue. He is patient with the sufferings of old age, sickness, death, and so forth that befall beings fallen into <s>saṃsāra</s>, placing compassion for beings foremost. Thus the patient <s>Bodhisattva</s> himself, in this very life, dwells in the pleasant contact of happiness, undefiled by evil, unwholesome <s>dharmas</s>. And he takes up the cause of happiness in the future. [And he takes up the cause of happiness for others as well.] And he practices for the happiness of others both in this life and in the future. Therefore this is called the patience that brings happiness here and hereafter.

body.text: tatra katamā bodhisattvasya viśuddhā kṣāntiḥ / sā daśavidhā draṣṭavyā / iha bodhisattvaḥ pareṣāmantikādapakāraṃ vighātaṃ vyatikramaṃ labhamāno nāpi pratyapakāraṃ karoti / nāpi manasā kupyati / nāpi pratyarthikāśayaṃ vahati / upakārāya cābhimukho bhavati yathā pūrvaṃ tathā paścānnopakārakriyayā 'pakāramupekṣate apakāriṣu ca svayameva saṃjñaptimanuprayacchati na ca khedayitvā pareṣāmantikāt saṃjñaptiṃ pratigṛhaṇāti khedito bhavatviti / etameva pratyayaṃ kṛtvā akṣāntimārabhya tīvreṇa [hrīvyapatrāpyena] samanvāgato bhavati / kṣāntimārabhya tīvreṇa śāstari premagauraveṇa samanvāgato bhavati / sattvāviheṭhanatāmārabhya tīvreṇa sattveṣu karuṇāśayena sanvāgato bhavati / sarveṇa vā sarvamakṣāntidharmasahāyaṃ prahāya kāmavītarāgo bhavati / sarveṇa ebhirdaśabhirākārairbodhisattvasya kṣāntiviśuddhā veditavyā nirmalā /
body.translated_text: There, what is the <s>Bodhisattva</s>'s pure patience (<s>viśuddhā kṣānti</s>)? It should be understood as tenfold. Here, the <s>Bodhisattva</s>, receiving harm, obstruction, and transgression from others, does not retaliate. Nor does he become angry in mind. Nor does he harbor a hostile disposition. And he is disposed toward benefiting [them]. As before, so afterward—he does not neglect beneficial action on account of the harm. And toward those who have done harm, he himself offers reconciliation and does not, having vexed [them], accept reconciliation from others [under the condition that] they should be distressed. Making this very [harm] the occasion, regarding impatience, he becomes endowed with intense moral shame and moral dread (<s>hrīvyapatrāpya</s>). Regarding patience, he becomes endowed with intense love and reverence for the Teacher. Regarding non-harm to beings, he becomes endowed with intense compassion toward beings. Or, abandoning entirely all dharma-companions of impatience, he becomes free from desire [for retaliation]. Through all these ten aspects, the <s>Bodhisattva</s>'s patience should be understood as pure and stainless.

body.text: ityetāṃ svabhāva-[kṣāntyādikaṃ viśuddha-]kṣāntiparyavasānāṃ kṣāntiṃ vipulāmapramāṇāṃ mahābodhiphalo[dayāṃ] niśritya bodhisattvo 'nuttarāṃ samyaksaṃbodhimabhisaṃbudhyate /
body.translated_text: Relying on this patience—from intrinsic-nature [patience] through to pure patience—vast and immeasurable, bearing the fruit of great awakening, the <s>Bodhisattva</s> fully awakens to unsurpassed perfect awakening.

body.text: iti bodhisattvabhūmāvādhāre yogasthāne ekādaśamaṃ kṣāntipaṭalaṃ samāptam /
body.translated_text: Thus, in the <s>Bodhisattvabhūmi</s>, in the Foundation section of the Yoga Place, the eleventh chapter on Patience (<s>Kṣāntipaṭala</s>) is completed.

body.text: uddānaṃ pūrvavadveditavyama /
body.translated_text: The summary verse is to be understood as before.

body.text: tatra katamadbodhisattvasya svabhāvavīryam / yo bodhisattvasya cittābhyutsāho 'prameyakuśaladharmasaṃgrahāya sattvārthakriyāyai / uttaptaśca niśchidraścāviparyastaśca tatsamutthitaśca kāyavāṅmanaḥ parispandaḥ / ayaṃ bodhisattvasya vīryasvabhāvo veditavyaḥ /
body.translated_text: There, what is the <s>Bodhisattva</s>'s intrinsic-nature vigor (<s>svabhāvavīrya</s>)? It is the <s>Bodhisattva</s>'s mental enthusiasm (<s>cittābhyutsāha</s>) for the collection of immeasurable wholesome <s>dharmas</s> and for acting for the welfare of beings. And it is the exertion of body, speech, and mind that is ardent, uninterrupted, undistorted, and arisen from that [enthusiasm]. This should be understood as the intrinsic nature of the <s>Bodhisattva</s>'s vigor.

body.text: tatra katamadbodhisattvasya sarvavīryaṃm / tatsamāsato dvividhaṃ veditavyam / gṛhipakṣāśritaṃ pravrajitapakṣāśritañca / tatpunarubhayapakṣāśritamapi trividhaṃ veditavyam / sannāhavīryaṃ kuśaladharmasaṃgrāhakaṃ sattvārthakriyāyai ca /
body.translated_text: There, what is the <s>Bodhisattva</s>'s all [encompassing] vigor (<s>sarvavīrya</s>)? In brief, it should be understood as twofold: pertaining to the household side and pertaining to the renunciant side. And that [vigor], pertaining to both sides, should further be understood as threefold: armor-like vigor (<s>sannāhavīrya</s>), vigor for gathering wholesome <s>dharmas</s> (<s>kuśaladharmasaṃgrāhaka</s>), and [vigor] for acting for the welfare of beings (<s>sattvārthakriyā</s>).

body.text: tatredaṃ bodhisattvasya sannāhavīryam / iha bodhisattvaḥ pūrvameva vīryārambhaprayogādevaṃ cetaso 'bhyutsāhapūrvakaṃ sannāhaṃ sannahyate / sa cedahamekasattvasyāpi duḥkhavimokṣahetormahākalpasahasratulyai rātrindivasairnaṃrakavāsenaiva nānyagativāsena yāvatā kālena bodhisattvā anuttarāṃ samyaksaṃbodhimabhisaṃbudhyante tenaiva koṭīniyutaśatasahasraguṇitena kālenāhamanuttarāṃ samyaksaṃbodhimāsādayeyam / tathāpi cotsaheyam / na nānuttarāyāḥ samyaksaṃbodherarthena prayujyeyam / na ca prayukta-vīryaṃ saṃsrayeyam / prāgeva nyūnatareṇa kālena tanutareṇa ca duḥkhena / idamevaṃrūpaṃ bodhisattvasya sannāhavīryam / yo bodhisattvaḥ evarūpe bodhisattvānāṃ sannāhavīrye 'dhimuktimātrakaṃ prasādamātrakamapyutpādayet so 'pi tāvadbodhisattvo dhīro 'pramāṇasya bodhāya vīryārambhasya dhātuṃ paripoṣayet / prāgeva yo bodhisattvaḥ īdṛśenaiva sannāhavīryeṇa samanvāgataḥ syāt na ca punastasya bodhisattvasya bodherarthe sattvānāmarthāya kiñcidasti duṣkaraṃ karaṇīyaṃ karma yatrāsya bodhisattvasya saṃkoco vā syāt cetaso duṣkaraṃ vā kartum /
body.translated_text: There, this is the <s>Bodhisattva</s>'s armor-like vigor (<s>sannāhavīrya</s>): Here, the <s>Bodhisattva</s>, even before the commencement and application of vigor, girds on the armor with such mental enthusiasm as this: 'If, for the sake of liberating even a single being from suffering, with days and nights equaling great thousands of <s>kalpas</s>, dwelling in the <s>naraka</s> realms alone—not in any other realm of rebirth—for as long a time as it takes <s>Bodhisattvas</s> to fully awaken to unsurpassed perfect awakening, multiplied by hundreds of thousands of <s>koṭīs</s> and <s>niyutas</s>, I would attain unsurpassed perfect awakening—even so, I would be willing. I would not fail to strive for the sake of unsurpassed perfect awakening. Nor, having strived vigorously, would I retreat—much less with a shorter time and lesser suffering!' This is the nature of the <s>Bodhisattva</s>'s armor-like vigor. A <s>Bodhisattva</s> who generates even mere aspiration or mere faith in such armor-like vigor of <s>Bodhisattvas</s>—even that one is courageous and would nurture the element (<s>dhātu</s>) for the commencement of immeasurable vigor toward awakening—much less a <s>Bodhisattva</s> who is endowed with precisely such armor-like vigor. And for that <s>Bodhisattva</s>, there is nothing difficult to do, no difficult task to perform for the sake of awakening and for the welfare of beings, where his mind would contract or [consider it] difficult to accomplish.

body.text: tatra katamadbodhisattvānāṃ kuśaladharmasaṃgrāhakaṃ vīryam / yadvīryaṃ dānapāramitāprāyogikaṃ dānapāramitāsamudāgamāya yadvīryaṃ śīlakṣāntivīryadhyānaprajñāpāramitāprāyogikaṃ
body.translated_text: There, what is the <s>Bodhisattvas</s>' vigor for gathering wholesome <s>dharmas</s> (<s>kuśaladharmasaṃgrāhakaṃ vīryam</s>)? It is the vigor applied toward the <s>Dānapāramitā</s> (perfection of generosity) for the accomplishment of the <s>Dānapāramitā</s>; the vigor applied toward the <s>Śīla</s>-, <s>Kṣānti</s>-, <s>Vīrya</s>-, <s>Dhyāna</s>-, and <s>Prajñāpāramitās</s>

body.text: yāvatprajñāpāramitāsamudāgamāya / tatpunaḥ samāsataḥ saptākāraṃ veditavyam / acalaṃ sarvakalpavikalpakleśopakleśaparapravādiduḥkhasaṃsparśairavicālyatvāt / gāḍhaṃ satkṛtya prayogitvāt / aprameyaṃ sarvavidyāsthānasamudāgamapratyupasthānatvāt / upāyaprayuktaṃ prāptavyasyārthasyāviparītamārgā nugatatvāt samatāprativedhācca / samyagvīryamarthopasaṃhitasya prāptavyasyārthasya prāptaye praṇihitatvāt / pratataṃ sātatyaprayogitvāt / vigatamānaṃ tena vīryārambheṇānunnamanāt / ityebhiḥ saptabhirākāraiḥ kuśaladharmasaṃgrahāya vīryārambhaprayogo bodhisattvānāṃ kṣipraṃ pāramitāparipūraye 'nuttarasamyaksaṃbodhyadhigamāya saṃvartate / yataśca sarveṣāṃ bodhikarakāṇāṃ kuśalānāṃ dharmaṇāmevaṃ samudāgamāya vīryameva pradhānaṃ śreṣṭhaṃ kāraṇaṃ na tathānyat / tasmādvīryamanuttarāyai samyaksaṃbodhaye iti nirdiśanti tathāgatāḥ /
body.translated_text: for the accomplishment of up to the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>. That, in brief, should be understood as sevenfold: unwavering—because it is not shaken by all conceptualizations, afflictions, secondary afflictions, opposing disputants, and painful contacts of suffering; firm—because of applying [effort] with earnestness; immeasurable—because of readiness for the accomplishment of all fields of knowledge; accompanied by skillful means—because of following the unerring path toward the goal to be attained and because of the penetration of equality; right vigor—because of being directed toward the attainment of the meaningful goal to be attained; continuous—because of constant application; and free from conceit—because of not being elated by that vigorous exertion. Through these seven aspects, the exertion and application of vigor for the gathering of wholesome <s>dharmas</s> by <s>Bodhisattvas</s> conduces to the swift fulfillment of the <s>pāramitās</s> and the attainment of unsurpassed perfect awakening. And since, for the accomplishment of all wholesome <s>dharmas</s> that lead to awakening, vigor alone is the foremost, supreme cause—and not anything else to the same degree—therefore the <s>Tathāgatas</s> declare: 'Vigor [leads] to unsurpassed perfect awakening.'

body.text: sattvārthakriyāvīryaṃ punarbodhisattvānāṃ veditavyamekādaśaprakāram / tadyathā śīlapaṭale / yattatra śīlayuktaṃ tadiha vīryaṃ vaktavyam / ayaṃ viśeṣaḥ /
body.translated_text: The <s>Bodhisattvas</s>' vigor for acting for the welfare of beings (<s>sattvārthakriyāvīrya</s>) should be understood as elevenfold—as in the chapter on moral conduct (<s>Śīlapaṭala</s>). What was there connected with moral conduct should here be stated as vigor. This is the distinction.

body.text: tatra katamadbodhisattvasya duṣkaravīryam / tat trividhaṃ draṣṭavyam / yadbodhisattvo nairantaryeṇa cīvarasaṃjñāṃ piṇḍapātasaṃjñāṃ śayanāsanasaṃjñāmapi ātmasaṃjñāmakurvan kuśaleṣu dharmeṣu bhāvanāsātatyena prayukto bhavati / idaṃ bodhisattvasya prathamaṃ duṣkaravīryam / punarbodhisattvastena tathārūpeṇa vīryārambheṇa ā-nikāyasabhāganikṣepāt sarvakālaṃ prayukto bhavati / idaṃ dvitīyaṃ bodhisattvasya duṣkaravīryam / punarbodhisattvaḥ samatāprativedhaguṇayuktena nātilīnena nātyārabdhenāviparītenārthopasaṃhitena vīryeṇa samanvāgato bhavati / idaṃ bodhisattvasya tṛtīyaṃ duṣkaravīryaṃ veditavyam / asya khalu bodhisattvānāṃ duṣkaravīryasya balaṃ sattveṣu karuṇā prajñā ca saṃgrahaheturveditavyaḥ /
body.translated_text: There, what is the <s>Bodhisattva</s>'s difficult vigor (<s>duṣkaravīrya</s>)? It should be understood as threefold. When the <s>Bodhisattva</s>, without interruption, without even giving rise to the notion of robes, alms-food, or lodging, or even of self, is engaged in continuous cultivation of wholesome <s>dharmas</s> with persistent effort—this is the <s>Bodhisattva</s>'s first difficult vigor. Furthermore, when the <s>Bodhisattva</s>, with that very kind of vigorous exertion, is engaged at all times until the casting off of this class of existence (<s>nikāyasabhāga</s>)—this is the <s>Bodhisattva</s>'s second difficult vigor. Furthermore, when the <s>Bodhisattva</s> is endowed with vigor that possesses the quality of penetrating equality—neither too lax nor too strained, undistorted, and connected with purpose—this is the <s>Bodhisattva</s>'s third difficult vigor. The power of this difficult vigor of <s>Bodhisattvas</s> should be understood as compassion toward beings and wisdom, which serve as its cause of collection.

body.text: tatra katamadbodhisattvasya sarvatomukhaṃ vīryam / taccaturvidha draṣṭavyam / kliṣṭadharmavivarjakaṃ śukladharmāvarjakaṃ karmapariśodhakaṃ jñānavivardhakañca / tatra kliṣṭadharmavivarjakaṃ bodhisattvasya vīryamanutpannānāñca saṃyojanabandhanānuśayopakleśaparyavasthānānāmanutpādāyotpannānāñca prahāṇāya / tatra śukladharmāvarjakaṃ bodhisattvasya
body.translated_text: There, what is the <s>Bodhisattva</s>'s all-embracing vigor (<s>sarvatomukhaṃ vīryam</s>)? It should be understood as fourfold: that which removes afflicted <s>dharmas</s>, that which attracts wholesome <s>dharmas</s>, that which purifies action, and that which increases knowledge. There, the <s>Bodhisattva</s>'s vigor that removes afflicted <s>dharmas</s> is for the non-arising of unarisen fetters, bonds, latent tendencies, secondary afflictions, and envelopments, and for the abandonment of those that have arisen. There, the <s>Bodhisattva</s>'s vigor that attracts wholesome <s>dharmas</s>

body.text: vīryaṃ yadanutpannānāñca kuśalānāṃ dharmāṇāmutpattaye vīryam / utpannānāñca sthitaye asaṃmoṣāyai vṛddhivipulatāyai yadvīryam / tatra karmapariśodhakaṃ bodhisattvasya vīryaṃ yat trayāṇāṃ karmaṇāṃ viśuddhaye saṃgrahāya kuśalasya kāyakarmaṇo vākkarmaṇo manaskarmaṇaśca / tatra jñānavivardhake bodhisattvasya vīryam / yacchru tacintābhāvanāmayyāḥ prajñāyāḥ samudāgamāya parivṛddhaye saṃvartate /
body.translated_text: is the vigor for the arising of unarisen wholesome <s>dharmas</s>, and the vigor for the maintenance, non-loss, growth, and abundance of those that have arisen. There, the <s>Bodhisattva</s>'s vigor that purifies action is for the purification and collection of the three kinds of action: wholesome bodily action, verbal action, and mental action. There, the <s>Bodhisattva</s>'s vigor that increases knowledge is that which conduces to the accomplishment and growth of wisdom born of hearing, thinking, and meditation (<s>śrutacintābhāvanāmayī prajñā</s>).

body.text: tatra katamadbodhisattvasya satpuruṣavīryam / tatpañcavidhaṃ draṣṭavyam / anirākṛtaṃ sarveṇa sarvaṃ chandaprayogānirākaraṇatayā / anyūnaṃ yathopāttatulyādhikavīryānubṛṃhaṇatayā / alīnamuttaptadīrghakālika-nirantaravīryārambhāyāsaṃkucitāviṣaṇṇacittatayā / aviparītamarthopasaṃhitopāyaparigṛhītatayā / uttaptaprayogañca bodhisattvānāṃ vīryamanuttarāyāṃ samyak saṃbodhāvabhikaraṇatayā /
body.translated_text: There, what is the <s>Bodhisattva</s>'s vigor of a good person (<s>satpuruṣavīrya</s>)? It should be understood as fivefold: unrejected—because of not rejecting any application of zeal whatsoever; undiminished—because of augmenting vigor equal to or greater than what has been undertaken; unslackened—because of ardent, long-term, uninterrupted vigorous exertion with an uncontracted and undejected mind; undistorted—because of being embraced by skillful means connected with purpose; and of ardent application—because of the <s>Bodhisattvas</s>' vigor being directed toward unsurpassed perfect awakening.

body.text: tatra katamadbodhisattvānāṃ sarvākāraṃ vīryam / tatṣaḍākāraṃ saptākārañca aikadhyamabhisaṃkṣipya trayodaśākāraṃ veditavyam / sātatyavīryaṃ nityakālaprayogitayā / satkṛtyavīryaṃ nipuṇaprayogitayā / naiṣyandikaṃ vīryaṃ pūrvavīryahetubalādhānatayā / prāyogikaṃ vīryaṃ pratisaṃkhyāya kuśalapakṣaprayogitayā / akopyavīryaṃ sarvaduḥkhasaṃsparśairavikopyatayā 'nanyathābhāvopagamanatayā asaṃtuṣṭivīryamalpāvaramātraviśeṣādhigamāsantuṣṭatayā / idaṃ tāvat ṣaḍvidhaṃ sarvākāraṃ vīryaṃ yena samanvāgato bodhisattvaḥ ārabdhavīryaḥ sthāmavān vīryavānutsāhī dṛḍhaparākramaḥ anikṣiptadhuraḥ kuśaleṣu dharmeṣvityucyate / saptavidhaṃ punaḥ chandasahagataṃ bodhisattvasya vīryaṃ punaḥ punaranuttarāyāṃ samyaksaṃbodhau tīvracchanda praṇidhānānuvṛṃhaṇatayā sāmyayuktaṃ bodhisattvasya vīryaṃ yadanyatamena kleśopakleśenāsaṃkliṣṭacetaso 'paryavasthitasya yena vīryeṇa bodhisattvaḥ kuśaleṣu dharmeṣu tulyocittavihārī saṃbhavati / vaiśeṣikaṃ vīryaṃ bodhisattvasyānyatamenopakleśenopakliṣṭacetasaḥ [paryavasitacetasaḥ] tasyopakleśasya prahāṇāya yadādīptaśiro nirvāṇopamaṃ vīryam / eṣakaṃ vīryaṃ bodhisattvasya sarvavidyāsthānaparyeṣaṇatayā / śikṣāvīryaṃ bodhisattvasya teṣveva paryeṣiteṣu dharmeṣu yathāyogyaṃ yathārhaṃ dharmānudharmapratipattisaṃpādanatayā / parārthakriyāvīryaṃ bodhisattvasya pūrvavadekādaśavidhaṃ veditavyam / ātmanaḥ samyakprayogārakṣāyai
body.translated_text: There, what is the <s>Bodhisattvas</s>' all-aspect vigor (<s>sarvākāraṃ vīryam</s>)? It should be understood as thirteen-fold, combining six and seven types into one. Continuous vigor—because of constant application at all times. Earnest vigor—because of applying [effort] with care. Naturally resultant vigor—because of the foundation of power from prior causes of vigor. Applied vigor—because of applying oneself to the wholesome side through analytical reflection. Unshakable vigor—because of not being shaken by all painful contacts of suffering and because of not changing one's course. Vigor of dissatisfaction—because of not being content with merely a small, inferior, or slight degree of attainment. This is the sixfold all-aspect vigor, endowed with which the <s>Bodhisattva</s> is called 'one who has aroused vigor, is strong, vigorous, enthusiastic, of firm heroic exertion, and who has not laid down the burden in wholesome <s>dharmas</s>.' And furthermore, the sevenfold: the <s>Bodhisattva</s>'s vigor accompanied by zeal—because of again and again augmenting intense zeal and aspiration for unsurpassed perfect awakening. The <s>Bodhisattva</s>'s vigor endowed with equanimity—the vigor by which the <s>Bodhisattva</s>, whose mind is unafflicted and unenveloped by any affliction or secondary affliction, becomes one who dwells with a balanced mind in wholesome <s>dharmas</s>. The <s>Bodhisattva</s>'s special vigor—when the mind has been afflicted by some secondary affliction [and enveloped], the vigor for the abandonment of that secondary affliction, like [extinguishing] a fire burning on one's head, is the special vigor. The <s>Bodhisattva</s>'s seeking vigor—because of seeking all fields of knowledge. The <s>Bodhisattva</s>'s training vigor—because of accomplishing practice in conformity with the <s>Dharma</s> as appropriate and fitting with respect to those very <s>dharmas</s> that have been sought. The <s>Bodhisattva</s>'s vigor for acting for the welfare of others should be understood as elevenfold, as before. The seventh is the <s>Bodhisattva</s>'s vigor

body.text: skhalitasya ca yathādharmapratikaraṇatāyai vīryaṃ saptamaṃ bodhisattvasya / itīdaṃ trayodaśākāraṃ bodhisattvasya vīrya sarvākāramityucyate /
body.translated_text: for guarding one's own correct practice and for properly remedying stumblings according to the <s>Dharma</s>. Thus this thirteen-fold vigor of the <s>Bodhisattva</s> is called all-aspect vigor.

body.text: vighātārthikavīryaṃ cehāmutrasukhañca bodhisattvānāṃ vīryaṃ kṣāntivad draṣṭavyam / tatrāyaṃ viśeṣaḥ / yā tatra kṣāntiḥ seha vīryamabhyutsāho vaktavyaḥ /
body.translated_text: The vigor for those in distress (<s>vighātārthikavīrya</s>) and the vigor that brings happiness here and hereafter (<s>ihāmutrasukhavīrya</s>) of <s>Bodhisattvas</s> should be understood as with patience. Here, the distinction is: what was there patience should here be stated as vigor, enthusiasm.

body.text: tatra katamadbodhisattvasya viśuddhaṃ vīryam / tatsamāsato daśavidhaṃ veditavyam / anurūpamabhyastamaślathaṃ sugṛhītaṃ kālābhyāsa-prayuktaṃ nimittaprativedhayuktamalīnamavidhuraṃ samaṃ mahābodhipariṇamitañceti /
body.translated_text: There, what is the <s>Bodhisattva</s>'s pure vigor (<s>viśuddhaṃ vīryam</s>)? In brief, it should be understood as tenfold: appropriate, practiced, unrelaxed, well-grasped, timely in application, endowed with the penetration of signs, unslackened, unbroken, balanced, and dedicated to great awakening.

body.text: iha bodhisattvo yena yenopakleśenātyarthaṃ bādhyate / tasya tasyopakleśasya prahāṇāyānurūpaṃ pratipakṣaṃ bhajate / kāmarāgasya pratipakṣeṇāśubhāṃ bhāvayati / vyāpādapratipakṣeṇa maitrīm / mohapratipakṣeṇedaṃpratyayatā-pratītyasamutpādaṃ bhāvayati / vitarkapratipakṣeṇānāpānasmṛtim / mānapratipakṣeṇa dhātuprabhedaṃ bhāvayati / idamevaṃbhāgīyaṃ bodhisattvasya anurūpaṃ [vīrya]mityucyate /
body.translated_text: Here, the <s>Bodhisattva</s>, by whichever secondary affliction he is exceedingly afflicted, cultivates the appropriate antidote for the abandonment of that very secondary affliction. As antidote to sensual desire, he cultivates the contemplation of the unattractive (<s>aśubhā</s>). As antidote to ill-will, he cultivates loving-kindness (<s>maitrī</s>). As antidote to delusion, he cultivates the contemplation of dependent origination (<s>idaṃpratyayatā-pratītyasamutpāda</s>). As antidote to discursive thought, he cultivates mindfulness of breathing (<s>ānāpānasmṛti</s>). As antidote to pride, he cultivates the analysis of elements (<s>dhātuprabhedha</s>). This is called the <s>Bodhisattva</s>'s appropriate vigor.

body.text: iha bodhisattvo na ādikarmika-tatprathamakarmikavīryeṇa samanvāgato bhavati / yaduta cittasthitaye ' 'vavādānuśāsanyām / nānyatrābhyastaprayogo bhavati paricitaprayogaḥ / itīdaṃ bodhisattvasyābhyastaṃ vīryamityucyate /
body.translated_text: Here, the <s>Bodhisattva</s> does not possess merely the vigor of a beginner, of one first starting the practice—that is, for the stabilization of mind and for instruction and admonition. Rather, he is one whose practice is well-practiced and well-familiarized. This is called the <s>Bodhisattva</s>'s practiced vigor.

body.text: na cāpi bodhisattvaḥ abhyastaprayogo bhavati avavādānuśāsanyāṃ cittasthitimārabhya / api tvādikarmika eva sa bodhisattvastasmin prayoge 'ślathaprayogo bhavati sātatyasatkṛtyaprayogitayā / itīdaṃ bodhisattvasyāślathaṃ vīryamityucyate /
body.translated_text: And the <s>Bodhisattva</s>, whose practice is well-familiarized in instruction and admonition, beginning with the stabilization of mind—even such a <s>Bodhisattva</s>, though a beginner in that practice, applies unrelaxed effort through constant and earnest application. This is called the <s>Bodhisattva</s>'s unrelaxed vigor.

body.text: punarbodhisattvo guruṇāmantikāta svayameva vā bāhuśrutyabalādhānatayā 'viparītagrāhitayā cittasthitaye vīryamārabhate / itīdaṃ bodhisattvasya sugṛhītaṃ vīryamityucyate /
body.translated_text: Furthermore, the <s>Bodhisattva</s>, from teachers or by himself through the power of great learning, commences vigor for the stabilization of mind with correct, undistorted apprehension. This is called the <s>Bodhisattva</s>'s well-grasped vigor.

body.text: punarbodhisattvaḥ evamaviparītagrāhī śamathakāle śamathaṃ bhāvayati / pragrahakāle cittaṃ pratigṛhaṇāti / upekṣākāle upekṣāṃ bhāvayati / idamasya kālaprayuktaṃ vīryamityucyate /
body.translated_text: Furthermore, the <s>Bodhisattva</s>, having thus apprehended correctly, cultivates calm (<s>śamatha</s>) at the time for calm, applies effort (<s>pragraha</s>) at the time for effort, and cultivates equanimity (<s>upekṣā</s>) at the time for equanimity. This is called his timely vigor.

body.text: punarbodhisattvaḥ śamathapragrahopekṣānimittānāṃ samādhisthitivyutthānanimittānāṃ copalakṣaṇāsaṃpramoṣa-prativedhāya sātatyakārī bhavati satkṛtyakārī / itīdaṃ bodhisattvasya nimittaprativedhaṃ vīryamityucyate /
body.translated_text: Furthermore, the <s>Bodhisattva</s> acts constantly and earnestly for the penetration and unforgetting observation of the signs of calm, effort, and equanimity, and of the signs of the stability and emergence from <s>samādhi</s>. This is called the <s>Bodhisattva</s>'s vigor of sign-penetration.

body.text: punarbodhisattvaḥ paramodārān paramagambhīrānacintyāprameyān bodhisattvānāṃ vīryārambhanirdeśān śrutvā nātmānaṃ paribhavati na salīnacitto bhavati / nāpi cālpamātrakeṇāvaramātrakeṇa viśeṣādhigamena santuṣṭo bhavati / nottari na vyāyacchate / itīdaṃ bodhisattvasyālīnaṃ vīryamityucyate /
body.translated_text: Furthermore, the <s>Bodhisattva</s>, upon hearing the supremely magnificent, supremely profound, inconceivable, and immeasurable descriptions of the vigorous exertion of <s>Bodhisattvas</s>, does not belittle himself, does not become dispirited in mind. Nor is he content with merely a small or inferior degree of attainment. He does not fail to exert himself further. This is called the <s>Bodhisattva</s>'s unslackened vigor.

body.text:
punarbodhisattvaḥ kālena kālamindriyairguptadvāratāṃ bhojane mātrajñatāṃ pūrvarātrāpararātraṃ jāgarikānuyuktatāṃ saprajānan vihāritāmityevaṃbhāgīyān samādhisaṃbhārān samādāya vartate / teṣu codyukto bhavati / aviparītañcārthopasaṃhitaṃ sarvatra yatnamārabhate / itīdaṃ bodhisattvasyāvidhuraṃ vīryamityucyate /
punarbodhisattvo nātilīnaṃ nātyārabdhaṃ vīryamārabhate / sama yogavāhi sarveṣu cārambhakaraṇīyeṣu samaṃ satkṛtyakārī bhavati / iyaṃ bodhisattvasya samaṃ vīryamityucyate /
body.translated_text: Furthermore, the <s>Bodhisattva</s>, from time to time, takes up and maintains the provisions for <s>samādhi</s> of this kind: guarding the doors of the sense-faculties, moderation in eating, devotion to wakefulness in the first and last watches of the night, and dwelling with clear comprehension. And in these he is diligent. And he undertakes effort everywhere that is undistorted and connected with purpose. This is called the <s>Bodhisattva</s>'s unbroken vigor. Furthermore, the <s>Bodhisattva</s> commences vigor that is neither too lax nor too strained—balanced, conducive to progress, and applying earnest effort equally in all tasks requiring exertion. This is called the <s>Bodhisattva</s>'s balanced vigor.

body.text: punarbodhisattvaḥ sarvavīryārambhānabhisaṃskṛtānanuttarāyāṃ samyaksaṃbodhau pariṇamayatīdaṃ bodhisattvasya samyak pariṇamitaṃ vīryamityucyate /
body.translated_text: Furthermore, the <s>Bodhisattva</s> dedicates all his unconditioned vigorous exertions to unsurpassed perfect awakening. This is called the <s>Bodhisattva</s>'s properly dedicated vigor.

body.text: ityetatsvabhāvavīryādikaṃ viśuddhavīryāvasānañca bodhisattvānāṃ vīrya mahābodhiphalaṃ yadāśritya bodhisattvā vīryapāramitāṃ paripūrya anuttarāṃ samyak saṃbodhimabhisaṃbuddhā abhisaṃbhotsyante 'bhisaṃbudhyante ca /
body.translated_text: Thus, this vigor of <s>Bodhisattvas</s>—from intrinsic-nature vigor through to pure vigor—bearing the fruit of great awakening, relying on which <s>Bodhisattvas</s>, having fulfilled the <s>Vīryapāramitā</s> (perfection of vigor), have fully awakened, will fully awaken, and are fully awakening to unsurpassed perfect awakening.

body.text: iti bodhisattvabhūmāvādhāre yogasthāne dvādaśamaṃ vīryapaṭalaṃ samāptam /
body.translated_text: Thus, in the <s>Bodhisattvabhūmi</s>, in the Foundation section of the Yoga Place, the twelfth chapter on Vigor (<s>Vīryapaṭala</s>) is completed.

body.text: uddānaṃ pūrvaṃvadveditavyam /
body.translated_text: The summary verse is to be understood as before.

body.text: tatra katamo bodhisattvānāṃ dhyānasvabhāvaḥ / bodhisattvapiṭakaśravaṇacintāpūrvakaṃ yallaukikaṃ lokottaraṃ bodhisattvānāṃ kuśalaṃ cittaikāgryañcittasthitiḥ śamathapakṣyā vā vipaśyanāpakṣyā vā yuganaddhavāhimārgaṃ tadubhayāpakṣyā vā / ayaṃ bodhisattvānāṃ dhyānasvabhāvo veditavyaḥ /
body.translated_text: There, what is the intrinsic nature of the <s>Bodhisattvas</s>' meditation (<s>dhyānasvabhāva</s>)? Preceded by hearing and reflecting on the <s>Bodhisattva</s>-piṭaka, it is the mundane and supramundane wholesome one-pointedness of mind, the mental stability of <s>Bodhisattvas</s>—whether on the side of calm (<s>śamatha</s>), on the side of insight (<s>vipaśyanā</s>), or on the side of the path of the yoking of both (<s>yuganaddhavāhimārga</s>). This should be understood as the intrinsic nature of the <s>Bodhisattvas</s>' meditation.

body.text: tatra katamadbodhisattvānāṃ sarvaṃdhyānam / tad dvividhaṃ draṣṭavyam / laukikaṃ lokottarañca / tatpunaryathāyogaṃ trividhaṃ veditavyam / dṛṣṭadharmasukhavihārāya dhyānaṃ bodhisattva-samādhiguṇanirhārāya dhyāna sattvārthakriyāyai dhyānam /
body.translated_text: There, what is the <s>Bodhisattvas</s>' all [encompassing] meditation (<s>sarvadhyāna</s>)? It should be understood as twofold: mundane and supramundane. And that, as appropriate, should further be understood as threefold: meditation for dwelling in the happiness of the present life (<s>dṛṣṭadharmasukhavihāra</s>), meditation for the accomplishment of the <s>Bodhisattva</s>'s <s>samādhi</s>-qualities, and meditation for acting for the welfare of beings.

body.text: tatra yadbodhisattvānāṃ sarvavikalpāpagataṃ kāyikacaittasikaprasrabdhijanakaṃ paramapraśāntaṃ manyanāpagatamanāsvāditaṃ sarvanimittāpagataṃ dhyānam / idameṣāṃ dṛṣṭadharmasukhavihārāya veditavyam /
body.translated_text: There, the meditation of <s>Bodhisattvas</s> that is free from all conceptualization, that generates physical and mental tranquility (<s>prasrabdhi</s>), that is supremely peaceful, free from conceit, untainted, and free from all signs—this should be understood as [their meditation] for dwelling in the happiness of the present life.

body.text: tatra yadbodhisattvānāṃ dhyānaṃ vicitrācintyāpramāṇadaśabalagotra-saṃgṛhītasamādhinirhārāya saṃvartate / yeṣāṃ samādhīnāṃ sarvaśrāvakapratyekabuddhā api nāmāpi na prajānanti kutaḥ punaḥ samāpatsyante / yacca bodhisattvavimokṣābhibhvāyatanakṛtsnāyatanānāṃ pratisaṃvid-araṇā-praṇidhijñānādīnāṃ [guṇānāṃ] śrāvakasādhāraṇānāmabhinirhārāya saṃvartate / idaṃ bodhisattvasya dhyānaṃ samādhiguṇābhinirhārāya veditavyam / sattvārthakarmaṇi dhyānaṃ bodhisattvasyaikādaśākāraṃ pūrvavadveditavyam / yaddhyānaṃ niśritya bodhisattvaḥ sattvānāṃ kṛtyeṣvarthopasaṃhiteṣu sahāyībhāvaṃ gacchati / duḥkhamanapanayati / duḥkhitānāṃ nyāyamupadiśati / kṛtajñaḥ kṛtavedī upakāriṣu pratyupakāraṃ karoti / bhayebhyo rakṣati / vyasanasthānāṃ śokaṃ prativinodayati / upakaraṇavikalānāmupakaraṇopasaṃhāraṃ karoti / samyak pariṣadaṃ parikarṣati / cittamanuvartate / bhūtairguṇairharṣayati / samyak ca nigṛhṇāti /
body.translated_text: There, the meditation of <s>Bodhisattvas</s> that conduces to the accomplishment of various, inconceivable, immeasurable <s>samādhis</s> embraced by the lineage of the Ten Powers (<s>daśabala</s>)—<s>samādhis</s> whose very names are not known even by all <s>Śrāvakas</s> and <s>Pratyekabuddhas</s>, let alone that they would attain them—and that conduces to the accomplishment of the <s>Bodhisattva</s>'s liberations (<s>vimokṣa</s>), bases of mastery (<s>abhibhvāyatana</s>), totality-spheres (<s>kṛtsnāyatana</s>), analytical knowledges (<s>pratisaṃvid</s>), non-contention (<s>araṇā</s>), aspiration-knowledge (<s>praṇidhijñāna</s>), and other qualities shared in common with <s>Śrāvakas</s>—this should be understood as the <s>Bodhisattva</s>'s meditation for the accomplishment of <s>samādhi</s>-qualities. The <s>Bodhisattva</s>'s meditation for acting for the welfare of beings should be understood as elevenfold, as before—the meditation relying on which the <s>Bodhisattva</s> becomes a companion in the purposeful tasks of beings; removes [their] suffering; rightly teaches the path to those who suffer; is grateful, appreciative, and reciprocates to those who have been helpful; protects from fears; consoles the grief of those in distress; provides supplies to those who lack them; properly leads his community; follows the minds [of beings]; gladdens [them] by [praising] their genuine qualities; and rightly disciplines [them].

body.text: ṛddhyā cotrāsayatyāvarjayati ceti / tadaitatsarvamekadhyamabhisaṃkṣipya bodhisattvānāṃ sarvadhyānamityucyate / nāta uttari nāto bhūyaḥ /
body.translated_text: And through supernatural power, he terrifies and attracts [them]. All of this, combined into one, is called the <s>Bodhisattvas</s>' all [encompassing] meditation. There is nothing beyond this, nothing more.

body.text: tatra katamadbodhisattvānāṃ duṣkaradhyānam / tat trividhaṃ draṣṭavyam / yadbadhisattvā udārairvicitraiḥ suparicitairdhyānavihārairabhinirhṛtairvihṛtya svecchayā tatparamaṃ dhyānasukhaṃ vyāvartya pratisaṃkhyāya sattvānukampā prabhūtāṃ sattvārthakriyāṃ sattvārthaparipākaṃ samanupaśyantaḥ kāmadhātāvupapadyante / idaṃ bodhisattvānāṃ prathama duṣkaradhyānaṃ veditavyam / punaryadbodhisattvo dhyānaṃ niśrityāprameyāsaṃkhyeyācintyānsarvaśrāvakapratyekabuddhaviṣayasamatikrāntān bodhisattvasamādhīnabhinirharati / idaṃ bodhisattvasya dvitīyaṃ duṣkaradhyānaṃ veditavyam / punaryadbodhisattvo dhyānaṃ niśrityānuttarāṃ samyaksaṃbodhimabhisaṃbudhyate / itīdaṃ bodhisattvasya tṛtīya duṣkaradhyānaṃ veditavyam /
body.translated_text: There, what is the <s>Bodhisattvas</s>' difficult meditation (<s>duṣkaradhyāna</s>)? It should be understood as threefold. When <s>Bodhisattvas</s>, having dwelt in magnificent, various, well-familiarized, accomplished meditation-states, voluntarily turn away from that supreme bliss of meditation, and contemplating the abundant welfare-activity for beings and the maturation of beings out of compassion for them, are reborn in the desire realm (<s>kāmadhātu</s>)—this should be understood as the <s>Bodhisattvas</s>' first difficult meditation. Furthermore, when the <s>Bodhisattva</s>, relying on meditation, accomplishes immeasurable, incalculable, inconceivable <s>Bodhisattva</s>-<s>samādhis</s> that transcend the domain of all <s>Śrāvakas</s> and <s>Pratyekabuddhas</s>—this should be understood as the <s>Bodhisattva</s>'s second difficult meditation. Furthermore, when the <s>Bodhisattva</s>, relying on meditation, fully awakens to unsurpassed perfect awakening—this should be understood as the <s>Bodhisattva</s>'s third difficult meditation.

body.text: tatra katamadbodhisattvasya sarvatomukhaṃ dhyānam / taccaturvidhaṃ draṣṭavyam / savitarkaṃ-savicāraṃ [vivekajaṃ samādhijaṃ] prītisahagataṃ sāta-sukhasahagatamupekṣāsahagata ca /
body.translated_text: There, what is the <s>Bodhisattva</s>'s all-embracing meditation (<s>sarvatomukhaṃ dhyānam</s>)? It should be understood as fourfold: with initial and sustained application (<s>savitarka-savicāra</s>), [born of seclusion, born of concentration,] accompanied by joy (<s>prīti</s>), accompanied by pleasure-happiness (<s>sātasukha</s>), and accompanied by equanimity (<s>upekṣā</s>).

body.text: tatra katamadbodhisattvasya satpuruṣadhyānam / tatpañcavidhaṃ draṣṭavyam / anākhāditaṃ maitrīsahagataṃ karuṇāsahagataṃ muditāsahagatamupekṣāsahagatañca /
body.translated_text: There, what is the <s>Bodhisattva</s>'s meditation of a good person (<s>satpuruṣadhyāna</s>)? It should be understood as fivefold: untainted, accompanied by loving-kindness (<s>maitrī</s>), accompanied by compassion (<s>karuṇā</s>), accompanied by sympathetic joy (<s>muditā</s>), and accompanied by equanimity (<s>upekṣā</s>).

body.text: tatra katamadbodhisattvasya sarvākāra-dhyānam / tatṣaḍvidhaṃ [saptavidhaṃ] caikadhyamabhisaṃkṣipya trayodaśavidhaṃ veditavyam / kuśalaṃ dhyānamavyākṛtaṃ ca nirmitanirmāṇāya dhyānaṃ śamathapakṣyaṃ vipaśyanāpakṣyaṃ svaparārthasamyagupanidhyānāya dhyānaṃ abhijñāprabhāvaguṇarnirhārāya dhyānaṃ nāmālambanaṃmarthālambanaṃ śamathanimittālambanaṃ pragrahanimittālambanamupekṣānimittālambanaṃ [dṛṣṭadharmasukha]vihārāya parārthakriyāyai ca dhyānam / itīdaṃ trayodaśākāraṃ bodhisattvānāṃ dhyānaṃ sarvākāramityucyate /
body.translated_text: There, what is the <s>Bodhisattva</s>'s all-aspected meditation (<s>sarvākāra dhyāna</s>)? Combining the sixfold [and] sevenfold together, it should be understood as thirteenfold: wholesome meditation and indeterminate [meditation]; meditation for creating emanations; meditation belonging to the side of calm (<s>śamatha</s>) and belonging to the side of insight (<s>vipaśyanā</s>); meditation for proper reflection on the benefit of self and others; meditation for the accomplishment of the qualities of supernatural knowledge and power (<s>abhijñā</s>); [meditation] having name as object, having meaning as object, having the sign of calm as object, having the sign of exertion as object, and having the sign of equanimity as object; and meditation for pleasant abiding [in this life] and for acting for the benefit of others. This thirteenfold meditation of <s>Bodhisattvas</s> is called 'all-aspected.'

body.text: tatra katamadbodhisattvasya vighātārthikadhyānam / tadaṣṭavidhaṃ draṣṭavyam / viṣāśani viṣamajvarabhūtagrahādyupadravasaṃśamakānāṃ siddhaye mantrāṇāmadhiṣṭhāyakaṃ dhyānam / dhātubhaiṣamyajātānāñca vyādhīnāṃ vividhānāṃ vyupaśamāya dhyānam / durbhikṣeṣu mahārauraveṣu pratyupasthiteṣu vṛṣṭinirhārakaṃ dhyānam / vividhebhyo bhayebhyo
body.translated_text: There, what is the <s>Bodhisattva</s>'s meditation for overcoming adversity (<s>vighātārthika dhyāna</s>)? It should be seen as eightfold: meditation that empowers <s>mantras</s> for the attainment of success in quelling afflictions such as poison, lightning, unhealthy fevers, spirit-possession, and the like; meditation for the alleviation of various diseases arising from elemental imbalance; meditation that produces rain when great and terrible famines arise; [meditation] for proper protection from various fears

body.text: manuṣyāmanuṣyakṛtebhyo jalasthalagatebhyaḥ samyak paritrāṇā dhyayānam / tathā bhojanapānahīnānāmaṭavīkāntāragatānāṃ bhojanapānopasaṃhārāya dhyānam / bhogavihīnānāṃ vineyānāṃ bhogopasahārāya dhyānam / daśasu dikṣu pramattānāṃ sattvānāṃ samyaksaṃbodhanāya dhyānam / utpannotpannānāñca sattvakṛtyānāṃ samyak kriyāyai dhyānam /
body.translated_text: caused by humans and non-humans, on water and on land; likewise, meditation for providing food and drink to those lacking food and drink who have gone into forests and wildernesses; meditation for providing wealth to those disciples deprived of possessions; meditation for properly awakening heedless beings in the ten directions; and meditation for properly carrying out the tasks of beings as they arise.

body.text: tatra katamadbodhisattvasyehāmutrasukhaṃ dhyānam / tannavavidhaṃ draṣṭavyam / ṛddhiprātihāryeṇa sattvānāṃ vinayāya dhyānam / ādeśanāprātihāryeṇānuśāstiprātihāryeṇa sattvānāṃ vinayāya dhyānam / pāpaśāriṇāmapāyabhūmividarśanaṃ dhyānam / naṣṭapratibhānānāṃ sattvānāṃ pratibhānopasaṃhārāya dhyānam / muṣitasmṛtīnāṃ sattvānāṃ smṛtyupasaṃhārāya dhyānam / aviparītaśāsrakāvyamātṛkānibandhavyavasthānāya saddharmacirasthitikatāyai dhyānam / laukikānāṃ śilpakarmasthānānāmarthopasaṃhitānāṃ sattvānugrāhakāṇāṃ lipigaṇananyasanasaṃkhyāmudrādīnāṃ mañcapīṭhacchatropānahādīnāñca vicitrāṇāṃ vividhānāṃ bhāṇḍopaskarāṇāmanupravartakaṃ dhyānam / apāyabhūmyupapannānāñca sattvānāṃ tat kālāpāyikaduḥkhapratiprasrambhaṇatāyai raśmipramocakaṃ dhyānam /
body.translated_text: There, what is the <s>Bodhisattva</s>'s meditation that is pleasant here and hereafter (<s>ihāmutrasukhā dhyāna</s>)? It should be seen as ninefold: meditation for training beings through the miracle of supernatural power (<s>ṛddhiprātihārya</s>); meditation for training beings through the miracle of mind-reading (<s>ādeśanāprātihārya</s>) and the miracle of instruction (<s>anuśāstiprātihārya</s>); meditation for showing the realms of misfortune to those inclined toward evil; meditation for restoring eloquence to beings who have lost their eloquence; meditation for restoring mindfulness to beings who have lost their mindfulness; meditation for the establishment of non-perverted <s>sūtras</s>, verses, <s>mātṛkā</s> texts, and treatises, for the long endurance of the true <s>Dharma</s>; meditation that sets in motion various and manifold worldly arts and crafts that are meaningful and beneficial to beings—such as writing, calculation, classification, enumeration, sealing, and the like, as well as various vessels and utensils such as beds, seats, parasols, sandals, and the like; and meditation that releases light rays for the alleviation of the sufferings of beings born in the realms of misfortune at that time.

body.text: tatra katamadbodhisattvasya viśuddhaṃ dhyānam / taddaśavidhaṃ draṣṭavyam / laukikyā śuddhyā [vi]śuddhamanāsvāditaṃ dhyānam / akliṣṭaṃ lokottarayā śuddhyā [vi]śuddhaṃ dhyānam / prayogaśuddhyā [vi]śuddhaṃ maulaviśuddhyā [vi]śuddhaṃ maulaviśeṣottaraviśuddhyā viśuddhaṃ dhyānam / praveśasthitivyutthānavaśitāviśuddhyā viśuddhaṃ dhyānam / dhyānavyāvartane punaḥ samādapanavaśitā-viśuddhyā viśuddhaṃ dhyānam abhijñāvikurvaṇavaśitā-viśuddhyā viśuddhaṃ dhyānam / sarvadṛṣṭigatāpagamaviśuddhyā viśuddhaṃ dhyānam / kleśajñeyāvaraṇaprahāṇaviśuddhyā ca viśuddhaṃ dhyānam / ityetaddhyānamaprameya bodhisattvānāṃ mahābodhiphalaṃ yadāśritya bodhisattvā dhyānapāramitāṃ paripūrya anuttarāṃ samyaksaṃbodhimabhisambuddhavanto 'bhisaṃ[bhotsyante 'bhisaṃ]budhyante ca /
body.translated_text: There, what is the <s>Bodhisattva</s>'s pure meditation (<s>viśuddha dhyāna</s>)? It should be seen as tenfold: meditation purified by worldly purity, unsavored and unafflicted; meditation purified by supramundane purity; meditation purified by the purity of preliminary practice; purified by the purity of the fundamental [absorption]; purified by the purity of the superior [stages] beyond the fundamental; meditation purified by mastery over entry, abiding, and emergence; meditation purified by mastery over re-entering after returning from <s>dhyāna</s>; meditation purified by mastery over supernatural knowledge and manifestation; meditation purified by the removal of all wrong views; and meditation purified by the abandonment of the obscurations of affliction and the knowable. This immeasurable meditation of <s>Bodhisattvas</s> has great awakening as its fruit; relying on it, <s>Bodhisattvas</s>, having fulfilled the perfection of meditation, have fully awakened, will fully awaken, and do fully awaken to the unsurpassed, perfect awakening.

body.text: iti bodhisattvabhūmāvādhāre yogasthāne trayodaśamaṃ dhyānapaṭalam /
body.translated_text: Thus, in the <s>Bodhisattvabhūmi</s>, in the Foundation Section of Yoga (<s>Ādhārayogasthāna</s>), the thirteenth chapter on Meditation (<s>Dhyānapaṭala</s>).

body.text: uddānaṃ pūrvavadveditavyam /
body.translated_text: The summary verse (<s>uddāna</s>) should be understood as before.

body.text: tatra katamo bodhisattvasya prajñāsvabhāvaḥ / sarvajñeyapraveśāya ca sarvajñeyānupraviṣṭaśca yo dharmāṇāṃ pravicayaḥ pañcavidyāsthānānyālambya pravartate adhyātmavidyāṃ hetuvidyāṃ śabdavidyāñcikitsāvidyāṃ śilpakarmasthānavidyāñca / ayaṃ bodhisattvānāṃ prajñāsvabhāvo veditavyaḥ /
body.translated_text: There, what is the <s>Bodhisattva</s>'s nature of wisdom (<s>prajñāsvabhāva</s>)? The investigation of <s>dharmas</s> that operates for the purpose of entering all that is knowable and [after] having entered all that is knowable, taking as its object the five fields of knowledge (<s>vidyāsthāna</s>)—the science of the inner [teaching] (<s>adhyātmavidyā</s>), the science of reasoning (<s>hetuvidyā</s>), the science of grammar (<s>śabdavidyā</s>), the science of medicine (<s>cikitsāvidyā</s>), and the science of arts and crafts (<s>śilpakarmasthānavidyā</s>)—this should be understood as the <s>Bodhisattvas</s>' nature of wisdom.

body.text: tatra katamā bodhisattvānāṃ sarvā prajñā / sā dvividhā draṣṭavyā / laukikī lokottarā ca / sā punaḥ samāsatastrividhā veditavyā / jñeyatattvānubodhaprativedhāya / pañcasu ca yathānirdiṣṭeṣu vidyāsthāneṣu triṣu ca rāśiṣu kauśalyakriyāyai sattvārthakriyāyai ca / yā bodhisattvānāmanabhilāpyaṃ dharmanairātmyamārabhya satyāvabodhāya vā satyāvabodhakāle vā satyābhisaṃbodhādvā urddhaṃ prajñā paramapraśamapratyupasthānā nirvikalpā sarvaṃprapañcāgatā sarvaṃdharmeṣu samatānugatā mahāsāmānyalakṣaṇapraviṣṭā jñeyaparyantagatā samāropāpavādāntadvaya vivarjitatvānmadhyamapratipadanusāriṇī / iyaṃ bodhisattvānāṃ tattvānubodhaprativedhāya prajñā veditavyā / pañcasu vidyāsthāneṣu kauśalyaṃ vistareṇa pūrvavadveditavyaṃ tadyathā balagotrapaṭale / trayaḥ punā rāśayorthopasaṃhitānāṃ dharmāṇāṃ rāśiḥ / anarthopasaṃhitānāṃ dharmāṇāṃ rāśiḥ / naivārthopasaṃhitānāṃ nānā 'rthopasaṃhitānāṃ dharmāṇāṃ rāśiḥ / ityeteṣvaṣṭāsu sthāneṣu prajñāyāḥ kauśalyaparigraho mahāntaṃ niruttaraṃ jñānasambhāraṃ paripūrayatyanuttarāyai samyaksaṃbodhaye / sattvārthakriyā punaḥ pūrvavadekādaśaprakāraiva veditavyā / teṣveva sthāneṣu yā prajñā sā sattvārthakriyāyai prajñā veditavyā /
body.translated_text: There, what is the <s>Bodhisattvas</s>' complete wisdom (<s>sarvā prajñā</s>)? It should be seen as twofold: worldly (<s>laukikī</s>) and supramundane (<s>lokottarā</s>). And it should be understood, in brief, as threefold: for the realization and penetration of the true nature of the knowable; for the practice of skill in the five fields of knowledge as described and in the three categories, and for acting for the welfare of beings. The wisdom of <s>Bodhisattvas</s> that, beginning with the inexpressible selflessness of <s>dharmas</s> (<s>dharmanairātmya</s>), [arises] for the realization of the truths, or at the time of realizing the truths, or subsequent to the full awakening to the truths—wisdom that is attended by supreme tranquility, non-conceptual, free from all conceptual elaboration (<s>prapañca</s>), following equality in all <s>dharmas</s>, having entered the great universal characteristic, reaching the limit of the knowable, and following the middle path (<s>madhyamā pratipad</s>) through being free from the two extremes of superimposition and denial—this should be understood as the <s>Bodhisattvas</s>' wisdom for the realization and penetration of the true nature. Skill in the five fields of knowledge should be understood in detail as before, as in the chapter on the Lineage of Powers. The three categories are: the category of <s>dharmas</s> that are meaningful, the category of <s>dharmas</s> that are not meaningful, and the category of <s>dharmas</s> that are neither meaningful nor not-meaningful. The application of skill in wisdom in these eight bases fulfills the great and unsurpassed accumulation of knowledge for the unsurpassed, perfect awakening. And the activity for the welfare of beings should be understood as the very same elevenfold [activity] as before. The wisdom [applied] in those same bases should be understood as wisdom for acting for the welfare of beings.

body.text: tatra katamā bodhisattvasya duṣkarā prajñā / sā trividhā draṣṭavyā gambhīrasya dharmanairātmyajñānāya duṣkarā / sattvānāṃ vinayopāyasya prajñānāya duṣkarā / sarvajñeyānāvaraṇajñānāya ca paramaduṣkarā /
body.translated_text: There, what is the <s>Bodhisattva</s>'s difficult wisdom (<s>duṣkarā prajñā</s>)? It should be seen as threefold: difficult for the knowledge of the profound selflessness of <s>dharmas</s>; difficult for the knowledge of the means of training beings; and supremely difficult for the unobstructed knowledge of all that is knowable.

body.text: tatra katamā bodhisattvasya sarvatomukhī prajñā / sā caturvidyā draṣṭavyā / śrāvakapiṭakaṃ bodhisattvapiṭakaṃ cārabhya śrutamayī prajñā cintāmayī prajñā / pratisaṃkhyāya bodhisattvakaraṇīyānuvṛttāvakaraṇīyanivṛttau ca pratisaṃkhyānabalasaṃgṛhītā prajñā / bhāvanābalasaṃgṛhītā ca samāhitabhūmikā apramāṇā prajñā /
body.translated_text: There, what is the <s>Bodhisattva</s>'s all-directional wisdom (<s>sarvatomukhī prajñā</s>)? It should be seen as fourfold: wisdom born of learning (<s>śrutamayī prajñā</s>) and wisdom born of reflection (<s>cintāmayī prajñā</s>) with reference to the <s>Śrāvaka Piṭaka</s> and the <s>Bodhisattva Piṭaka</s>; wisdom comprised in the power of reflection, for the engagement in what should be done and the cessation of what should not be done by the <s>Bodhisattva</s>, through deliberation; and wisdom that is comprised in the power of cultivation (<s>bhāvanā</s>), on the level of concentration, and immeasurable.

body.text: tatra katamā bodhisattvasya satpuruṣasya satpuruṣaprajñā / sā pañcavidhā draṣṭavyā / saddharmaśravaṇasamudāgatā pratyātmaṃ yoniśo manaskārasahagatā svaparārthaniścitā prajñā kleśavijahanā ca prajñā / aparaḥ paryāyaḥ / sūkṣmā yathāvad bhāvikatayā jñeyapraveśāt / nipuṇā yāvadbhāvikatayā jñeyapraveśāt / sahajā pūrvakajñānasaṃbhārasamudāgamāt / āgamopetā buddhairmahābhūmipraviṣṭaiśca bodhisattvaiḥ saṃprakāśitadharmārthasyodgrahaṇadhāraṇāt / adhigamopetā śuddhāśayabhūmimupādāya yāvanniṣṭhāgamanabhūmiparigrahāt /
body.translated_text: There, what is the good person's wisdom belonging to the good person (<s>satpuruṣaprajñā</s>) of the <s>Bodhisattva</s>? It should be seen as fivefold: wisdom that has arisen from hearing the true <s>Dharma</s>, accompanied by proper attention within oneself, certain regarding the benefit of self and others, and that abandons afflictions. Another enumeration: subtle, through entering the knowable according to the mode of being (<s>yathāvadbhāvikatā</s>); skillful, through entering the knowable according to the extent of being (<s>yāvadbhāvikatā</s>); innate, through the maturation of previous accumulations of knowledge; endowed with scripture (<s>āgama</s>), through the comprehension and retention of the meaning of <s>Dharma</s> illuminated by <s>Buddhas</s> and <s>Bodhisattvas</s> who have entered the great stages; and endowed with realization (<s>adhigama</s>), from the stage of pure intention up to the stage of reaching culmination.

body.text: tatra katamā bodhisattvasya sarvākārā prajñā / sā ṣaḍvidhā saptavidhā caikadhyamabhisaṃkṣipya trayodaśavidhā veditavyā / satyeṣu duḥkhajñānaṃ samudayajñānaṃ nirodhajñānaṃ mārgajñānam / niṣṭhāyāṃ kṣayajñānamanutpādajñānam / iyaṃ tāvat ṣaḍvidhā prajñā / saptavidhā punaḥ dharmajñānamanvayajñānaṃ saṃvṛtijñānamabhijñājñānaṃ lakṣaṇajñānaṃ daśabalapūrvaṅgamaṃ jñānaṃ catasṛṣu ca yuktiṣu yuktijñānam /
body.translated_text: There, what is the <s>Bodhisattva</s>'s all-aspected wisdom (<s>sarvākārā prajñā</s>)? Combining the sixfold and sevenfold together, it should be understood as thirteenfold. Regarding the truths: knowledge of suffering (<s>duḥkhajñāna</s>), knowledge of the origin (<s>samudayajñāna</s>), knowledge of cessation (<s>nirodhajñāna</s>), and knowledge of the path (<s>mārgajñāna</s>). Regarding the culmination: knowledge of destruction (<s>kṣayajñāna</s>) and knowledge of non-arising (<s>anutpādajñāna</s>). This is the sixfold wisdom. The sevenfold, moreover: <s>dharma</s>-knowledge (<s>dharmajñāna</s>), inferential knowledge (<s>anvayajñāna</s>), conventional knowledge (<s>saṃvṛtijñāna</s>), knowledge of supernatural powers (<s>abhijñājñāna</s>), knowledge of characteristics (<s>lakṣaṇajñāna</s>), knowledge that is the precursor to the ten powers (<s>daśabalapūrvaṅgama jñāna</s>), and knowledge of reasoning regarding the four types of reasoning (<s>yuktijñāna</s>).

body.text: tatra katamā bodhisattvasya vidhātārthikaprajñā / sā 'ṣṭavidhā draṣṭavyā / dharmāṇāṃ paryāyajñānamārabhya bodhisattvasya dharmapratisaṃvit / dharmāṇāṃ lakṣaṇajñānamārabhyārthapratisaṃvit / dharmāṇāṃ nirvacanajñānamārabhya niruktipratisaṃvit / dharmāṇāṃ prakārapadaprabhedamārabhya pratibhānapratisaṃvit / sarvaparapravādinigrahāya bodhisattvasya prajñā / sarvasvavādavyavasthānapratiṣṭhāpanāya ca prajñā / gṛhatantrasamyak praṇayanāya kulodayāya prajñā / rājanītilaukikavyavahāranītiṣu ca bodhisattvasya yā niścitā prajñā /
body.translated_text: There, what is the <s>Bodhisattva</s>'s wisdom for overcoming adversity (<s>vighātārthika prajñā</s>)? It should be seen as eightfold: the <s>Bodhisattva</s>'s analytical knowledge of <s>dharmas</s> (<s>dharmapratisaṃvid</s>), through the knowledge of the methods of <s>dharmas</s>; analytical knowledge of meaning (<s>arthapratisaṃvid</s>), through the knowledge of the characteristics of <s>dharmas</s>; analytical knowledge of etymology (<s>niruktipratisaṃvid</s>), through the knowledge of the definitions of <s>dharmas</s>; analytical knowledge of eloquence (<s>pratibhānapratisaṃvid</s>), through the knowledge of the various classifications and terms of <s>dharmas</s>; the <s>Bodhisattva</s>'s wisdom for defeating all opposing debaters; wisdom for establishing and firmly grounding all one's own doctrinal positions; wisdom for the proper management of household affairs and for the prosperity of families; and the <s>Bodhisattva</s>'s determined wisdom in matters of statecraft, worldly conduct, and social norms.

body.text: tatra katamā bodhisattvasyehāmutrasukhā prajñā / sā navavidhā draṣṭavyā / adhyātmavidyāyāṃ suvyavadātā supratiṣṭhitā prajñā / hetuvidyāyāṃ śabdavidyāyāṃ cikitsāvidyāyāṃ laukikaśilpakarmasthānavidyāyāṃ suvyavadātā no tu pratiṣṭhitā prajñā / tāmeva ca suvyavadātāṃ pañcaprakārāṃ vidyāṃ niśritya yā bodhisattvasya
body.translated_text: There, what is the <s>Bodhisattva</s>'s wisdom that is pleasant here and hereafter (<s>ihāmutrasukhā prajñā</s>)? It should be seen as ninefold: wisdom well-purified and well-established in the science of the inner [teaching] (<s>adhyātmavidyā</s>); wisdom well-purified but not [necessarily] established in the science of reasoning (<s>hetuvidyā</s>), the science of grammar (<s>śabdavidyā</s>), the science of medicine (<s>cikitsāvidyā</s>), and the worldly science of arts and crafts (<s>śilpakarmasthānavidyā</s>); and relying on that very well-purified fivefold knowledge, the <s>Bodhisattva</s>'s

body.text: pareṣāṃ vineyānāṃ mūḍhānāṃ pramattānāṃ saṃlīnānāṃ samyak pratipannānāṃ yathākramaṃ saṃdarśanī samādāpanī samuttejanī saṃpraharṣaṇī ca prajñā /
body.translated_text: wisdom that, for the disciples to be trained—the confused, the heedless, the withdrawn, and the correctly practicing—is, respectively, instructing, encouraging, inspiring, and gladdening.

body.text: tatra katamā bodhisattvasya viśuddhā prajñā / sā samāsato daśavidhā veditavyā / tattvārthe dvividhā yāvadbhāvikatayā yathāvadbhāvikatayā ca tattvārthasya grahaṇāt / pravṛttyarthe dvividhā samyagahetutaḥ phalataśca grahaṇāt / upādānārthe dvividhā viparyāsāviparyāsa-yathābhūtaparijñānāt / upāyārthe dvividhā sarvakaraṇīyākaraṇīya-yathābhūtaparijñānāt / itīyaṃ bodhisattvānāṃ paścākārā daśaprabhedā prajñā viśuddhā paramayā viśuddhyā veditavyā /
body.translated_text: There, what is the <s>Bodhisattva</s>'s pure wisdom (<s>viśuddhā prajñā</s>)? In brief, it should be understood as tenfold: twofold regarding the meaning of reality (<s>tattvārtha</s>), through grasping the meaning of reality according to its extent (<s>yāvadbhāvikatā</s>) and according to its mode (<s>yathāvadbhāvikatā</s>); twofold regarding the meaning of activity (<s>pravṛttyartha</s>), through correct grasping from the [perspective of] cause and of result; twofold regarding the meaning of clinging (<s>upādānārtha</s>), through the true comprehension of inversion and non-inversion; twofold regarding the meaning of means (<s>upāyārtha</s>), through the true comprehension of all that should and should not be done. This eightfold [actually tenfold] wisdom of the <s>Bodhisattvas</s>, with ten divisions, should be understood as pure wisdom, purified by supreme purity.

body.text: itīyaṃ bodhisattvānāṃ su-viniścitā cāprameyā ca prajñā mahābodhiphalā yāmāśritya bodhisattvāḥ prajñāpāramitāṃ paripūryānuttarāṃ samyaksambodhimabhisaṃbudhyante /
body.translated_text: Thus, this well-determined and immeasurable wisdom of <s>Bodhisattvas</s>, having great awakening as its fruit—relying on it, <s>Bodhisattvas</s>, having fulfilled the perfection of wisdom (<s>prajñāpāramitā</s>), fully awaken to the unsurpassed, perfect awakening.

body.text: sa khalveṣa ṣaṇṇāṃ pāramitānāṃ teṣu-teṣu sūtrāntareṣu bhagavatā vyagrāṇāṃ nirdiṣṭānāmayaṃ samāsa-saṃgraha-nirdeśo veditavyaḥ / yasmiṃtathāgata-bhāṣite sūtre dānapāramitā vā yāvat prajñāpāramitā vā uddeśamāgacchati nirdeśaṃ vā sā svabhāva-dāne vā yāvat viśuddhe vā dāne 'vatārayitavyā / saṃgrahaśca tasyā yathā yogaṃ veditavyaḥ / evamanyeṣāṃ śīlādīnāṃ prajñāvasānānāṃ yathānirdiṣṭānāmavatāraḥ saṃgrahaśca yathāyogaṃ veditavyaḥ / yāni ca tathāgatānāṃ bodhisattvacaryā-janmāprameyāṇi jātakāni duṣkaracaryā-pratisaṃyuktāni tāni sarvāṇi dānapratisaṃyuktāni dānamārabhya veditavyāni / yathā dānamevaṃ śīlaṃ kṣāntiṃ vīryaṃ dhyānaṃ sarvāṇiṃ prajñāpratisaṃyuktāni prajñāmārabhya veditavyāni / kāniciddānamevārabhya kānicidyāvat prajñāmevārabhya kāniciddvayasaṃsṛṣṭāni kānicitrayasaṃsṛṣṭāni kāniciccatuḥsaṃsṛṣṭāni kānicitpañcasaṃsṛṣṭāni kānicitsarvā eva ṣaṭpāramitā ārabhya veditavyāni / ābhiḥ ṣaḍbhiḥ pāramitābhiranuttarāyai samyak saṃbodhaye samudāgacchanto bodhisattvā mahāśukladharmārṇavā mahāśukladharmasamudrā ityucyante / sarvasattvasarvākārasaṃpattihetumahāratnahradā ityucyante / asya punareṣāmevamapramāṇasya puṇyajñānasaṃbhārasamudāgamasya nānyatphalamevamanurūpaṃ yathānuttaraivaṃ samyaksaṃbodhiriti /
body.translated_text: This, indeed, should be understood as the summary collection and exposition of the six <s>pāramitās</s> that have been proclaimed in scattered form by the <s>Bhagavān</s> throughout the various <s>sūtras</s>. In whichever <s>sūtra</s> spoken by the <s>Tathāgata</s> the perfection of generosity up to the perfection of wisdom comes under consideration or exposition, it should be subsumed under generosity in its essential nature up to purified generosity, and its classification should be understood as appropriate. Likewise, the subsumption and classification of the remaining [perfections] from moral conduct onward up to wisdom, as described, should be understood as appropriate. And the immeasurable <s>Jātakas</s> (birth-stories) of the <s>Tathāgatas</s> connected with the practice of <s>Bodhisattva</s>-conduct and difficult practices—all of those should be understood as connected with generosity beginning with generosity. Just as with generosity, so with moral conduct, patience, vigor, and meditation—all of them connected with wisdom should be understood beginning with wisdom. Some concern generosity alone, some concern up to wisdom alone, some are connected with two [perfections], some with three, some with four, some with five, and some should be understood as concerning all six <s>pāramitās</s>. <s>Bodhisattvas</s> who are accumulating [merit] for the unsurpassed, perfect awakening through these six <s>pāramitās</s> are called great oceans of bright <s>dharmas</s>, great seas of bright <s>dharmas</s>. They are called great jewel-lakes that are the cause of the accomplishment of all aspects for all beings. For this immeasurable accumulation of merit and knowledge, there is no other fitting fruit than the unsurpassed, perfect awakening itself.

body.text: iti bodhisattvabhūmāvādhāre yogasthāne caturdaśamaṃ prajñāpaṭalam /
body.translated_text: Thus, in the <s>Bodhisattvabhūmi</s>, in the Foundation Section of Yoga, the fourteenth chapter, the <s>Prajñā-paṭala</s> (Chapter on Wisdom), [is completed].

body.text: (Chapter 1.15)
body.translated_text: (Chapter 1.15)

body.text: Saṃgrahavastupaṭalam
body.translated_text: <s>Saṃgrahavastu-paṭala</s> (Chapter on the Means of Attraction)

body.text: uddānaṃ pūrvavadveditavyam /
body.translated_text: The summary verse (<s>uddāna</s>) should be understood as before.

body.text: tatra katamo bodhisattvānāṃ priyavāditāsvabhāvaḥ / iha bodhisattvo manāpāṃ satyāṃ dharmyāñcārthopasaṃhitāñca sattveṣu vācamudāharati / ayaṃ bodhisattvānāṃ samāsataḥ priyavāditāsvabhāvaḥ /
body.translated_text: There, what is the essential nature of kind speech (<s>priyavāditā</s>) for <s>Bodhisattvas</s>? Here, the <s>Bodhisattva</s> speaks to beings words that are agreeable, truthful, in accordance with the <s>Dharma</s>, and conducive to their purpose. This is, in brief, the essential nature of kind speech for <s>Bodhisattvas</s>.

body.text: tatra katamā bodhisattvasya sarvā priyavāditā / sā trividhā draṣṭavyā / iha bodhisattvasya yā vāksammodanī yayā vācā bodhisattvo vigatabhṛkuṭiḥ pūrvābhilāpī uttānamukhavarṇaḥ smitamukha pūrvaṅgamaḥ kṣemasvastyayanaparipṛcchayā vā dhātusāmyaparipṛcchayā vā sukharātrindivaparipṛcchayā vā ehīti svāgata[vādi]tayā vā ityevamādibhirākāraiḥ sattvān pratisammodayati lokayātrāṃ nāgarakabhāvamanuvartamānaḥ / yā ca vāgbodhisattvasyānandanī yayā vācā bodhisattvaḥ putravṛddhiṃ [dāravṛddhiṃ] jñātivṛddhiṃ dhanavṛddhiṃ dhānyavṛddhiṃ vā dṛṣṭvā apratisaṃviditātmavṛddhikānāṃ sattvānāmāvedayannānandayati śraddhāśīlaśrutatyāgaprajñāvṛddhyā vā punarānandayati / yā ca bodhisattvasya sarvākāraguṇopetadharmadeśanāpratisaṃyuktā vāk sattvānāṃ hitasukhāya satatasamitaṃ pratyupasthitā parameṇopakāreṇopakāribhūtā / iyaṃ bodhisattvānāṃ priyavāditā prabhedaśaḥ sarvā veditavyā /
body.translated_text: There, what is the entire kind speech of the <s>Bodhisattva</s>? It should be seen as threefold. First, the <s>Bodhisattva</s>'s greeting speech (<s>sammodanī vāk</s>), by which the <s>Bodhisattva</s>, free from frowning, speaking first, with an open and bright countenance, preceded by a smiling face, greets beings with such modes as inquiring about their safety and well-being, inquiring about the balance of their bodily elements, inquiring about happy nights and days, and welcoming words such as 'Come, welcome!'—following the ways of the world and the manner of the urbane. Second, the <s>Bodhisattva</s>'s gladdening speech (<s>ānandanī vāk</s>), by which the <s>Bodhisattva</s>, upon seeing the increase of sons, [wives,] relatives, wealth, or grain for beings who are unaware of their own increase, informs and gladdens them—or gladdens them by [proclaiming] the increase of their faith, moral conduct, learning, generosity, and wisdom. Third, the speech connected with teaching the <s>Dharma</s> endowed with all aspects of qualities, constantly present for the benefit and happiness of beings, and standing as a supreme benefactor with the greatest assistance. This should be understood as the entire kind speech of <s>Bodhisattvas</s> in its differentiated forms.

body.text: tatra katamā bodhisattvānāṃ samāsataḥ sarvā priyavāditā / sā dvividhā draṣṭavyā / lokayātrānugatā samyagdharmadeśanānugatā ca / tatra yā ca sammodanīvāg yā cānandanī iyaṃ lokayātrānugatā veditavyā / tatra yeyaṃ vāgupakarā parameṇopakāreṇa pratyupasthitā nirdiṣṭā iyaṃ samyagdharmadeśanānugratā veditavyā /
body.translated_text: There, what is the entire kind speech of <s>Bodhisattvas</s> in brief? It should be seen as twofold: that which follows worldly custom and that which follows the correct teaching of the <s>Dharma</s>. There, the greeting speech and the gladdening speech—this should be understood as following worldly custom. The speech that is beneficial, standing as a supreme benefactor, as described—this should be understood as following the correct teaching of the <s>Dharma</s>.

body.text: tatra katamā bodhisattvasya duṣkarā priyavāditā / sā trividhā draṣṭavyā / yadbodhisattvo vadhakeṣu pratyarthiṣu pratyamitreṣu suviśuddhena niṣkaluṣeṇa cetasā pratisaṃkhyāya sammodanīṃ vā ānandanīṃ vā upakarāṃ vācamudīrayati iyaṃ
body.translated_text: There, what is the difficult kind speech (<s>duṣkarā priyavāditā</s>) of the <s>Bodhisattva</s>? It should be seen as threefold. When the <s>Bodhisattva</s>, toward murderers, adversaries, and enemies, with a thoroughly pure and stainless mind, having reflected, utters greeting, gladdening, or beneficial speech—this

body.text: bodhisattvasya prathamā duṣkarā priyavāditā veditavyā / yatpunarbodhisattvaḥ adhimātraṃ saṃmūḍheṣu sattveṣu dhandhendriyeṣvaparitasyamānaḥ pratisaṃkhyāya dharmyāṃ kathāṃ kathayati khedamabhyupagamya grāhayati nyāyaṃ dharmaṃ kuśalam iyaṃ dvitīyā bodhisattvasya duṣkarā priyavāditā veditavyā / punaryadbodhisattvaḥ śaṭheṣu māyāviṣu sattveṣvācāryopādhyāyagurudakṣiṇīyavisaṃvādakeṣu mithyāpratipanneṣu anāghātacitto 'pratighacittaḥ sammodanīmānandanīmupakarāṃ vācamudīrayati iyaṃ bodhisattvasya tṛtīyā duṣkarā priyavāditā veditavyā /
body.translated_text: should be understood as the <s>Bodhisattva</s>'s first difficult kind speech. When the <s>Bodhisattva</s>, toward beings who are extremely deluded and of dull faculties, without becoming weary, having reflected, speaks a discourse on the <s>Dharma</s> and, undertaking the hardship, causes them to grasp what is reasonable, the <s>Dharma</s>, and the wholesome—this should be understood as the <s>Bodhisattva</s>'s second difficult kind speech.
