When the <s>Bodhisattva</s>, toward beings who are deceitful and fraudulent, who betray their teachers, preceptors, elders, and those worthy of offerings, and who practice wrongly—without a mind of hostility, without a mind of aversion—utters greeting, gladdening, and beneficial speech—this should be understood as the <s>Bodhisattva</s>'s third difficult kind speech.

body.text: tatra katamā bodhisattvasya sarvato-mukhī priyavāditā / sā caturvidhā draṣṭavyā / nivaraṇa-prahāṇāya sugatigamanāya pūrvakālakaraṇīyā dharmadeśanā / vigatanivaraṇasya kalya-cittasya sāmutkarṣikī caturāryasatya-pratisaṃyuktā dharmadeśanā / pramattānāṃ sattvānāṃ gṛhi-pravrajitānāṃ samyaksaṃcodanā pramādacaryāyā utthāpya apramādacaryāyāṃ pratiṣṭhāpanārtham / utpannotpannāñca saṃśayānāmapanayāya yā dharmadeśanā sāṃkathyaviniścaya-kriyā /
body.translated_text: There, what is the all-encompassing kind speech (<s>sarvatomukhī priyavāditā</s>) of <s>Bodhisattvas</s>? It should be seen as fourfold. Teaching of the <s>Dharma</s> for the purpose of abandoning the hindrances (<s>nīvaraṇa</s>) and going to happy destinies, which is preliminary. Teaching of the <s>Dharma</s> connected with the four noble truths (<s>caturāryasatya</s>), which is elevating, for one who is free from hindrances and whose mind is fit. Correct admonition of negligent beings, whether householders or renunciants, for the purpose of raising them from negligent conduct and establishing them in heedful conduct. And the teaching of the <s>Dharma</s> for the dispelling of doubts that arise again and again—the activity of determining through discussion.

body.text: tatra katamā bodhisattvānāṃ sat-puruṣāṇāṃ satpuruṣapriyavāditā / sā pañcavidhā draṣṭavyā / iha bodhisattvabhūtāstathāgatabhūtāśca bodhisattvāḥ sanidānameva vineyānāṃ dharmaṃ deśayanti saniḥsaraṇaṃ sapratisaraṇaṃ saparākramaṃ saprātihāryam / sthāne sotpattikaṃ śikṣāpadaṃ prajñapayanti / tasmāt eṣāṃ dharmaḥ sanidāno bhavati / samāttaśikṣāṇāñcāpannānāmāpatteḥ vyutthānaṃ prajñapayanti / tasmāt eṣā dharmaḥ saniḥsaraṇo bhavati / caturbhiḥ pratisaraṇaiḥ saṃgṛhītāmaviparītāṃ dharmavinaye 'smin pratipattiṃ prajñapayanti / tasmādeṣāṃ dharmaḥ sapratisaraṇo bhavati / sarvaduḥkha-nairyāṇikīmapratyudāvartāṃ pratipadaṃ saṃprakāśayanti / tasmādeṣāṃ dharmaḥ saparākramo bhavati / tribhiśca prātihāryaiḥ sarvāṃ deśanāmabandhyāṃ kurvanti / tasmādeṣāṃ dharmaḥ saprātihāryo bhavati /
body.translated_text: There, what is the kind speech of <s>Bodhisattvas</s> who are true persons, the kind speech of true persons? It should be seen as fivefold. Here, <s>Bodhisattvas</s> who are [true] <s>Bodhisattvas</s> and those who are <s>Tathāgatas</s> teach the <s>Dharma</s> to those to be trained only with a foundation, with a way of escape, with a refuge, with a progression, and with a miracle. They prescribe training-rules on proper occasion, with arising [conditions]. Therefore, their <s>Dharma</s> has a foundation. They prescribe the rising from offense for those who have undertaken the training and have committed an offense. Therefore, their <s>Dharma</s> has a way of escape. They prescribe a practice that is without error in this <s>Dharma</s> and <s>Vinaya</s>, comprised in the four reliances (<s>pratisaraṇa</s>). Therefore, their <s>Dharma</s> has a refuge. They illuminate the path that leads out of all suffering, from which there is no turning back. Therefore, their <s>Dharma</s> has a progression. And through the three miracles (<s>prātihārya</s>), they make all teaching fruitful. Therefore, their <s>Dharma</s> has a miracle.

body.text: tatra katamā bodhisattvānāṃ sarvākārā priyavāditā / sā ṣaḍvidhā saptavidhā caikadhyamabhisaṃkṣipya trayodaśavidhā draṣṭavyā / anujñeyeṣu dharmeṣvanujñāne priyavāditā / pratiṣeddhavyeṣu dharmeṣu pratiṣedhe / dharmāṇāṃ dharmaparyāyodbhāvikā priyavāditā / dharmalakṣaṇāviparītodbhāvikā / dharma-nirvacanāviparītodbhāvikā / dharmapadaprakāraprabhedodbhāvikā
body.translated_text: There, what is the all-aspect kind speech (<s>sarvākārā priyavāditā</s>) of <s>Bodhisattvas</s>? It should be seen as sixfold and sevenfold—gathered together as thirteenfold. Kind speech in the approval of <s>dharmas</s> that should be approved. Kind speech in the prohibition of <s>dharmas</s> that should be prohibited. Kind speech that elucidates the discourse-methods of <s>dharmas</s>. Kind speech that elucidates the characteristics of <s>dharmas</s> without error. Kind speech that elucidates the definitions of <s>dharmas</s> without error. Kind speech that elucidates the analysis of categories and types of <s>dharmas</s>.

body.text: priyavāditā / sammodanī priyavāditā / ānandanī priyabāditā / pareṣāṃ sarvopakaraṇairalpotsukatāyāṃ sarvakṛtyeṣu ca samyaggateṣvalpotsukatāyāṃ viśadapravāraṇī priyavāditā / vividheṣu ca bhayeṣu bhītānāmāśvāsanī priyavāditā / nyāyopadeśasaṃgahītā ca priyavāditā / akuśalāt sthānād vutthāpya kuśale sthāne pratiṣṭhāpanārthaṃ samyagdṛṣṭa-śruta-pariśaṅkita-saṃcodanāvasādanī priyavāditā / paraṃ pratibalamadhyeṣyopasaṃhṛtā priyavāditā / iyaṃ bodhisattvānāṃ trayodaśākārā priyavāditā sarvākārā veditavyā /
body.translated_text: Greeting kind speech. Gladdening kind speech. Kind speech of clear invitation, when others have little concern for all provisions and when all tasks have gone well. Kind speech of reassurance for those frightened by various fears. Kind speech comprised in proper guidance. Kind speech of correct admonition—reprimanding and humbling—for the purpose of raising from an unwholesome state and establishing in a wholesome state, what has been seen, heard, or suspected. Kind speech that is withdrawn and deferred to another capable person. This should be understood as the thirteenfold all-aspect kind speech of <s>Bodhisattvas</s>.

body.text: tatra katamā bodhisattvānāṃ vidhātārthika-priyavāditā / sā 'ṣṭavidhā draṣṭavyā / yā bodhisattvasya caturvidhāṃ vāgviśuddhiṃ niśrityāṣṭaskāryeṣu vyavahāreṣu vāk / iyaṃ vighātārthika-priyavāditā bodhisattvānāmucyate / tatreyaṃ catuvidhā vāgviśuddhiḥ / mṛṣāvādātprativiratiḥ / paiśunyātpāruṣyātsaṃbhinnapralāpāt prativiratiḥ / tatreme 'ṣṭāvāryā vyavahārāḥ / dṛṣṭe dṛṣṭavāditā śrute mate vijñāte vijñātabāditā / adṛṣṭe 'dṛṣṭavāditā / aśrute 'mate avijñāte 'vijñātavāditā /
body.translated_text: There, what is the kind speech of <s>Bodhisattvas</s> that removes harm? It should be seen as eightfold. That speech of the <s>Bodhisattva</s> which, relying on the fourfold purity of speech, operates in the eight noble modes of expression—this is called the kind speech of <s>Bodhisattvas</s> that removes harm. There, this is the fourfold purity of speech: abstention from false speech, abstention from slander, abstention from harsh speech, and abstention from frivolous talk. And these are the eight noble modes of expression: saying one has seen what one has seen, saying one has heard what one has heard, saying one has thought what one has thought, saying one has cognized what one has cognized; saying one has not seen what one has not seen, saying one has not heard what one has not heard, saying one has not thought what one has not thought, and saying one has not cognized what one has not cognized.

body.text: tatra katamā bodhisattvānāmihāmutrasukhā priyavāditā / sā navavidhā draṣṭavyā / jñātivyasanaśokaprahāṇāya priyavāditā / bhogavyasanaśoka prahāṇāya ārogyavyasanaśokaprahāṇāya priyavāditā / śīlavyasanaprahāṇāya dṛṣṭivyasanaprahāṇāya priyavāditā / śīlasaṃpade dṛṣṭisaṃpade ācārasaṃpade ājīvasaṃpade ca yā priyavāditā saddharmadeśanā /
body.translated_text: There, what is the kind speech of <s>Bodhisattvas</s> that brings happiness in this life and the next? It should be seen as ninefold. Kind speech for the abandonment of grief over the loss of relatives. Kind speech for the abandonment of grief over the loss of possessions. Kind speech for the abandonment of grief over the loss of health. Kind speech for the abandonment of the loss of moral conduct. Kind speech for the abandonment of the loss of right views. And the kind speech that is the teaching of the <s>Dharma</s> for the accomplishment of moral conduct, the accomplishment of right views, the accomplishment of conduct, and the accomplishment of livelihood.

body.text: tatra katamā bodhisattvasya viśuddhā priyavādittā / saḥ viṃśatividhā draṣṭavyā / viṃśatyākārairyā dharmadeśanā sā punaḥ pūrvavadveditavyā / tadyathā balagotrapaṭale / tatrārthacaryā yathaiva priyavāditā tathaiva vistareṇa veditavyā / eyadviśiṣṭāñcārthacaryāmanyāṃ vakṣyāmi / tathā hi bodhisattvaḥ sarvaprakārayā 'nayā priyavāditayā tatra-tatropagamārthaṃ sattvānāmācarati / tatra katamo bodhisattvānāmarthacaryāsvabhāvaḥ / evaṃ priyavāditayā yuktisaṃdarśitānāṃ sattvānāṃ yathāyogaṃ śikṣāsvarthacaryāyāṃ dharmānudharmapraticaryāyāṃ kāruṇyacittamupasthāpya nirāmiṣeṇa
body.translated_text: There, what is the purified kind speech (<s>viśuddhā priyavāditā</s>) of the <s>Bodhisattva</s>? It should be seen as twentyfold. The teaching of the <s>Dharma</s> in twenty aspects should be understood as before—namely, as in the <s>Balagotra-paṭala</s>. There, beneficent conduct (<s>arthacaryā</s>) should be understood in detail just as kind speech. And I shall state a further distinctive beneficent conduct. For the <s>Bodhisattva</s>, through this entire kind speech of every kind, acts for the purpose of the approach of beings in each case. There, what is the essential nature of <s>Bodhisattvas</s>' beneficent conduct? For beings who have been shown what is reasonable through kind speech, the <s>Bodhisattva</s>, having established a compassionate mind, with a mind free from worldly gain,

body.text: cetasā samādāpanā vinayanā niveśanā pratiṣṭhāpanā / ayamarthacaryāyāḥ samāsataḥ svabhāvanirdeśaḥ
body.translated_text: encourages, trains, settles, and firmly grounds them as appropriate in the trainings and in the practice in accordance with the <s>Dharma</s>, through beneficent conduct. This is, in brief, the exposition of the essential nature of beneficent conduct.

body.text: tatra katamā bodhisattvānāṃ sarvārthacaryā / sā dvividhā draṣṭavyā / aparipakvānāñca sattvānāṃ paripācanā / paripakvānāñca sattvānāṃ vimocanā / sā punastribhirmukhaiḥ veditavyā / dṛṣṭadhārmike 'rthe samādāpanā / sāṃparāyike 'rthe samādāpanā / dṛṣṭadharma-sāṃparāyike 'rthe samādāpanā / tatra dhārmikaiḥ karmaguṇaiḥ bhogānāmarjana-rakṣaṇa-vardhana-samyak-samādāpanatayā dṛṣṭadhārmike 'rthe samādāpanā veditavyā / yenāyaṃ parataśca praśaṃsāṃ labhate dṛṣṭe ca dharmai sukham / upakaraṇasukhenānugṛhīto viharati / tatra bhogān utsṛjya bhikṣākavṛtta-jīvikā-pratibaddhamavrajyā-samādāpanā / sāṃparāyike 'rthe samādāpanā veditavyā / yenāyaṃ niyataṃ saṃparāyasukhito bhavati na tvavaśyaṃ dṛṣṭe dharme / tatra yā gṛhiṇo vā pravrajitasya vānupūrveṇa vairāgya-gamana-samādāpanā / iyaṃ dṛṣṭadharma-sāṃparāyike 'rthe samādāpanā veditavyā / yenāyaṃ dṛṣṭe ca dharme prasrabdha-kāya prasrabdha-cittaḥ sukhaṃ sparśaṃ viharati / saṃparāye ca viśuddhideveṣūpadyate / nirūpadhiśeṣe nirvāṇadhātau parinirvāti /
body.translated_text: There, what is the entire beneficent conduct (<s>sarvārthacaryā</s>) of <s>Bodhisattvas</s>? It should be seen as twofold: the ripening of beings who are not yet ripened, and the liberation of beings who are already ripened. That, moreover, should be understood through three approaches: encouraging in the purpose of this present life, encouraging in the purpose of the future life, and encouraging in the purpose of both this present and the future life. There, through <s>dharma</s>-based qualities of action—the proper encouragement in the earning, guarding, increasing, and right employment of possessions—this should be understood as encouragement in the purpose of this present life. By this, one obtains praise from others and happiness in this present life, and abides assisted by the happiness of material provisions. There, the encouragement to go forth, relinquishing possessions, to a livelihood dependent on alms—this should be understood as encouragement in the purpose of the future life. By this, one is certainly made happy in the hereafter, but not necessarily in this present life. There, the encouragement of a householder or renunciant in the gradual progress toward dispassion—this should be understood as encouragement in the purpose of both this present and the future life. By this, in this present life one abides with a tranquil body and tranquil mind, in comfortable contact. In the hereafter, one is reborn among the pure gods. And one attains <s>parinirvāṇa</s> in the <s>Nirvāṇa</s>-element without remainder.

body.text: tatra katamā bodhisattvānāṃ duṣkarā arthacaryā / sā trividhā draṣṭavyā / pūrvakuśalamūlahetvacariteṣu sattveṣvarthacaryā bodhisattvānāṃ duṣkarā / tathā hi te duḥkhasamādāpyā bhavanti kuśale / mahatyāṃ bhogasaṃpadi vartamāneṣu sattveṣu tadadhyavasānagateṣvarthacaryā bodhisattvānāṃ duṣkarā / tathāhi te mahati pramādapade pramādasthāne vartante / ito bāhyakeṣu tīrthikeṣu pūrvaṃ [ca] tīrthika dṛṣṭicariteṣu sattveṣvarthaṃcaryā bodhisattvānāṃ duṣkarā / tathā hi te svayaṃ saṃmūḍhāścābhiniviṣṭāścāsmin dharmavinaye /
body.translated_text: There, what is the <s>Bodhisattvas</s>' difficult welfare-activity (<s>duṣkarā arthacaryā</s>)? It should be understood as threefold. Welfare-activity toward beings in whom no prior wholesome roots have been cultivated is difficult for <s>Bodhisattvas</s>. For indeed, they are difficult to establish in the wholesome. Welfare-activity toward beings who are established in great abundance of wealth and are immersed in it is difficult for <s>Bodhisattvas</s>. For indeed, they abide in a great occasion for heedlessness, a ground of heedlessness. Welfare-activity toward beings who are outsiders, heretics (<s>tīrthikas</s>), and have formerly conducted themselves according to heretical views is difficult for <s>Bodhisattvas</s>. For indeed, they are themselves deluded and attached to this <s>Dharma</s> and <s>Vinaya</s>.

body.text: tatra katamā bodhisattvānāṃ sarvatomukhī arthacaryā / sā caturvidhā draṣṭavyā / iha bodhisattvaḥ aśrāddhaṃ śraddhāsaṃpadi samādāpayati yāvatpratiṣṭhāpayati / duḥśīlaṃ śīlasaṃpadi duṣprajñaṃ prajñāsaṃpadi matsariṇaṃ tyāgasaṃpadi samādāpayati yāvatpratiṣṭhāpayati /
body.translated_text: There, what is the <s>Bodhisattvas</s>' all-embracing welfare-activity (<s>sarvatomukhī arthacaryā</s>)? It should be understood as fourfold. Here, the <s>Bodhisattva</s> leads one who lacks faith to the accomplishment of faith, and so on up to establishing [them in it]. He leads one of poor morality to the accomplishment of morality, one of poor wisdom to the accomplishment of wisdom, and one who is miserly to the accomplishment of generosity, and so on up to establishing [them in it].

body.text: tatra katamā bodhisattvasya satpuruṣārthacaryā / sā pañcavidhā draṣṭavyā / iha bodhisattvaḥ sattvān bhūte 'rthe samādāpayati / kālena samādāyapati / arthopasaṃhite 'rthe samādāpayati / ślakṣṇena samādāpayati / maitracittena samādāpayati /
body.translated_text: There, what is the <s>Bodhisattva</s>'s welfare-activity of a good person (<s>satpuruṣārthacaryā</s>)? It should be understood as fivefold. Here, the <s>Bodhisattva</s> leads beings to engage in what is true. He leads [them] at the proper time. He leads [them] to engage in what is purposeful. He leads [them] gently. And he leads [them] with a mind of loving-kindness.

body.text: tatra katamā bodhisattvānāṃ sarvākārārthacaryā / sā ṣaḍvidhā saptavidhā caikadhyamabhisakṣipya trayodaśavidhā draṣṭavyā / iha bodhisattvaḥ saṃgrahītavyāṃśca sattvān samyak saṃgṛhṇāti / nigrahītavyāṃśca sattvān samyagnigṛhṇāti / śāsanapratihatānāñca sattvānāṃ pratighātamapanayati / madhyasthān sattvānasmin śāsanee 'vatārayati / avatīrṇāśca sattvān samyak triṣu yāneṣu paripācayati / paripakvāṃśca sattvān vimocayati / tadekatyāṃśca sambhāra-rakṣopacaye saṃniyojayati / yaduta hīnayāna-niḥsṛtiṃ vārabhya mahāyāna-niḥsṛtiṃ vārabhya / yathā sambhārarakṣopacaye evaṃ praviveke cittaikāgratāyāmāvaraṇaviśudau manaskārabhāvanāyāṃ ca sanniyojayati / śrāvaka-pratyeka-buddhagotrān śrāvaka-pratyeka-buddhayāne sanniyojayati / tathāgata-gotrānanuttare samyaksaṃbodhiyāne niyojayati /
body.translated_text: There, what is the <s>Bodhisattvas</s>' all-aspect welfare-activity (<s>sarvākārārthacaryā</s>)? It should be understood as thirteenfold, combining six and seven types into one. Here, the <s>Bodhisattva</s> properly gathers those beings who should be gathered. He properly disciplines those beings who should be disciplined. He removes the obstructions of those beings who are obstructed by the teaching. He introduces neutral beings into this teaching. He properly matures those beings who have entered into the three vehicles. And he liberates those beings who are matured. And he yokes some of them to the accumulation, protection, and increase of provisions—whether beginning with the escape into the <s>Hīnayāna</s> or beginning with the escape into the <s>Mahāyāna</s>. Just as with the accumulation, protection, and increase of provisions, so he yokes [them] to seclusion, one-pointedness of mind, purification of obscurations, and the cultivation of mental attention. He yokes those of <s>Śrāvaka</s>- and <s>Pratyekabuddha</s>-lineage to the <s>Śrāvaka</s>- and <s>Pratyekabuddha</s>-vehicle. And he yokes those of the <s>Tathāgata</s>-lineage to the vehicle of unsurpassed perfect awakening.

body.text: tatra katamā bodhisattvānāṃ vighātārthikārthacaryā / sā 'ṣṭavidhā draṣṭavyā / hretavyeṣu sthāneṣvāhrīkyaparyavasthāna-paryavasthitānāṃ sattvānāmāhrīkyaparyavasthānaṃ vinodayatyapanayati / yathā āhrīkyaparyavasthānamevamapatrapitavyeṣu anapatrāpyaparyavasthānaṃ middhaparyasthānamauddhatyaparyavasthānaṃ kaukṛtyaparyaṃvasthānamīrṣāparyasthānaṃ [mātsaryaparyavasthānaṃ] vinodayatyapanayati /
body.translated_text: There, what is the <s>Bodhisattvas</s>' welfare-activity for those in distress (<s>vighātārthikārthacaryā</s>)? It should be understood as eightfold. For beings who, in situations where they should feel moral shame, are enveloped by the envelopment of shamelessness (<s>āhrīkya</s>), [the <s>Bodhisattva</s>] dispels and removes the envelopment of shamelessness. Just as with the envelopment of shamelessness, so too with the envelopment of lack of moral dread (<s>anapatrāpya</s>) in situations where they should feel moral dread, the envelopment of sloth (<s>middha</s>), the envelopment of restlessness (<s>auddhatya</s>), the envelopment of remorse (<s>kaukṛtya</s>), the envelopment of jealousy (<s>īrṣā</s>), [and the envelopment of miserliness (<s>mātsarya</s>)]—he dispels and removes [them].

body.text: tatra katamā bodhisattvasyehāmutrasukhā 'rthacaryā / sā navavidhā draṣṭavyā / parasattvānāṃ kāyakarmapariśuddhimārabhya sarvākārā prāṇātipātāt prativiratisamānāpanatā / sarvākārādattādānāt-prativirati-samādāpanatā / sarvākārā kāmamithyācārāt-prativirati-samādāpanatā / sarvākārā surāmaireyamadyapramādasthānāt prativirati-samādāpanatā / vākkarmapariśuddhimārabhya sarvākārā mṛṣāvāda-prativirati-samādāpanatā / sarvākārā paiśunya-prativirati-samādāpanatā / sarvākārā pāruṣya-prativirati-samādāpanatā / sarvākārā sambhinnapralāpa-prativirati-samādāpanatā /
body.translated_text: There, what is the <s>Bodhisattva</s>'s welfare-activity that brings happiness here and hereafter (<s>ihāmutrasukhā arthacaryā</s>)? It should be understood as ninefold. Beginning with the purification of bodily action of other beings: leading [them] to complete abstention from the taking of life in all its aspects; leading [them] to complete abstention from taking what is not given in all its aspects; leading [them] to complete abstention from sexual misconduct in all its aspects; leading [them] to complete abstention from the use of intoxicants, the basis of heedlessness, in all its aspects. Beginning with the purification of verbal action: leading [them] to complete abstention from false speech in all its aspects; leading [them] to complete abstention from divisive speech in all its aspects; leading [them] to complete abstention from harsh speech in all its aspects; leading [them] to complete abstention from idle chatter in all its aspects.

body.text: manaskarmapariśuddhimārabhya sarvākārābhidhyāvyāpādamithyādṛṣṭi-prativirati-samādāpanatā /
body.translated_text: Beginning with the purification of mental action: leading [them] to complete abstention from covetousness, ill-will, and wrong views in all their aspects.

body.text: tatra katamā bodhisattvasya viśuddhā 'rthacaryā / sā daśavidhā draṣṭavyā / bahiḥśuddhimupādāya pañcavidhā / antaḥśuddhimupādāya pañcavidhā / bahiḥśuddhimupādāya bodhisattvānāṃ pañcavidhā sattveṣvarthacaryā katamā / anavadyā 'parāvṛttā 'nupūrvā sarvatragā yathāyogaṃ ca /
body.translated_text: There, what is the <s>Bodhisattva</s>'s pure welfare-activity (<s>viśuddhā arthacaryā</s>)? It should be understood as tenfold: fivefold based on external purity and fivefold based on internal purity. What is the fivefold welfare-activity of <s>Bodhisattvas</s> toward beings based on external purity? It is blameless, irreversible, gradual, all-pervading, and as-appropriate.

body.text: iha bodhisattvaḥ sattvānna duścaritavyāmiśre duścaritapūrvagame sāvadye sakliṣṭe 'kuśale sanniyojayati / iyamasyānavadyā bhavatyarthacaryā sattveṣu /
body.translated_text: Here, the <s>Bodhisattva</s> does not yoke beings to what is mixed with misconduct, preceded by misconduct, blameworthy, afflicted, and unwholesome. This is his blameless welfare-activity toward beings.

body.text: punarbodhisattvo nāmokṣe cānekāntaviśuddhe cāyatane mokṣa eṣa ekāntaviśuddha eṣa iti sattvāṃstatraiva samādāpayati / iyamasyāparāvṛttā sattveṣvarthacaryā /
body.translated_text: Furthermore, the <s>Bodhisattva</s> does not lead beings to establish them in what is not liberation and not exclusively pure, [saying:] 'This is liberation, this is exclusively pure.' This is his irreversible welfare-activity toward beings.

body.text: punarbodhisattvaḥ pūrvaṃ bālaprajñānāṃ sattvānāmuttānāṃ dharmadeśanāṃ karoti / uttānāmavavādānuśāsanīmanupravartayati / madhyaprajñāṃścaināṃviditvā madhyāṃ dharmadeśanāṃ sūkṣmāmavavādānuśāsanīmanupravartayati anupūrveṇa kuśalapakṣasamudāgamāya / iyamasyānupūrvā sattveṣvarthacaryā /
body.translated_text: Furthermore, the <s>Bodhisattva</s> first gives plain <s>Dharma</s>-teaching to beings of weak wisdom, and imparts plain instruction and admonition. And knowing those of middling wisdom, he gives them a middling <s>Dharma</s>-teaching and imparts subtle instruction and admonition—gradually, for the accomplishment of the wholesome side. This is his gradual welfare-activity toward beings.

body.text: punarbodhisattvaścaturṇāṃ varṇānām ā-devamanuṣyāṇāṃ sarvasattvānāṃ yathāśaktiyathābalamarthamācarati / hitasukhaṃ paryeṣate / tatraiva samādāpayati / imamasya marvatrḥgā sattveṣvarthacaryā /
body.translated_text: Furthermore, the <s>Bodhisattva</s> acts for the welfare of all beings of the four classes (<s>varṇas</s>), up to gods and humans, according to his ability and power. He seeks [their] benefit and happiness and leads them to establish [themselves] therein. This is his all-pervading welfare-activity toward beings.

body.text: punarbodhisattvo ye sattvā yasmin svārthe kuśale parītte madhye 'dhimātre vā śakyarūpāḥ samādāpayituṃ yena copāyena śakyarūpāḥ samādāyituṃ tān yathāyogaṃ tatra tathā samādāpayati / iyaṃ tāvadbodhisattvānāṃ sattveṣu pañcavidhā vahiḥśuddhā arthacaryā /
body.translated_text: Furthermore, the <s>Bodhisattva</s>, as for those beings who are capable of being led to engage in whichever wholesome self-interest—whether limited, middling, or extensive—and by whichever skillful means they are capable of being led, he leads them accordingly and appropriately. This, then, is the <s>Bodhisattvas</s>' fivefold externally pure welfare-activity toward beings.

body.text: tatra katamā bodhisattvānāṃ pañcavidhā 'ntaḥśuddhā sattveṣvarthacaryā / iha bodhisattvo vipulena sattveṣu kāruṇyāśayena pratyupasthitenārthamācarati / punarbodhisattvaḥ sattvānāmarthe sarvaduḥkhapariśramairapyaparikhinnamānasaḥ pramudita evaṃ sattvānāmarthamācarati / punarbodhisattvaḥ pravarāyāmagryāyāmapi saṃpadi vartamāno dāsavatpreṣyavadvaśyaputravaccaṇḍāladārakavannīcacitto nihatamadamānāhaṃkāraḥ nāmarthamācarati /
body.translated_text: There, what is the <s>Bodhisattvas</s>' fivefold internally pure welfare-activity toward beings? Here, the <s>Bodhisattva</s> acts for [their] welfare with a vast disposition of compassion toward beings that is present [in him]. Furthermore, the <s>Bodhisattva</s>, even when [undergoing] all sufferings and fatigues for the welfare of beings, with an unwearied mind, acts for the welfare of beings with gladness.

body.text: punarbodhisattvo nirāmiṣeṇākṛtrimeṇa ca parameṇa ca premṇā sattvānāmarthamācarati / punarbodhisattva ātyantikenāpunaḥ pratyudāvartyena maitreṇa cetasā sattvānāmarthamācarati / iyaṃ bodhisattvasya pañcavidhā 'ntaḥśuddhā sattveṣvarthacaryā veditavyā / yā ca pañcavidhā vahiḥśuddhā yā ca pañcavidhā 'ntaḥśuddhā tāṃ sarvāmekadhyamabhisaṃkṣipya daśavidhā bodhisattvānāṃ viśuddhā 'rthacaryetyucyate /
body.translated_text: Furthermore, the <s>Bodhisattva</s>, even while established in the most eminent and supreme prosperity, acts for the welfare of beings with a humble mind—like a servant, like an attendant, like an obedient son, like a <s>caṇḍāla</s> youth—with lowered mind, with pride, conceit, and ego-sense struck down. Furthermore, the <s>Bodhisattva</s> acts for the welfare of beings with supreme affection that is free from material [motivation] and uncontrived. Furthermore, the <s>Bodhisattva</s> acts for the welfare of beings with a mind of loving-kindness that is ultimate and irreversible. This fivefold internally pure welfare-activity of the <s>Bodhisattva</s> toward beings should be understood. The fivefold externally pure and the fivefold internally pure [welfare-activities], all combined into one, are called the <s>Bodhisattvas</s>' tenfold pure welfare-activity.

body.text: tatra katamā bodhisattvasya samānārthatā / iha bodhisattvo yasminnarthe yasmin kuśalamūle parān samādāpayati tasminnarthe tasmin kuśalamūla samādāpane tulye vā 'dhike vā svayaṃ saṃśikṣyate / iti yaivaṃ bodhisattvasya paraistulyārthatā iyamucyate samānārthatā / tāṃ samānārthatāṃ pare vineyā bodhisattvebhya upalabhya dṛḍhaniścayā bhavantyapratyudāvartyāstasmin kuśala[mūla]samādāpane / tatkasya hetoḥ / teṣāmevaṃ bhavati / nūnametadasmākaṃ hitametatsukhaṃ yatrāyaṃ bodhisattvo 'smān samādāpitavān / yasmādayaṃ bodhisattvo yatraivāsmān sanniyojayati tadevātmanā samudācarati / tatrāyaṃ jānannahitamasukhaṃ nātmanā samudācarediti na cāsya samānārthasya bodhisattvasyaivaṃ bhavanti pare vaktāraḥ / tvaṃ tāvat svayaṃ na kuśalaṃ samādāya vartase / kasmāttvaṃ paraṃ kuśale 'tyartha samādāpayitavyaṃ vaktavyamavavaditavyaṃ manyase / tvameva tāvadanyairvaktavyo 'vavaditavyo 'nuśāsitavya iti / asti bodhisattvaḥ paraiḥ samānārtha eva saṃstāṃ samānārthatāṃ pareṣāṃ nopadarśayati / astyasamānārtha eva san samānārthatāmupadarśayati / asti samānārthaḥ sasānārthatāmupadarśayati / asti naiva samānārtho nāpi samānārthatāmupadarśayati / tatra prathamā koṭi tulyaguṇaprabhāvānāṃ bodhisattvānāṃ bodhisattvamārge ācāryatvamabhyupagatānāṃ tulyaguṇaprabhāvo bodhisattvaḥ praticchannakalyāṇatayā guṇān prabhāvañca nopadarśayati / dvitīyā koṭī hīnādhimuktikānāṃ sattvānāṃ gaṃbhīreṣu sthāneṣūttrastānāṃ pratisaṃkhyāya bodhisattvaḥ teṣāmeva sattvānāṃ tenopāyena vinayanārthaṃ sahadhārmikamātmānamupadarśayati / saṃcintya ā-caṇḍālānām ā-śunāmarthaṃ kartukāma upadravaṃ saṃśamitukāmo vinayitukāma ā-caṇḍālānām āśunāṃ
body.translated_text: There, what is the <s>Bodhisattva</s>'s shared purpose (<s>samānārthatā</s>)? Here, the <s>Bodhisattva</s>, in whatever purpose and in whatever wholesome root he leads others to engage, in that very purpose and in that very wholesome root he himself trains equally or to a greater degree. Thus, the <s>Bodhisattva</s>'s sharing of purpose equally with others is called shared purpose. When the trainees perceive this shared purpose from <s>Bodhisattvas</s>, they become firmly resolved and irreversible in that engagement with wholesome [roots]. For what reason? For they think thus: 'Surely this is our benefit and this is our happiness, to which this <s>Bodhisattva</s> has led us to engage. For the <s>Bodhisattva</s> himself practices that very thing to which he yokes us. Knowing [the matter], he would not himself practice what is not beneficial and not happiness.' And others cannot say to this <s>Bodhisattva</s> of shared purpose: 'You yourself do not take up the wholesome and practice it. Why then do you think that you should excessively lead, speak to, instruct, and admonish others in the wholesome? You yourself should first be spoken to, instructed, and admonished by others.' There is a <s>Bodhisattva</s> who shares purpose equally with others but does not display that shared purpose. There is one who, not sharing purpose, displays shared purpose. There is one who shares purpose and displays shared purpose. And there is one who neither shares purpose nor displays shared purpose. There, the first case is of <s>Bodhisattvas</s> of equal qualities and power who have assumed the role of teacher on the <s>Bodhisattva</s> path—a <s>Bodhisattva</s> of equal qualities and power does not display his qualities and power because of being one who conceals his virtues. The second case: having reflected, for the sake of disciplining beings of inferior aspiration who are alarmed at profound matters, the <s>Bodhisattva</s> displays himself as a fellow practitioner as a skillful means for disciplining those very beings. Deliberately wishing to benefit even down to <s>caṇḍālas</s> and even dogs, wishing to pacify misfortune, wishing to discipline, [he] is reborn in the class of beings even down to <s>caṇḍālas</s> and even dogs.

body.text: sabhāgatāyāmupapadyate / tṛtīyā koṭī calakuśalamūlasamādānānāṃ vineyānāṃ sthirīkaraṇārthaṃ bodhisattvaḥ samānārthaḥ adhikārtho vā samānārthatāmupadarśayati / caturthī koṭī svayaṃ pramattaḥ parārthamapyabhyupekṣate /
body.translated_text: The third case: for the purpose of stabilizing trainees whose engagement with wholesome roots is wavering, the <s>Bodhisattva</s>, sharing purpose equally or even more, displays shared purpose. The fourth case: one who is himself heedless and also neglects the welfare of others.

body.text: tatra yacca dānamanekavidhaṃ nirdiṣṭaṃ yacca śīlaṃ vistareṇa yāvadyā ca samānārthatā tatra pāramitābhiradhyātmaṃ buddhadharmaparipākaḥ / saṃgrahavastubhiḥ [sarva]sattvaparipākaḥ / samāsato bodhisattvasyaitatkuśalānāṃ dharmāṇāṃ karma veditavyam / tatra yacca dānamanekavidhaṃ pūrvavadyāvat samānārthatā ityeṣāmanekavidhānāmaprameyāṇāṃ kuśalānāṃ dharmāṇāṃ bodhipākṣikānāṃ tribhiḥ kāraṇaiḥ samudācāro veditavyaḥ / dvābhyāṃ kāraṇābhyāṃ śreṣṭhatā veditavyā / tribhiḥ kāraṇairviśuddhirveditavyā /
body.translated_text: There, the manifold generosity that has been taught, the moral conduct in detail, up to the shared purpose—there, through the <s>pāramitās</s>, the inner maturation of the <s>Buddha</s>-<s>dharmas</s> [is accomplished]. Through the means of attraction (<s>saṃgrahavastu</s>), the maturation of all beings [is accomplished]. In brief, this should be understood as the activity of the <s>Bodhisattva</s>'s wholesome <s>dharmas</s>. There, the manifold generosity as before, up to shared purpose—of these manifold and immeasurable wholesome <s>dharmas</s> that are conducive to awakening, the practice should be understood through three causes. The excellence should be understood through two causes. And the purification should be understood through three causes.

body.text: kāyena vācā manasā samudācāro veditavyaḥ / udāratvādasaṃkliṣṭatvācca śreṣṭhatā niruttaratā asādhāraṇatā ca veditavyā / tatra sattvābhedato vastvabhedataḥ kālābhedattaścodāratā veditavyā / tatra sattvābhedo yadbodhisattvaḥ sarvasattvānadhiṣṭhāya sarvasattvānārabhya tāni dānādīni kuśalamūlāni samudācarati na kevalasyātmana evārthe / tatra vastvabhedo yadbodhisattvaḥ sarvāṇi sarvākārāṇi tāni kuśalamūlāni dānādikāni samādāya vartate / tatra kālābhedo yadbodhisattvaḥ satatasamitamanirākṛtaprayogo 'nikṣiptadhuro rātrau ca divā vā dṛṣṭe vā dharme tenaiva ca hetunā 'bhisaṃparāye 'pi tāni dānādīni kuśalamūlāni samudācarati / tatra caturbhirākārairasaṃkliṣṭatā veditavyā / iha bodhisattvo muditacittaḥ tān kuśalān dharmānniṣevate na duḥkhī na durmanā avipratisārī bhavati tato nidānam / punarbodhisattvaḥ paramanapahatya dṛṣṭigatānyanabhiniviśya duścaritenāvyāmiśrāṇi tāni kuśalamūlāni dānādikāni samudācarati / punarbodhisattvaḥ satkṛtya sarvātmanā teṣveva guṇadarśī sāradarśī śāntadarśī suniścito 'parapratyayo 'nanyaneyaḥ tān kuśalān dharmān dānādīn samādāya vartate / punarbodhisattvo na terṣā dānādīnāṃ kuśalānāṃ dharmāṃṇāṃ vipākaṃ pratikāṃkṣate cakravartitvaṃ vā śakratvaṃ vā māratvaṃ vā brahmatvaṃ vā nāpi parataḥ pratikāraṃ pratyāśaṃsate / na tatra niśrito bhavati / na sarvalābhasatkāraślokeṣu nāpyantataḥ kāyajīvite 'pi niśrito bhavati / iti ya ebhirākāraiḥ prasādaprāmodyasahagataścāviṣamaśca satkṛtya cāniśritaśca dānādīnāṃ samānārthatāparyavasānānāṃ
body.translated_text: The conduct through body, speech, and mind should be understood. And due to magnanimity and non-defilement, excellence, unsurpassedness, and uncommonness should be understood. There, magnanimity should be understood in terms of non-differentiation of beings, non-differentiation of objects, and non-differentiation of time. There, non-differentiation of beings means that the <s>Bodhisattva</s>, having taken all beings as his basis and commencing from all beings, practices those wholesome roots such as generosity (<s>dāna</s>) and the rest — not merely for the sake of himself alone. There, non-differentiation of objects means that the <s>Bodhisattva</s>, having undertaken all wholesome roots of every kind — generosity and the rest — abides [in them]. There, non-differentiation of time means that the <s>Bodhisattva</s>, with constant, uninterrupted application, not laying down the burden, by night and by day, both in the present life and by that very cause in future lives as well, practices those wholesome roots such as generosity and the rest. There, non-defilement should be understood through four aspects. Here, the <s>Bodhisattva</s>, with a joyful mind, cultivates those wholesome <s>dharmas</s> — he is neither suffering nor dejected, and is free from remorse on that account. Furthermore, the <s>Bodhisattva</s>, without disparaging others, without clinging to wrong views, and unmixed with misconduct, practices those wholesome roots such as generosity and the rest. Furthermore, the <s>Bodhisattva</s>, with reverence, with his whole being, seeing only virtue in them, seeing their essence, seeing their peace, firmly resolved, not dependent on others, not led astray by others, undertakes those wholesome <s>dharmas</s> — generosity and the rest — and abides [in them]. Furthermore, the <s>Bodhisattva</s> does not expect the ripening of those wholesome <s>dharmas</s> such as generosity and the rest — neither <s>Cakravartin</s>-ship, nor <s>Śakra</s>-ship, nor <s>Māra</s>-ship, nor <s>Brahmā</s>-ship — nor does he expect reciprocation from others. He is not attached thereto. He is not attached to any gain, honor, or fame, nor even ultimately to his own body or life. Thus, one whose practice of wholesome <s>dharmas</s> such as generosity and the rest — culminating in equal benefit [for all] — is accompanied by these aspects of faith and delight, is impartial, is reverential, and is unattached

body.text: kuśalānāṃ dharmāṇāṃ samudācāraḥ / sā eṣāmasaṃkliṣṭatetyucyate / viśuddhiruttaptatā acalatā suviśuddhatā ca veditavyā / tatrāśaya śuddhibhūmipraviṣṭasya bodhisattvasya uttaptānyacalāni caitāni kuśalamūlāni bhavanti / tatreyamuttaptatā yadāśayaśuddhasya bodhisattvasya sarve te kuśalā dharmā apratisaṃkhyānakaraṇīyā bhavanti / tatreyamacalanatā yadāśayaśuddho bodhisattvo yathā pratilabdhebhyo yathopacitebhyaśca ebhyaḥ kuśalebhyo dharmebhyo na parihīyate / na bhavyo bhavatyāyatyāṃ parihāṇāya / nānyatra teṣāṃ teṣāṃ rātridivānāmatyayātteṣāṃ teṣāmātmabhāvānāṃ samatikramāccandro vā śuklapakṣe pratyupasthite vardhata eva ebhiḥ kuśalairdharmairna [pari]hīyate bodhisattvaḥ niṣṭhāgamanabhūmibyavasthitasya punarbodhisattvasyaikajātipratibaddhasya caramabhavikasya vā ete kuśalā dharmāḥ suviśuddhā veditavyā yeṣāmuttari bodhisattvabhūmau pariśuddhataratā nāsti / evaṃ tribhiḥ kāraṇaireṣāṃ kuśalānāṃ dharmāṇāṃ samudācāraḥ / dvābhyāṃ kāraṇābhyāṃ śreṣṭhatā / tribhiḥ kāraṇaiḥ suviśuddhatā veditavyā dānādīnāṃ samānarthatāvasānānām /
body.translated_text: — that is called their non-defilement. Purity, refinement, immovability, and supreme purity should be understood. There, for the <s>Bodhisattva</s> who has entered the stage of purity of intention (<s>āśayaśuddhibhūmi</s>), these wholesome roots are refined and immovable. There, this is the refinement: for the <s>Bodhisattva</s> of pure intention, all those wholesome <s>dharmas</s> become effortless, requiring no deliberate effort. There, this is the immovability: the <s>Bodhisattva</s> of pure intention does not decline from those wholesome <s>dharmas</s> that have been obtained and accumulated. He is not capable of future decline. Just as the moon in the bright fortnight, with the passing of each successive day and night and the succession of each successive bodily existence, only waxes — so the <s>Bodhisattva</s> does not decline in these wholesome <s>dharmas</s> but [only increases]. Furthermore, for the <s>Bodhisattva</s> established on the final stage, or for one whose [next] birth is the last, or one in his final existence — these wholesome <s>dharmas</s> should be understood as supremely pure, beyond which there is no higher purity on the <s>Bodhisattva</s> stages. Thus, through three causes, there is the practice of these wholesome <s>dharmas</s>; through two causes, their excellence; and through three causes, their supreme purity should be understood — [all this] for generosity and the rest, culminating in equal benefit [for all].

body.text: tatra sarvadānasya sarvaśīlasya vistareṇa yāvatsarvasamānarthatāyā āsevitāyāḥ suviśodhitāyāḥ sakalasaṃpūrṇāyā anuttarā samyaksaṃbodhirvajrasāraśarīratā saddharmacirasthitikatā ca phalamabhinirvartate / tatra duṣkaradānena duṣkaraśīlena yāvadduṣkarasamānārthatayā āsevitayā suviśodhitayā tathāgatasyāpratisamāścaryādbhutadharmasamanvāgatatvaṃ phalamabhinirvartate / tatra sarvatomukhena dānena sarvatomukhena śīlena vistareṇa yāvatsarvatomukhayā samānārthatayā tathāgatasya sarvataḥ pradhānasattvairdevamanuṣyaiḥ pūjyatvaṃ phalamabhinivartate / tatra satpuruṣadānasya satpuruṣaśīlasya yāvatsatpuruṣasamānārthatāyāḥ tathāgatasya ye kecitsattvā apadā vā [dvipadā vā] catuṣpadā vā bahupadā vā rūpiṇo vā 'rūpiṇo vā saṃjñino vāsaṃjñino vā naivasaṃjñānāsaṃjñāyatanopagā vā [teṣāṃ] sarveṣāṃ sattvānāmagryatvaṃ phalamabhinirvartate / tatra sarvākārasya dānasya [sarvākārasya] śīlasya vistareṇa yāvatsarvākārāyāḥ samānārthatāyāstathāgatasyāprameyavicitrapuṇyaparigṛhītaṃ dvātriṃśanmahāpuruṣalakṣaṇāśītyanuvyañjanakāyatā phalamabhinirvartate /
body.translated_text: There, through all generosity, all moral conduct, and in detail up to all equal benefit, when cultivated, well-purified, and complete in all aspects, the fruit that is produced is unsurpassed perfect awakening, a <s>vajra</s>-like body, and the long endurance of the True <s>Dharma</s>. There, through difficult generosity, difficult moral conduct, and in detail up to difficult equal benefit, when cultivated and well-purified, the fruit that is produced is the <s>Tathāgata</s>'s possession of incomparable, marvelous, and wondrous qualities. There, through all-embracing generosity, all-embracing moral conduct, and in detail up to all-embracing equal benefit, the fruit that is produced is the <s>Tathāgata</s>'s being worthy of worship by all principal beings — gods and humans — in every direction. There, through the generosity of a good person, the moral conduct of a good person, and up to the equal benefit of a good person, the fruit that is produced is the <s>Tathāgata</s>'s supremacy among all beings — whether footless, two-footed, four-footed, or many-footed, whether with form or formless, whether with perception, without perception, or in the sphere of neither-perception-nor-non-perception. There, through all-aspect generosity, all-aspect moral conduct, and in detail up to all-aspect equal benefit, the fruit that is produced is the <s>Tathāgata</s>'s body adorned with the thirty-two marks of a great person (<s>mahāpuruṣalakṣaṇa</s>) and eighty secondary marks (<s>anuvyañjana</s>), embraced by immeasurable and varied merit.

body.text: tatra vighātārthikadānasya vighātārthikaśīlasya vistareṇa yāvadvighātārthikasamānārthatāyāḥ tathāgatasya bodhimaṇḍa niṣaṇṇasya sarvamārapratyarthikavidhātāviheṭhāvikampanāpratibalanatā phalamabhinirvartate / tatrehāmutrasukhasya dānasya ihāmutrasukhasya śīlasya vistareṇa yāvadihāmutrasukhāyāḥ samānārthatāyāstathāgatasya paramadhyānavimokṣasamādhisamāpattisukhaṃ phalamabhinirvartate / tatra viśuddhasya dānasya viśuddhasya śīlasya vistareṇa yāvadviśuddhāyāḥ samānārthaṃtāyā āsevitāyāḥ suviśodhitāyāḥ sakalasaṃpūrṇayāstathāgatasya sarvākārāścatasraḥ pariśuddhayaḥ āśrayapariśuddhirālambanapariśuddhiścittapariśuddhirjñānapariśuddhiḥ phalamabhinirvartate / tathā trīṇyārakṣyāṇi daśabalavaiśāradyasmṛtyupasthāna-sarvāveṇikabuddhadharmaviśuddhiśca phalamabhinirvartate / idamasya bodhisattvasya dānādīnāṃ kuśalānāṃ dharmāṇāṃ paryantagataṃ phalaṃ niruttaram / anyaccāsyāpramāṇamiṣṭamanavadyaṃ bodhisattvacaryāsu saṃsarato veditavyam /
body.translated_text: There, through generosity for those in distress, moral conduct for those in distress, and in detail up to equal benefit for those in distress, the fruit that is produced is the <s>Tathāgata</s>'s inability to be overcome, harassed, shaken, or overpowered by all opposing forces of <s>Māra</s> while seated at the seat of awakening (<s>bodhimaṇḍa</s>). There, through generosity that brings happiness here and hereafter, moral conduct that brings happiness here and hereafter, and in detail up to equal benefit that brings happiness here and hereafter, the fruit that is produced is the <s>Tathāgata</s>'s supreme bliss of <s>dhyāna</s>, liberation (<s>vimokṣa</s>), <s>samādhi</s>, and <s>samāpatti</s>. There, through pure generosity, pure moral conduct, and in detail up to pure equal benefit, when cultivated, well-purified, and complete in all aspects, the fruit that is produced is the <s>Tathāgata</s>'s four purities in all their aspects: purity of basis (<s>āśrayapariśuddhi</s>), purity of object (<s>ālambanapariśuddhi</s>), purity of mind (<s>cittapariśuddhi</s>), and purity of knowledge (<s>jñānapariśuddhi</s>). Likewise, the fruit that is produced is the three things that need no guarding, the Ten Powers (<s>daśabala</s>), the Fearlessnesses (<s>vaiśāradya</s>), the Foundations of Mindfulness (<s>smṛtyupasthāna</s>), and the purity of all the exclusive <s>Buddha</s>-<s>dharmas</s>. This is the ultimate, unsurpassed fruit of the <s>Bodhisattva</s>'s wholesome <s>dharmas</s> such as generosity and the rest. And other immeasurable, desirable, and blameless [fruits] should be understood [as accruing] while wandering in <s>saṃsāra</s> during the <s>Bodhisattva</s> practices.

body.text: iti bodhisattvabhūmāvādhāre yogasthāne pañcadaśamaṃ saṃgrahavastupaṭalam /
body.translated_text: Thus, in the <s>Bodhisattvabhūmi</s>, in the Foundation section of the Yoga Place, the fifteenth chapter on the Means of Gathering (<s>Saṃgrahavastu-paṭala</s>) is completed.

children.translated_text: <s>Pūjāsevāpramāṇa-paṭala</s> (Chapter on Worship, Service, and the Immeasurables)

body.text: uddānam /
body.translated_text: The summary verse (<s>uddāna</s>):

body.text: ratna-pūjā mitra-sevā apramāṇaiśca paścimam /
body.translated_text: Worship of the [Three] Jewels (<s>ratna</s>), service of [spiritual] friends (<s>mitra</s>), and lastly the immeasurables (<s>apramāṇa</s>).

body.text: tatra bodhisattvasya tathāgateṣu tathāgata-pūjā katamā / sā sāmāsato daśavidhā veditavyā / śarīra-pūjā caitya-pūjā sammukha-pūjā vimukha-pūjā svayaṃkṛta-pūjā para-kārita-pūjā lābha-satkāra-pūjā udāra-pūjā asaṃkliṣṭapūjā pratipatti-pūjā ca /
body.translated_text: There, what is the <s>Bodhisattva</s>'s worship of <s>Tathāgatas</s> (<s>tathāgata-pūjā</s>)? In brief, it should be understood as tenfold: bodily worship (<s>śarīra-pūjā</s>), <s>caitya</s>-worship (<s>caitya-pūjā</s>), face-to-face worship (<s>sammukha-pūjā</s>), in-absence worship (<s>vimukha-pūjā</s>), self-performed worship (<s>svayaṃkṛta-pūjā</s>), worship performed through others (<s>parakārita-pūjā</s>), worship with gains and honors (<s>lābhasatkāra-pūjā</s>), magnificent worship (<s>udāra-pūjā</s>), undefiled worship (<s>asaṃkliṣṭa-pūjā</s>), and worship through practice (<s>pratipatti-pūjā</s>).

body.text: tatra yadbodhisattvaḥ sākṣāt tathāgata-rūpa-kayameva pūjayati / iyamasyocyate śarīra pūjā /
body.translated_text: There, when the <s>Bodhisattva</s> worships the actual physical body (<s>rūpakāya</s>) of the <s>Tathāgata</s> directly — this is called his bodily worship (<s>śarīra-pūjā</s>).

body.text: tatra yadbodhisattvastathāgatamuddisya stūpaṃ vā gahaṃ vā kūṭaṃ vā purāṇacaitya vā abhinava-caityaṃ vā pūjayati / iyamasyocyate caitya-pūjā /
body.translated_text: There, when the <s>Bodhisattva</s>, in dedication to the <s>Tathāgata</s>, worships a <s>stūpa</s>, a shrine (<s>gaha</s>), a pinnacled hall (<s>kūṭa</s>), an ancient <s>caitya</s>, or a newly-built <s>caitya</s> — this is called his <s>caitya</s>-worship.

body.text: yad bodhisattvastathāgata-kāya vā tathāgata-caityaṃ vā sammukhībhūtamadhyakṣa pūjayati / iyamasya sammukha-pūjetyucyate /
body.translated_text: When the <s>Bodhisattva</s> worships the <s>Tathāgata</s>'s body or a <s>Tathāgata</s>-<s>caitya</s> that is present before him, face to face — this is called his face-to-face worship (<s>sammukha-pūjā</s>).

body.text: tatra yad bodhisattvastathāgate vā tathāgate-caitye vā sammukha-pūjāṃ kurvannevamadhyāśaya-sahagataṃ prasāda-sahagataṃ cittamabhisaṃskaroti / yā ekasya tathāgatasya dharmatā sā sarveṣāṃ tathāgatānāmatītānāgatapratyutpannānāṃ dharmatā / yā ekasya tathāgata-caityasya dharmatā sā sarveṣāṃ tathāgata-caityānāṃ dharmatā / ityato 'hametañca sammukhībhūtaṃ tathāgataṃ pūjayāmi sarvāṃśca tān atītānāgatapratyutpannāṃśca tathāgatān pūjayāmi / etacca sammukhībhūta tathāgata-caityaṃ pūjayāmi / tadanyāni ca daśasu dikṣvanantāparyanteṣu lokadhātuṣu sarvāṇi stūpāni gahāni kūṭāgārāṇi purāṇa-caityāni abhinava-caityāni pūjayāmi / itīyaṃ tāvad bodhisattvasya sādhāraṇā sammukhā /
body.translated_text: There, when the <s>Bodhisattva</s>, while performing face-to-face worship of a <s>Tathāgata</s> or a <s>Tathāgata</s>-<s>caitya</s>, forms such a mental resolution accompanied by deep conviction and faith: 'The nature (<s>dharmatā</s>) of one <s>Tathāgata</s> is the nature of all <s>Tathāgatas</s> — past, future, and present. The nature of one <s>Tathāgata</s>-<s>caitya</s> is the nature of all <s>Tathāgata</s>-<s>caityas</s>. Therefore, I worship this <s>Tathāgata</s> present before me and I worship all those <s>Tathāgatas</s> — past, future, and present. I worship this <s>Tathāgata</s>-<s>caitya</s> present before me, and I worship all the <s>stūpas</s>, shrines, pinnacled halls, ancient <s>caityas</s>, and newly-built <s>caityas</s> in the infinite and boundless world-systems in the ten directions.' — This, then, is the <s>Bodhisattva</s>'s combined face-to-face

body.text: vimukhā ca tathāgata-pūjā tathāgata-caitya-pūjā ca veditavyā / yatpunarbodhisattvaḥ asammukhībhūte tathāgate tathāgata-caitye vā tathāgatacittamabhisaṃskṛtya
body.translated_text: and in-absence worship of <s>Tathāgatas</s> and <s>Tathāgata</s>-<s>caityas</s>, which should be understood [as follows]. Furthermore, when the <s>Bodhisattva</s>, in the absence of the <s>Tathāgata</s> or the <s>Tathāgata</s>-<s>caitya</s>, having formed a mental image of the <s>Tathāgata</s>

body.text: pūjāṃ prayojayati sarvabuddhānuddiśya sarvatathāgatacaityāni coddiśya / sāsya kevalā vimukhaiva pūjā veditavyā / yadapi bodhisattvaḥ parinirvṛte tathāgate tathāgatamuddiśya tathāgatasya śarīraṃ stūpaṃ vā kārayati gahaṃ vā kūṭaṃ vā ekaṃ vā dvau vā sambahulāni vā yāvat koṭi-śatasahasrāṇi yathāśakti-yathābalam / iyamapi bodhisattvasya tathāgateṣu vimukhā vipulā pūjā apramāṇa-puṇya-phalā 'nekabrāhmapuṇyaparigṛhītā / yathā bodhisattvaḥ anekaireva kalpai[rmahākalpai]ravinipātagāmī bhavati / na cānuttarāyāḥ samyaksaṃbodheḥ sambhāraṃ na paripūrayati tannidānam / tatra yeyaṃ bodhisattvasya kevalaiva tathāgate tathāgatacaitye vā pūjā iyameva tāvadvipulapuṇyaphalā draṣṭavyā tato vipulatarapuṇyaphalā kevalaiva vimukhā draṣṭavyā / tato vipulatamapuṇyaphalā sādhāraṇasamsukhavimukhā pūjā draṣṭavyā /
body.translated_text: offers worship directed toward all <s>Buddhas</s> and toward all <s>Tathāgata</s>-<s>caityas</s> — that should be understood as his exclusively in-absence worship. Furthermore, when the <s>Bodhisattva</s>, after the <s>Tathāgata</s>'s <s>parinirvāṇa</s>, in dedication to the <s>Tathāgata</s>, has a <s>stūpa</s>, a shrine, or a pinnacled hall built for the <s>Tathāgata</s>'s relics — one, two, many, or up to hundreds of thousands of <s>koṭīs</s>, according to his ability and power — this too is the <s>Bodhisattva</s>'s in-absence, vast worship of <s>Tathāgatas</s>, bearing the fruit of immeasurable merit, embraced by merit of many <s>Brahmā</s>-[worlds]. It is such that the <s>Bodhisattva</s>, for many <s>kalpas</s> and great <s>kalpas</s>, becomes one who does not fall into lower rebirths, and on account of it, does not fail to fulfill the accumulation toward unsurpassed perfect awakening. There, that which is the <s>Bodhisattva</s>'s merely face-to-face worship of the <s>Tathāgata</s> or <s>Tathāgata</s>-<s>caitya</s> alone — this much should be seen as bearing vast meritorious fruit. More vastly meritorious than that should be seen the exclusively in-absence worship. And most vastly meritorious of all should be seen the combined face-to-face and in-absence worship.

body.text: tatra yad bodhisattvastathāgate vā tathāgatacaitye vā pūjāṃ kartukāmaḥ svayameva svahastaṃ karoti na dāsīdāsakarmaṃkara-[pauruṣeya-]mitrāmātyajñātisālohitaiḥ kārayatyālasyakausīdyaṃ pramādasthānaṃ vā niśritya / iyaṃ bodhisattvasya svayaṃkṛtā pūjā veditavyā / tatra yadbodhisattvastathāgate vā tathāgatacaitye vā pūjāṃ kartukāmo na kevalaṃ svayeva karotyapi tu mātāpitṛbhyāṃ kārayati putradāreṇa dāsīdāsakarmakarapauruṣeyairmitrāmātyajñātisālohitaiḥ paraiśca rājabhiḥ rājamahāmātrairbrāhmaṇaigṛhapatibhirnaigamairjānapadairdhanibhiḥ śreṣṭhabhiḥ sārthavāhairantataḥ strīpuruṣadārakadārikābhiḥ kṛpaṇaiduḥkhitaira ā-caṇḍālairapi kārayati / tathā 'cāryopādhyāyaiḥ sārdhavihāryantevāsibhiḥ sabrahmacāribhiśca pravrajitairapyanyatīrthyaistathāgate [vā tathāgata-]caitye vā pūjāṃ kārayati / iyaṃ bodhisattvasya sādhāraṇā pūjā svaparakṛtā veditavyā /
body.translated_text: There, when the <s>Bodhisattva</s>, wishing to worship a <s>Tathāgata</s> or a <s>Tathāgata</s>-<s>caitya</s>, performs it himself with his own hands, and does not have it done by servants, slaves, workers, employees, friends, ministers, relatives, or kinsmen out of laziness, indolence, or heedlessness — this should be understood as the <s>Bodhisattva</s>'s self-performed worship (<s>svayaṃkṛtā pūjā</s>). There, when the <s>Bodhisattva</s>, wishing to worship a <s>Tathāgata</s> or a <s>Tathāgata</s>-<s>caitya</s>, not only performs it himself but also has it performed by his mother and father, by his wife and children, by servants, slaves, workers, and employees, by friends, ministers, relatives, and kinsmen, and by others — kings, chief ministers, <s>brāhmaṇas</s>, householders, townspeople, countryfolk, the wealthy, guild-masters, caravan-leaders, and even by women, men, boys, and girls, by the poor and miserable, down to <s>caṇḍālas</s> — and likewise has worship of the <s>Tathāgata</s> or <s>Tathāgata</s>-<s>caitya</s> performed by teachers, preceptors, co-residents, pupils, fellow practitioners, and even by non-Buddhist renunciants — this should be understood as the <s>Bodhisattva</s>'s combined worship, performed by both self and others.

body.text: yatpunarbodhisattvaḥ parītte pūjākaraṇīye deyavastuni saṃvidyamāne karuṇāsahagatena cetasā saṃcintya pareṣāmeva tadvastvanuprayacchatyete duḥkhitāḥ sattvā alpapuṇyāścāśaktāśca tathāgate vā tathāgatacaitye vā kārāṃ kṛtvā sukhitā bhavantviti / pare ca tena vastunā tathāgate vā tathāgatacaitye vā pūjāṃ kurvanti na bodhisattvaḥ iyaṃ bodhisattvasya kevalā parakāritā pūjā veditavyā /
body.translated_text: Furthermore, when there is only a small, worship-worthy object to give, the <s>Bodhisattva</s>, with a mind accompanied by compassion, deliberately gives that object to others [thinking:] 'May these suffering beings who have little merit and are unable, having made an offering to the <s>Tathāgata</s> or to a <s>Tathāgata</s>'s shrine, become happy.' And others, with that object, make offerings to the <s>Tathāgata</s> or the <s>Tathāgata</s>'s shrine, not the <s>Bodhisattva</s> himself. This is to be known as the <s>Bodhisattva</s>'s exclusively other-caused worship.

body.text: tatra yā kevalā svayaṃkṛtā sā mahāpuṇyaphalā / yā kevalā parakāritā sā mahattarapuṇyaphalā / yā punaḥ sādhāraṇā yā mahattamapuṇyaphalā niruttarā veditavyā /
body.translated_text: Therein, that which is exclusively self-performed is of great merit as its fruit. That which is exclusively other-caused is of greater merit as its fruit. But that which is shared is to be known as of the greatest merit as its fruit—unsurpassed.

body.text: tatra yadbodhisattvaḥ tathāgate vā tathāgatacaitye vā cīvarapiṇḍapātaśayanāsanaglānapratyayabhaiṣajyapariṣkārairabhivādanavandanapratyutthānāñjalikarmabhiśca dhūpagandhaiścūrṇagandhairanulepanagandhairvicitraiśca mālyairvicitrairvādyai rvicitraiśchatradhvajapatākāpradīpadānairvicitraiḥ stotrābhivyāhāraiḥ pañcamaṇḍalapraṇāmaiḥ pradakṣiṇāvartaiḥ pūjāṃ karoti / tathā 'kṣayaṇikāpradānaiḥ maṇimuktāvaidūryaśaṃkhaśilāpravāḍāśmagarbhamusāragalvajātarūparajatalohitikā-dakṣiṇāvartaprabhṛtibhiḥ ratnapradānairmaṇikuṇḍalakeyūrādyalaṅkārapradānairantataśca ghaṇṭāpradānakārṣāpaṇa-kṣepasūtrapariveṣṭanaiḥ pūjayati / iyaṃ bodhisattvasya tathāgate vā tathāgatacaitye vā lābhasatkārapūjā veditavyā /
body.translated_text: Therein, when the <s>Bodhisattva</s> makes offerings to the <s>Tathāgata</s> or to a <s>Tathāgata</s>'s shrine with robes, alms-food, lodging, and medicine for the sick, as well as with salutations, prostrations, rising [from one's seat], and the gesture of joined palms (<s>añjali</s>); with incense fragrances, powder fragrances, and ointment fragrances; with various garlands, various musical instruments, various offerings of umbrellas, banners, flags, and lamps; with various utterances of praise; with prostrations to the five points [of the body]; and with circumambulations—and likewise with offerings of imperishable gifts, with gifts of jewels such as gems, pearls, <s>vaiḍūrya</s>, conch shells, crystal, coral, emerald, <s>musāragalva</s>, gold, silver, and right-spiraling [conch]; with gifts of ornaments such as gem-earrings, armlets, and so forth; and even with gifts of bells, the casting of coins, and the wrapping of threads—this is to be known as the <s>Bodhisattva</s>'s worship of gain and honor toward the <s>Tathāgata</s> or the <s>Tathāgata</s>'s shrine.

body.text: tatra yadbodhisattvo dīrghakālikīñca tathāgate vā tathāgatacaitye vā etāmeva lābhasatkārapūjāṃ karoti prabhūtavastukāñca praṇītavastukāñca sammukhavimukhāñca svayaṃkṛtaparakṛtāñca ghanarasena ca prasādena sammukhībhūtena tīvrayā cādhimuktyā pūjāṃ karoti / tacca kuśalamūlamanuttarāyai samyaksaṃbodhaye pariṇāmayati / iyaṃ bodhisattvasya saptākārā udārapūjetyucyate /
body.translated_text: Therein, when the <s>Bodhisattva</s> performs this very worship of gain and honor toward the <s>Tathāgata</s> or the <s>Tathāgata</s>'s shrine over a long period, with abundant materials, with excellent materials, both in person and in absence, both self-performed and other-caused, with dense essence of faith directly present, and with intense conviction; and dedicates that wholesome root toward unsurpassed perfect awakening—this is called the <s>Bodhisattva</s>'s sevenfold noble worship.

body.text: tatra yadbodhisattvaḥ svahastaṃ tathāgate vā tathāgatacaitye vā kārāṃ karoti na parairavajñayā kārayati pramādakausīdyādvā / satkṛtya karoti / nāpaviddhamavikṣiptacittaḥ karotyasaṃkliṣṭacittaḥ / na buddhābhiprasannānāṃ rājādīnāmudārasattvānāṃ lābhasatkārahetoḥ kuhanārthaṃ pratirūpeṇa ca vastunā pūjayati / na haritāla-lepana-dhṛtasnāna-gugguludhūpārkapuṣpādibhiranyaiścākalpikairupakaraṇaiḥ / iyaṃ bodhisattvasya ṣaḍākārā 'saṃkliṣṭā pūjā veditavyā /
body.translated_text: Therein, when the <s>Bodhisattva</s> performs the offering to the <s>Tathāgata</s> or the <s>Tathāgata</s>'s shrine with his own hands, and does not have it done by others through contempt, or through heedlessness and sloth; performs it with reverence; performs it not carelessly, with an undistracted, undefiled mind; does not worship for the sake of gain and honor from kings and noble beings who are devoted to the <s>Buddha</s>, with deception or with counterfeit objects; and does not use improper materials such as orpiment-paste, oil-bath, <s>guggulu</s>-incense, <s>arka</s>-flowers, and other unsuitable implements—this is to be known as the <s>Bodhisattva</s>'s sixfold undefiled worship.

body.text: tāṃ punaretāmudārāmasaṃkliṣṭāṃ lābhasatkārapūjāṃ bodhisattvastathāgate vā tathāgatacaitye vā svabāhubalopārjitairbhogaiḥ karoti parato vā paryeṣitaiḥ / ṣariṣkāravaśitā-pratilabdhairvā / tatra pariṣkāravaśitāprāpto bodhisattvaḥ dvau vā
body.translated_text: Furthermore, the <s>Bodhisattva</s> performs this noble, undefiled worship of gain and honor toward the <s>Tathāgata</s> or the <s>Tathāgata</s>'s shrine with possessions earned by the strength of his own arms, or obtained through seeking from others, or obtained through the mastery of magical creations. Therein, the <s>Bodhisattva</s> who has attained mastery of magical creations, having created two or—

body.text: trīnvā saṃbahulān vā samucchrayān yāvat samucchryakoṭīniyutaśatasahastrāṇyanekānyabhinirmāya sarvaistaiḥ samucchrayaistathāgateṣu praṇāmaṃ karoti / teṣāñca samucchrayāṇāmekaikasya hastaśataṃ hastasahasraṃ vā tato vā pareṇa nirmāya sarvaistairdivyasamatikrāntaiḥ kusumaiḥ paramasugandhibhiḥ paramamanoramaiḥ tāṃstathāgatānabhyavakirati / sarve ca te samucchrayā atyudārāṇi tathāgatabhūtaguṇopasaṃhitāni stotrāṇi bhāṣante / sarvaireva ca taiḥ samucchrayairvicitrāṇyamātrāṇi [agrāṇi] praṇītāni keyūramaṇikuṇḍalāni chatradhvajapatākāśca tathāgateṣūtsṛjayattyāropayati / iyamevaṃbhāgīyā pariṣkāravaśitā-prāptasya bodhisattvasya svacittapratibaddhā pūjā / na cāsya punarbuddhotpādaḥ pratyāśaṃsitavyaḥ prārthayitavyo vā bhavati / tatkasya hetoḥ / tathāhi tasyāvaivartikabhūmipraviṣṭatvāt sarvabuddhakṣetreṣvavyāhatā gatirbha vati / no cāpi bodhisattvasya svabāhubalopārjitā bhogā bhavantināpi ca parataḥ paryeṣitalabdhā vā / nāpi ca bodhisattvaḥ pariṣkāravaśitāprāpto bhavati / api tu yā kācit tathāgatapūjā jambūdvīpe [vā] cāturdvīpe vā sāhasre [vā dvisāhasre vā trisāhasra-]mahāsāhasre vā yāvaddaśasu dikṣvanantāparyanteṣu lokadhātuṣu mṛdumadhyādhimātrā pravartate / tāṃ sarvāṃ śrāddho bodhisattvaḥ prasādasahagatenodārādhimuktisahagatena cetasā spharitvābhyanumodate / iyamapi bodhisattvasyālpakṛcchreṇa mahatī apramāṇā tathāgatapūjā bodhāya mahāsaṃbhāraparigṛhītā yasyāṃ bodhisattvena satata-samitaṃ kalyāṇacittena hṛṣṭacittena yogaḥ karaṇīyaḥ / tatra yadbodhisattvaḥ stokastokaṃ muhūrtamuhūrtamantato godohamātramapi sarvasattva prāṇibhūteṣu maitracittaṃ bhāvayati / karuṇāsahagataṃ muditāsahagatamupekṣāsahagataṃ cittaṃ bhāvayati / tathā sarvasaṃskāreṣvanityasaṃjñāmanitye duḥkhasaṃjñāṃ duḥkhe 'nātmasaṃjñāṃ nirvāṇe cānuśaṃsasaṃjñāṃ bhāvayati / tathā tathāgatānusmṛtiṃ dharmasaṃghapāramitānusmṛtiṃ bhāvayati / tathā stokastokaṃ muhūrtamuhūrtaṃ sarvadharmāṇāṃ prādeśikena mṛdukṣāntikenāpi jñānena nirabhilāpyadharmasvabhāvatathatādhimukto nirvikalpena nirnimittena cetasā viharati / prāgeva tata uttari tato bhūyaḥ / tathā bodhisattvaśīlasaṃvaraparipālanā / śamathavipaśyanāyāṃ bodhipākṣikeṣu ca dharmeṣu yogakriyā / tathā pāramitāsu saṃgrahavastuṣu ca samyagyogakriyā / itīyaṃ bodhisattvasya pratipattisahagatā tathāgata pūjā 'gryāvarā
body.translated_text: three, or many, up to many ten-millions of hundreds of thousands of bodies, with all those bodies makes prostrations to the <s>Tathāgatas</s>. And for each of those bodies, having created hands of a hundred, a thousand, or more, he showers upon those <s>Tathāgatas</s> all those divine-surpassing flowers, supremely fragrant and supremely delightful. And all those bodies utter exceedingly noble praises connected with the true qualities of the <s>Tathāgata</s>. And with all those bodies he releases and places upon the <s>Tathāgatas</s> various immeasurable, foremost, and excellent armlets, gem-earrings, umbrellas, banners, and flags. Such is the worship of the <s>Bodhisattva</s> who has attained mastery of magical creations, dependent upon his own mind. And the arising of <s>Buddhas</s> need not be expected or wished for by him. For what reason? Because, having entered the irreversible stage (<s>avaivartikabhūmi</s>), his passage is unobstructed in all <s>Buddha</s>-fields. But when the <s>Bodhisattva</s> does not have possessions earned by his own strength, nor obtained through seeking from others, nor has he attained mastery of magical creations—whatever worship of the <s>Tathāgata</s> is being performed in <s>Jambudvīpa</s>, the four continents, the thousand-world system, [the two-thousand, or the great three-thousand-fold world system,] or in the infinite, boundless world-realms in the ten directions, whether mild, moderate, or intense—all of that the faithful <s>Bodhisattva</s>, pervading it with a mind accompanied by faith and noble conviction, rejoices in (<s>anumodana</s>). This too is the <s>Bodhisattva</s>'s great, immeasurable worship of the <s>Tathāgata</s> with little effort, encompassed by the great accumulation for awakening, in which the <s>Bodhisattva</s> should constantly and continuously engage with a wholesome mind and a joyful mind. Furthermore, when the <s>Bodhisattva</s>, little by little, moment by moment, even for the duration of a cow's milking, cultivates a mind of friendliness (<s>maitrī</s>) toward all beings and creatures; cultivates a mind accompanied by compassion (<s>karuṇā</s>), accompanied by sympathetic joy (<s>muditā</s>), and accompanied by equanimity (<s>upekṣā</s>); and likewise cultivates the perception of impermanence in all conditioned formations, the perception of suffering in the impermanent, the perception of non-self in suffering, and the perception of benefit in <s>nirvāṇa</s>; and likewise cultivates the recollection of the <s>Tathāgata</s>, the recollection of the <s>Dharma</s>, the <s>Saṃgha</s>, and the <s>pāramitās</s>; and likewise, little by little, moment by moment, with even a partial, mild, and patient knowledge of all <s>dharmas</s>, convinced of the <s>tathatā</s> (suchness) of the inexpressible nature of <s>dharmas</s>, abides with a non-conceptual, signless mind—and all the more beyond that. Likewise, the guarding of the <s>Bodhisattva</s>'s moral restraint; the practice of <s>śamatha</s> (calm) and <s>vipaśyanā</s> (insight) and the factors conducive to awakening; and likewise the correct practice of the <s>pāramitās</s> and the means of gathering [beings]—this is the <s>Bodhisattva</s>'s worship accompanied by practice of the <s>Tathāgata</s>, the foremost and supreme—

body.text: praṇītā niruttarā / yasyāḥ pūjāyāḥ pūrvikā lābhasatkārapūjā sarvākārāpi śatatamīmapi kalāṃ nopaiti sahasratamīmapi kalāṃ nopaiti vistareṇa yāvadupaniṣadamapi nopaiti / itīyaṃ daśabhirākāraiḥ sarvākārā tathāgatapūjā veditavyā /
body.translated_text: excellent and unsurpassed. Compared to this worship, the prior worship of gain and honor, even in its complete form, does not reach even a hundredth part, nor even a thousandth part, and in detail, does not even reach the fraction of a comparison. Thus this tenfold worship of the <s>Tathāgata</s> in all its aspects is to be understood.

body.text: yathā tathāgatapūjā evaṃ dharmapūjā saṃghapūjā yathāyogaṃ veditavyā /
body.translated_text: Just as the worship of the <s>Tathāgata</s>, so too the worship of the <s>Dharma</s> and the worship of the <s>Saṃgha</s> are to be understood as appropriate.

body.text: tatra triṣu ratneṣvetāṃ daśākārāṃ pūjāṃ kurvanbodhisattvastathāgatālambanaiḥ ṣaḍmiradhyāśayaiḥ karoti / guṇakṣetraniruttarādhyāśayatayā upakāriniruttarādhyāśayatayā 'padadvipadādisarvasattvāgryādhyāśayatayā udumbarapuṣpavat sudurlaṃbhā 'dhyāśayatayā ekākinastrisāhasrama sāhasre loka utpādātkevalādhyāśayatayā laukikalokottarasampatsarvārthaṃpratisaraṇādhyāśayatayā / tasyaibhiḥ ṣaḍbhiradhyāśayaiḥ tathāgate tasya vā dharme tasya vā saṃghe pūjā prakalpitā parīttāpyaprameyaphalā bhavanti prāgeva prabhūtā /
body.translated_text: Therein, the <s>Bodhisattva</s> who performs this tenfold worship toward the Three Jewels does so with six superior intentions (<s>adhyāśaya</s>) having the <s>Tathāgata</s> as their object: with the superior intention that he is an unsurpassed field of qualities; with the superior intention that he is an unsurpassed benefactor; with the superior intention that he is supreme among all beings including those without feet and those with two feet and so on; with the superior intention that he is as rare as the <s>udumbara</s> flower; with the superior intention that he alone arises in the great three-thousand-fold world system; and with the superior intention that he is the refuge for all purposes, both worldly and supramundane attainments. With these six superior intentions, the worship arranged toward the <s>Tathāgata</s>, his <s>Dharma</s>, or his <s>Saṃgha</s>—even if small—bears immeasurable fruit, how much more so when abundant.

body.text: tatra katibhirākāraiḥ samanvāgataṃ bodhisattvasya kalyāṇamitraṃ veditavyam / katibhiścākāraiḥ kalyāṇamitratā 'bandhyā bhavati / katibhikārāraiḥ samanvāgataṃ kalyāṇamitraṃ prasādapadasthānagataṃ bhavati / kati kalyāṇamitrabhūtasya [bodhisattvasya] vineyeṣu kalyāṇamitra-karaṇīyāni bhavanti / katividhā ca kalyāṇamitrasaṃsevā bodhisattvasya / katyākārayā ca saṃjñayā kalyāṇamitrasyāntikādbodhisattvena dharmaḥ śrotavyaḥ / katiṣu ca sthāneṣu kalyāṇamitrasyāntikād bodhisattvena dharmaṃ śruṇvatā tasmindharmabhāṇake pudgale 'manasikāraḥ karaṇīyaḥ /
body.translated_text: How many aspects should the <s>Bodhisattva</s>'s virtuous friend (<s>kalyāṇamitra</s>) be endowed with? By how many aspects is the function of a virtuous friend unfruitless? By how many aspects does the virtuous friend become a ground for faith? How many are the functions of a virtuous friend of a <s>Bodhisattva</s> toward those to be trained? How many kinds of association with a virtuous friend does the <s>Bodhisattva</s> have? With what kinds of perception should the <s>Bodhisattva</s> listen to the <s>Dharma</s> from the virtuous friend? In how many matters, when listening to the <s>Dharma</s> from the virtuous friend, should the <s>Bodhisattva</s> not pay attention to the person of the <s>Dharma</s>-speaker?

body.text: tatrāṣṭābhiraṅgaiḥ samanvāgataṃ bodhisattvasya kalyāṇamitraṃ sarvākāraparipūrṇaṃ veditavyam / vṛttastho bhavati bodhisattvasaṃvaraśīleṣu vyavasthito 'khaṇḍacchidrakārī / bahuśruto bhavati nāvyutpannabuddhiḥ / adhigamayuktaśca bhavati lābhī bhāvanāmayasyānyatamānyatamasya kuśalasya lāmī śamathavipaśyanāyāḥ / anukampakaśca bhavati kāruṇikaḥ so 'dhyupekṣya svaṃ dṛṣṭadharmaṃsukhavihāraṃ pareṣāmarthāya parayujyate / viśārado bhavati na pareṣāmasya dharmaṃ deśayataḥ smṛtiḥ pratibhānaṃ - va śāradyabhayāt pramuṣyate / kṣamaśca bhavati parato 'vamānanāvahasanāvaspandana durukta-durāga-tādīnāmaniṣṭānāṃ vacanspathānāṃ vividhānañca sattvavipratipattīnām / aparikhinnamānasaśca
body.translated_text: Therein, the <s>Bodhisattva</s>'s virtuous friend, endowed with eight qualities, is to be known as complete in all aspects. He is established in conduct, settled in the <s>Bodhisattva</s> moral restraint-precepts, making no breach or break. He is learned, not of undeveloped intelligence. He is endowed with realization, a gainer of some wholesome [attainment] born of cultivation, a gainer of <s>śamatha</s> (calm) and <s>vipaśyanā</s> (insight). He is compassionate and caring; setting aside his own pleasant abiding in this present life, he exerts himself for the welfare of others. He is confident; when teaching the <s>Dharma</s> to others, his mindfulness and ready wit are not lost through fear of shyness. He is patient with contempt, ridicule, mockery, harsh and hostile words, and various wayward behaviors from beings. He is of unwearied mind—

body.text: bhavati balavān pratisaṃkhyānabahulaḥ akilāsī catasṛṇāṃ pariṣadāṃ dharmadeśanāyai / kalyāṇavākyaśca bhavati vākkaraṇenopeto dharmatāpraṇaṣṭaspaṣṭavāk /
body.translated_text: strong, rich in discernment, and untiring in teaching the <s>Dharma</s> to the four assemblies. And he is of beautiful speech, endowed with the instrument of speech, with clear articulation true to the nature of reality.

body.text: tatra pañcabhirākāraireva sarvākāraguṇayuktasya bodhisattvasya kalyāṇamitrasyābandhyaṃ kalyāṇamitrakaraṇīyaṃ bhavati / sa hi pareṣāmādita eva hitasukhaiṣī bhavati / tacca hitasukhaṃ yathābhūtaṃ prajānāti / na tatra viparyastabuddhirbhavati / yena copāyena yadrupayā dharmadeśanayā yaḥ sattvaḥ śakyarūpo bhavati vinetuṃ tatra śakto bhavati pratibalaḥ / aparikhinnamānasaśca bhavati / samakāraṇyaśca bhavati / sarvasattveṣu hīnamadhyaviśiṣṭeṣu na pakṣapatitaḥ /
body.translated_text: Therein, by five aspects, the function of a virtuous friend of a <s>Bodhisattva</s> endowed with all aspects and qualities becomes unfruitless [i.e., never in vain]. For he is, from the very beginning, desirous of the welfare and happiness of others. And he truly understands that welfare and happiness; he does not have a mistaken understanding therein. And by whatever method, with whatever kind of <s>Dharma</s>-teaching, a given being is capable of being trained—in that he is capable and competent. He is of unwearied mind. He is impartial; toward all beings, inferior, middling, and superior, he does not take sides.

body.text: tatra pañcabhirākāraistatkalyāṇamitraṃ prasādapadasthitaṃ bhavati yenainaṃ pare 'tyarthamabhiprasīdantyanuśraveṇāpi śrutvā prāgeva sammukhaṃ nirīkṣya / īryāpathasaṃpanno bhavati praśānteryāpathaḥ sarvāṅgapratyaṅgainirvikāraḥ / sthito bhavatyanuddhataacapalakāyavāṅmanaḥkarmāntapracāraḥ / niṣkuhakaśca bhavati na pareṣāṃ kuhanārthamīryāpathaṃ sthairyaṃ vā pratisaṃkhyāya kalpayati / anīrṣukaśca bhavati na pareṣāṃ dharmyaṃ kathāṃ lābhasatkāraṃ vā ārabhyāmarṣamutpādayati / api tu svayamadhyeṣyamāṇo 'pi dharmakathane paraiḥ labhamāno 'pi vipulaṃ lābhasatkāraṃ paramapadiśati aśaṭhena cetasā prasannena / pareṣāṃ tacca dhārmakathikatvaṃ tañca lābhasatkāramārabhyānujanāti / yathā svena lābhasatkāreṇa tuṣṭo bhavati tathā bhṛśataraṃ paralābhena parasatkāreṇa tuṣṭo bhavati / [sumanāḥ] saṃlikhitaśca bhavatyalpabhāṇḍo 'lpapariṣkāraḥ utpannotpannaparityaktasarvopakaraṇaḥ /
body.translated_text: There, by five aspects that virtuous friend (<s>kalyāṇamitra</s>) stands in a position of inspiring faith, so that others are exceedingly inspired merely by hearing of him by reputation, much more so by seeing him face to face. One is endowed with proper deportment (<s>īryāpatha</s>), calm in conduct, with all limbs and minor limbs free from agitation. One is stable, with un-agitated, un-fickle conduct of body, speech, and mental activity. One is free from hypocrisy—one does not deliberately arrange one's deportment or composure for the purpose of deceiving others. One is free from jealousy—one does not generate resentment regarding others' <s>Dharma</s>-discourse or their gains and honors. Rather, even when personally requested for <s>Dharma</s>-discourse, or when others receive abundant gains and honors, one directs [beings] to others with an honest and serene mind. One approves of others' role as <s>Dharma</s>-teachers and of their gains and honors. Just as one is content with one's own gains and honors, even more so one is content with others' gains and others' honors. One is cheerful and refined, with few possessions and few requisites, relinquishing all equipment as it arises.

body.text: tatra pañcabhirākārairayaṃ kalyāṇamitrabhūto bodhisattvaḥ pareṣāṃ vineyānāṃ kalyāṇamitrakāryaṃ karoti / codako bhavati / smārako bhavati / avavādako bhavati / anuśāsako bhavati / dharmadeśako bhavati / eṣāñca padānāṃ vistareṇa vibhāgo veditavyaḥ / tadyathā śrāvakabhūmāvavavādānuśāsanañca bhūyastata uttari veditavyaṃ tadyathā balagotrapaṭale /
body.translated_text: There, by five aspects this <s>Bodhisattva</s> who has become a virtuous friend performs the duty of a virtuous friend for the disciples to be trained: one is an admonisher (<s>codaka</s>); one is a reminder (<s>smāraka</s>); one is an instructor (<s>avavādaka</s>); one is a guide (<s>anuśāsaka</s>); one is a teacher of the <s>Dharma</s> (<s>dharmadeśaka</s>). The detailed classification of these terms should be understood as in the <s>Śrāvakabhūmi</s> regarding instruction and guidance, and further beyond that as in the chapter on the Lineage of Powers.

body.text: tatra caturbhirākārairbodhisattvasya kalyāṇamitrasevā paripūrṇā veditavyā / kālena kālaṃ glānopasthānasvasthopasthāna kriyayā premagauravaprasādopasaṃhṛtayā /
body.translated_text: There, the <s>Bodhisattva</s>'s complete service to the virtuous friend should be understood through four aspects: from time to time, through the act of attendance on the sick and on the healthy, infused with affection, respect, and faith;

body.text: kālena kālamabhivādanavandanapratyutthānāñjalisāmicīkarmapūjākriyayā dharmacīvarapiṇḍapātaśayanāsanaglānapratyayabhaiṣajyapariṣkāradānapūjayā ca / niśritasya ca dhārmikeṣvarthasaṃyoga-viyogeṣu vaśavartanatayā avikampanatayā yathābhūtatvāviṣkaraṇatayā / kālena ca cājñāmiprāyasyopasaṃkramaṇaparyupāsanaparipṛcchanaśravaṇatayā /
body.translated_text: from time to time, through the act of salutation, veneration, rising from one's seat, gesture of joined palms, proper service, and worship; through the offering and worship of <s>Dharma</s>-robes, alms-food, bedding and seating, and requisites of medicine for the sick; through compliance and unshakeability regarding righteous gains and losses of the one relied upon, and through revealing things as they truly are; and from time to time, through approaching, attending upon, questioning, and listening to one who is knowledgeable.

body.text: tatra kalyāṇamitrasyāntikāddharmaṃ śrotukāmena bodhisattvena pañcākārayā saṃjñayā dharmaḥ śrotavyaḥ / ratnasaṃjñayā durlabhārthena / cakṣuḥsaṃjñayodārasahajaprajñāpratilābhāya hetubhāvārthena / ālokasaṃjñayā pratilabdhasahajajñānacakṣuṣā sarvākāra-yathābhūta-jñeyasaṃprakāśanārthena / mahāphalānuśaṃsasaṃjñayā nirvāṇasaṃbodhiniruttarapadaprāptihetubhāvārthena / anavadyaratisaṃjñayā dṛṣṭe dharme 'prāpta nirvāṇasaṃbodhidharmayathābhūtapravicayaśamathavipaśyanā 'navadyamahāratihetubhāvārthe /
body.translated_text: There, a <s>Bodhisattva</s> wishing to hear the <s>Dharma</s> from a virtuous friend should listen with a fivefold perception: with the perception of a jewel, because of its rarity; with the perception of an eye, because of its being a cause for obtaining noble innate wisdom; with the perception of light, because of its illuminating all that is knowable in all aspects as it truly is through the innate knowledge-eye once obtained; with the perception of great fruit and benefit, because of its being a cause for attaining <s>nirvāṇa</s>, awakening, and the unsurpassed state; and with the perception of blameless delight, because of its being a cause for the great blameless delight of investigating the <s>Dharma</s> as it truly is, calm and insight, in this very life even before attaining <s>nirvāṇa</s> and awakening.

body.text: tatra bodhisattvena kalyāṇamitrasyāntikāddharmaṃ śruṇvatā tasmindharmabhāṇake pudgale pañcasthāneṣvamanasikāraṃ kṛtvā 'vahitaśrotreṇa prasannamānasena dharmaḥ śrotavyaḥ / śīlabhraṃśe 'manasikāraḥ karaṇīyaḥ / naivaṃ cittamabhisaṃskartavyaṃ duḥśīlo 'yamasaṃvarasthaḥ nāhamataḥ śroṣyāmi / kulabhraṃśe 'pyamanasikāraḥ karaṇīyaḥ / naivaṃ cittamabhisaṃskartabyaṃ nīlakulo 'yaṃ nāhamataḥ śroṣyāmi / rūpabhraṃśe 'pyamanasikāraḥ karaṇīyaḥ / naivaṃ cittamabhisaṃskartavyaṃ virupo 'yaṃ nāhamataḥ śroṣyāmi / vyañjanabhraṃśe 'pyamanasikāraḥ karaṇīyaḥ / naivaṃ cittamabhisaṃskartavyam anabhisaṃskṛtavākyo 'yaṃ nāhamataḥ śroṣyāmi / nānyatrārthapratisaraṇena bhavitavyaṃ na vyañjanapratisaraṇena / mādhuryabhraṃśe 'pyamanasikāraḥ karaṇīyaḥ / naivaṃ cittamabhisaṃskartavyaṃ paruṣavākyoyaṃ krodhano na ca madhuraṃ dharmaṃ bhāṣate nāhamataḥ śroṣyāmīti / ityevaṃ pañcasu sthāneṣvamanasikāraṃ kṛtvā bodhisattvena sādareṇa saddharmaparigrahaḥ kāryo na jātu dharmaḥ pudgaladoṣeṇa duṣṭo bhavati / tatra yo 'sau mandaprajño bodhisattvaḥ pudgaladoṣeṣūpahatacitto dharmaṃ necchati śrotuṃ sa ātmana evāhitāya prajñāparihāṇāya pratipanno veditavyaḥ /
body.translated_text: And how should a <s>Bodhisattva</s>, when hearing the <s>Dharma</s> from a virtuous friend, listen with attentive ears and a serene mind, having disregarded five aspects regarding that <s>Dharma</s>-teacher? One should disregard a deficiency of moral conduct—one should not form the thought: 'This person is immoral and not established in restraint; I will not listen to him.' One should disregard a deficiency of family—one should not form the thought: 'This person is of low caste; I will not listen to him.' One should disregard a deficiency of appearance—one should not form the thought: 'This person is ugly; I will not listen to him.' One should disregard a deficiency of expression—one should not form the thought: 'This person's speech is unpolished; I will not listen to him.' One should take refuge in meaning, not in the letter. One should also disregard a deficiency of pleasantness—one should not form the thought: 'This person speaks harshly, is irascible, and does not teach the <s>Dharma</s> sweetly; I will not listen to him.' Thus, having disregarded these five aspects, the <s>Bodhisattva</s> should earnestly embrace the true <s>Dharma</s>. The <s>Dharma</s> is never corrupted by the faults of the person. There, a <s>Bodhisattva</s> of weak wisdom whose mind is affected by the faults of the person and who does not wish to listen to the <s>Dharma</s> should be understood as one who is proceeding toward harm for himself and toward the decline of wisdom.
