And beyond that, they do not seek any other intrinsic nature of it. Therefore <s>dharmas</s> are called equal to space (<s>ākāśasama</s>). Just as an illusion (<s>māyā</s>) does not exist as it appears, yet that which is created by illusion is not entirely non-existent in every respect; so too, these <s>dharmas</s> do not exist in the manner they appear through the force of verbal designation to the ignorant, yet they are not entirely non-existent in every respect, [being real] in their ultimate, inexpressible nature. And by this mode of entry, being neither existent nor non-existent, they are non-dual — like an illusion. Therefore they are called illusion-like (<s>māyopama</s>). Thus the <s>Bodhisattva</s> neither removes anything from the entire <s>dharmadhātu</s> (realm of reality) nor adds anything to it; he neither diminishes nor augments it; he does not destroy it. He knows what is real as it truly is. And he reveals it just as it is. This should be understood as the <s>Bodhisattva</s>'s conforming means.

body.text: tatra katamo bodhisattvasya vibandhasthāyī upāyaḥ iha bodhisattvo bhojanapānādi-daśa-kāyādipariṣkārārthikānāṃ [sattvānāṃ] vipratibandhenāvatiṣṭhate / sa cenmātṛjñā bhavatheti pitṛjñāḥ śrāmaṇyāḥ brāhmaṇyā vistareṇa pūrvavat yāvatsacecchīlaṃ samādāya vartadhve evamahaṃ yuṣmākaṃ bhojanapānādīn kāyapariṣkārānyāvadarthamanupradāsyāmi / anyathā na dāsyāmīti / tathā kṣetravastugṛhavastvāpaṇavastu-rājyavastu-deśavastu-dhanavastu-dhānyavastu arthikānāṃ
body.translated_text: There, what is the <s>Bodhisattva</s>'s obstacle-based means (<s>vibandhasthāyī upāya</s>)? Here, the <s>Bodhisattva</s> imposes an obstacle upon beings who seek food, drink, and the tenfold provisions for the body and so forth. [He says:] 'If you are grateful to your mothers,' — 'if to your fathers, if to <s>śramaṇas</s>, if to <s>brāhmaṇas</s>,' and so on in detail as before, up to — 'if you undertake and abide by moral conduct, then I will provide you with food, drink, and provisions for the body as needed. Otherwise I will not.' Likewise, to those who seek fields, houses, shops, kingdoms, territories, wealth, and grain

body.text: tathā śilpakarmasthānavidyārthikānāṃ tathā tena saha sakhyārthikānāmāvāhavivāhārthikānāmābhakṣaṇasaṃbhakṣaṇārthikānāṃ kṛtyasahāyārthikānāñca sattvānāṃ kāryavipratibandhenāvatiṣṭhate / evamahaṃ yuṣmākaṃ vistareṇa yāvatkṛtyeṣu sahāyībhāvaṃ gamiṣyāmi sa cenmātṛjñā bhavatheti pūrvavat / punarbodhisattvaḥ aparādhiṣu duṣiṣvapakāriṣu sattveṣu parairvadhabandhanacchedanatāḍanakutsanatarjanapravāsanāyopātteṣvādhamanabandhana-vikrayāya copātteṣu vipratibandhe nāvatiṣṭhate śaktaḥ pratibalaḥ / sa cenmātṛjñāḥ [pitṛjñā] bhavatheti vistareṇa pūrvavat evamahaṃ bhavato 'smādvyasanādvimocayiṣyāmīti / punarbodhisattvo rājacaurodakāgnimanuṣyāmanuṣyājīvikāślokādibhayabhītānāṃ sattvānāṃ vipratibandhenāvatiṣṭhate / sa cenmātṛjñā bhavatheti pūrvavat vistareṇaivamahaṃ bhavato 'smādbhayāt paritrāsyāmīti / punarbodhisattvaḥ priyasamāgamakāmānāṃ vāpriyaviyogakāmānāñca sattvānāṃ vipratibandhenāvatiṣṭhate / sa cenmātṛjñā bhavatha vistareṇa pūrvavat evamahaṃ bhavatāṃ priyasamāgamamapriyavinābhāvaṃ copasaṃhariṣyāmīti / punarbodhisattva ābādhikānāṃ sattvānāṃ vyādhitānāṃ vipratibandhenāvatiṣṭhate / sa cenmātṛjñā bhavatha vistareṇa pūrvavat evamahaṃ bhavato 'smādvyādhiduḥkhāt parimocayiṣyāmīti / te ca sattvāḥ evaṃ vibandhāvasthitasya bodhisattvasya laghuladhveva tasmin kuśalasamādāne pāpaprahāṇe ca yathākāmaṃ karaṇīyā bhavanti / ayaṃ bodhisattvasya vibandhasthāyī upāya ityucyate /
body.translated_text: ; likewise, to those who seek training in crafts and sciences; likewise, to those who seek friendship with him, those who seek marriage alliances, those who seek communal dining and fellowship, and those who seek companionship in tasks — the <s>Bodhisattva</s> imposes an obstacle in their affairs. [He says:] 'Thus I will, in detail, up to becoming a companion in your tasks — if you are grateful to your mothers,' and so on as before. Furthermore, the <s>Bodhisattva</s>, when beings who have transgressed, committed offenses, and caused harm have been seized by others for execution, imprisonment, cutting off [of limbs], beating, reviling, threatening, and banishment, or have been seized for enslavement, bondage, and sale — when he has the power and ability, he does not stand by as an obstacle [to their rescue, but instead says:] 'If you are grateful to your mothers [and fathers],' and so on in detail as before — 'thus I will liberate you from this calamity.' Furthermore, the <s>Bodhisattva</s> imposes an obstacle upon beings frightened by fears from kings, thieves, water, fire, humans, non-humans, loss of livelihood, loss of reputation, and so forth. [He says:] 'If you are grateful to your mothers,' and so on as before in detail — 'thus I will protect you from this fear.' Furthermore, the <s>Bodhisattva</s> imposes an obstacle upon beings who wish to meet with the beloved or to separate from the unbeloved. [He says:] 'If you are grateful to your mothers,' and so on in detail as before — 'thus I will bring about for you the meeting with the beloved and the separation from the unbeloved.' Furthermore, the <s>Bodhisattva</s> imposes an obstacle upon beings who are afflicted with illness and disease. [He says:] 'If you are grateful to your mothers,' and so on in detail as before — 'thus I will liberate you from this suffering of disease.' And those beings, when the <s>Bodhisattva</s> stands firm with these obstacles, quickly and easily become amenable to his wishes in that undertaking of wholesome [conduct] and abandonment of evil. This is called the <s>Bodhisattva</s>'s obstacle-based means.

body.text: ye punaḥ sattvā evaṃ vibandhasthāyino bodhisattvasya yathāparikīrtiteṣu vastuṣu na laghu-laghveva yathākāmaṃ pratipadyante teṣāṃ bodhisattvo yathā parikīrtitairvastubhirarthikānāṃ tāni vastūni nānuprayacchati hitakāmatayā / na cādātukāmāśayo bhavati / vyasanasthān bhītānpriyāpriyasaṃyogavisaṃyogakāmān vyādhiduḥkhena ārtān sattvān kañcitkālamadhyupekṣate hitakāmatayā / na copekṣaṇāśayo bhavati nāparitrāṇāśayaḥ / te ca sattvā evaṃ niṣṭhurakarmaṇā pratipadyamānasya bodhisattvasya na tvāśayataḥ apareṇa samayena yathākāmakaraṇīyā bhavanti pāpaprahāṇāya kuśalasamādānāya ca / ye ca sattvā nāpyarthino
body.translated_text: But those beings who, even when the <s>Bodhisattva</s> stands firm with obstacles as described, do not quickly and easily comply as he wishes in those matters — to those beings who seek the aforesaid things, the <s>Bodhisattva</s> does not provide those things, out of a desire for their welfare. And he has no intention of not giving. He overlooks for a time beings in calamity, in fear, those wishing to meet the beloved or part from the unbeloved, and those afflicted by the suffering of disease — out of a desire for their welfare. He has no intention of indifference, nor an intention of non-protection. And those beings, when the <s>Bodhisattva</s> acts with such stern conduct — though not in intention — at a later time become amenable to his wishes for the abandonment of evil and the undertaking of wholesome [conduct]. And those beings who are neither in need

body.text: bodhisattvasya nāpi ca vyasanasthā nāpi vistareṇa yāvadvyādhitāste cāsya saṃstutāḥ sapraṇayāḥ / tānapi bodhisattvastasminneva kuśala-[mūle] samādāpayati yaduta mātṛjñatāyāṃ vistareṇa yāvacchīlasamādānānuvartanāyām / ta evaṃ bodhisattvena samādāpyamānāḥ sa cedvikampanena [na] pratipadyante teṣāṃ bodhisattvaḥ kupitamapyātmānamupadarśayati hitakāmatayā / na cāśayataḥ kupito bhavati / kṛtyeṣu vaimukhyamupadarśayati hitakāmatayā / na cāśayato vimukho bhavati / tadekatvamapyasyānarthaṃ laukikamupasaṃharati hitakāmatayā / na cāśayato 'narthakāmo bhavati / visabhāgo 'sya bodhisattvasya teṣu [sattveṣu] tasyāśceṣṭāyāḥ sa āśayo bhavati / tena ca tānsattvāṃstasmin pāpaprahāṇe kuśalasamādāne ca sanniyojayati / tasmādayaṃ sattvavinayopāyo bodhisattvasya visabhāgāśaya ityucyate /
body.translated_text: of the <s>Bodhisattva</s>, nor in calamity, nor in detail up to being ill — but who are his intimates and dear ones — the <s>Bodhisattva</s> leads even them to undertake that very wholesome root, namely gratitude toward mothers, and so on in detail up to the observance of moral conduct. If, when being thus led by the <s>Bodhisattva</s>, they do not comply due to wavering, the <s>Bodhisattva</s> displays anger toward them — out of a desire for their welfare, though he is not actually angry in intention. He displays indifference to their affairs — out of a desire for their welfare, though he is not actually indifferent in intention. He even brings about some worldly misfortune for them — out of a desire for their welfare, though he has no actual intention of harming. The <s>Bodhisattva</s>'s intention is contrary to his outward conduct toward those beings. And through that [means], he yokes those beings to the abandonment of evil and the undertaking of wholesome [conduct]. Therefore this skillful means of disciplining beings is called the <s>Bodhisattva</s>'s contrary-intention means (<s>visabhāgāśaya</s>).

body.text: tatra katamo bodhisattvasyāvaṣṭambhaja upāyaḥ / iha bodhisattvaḥ svāmibhūto vā rājabhūto vā ādhipatyaprāptaḥ svaṃ vā parijanaṃ sva vā vijitamevaṃ samyak samanuśāsti / yo me kaścitparijane vā vijite vā 'mātṛjño bhaviṣyati vistareṇa yāvaddauśīlyaṃ samādāya vartiṣyate tasyāhamucitaṃ vā bhaktācchādanaṃ samucchetsyāmi vārayiṣyāmi vā tāḍayiṣyāmi vā sarvasvena vā viyojayiṣyāmi sarveṇa vā sarva vijitāt pravāsayiṣyāmīti / tatra ca karmaṇi kuśalān dakṣān pauruṣeyānviniyojayati / te ca sattvāstasmānmahato daṇḍakarmaṇo bhītāḥ pāpañca prajahati kuśalañca samādāya vartante / akāmakā api tena balāvaṣṭambhena kuśale sanniyojyante te sattvā anenopāyena / tasmādayamavaṣṭambhaja upāya ityucyate /
body.translated_text: There, what is the <s>Bodhisattva</s>'s compulsion-born means (<s>avaṣṭambhaja upāya</s>)? Here, the <s>Bodhisattva</s>, being a master or king who has obtained sovereignty, rightly admonishes his own retinue and his own domain thus: 'Whoever among my retinue or in my domain is ungrateful to his mother,' and so on in detail — 'up to whoever undertakes and abides in misconduct — I will cut off his rightful food and clothing, or I will prohibit him, or I will beat him, or I will deprive him of all his possessions, or I will banish him entirely from my domain.' And he appoints skilled, capable, and reliable officers to [enforce] that task. And those beings, frightened by that great punishment, abandon evil and undertake and abide in wholesome [conduct]. Even unwillingly, those beings are yoked to the wholesome through that compulsion. Therefore this is called the compulsion-born means.

body.text: tatra katamo bodhisattvasya kṛtapratikṛtika upāyaḥ / saha bodhisattvena yeṣāṃ sattvānāṃ pūrvamevopakāraḥ parīttaḥ prabhūto vā kṛto bhavati dānena vā vyasanaparitrāṇatayā
body.translated_text: There, what is the <s>Bodhisattva</s>'s action-and-reaction means (<s>kṛtaprakṛtika upāya</s>)? Those beings toward whom the <s>Bodhisattva</s> has previously performed some prior service — small or great — whether through giving, through protection from calamity

body.text: vā bhayaparitrāṇatayā vā priyāpriyasaṃyogavisayogopasaṃharaṇatayā vā vyādhisaśamanatayā vā teṣāṃ kṛtajñānāṃ kṛtavedināṃ pratyupakāra-kāmānāmantikādbodhisattvaḥ kuśalasamādānameva pratikārato yācate saṃpratīcchati / na kiñcidanyallokāmiṣam / evaṃ cāha / ayameva me bhavatāmantikānmahāpratyupakāro bhaviṣyati / sa cedyūyameva mātṛjñā bhavatha pitṛjñā vistareṇa yāvacchīlaṃ samādāya vartadhve kṛtasya pratikṛtaṃ kuśalasamādānaṃ parataḥ pratyāsaṃśate tena copāyena parāṃstatra kuśale samādāpayati / tasmādayamupāyaḥ kṛtipratikṛtika ityucyate /
body.translated_text: or through protection from danger, or through bringing about the union with the agreeable and separation from the disagreeable, or through the alleviation of disease—from those grateful and appreciative beings who desire to reciprocate, the <s>Bodhisattva</s> requests and accepts as reciprocation only the undertaking of wholesome [actions], not any worldly material gain. And one says thus: 'This alone will be the great reciprocation for me from you: if you yourselves become grateful to your mothers, grateful to your fathers'—and so on in detail—'up to: if you take up and practice moral conduct.' One expects the undertaking of the wholesome as reciprocation for what has been done, and by that means one establishes others in the wholesome. Therefore, this means is called 'the [means of] reciprocation for what has been done.'

body.text: tatra katamo bodhisattvasya viśuddha upāyaḥ / iha niṣṭhāgamana-bodhisattvabhūmi-sthito bodhisattvaḥ suviśodhitabodhisattvamārgastuṣite devanikāye upapadyate / amuko bodhisattvavastuṣite devanikāye upapannaḥ / sa na cirasyedānīṃ jambūdvīpe anuttarāṃ samyaksaṃbodhimabhisaṃbhotsyate / taṃ vayamārāgayema na virāgayema / tasya ca bodhisattvasyāntike 'smākaṃ janma bhavedityaparimitasattva-samyak-chanda-jananārthaṃ chandabahulīkaraṇārtham / punarbodhisattvastuṣitāddevanikāyāccyutvā ucce vā sammate vā kule upapadyate yaduta rājakule vā purohitakule vā / tathodārān kāmānutsṛjya niṣkrāmati sattvānāṃ bahumānotpādanārtham / punarduṣkaracaryāmabhyupagacchati duṣkaracaryādhimuktānāṃ sattvāna vicchandanārtham / punaranuttarāṃ samyak saṃbodhimabhisaṃbudhyate / tadanyeṣāṃ sattvānāṃ bodhivimuktisāmānyopagamanapariharṣaṇārtham / punaranuttarāṃ samyaksaṃbodhimabhisaṃbudhya brahmādhyeṣaṇāṃ pratīkṣate / na tāvatsattvānāṃ dharmaṃ deśayati / teṣāṃ sattvānāṃ dharmagauravotpādanārtham / nāvaramātrakametaddharmākhyānaṃ bhavati yatredānīṃ brahmā [svayaṃ] dharmadeśanāyai bhagavantamadhyeṣata iti / punarbuddhacakṣuṣā lokaṃ vyavalokāṃ yati / brahmādhyeṣite 'nena dharmo deśito brahmagauravāt / paravyāpāritena na tu svena sattveṣu kāruṇyacittena nātmana eva pratirupatāṃ viditveti / tadekatyānāṃ sattvānāmevaṃrūpasya mithyāgrāhasya vipraṇāśārtham / punardharmacakramapravartitapūrvaṃ loke pravartayati / tathā dharmaṃ deśayati / śikṣāpadāni ca prajñapayati / ayamucyate bodhisattvasya viśuddha upāyaḥ / yasmādupāyādanya upāya uttari atikrāntataraśca praṇītataraśca nāsti /
body.translated_text: There, what is the <s>Bodhisattva</s>'s pure skillful means (<s>viśuddha upāya</s>)? Here, a <s>Bodhisattva</s> established on the final <s>Bodhisattva</s> stage, having well-purified the <s>Bodhisattva</s> path, is born in the <s>Tuṣita</s> heaven—[so that beings say:] 'Such-and-such a <s>Bodhisattva</s> has been born in the <s>Tuṣita</s> heaven. Before long he will fully awaken to the unsurpassed, perfect awakening in <s>Jambudvīpa</s>. Let us be attached to him, not detached. May our birth be in the presence of that <s>Bodhisattva</s>'—for the purpose of generating proper aspiration in limitless beings and for increasing their aspiration. Furthermore, the <s>Bodhisattva</s>, falling from the <s>Tuṣita</s> heaven, is born in a high or esteemed family—namely, a royal family or a priestly family. Then one renounces magnificent pleasures and goes forth—for the purpose of generating respect in beings. Furthermore, one undertakes difficult practices—for the purpose of dissuading beings who are inclined toward asceticism. Furthermore, one fully awakens to the unsurpassed, perfect awakening—for the purpose of delighting other beings through their common attainment of awakening and liberation. Furthermore, having fully awakened, one awaits the request of <s>Brahmā</s> and does not immediately teach the <s>Dharma</s> to beings—for the purpose of generating respect for the <s>Dharma</s> in those beings. [So they say:] 'This <s>Dharma</s>-teaching is no trifling matter, since <s>Brahmā</s> himself requested the <s>Bhagavān</s> for <s>Dharma</s>-teaching.' Furthermore, one surveys the world with the <s>Buddha</s>-eye. The <s>Dharma</s> was taught at <s>Brahmā</s>'s request, out of reverence for <s>Brahmā</s>, prompted by another and not by oneself—not knowing one's own suitability, with a mind of compassion toward beings. This is for the destruction of the wrong grasping of some beings [who would think otherwise]. Furthermore, one turns the <s>Dharma</s>-wheel, never before turned in the world. Thus one teaches the <s>Dharma</s> and also establishes rules of training. This is called the <s>Bodhisattva</s>'s pure skillful means—because no skillful means beyond this exists that is higher, more surpassing, or more excellent.

body.text: itīdaṃ ṣaḍvidhamupāyakauśalyaṃ bodhisattvānāṃ samāsavyāsanirdeśataḥ pratihatānāṃ sattvānāṃ pratighātāya nayanāya madhyasthānāmavatārāyāvatīrṇānāṃ paripākāya paripakkānāṃ vimocanāya / iti nāstyata uttari nāstyato bhūyaḥ / idaṃ bodhisattvānāmupāyakauśalyam /
body.translated_text: Thus, this sixfold skill in means of <s>Bodhisattvas</s>, in summary and in detail, is for the removal and guidance of obstructed beings, for the entry of those who are indifferent, for the maturation of those who have entered, and for the liberation of those who have matured. There is nothing beyond this, nothing more than this. This is the <s>Bodhisattvas</s>' skill in means.

body.text: tatra katamā bodhisattvānāṃ dhāraṇī / samāsataścaturvidhā draṣṭavyā / dharmadhāraṇī / arthadhāraṇī / mantradhāraṇī / bodhisattvakṣāntilābhāya ca dhāraṇī /
body.translated_text: There, what is the <s>Bodhisattvas</s>' <s>dhāraṇī</s> (retention)? In brief, it should be seen as fourfold: retention of <s>dharmas</s> (<s>dharmadhāraṇī</s>); retention of meaning (<s>arthadhāraṇī</s>); retention of <s>mantras</s> (<s>mantradhāraṇī</s>); and retention for the attainment of the <s>Bodhisattva</s>'s patience (<s>bodhisattvakṣāntilābhāya dhāraṇī</s>).

body.text: tatra dharmādhāraṇī katamā / iha bodhisattvastadrūpāṃ smṛtiprajñābalādhānatāṃ pratilabhate yathā śrutamātrakeṇaivānāmnātān vacasā 'paricitān nāmapadavyañjanakāyasaṃgṛhītānanupūrvacaritānanupūrvasamāyuktān pramāṇān granthānapramāṇaṃ kālaṃ dhārayati /
body.translated_text: There, what is the retention of <s>dharmas</s>? Here, the <s>Bodhisattva</s> obtains such a strength of mindfulness and wisdom that, merely by hearing them once, one retains for an immeasurable time authoritative texts that have not been handed down, not familiarized by speech, comprised of groups of names, words, and syllables, composed in sequence, and arranged in order.

body.text: tatrārthadhāraṇī katamā / pūrvavat / tatrāyaṃ viśeṣaḥ / teṣāmeva dharmāṇāmapramāṇamarthamanāmnātamaparicitaṃ manasā 'pramāṇaṃ kālaṃ dhārayati /
body.translated_text: There, what is the retention of meaning? As before. The distinction here is: one retains in the mind for an immeasurable time the immeasurable meaning of those very <s>dharmas</s>, [meaning] that has not been handed down and not familiarized.

body.text: tatra mantradhāraṇī katamā / iha bodhisattvastadrūpaṃ samādhivaśitāṃ pratilabhate yathā yāni mantrapadānīti saṃśamanāya sattvānāmadhitiṣṭhanti / tāni siddhāni bhavanti / paramasiddhānyamoghānyenekavidhānāmītīnāṃ saṃśamanāya / iyamucyate bodhisattvasya mantradhāraṇī /
body.translated_text: There, what is the retention of <s>mantras</s>? Here, the <s>Bodhisattva</s> obtains such mastery over concentration that whatever <s>mantra</s>-syllables one empowers for the pacification of beings, those become efficacious—supremely efficacious and unfailing, for the pacification of manifold calamities. This is called the <s>Bodhisattva</s>'s <s>mantra</s>-retention.

body.text: tatra katamā bodhisattvasya bodhisattvakṣāntilābhāya dhāraṇī / iha bodhisattvaḥ svayaṃ pragāḍhahetucaritaḥ prajñāvān praviviktavihārī vācamapyanudīrayan darśanapathamapyanāgacchan kenacit saha tathā mātrābhojī asaṃkīrṇabhojī ekaprakārāśanabhojī pradhyānaparataḥ alpaṃ rātrau svapan bahu jāgran yānīmāni tathāgatabhāṣitāni bodhisattvakṣāntilābhāya mantrapadāni tadyathā iṭi miṭi kiṭibhiḥ kṣāntipadāni svāhā / ityeteṣāṃ mantrapadānāmarthaṃ cintayati tulayatyupaparīkṣate / sa teṣāṃ mantrapadānāmevaṃ samyak pratipanna evamarthaṃ svayamevāśrutvā kutaścit pratividhyati / tad yathā nāstyeṣāṃ mantrapadānāṃ kācidarthapariniṣpattiḥ nirarthā evaite / ayameva caiṣāmartho yaduta nirarthatā / tasmācca paraṃ punaraparamarthaṃ na samanveṣate / iyatā tena teṣāṃ mantrapadānāmarthaḥ supratividdho bhavati / sa
body.translated_text: There, what is the <s>Bodhisattva</s>'s retention for the attainment of <s>Bodhisattva</s>-patience (<s>bodhisattvakṣānti</s>)? Here, the <s>Bodhisattva</s>, having personally practiced profound causal [practices], wise, dwelling in seclusion, not even uttering speech, not even coming into the sight of anyone, moderate in eating, eating separately, eating one type of food, devoted to meditation, sleeping little at night and staying much awake—the <s>mantra</s>-syllables spoken by the <s>Tathāgata</s> for the attainment of the <s>Bodhisattva</s>'s patience, namely: '<s>iṭi miṭi kiṭibhiḥ kṣāntipadāni svāhā</s>'—one reflects on, weighs, and examines the meaning of these <s>mantra</s>-syllables. That one, correctly practicing with regard to those <s>mantra</s>-syllables, penetrates their meaning by oneself without having heard it from anyone. Namely: 'There is no accomplishment of meaning in these <s>mantra</s>-syllables; they are indeed meaningless. And this very meaninglessness is their meaning.' Beyond that, one does not seek any further meaning. By this much, the meaning of those <s>mantra</s>-syllables has been well-penetrated. That one

body.text: teṣāṃ mantrapadānāmarthaṃ samyak pratividhya tenaivārthānusāreṇa sarvadharmāṇāmatyarthaṃ samyak pratividhyati svayamevāśrutvā parataḥ / evañca punararthaṃ pratividhyati / sarvābhilāpaiḥ sarvadharmāṇāṃ svabhāvārthāpariniṣpattiḥ / yā punareṣāṃ nirabhilāpyasvabhāvatā ayamevaiṣāṃ svabhāvārthaḥ / sa evaṃ sarvadharmāṇāṃ svabhāvārthaṃ samyak pratividhya tasmātparamarthaṃ na samanveṣate / udārañca tasyārthasya prativedhāt prītiprāmodyaṃ pratilabhate / tena bodhisattvena pratilabdhā tāni dhāraṇīpadānyadhiṣṭhāya bodhisattvakṣāntirvaktavyā / tasyāśca lābhāt sa bodhisattvo na cirasyedānīmadhyāśayaviśuddhiṃ pratilabhate / adhimātrāyāmadhimutticaryābhūmikṣāntau vartate / iyaṃ bodhisattvasya bodhisattvakṣāntilābhāya dhāraṇī veditavyā /
body.translated_text: having correctly penetrated the meaning of those <s>mantra</s>-syllables, by that very following of meaning, one exceedingly well penetrates the [nature of] all <s>dharmas</s> by oneself, without hearing from another. And thus one penetrates the meaning: through all designations, there is no accomplishment of the intrinsic-nature meaning of all <s>dharmas</s>. Their inexpressible nature—this alone is their intrinsic-nature meaning. Having correctly penetrated the intrinsic-nature meaning of all <s>dharmas</s> thus, one does not seek any meaning beyond that. And through the noble penetration of that meaning, one obtains joy and delight. Having obtained [this], the <s>Bodhisattva</s>, empowering those <s>dhāraṇī</s>-syllables, is to be said [to have attained] the <s>Bodhisattva</s>-patience. And through the attainment of that, the <s>Bodhisattva</s> will before long obtain the purification of [superior] intention. One abides in the patience of the stage of the practice through supreme aspiration (<s>adhimukticaryābhūmikṣānti</s>). This should be understood as the <s>Bodhisattva</s>'s retention for the attainment of the <s>Bodhisattva</s>'s patience.

body.text: tatra dharmadhāraṇīmarthadhāraṇīñca bodhisattvaḥ prathamasya kalpāsaṃkhyeyasyātyayācchuddhādhyāśayabhūmipraviṣṭo labhate niyatāṃ sthirāmudārāñca / tataḥ punararvāg labhate praṇidhānavaśena vā dhyānasanniśrayeṇa vā natu niyatāṃ na sthirāṃ nodārām / yathādharmārthadhāraṇī evaṃ mantradhāraṇī veditavyā / bodhisattvakṣāntilābhāya tu dhāraṇī yathaiva vyākhyātā tathaiva labhyate /
body.translated_text: There, the <s>Bodhisattva</s> obtains the retention of <s>dharmas</s> and the retention of meaning—fixed, stable, and noble—upon entering the stage of pure intention (<s>śuddhādhyāśayabhūmi</s>) after the end of the first incalculable <s>kalpa</s>. Before that, one obtains them through the power of aspiration or through reliance on meditation, but not fixed, not stable, and not noble. Just as with the retention of <s>dharmas</s> and meaning, so the <s>mantra</s>-retention should be understood. But the retention for the attainment of the <s>Bodhisattva</s>'s patience is obtained just as described.

body.text: etāḥ punaḥ sarvā dhāraṇīrbodhisattvaścaturbhiguṇairyukto labhate nānyatamavikalaḥ / katamaiścaturbhiḥ / kāmeṣvanadhvavasito bhavati parasamucchrayeṣvīryāṃ notpādayati / anīrṣurbhavati sarva-yācita-pradaśca bhavatyananutāpyadāyī / dharmārāmaśca bhavati dharmarato bodhisattvapiṭakamārabhya piṭakamātṛkāṃ vā
body.translated_text: All these <s>dhāraṇīs</s> the <s>Bodhisattva</s> obtains when endowed with four qualities, not when deficient in any one [of them]. Which four? One is not attached to sensual pleasures; one does not generate jealousy at the accomplishments of others; one is free from envy and gives everything that is requested, giving without regret; and one delights in the <s>Dharma</s> and takes pleasure in the <s>Dharma</s>, beginning with the <s>Bodhisattva Piṭaka</s> and the <s>mātṛkā</s> of the <s>Piṭaka</s>.

body.text: tatra katamadbodhisattvasya bodhisattvapraṇidhānam / tat samāsataḥ pañcavidhaṃ draṣṭavyam / cittotpādapraṇidhānaṃ upapattipraṇidhānaṃ gocarapraṇidhānaṃ samyakpraṇidhānaṃ mahāpraṇidhānañca /
body.translated_text: There, what is the <s>Bodhisattva</s>'s aspiration (<s>praṇidhāna</s>)? In brief, it should be seen as fivefold: the aspiration of the generation of the mind (<s>cittotpādapraṇidhāna</s>), the aspiration of rebirth (<s>upapattipraṇidhāna</s>), the aspiration of domain (<s>gocarapraṇidhāna</s>), the proper aspiration (<s>samyakpraṇidhāna</s>), and the great aspiration (<s>mahāpraṇidhāna</s>).

body.text: tatra prathamacittotpādo bodhisattvasyānuttarāyāṃ samyaksaṃbodhau cittotpādapraṇidhānamityucyate /
body.translated_text: There, the first generation of the mind toward the unsurpassed, perfect awakening is called the <s>Bodhisattva</s>'s aspiration of the generation of the mind.

body.text: āyatyāṃ sattvārthānukūlāsu sugatyupapattiṣu praṇidhānaṃ bodhisattvasyopapattipraṇidhānamityucyate /
body.translated_text: The aspiration for rebirth in fortunate destinies that are favorable to the welfare of beings in the future is called the <s>Bodhisattva</s>'s aspiration of rebirth.

body.text: samyagdharmapravicayapraṇidhānaṃ apramāṇādikuśaladharmabhāvanā-viṣaya-praṇidhānañca bodhisattvasya gocarapraṇidhānamityucyate /
body.translated_text: The aspiration for proper investigation of the <s>Dharma</s> and the aspiration regarding the domain of cultivating immeasurable and other wholesome <s>dharmas</s> is called the <s>Bodhisattva</s>'s aspiration of domain.

body.text: āyatyāṃ sarvabodhisattvakuśalasaṃgrahāya sarvaguṇasaṃgrahāya ca samāsato vyāsato vā praṇidhānaṃ bodhisattvasya samyak praṇidhānamityucyate /
body.translated_text: The aspiration, in summary or in detail, for the future collection of all <s>Bodhisattva</s> wholesome [qualities] and for the collection of all qualities is called the <s>Bodhisattva</s>'s proper aspiration.

body.text: mahāpraṇidhānaṃ punarbodhisattvasattvasyāsmādeva samyakpraṇidhānādveditavyam / tat punardaśaviṃdham / āyatyāṃ sarvākārāprameya-tathāgata-pūjopasthānatāyai prathamaṃ praṇidhāna bodhisattvasya mahāpraṇidhānamityucyate / buddhānāṃ ca bhagavatāṃ saddharma-parigrahārakṣaṇatāyai dharmanetrīsandhāraṇāya mahāpraṇidhānam / tuṣitabhavanavāsamupādāya purvavadyāvat parinirvāṇāya mahāpraṇidhānam / bodhisattva-sarvākārasamyakcaryācaraṇatāyai mahāpraṇidhānam / sarvasattvaparipākāya mahāpraṇidhānam / sarvalokadhātusandarśanāya mahāpraṇidhānam / buddhakṣetrapariśodhanāya mahāpraṇidhānam / sarvabodhisattvaikāśayaprayogatāyai mahāyānāvataraṇatāyai mahāpraṇidhānam / abandhyasarva-samyakprayogatāyai mahāpraṇidhānam / anuttarasamyaksaṃbodhyabhisaṃbodhāya mahāpraṇidhānam /
body.translated_text: The great aspiration of the <s>Bodhisattva</s> should be understood as arising from this very proper aspiration. It is tenfold: the first aspiration, for the future worship and attendance upon the <s>Tathāgatas</s> in all aspects and immeasurably, is called the <s>Bodhisattva</s>'s great aspiration. The great aspiration for the embracing, protecting, and sustaining of the true <s>Dharma</s> of the <s>Buddha Bhagavāns</s> and the <s>Dharma</s>-lineage. The great aspiration [for the entire sequence] from abiding in the <s>Tuṣita</s> heaven, as before, up to <s>parinirvāṇa</s>. The great aspiration for carrying out the <s>Bodhisattva</s>'s proper practice in all aspects. The great aspiration for the maturation of all beings. The great aspiration for seeing all world-systems. The great aspiration for purifying <s>Buddha</s>-fields. The great aspiration for being of one intention and one endeavor with all <s>Bodhisattvas</s>, and for entering the <s>Mahāyāna</s>. The great aspiration for all proper endeavors being fruitful. The great aspiration for the full awakening to the unsurpassed, perfect awakening.

body.text: tatra katamo bodhisattvasya śūnyatāsamādhiḥ / iha bodhisattvasya sarvābhilāṣātmakena svabhāvena virahitaṃ nirabhilāpyasvabhāvaṃ vastu paśyataḥ yā cittasya sthitiḥ / ayamasyocyate śūnyatāsamādhiḥ /
body.translated_text: There, what is the <s>Bodhisattva</s>'s concentration on emptiness (<s>śūnyatāsamādhi</s>)? Here, the stability of mind of the <s>Bodhisattva</s> who sees a thing as devoid of any expressible intrinsic nature, as having an inexpressible nature—this is called one's concentration on emptiness.

body.text: apraṇihitaḥ samādhiḥ katamaḥ / iha bodhisattvasya tadeva nirabhilāpyasvabhāvaṃ vastu mithyāvikalpasamutthāpitena kleśena duḥkhena ca parigṛhītatvādanekadoṣaduṣṭaṃ samanupaśyato yā āyatyāṃ tatrāpraṇidhānapūrvikā cittasthitiḥ / ayamasyāpraṇihitaḥ samādhirityucyate /
body.translated_text: What is the concentration on the wishless (<s>apraṇihita samādhi</s>)? Here, the stability of mind of the <s>Bodhisattva</s> who sees that very thing of inexpressible nature as corrupted by manifold faults—because it is encompassed by affliction and suffering generated by wrong conceptualization—[a stability] preceded by non-wishing toward that [conditioned existence] in the future—this is called one's concentration on the wishless.

body.text: animittaḥ samādhiḥ katamaḥ / iha bodhisattvasya tadeva nirabhilāpyasvabhāvaṃ vastu sarvavikalpaprapañca nimittānyapanīya yathābhūtaṃ śāntato manasi kurvato yā cittasthitiḥ / ayamasyocyate animittaḥ samādhiḥ / kasmātpunareṣāmeva trayāṇāṃ samādhīnāṃ prajñaptirbhavati / nāta uttari nāto bhūyaḥ dvayamidaṃ saccāsacca / tatra saṃskṛtamasaskṛtañca sat asadātmā vātmīyaṃ vā / tatraḥ
body.translated_text: What is the concentration on the signless (<s>animitta samādhi</s>)? Here, the stability of mind of the <s>Bodhisattva</s> who, having removed all signs of conceptual elaboration from that very thing of inexpressible nature, attends to it as it truly is, as peaceful—this is called one's concentration on the signless. And why are only these three concentrations designated? There is nothing beyond this, nothing more than this. There is this duality of the real and the unreal. There, the conditioned and the unconditioned are real; the self and what belongs to self are unreal. There

body.text: saṃskṛte satyapraṇidhānataḥ prātikūlyato 'praṇihitasamādhivyavasthānam / asaṃskṛte punarnirvāṇe praṇidhānataḥ samyagabhiratigrahaṇato nirnimittasamādhivyavasthānam / yat punaretadasadeva vastu tatra bodhisattvena na praṇidhānaṃ nāpraṇidhānaṃ karaṇīyam / api tu tadasadasadityeva yathābhūtaṃ draṣṭavyam / tacca darśanamadhikṛtya śūnyatāsamādhivyavasthānaṃ veditavyam / evaṃ hi bodhisattva eṣu triṣu samādhiṣu yogaṃ karoti / evaṃ ca vyavasthānaṃ yathābhūtaṃ prajānāti / tadanyākārānapi trīnsamādhīnyathābhūta-vyavasthāna-nayapraveśena bhāvanā-nayapraveśena ca yathābhūtaṃ prajānāti yeṣu śrāvakāḥ śikṣante samudāgacchati ca /
body.translated_text: with regard to the conditioned, the establishment of the signless <s>samādhi</s> (<s>apraṇihitasamādhi</s>) is through the non-aspiration of aversion toward it, through the true vow [to escape]. With regard to the unconditioned, namely <s>Nirvāṇa</s>, the establishment of the signless <s>samādhi</s> (<s>ānimittasamādhi</s>) is through the [right] aspiration toward it, through the correct grasping of delight. But regarding that very thing which is actually neither existent nor non-existent, the <s>Bodhisattva</s> should neither aspire toward it nor not aspire toward it. Rather, it should be seen as it truly is—namely, as neither existent nor non-existent. And with reference to that seeing, the establishment of the emptiness <s>samādhi</s> (<s>śūnyatāsamādhi</s>) should be understood. Thus the <s>Bodhisattva</s> practices in these three <s>samādhis</s>. And he truly knows their establishment in this way. He also truly knows the three <s>samādhis</s> of other modes—through the approach of true-nature establishment and through the approach of cultivation—those in which <s>Śrāvakas</s> train and which they accomplish.

body.text: catvārīmāni dharmoddānāni yāni buddhāśca bodhisattvāśca sattvānāṃ viśuddhaye deśayanti / katamāni catvāri / anityāḥ sarvasaṃskārā iti dharmoddānam / duḥkhāḥ sarvasaṃskārā iti dharmoddānam / anātmānaḥ sarvadharmā iti dharmoddānam / śāntaṃ nirvāṇamiti dharmoddānam / etat pratisaṃyuktārtha yadbhūyasā dharmamudīrayanti buddhabodhisattvāḥ sattvānām / tasmādetāni dharmoddānānītyucyante / paurāṇeśca śāntamānasairmunibhiruditoditatvānnityakālamuddānānītyucyante / mahodayagāminī bhavāgrordhvaṃgāminī caiṣā pratipat tasmāduddānānītyucyante /
body.translated_text: There are these four <s>Dharma</s>-summaries (<s>dharmoddāna</s>) which <s>Buddhas</s> and <s>Bodhisattvas</s> teach for the purification of beings. Which four? 'All conditioned things are impermanent'—this is a <s>Dharma</s>-summary. 'All conditioned things are suffering'—this is a <s>Dharma</s>-summary. 'All <s>dharmas</s> are non-self'—this is a <s>Dharma</s>-summary. '<s>Nirvāṇa</s> is peace'—this is a <s>Dharma</s>-summary. It is in connection with these meanings that <s>Buddhas</s> and <s>Bodhisattvas</s> for the most part expound the <s>Dharma</s> to beings. Therefore they are called <s>Dharma</s>-summaries. And because they have been declared again and again by the sages of old, of peaceful mind, they are called 'perpetual summaries.' And because this path leads to the great outcome, ascending above the summit of existence, they are called 'summaries.'

body.text: kathaṃ ca bodhisattvaḥ sarvasaṃskārānanityataḥ samanupaśyati / iha bodhisattvaḥ sarvasaṃskārāṇāmabhilāpyasvabhāvaṃ nityakālameva nāstītyupalabhyānityataḥ sarvasaṃskārān paśyati / punaravijñātasya bhūtatastasyaiva nirabhilāpyasya vastunaḥ aparijñānahetukamudayavyayamupalabhyatān nirabhilāpyasvabhāvān sarvasaṃskārānanityataḥ samanupaśyati / so 'tītān saṃskārānutpannaniruddhānsamanupaśyati / teṣāṃ naiva hetumupalabhate nāpi svabhāvam / tasmātteṣāṃ naiva hetuto naiva svabhāvato vidyamānatāṃ samanupaśyati / pratyutpannāniruddhānsamanupaśyati / teṣāṃ hetuṃ nopalabhate dattaphalatvāt / svabhāvaṃ punarupalabhate aniruddhatvāt / tasmātteṣāṃ svabhāvato vidyamānatāṃ samanupaśyati no tu hetutaḥ / anāgatān saṃskārānanutpannāniruddhān paśyati / teṣāṃ hetumupalabhate adattaphalatvāt / no tu svabhāvamanutpannatvāt / tasmātteṣāṃ bodhisattvo hetuto vidyamānatāṃ
body.translated_text: And how does the <s>Bodhisattva</s> regard all conditioned things as impermanent? Here, the <s>Bodhisattva</s>, having ascertained that the expressible nature (<s>abhilāpyasvabhāva</s>) of all conditioned things never exists at any time, regards all conditioned things as impermanent. Furthermore, having ascertained the arising and ceasing—which is due to the non-comprehension of that very inexpressible reality (<s>nirabhilāpya vastu</s>) as it truly is—he regards all conditioned things, whose nature is inexpressible, as impermanent. He regards past conditioned things as having arisen and ceased. Of them he finds neither their cause nor their intrinsic nature. Therefore he does not regard them as existing either through their cause or through their intrinsic nature. He regards present [conditioned things] as not having ceased. Of them he does not find the cause, since it has already given its fruit. But he does find the intrinsic nature, since they have not ceased. Therefore he regards them as existing through their intrinsic nature but not through their cause. He regards future conditioned things as not having arisen and not having ceased. Of them he finds the cause, since it has not yet given its fruit. But not the intrinsic nature, since they have not arisen. Therefore the <s>Bodhisattva</s> regards them as existing through their cause

body.text: paśyati no tu svabhāvataḥ / sa eva triṣvadhvasvavyavacchinnāṃ saṃskāra-santatiṃ pravartamānāṃ dṛṣṭvā ekaikasmin saṃskārakṣaṇe trīṇi saṃskṛtasya saṃskṛtalakṣaṇāni paśyati / kṣaṇādurkṣvaṃ caturthaṃ saṃskṛtalakṣaṇaṃ samanupaśyati / tatra pūrvasaṃskārakṣaṇe svabhāvavināśānantara yo 'pūrvasaṃskārakṣaṇasvabhāvaprādurbhāvaḥ sā jātiriti paśyati / utpannasya yastatkālāvipraṇāśaḥ sā sthitiriti paśyati / taṃ pūrvaniruddhaṃ saṃskārajñaṇasvabhāvamapekṣya tasyotpannasya yadanyatvamanyathātvaṃ vā sā jareti paśyati / tasmājjātikṣaṇādūrdhvaṃ tasyaivotpannasya saṃskārakṣaṇasya yaḥ svabhāvavināśaḥ sa vyaya iti paśyati / sa yatsvabhāvameva tamutpannaṃ saṃskārakṣaṇaṃ samanupaśyati / tatsvabhāvāneva tasya jātiṃ sthitiṃ jarāṃ ca / [na] paśyati tadanyasvabhāvān /
body.translated_text: but not through their intrinsic nature. And having seen the uninterrupted continuum of conditioned things flowing through the three times, he perceives in each single momentary conditioned event (<s>saṃskārakṣaṇa</s>) three marks of the conditioned (<s>saṃskṛtalakṣaṇa</s>). And from the moment onward, a fourth mark of the conditioned. There, the arising of a new momentary conditioned event immediately following the destruction of the intrinsic nature of the prior momentary conditioned event—that he perceives as birth (<s>jāti</s>). The non-destruction of what has arisen at that very time—that he perceives as persistence (<s>sthiti</s>). The otherness or alteration of that arisen [event] relative to the prior ceased momentary conditioned nature—that he perceives as aging (<s>jarā</s>). And from the moment of birth onward, the destruction of the intrinsic nature of that very arisen momentary conditioned event—that he perceives as decay (<s>vyaya</s>). He perceives that arisen momentary conditioned event as being of that very intrinsic nature. And [he perceives] its birth, persistence, and aging as being of that very intrinsic nature. He does not perceive them as being of another intrinsic nature.

body.text: tasmācca kṣaṇādūrdhvaṃ ca eva tasya saṃskārakṣaṇa[svabhāva]syāpagamaḥ sa eva teṣāṃ jātyādīnāmiti yathābhūtaṃ paśyati tānyetāni catvāryaṣi saṃskṛtalakṣaṇānyabhisamasya saṃskārāṇāṃ samāsato dvayāvasthā-prabhāvitāni / bhāvaprabhāvitānyabhāvaprabhāvitāni ca / tatra bhagavatā yo bhāvastadekaṃ saṃskṛtalakṣaṇaṃ vyavasthāpitam / yastvabhāvastat dvitīyaṃ saṃskṛtalakṣaṇaṃ vyavasthāpitam / sa ca bhāvasteṣāṃ saṃskārāṇāṃ sthityanyathātvaprabhāvita iti kṛtvā tṛtīyaṃ saṃskṛtalakṣaṇaṃ vyavasthāpitam / tatra bodhisattvaḥ saṃskāramātraṃ sthāpayitvā na tasya jātiṃ na sthitiṃ na jarāṃ nānityatāṃ sarvakālaṃ dravyasvabhāvapariniṣpattitaḥ paśyati / tatkasya hetoḥ / saṃskāramātraṃ sa utpadyamānamupalabhate / nāsyānyāṃ jātiṃ na sthitiṃ na jarāṃ nānityatām / saṃskāramātrameva ca jāyamānaṃ tiṣṭhantaṃ jīryamāṇaṃ vinaśyamānamupalabhate / na tasyānyāṃ jātiṃ sthitiṃ jarāmanityatāñca / yuktyāpi bodhisattvo vimṛśannetān jātyādīn dravyato nopalabhate / evañca punarvimṛśannopalabhate / sa cedrūpādisaṃskāravinirmuktaḥ anyo jātidharmaḥ syāt sa yathaiva rūpādikaḥ saṃskāraḥ svātmanotpadyate / tathaiva so 'pyutpadyeta / evaṃ sati dve janmanī syātām yacca saṃskāra-janma yacca jāti-janma tatra tatsaṃskārajanma tasmājjātijanmanaḥ ananyadeva vā syāt / [anyadeva vā /] yadi tāvadananyadevaṃ satyapārthikā jātidravyakalpanā / anyā jātirdravyato 'stītiṃ na yujyate /
body.translated_text: And from the moment onward, the departure of that very intrinsic nature of the momentary conditioned event—that is itself [the departure] of birth and the rest. He sees this as it truly is. Having thus comprehended these four marks of the conditioned, [he understands that] they are, in brief, manifested through two conditions of conditioned things: manifested through existence and manifested through non-existence. There, the <s>Bhagavān</s> established one mark of the conditioned based on what is existence. And he established a second mark of the conditioned based on what is non-existence. And that existence of conditioned things, being manifested through persistence and alteration, serves as the basis for establishing the third mark of the conditioned. There, the <s>Bodhisattva</s>, setting aside the mere conditioned thing itself, does not perceive its birth, persistence, aging, or impermanence as ever established as a substantial nature (<s>dravyasvabhāva</s>). For what reason? He finds the mere conditioned thing arising. He does not find a separate birth, persistence, aging, or impermanence of it. And he finds the mere conditioned thing itself being born, persisting, aging, and perishing. He does not find a separate birth, persistence, aging, or impermanence of it. And the <s>Bodhisattva</s>, examining with reasoning, does not find these—birth and the rest—as substantial. And examining thus, he finds [the following]: if birth-nature (<s>jātidharma</s>) were something other than and separate from conditioned things such as form and the rest, it would arise by its own nature just as the conditioned things such as form arise. In that case there would be two births—the birth of the conditioned thing and the birth of birth itself. Now that birth of the conditioned thing, with respect to the birth of birth, would be either non-different [or different]. If non-different, then the conceptual construction of birth as a substantial entity is pointless. That birth exists as a substantial entity different [from the conditioned thing]—this is not logically tenable.

body.text: atha ca punaranyadevaṃ sati saṃskāra-janma jātirna bhavati / saṃskāra-janma jātiriti na yujyate / yathā jātirevaṃ sthitirjarā vināśaśca vistareṇa veditavyaḥ / sa cedvināśo nāma svabhāvato dharmaḥ pariniṣpannaḥ syāt so 'pyutpadyeta nirudhyeta vā / yadā ca vināśa utpannaḥ syāttadā sarvasaṃskārairniruddhairbhavitavyaṃ syāt / evaṃ satyalpakṛcchreṇa nirodhasamāpannasyeva cittacaitasikānāṃ dharmāṇāmapravṛttiḥ syāt / tasya ca punarvināśasya nirodhāt niruddhairapi taiḥ saṃskāraiḥ punareva bhavitavyaṃ syāt vināśa eṣāṃ nāstīti kṛtvā / ato vināśa utpadyate nirudhyate ceti na yujyate / na ca punaḥ kulaputrasya vā kuladuhiturvā sarvakālāstitāñca dravyasatāṃ svabhāvapariniṣpatiñca prajñapti satāṃ paśyato nirvidvirāgo vimuktiśca yujyate / ato viparyayeṇa tu yujyate / ityebhirākārairbodhisattvaḥ sarvasaṃskārā anityā iti yathābhūtaṃ prajānāti /
body.translated_text: But if they are different, then the birth of the conditioned thing would not be birth [in itself]. That the birth of the conditioned thing is birth—this is not logically tenable. Just as with birth, so persistence, aging, and destruction should be understood in detail. If destruction were a <s>dharma</s> established as a substantial nature, it too would arise or cease. And if destruction had arisen, then all conditioned things would have to cease [simultaneously]. In that case, with little effort, there would be a non-functioning of mind and mental factors just as for one who has entered the cessation attainment (<s>nirodhasamāpatti</s>). And from the cessation of that very destruction, those conditioned things that have ceased would have to exist again—since their destruction is no more. Therefore, it is not logically tenable that destruction arises and ceases. And for a son or daughter of good family who sees the permanent existence, substantial reality, and established intrinsic nature of all things at all times, revulsion, dispassion, and liberation are not logically tenable. But the opposite is [logically tenable]. Through these modes, the <s>Bodhisattva</s> truly knows: 'All conditioned things are impermanent.'

body.text: tān punareva anityān saṃskārān prabandhena vartamānādbodhisattvaḥ triḥprakārāyā duḥkhatāyāḥ sanniśrayabhāvena paśyati saṃskāraduḥkhatāyāḥ vipariṇāmaduḥkhatāyāḥ duḥkhaduḥkhatāyāśca / evaṃ hi bodhisattvaḥ sarvasaṃskārā duḥkhā iti yathābhūtaṃ prajānāti /
body.translated_text: Furthermore, the <s>Bodhisattva</s> regards those very impermanent conditioned things, flowing in continuity, as the basis for three kinds of suffering: the suffering of conditioned existence (<s>saṃskāraduḥkhatā</s>), the suffering of change (<s>vipariṇāmaduḥkhatā</s>), and the suffering of suffering (<s>duḥkhaduḥkhatā</s>). Thus the <s>Bodhisattva</s> truly knows: 'All conditioned things are suffering.'

body.text: punaḥ sarvadharmāṇāṃ bodhisattvaḥ saṃskṛtāsaṃskṛtānāṃ dvividhaṃ nairātmyaṃ yathābhūtaṃ prajānāti / pudgalanairātmyaṃ dharmanairātmyaṃ ca / tatredaṃ pudgalanairātmyam / yannaivate vidyamānā dharmāḥ pudgalāḥ / nāpi vidyamānadharmavinirmukto 'nyaḥ pudgalo vidyate / tatredaṃ dharmanairātmyam / yatsarveṣvabhilāpyeṣu vastuṣu sarvābhilāpasvabhāvo dharmo na saṃvidyate / evaṃ hi bodhisattvaḥ sarvadharmā anātmāna iti yathābhūtaṃ prajānāti /
body.translated_text: Furthermore, the <s>Bodhisattva</s> truly knows the twofold selflessness (<s>nairātmya</s>) of all <s>dharmas</s>, both conditioned and unconditioned: the selflessness of the person (<s>pudgalanairātmya</s>) and the selflessness of <s>dharmas</s> (<s>dharmanairātmya</s>). There, this is the selflessness of the person: these existing <s>dharmas</s> are not persons; nor is there any person existing apart from existing <s>dharmas</s>. There, this is the selflessness of <s>dharmas</s>: in all inexpressible entities, no <s>dharma</s> of an expressible nature is found. Thus the <s>Bodhisattva</s> truly knows: 'All <s>dharmas</s> are non-self.'

body.text: yaḥ punareṣāmeva saṃskārāṇāṃ pūrvaṃ hetusamucchinnānāṃ paścādaśeṣoparamastadanyeṣāñcātyantamanabhinirvṛttiraprādurbhāvaḥ / idamucyate nirvāṇam / tacca śāntaṃ kleśopaśamāt duḥkhopaśamācca veditavyam / evaṃ ca tāvadanadhyāśayaśuddho bodhisattvaḥ adṛṣṭasatyo vā śrāvakāyānīyo nirvāṇamadhimukto bhavati / evañcābhivadati-śāntaṃ nirvāṇamiti / na cāsya tasminnirvāṇe yathābhūtāvagamo yathāvajjñānadarśanaṃ
body.translated_text: Furthermore, the complete subsiding of all remaining [conditioned things] after the prior elimination of their causes—of these very conditioned things—and the absolute non-production and non-manifestation of anything else: this is called <s>Nirvāṇa</s>. And it should be understood as peaceful, due to the pacification of afflictions and the pacification of suffering. Thus far, a <s>Bodhisattva</s> whose intention is not yet pure, or a <s>Śrāvaka</s>-vehicle follower who has not yet seen the truths, aspires toward <s>Nirvāṇa</s>. And declares thus: '<s>Nirvāṇa</s> is peaceful.' But he does not have a true-nature comprehension of that <s>Nirvāṇa</s>, a knowledge-and-vision as it truly is.

body.text: pravartate / asti tveṣa yoniśo manaskāraḥ / tadyathā rājaputro vā gṛhapatiputro vā rājñā gṛhapatinā vā 'ntargṛhe saṃvardhitaḥ syāt tasya ca daharasyaiva kumārabhūtasya tena rājñā gṛhapatinā vā kṛtrimakā mṛgarathakā vā go-aśvarathakā vā hastirathakā vā upasaṃhṛtā bhaveyuḥ / sa ca rājaputro vā gṛhapatiputro vā taiḥ krīḍan ramamāṇaḥ paricārayaṃsteṣveva kṛtrimeṣu mṛgeṣu mṛgasaṃjñī syāt kṛtrimeṣu go 'śveṣu hastiṣu hastisaṃjñī syāt / athaikadā sa rājā vā gṛhapatirvā svasya putrasya vṛddheranvayādindriyāṇāṃ paripākādbhūtānāṃ mṛgāṇāṃ varṇaṃ bhāṣeta / bhūtānāṃ yāvaddhastināṃ varṇaṃ bhāṣeta / tasya punā rājaputrasya [vā] gṛhapatiputrasya vā ta varṇavādaṃ śrutvā evaṃ syāt / eṣāmayaṃ rājā gṛhapatirvā asmākaṃ mṛgarathakānāṃ yāvaddhastirathakānāṃ vā varṇaṃ bhāṣata iti / athāpareṇa samayena sa rājā gahapatirvā svaṃ putraṃ bahirāgārānnivīṣya bhūtāneva mṛgāṃstasmai upadarśayedbhūtāneva yāvaddhastina upadarśayet / tasya tān dṛṣṭvā tasminsamaye pratyātmaṃ pratyavagamo yathābhūta utpadyeta / ime te bhūtārthikā mṛgarathakā vistareṇa yāvaddhastirathakā yeṣāmasmākaṃ pitā dīrgharātraṃ varṇaṃ bhāṣitavānasmākameva tvayathābhūte arthe tat pratirūpamātrake tatpratibimbapratibhāsamātrake adhimokṣaḥ pravṛtta iti / tena pūrvakeṇādhimokṣeṇāritīyeran / evameva saṃsārāntargṛhasaṃvṛddhānāmaśuddhāśayānāṃ bodhisattvānāmadṛṣṭasatyānāñca śrāvakāṇāṃ putrasthānīyānāṃ pitṛkalpairbuddhairbodhisattvaiśca mahābhūmipraviṣṭairnirvāṇapratyakṣadarśibhisteṣāṃ bodhisattvānāṃ śrāvakāṇāñca purastānnirvāṇasya yathādṛṣṭasya varṇo bhāṣitaḥ / taiśca tannirvāṇaṃ guṇato ghoṣamātrānusariṇyā buddhyā dīrgharātramadhimuktam / yadā punasteṣāṃ saṃbhāraparipākavṛddheranvayāt śraddhāśayānāñca bodhisattvānāṃ dṛṣṭasatyānāñca śrāvakāṇāṃ nirvāṇe pratyakṣaṃ jñānadarśanamutpadyate / tadā teṣāmapi yathābhūtaḥ pratyavagama utpadyate / idaṃ tannirvāṇaṃ sarvaśrāvakapratyekabuddhānāṃ yasya buddhabodhisattvairvarṇā bhāṣitaḥ / asmābhistu pūrvabālaprajñatayā na yathābhūtamadhimuktam / asti tu tadasya pratirūpakam / asti pratibhāsamātrakam / te tena pūrvakeṇādhimokṣeṇa
body.translated_text: it proceeds. But there is this proper mental attention (<s>yoniśo manaskāra</s>). It is as follows: Suppose a prince or a householder's son were raised by the king or householder inside the inner chambers, and for that young child, the king or householder had procured toy deer-chariots, or cow-and-horse-chariots, or elephant-chariots. That prince or householder's son, playing and delighting with them, attending to them, would perceive those very toy deer as real deer, and the toy cows, horses, and elephants as real elephants. Then one day, that king or householder, in accordance with his son's growth and the maturation of his faculties, would describe the qualities of real deer, and in detail up to real elephants. That prince or householder's son, having heard that description, would think: 'This king or householder is describing the qualities of our toy deer-chariots, and in detail up to our toy elephant-chariots.' Then at another time, that king or householder, having led his son outside the home, would show him real deer, and in detail up to real elephants. Having seen those, at that moment an understanding as it truly is would arise in him personally: 'These are the real deer-chariots, and in detail up to elephant-chariots, whose qualities our father has long described. But our conviction had been directed at what was not the real thing—at a mere semblance, a mere reflection and appearance of that.' He would be ashamed of his former conviction. In just the same way, for <s>Bodhisattvas</s> of impure intention who have been raised in the inner chambers of <s>saṃsāra</s>, and for <s>Śrāvakas</s> who have not seen the truths, who are in the position of sons—by the <s>Buddhas</s> and <s>Bodhisattvas</s> who have entered the great stages, who are like fathers and who directly perceive <s>Nirvāṇa</s>—the qualities of <s>Nirvāṇa</s> as they have seen it have been described before those <s>Bodhisattvas</s> and <s>Śrāvakas</s>. And they have long had conviction in that <s>Nirvāṇa</s> through its qualities, by means of an understanding that merely follows the sound. But when, through the maturation of their accumulations and the progression of growth, the direct knowledge-and-vision of <s>Nirvāṇa</s> arises for those <s>Bodhisattvas</s> of faithful intention and those <s>Śrāvakas</s> who have seen the truths—then an understanding as it truly is arises in them too: 'This is that <s>Nirvāṇa</s> of all <s>Śrāvakas</s> and <s>Pratyekabuddhas</s>, whose qualities have been described by <s>Buddhas</s> and <s>Bodhisattvas</s>. But formerly, through the childishness of our wisdom, we did not have conviction as it truly is. There is, however, a semblance of it; there is a mere appearance of it.' They would be ashamed of their former conviction,

body.text: ritīyante paścimakaṃ yathābhūtādhimokṣaṃ niśritya / tadyathā kiñcidvyādhitaṃ puruṣaṃ kaścinmahāvaidyastasya prapyupasthitasya vyādheḥ praśamāyānulomikairbhaiṣajyairūpatiṣṭhet / sa ca vyādhitapuruṣo dīrghakālapratiniṣevaṇātteṣāṃ bhaiṣajyānāṃ tadadhimukta eva bhavet tadārāmaḥ / teṣveva sāradarśī bhavet / atha tasyaiva vyādhitapuruṣasya sa ca pūrvako vyādhistayā bhaiṣajyāsevayā vyupaśāmyedanyaścāpūrvo vyādhiranyabhaiṣajyasādhyaḥ prādurbhavet / atha sa mahāvaidyaḥ pūrvakasya ca vyādheḥ praśamaṃ paścimakasya cotpādamanyabhaiṣajyasādhyaṃ viditvā tañca pūrvakaṃ bhaiṣajyaprayogaṃ pratikṣipedanyaṃ cānulomikaṃ vyapadiśed bhaiṣajyam / sa bālo vyādhita puruṣaḥ pūrvabhaiṣajyādhimuktasteṣveva pathyasaṃjñī yenaiva mahāvaidyena tāni pūrvapaścimāni bhaiṣajyāni vyapadiṣṭāni / evamapyucyamānastena saṃmukhamapathyānyetāni pūrvakāṇi bhaiṣajyāni paścime vyādhāviti saṃpratyayena na gacchannāṣya vacanamabhiśraddhavyādevameva tadupamāste bālā bodhisattvāḥ śrāvakāśca veditavyāḥ / ye vyādhitapuruṣā eva kleśagrastā mahāvaidyasya tathāgatasyottarāduttaratarāmuttamatamāmuttānāduttānatarāṃ gambhīrād gambhīratarāṃ gambhīratamāṃ hīnādudārāmudāratarāmudāratamāṃ dharmadeśanāṃ samyagvyapadeśamavavādānuśāsanīṃ nāvataranti nādhimucyante na pratipadyante dharmasyānudharmam / tatra śrāddho bodhisattvaḥ śrāvako vā na kasmiṃścittathāgatabhāṣite vimatisandehamutpādayati / sa punaḥ sarvāṅgapariṣkārasusamāyuktamivājanyarathaṃ taṃ tathāgatabhāṣitaṃ dharmarathamabhirūhya kuśala iva sārathiryāvatī tena bhūmirgantavyā bhavatyanuprāptavyā tāṃ laghuladhveva gantā bhavatyadhandhāyamānaḥ /
body.translated_text: relying on the latter conviction that is in accordance with reality. It is as if a great physician were to attend to a certain sick person, treating the illness that had befallen him with medicines conducive to its pacification. That sick person, through long use of those medicines, would have conviction in them, delight in them, and see essence in them. Then suppose that very sick person's former illness were pacified through that course of medicine, but a new, different illness, treatable by different medicine, were to arise. Then that great physician, knowing the pacification of the former illness and the arising of the latter one treatable by different medicine, would reject the former course of medicine and prescribe another, appropriate medicine. That foolish sick person, having conviction in the former medicines and perceiving only those as wholesome—even when told face to face by that very great physician who had prescribed both the former and the latter medicines, 'These former medicines are unwholesome for the latter illness'—would not go along with that trust and would not believe his word. In just the same way, those foolish <s>Bodhisattvas</s> and <s>Śrāvakas</s> should be understood as being like the sick person—those who, afflicted by defilements, do not penetrate, do not have conviction in, and do not practice in accordance with the <s>Dharma</s> the <s>Tathāgata</s>'s progressively higher, subtler, deeper, and more sublime <s>Dharma</s>-teaching, correct instruction, and admonition. Therein, the faithful <s>Bodhisattva</s> or <s>Śrāvaka</s> does not generate doubt or uncertainty regarding anything spoken by the <s>Tathāgata</s>. Rather, mounting the <s>Dharma</s>-chariot spoken by the <s>Tathāgata</s>—like a well-equipped noble chariot with all its parts—like a skilled charioteer, whatever ground there is to be traversed and to be reached, he traverses it swiftly and without delay.

body.text: iti bodhisattvabhūmāvādhāre yogasthāne saptadaśamaṃ bodhipakṣyapaṭalam /
body.translated_text: Thus, in the <s>Bodhisattvabhūmi</s>, in the Foundation Section of Yoga, the seventeenth chapter, the <s>Bodhipakṣya-paṭala</s> (Chapter on the Factors of Awakening), [is completed].

body.text: uddānam /
body.translated_text: Summary verse (<s>uddāna</s>):

children.translated_text: The marvelous and the non-marvelous, equal-mindedness and benefiting,
reciprocation, and likewise the teacher; and unfailing endeavor.

body.text: pañceme bodhisattvāsyāścaryādbhūtā dharmā anuttare samyaksaṃbodhiyāne śikṣamāṇasya veditavyāḥ / katame pañca / niṣkāraṇavatsalatā sarvasattveṣu / sattvānāmevārthāya saṃsāre 'prameyaduḥkhasahiṣṇutā / bahukleśānāṃ durvineyānāṃ ca sattvānāṃ vinayopāyajñatā / paramadurvijñānatattvārthānupraveśaḥ / acintyaprabhāvatā ca / ime pañca bodhisattvānāmāścaryādbhutā dharmā asādhāraṇastadanyaiḥ sarvasattvaiḥ /
body.translated_text: These five marvelous and wonderful <s>dharmas</s> of the <s>Bodhisattva</s> training in the unsurpassed vehicle of perfect awakening should be understood. What are the five? Unconditional affection toward all beings; endurance of immeasurable suffering in <s>saṃsāra</s> for the very sake of beings; knowledge of the means of disciplining beings who have many defilements and are difficult to train; penetration into the reality of things (<s>tattvārtha</s>) that is supremely difficult to comprehend; and inconceivable power (<s>prabhāva</s>). These are the five marvelous and wonderful <s>dharmas</s> of <s>Bodhisattvas</s>, not shared with any other beings.

body.text: pañcemāni bodhisattvasyānāścaryāṇi yaiḥ samanvāgato bodhisattvaḥ anāścaryādbhutadharmasamanvāgata ityucyate / katamāni pañca / yad bodhisattvaḥ parahitahetukena duḥkhena sukhātmaka eva san kṛtsnaṃ parahitahetukaṃ duḥkhamabhyupagacchati / idaṃ bodhisattvasya prathamamanāścaryaṃ yena samanvāgato bodhisattvaḥ anāścaryādbhutadharmasamanvāgata ityucyate / punaraparaṃ yad bodhisattvaḥ saṃsāradoṣajño nirvāṇaguṇajña eva ca san sattvapariśuddhipriyastenaiva ca sukhātmakaḥ sattvapariśuddhimevādhipatiṃ kṛtvā saṃsāramabhyupagacchati / idaṃ bodhisattvasya dvitīyamanāścaryaṃ pūrvavat / punaraparaṃ yad bodhisattvastūṣṇīṃbhāva-sukharasajña eva san sattvapariśuddhipriyastenaiva ca sukhātmakaṃ sattvapariśuddhimevādhipatiṃ kṛtvā sattvānāṃ dharmedeśanāyai prayujyate / idaṃ bodhisattvasya tṛtīyamanāścaryaṃ pūrvavat / punaraparaṃ yad bodhisattvaḥ [ṣaṭ] pāramitopacitaṃ kuśalamūlaṃ sattvapariśuddhipriyastenaiva ca sukhātmakaḥ sattvapariśuddhimevādhipatiṃ kṛtvā sarvasattvānāmāśayataḥ samutsṛjati / na ca punastasya samutsargasya vipākenārthī bhavati / idaṃ bodhisattvasya caturthamanāśvaryaṃ pūrvavat / punaraparaṃ yad bodhisattvaḥ parakāryasvakārya iva sarvaparakāryārthakriyāsu saṃdṛśyate / idaṃ bodhisattvasya pañcamamanāścaryaṃ yena samanvāgato bodhisattvaḥ anāścaryādbhutadharmasamanvāgata ityucyate /
body.translated_text: These are the five non-marvels of the <s>Bodhisattva</s>, endowed with which the <s>Bodhisattva</s> is said to be 'endowed with non-marvelous and wonderful <s>dharmas</s>.' What are the five? First, that the <s>Bodhisattva</s>, being by nature one who experiences happiness, accepts the entirety of suffering caused by the welfare of others, for the sake of benefiting others—this is the first non-marvel of the <s>Bodhisattva</s>, endowed with which the <s>Bodhisattva</s> is said to be endowed with non-marvelous and wonderful <s>dharmas</s>. Furthermore, that the <s>Bodhisattva</s>, though knowing the faults of <s>saṃsāra</s> and knowing the virtues of <s>Nirvāṇa</s>, being one who delights in the purification of beings and who thereby experiences happiness, making the purification of beings his priority, accepts <s>saṃsāra</s>—this is the second non-marvel, as before. Furthermore, that the <s>Bodhisattva</s>, though knowing the bliss of the taste of silence, being one who delights in the purification of beings and who thereby experiences happiness, making the purification of beings his priority, applies himself to teaching the <s>Dharma</s> to beings—this is the third non-marvel, as before. Furthermore, that the <s>Bodhisattva</s>, being one who delights in the purification of beings and who thereby experiences happiness, making the purification of beings his priority, relinquishes to all beings from the depths of his intention the wholesome roots accumulated through the six <s>pāramitās</s>, yet does not desire the fruits of that relinquishment—this is the fourth non-marvel, as before. Furthermore, that the <s>Bodhisattva</s> is seen performing the tasks of others as though they were his own, in all activities for the welfare of others—this is the fifth non-marvel, endowed with which the <s>Bodhisattva</s> is said to be endowed with non-marvelous and wonderful <s>dharmas</s>.

body.text: pañcabhirākārairbodhisattvaḥ sarvasattveṣu samacitto veditavyaḥ / katamaiḥ pañcabhiḥ / prathamena bodhāya cittotpāda-praṇidhānena / tathā hi bodhisattvaḥ sarvasattvānāmarthe samaṃ taccittamutpādayati / anukampāsahagatena cittena samacitto bhavati / bodhisattvaḥ sarvasattveṣu ekaputraka iva premasahagatena cittena samacitto bhavati / bodhisattvaḥ sarvasattveṣu ekaputraka eva premasahagatena cittena samacitto bhavati / bodhisattvaḥ sarvasattveṣu pratītyasamutpanneṣu ca [sarva]saṃskāreṣu sattvasaṃjñeti viditvā bodhisattvo yā ekasya sattvasya dharmatā sā sarveṣāmiti dharmasamatānugatena cetasā sarvasattveṣu samacitto viharati / yathā caikasya sattvasyārthamācarati tathā sarveṣām / evaṃ hi bodhisattvaḥ sarvārthakriyāsahagatena cetasā sarvasattveṣu smacitto viharati / ebhiḥ pañcabhirākārairbodhisattvaḥ sattveṣu samacitto bhavati /
body.translated_text: The <s>Bodhisattva</s> should be understood as equal-minded toward all beings through five aspects. What are the five? Through the initial aspiration of generating the mind for awakening (<s>bodhicittotpāda</s>)—for the <s>Bodhisattva</s> generates that mind equally for the welfare of all beings. He is equal-minded toward all beings with a mind accompanied by compassion. The <s>Bodhisattva</s> is equal-minded toward all beings with a mind accompanied by love, as toward an only child. The <s>Bodhisattva</s> is equal-minded toward all beings with a mind accompanied by love, just as toward an only child. The <s>Bodhisattva</s>, knowing that beings and all conditioned formations (<s>saṃskāras</s>) are dependently arisen, and knowing that the perception of a 'being' is merely a conception—understanding that the <s>dharmatā</s> (nature of reality) of one being is the <s>dharmatā</s> of all—abides equal-minded toward all beings with a mind that follows the equality of <s>dharmas</s> (<s>dharmasamatā</s>). And just as he acts for the welfare of one being, so he acts for all. Thus the <s>Bodhisattva</s> abides equal-minded toward all beings with a mind accompanied by all beneficial activity. Through these five aspects, the <s>Bodhisattva</s> is equal-minded toward beings.

body.text: pañcabhirākārairbodhisattvānāṃ sattveṣu sarvopakārakriyā veditavyā / katamaiḥ pañcabhiḥ / samyagājīvavyapadeśopasaṃhāreṇa / vilomeṣu ca kṛtyeṣvarthopasaṃhiteṣvanulomopadeśopasaṃhāreṇa / anāthānāṃ ca duḥkhitānāṃ kṛpaṇānāmapratiśaraṇānāṃ sanāthakriyayā / sugatigamanāya mārgavyapadeśopasaṃhāreṇa yānatrayavyapadeśopasaṃhāreṇa ca /
body.translated_text: The <s>Bodhisattva</s>'s benefiting of all beings should be understood through five aspects. What are the five? Through providing guidance toward right livelihood; through providing instruction in accordance [with the <s>Dharma</s>] in matters that are contrary and connected with purpose; through acting as protector for those who are helpless, suffering, wretched, and without refuge; through providing guidance on the path to happy destinies; and through providing guidance on the three vehicles.

body.text: pañcabhirākāraiḥ sattvā upakāriṇo bodhisattvasya pratyupakāreṇa pratyupasthito bhavanti / katamaiḥ pañcabhiḥ / ātmānaṃ guṇaiḥ saṃyojayanti paraguṇādhānāya prayuktāro bhavanti / anātheṣu duḥkhiteṣu kṛpaṇeṣvapratiśaraṇeṣu sattveṣu sānāthyaṃ kurvanti / tathāgatān pūjayanti / tathāgatābhāṣitañca dharmamukhena vā lekhayitvā vā dhārayanti tañca pūjayanti /
body.translated_text: Beings who are benefactors of the <s>Bodhisattva</s> stand ready with five kinds of reciprocation. What are the five? They endow themselves with virtues, being engaged in establishing virtues in others. They act as protectors for beings who are helpless, suffering, wretched, and without refuge. They worship the <s>Tathāgatas</s>. And they retain the <s>Dharma</s> spoken by the <s>Tathāgatas</s>, either orally or in writing, and they worship it.

body.text: pañcemāni sthānāni bodhisattvena nityamevamāśaṃsitavyāni bhavanti / katamāni pañca / buddhotpādārāgaṇatā / teṣāmeva ca buddhānāmantikāt ṣaṭe pāramitā-bodhisattvapiṭakaśravaṇam / sarvākārasattvaparipācanapratiabalatā / anuttarasamyaksaṃbodhiprāptiḥ / abhisaṃbodheśca śrāvakasāmagrī /
body.translated_text: These five things should be constantly aspired to by the <s>Bodhisattva</s>. What are the five? The arising of <s>Buddhas</s> and the opportunity to attend [them]. Hearing the six <s>pāramitās</s> and the <s>Bodhisattva</s>-<s>piṭaka</s> from those very <s>Buddhas</s>. The ability to ripen beings in all aspects. The attainment of unsurpassed perfect awakening. And, upon awakening, the assembly of <s>Śrāvakas</s>.

body.text: pañcabhiḥ kāraṇaiḥ bodhisattvasya sattveṣvvabandhyo 'rthakriyā-prayogo bhavati / katamaiḥ pañcabhiḥ / iha bodhisattva ādita eva sattveṣu hitasukhaiṣī bhavati / tacca hitasukhaṃ yathābhūtaṃ prajānāti / aviparyastabuddhirbhavati / iti sarvaṃ pūrvavad veditavyaṃ yadyathā pūjāsevā 'pramāṇapaṭale /
body.translated_text: The <s>Bodhisattva</s>'s endeavor in beneficial activity toward beings is unfailing for five reasons. What are the five? Here, the <s>Bodhisattva</s> from the very beginning desires the benefit and happiness of beings. And he truly knows that benefit and happiness as it really is. He has an undistorted understanding. Thus, all the rest should be understood as before, just as in the <s>Pūjāsevāpramāṇa-paṭala</s> (Chapter on Worship, Service, and the Immeasurables).

body.text: uddānam /
body.translated_text: Summary verse (<s>uddāna</s>):

children.translated_text: Correct endeavor, decline, and likewise attainment of distinction,
the seeming and the genuine qualities, and likewise discipline.

body.text: pañcabhiḥ prayogairbodhisattvasya sarvasamyaksaṃprayoga saṃgraho veditavyaḥ katamaiḥ pañcabhiḥ / anurakṣaṇā-prayogeṇa / anavadyaprayogeṇa pratisaṃkhyānabalaprayogeṇa / adhyāśayaśuddhiprayogeṇa / niyatapatitaprayogeṇa ca /
body.translated_text: The <s>Bodhisattva</s>'s entire collection of correct endeavors should be understood through five endeavors. What are the five? Through the endeavor of safeguarding; through the endeavor of blamelessness; through the endeavor of the power of discernment (<s>pratisaṃkhyānabala</s>); through the endeavor of purity of superior intention (<s>adhyāśayaśuddhi</s>); and through the endeavor of being firmly established (<s>niyatapatita</s>).

body.text: tatra bodhisattvo 'nurakṣaṇā prayogeṇa medhāṃ rakṣati yena sahajena jñānena dharmān laghuladhvevodgṛhṇāti / smṛtiṃ rakṣati yayā smṛtyā udgṛhītān dharmān dhārayati / jñānamārakṣati yena jñānena dhṛtānāṃ dharmāṇāmarthamupaparīkṣate / samyak prajñayā pratividhyati medhāsmṛtibuddhihānabhāgīyanidānaparivarjanatayā sthitivṛddhibhāgīyanidānapratiniṣevaṇatayā ca / svacittamārakṣati indriyāṇāṃ guptadvāratayā / paracittamārakṣati samyakparicittānuvartanatayā / tatra bodhisattvasyānavadyaprayogo yaḥ kuśaleṣu dharmeṣvaviparītaścottaptaścāpramāṇaśca satataśca bodhipariṇāmitaśca / pratisaṃkhyānabalaprayogaḥ punarasya sarvasyāmadhimukticaryābhūmau draṣṭavyaḥ / [śuddhādhyāśayaprayogaḥ] śuddhādhyāśayabhūmau caryā pratipattibhūmau ca draṣṭavyaḥ / niyatipatitaprayogo niyatāyāṃ bhūmau niṣṭhāgamanabhūmau ca draṣṭavyaḥ / ivamebhiḥ pañcabhiḥ prayogairbodhisattvasya sarvasamyakprayogasaṃgraho bhavati /
body.translated_text: There, the <s>Bodhisattva</s>, through the application of guarding (<s>anurakṣaṇā</s>), guards his intelligence (<s>medhā</s>) — the innate knowledge by which he swiftly grasps <s>dharmas</s>. He guards his memory (<s>smṛti</s>) — the mindfulness by which he retains <s>dharmas</s> that have been grasped. He guards his knowledge (<s>jñāna</s>) — the knowledge by which he investigates the meaning of <s>dharmas</s> that have been retained. He penetrates rightly with wisdom, by avoiding the causes conducive to the decline of intelligence, memory, and understanding, and by cultivating the causes conducive to their stability and increase. He guards his own mind through guarding the doors of the sense-faculties. He guards the minds of others by properly adapting to their thoughts. There, the <s>Bodhisattva</s>'s blameless application (<s>anavadyaprayoga</s>) is that which, with respect to wholesome <s>dharmas</s>, is undistorted, refined, immeasurable, constant, and dedicated to awakening. The application of the power of analytical reflection (<s>pratisaṃkhyānabalaprayoga</s>) should be seen on the stage of aspiration-conduct (<s>adhimukticaryābhūmi</s>) in its entirety. The application of pure superior intention (<s>śuddhādhyāśayaprayoga</s>) should be seen on the stage of pure superior intention (<s>śuddhādhyāśayabhūmi</s>) and on the stage of practice-conduct (<s>pratipattibhūmi</s>). The application of determined course (<s>niyatipatitaprayoga</s>) should be seen on the determined stage (<s>niyatā bhūmi</s>) and the stage of final attainment (<s>niṣṭhāgamanabhūmi</s>). Thus, through these five applications, the <s>Bodhisattva</s>'s entire collection of correct applications is encompassed.

body.text: pañceme bodhisattvasya hānabhāgīyā dharmā veditavyāḥ / katame pañca / agauravatā dharme dharmabhāṇake ca / pramādakausīdyam / kleśa-āsevā 'dhivāsanatā / duścarita-āsevā 'dhivāsanatā / tadanyaiśca bodhisattvaiḥ saha paritulanābhimānatā dharmaviparyāsābhimānatā ca /
body.translated_text: These five <s>dharmas</s> of the <s>Bodhisattva</s> should be understood as conducing to decline (<s>hānabhāgīya</s>). Which five? Disrespect toward the <s>Dharma</s> and toward teachers of the <s>Dharma</s>; heedlessness and indolence; habitual indulgence in and tolerance of afflictions (<s>kleśa</s>); habitual indulgence in and tolerance of misconduct; and the conceit of comparing oneself with other <s>Bodhisattvas</s> and the conceit of holding distorted <s>dharmas</s> [as correct].

body.text: pañceme bodhisattvasya dharmā viśeṣabhāgīyā veditavyāḥ / te punareṣāmeva pañcānāṃ kṛṣṇapakṣyāṇāṃ dharmāṇāṃ yathākramaṃ viparyayeṇa veditavyāḥ /
body.translated_text: These five <s>dharmas</s> of the <s>Bodhisattva</s> should be understood as conducing to distinction (<s>viśeṣabhāgīya</s>). They should be understood as the exact opposites, in order, of those five dark-side <s>dharmas</s>.

body.text: pañceme bodhisattvānāṃ guṇapratirūpakaḥ bodhisattvadoṣā veditavyāḥ / katame pañca / raudraduḥśīleṣu sattveṣu tato nidānamapakārakriyā / kuhakasyeryāpathasampattikralpanā / lokāyatairmantraistīrthikaśāstrapravisaṃyuttairjñātra pratilambhaḥ paṇḍitasaṃkhyā-gamanatā ca / sāvadyasya ca dānādikasya kuśalasyādhyācāraḥ / saddharmapratirūpakāṇāṃ ca / rocanā deśanā vyavasthāpanā /
body.translated_text: These five faults of <s>Bodhisattvas</s>, which are counterfeits of [genuine] qualities, should be understood. Which five? Causing harm to beings who are fierce and immoral on account of their [fiereceness and immorality]; the pretense of deportmental perfection by a hypocrite; the acquisition of a reputation as learned and the attainment of being counted among the wise through <s>Lokāyata</s> [materialist philosophy], mantras, and treatises connected with non-Buddhist systems; the practice of blameworthy generosity and other [seeming] wholesome [acts]; and the promotion, teaching, and establishment of counterfeits of the True <s>Dharma</s>.

body.text: pañceme bodhisattvasya bhūtā bodhisattvaguṇā veditavyāḥ / katame pañca / raudraduḥśīleṣu sattveṣu viśeṣeṇa kāruṇyacittatā / prakṛtyā īryāpathasaṃpannatā / tathāgatapraṇītenāgamādhigamena jñātrapratilambhaḥ / paṇḍitasaṃkhyāgamanatā ca / anavadyasya ca dānādikasya kuśalasya kriyā / saddharmasya ca prakāśanā saddharmapratirūpakāṇāṃ ca pratikṣepaṇatā /
body.translated_text: These five genuine qualities of <s>Bodhisattvas</s> should be understood. Which five? Having a mind especially [filled with] compassion toward beings who are fierce and immoral; natural perfection of deportment; the acquisition of a reputation as learned and the attainment of being counted among the wise through the scriptural tradition (<s>āgama</s>) and realization (<s>adhigama</s>) taught by the <s>Tathāgata</s>; the practice of blameless generosity and other wholesome [acts]; and the illumination of the True <s>Dharma</s> and the refutation of counterfeits of the True <s>Dharma</s>.

body.text: daśasu sthāneṣu samāsato bodhisattvā vineyān sattvān samyageva vinayanti / katameṣu daśasu / duścaritaviveke / [kāmaviveke] / āpattyana dhyācāravyutthāne / indriyairguptadvāratāyām / saṃprājanavihāritāyām / saṃsargaviveke praviviktasyāsadvitarkaṃviveke / āvaraṇaviveke / kleśaparyavasthānaviveke / kleśapakṣadauṣṭhulyaviveke ca /
body.translated_text: In ten areas, in brief, <s>Bodhisattvas</s> rightly discipline trainable beings. In which ten? Seclusion from misconduct; seclusion from sensual desires; rising from offenses and transgressions; guarding the doors of the sense-faculties; dwelling with clear comprehension; seclusion from [unwholesome] association; seclusion of one who has retired from evil thoughts; seclusion from obscurations; seclusion from the dominance of afflictions; and seclusion from the mental rigidity (<s>dauṣṭhulya</s>) belonging to the side of afflictions.

body.text: uddānam /
body.translated_text: The summary verse (<s>uddāna</s>):

children.translated_text: Prediction, the determined fall, and the essential duties;
the constant duties and lastly the foremost [dharmas].

body.text: ṣaḍbhirākāraiḥ samāsatastathāgatā bodhisattvamanuttarāyāṃ samyaksaṃbodhau vyākurvanti / katamaiḥ ṣaḍbhiḥ / gotrasthamanutpāditacittam / tathotpāditaṃ cittam sammukhāvasthitam / viparokṣāvasthitam / parimitaṃ kālamiyatā kālenānuttarāṃ samyaksaṃbodhimabhisaṃbhotsyata iti / aparimitakālaṃ vyākurvanti na tu kālaniyama kurvanti /
body.translated_text: In six aspects, in brief, <s>Tathāgatas</s> predict a <s>Bodhisattva</s>'s [attainment of] unsurpassed perfect awakening. In which six? [They predict] one who possesses the lineage (<s>gotra</s>) but has not yet generated the [awakening-]mind; likewise, one who has generated the mind; one who is present face to face; one who is present in absence; [they predict] for a limited period of time — 'Within such-and-such a period, he will fully awaken to unsurpassed perfect awakening'; [and they predict] for an unlimited period of time, without specifying a time-limit.

body.text: traya ime bodhisattvasya niyatipātāḥ / katame trayaḥ / gotrastha eva bodhisattvo niyatipatita ityucyate / tatkasya hetoḥ / bhavyo 'sau pratyayānāsādya niyatamanuttarāṃ samyaksaṃbodhimabhisaṃboddhum / punarekatyo bodhisattvo niyataṃ cittamutpādayatyanuttarāyāṃ samyaksaṃbodhau na punastāvatpratyudāvartayati yāvadanuttarāṃ samyaksaṃbodhimabhisaṃbudhyate / punarbodhisattvo vaśitāprāptaḥ sarvāṃ sattvārthacaryāṃ yathecchati yathārabhate tathaivābandhyāṃ karoti / ta ete trayo niyatipātā bhavanti / gotrasthaniyatipātaḥ / cittotpādaniyatipātaḥ / abandhya-caryā-niyatipātaśca / tatra paścimaṃ niyatipātamārabhya tathāgatā niyatipatitaṃ bodhisattvaṃ vyākurvāṇā vyākurvanti /
body.translated_text: There are these three determined falls (<s>niyatipāta</s>) of the <s>Bodhisattva</s>. Which three? The <s>Bodhisattva</s> who merely possesses the lineage (<s>gotra</s>) is called 'one who has fallen into determination.' For what reason? Because that one is capable, upon encountering conditions, of definitely fully awakening to unsurpassed perfect awakening. Furthermore, a certain <s>Bodhisattva</s> generates a determined mind toward unsurpassed perfect awakening and does not turn back until he fully awakens to unsurpassed perfect awakening. Furthermore, the <s>Bodhisattva</s> who has obtained mastery (<s>vaśitā</s>) makes all his welfare-activity for beings infallible — whatever he wishes and whatever he undertakes, that very [result] he accomplishes. These are the three determined falls: the determined fall of possessing the lineage, the determined fall of generating the [awakening-]mind, and the determined fall of infallible conduct. There, beginning from the last determined fall, <s>Tathāgatas</s>, when predicting a <s>Bodhisattva</s> who has fallen into determination, make their prediction.

body.text: pañcemāni sthānāni bodhisattvasyāvaśyakaraṇīyāni bhavanti yānyakṛtvā bodhisattvaḥ abhavyo bhavatyanuttarāṃ samyaksaṃbodhimabhisaṃboddhum / katamāni pañca / prathamaścittotpādaḥ / sattveṣvanukampā / uttaptavīryam / sarvavidyāsthāneṣu yogyatā / akhedaśca /
body.translated_text: These five things are essential tasks that the <s>Bodhisattva</s> must perform, without which a <s>Bodhisattva</s> is incapable of fully awakening to unsurpassed perfect awakening. Which five? The initial generation of the [awakening-]mind; compassion toward beings; refined vigor; expertise in all fields of knowledge; and indefatigability.

body.text: pañcemāni bodhisattvasya sthānāni sātatyakaraṇīyāni / katamāni pañca / apramādo bodhisattvasya sātatyakaraṇīyaḥ / anātheṣu sattveṣu [duḥkhiteṣu ca] apratiśaraṇeṣu sanāthakriyā / tathāgatapūjā skhalitaparijñānam / sarvakriyācāravihāramanasikāreṣu bodhicittapūrvaṅgamatā bodhisattvasya pañcamaṃ sātatyakaraṇīyam /
body.translated_text: These five things are constant duties of the <s>Bodhisattva</s>. Which five? Non-heedlessness (<s>apramāda</s>) is the <s>Bodhisattva</s>'s constant duty. Acting as protector for beings who are helpless, suffering, and without refuge [is the second]. Worship of the <s>Tathāgata</s> [is the third]. Recognition of one's own stumblings [is the fourth]. And the fifth constant duty of the <s>Bodhisattva</s> is making the awakening-mind (<s>bodhicitta</s>) the forerunner of all his activities, conduct, abiding, and mental attention.

body.text: daśeme dharmā bodhisattvānāṃ pradhānasammatā yān bodhisattvā agrato dhārayantyagryaprajñaptiṣu ca prajñapayanti / katame daśa / bodhisattvagotraṃ sarvagotrāṇāṃ pradhānam / prathamaścittotpādaḥ sarvasamyak praṇidhānānaṃ pradhānam / vīryaṃ ca prajñā ca sarvapāramitānāṃ pradhānam / priyavāditā sarvasaṃgrahavastūnāṃ pradhānam / tathāgataḥ sarvasattvānāṃ pradhānam / karūṇā 'pramāṇānāṃ pradhānam / caturthaṃ dhyānaṃ [sarvadhyānānāṃ pradhānam /] trayāṇāṃ samādhīnāṃ śūnyatāsamādhiḥ pradhānam / sarvasamāpattīnāṃ
body.translated_text: These ten <s>dharmas</s> are held as foremost by <s>Bodhisattvas</s> — those which <s>Bodhisattvas</s> place at the head and designate among the foremost designations. Which ten? The <s>Bodhisattva</s>-lineage (<s>gotra</s>) is foremost among all lineages. The initial generation of the [awakening-]mind is foremost among all right aspirations. Vigor and wisdom are foremost among all <s>pāramitās</s>. Loving speech (<s>priyavāditā</s>) is foremost among all means of gathering [beings] (<s>saṃgrahavastu</s>). The <s>Tathāgata</s> is foremost among all beings. Compassion (<s>karuṇā</s>) is foremost among the immeasurables (<s>apramāṇa</s>). The fourth <s>dhyāna</s> is foremost among all <s>dhyānas</s>. Among the three <s>samādhis</s>, the emptiness-<s>samādhi</s> (<s>śūnyatāsamādhi</s>) is foremost. Among all attainments (<s>samāpatti</s>),

body.text: nirodhasamāpattiḥ pradhānam / sarvopāyakauśalyānāṃ viśuddhamupāyakauśalyaṃ yathānirdiṣṭaṃ pradhānam /
body.translated_text: the attainment of cessation (<s>nirodhasamāpatti</s>) is foremost. Among all types of skill in means (<s>upāyakauśalya</s>), the pure skill in means as described [above] is foremost.

body.text: uddānam /
body.translated_text: The summary verse (<s>uddāna</s>):
