body.text: prajñapteḥ syādvyavasthānaṃ dharmāṇāmeṣaṇā tathā / yathābhūtaparijñānamaprameyāstathaiva ca //
body.translated_text: The establishment of designations, the investigation of <s>dharmas</s>, likewise the true comprehension as it really is, and the immeasurables;

children.translated_text: the fruit of teaching and its greatness, the vehicle-collection;
<s>Bodhisattvas</s> should be known [as] ten, and likewise the name-designations.

body.text: catvārīmāni bodhisattvānāṃ prajñaptivyavasthānāni yāniṃ bodhisattvā eva samyak prajñapayanti vyavasthāpayanti tathāgatā vā / na tvanyaḥ kaściddevabhūto vā manuṣyabhūto vā śramaṇabrāhmaṇabhūto vānyatraitebhya evaṃ śrutvā / katamāni catvāri / dharmaprajñaptivyavasthānaṃ satyaprajñaptivyavattthānaṃ yuktiprajñaptivyavasthānaṃ yānaprajñaptivyavasthānañca /
body.translated_text: There are these four designation-establishments (<s>prajñaptivyavasthāna</s>) of <s>Bodhisattvas</s>, which <s>Bodhisattvas</s> alone rightly designate and establish — or <s>Tathāgatas</s>. But no other being — whether god, human, or <s>śramaṇa</s> or <s>brāhmaṇa</s> — [can do so,] except by having heard from these very [<s>Bodhisattvas</s> and <s>Tathāgatas</s>]. Which four? The establishment of the designation of <s>Dharma</s> (<s>dharmaprajñaptivyavasthāna</s>); the establishment of the designation of truth (<s>satyaprajñaptivyavasthāna</s>); the establishment of the designation of reasoning (<s>yuktiprajñaptivyavasthāna</s>); and the establishment of the designation of vehicles (<s>yānaprajñaptivyavasthāna</s>).

body.text: tatra yā dvādaśāṅgasya sūtrādikasya vacogatasyānupūrvaracanā anupūrvavyavasthānasamāyogaḥ / idamucyate dharmaprajñaptivyavasthānam /
body.translated_text: There, the sequential arrangement and sequential organization of the twelvefold canonical collection (<s>dvādaśāṅga</s>) beginning with <s>sūtra</s> — consisting of speech [of the <s>Buddha</s>] — this is called the establishment of the designation of <s>Dharma</s>.

body.text: satyaprajñaptivyavasthānaṃ punaranekavidham / avitathārthena tāvadekameva satyaṃ na dvitīyamasti / dvividhaṃ satyam / saṃvṛtisatyaṃ paramārthasatyaṃ ca / trividhaṃ satyam / lakṣaṇasatyaṃ vāksatyaṃ kriyāsatyaṃ ca / [caturvidhaṃ satyam /] duḥkhasatyaṃ yāvanmārgasatyam / pañcavidhaṃ [satyam /] hetusatyaṃ phalasatyaṃ jñānasatyaṃ jñeyasatyaṃ agryasatyaṃ ca / ṣaḍvidhaṃ [satyam] / satyasatyaṃ mṛṣāsatyaṃ parijñeyasatyaṃ prahātavyasatyaṃ sākṣātkartavyasatyaṃ bhāvayitavyasatyaṃ ca / saptavidhaṃ satyam / āsvādasatyaṃ ādīnavasatyaṃ niḥsaraṇasatyaṃ dharmatāsatyaṃ adhimuktisatyaṃ āryāṇāṃ satyaṃ anāryāṇāṃ satyaṃ ca / aṣṭavidhaṃ [satyaṃ] / saṃskāraduḥkhatāsatyaṃ vipariṇāmaduḥkhatāsatyaṃ duḥkhaduḥkhatāsatyaṃ pravṛttisatyaṃ nivṛtisatyaṃ saṃkleśasatyaṃ vyavadānasatyaṃ samyakprayogasatyaṃ ca / navavidhaṃ [satyam] / anityasatyaṃ duḥkhasatyaṃ śūnyatāsatyaṃ nairātmyasatyaṃ [bhavatṛṣṇāsatyaṃ]
body.translated_text: The establishment of the designation of truth (<s>satyaprajñaptivyavasthāna</s>) is furthermore manifold. First, in the sense of being non-false, truth is one alone — there is no second. Twofold is truth: conventional truth (<s>saṃvṛtisatya</s>) and ultimate truth (<s>paramārthasatya</s>). Threefold is truth: truth of characteristics (<s>lakṣaṇasatya</s>), truth of speech (<s>vāksatya</s>), and truth of action (<s>kriyāsatya</s>). Fourfold is truth: the truth of suffering (<s>duḥkhasatya</s>) up to the truth of the path (<s>mārgasatya</s>). Fivefold is truth: the truth of cause (<s>hetusatya</s>), the truth of fruit (<s>phalasatya</s>), the truth of knowledge (<s>jñānasatya</s>), the truth of the knowable (<s>jñeyasatya</s>), and the supreme truth (<s>agryasatya</s>). Sixfold is truth: the truth of truth (<s>satyasatya</s>), the truth of falsehood (<s>mṛṣāsatya</s>), the truth to be fully known (<s>parijñeyasatya</s>), the truth to be abandoned (<s>prahātavyasatya</s>), the truth to be directly realized (<s>sākṣātkartavyasatya</s>), and the truth to be cultivated (<s>bhāvayitavyasatya</s>). Sevenfold is truth: the truth of gratification (<s>āsvādasatya</s>), the truth of danger (<s>ādīnavasatya</s>), the truth of escape (<s>niḥsaraṇasatya</s>), the truth of the nature of reality (<s>dharmatāsatya</s>), the truth of conviction (<s>adhimuktisatya</s>), the truth of the noble ones (<s>āryāṇāṃ satya</s>), and the truth of the non-noble (<s>anāryāṇāṃ satya</s>). Eightfold is truth: the truth of the suffering of formations (<s>saṃskāraduḥkhatā</s>), the truth of the suffering of change (<s>vipariṇāmaduḥkhatā</s>), the truth of the suffering of suffering (<s>duḥkhaduḥkhatā</s>), the truth of arising (<s>pravṛtti</s>), the truth of cessation (<s>nivṛtti</s>), the truth of defilement (<s>saṃkleśa</s>), the truth of purification (<s>vyavadāna</s>), and the truth of correct application (<s>samyakprayoga</s>). Ninefold is truth: the truth of impermanence (<s>anitya</s>), the truth of suffering (<s>duḥkha</s>), the truth of emptiness (<s>śūnyatā</s>), the truth of non-self (<s>nairātmya</s>), the truth of craving for existence (<s>bhavatṛṣṇā</s>),

body.text: vibhavatṛṣṇāsatyaṃ tatprahāṇopāyasatyaṃ sopadhiśeṣanirvāṇasatyaṃ nirupadhiśeṣanirvāṇasatyaṃ [ca] / daśavidhaṃ satyam / aupakramikaduḥkhasatyaṃ bhogavaikalyaduḥkhasatyaṃ dhāturvaiṣamyaduḥkhasatyaṃ priyavipariṇāmaduḥkhasatyaṃ dauṣṭhulyaduḥkhasatyaṃ karmasatyaṃ kleśasatyaṃ tathā śravaṇayoniśomanaskārasatyaṃ samyakdṛṣṭisatyaṃ samyagdṛṣṭiphalasatyaṃ ceti / idamucyate bodhisattvānāṃ satyaprajñaptivyavasthānam / prabhedaśaḥ punaretadapramāṇa veditavyam /
body.translated_text: the truth of craving for non-existence (<s>vibhavatṛṣṇā</s>), the truth of the means to their abandonment (<s>tatprahāṇopāya</s>), the truth of <s>nirvāṇa</s> with remainder (<s>sopadhiśeṣanirvāṇa</s>), and the truth of <s>nirvāṇa</s> without remainder (<s>nirupadhiśeṣanirvāṇa</s>). Tenfold is truth: the truth of intentionally caused suffering (<s>aupakramika</s>), the truth of the suffering of deprivation of enjoyments (<s>bhogavaikalya</s>), the truth of the suffering of elemental imbalance (<s>dhāturvaiṣamya</s>), the truth of the suffering of the change of the beloved (<s>priyavipariṇāma</s>), the truth of the suffering of mental rigidity (<s>dauṣṭhulya</s>), the truth of action (<s>karma</s>), the truth of afflictions (<s>kleśa</s>), the truth of hearing and proper attention (<s>śravaṇa-yoniśomanaskāra</s>), the truth of right view (<s>samyagdṛṣṭi</s>), and the truth of the fruit of right view (<s>samyagdṛṣṭiphala</s>). This is called the establishment of the designation of truth of <s>Bodhisattvas</s>. In terms of detailed classification, this should be understood as immeasurable.

body.text: catasro yuktayo yuktiprajñaptivyavasthānamityucyate / tāsāṃ punaḥ pravibhāgaḥ pūrvavadveditavyaḥ /
body.translated_text: The four reasonings (<s>yukti</s>) are called the establishment of the designation of reasoning (<s>yuktiprajñaptivyavasthāna</s>). Their detailed classification should be understood as before.

body.text: trayāṇāṃ yānānāṃ ekaikasya saptabhirākāraiḥ prajñaptivyavasthānam / śrāvakayānasya pratyekabuddhayānasya mahāyānasya yānaprajñaptivyavasthānamityucyate / caturṣvāryasatyeṣu yā prajñā tasyā eva ca prajñāyā ya āśrayaḥ ālambanaṃ sahāyaḥ karma saṃbhārastasyā eva ca prajñāyā yat phalam ebhiḥ saptabhirākāraiḥ śrāvakayānaprajñaptivyavasthānaṃ sākalyena veditavyam / yathā śrāvakayānamevaṃ pratyekabuddhayānaprajñaptivyavasthānam / nirabhilāpyaṃ vastvālambanīkṛtya sarvadharmeṣu yā tathatā nirvikalpasamatā niryāṇatā prajñā tasyā eva ca prajñāyā ya āśraya ālambanaṃ sahāyaḥ karma sambhārastasyā eva ca prajñāyā yatphalam / ityebhiḥ saptabhirākārairmahāyānaprajñaptivyavasthānaṃ veditavyam / atītānāgatapratyutpanneṣvadhvaṣu ye kecidbodhisattvāḥ samyakprajñaptivyavasthānaṃ kṛtavantaḥ kariṣyanti kurvanti vā punaḥ sarve ta ebhiścatubhirvastubhiḥ / nāta uttari nāto bhūyaḥ /
body.translated_text: For each of the three vehicles, the establishment of the designation is through seven aspects. The establishment of the designation of the <s>Śrāvaka</s>-vehicle, the <s>Pratyekabuddha</s>-vehicle, and the <s>Mahāyāna</s> is called the establishment of the designation of vehicles. With respect to the Four Noble Truths, that very wisdom [which knows them]; the basis of that wisdom; its object; its aid; its function; its accumulation; and the fruit of that wisdom — through these seven aspects, the establishment of the designation of the <s>Śrāvaka</s>-vehicle should be understood in its entirety. Just as the <s>Śrāvaka</s>-vehicle, so too the establishment of the designation of the <s>Pratyekabuddha</s>-vehicle [should be understood]. Taking the inexpressible (<s>nirabhilāpya</s>) reality as its object, that wisdom which, with respect to all <s>dharmas</s>, [realizes] their suchness (<s>tathatā</s>), non-conceptual equality (<s>nirvikalpasamatā</s>), and the way of deliverance (<s>niryāṇatā</s>); the basis of that wisdom; its object; its aid; its function; its accumulation; and the fruit of that wisdom — through these seven aspects, the establishment of the designation of the <s>Mahāyāna</s> should be understood. Whatever <s>Bodhisattvas</s> in the past, future, and present have made, will make, or are making the correct establishment of designations — all of them [do so] through these four topics. There is nothing beyond this, nothing more.

body.text: catvārīmāni bodhisattvānāṃ sarvadharmāṇāṃ yathābhūtaparijñāyai paryeṣaṇāvastūni / katamāni catvāri / nāmaparyeṣaṇā / vastuparyeṣaṇā / svabhāvaprajñaptiparyeṣaṇā / viśeṣaprajñaptiparyeṣaṇā ca / eṣāṃ ca vibhāgaḥ pūrvavadveditavyaḥ tadyathā tattvārthapaṭale /
body.translated_text: There are these four topics of investigation (<s>paryeṣaṇāvastu</s>) for <s>Bodhisattvas</s>' true comprehension of all <s>dharmas</s> as they really are. Which four? Investigation of names (<s>nāmaparyeṣaṇā</s>); investigation of objects (<s>vastuparyeṣaṇā</s>); investigation of the designation of intrinsic nature (<s>svabhāvaprajñaptiparyeṣaṇā</s>); and investigation of the designation of distinctions (<s>viśeṣaprajñaptiparyeṣaṇā</s>). The detailed classification of these should be understood as before — namely, as in the Chapter on the True Nature of Reality (<s>Tattvārthapaṭala</s>).

body.text: catvārīmāni bodhisattvānāṃ sarvadharmāṇāṃ yathābhūtaparijñānāni / katamāni catvāri / nāmaparyeṣaṇāgataṃ yathābhūtaparijñānaṃ vastuparyeṣaṇāgataṃ svabhāvaprajñaptiparyeṣaṇāgataṃ viśeṣaprajñaptiparyeṣaṇāgataṃ yathābhūtaparijñānam / eṣāmapi vibhāgaḥ pūrvavadveditavyaḥ / [tadyathā tattvārthapaṭale /] /
body.translated_text: These are the four true complete knowledges of all <s>dharmas</s> for <s>Bodhisattvas</s>. What are the four? The true complete knowledge arrived at through investigation of names (<s>nāmaparyeṣaṇā</s>), the true complete knowledge arrived at through investigation of things (<s>vastuparyeṣaṇā</s>), the true complete knowledge arrived at through investigation of own-nature designation (<s>svabhāvaprajñaptiparyeṣaṇā</s>), and the true complete knowledge arrived at through investigation of distinction designation (<s>viśeṣaprajñaptiparyeṣaṇā</s>). The classification of these too is to be understood as before [namely, as in the Chapter on the True Meaning of Reality (<s>Tattvārthapaṭala</s>)].

body.text: pañceme aprameyā bodhisattvānāṃ sarvakauśalyakriyāyai saṃvartante / katame pañca / sattvadhāturaprameyo lokadhāturaprameyo dharmadhāturaprameyaḥ / vineyadhāturaprameyo vineyopāyaścāprameyaḥ / catuḥṣaṣṭiḥ sattvanikāyāḥ sattvadhātustadyathā manomapyāṃ bhūmau / santānabhedena punaraprameyaḥ / daśasu dikṣuprameyā aprameyanāmalokadhātavastadyathā iyaṃ sahā nāma lokadhāturyasya nāmnā brahmā sahāṃpatirityucyate / kuśalākuśalāvyākṛtā dharmāḥ prabhedanayenāprameyā veditavyāḥ / syādekavidho vineyaḥ sarvasattvā vineyā iti kṛtvā / syād dvividhaḥ / sakalabandhano vikalabandhanaśca / syāt trividhaḥ mṛdvindriyo madhyendriyastīkṣṇendriyaśca / caturvidhaḥ / kṣatriyo brāhmaṇo vaiśyaḥ śūdraśca / pañcavidhaḥ / rāgacarito dveṣacarito mohacarito mānacarito vitarkacaritaśca / ṣaḍvidhaḥ / gṛhī pravrajitaḥ aparipakvaḥ paripakvo ['vimuktaśca] vimuktaśca / saptavidhaḥ / pratihato madhyasthaḥ vipañcitajñaḥ uddhaṭitajñaḥ tadātvavineyaḥ āpattivineyaḥ pratyayahāryaścavineyo yādṛśān pratyayān labhate tathā tathā pariṇamati / aṣṭavidhaḥ / aṣṭau pariṣadaḥ / kṣatriyapariṣadamādiṃ kṛtvā yāvadbrahmapariṣat / navavidhaḥ / tathāgatavineyaḥ śrāvakapratyekabuddhavineyaḥ bodhisattvavineyaḥ kṛcchrasādhyaḥ [akṛcchrasādhyaḥ] ślakṣṇasādhyaḥ avasādanā-sādhyaḥ dūre vineyaḥ antike ca vineyaḥ / daśavidhaḥ / nārakaḥ tairyakyonikaḥ yāmalaukikaḥ kāmāvacaro divyamānuṣyakaḥ āntarābhavikaḥ rūpī arūpī sajñī asaṃjñī naivasajñīnāsaṃjñī ca / ayaṃ tāvat prakārabhedena pañcapañcāśadākāraḥ / apramāṇastu santānaprabhedena veditavyaḥ / tatra
body.translated_text: These five immeasurables conduce to the <s>Bodhisattvas</s>' activity of complete skill. What are the five? The realm of beings (<s>sattvadhātu</s>) is immeasurable, the world-realm (<s>lokadhātu</s>) is immeasurable, the <s>dharma</s>-realm (<s>dharmadhātu</s>) is immeasurable, the realm of those to be trained (<s>vineyadhātu</s>) is immeasurable, and the means of training (<s>vineyopāya</s>) is immeasurable. There are sixty-four classes of beings constituting the realm of beings, as in the Mind-Made Stage (<s>manomayā bhūmi</s>). Moreover, it is immeasurable by differentiation of individual continuums. In the ten directions there are immeasurable world-realms of immeasurable names—for example, this world-realm called <s>Sahā</s>, after whose name <s>Brahmā</s> is called <s>Sahāṃpati</s>. Wholesome, unwholesome, and indeterminate <s>dharmas</s> are to be known as immeasurable through the method of classification. Those to be trained may be of one kind, taking all beings as trainable. They may be of two kinds: those with complete fetters and those with incomplete fetters. Of three kinds: those of mild faculties, medium faculties, and sharp faculties. Of four kinds: <s>Kṣatriya</s>, <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>, <s>Vaiśya</s>, and <s>Śūdra</s>. Of five kinds: those of passion-temperament, hatred-temperament, delusion-temperament, pride-temperament, and discursive-thought-temperament. Of six kinds: householder, renunciant, unripened, ripened, unliberated, and liberated. Of seven kinds: the opposed, the neutral, one of detailed knowledge, one of prompt knowledge, one trainable on the spot, one trainable through transgression, and one guided by conditions—who transforms according to whatever conditions he encounters. Of eight kinds: the eight assemblies, beginning with the assembly of <s>Kṣatriyas</s> up to the assembly of <s>Brahmā</s>. Of nine kinds: trainable by a <s>Tathāgata</s>, trainable by a <s>Śrāvaka</s> or <s>Pratyekabuddha</s>, trainable by a <s>Bodhisattva</s>, achievable with difficulty, achievable without difficulty, achievable gently, achievable through humbling, trainable from afar, and trainable nearby. Of ten kinds: hell-being, animal-born, of <s>Yama</s>'s world, desire-realm divine-human, intermediate-existence being, form-being, formless-being, percipient being, non-percipient being, and one who is neither percipient nor non-percipient. Thus far, by differentiation of types, there are fifty-five aspects; but by differentiation of individual continuums, they are to be known as immeasurable. Therein,

body.text: sattvadhātu vineyadhātvoḥ kiṃ nānākaraṇam sattvadhāturaviśeṣeṇa sarvasattvā gotrasthāścāgotrasthāśca / ye purnagotrasthā eva tāsu tāṣvavasthāsu vartante / sa vineyadhāturityucyate / vineyopāyaḥ punaḥ pūrvavadyathā nirdiṣṭo veditavyaḥ / so 'pi cāprabheyaḥ prakārabhedataḥ /
body.translated_text: what is the difference between the realm of beings (<s>sattvadhātu</s>) and the realm of those to be trained (<s>vineyadhātu</s>)? The realm of beings, without distinction, includes all beings—those established in the spiritual lineage (<s>gotra</s>) and those not established in it. But those who are established in the lineage alone, existing in their various states—that is called the realm of those to be trained. The means of training, moreover, is to be understood as previously taught; and that too is immeasurable by differentiation of types.

body.text: ta ete 'bhisamasya pañcāprameyā bhavanti / tatkasya hetoḥ / iha bodhisattvo yeṣāṃ sattvānāmarthe prayujyate sa prathamo 'prameyaḥ / tānpunaḥ sattvān yatrasthānupalabhate / sa dvitīyo 'prameyaḥ tānpunaḥ sattvāṃsteṣu teṣu lokadhātuṣu yairdharmaiḥ saṃkliśyamānāṃśca viśudhyamānāṃścopalabhate / sa tṛtīyo 'prameyaḥ / tebhyaśca sattvebhyo yānsattvān bhavyān śakyarupānatyantaduḥkhavimokṣāya paśyati / sa caturtho 'prameyaḥ / yaścopāyasteṣāmeva sattvānāṃ vimokṣāya sa pañcamoprameyaḥ / tasmādete pañcāprameyā bodhisattvānāṃ sarva[kauśala]kriyāyai saṃvartante /
body.translated_text: In summary, these five are immeasurable. For what reason? Here, the beings for whose welfare the <s>Bodhisattva</s> exerts himself—that is the first immeasurable. The world-realms where he perceives those beings—that is the second immeasurable. The <s>dharmas</s> by which he perceives those beings in those various world-realms as being defiled and as being purified—that is the third immeasurable. From among those beings, those whom he sees as capable and amenable to ultimate liberation from suffering—that is the fourth immeasurable. And the means for the liberation of those very beings—that is the fifth immeasurable. Therefore these five immeasurables conduce to the <s>Bodhisattvas</s>' activity of complete skill.

body.text: pañceme buddhabodhisattvānāṃ sattveṣu dharmadeśanāyā vipulāḥ phalānuśaṃsā veditavyāḥ / katame pañca / tadekatyāḥ sattvāḥ tasminneva saddharme deśyamāne virajo vigatamalaṃ dharmeṣu dharmacakṣurūtpādayanti / tadekatyāḥ sattvā deśyamāna eva saddharmataḥ āsravakṣayamanuprāpnuvanti / tadekatyāḥ sattvā anuttarāyāṃ samyaksaṃbodhau cittamutpādayanti / tadekatyāḥ sattvāḥ paramāṃ bodhisattvakṣāntiṃ pratilabhante / śrutamātra eva tasminsaddharme deśitaśca saddharmo buddhairbodhisattvaiśca uddeśasvādhyāyasaṃpratipattipāraṃparyayogena saddharmanetryāścirasthitikatāyai saṃvartate / itīme pañca deśanāyā vipulāḥ phalānuśaṃsā veditavyāḥ /
body.translated_text: These five are to be known as the abundant fruits and benefits of the <s>Dharma</s>-teaching of <s>Buddhas</s> and <s>Bodhisattvas</s> to beings. What are the five? Certain beings, while that true <s>Dharma</s> is being taught, generate the stainless, purified <s>Dharma</s>-eye regarding <s>dharmas</s>. Certain beings, from the very teaching of the true <s>Dharma</s>, attain the destruction of the <s>āsravas</s> (defilements). Certain beings generate the mind directed toward unsurpassed perfect awakening (<s>bodhicitta</s>). Certain beings attain the supreme <s>Bodhisattva</s>-patience (<s>kṣānti</s>). And the true <s>Dharma</s> that has merely been heard, along with the true <s>Dharma</s> that has been taught by <s>Buddhas</s> and <s>Bodhisattvas</s>, conduces to the long duration of the true <s>Dharma</s>-eye through the succession of recitation, study, and practice. These are the five abundant fruits and benefits of teaching.

body.text: saptemāni mahattvāni yairyuktaṃ bodhisattvānāṃ yānaṃ mahāyānamityucyate / katamāni sapta / dharmamahattvam / tadyathā dvādaśāṅgādvacogatād bodhisattvapiṭakavaipulyam / cittotpādamahattvam / tadyathā ekatyo 'nuttarāyāṃ samyaksaṃbodhau cittamutpādayati / adhimuktimahattvam / tadyathaikatyaḥ tasminneva ca dharmamahattve 'dhimukto bhavati / adhyāśayamahattvam / tadyathaikatyaḥ adhimukticaryābhūmiṃ
body.translated_text: These are the seven greatnesses by which the vehicle of <s>Bodhisattvas</s> is called the Great Vehicle (<s>Mahāyāna</s>). What are the seven? Greatness of <s>Dharma</s>—namely, the extensive <s>Bodhisattvapiṭaka</s>, comprising the twelve divisions of the word. Greatness of mind-generation—namely, one generates the mind toward unsurpassed perfect awakening. Greatness of aspiration (<s>adhimukti</s>)—namely, one has aspiration toward that very greatness of <s>Dharma</s>. Greatness of superior intention (<s>adhyāśaya</s>)—namely, one,

body.text: samatikramyādhyāśayaśuddhibhūmimanupraviśati / sambhāramahattvam / yasya puṇyasambhārasya jñānasambhārasya samudāgamādanuttarāṃ samyaksaṃbodhimabhisambudhyate / kālamahattvam / yena kālena yaistribhiṣkalpāsaṃkhyeyairanuttarāṃ samyaksaṃbodhimabhisaṃbudhyate / samudāgamamahattvam / saivānuttarā samyaksaṃbodhiḥ / yasyātmabhāvasamudāgamasyānyaḥ ātmabhāvasamudāgamaḥ samo nāsti / kutaḥ punaruttari kuto bhūyaḥ / tatra yacca dharmamahattvaṃ yacca cittotpādamahattvaṃ yaccādhimuktimahattvaṃ yaccādhyāśayamahattvaṃ yacca sambhāramahattvaṃ yacca kālamahattvamitīmāni ṣaṭmahattvāni hetubhūmāni samudāgama-mahattvasya / tatpunarekaṃ samudāgama-mahattvaṃ phalasthānīyameṣāṃ ṣaṇṇāṃ veditavyam /
body.translated_text: having surpassed the stage of aspiration-practice, enters the stage of pure superior intention. Greatness of accumulation—through the complete gathering of the accumulation of merit and the accumulation of knowledge, one awakens to unsurpassed perfect awakening. Greatness of time—by means of three incalculable <s>kalpas</s> (eons), one awakens to unsurpassed perfect awakening. Greatness of attainment—that very unsurpassed perfect awakening itself, to whose attainment of self-nature no other attainment of self-nature is equal, let alone superior or greater. Therein, the greatness of <s>Dharma</s>, the greatness of mind-generation, the greatness of aspiration, the greatness of superior intention, the greatness of accumulation, and the greatness of time—these six greatnesses are on the level of cause for the greatness of attainment. And that one greatness of attainment is to be known as the fruit-level of those six.

body.text: aṣṭāvime dharmāḥ sarvasya mahāyānasya saṃgrahāya saṃvartante / bodhisattvapiṭakadeśanā / tasminneva ca bodhisattvapiṭake ya sarvadharmāṇāṃ tattvārthaprakāśanā / tasminneva bodhisattvapiṭake yā sarvabuddhabodhisattvānāmacintyā paramodārā prabhāvasaṃprakāśanā / tasya ca yadyoniśaḥ śravaṇam / yoniśaśca cintāpūrvakamadhyāśayopagamanam / adhyāśayopagamanapūrvaṃkaśca bhāvanākārapraveśaḥ / bhāvanākārapraveśapūrvikā ca bhāvanāphalapariniṣpattiḥ / taśyā eva ca bhāvanāphalapariniṣpatteratyantanairyāṇikatā / evaṃ hi bodhisattvāḥ śikṣamāṇā anuttarāṃ samyaksaṃbodhimabhisaṃbudhthante /
body.translated_text: These eight <s>dharmas</s> conduce to the encompassing of the entire <s>Mahāyāna</s>: the teaching of the <s>Bodhisattvapiṭaka</s>; the illumination of the true meaning of all <s>dharmas</s> therein; the display of the inconceivable and supremely generous powers of all <s>Buddhas</s> and <s>Bodhisattvas</s> therein; its proper hearing; and, preceded by proper reflection, the adoption of superior intention; preceded by the adoption of superior intention, the entering into the mode of cultivation; preceded by the entering into the mode of cultivation, the ripening of the fruit of cultivation; and the irreversibility of that very ripening of the fruit of cultivation. Thus indeed do <s>Bodhisattvas</s>, while training, awaken to unsurpassed perfect awakening.

body.text: ke punaste bodhisattvā ya evaṃ śikṣamāṇā anuttarāṃ samyaksaṃbodhimabhisaṃbudhyante / te samāsato daśa veditavyāḥ / gotrasthaḥ / avatīrṇaḥ / aśuddhāśayaḥ / śuddhāśayaḥ / aparipakvaḥ / paripakvaḥ / aniyatipatitaḥ / niyatipatitaḥ / ekajātipratibaddhaḥ / caramabhavikaśceti / tatra gotrastho bodhisattvaḥ śikṣamāṇaścittamutpādayati / so 'vatīrṇa ityucyate / sa eva punaravatīrṇo yāvat śuddhāśayabhūmimapraviṣṭo bhavati tāvadaśuddhāśaya ityucyate / praviṣṭastu śuddhāśayo bhavati / sa eva punaḥ śuddhāśayo yāvanniṣṭhāgamanabhūmimapraviṣṭo bhavati tāvadaparipakva ityucyate / praviṣṭastu paripakvo bhavati / sa punaraparipakvo yāvanniyataniyatācaryābhūmau
body.translated_text: Who then are those <s>Bodhisattvas</s> who, thus training, awaken to unsurpassed perfect awakening? In brief, they are to be known as ten: one established in the spiritual lineage (<s>gotrastha</s>); one who has entered (<s>avatīrṇa</s>); one of impure intention (<s>aśuddhāśaya</s>); one of pure intention (<s>śuddhāśaya</s>); one unripened (<s>aparipakva</s>); one ripened (<s>paripakva</s>); one fallen into the undetermined (<s>aniyatipatita</s>); one fallen into the determined (<s>niyatipatita</s>); one bound by one birth (<s>ekajātipratibaddha</s>); and one in his final existence (<s>caramabhavika</s>). Therein, the <s>Bodhisattva</s> established in the lineage, while training, generates the mind [of awakening]—he is called one who has entered. That very one who has entered, so long as he has not entered the stage of pure intention, is called one of impure intention. But having entered, he becomes one of pure intention. That very one of pure intention, so long as he has not entered the stage of final completion, is called unripened. But having entered, he becomes ripened. Moreover, the unripened one, so long as he has not entered the stage of determined and definite conduct,

body.text: vā nānupraviṣṭo bhavati tāvadaniyata ityucyate / praviṣṭastu niyato bhavati / sa eva punaḥ paripakvau dvividhaḥ / ekajātipratibaddho yasya janmano 'nantaramanuttarāṃ samyaksaṃbodhimabhisaṃbhotsyate / caramabhavikaśca tasminneva janmani sthito 'nuttarāṃ samyaksaṃbodhimabhisaṃbudhyate / tatra te gotramupādāya yāvadanuttarāyāḥ samyaksaṃbodherdaśa bodhisattvā nirdiṣṭāḥ / ye bodhisattvaśikṣāsu śikṣante teṣāṃ nāta uttari śikṣā vidyate / yatra śikṣeran yathā ca śikṣeran na ca ebhyo yathā nirdiṣṭebhyo bodhisattvebhya uttari bodhisattvo vidyate yo bodhisattvaśikṣāsu śikṣate /
body.translated_text: is called undetermined. But having entered, he becomes determined. That very ripened one is of two kinds: one bound by one birth, who, in the birth immediately following, will awaken to unsurpassed perfect awakening; and one in his final existence, who, established in that very birth, awakens to unsurpassed perfect awakening. Therein, from the spiritual lineage up to unsurpassed perfect awakening, these ten <s>Bodhisattvas</s> have been described. For those <s>Bodhisattvas</s> who train in the <s>Bodhisattva</s> trainings, there exists no training higher than this in which they might train; nor does there exist any <s>Bodhisattva</s> higher than these <s>Bodhisattvas</s> as described who trains in the <s>Bodhisattva</s> trainings.

body.text: teṣāṃ punaḥ sarveṣāṃ eva bodhisattvānāmabhedenimānyevaṃ bhāgīyāni gauṇāni nāmāni veditavyāni / tadyathā bodhisattvo mahāsattvaḥ dhīmānuttamadyutiḥ jinaputro jinādhāraḥ vijetā jināṅkuraḥ vikrāntaḥ paramāryaḥ sārthavāho mahāyaśaḥ kṛpālurmahāpuṇyaḥ īśvaro dhārmikaśceti / teṣāṃ punardaśasu dikṣvanantāparyanteṣu lokadhātuṣvanantānāṃ bodhisattvānāmaprameyāḥ prayātmagatāḥ saṃjñāprāptayo veditavyāḥ / tatra ye bodhisattvāḥ sma iti pratijñāyāṃ bodhisattvā vartante na ca bodhisattvaśikṣāsu samyak pratipadyante te bodhisattvapratirūpakā veditavyāḥ / no tu bhūtāḥ / bodhisattvāḥ sma iti pratijñāyāṃ vartante samyak [ca ye] bodhisattvaśikṣāṣu śikṣante te bhūtā bodhisattvā veditavyāḥ /
body.translated_text: Moreover, for all those <s>Bodhisattvas</s> without distinction, these are to be known as the fitting honorific names: <s>Bodhisattva</s>, <s>Mahāsattva</s> (Great Being), <s>Dhīmān</s> (Wise One), <s>Uttamadyuti</s> (Supreme Splendor), <s>Jinaputra</s> (Son of the Conqueror), <s>Jinādhāra</s> (Support of the Conqueror), <s>Vijetā</s> (Victor), <s>Jināṅkura</s> (Sprout of the Conqueror), <s>Vikrānta</s> (Valiant One), <s>Paramārya</s> (Supremely Noble), <s>Sārthavāha</s> (Caravan Leader), <s>Mahāyaśas</s> (Great Fame), <s>Kṛpālu</s> (Compassionate One), <s>Mahāpuṇya</s> (Great Merit), <s>Īśvara</s> (Sovereign), and <s>Dhārmika</s> (Righteous One). Furthermore, in the infinite, boundless world-realms in the ten directions, the personal designations and recognized names of the infinite <s>Bodhisattvas</s> are to be known as immeasurable. Therein, those <s>Bodhisattvas</s> who claim 'We are <s>Bodhisattvas</s>' but do not properly practice the <s>Bodhisattva</s> trainings—they are to be known as counterfeit <s>Bodhisattvas</s>, not genuine. But those who claim 'We are <s>Bodhisattvas</s>' and properly train in the <s>Bodhisattva</s> trainings—they are to be known as genuine <s>Bodhisattvas</s>.

body.text: iti bodhisattvabhūmāvādhāre yogasthāne bodhisattvaguṇapaṭalamaṣṭādaśamam /
body.translated_text: Thus, in the <s>Bodhisattvabhūmi</s>, in the Ādhāra Yogasthāna (Foundational Stage of Practice), the eighteenth chapter, the Chapter on the Qualities of the <s>Bodhisattva</s> (<s>Bodhisattvaguṇapaṭala</s>).

body.text: samāptaṃ cādhārayogasthānam /
body.translated_text: Thus concludes the Ādhāra Yogasthāna (Foundational Stage of Practice).

body.text: Ādhārānudharmayogasthānam
body.translated_text: Ādhārānudharmayogasthāna (Stage of Practice in Accordance with the Foundation)

body.text: (Book 2)
body.translated_text: (Book 2)

body.text: bodhisattvaliṅgapaṭalam
body.translated_text: <s>Bodhisattvaliṅgapaṭala</s> (Chapter on the Marks of a <s>Bodhisattva</s>)

body.text: (Chapter 2.1)
body.translated_text: (Chapter 2.1)

body.text: uddānam /
body.translated_text: <s>Uddāna</s> (Summary Verse):

body.text: svabhāvo 'dhiṣṭhānaṃ [phalānuśaṃsaḥ] anukramaḥ saṃgraheṇa ca /
body.translated_text: Own-nature, basis, [fruits and benefits,] sequence, and in summary.

body.text: pañcemāni bhūtasya bodhisattvasya bodhisattvaliṅgāni yaiḥ samanvāgato [bodhisattvo] bodhisattva iti saṃkhyāṃ gacchati / katamāni pañca / anukampā priyavāditā vairyaṃ muktahastatā gambhīrārthasandhinirmocanatā ca / ime punaḥ pañca dharmāḥ pañca parivartena veditavyāḥ / svabhāvato 'dhiṣṭhānataḥ phalānusaṃśataḥ anukramataḥ saṃgrahataśca /
body.translated_text: These are the five marks of a genuine <s>Bodhisattva</s>, endowed with which a [<s>Bodhisattva</s>] comes to be counted as a <s>Bodhisattva</s>. What are the five? Compassion (<s>anukampā</s>), pleasant speech (<s>priyavāditā</s>), heroism (<s>vairya</s>), open-handedness (<s>muktahastatā</s>), and the ability to elucidate the meaning of the profound (<s>gambhīrārthasandhinirmocanatā</s>). These five qualities are to be understood through five aspects: by own-nature (<s>svabhāva</s>), by basis (<s>adhiṣṭhāna</s>), by fruits and benefits (<s>phalānuśaṃsa</s>), by sequence (<s>anukrama</s>), and comprehensively (<s>saṃgraha</s>).

body.text: tatrānukampāyāḥ svabhāvo dvividhaḥ / āśayagataḥ pratipattigataśca / tatrāśayagato hitāśayaḥ sukhāśayaśca bodhisattvasya sattveṣvanukampetyucyate / pratipattigataśca svabhāvato 'nukampāyāḥ yadāśayo bhavati bodhisattvaḥ sattveṣu tadeva yathāśaktyā yathābalaṃ kāyena vācā upasaṃharati / tatra priyavāditāyāḥ svabhāvaḥ pūrvavadāmodanī saṃmodanī upakarā ca vāgveditavyā / tadyathā saṃgrahavastupaṭale / tatra sattvaṃ dhṛtiralīnatvaṃ ca yadbalaṃ bodhisattvasya ayaṃ vairyaṃsvabhāva ityucyate / tatra yā bodhisattvasyodāradānatā asaṃkliṣṭadānatā vā / ayaṃ muktahastatāyāḥ svabhāvo veditavyaḥ / catasraḥ pratisaṃvidastāsāmeva cābhinirhārāya yatsamyak prāyogikaṃ jñānamayaṃ bodhisattvānāṃ gambhīrārthasandhinirmocanatāyāḥ svabhāvo veditavyaḥ /
body.translated_text: There, the intrinsic nature of compassion (<s>anukampā</s>) is twofold: pertaining to intention and pertaining to practice. There, the intention-based [compassion] is called the <s>Bodhisattva</s>'s compassion toward beings—the intention of benefit and the intention of happiness. And the practice-based intrinsic nature of compassion: whatever intention the <s>Bodhisattva</s> has toward beings, that very [intention] he carries out through body and speech according to his ability and power. There, the intrinsic nature of kind speech (<s>priyavāditā</s>) should be understood as the greeting, gladdening, and beneficial speech—as stated previously, as in the chapter on the Means of Attraction (<s>Saṃgrahavastu-paṭala</s>). There, the strength, firmness, and non-slackening which is the <s>Bodhisattva</s>'s power—this is called the intrinsic nature of courage (<s>vairya</s>). There, the <s>Bodhisattva</s>'s magnificent generosity or undefiled generosity—this should be understood as the intrinsic nature of open-handedness (<s>muktahastatā</s>). The four analytical knowledges (<s>pratisaṃvid</s>), and the wisdom that is born of right application and directed toward their accomplishment—this should be understood as the intrinsic nature of the <s>Bodhisattvas</s>' skill in unraveling profound meanings (<s>gambhīrārthasandhinirmocanatā</s>).

body.text: tatrānukampāyāḥ pañcādhiṣṭhānāni / katamāni pañca / duḥkhitāḥ sattvā duścaritacāriṇaḥ pramattā mithyāpratipannāḥ kleśānuśayitāśca / nārakānsattvānupādāya śeṣāṃ keṣāṃcitsattvānāṃ duḥkhā vedanā prābandhikī santatisamārūḍhā vartate /
body.translated_text: There, there are five bases (<s>adhiṣṭhāna</s>) of compassion. Which five? Beings who are suffering, beings who engage in misconduct, beings who are heedless, beings who are wrongly engaged, and beings who are latent with afflictions. Beginning with beings in the <s>naraka</s> realms, for some of the remaining beings there operates a continuous, unbroken stream of painful feeling.

body.text: ime [te] sattvā duḥkhitā ityucyante / ye punarnāvaśyaṃ duḥkhitāapi tu bahulaṃ kāyaduścaritamadhyācaranti vāgduścaritaṃ manoduścaritamadhyācaranti / tatra cābhiratarūpā viharanti / ime sattvā duścaritacāriṇa ityucyante tadyathā aurabhrika-śaukarika-kaukkuṭikaprabhṛtayaḥ / ye punarnāvaśyaṃ duḥkhitā na duścaritacāriṇo 'pi tvadhyavasitāḥ kāmānupabhuñjate naṭanartakahāsakalāsakaprekṣaṇaparā viharanti ātmopalāḍanaparāḥ / ime sattvāḥ pramattā ityucyante tadyathā tadekatyāḥ kāmopabhoginaḥ / ye punarnāvaśyaṃ duḥkhitā na duścaritacāriṇo na vāpi pramattāḥ api tu dṛṣṭivipattimāśritya duḥkhavimokṣāya pratipannāḥ / ime sattvā mithyāpratipannā ityucyante tadyathā kāmānutsṛjya durākhyāte dharmavinaye pravrajitāḥ / ye punaḥ sattvā nāvaśyaṃ duḥkhitā vistareṇa yāvan na mithyāpratipannāḥ api tu sakalabandhanāśca vikalabandhanāśca kleśaiḥ ime sattvāḥ kleśānuśayitā ityucyante tadyathā ye ca samyak prayuktāḥ pṛthagjanā kalyāṇakā ye ca śaikṣāḥ etāvadanukampādhiṣṭhānaṃ bodhisattvānāṃ yenādhiṣṭhānena yenālambanenānukampā pravartate / nāta uttari nāto bhūyaḥ /
body.translated_text: These beings are called 'suffering.' Those who are not necessarily suffering but who abundantly engage in misconduct of body, speech, and mind—and who dwell delighting in it—these beings are called 'engaging in misconduct,' such as sheep-butchers, pig-butchers, chicken-butchers, and the like. Those who are not necessarily suffering nor engaging in misconduct, but who are indulgently given over to enjoying sensual pleasures, devoted to entertainments such as acting, dancing, comedy, acrobatics, and spectacles, and given over to self-indulgence—these beings are called 'heedless,' such as certain enjoyers of sensual pleasures. Those who are not necessarily suffering, nor engaging in misconduct, nor heedless, but who, relying on wrong views, are engaged in a practice for liberation from suffering—these beings are called 'wrongly engaged,' such as those who, having renounced sensual pleasures, have gone forth into an ill-proclaimed <s>Dharma</s> and <s>Vinaya</s>. Those beings who are not necessarily suffering, in detail up to not wrongly engaged, but who have either complete or partial fetters of afflictions—these beings are called 'latent with afflictions,' such as rightly engaged ordinary persons of wholesome disposition and those who are learners (<s>śaikṣa</s>). This is the extent of the bases of the <s>Bodhisattvas</s>' compassion—the basis and object by which compassion operates. There is nothing beyond this, nothing more.

body.text: pañcemāni bodhisattvānāṃ priyavāditāyā adhiṣṭhānāni / katamāni pañca / samyagālapanā samyagānandanā samyagāśvāsanā samyakpravāraṇā nyāyopadeśaśca / teṣāṃ punaḥ pratibhāgo veditavyaḥ / tadyathā saṃgrahavastupaṭale / ebhiḥ paccabhiradhiṣṭhānairebhirālambanairbodhisattvānāṃ priyavāditā pravartate / nāta uttari nāto bhūyaḥ /
body.translated_text: There are these five bases of the <s>Bodhisattvas</s>' kind speech (<s>priyavāditā</s>). Which five? Proper conversing, proper gladdening, proper reassuring, proper inviting, and righteous counsel. Their detailed classification should be understood as in the chapter on the Means of Attraction (<s>Saṃgrahavastu-paṭala</s>). Through these five bases and objects, the <s>Bodhisattvas</s>' kind speech operates. There is nothing beyond this, nothing more.

body.text: pañcemāni bodhisattvasya vairyādhiṣṭhānāni veditavyāni / katamāni pañca / yaireva pañcabhirākārairbodhipakṣapaṭale dhṛtibalādhānatā bodhisattvānāmuktā tānyeva bodhisattvasya vairyādhiṣṭhānāni ve ditavyāni / yairadhiṣṭhānairyairālambanairbodhisattvasya vairya pravartate / nāta uttari nāto bhūyaḥ /
body.translated_text: There are these five bases of the <s>Bodhisattva</s>'s courage (<s>vairya</s>). Which five? The very five aspects by which the foundation of the power of firmness of <s>Bodhisattvas</s> has been stated in the chapter on the Factors Conducive to Awakening (<s>Bodhipakṣa-paṭala</s>)—those very [aspects] should be understood as the bases of the <s>Bodhisattva</s>'s courage. Through these bases and objects, the <s>Bodhisattva</s>'s courage operates. There is nothing beyond this, nothing more.

body.text: pañcemāni bodhisattvasya muktahastatāyā adhiṣṭhānāni / katamāni pañca / abhīkṣṇadānatā pramuditadānatā satkṛtyadānatā asaṃkliṣṭadānatā aniśrityadānatā ca / eṣāṃ punarvistareṇa vibhāgo veditavyaḥ / tadyathā dānapaṭale / ebhiradhiṣṭhānairebhirālambanairbodhisattvānāṃ muktahastatā pravartate / nāt uttari nāto bhūyaḥ /
body.translated_text: There are these five bases of the <s>Bodhisattva</s>'s open-handedness (<s>muktahastatā</s>). Which five? Frequent giving, joyful giving, earnest giving, undefiled giving, and giving without attachment. Their detailed classification should be understood as in the chapter on Generosity (<s>Dāna-paṭala</s>). Through these bases and objects, the <s>Bodhisattvas</s>' open-handedness operates. There is nothing beyond this, nothing more.

body.text: pañcemāni bodhisattvasya gambhīrārthasandhinirmocanatāyā adhiṣṭhānāni / katamāni pañca / ye te tathāgatabhāṣitāḥ sūtrāntāḥ gambhīrāgambhīrāvabhāṣāḥ śūnyatā-pratisaṃyuktā idaṃpratyayatā / pratītyasamutpādānulomāḥ / idaṃ prathamamadhiṣṭhānam / vinaye vā punarāpattikauśalyamāpattivyutthāna-kauśalyaṃ ca / idaṃ dvitīyamadhiṣṭhānam / mātṛkāyāṃ vā punaraviparītaṃ dharmalakṣaṇavyavasthānam / idaṃ tṛtīyamadhiṣṭhānam / ābhiprāyikanigūḍhadharmasaṃjñārthavibhāvanatā / idaṃ caturthamadhiṣṭhānam / sarvadharmāṇāñca dharmārthanirvacanaprakārabhedaḥ / idaṃ pañcamamadhiṣṭhānam / yenādhiṣṭhānena yenālambanena bodhisattvānāṃ gambhīrārthasandhinirmocanatā pravartate / nāta uttari nāto bhūyaḥ /
body.translated_text: There are these five bases of the <s>Bodhisattva</s>'s skill in unraveling profound meanings (<s>gambhīrārthasandhinirmocanatā</s>). Which five? The <s>sūtras</s> spoken by the <s>Tathāgata</s> that have deep expressions and are connected with emptiness (<s>śūnyatā</s>) and conditionality (<s>idaṃpratyayatā</s>), and that conform to dependent origination (<s>pratītyasamutpāda</s>)—this is the first basis. Skill in offenses and skill in recovery from offenses in the <s>Vinaya</s>—this is the second basis. The unerring establishment of the characteristics of <s>dharmas</s> in the <s>Mātṛkā</s> (matrix/Abhidharma)—this is the third basis. The elucidation of the intended, hidden meanings of the <s>Dharma</s>-designations—this is the fourth basis. And the differentiation of the modes of etymological explanation of all <s>dharmas</s> and their meanings—this is the fifth basis. Through these bases and objects, the <s>Bodhisattvas</s>' skill in unraveling profound meanings operates. There is nothing beyond this, nothing more.

body.text: anukampā bodhisattvasya sattveṣvādita eva tāvadvairaprahāṇāya saṃvartate / tathānukampako bodhisattvaḥ sarvasattvārthakriyāsu adinamanāḥ prayujyate / tasmiṃśca prayoge na parikhidyate / anukampā tad-bahulavihāritā cāsyānavadyadṛṣṭadharmasukhavihārāya parānugrahāya ca saṃvartate / ye ca bhagavatā maitryā anuśaṃsā uktānāsya kāye viṣaṃ krāmati na śasramityevamādayaḥ / te 'pyanukampakasya bodhisattvasya sarve veditavyāḥ / ityayamanukampāyā bodhisattvānāṃ phalānuśaṃso draṣṭavyaḥ /
body.translated_text: The <s>Bodhisattva</s>'s compassion toward beings first conduces to the abandonment of enmity. Thus the compassionate <s>Bodhisattva</s> applies himself to all activities for the welfare of beings with an unwearied mind. And in that endeavor, he does not become fatigued. Compassion and frequent dwelling in it conduce to his blameless and pleasant abiding in the present life and to the benefit of others. And whatever benefits the <s>Bhagavān</s> has declared regarding loving-kindness—'Poison does not spread in his body, weapons [do not harm him],' and so forth—all of these should be understood as applying to the compassionate <s>Bodhisattva</s>. This should be seen as the fruit and benefit of the <s>Bodhisattvas</s>' compassion.

body.text: priyavādī bodhisattvo dṛṣṭe dharme caturvidhaṃ vāgdoṣaṃ vijahāti mṛṣāvādaṃ paiśūnyaṃ ṣāruṣyaṃ sambhinnapralāpañca / sā cāsya bāgātmānugrahāya parānugrahāya ca pravṛttā bhavati / dṛṣṭa eva ca dharme āyatyāṃ ca priyavādī bodhisattvaḥ ādeyavacano bhavati grāhyavacanaḥ / ityayaṃ bodhisattvasya priyavāditāyāḥ [phalā]nuśaṃso veditavyaḥ /
body.translated_text: The <s>Bodhisattva</s> who speaks kindly, in this very life, abandons the fourfold fault of speech: false speech, slander, harsh speech, and idle chatter. And that speech of his operates for both self-benefit and the benefit of others. And the <s>Bodhisattva</s> who speaks kindly, both in this very life and in the future, becomes one whose words are heeded, one whose words are accepted. This should be understood as the fruit and benefit of the <s>Bodhisattva</s>'s kind speech.

body.text: dhīro bodhisattvo dṛṣṭe [tāvata] dharme sarveṇa sarvamālasyakausīdyāpagato bhavati pramuditacittaśca / bodhisattvaśīlasaṃvarasamādānaṃ karoti / kṛtvā ca na
body.translated_text: The courageous <s>Bodhisattva</s>, in this very life, becomes entirely free from laziness and sloth, and is of joyful mind. He undertakes the <s>Bodhisattva</s>-moral-conduct-restraint. And having undertaken it, he does not

body.text: viṣīdati / ātmānaṃ ca parañca kṣāntyānugṛhṇāti / āyatyāṃ ca sarvabodhisattvakṛtyasamārambheṣu prakṛtyā dṛḍhasamāraṃbho bhavati / nākṛtvā vinivartate / itīme bodhisattvānāṃ vairyaphalānuśaṃsā veditavyā /
body.translated_text: become dejected. And he benefits both himself and others through patience. And in the future, in all undertakings of <s>Bodhisattva</s>-tasks, he is by nature one of firm undertaking. He does not turn back without accomplishing [them]. These should be understood as the fruits and benefits of the <s>Bodhisattvas</s>' courage.

body.text: muktahastatāyā gambhīrārthasandhinirmocanatāyāśca phalānuśaṃsā veditavyāḥ / tadyathā prabhāvapaṭale dānaprabhāve prajñāprabhāve ca / ayameṣāṃ bodhisattvavijñānāṃ phalānuśaṃsaḥ /
body.translated_text: The fruits and benefits of open-handedness and of skill in unraveling profound meanings should be understood as in the chapter on Power (<s>Prabhāva-paṭala</s>), regarding the power of generosity and the power of wisdom. This is the fruit and benefit of these <s>Bodhisattva</s>-marks.

body.text: kaścaiṣāmanukramaḥ / pūrvaṃ tāvadbodhisattvo 'nukampayā sattvānanugṛhṇāti teṣu ca sāpekṣo bhavatyarthakāmaḥ / tataścākuśalātsthānādvyutthāpya kuśale sthāne pratiṣṭhāpanāya yuktiṃ bhāṣate grāhayati vyapadiśati / evamavatīrṇeṣu ca sattveṣu sattvavipratipattiṣu [ca] kleśaviprakṛtāsvarthavidhāsu vimardasaho bhavati / pratipattiviprati[patti]sthitānāṃ sattvānāmanutsargatayā / sa evaṃ dhīraḥ ekatyānsattvānāmiṣasaṃgraheṇa paripācayati ekatyāndharmasaṃgraheṇa tadekatyāṃstadubhābhyāṃ dharmābhiṣasaṃgrahābhyām / ayameṣāṃ pañcānāṃ bodhisattvaliṅgānāmanukramo veditavyaḥ /
body.translated_text: And what is their sequence? First, the <s>Bodhisattva</s>, through compassion, benefits beings and becomes attentive toward them, desiring their welfare. Then, for the purpose of raising them from an unwholesome state and establishing them in a wholesome state, he speaks reasonably, causes them to understand, and instructs them. And when beings have thus entered [the path], and when there are opposition and adversity among beings, and when affairs are disrupted by afflictions, he becomes able to endure hardship—through not abandoning beings who are established in [right] practice and [wrong] practice. Being thus courageous, he matures some beings through the gathering of material things, some through the gathering of <s>Dharma</s>, and some through both kinds of gathering—<s>Dharma</s>-gathering and material-gathering. This should be understood as the sequence of these five <s>Bodhisattva</s>-marks.

body.text: pañcemāni bodhisattvaliṅgāni ṣaṭpāramitāḥ / āsāṃ ṣaṇṇāṃ pāramitānāṃ katamayā pāramitayā katamadbodhisattvaliṅgaṃ saṃgṛhītam / anukampā dhyānapāramitayā saṃgṛhītā / priyāvāditā śīlapāramitayā prajñāpāramitayā ca saṃgṛhītā / vairyaṃ vīryapāramitayā kṣāntipāramitayā prajñāpāramitayā ca saṃgṛhītam / muktahastatā dānapāramitāyaiva saṃgṛhītā / gambhīrārthasandhinirmocanatā dhyānapāramitayā prajñāpāramitayā ca saṃgṛhītā evamimāni [pañca bodhi]sattvaliṅgāni pañcaparivartena veditavyāni / svabhāvato 'dhiṣṭhānataḥ phalānusaṃśato 'nukramataḥ saṃgrahataśca veditavyāni /
body.translated_text: These five <s>Bodhisattva</s>-marks are the six <s>pāramitās</s>. By which <s>pāramitā</s> is which <s>Bodhisattva</s>-mark embraced? Compassion is embraced by the <s>Dhyānapāramitā</s> (perfection of meditation). Kind speech is embraced by the <s>Śīlapāramitā</s> (perfection of moral conduct) and the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> (perfection of wisdom). Courage is embraced by the <s>Vīryapāramitā</s> (perfection of vigor), the <s>Kṣāntipāramitā</s> (perfection of patience), and the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>. Open-handedness is embraced by the <s>Dānapāramitā</s> (perfection of generosity) alone. Skill in unraveling profound meanings is embraced by the <s>Dhyānapāramitā</s> and the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>. Thus these five <s>Bodhisattva</s>-marks should be understood through five aspects: through their intrinsic nature, through their bases, through their fruits and benefits, through their sequence, and through their inclusion [in the pāramitās].

body.text: iti bodhisattvabhūmāvādhārānudharme yogasthāne prathamaṃ bodhisattvaliṅgapaṭalam /
body.translated_text: Thus, in the <s>Bodhisattvabhūmi</s>, in the Conforming Foundation (<s>Ādhārānudharma</s>) section of the Yoga Place, the first chapter on the Marks of the <s>Bodhisattva</s> (<s>Bodhisattvaliṅga-paṭala</s>) [is completed].

body.text: uddānam /
body.translated_text: Summary verse (<s>uddāna</s>):

body.text: sukṛtakarmāntatā kauśalyaṃ parānugrahaḥ pariṇāmanaṃ ca paścimam /
body.translated_text: Well-accomplished action, skill, benefit of others, and lastly dedication.

body.text: gṛhipakṣe vā pravrajitapakṣe vā vartamānasya bodhisattvasya samāsataścatvāro dharmā veditavyāḥ / yeṣu gṛhī pravrajito va bodhisattvaḥ śikṣamāṇaḥ kṣipramevānuttarāṃ samyaksaṃbodhimabhisaṃbudhyante / katame catvāraḥ / sukṛtakarmāntatā kauśalyaṃ parānugrahaḥ pariṇāmanā ca /
body.translated_text: For the <s>Bodhisattva</s> who abides either in the household side or the renunciant side, in brief, four <s>dharmas</s> should be understood—[<s>dharmas</s>] in which the <s>Bodhisattva</s>, whether householder or renunciant, training, swiftly awakens to unsurpassed perfect awakening. Which four? Well-accomplished action (<s>sukṛtakarmāntatā</s>), skill (<s>kauśalya</s>), benefit of others (<s>parānugraha</s>), and dedication (<s>pariṇāmanā</s>).

body.text: tatra katamā bodhisattvasya sukṛtakarmāntatā / yā pāramitāsu niyatakāritā nipuṇakāritā nityakāritā anavadyakāritā ca / kathañca bodhisattvo niyatakārī bhavati yaduta dāne / iha bodhisattvaḥ saṃvidyamāne deyadharme yācanake samyak prapyupasthite apakāriṇyupakāriṇi vā guṇavati doṣavati vā 'vaśyaṃ dadāti / nāsya dānacittaṃ kaścidvikampayituṃ samartho bhavati manuṣyo vā 'manuṣyo vā śramaṇo vā brāhmaṇo vā kaścidvā punarloke sahadharmeṇa / kathaṃ ca bodhisattvo nipuṇakārī bhavati yadut dāne / iha bodhisattvaḥ saṃvidyamāne deyadharme samyak pratyupasthite yācanake sarvaṃ dadāti / nāstyasya kiñcidyadaparityājyaṃ bhavati sattvebhyaḥ ādhyātmikamapi vastu prāgeva bāhyam / kathaṃ ca bodhisattvo nityakārī bhavati yaduta dāne / iha bodhisattvo aparikhidyamāno dānena satatasamitameva sarvakālaṃ yathotpannaṃ dānaṃ dadāti / kathaṃ ca bodhisattvaḥ anavadyakārī bhavati yaduta dāne / iha bodhisattvo yattatsaṃkliṣṭaṃ dānaṃ varṇitaṃ dānapaṭale tatsaṃkliṣṭaṃ varjayitvā asaṃkliṣṭaṃ dānaṃ dadāti / evaṃ hi bodhisattvaḥ sukṛtakārī bhavati yaduta dāne / yathā dāne evaṃ śīlakṣāntivīryadhyānaprajñāpāramitāsu
body.translated_text: There, what is the <s>Bodhisattva</s>'s well-accomplished action (<s>sukṛtakarmāntatā</s>)? It is the definite performance, skillful performance, constant performance, and blameless performance in the <s>pāramitās</s>. And how is the <s>Bodhisattva</s> a definite performer, namely in generosity? Here, the <s>Bodhisattva</s>, when there is something to give and a supplicant has properly presented himself—whether a harmer or a benefactor, whether virtuous or faulty—he necessarily gives. No one is able to shake his intention of giving—whether human or non-human, whether ascetic or brahmin, or anyone in the world through righteous argument. And how is the <s>Bodhisattva</s> a skillful performer, namely in generosity? Here, the <s>Bodhisattva</s>, when there is something to give and a supplicant has properly presented himself, gives everything. There is nothing that he considers not to be relinquished for beings—even internal things, much less external. And how is the <s>Bodhisattva</s> a constant performer, namely in generosity? Here, the <s>Bodhisattva</s>, unfatigued by giving, constantly and continuously at all times gives whatever gift arises. And how is the <s>Bodhisattva</s> a blameless performer, namely in generosity? Here, the <s>Bodhisattva</s>, avoiding that defiled giving described in the chapter on Generosity (<s>Dāna-paṭala</s>), gives undefiled gifts. Thus the <s>Bodhisattva</s> is a well-accomplished performer, namely in generosity. Just as in generosity, so in the <s>pāramitās</s> of moral conduct, patience, vigor, meditation, and wisdom

body.text: yathāyogaṃ veditavyam / eta eva catvāra ākārā niyatakāritā nipuṇakāritā nityakāritā anavadyakāritā ca /
body.translated_text: it should be understood as appropriate. These very four aspects—definite performance, skillful performance, constant performance, and blameless performance—

body.text: tatra katamadbodhisattvasya kauśalyam / tatsamāsato daśavidhaṃ veditavyam pratihatānāṃ sattvānāṃ pratighātāpanayāyopāyakauśalyam / madhyasthānāmavatāraṇāya avatīrṇānāṃ paripācanāya paripakvānāṃ vimocanāyopāyakauśalyam / laukikeṣu sarvaśāstreṣu kauśalyam / bodhisattvaśīlasaṃvarasamādāne skhalitapratyavekṣaṇākauśalyam samyakpraṇidhānakauśalyam / [śrāvakayānakauśalyaṃ] pratyekabuddhāyānakauśalyam mahāyānakauśaśalyañca / eṣāṃ sarveṣāmeva kauśalyānāṃ pūrvavadyathāyogaṃ tatra tatrāsyāmeva bodhisattvabhūmau pravibhāgo veditavyaḥ / etāni punarbodhisattvasya daśa kauśalyāni pañcakṛtyāni kurvanti / pūrvakaiścaturbhiḥ kauśalyairbodhisattvaḥ sattvān svārthe sanniyojayati / laukikeṣu sarvaśāstreṣu kauśalyena bodhisattvaḥ sarvaparapravādānabhibhavati / bodhisattvaśīlasaṃvarasamādāne skhalitapratyavekṣaṇākauśalyena bodhisattvaḥ āpattiṃ [na] vāpadyate / āpanno vā yathādharmaṃ pratikaroti / suviśuddhaṃ śīlasaṃvarasamādānaṃ parikarṣati / samyak praṇidhānakauśalyena bodhisattvaḥ āyatyāṃ sarvābhipretārthasamṛddhimadhigacchati / tribhinnaṃ kauśalyairbodhisattvo yathā gotrendriyādhimuktānāṃ tadupamaṃ dharmaṃ deśayati / anukūlāṃ yuktiṃ vyapadiśati / evamebhirdaśabhiḥ kauśalyairbodhisattvaḥ pañcakṛtyāni karoti / yairasya pañcabhiḥ kṛtyaiḥ sarvakṛtyasamāptirbhavati / dṛṣṭadhārmikasāṃparāyikaṃ cārthamārabhya /
body.translated_text: There, what is the <s>Bodhisattva</s>'s skill (<s>kauśalya</s>)? In brief, it should be understood as tenfold: skill in means for removing the obstruction of obstructed beings; for the entry of the indifferent; for the maturation of those who have entered; and for the liberation of those who have matured — [this is] skill in means (<s>upāyakauśalya</s>). Skill in all worldly sciences. Skill in examining transgressions in undertaking the <s>Bodhisattva</s> moral restraint. Skill in proper aspiration. Skill in the <s>Śrāvaka</s> vehicle, skill in the <s>Pratyekabuddha</s> vehicle, and skill in the <s>Mahāyāna</s>. The classification of all these skills should be understood as before, applied in the appropriate places throughout this very <s>Bodhisattvabhūmi</s>. Furthermore, these ten skills of the <s>Bodhisattva</s> accomplish five functions. Through the first four skills, the <s>Bodhisattva</s> yokes beings to their own welfare. Through skill in all worldly sciences, the <s>Bodhisattva</s> overcomes all the doctrines of opponents. Through skill in examining transgressions in undertaking the <s>Bodhisattva</s> moral restraint, the <s>Bodhisattva</s> either does not incur a transgression, or, having incurred one, makes amends as prescribed by the <s>Dharma</s> and maintains a well-purified undertaking of moral restraint. Through skill in proper aspiration, the <s>Bodhisattva</s> attains the fulfillment of all desired aims in the future. Through the last three skills, the <s>Bodhisattva</s> teaches the <s>Dharma</s> appropriate to the lineage, faculties, and inclinations [of beings] and points out the suitable reasoning. Thus, through these ten skills, the <s>Bodhisattva</s> accomplishes five functions. Through these five functions, one achieves the completion of all functions — with respect to the welfare in this life and the next.

body.text: tatra katamo bodhisattvasya parānugrahaḥ / iha bodhisattvaścatvāri saṃgrahavastūni niśritya dānaṃ priyavāditāmarthacaryāṃ samānārthatāñca tadekatyānāṃ sattvānāṃ hitamapyupasaṃharati / sukhamapyupasaṃharati / [hitasukhamapyupasaṃharati /] ayaṃ bodhisattvānāṃ parānugrahasya samāsanirdeśaḥ / vistaranirdeśaḥ punaḥ pūrvavadveditavyaḥ tadyathā svaparārthapaṭale /
body.translated_text: There, what is the <s>Bodhisattva</s>'s benefiting of others (<s>parānugraha</s>)? Here, the <s>Bodhisattva</s>, relying on the four means of attraction (<s>saṃgrahavastu</s>) — giving (<s>dāna</s>), kind speech (<s>priyavāditā</s>), beneficial conduct (<s>arthacaryā</s>), and consistency of purpose (<s>samānārthatā</s>) — brings about welfare for certain beings, brings about happiness [for them], and brings about both welfare and happiness [for them]. This is the summary teaching of the <s>Bodhisattvas</s>' benefiting of others. The detailed teaching should be understood as before, as in the chapter on the Welfare of Self and Others.

body.text: tatra katamā bodhisattvasya pariṇāmanā / iha bodhisattvo yatkiñcidebhistribhirmukhairupacitopacitaṃ kuśalamūlaṃ sukṛtakarmāntatayā kauśalyena parānugraheṇa ca tatsarvamatītānāgatapratyutpannamanuttarāyāṃ samyaksaṃbodhau ghanarasena prasādena pariṇāmayati / na tasya kuśalamūlasyānyaṃ phalavipākaṃ pratikāṃkṣati nānya[trā]nuttarāmeva samyaksaṃbodhim / ye ca kecidbhagavatā gṛhiṇāṃ vā pravrajitānāṃ vā bodhisattvānāṃ śikṣādharmā vyapadiṣṭāḥ sarveṣāṃ teṣāmeṣveva caturṣu saṃgraho veditavyaḥ sukṛtakarmāntatāyāṃ kauśalye parānugrahe pariṇāmanāyāṃ ca / tasmādevaṃ sukṛtakarmāntasya bodhisattvasya kuśalasya parānugrahapravṛttasya pariṇāmakasya evaṃ duṣprāpā duradhigamā ca bodhirāsannā samāsannā veditavyā / atītānāgatapratyutpanneṣvadhvasu ye kecidbodhisattvā gṛhi-pravrajita pakṣeṣu śikṣamāṇā anuttarāṃ samyaksaṃbodhimabhisaṃbuddhavanto 'bhisaṃbhotsyante 'bhisaṃbudhyante ca sarve te ebhireva caturbhirdharmaiḥ / nāta uttari nāto bhūyaḥ / evamapi caturṣu dharmeṣu samyakprayukto gṛhī pravrajito vā bodhisattvo bhavati / api tu gṛhiṇo bodhisattvasyāntikātpravrajitasya bodhisattvasya sumahān viśeṣaḥ / sumahān nānākaraṇaṃ veditavyam / tathāhi pravrajito bodhisattvaḥ parimukto bhavatyādita eva tāvanmātāpitṛputtadārādikalatraparigrahadoṣāt / aparimuktastu gṛhī veditavyaḥ / punaḥ pravrajito bodhisattvaḥ parimukto bhavati tasyaiva parigrahasyārthe kṛṣivaṇijyā-rājapauruṣyādi-parikleśe vyāsaṅgaduḥkhebhyaḥ / aparimuktastu gṛhī veditavyaḥ / punaḥ pravrajito bodhisattva ekāntasaṅkalīkṛtaṃ brahmacaryaṃ śaknoti carituṃ [na tu] gṛhī bodhisattvaḥ / punaḥ pravrajito bodhisattvaḥ sarveṣu bodhipakṣyeṣu dharmeṣu kṣiprābhijño bhavati / yadyadeva kuśalamārabhate tatra tatraiva laghuladhveva niṣṭhāṃ gacchati / na tu tathā gṛhī bodhisattvaḥ / punaḥ pravrajito bodhisattvaḥ pareṣāṃ vrataniyame sthitatvād ādeyavacano bhavati / na tu tathā gṛhī bodhisattvaḥ / ityevaṃbhāgīyairdharmaiḥ sumahadantaraṃ gṛhi-pravrajitayorbodhisattvayorveditavyam /
body.translated_text: There, what is the <s>Bodhisattva</s>'s dedication (<s>pariṇāmanā</s>)? Here, the <s>Bodhisattva</s>, whatever wholesome roots have been accumulated through these three means — through well-performed action, through skill, and through benefiting others — dedicates all of that, past, future, and present, to the unsurpassed, perfect awakening with dense and heartfelt faith. One does not wish for any other fruit or ripening of that wholesome root, nor for anything other than the unsurpassed, perfect awakening itself. And whatever training <s>dharmas</s> have been taught by the <s>Bhagavān</s> for <s>Bodhisattvas</s>, whether householders or renunciants, all of those should be understood as comprised in these very four: in well-performed action, in skill, in benefiting others, and in dedication. Therefore, for a <s>Bodhisattva</s> who performs actions well, who is skillful, who is engaged in benefiting others, and who dedicates — awakening, though difficult to obtain and difficult to reach, should be understood as near and close at hand. In all past, future, and present times, whatever <s>Bodhisattvas</s> training in the householder and renunciant classes have fully awakened, will fully awaken, and do fully awaken to the unsurpassed, perfect awakening — all of them [do so] through these very four <s>dharmas</s>. There is nothing beyond this, nothing more than this. And thus a <s>Bodhisattva</s> rightly engaged in these four <s>dharmas</s> is a <s>Bodhisattva</s>, whether householder or renunciant. However, the renunciant <s>Bodhisattva</s> has a very great distinction and a very great difference from the householder <s>Bodhisattva</s>. For indeed, the renunciant <s>Bodhisattva</s> is freed from the very outset from the faults of the household encumbrance of mother, father, sons, wife, and the like. But the householder should be understood as not freed. Furthermore, the renunciant <s>Bodhisattva</s> is freed from the hardships, entanglements, and sufferings of agriculture, trade, royal service, and the like that serve the needs of that very household. But the householder should be understood as not freed. Furthermore, the renunciant <s>Bodhisattva</s> is able to practice the holy life (<s>brahmacarya</s>) in a wholly dedicated manner, but not the householder <s>Bodhisattva</s>. Furthermore, the renunciant <s>Bodhisattva</s> quickly attains higher knowledge in all <s>dharmas</s> conducive to awakening. Whatever wholesome [practice] one undertakes, one quickly reaches its culmination. But not so the householder <s>Bodhisattva</s>. Furthermore, the renunciant <s>Bodhisattva</s>, being established in observance of rules before others, becomes one whose words are heeded. But not so the householder <s>Bodhisattva</s>. By such categories of <s>dharmas</s>, a very great difference between the householder and the renunciant <s>Bodhisattva</s> should be understood.

body.text: iti bodhisattvabhumāvādhārānudharme yogasthāne dvitīyaṃ pakṣapaṭalam /
body.translated_text: Thus, in the <s>Bodhisattvabhūmi</s>, in the Foundation Section (<s>Ādhāra</s>) and Auxiliary Section (<s>Anudharma</s>) of the Yoga-ground (<s>Yogasthāna</s>), the second chapter, the Chapter on the Auxiliary Aspects (<s>Pakṣapaṭala</s>).

body.text: uddānam /
body.translated_text: Summary verse (<s>uddāna</s>):

children.translated_text: The affection (<s>vātsalya</s>) of the wise toward all beings is sevenfold;
Their intentions (<s>āśaya</s>) are fifteen, of which ten are considered to be productive of function.

body.text: saptākāraṃ bodhisattvānāṃ sattveṣu vātsalyaṃ pravartate yena vātsalyenopetā bodhisattvāḥ kalyāṇāśayāḥ paramakalyāṇāśayā ityucyante / saptākāraṃ vātsalyaṃ katamat / abhayaṃ yuktamakhedamayācitamanāmiṣaṃ vistīrṇaṃ samañceti / na hi bodhisattvaḥ kasyacidbhayādvatsalo bhavati / ānulomikena kāyavāṅmanaskarmaṇā samudācarati manāpena hitasukhena ca / na ca punarbodhisattvasya sattveṣu yogarahitaṃ vātsalyaṃ pravartate tadyathā adharme 'vinaye 'satyasamudācāre asthāne samādāpanatāyai / tathā ca bodhisattvo vatsalo bhavati sattveṣu yathā teṣāmarthe sarvārambhairna parikhidyate / ayācita eva ca bodhisattvaḥ sattveṣu vatsalo bhavati na tu kenacidyācitaḥ / nirāmiṣeṇa ca cittena vatsalo [bhavati] na parataḥ pratyupakāraṃ pratikāṃkṣamāṇaḥ paratra ca vipākamiṣṭaṃ pratyāśaṃsamāna iti niṣkāraṇavatsalo bhavati sattveṣu bodhisattvaḥ / vipulañca tadbodhisattvasya vātsalyaṃ bhavati sattveṣu na parīttam / tathā ca vipulaṃ bhavati yathaiṣāṃ sattvānāmantikādbodhisattvaḥ sarvākāramapyapakāraṃ labhamāno notsṛjati ātmānaṃ kāmamapriyaṃ karoti / na tu kenacitparyāyeṇa pareṣāṃ pāpakarmecchati / tatpunarevaṃ lakṣaṇameva guṇayuktaṃ vātsalyaṃ bodhisattvānāṃ sarvasattveṣveva samamāsamanta sattvadhātuprādeśikaḥ / evamanena saptākāreṇaiva vātsalyena yuktā bodhisattvāḥ kalyāṇāśayāḥ paramakalyāṇāśayā ityucyante /
body.translated_text: The <s>Bodhisattvas</s>' affection (<s>vātsalya</s>) toward beings operates in seven aspects. Endowed with this affection, <s>Bodhisattvas</s> are called 'of good intention' (<s>kalyāṇāśaya</s>) and 'of supremely good intention' (<s>paramakalyāṇāśaya</s>). What is the sevenfold affection? It is: fearless (<s>abhaya</s>), appropriate (<s>yukta</s>), unwearying (<s>akheda</s>), unsolicited (<s>ayācita</s>), without material motive (<s>anāmiṣa</s>), vast (<s>vistīrṇa</s>), and equal (<s>sama</s>). For the <s>Bodhisattva</s> is not affectionate out of fear of anyone. One acts with conforming bodily, verbal, and mental conduct that is agreeable and conducive to welfare and happiness. Moreover, the <s>Bodhisattva</s>'s affection toward beings does not operate without propriety — that is, it does not serve to induce them into what is contrary to <s>Dharma</s>, to <s>Vinaya</s>, to truthful conduct, or into what is improper. And the <s>Bodhisattva</s> is so affectionate toward beings that one does not become wearied by any exertion on their behalf. The <s>Bodhisattva</s> is affectionate toward beings unsolicited — not because one has been asked by anyone. With an unmotivated mind one is affectionate — not expecting reciprocation from others, nor anticipating a desired ripening in the future. Thus the <s>Bodhisattva</s> is affectionate toward beings without any [selfish] cause. And the <s>Bodhisattva</s>'s affection toward beings is vast, not limited. And it is so vast that even receiving all manner of harm from those beings, the <s>Bodhisattva</s> does not abandon them. One willingly makes oneself disagreeable [to some], yet by no means whatsoever does one wish for evil action toward others. Furthermore, that very affection of <s>Bodhisattvas</s>, endowed with such qualities, is equal (<s>sama</s>) toward all beings without exception throughout the entire realm of beings without partiality. Thus, endowed with this very sevenfold affection, <s>Bodhisattvas</s> are called 'of good intention' and 'of supremely good intention.'

body.text: tatra śraddhāpūrvaṃko dharmavicayapūrvakaśca buddhadharmeṣu yo 'dhimokṣaḥ pratyavagamo niścayo bodhisattvasya so 'dhyāśaya ityucyate / te punaradhyāśayā bodhisattvasya samāsataḥ pañcadaśa veditavyāḥ / katame pañcadaśa / agryāśayo vṛttāśayaḥ pāramitāśayaḥ tattvārthāśayaḥ prabhāvāśayaḥ hitāśayaḥ sukhāśayo vinirmuktāśayaḥ dṛḍhāśayaḥ avisaṃvādanāśayaḥ aśuddhāśayaḥ śuddhāśayaḥ suśuddhāśayaḥ nigṛhītāśayaḥ sahajaścāśayaḥ / tatra yo buddhadharmasaṃgharatneṣu bodhisattvasyādhyāśayaḥ so 'gryāśaya ityucyate / bodhisattvaśīlasaṃvarasamādāne yo 'dhyāśayo 'yaṃ vṛttāśaya ityucyate / dānaśīlakṣāntivīryadhyānaprajñāsamudāgamāya yo 'dhyāśayo 'yaṃ pāramitāśaya ityucyate / dharmapugdalanairātmye paramārthe ca dharmatathatāyāṃ gambhīrāyāṃ yo 'dhyāśayo 'yaṃ tattvārthāśaya ityucyate / buddhabodhisattvānāmacintye 'bhijñāprabhāve sahaje vā prabhāve yo 'dhyāśayo 'yaṃ prabhāvāśaya ityucyate / sattveṣu kuśalopasaṃhartukāmatā hitāśaya ityucyate / sattveṣvevānugrahopasaṃhartukāmatā sukhāśaya ityucyate / sattveṣveva nirāmiṣacittatā iṣṭe ca vipāke niṣpratibaddhacittatā vinirmuktāśaya ityucyate / anuttarāyāṃ samyaksaṃbodhau yā citaikāntikatāyaṃ dṛḍhāśaya ityucyate / sattvārthopāye bodhyupāye aviparītajñānasahagato 'dhimokṣaḥ avisaṃvādanāśaya ityucyate / sarvasyāmadhimuktivaryābhūmau yo 'dhyāśayo bodhisattvānāṃ so 'śuddhāśaya ityucyate / śuddhāśayabhūmimupādāya yāvanniyatacaryābhūmeradhyāśayo bodhisattvānāṃ śuddhāśaya ityucyate / niṣṭhāgamanabhūmāvadhyāśayo bodhisattvānāṃ suśuddhāśaya ityucyate / tatra yo hi [a]śuddhāśayaḥ sa eva nigṛhī[tāśaya] ityucyate pratisaṃkhyānakaraṇīyatayā / yaḥ punaḥ śuddhaḥ suśuddhaścādhyāśayaḥ sa sahajo 'dhyāśaya ityucyate prakṛtyā tanmayatayā āśrayasusaṃniviṣṭatayā ca /
body.translated_text: There, the conviction (<s>adhimokṣa</s>), discernment, and certainty regarding the <s>Buddha</s>-qualities that is preceded by faith and preceded by investigation of <s>dharmas</s> — that is called the <s>Bodhisattva</s>'s superior intention (<s>adhyāśaya</s>). Those superior intentions of the <s>Bodhisattva</s>, in brief, should be understood as fifteen. Which fifteen? The supreme intention (<s>agryāśaya</s>), the conduct intention (<s>vṛttāśaya</s>), the perfection intention (<s>pāramitāśaya</s>), the reality intention (<s>tattvārthāśaya</s>), the power intention (<s>prabhāvāśaya</s>), the welfare intention (<s>hitāśaya</s>), the happiness intention (<s>sukhāśaya</s>), the liberated intention (<s>vinirmuktāśaya</s>), the firm intention (<s>dṛḍhāśaya</s>), the non-deceiving intention (<s>avisaṃvādanāśaya</s>), the impure intention (<s>aśuddhāśaya</s>), the pure intention (<s>śuddhāśaya</s>), the supremely pure intention (<s>suśuddhāśaya</s>), the restrained intention (<s>nigṛhītāśaya</s>), and the innate intention (<s>sahajāśaya</s>). There, the <s>Bodhisattva</s>'s superior intention regarding the three jewels — <s>Buddha</s>, <s>Dharma</s>, and <s>Saṅgha</s> — is called the supreme intention. The superior intention regarding the undertaking of the <s>Bodhisattva</s>'s moral restraint is called the conduct intention. The superior intention for the accomplishment of giving (<s>dāna</s>), moral conduct (<s>śīla</s>), patience (<s>kṣānti</s>), vigor (<s>vīrya</s>), meditation (<s>dhyāna</s>), and wisdom (<s>prajñā</s>) is called the perfection intention. The superior intention regarding the selflessness of <s>dharmas</s> and persons (<s>dharma-pudgala-nairātmya</s>), and regarding the ultimate reality, the profound <s>dharma</s>-suchness (<s>dharmatathatā</s>) — is called the reality intention. The superior intention regarding the inconceivable power of supernatural knowledge (<s>abhijñāprabhāva</s>) of <s>Buddhas</s> and <s>Bodhisattvas</s>, or their innate power — is called the power intention. The wish to bring about wholesome [qualities] in beings is called the welfare intention. The wish to bring about benefit for those very beings is called the happiness intention. An unmotivated mind toward beings and an unattached mind toward desired ripening is called the liberated intention. Single-minded devotion to the unsurpassed, perfect awakening is called the firm intention. Conviction accompanied by non-erroneous knowledge regarding the means for the welfare of beings and the means to awakening is called the non-deceiving intention. The superior intention of <s>Bodhisattvas</s> on the entire stage of the practice through supreme aspiration (<s>adhimukticaryābhūmi</s>) is called the impure intention. From the stage of pure intention onward up to the stage of determined practice, the superior intention of <s>Bodhisattvas</s> is called the pure intention. On the stage of reaching culmination, the superior intention of <s>Bodhisattvas</s> is called the supremely pure intention. There, the impure intention itself is called the restrained intention, because it requires deliberate examination. But the pure and supremely pure superior intention is called the innate intention, because of its being naturally constituted by that [quality] and because of its being well-established in the basis [of character].

body.text: ityebhirbodhisattvāḥ pañcadaśabhiḥ kalyāṇairadhyāśayaiḥ sarvabhūmigataiḥ samāsato daśakṛtyāni kurvanti / katamāni daśa / agryāśayena ratnapūjāṃ sarvākārāṃ prayojayanti sarvabodhisambhārāṇāmagryabhūtām / vṛttāśayena bodhisattvaśīlasaṃvarasamādāne
body.translated_text: Thus, through these fifteen good superior intentions belonging to all stages, <s>Bodhisattvas</s>, in brief, accomplish ten functions. Which ten? Through the supreme intention, they motivate worship of the jewels in all aspects — worship that is the foremost among all accumulations for awakening. Through the conduct intention, in the undertaking of the <s>Bodhisattva</s>'s moral restraint

body.text: jīvitahetorapi [na] saṃcintyāpattimāpadyante / āpannāśca tvaritatvaritaṃ pratideśayanti / pāramitāśayena kuśalānāṃ dharmāṇāṃ bhāvanāsātatyakriyayā 'pramādavihāriṇo bhavanti paramāpramādavihāriṇaśca / tattvārthādhyāśayenāsaṃkliṣṭacittāśca saṃsāre sattvahetoḥ saṃsaranti / avinirmukta-nirvāṇādhyāśayāśca bhavanti / prabhāvādhyāśayena ghanarasaṃ ca śāsane prasādaṃ pravedayanti / bhāvanāyāṃ ca sārasaṃjñinaḥ spṛhājātā bahulaṃ viharanti / na tu śrutamātracintāmātrasaṃtuṣṭāḥ / hitāśayena sukhāśayena vinirmuktāśayena ca sarvākarāsu sattvārthakriyāsu prayujyante / prayuktāśca na parikhidyante / dṛḍhāśayena uttaptavīryā vipulavīryāḥ samārambhā viharanti / na śithilaprayogāḥ / na chidraprayogāḥ / avisaṃvādanādhyāśayena kṣiprābhijñā bhavanti teṣu teṣu kuśaladharmābhinirhāreṣu / na cālpamātrakeṇāvaramātrakeṇa hīnena viśeṣādhigamena tuṣṭimāpadyante / nigṛhītenādhyāśayena sahajādhyāśayamākarṣanti / sahajena punaradhyāśayena kṣipramanuttarāṃ samyaksaṃbodhimabhisaṃbudhyante arthāya hitāya sukhāya devamanuṣyāṇām / tatra ye kecidbhagavatā bodhisattvānāmadhyāśayā ākhyātāḥ prajñaptāḥ prakāśitāsteṣu teṣvadhikaraṇeṣu teṣāṃ sarveṣāmebhireva pañcadaśabhiradhyāśayaiḥ saṃgraho veditavyaḥ / tasmādatītānāgatapratyutpanneṣvadhvasu ye bodhisattvāḥ kalyāṇairadhyāśayairanuttarāṃ samyaksaṃbodhimabhisaṃbuddhavanto 'bhisaṃbhotsyante 'bhisaṃbudhyante ca sarve ta ebhireva pañcadaśabhiradhyāśayaiḥ / nāta uttari nāto bhūyaḥ / evamete pañcadaśa bodhisattvādhyāśayā mahāphalānuśaṃsāḥ / tasmāttānāśritya bodhisattvo 'nuttarāṃ samyaksaṃbodhimadhigacchediti /
body.translated_text: they do not deliberately incur an offense even for the sake of their lives. And having incurred an offense, they confess it with the utmost haste. Through the intention of the <s>pāramitās</s>, they abide in heedfulness, supremely heedful, through the continuity of cultivating wholesome <s>dharmas</s>. Through the intention of the reality of things (<s>tattvārtha</s>), they transmigrate in <s>saṃsāra</s> for the sake of beings with an undefiled mind. And they possess the intention of not being separated from <s>Nirvāṇa</s>. Through the intention of power (<s>prabhāva</s>), they experience a deeply savored faith in the teaching. And perceiving essence in cultivation, with longing arisen, they abide therein abundantly—not being content with mere hearing and mere reflection. Through the intention of benefit, the intention of happiness, and the intention of liberation, they apply themselves to all forms of beneficial activity for beings. And having applied themselves, they are not wearied. Through firm intention, they abide with blazing vigor, vast vigor, and exertion—not slack in endeavor, not with gaps in endeavor. Through the intention of non-deception, they quickly attain higher knowledges (<s>abhijñā</s>) in the respective accomplishments of wholesome <s>dharmas</s>. And they are not satisfied with a mere trifle, a mere minimum, an inferior attainment of distinction. Through restrained intention, they draw forth the innate intention. And through innate intention, they quickly awaken to the unsurpassed, perfect awakening for the welfare, benefit, and happiness of gods and humans. There, whatever superior intentions of <s>Bodhisattvas</s> have been declared, designated, and illuminated by the <s>Bhagavān</s> in the respective contexts—all of those should be understood as subsumed under these very fifteen superior intentions. Therefore, <s>Bodhisattvas</s> of the past, future, and present ages who have awakened, will awaken, and do awaken to the unsurpassed, perfect awakening with wholesome superior intentions—all of them [do so] through these very fifteen superior intentions. There is nothing beyond this, nothing more than this. Thus these fifteen superior intentions of <s>Bodhisattvas</s> bear great fruit and benefit. Therefore, relying on them, the <s>Bodhisattva</s> should attain the unsurpassed, perfect awakening.

body.text: iti bodhisattvabhūmāvādhārānudharme yogasthāne tṛtīyamadhyāśayapaṭalam /
body.translated_text: Thus, in the <s>Bodhisattvabhūmi</s>, in the Foundation Section Conforming to the <s>Dharma</s> in the Yoga Division, the third chapter, the <s>Adhyāśaya-paṭala</s> (Chapter on Superior Intention), [is completed].

body.text: uddānam /
body.translated_text: Summary verse (<s>uddāna</s>):

children.translated_text: The lineage (<s>gotra</s>), and likewise aspiration-practice (<s>adhimukti</s>), the Joyful (<s>pramudita</s>), higher morality (<s>adhiśīla</s>), higher mind (<s>adhicitta</s>),
three of higher wisdom (<s>prajñā</s>), two signless (<s>animitta</s>)—with effort (<s>sābhoga</s>) and without effort (<s>anābhoga</s>),
and the analytical knowledges (<s>pratisaṃvid</s>), and the supreme, and the <s>Tathāgata</s>-abode, the highest.

body.text:
evaṃ gotrasaṃpadamupādāya yathoktāyāṃ bodhisattvaśikṣāyāṃ śikṣamāṇānāṃ yathokteṣu ca bodhisattvaliṅgeṣu saṃdṛśyamānānāṃ bodhisattvapakṣyaprayogeṣu ca samyak prayuktānāṃ bodhisattvādhyāśayāñca yathoktāṃ viśodhayatāṃ bodhisattvānāṃ samāsato dvādaśabodhisattvavihārā bhavanti / yairbodhisattvavihāraiḥ sarvā bodhisattvacaryā saṃgṛhītā veditavyāḥ / trayodaśaśca tathāgato vihāro yo 'sya bhavatyabhisaṃbodherniruttaro vihāraḥ /
tatra dvādaśabodhisattvavihārāḥ katame / [gotravihāraḥ /] adhimukticaryāvihāraḥ / pramuditavihāraḥ / adhiśīlavihāraḥ / adhicittavihāraḥ / adhiprajñavihārāstrayaḥ / bodhipakṣyapratisaṃyuktaḥ / satyapratisaṃyuktaḥ / pratītyasamutpādapravṛttinivṛttipratisaṃyuktaśca / iti yena [ca] bodhisattvastattvaṃ paśyati yañca tattvaṃ paśyati tasya ca tattvasyājñānād yathā pravṛttirduḥkhasya jñānācca punarapravṛttirduḥkhasya bhavati sattvānām / tadetadbodhisattvasya tribhirmukhaiḥ prajñayā vyavacārayataḥ trayoradhiprajñavihārā bhavanti / sābhisaṃskāraḥsābhāgo niśchidramārgavāhano nirnimitto vihāraḥ / anabhisaṃskāro 'nābhogamārgavāhano nirnimitta eva vihāraḥ / [pratisaṃvidvihāraḥ] paramaśca pariniṣpanno bodhisattvavihāraḥ / ime te dvādaśa[vidhā] bodhisattvānāṃ bodhisattvavihārāḥ / yairvihāraireṣāṃ sarvavihārasaṃgrahaḥ sarvabodhisattvacaryāsaṃgraho bhavati / tāthāgataḥ
body.translated_text: Thus, for <s>Bodhisattvas</s> who, beginning with the endowment of lineage (<s>gotrasaṃpad</s>), are training in the <s>Bodhisattva</s>-training as described, who are manifesting the <s>Bodhisattva</s>-marks as described, who are properly engaged in the endeavors conducive to the <s>Bodhisattva</s>-path, and who are purifying the <s>Bodhisattva</s>'s superior intention as described—there are, in summary, twelve <s>Bodhisattva</s>-abodes (<s>vihāra</s>). Through these <s>Bodhisattva</s>-abodes, all <s>Bodhisattva</s>-conduct should be understood as subsumed. And the thirteenth is the <s>Tathāgata</s>-abode, which, upon awakening, is his unsurpassed abode. There, what are the twelve <s>Bodhisattva</s>-abodes? The lineage-abode (<s>gotravihāra</s>). The abode of aspiration-practice (<s>adhimukticaryāvihāra</s>). The Joyful abode (<s>pramuditavihāra</s>). The abode of higher morality (<s>adhiśīlavihāra</s>). The abode of higher mind (<s>adhicittavihāra</s>). Three abodes of higher wisdom (<s>adhiprajñavihāra</s>): that connected with the factors of awakening (<s>bodhipakṣya</s>), that connected with the truths (<s>satya</s>), and that connected with the arising and cessation of dependent origination (<s>pratītyasamutpāda</s>). That is, by which the <s>Bodhisattva</s> sees reality and what reality he sees—and through ignorance of that reality, how the arising of suffering occurs for beings, and through knowledge, how the non-arising of suffering occurs—this, as the <s>Bodhisattva</s> investigates with wisdom through three approaches, constitutes the three abodes of higher wisdom. The signless abode with volition and effort, with an uninterrupted path-vehicle (<s>sābhisaṃskāra sābhoga nirnimitta vihāra</s>). The signless abode without volition and without effort, with a path-vehicle [that flows spontaneously] (<s>anabhisaṃskāra anābhoga nirnimitta vihāra</s>). The abode of analytical knowledge (<s>pratisaṃvidvihāra</s>). And the supreme, fully accomplished <s>Bodhisattva</s>-abode. These are the twelve kinds of <s>Bodhisattva</s>-abodes. Through these abodes, all their abodes are subsumed, and all <s>Bodhisattva</s>-conduct is subsumed. And the <s>Tathāgata</s>-abode

body.text: punarvihāro yaḥ sarvabodhisattvavihārasamatikrāntasyābhisaṃbuddhabodhervihāraḥ tatra tathāgatasya paścimasya vihārasya pratiṣṭhāyogasthāne paścime sākalyena nirdeśo bhaviṣyati /
body.translated_text: —which is the abode of one who has surpassed all <s>Bodhisattva</s>-abodes and has fully awakened—the complete exposition of that final abode of the <s>Tathāgata</s> will be given in its entirety in the final section, the Yoga Division on Establishment (<s>pratiṣṭhāyogasthāna</s>).

body.text: dvādaśānāṃ punarbodhisattvavihārāṇāṃ yathā vyavasthānaṃ bhavati tathā nirdekṣāmi /
body.translated_text: I shall now explain how the twelve <s>Bodhisattva</s>-abodes are established.

body.text: katamaśca bodhisattvasya gotravihāraḥ / kathaṃ ca bodhisattvo gotrastho viharati / iha bodhisattvo gotravihārī prakṛtibhadrasantānatayā prakṛtyā bodhisattvaguṇairbodhisattvārhaiḥ kuśalairdharmaiḥ samanvāgato bhavati / tatsamudācāre saṃdṛśyate / prakṛtibhadratayaiva na haṭhayogena tasmin kuśale pravarttate / api tu pratisaṃkhyānataḥ sāvagrahaḥ sambhṛto bhavati / sarveṣāṃ ca buddhadharmāṇāṃ gotravihārī bodhisattvo bījadharo bhavati / sarvabuddhadharmāṇāmasya [sarva]bījānyātmabhāvagatānyāśrayagatāni vidyante / audārikamalavigataśca bodhisattvo gotravihārī bhavati / abhavyaḥ sa tadrūpaṃ [saṃ]kleśaparyavasthānaṃ sammukhīkartum / yena paryavasthānena paryavasthitaḥ anyatamadānantaryakarma samudācaret / kuśalamūlāni vā samucchindyāt / yaśca vidhirgotrasthasya gotrapaṭale nirdiṣṭaḥ / sa gotravihāriṇo bodhisattvasya vistareṇa veditavyaḥ / [iti] ayamucyate bodhisattvasya gotravihāraḥ /
body.translated_text: What is the <s>Bodhisattva</s>'s lineage-abode (<s>gotravihāra</s>)? And how does the <s>Bodhisattva</s> who is established in the lineage abide? Here, the <s>Bodhisattva</s> abiding in the lineage-abode, through the nature of an inherently virtuous mental continuum, is endowed by nature with virtuous, wholesome <s>dharmas</s> worthy of a <s>Bodhisattva</s>.
