He is seen to engage in their practice. Through inherent virtue alone, without forceful effort, he engages in the wholesome—yet through discernment, he becomes equipped and provisioned. The <s>Bodhisattva</s> abiding in the lineage-abode is a seed-bearer of all <s>Buddha</s>-qualities. All the seeds of all <s>Buddha</s>-qualities exist within his personal existence, located in his basis (<s>āśraya</s>). And the <s>Bodhisattva</s> abiding in the lineage-abode is free from coarse defilements. He is incapable of bringing about that kind of defilement-ensnarement by which, being ensnared, one would commit one of the heinous crimes (<s>ānantarya</s>), or sever wholesome roots. And the manner of the one established in the lineage that has been described in the <s>Gotra-paṭala</s> (Chapter on the Lineage) should be understood in detail for the <s>Bodhisattva</s> abiding in the lineage-abode. This is called the <s>Bodhisattva</s>'s lineage-abode.

body.text: tatra katamo bodhisattvasyādhimukticaryāvihāraḥ / iha bodhisattvasya prathamaṃ cittotpādamupādāya aśuddhādhyāśayasya yā kācidbodhisattvacaryā ayamasyādhimukticaryāvihāra ityucyate / tatra gotravihārī bodhisattvastadanyeṣāṃ [sarveṣāṃ] bodhisattvavihārāṇāmekādaśānāṃ tāthāgatasya ca vihārasya hetumātre vartate hetu parigraheṇa / no tu tena kaścitu tadanyo bodhisattvavihāra ārabdho bhavati na pratilabdho na viśodhitaḥ / kutaḥ punastathāgatavihāraḥ / adhimukticaryāvihāriṇā punarbodhisattvena sarve bodhisattvavihārāstāthāgataśca vihāra ārabdhā bhavanti
body.translated_text: There, what is the <s>Bodhisattva</s>'s abode of aspiration-practice (<s>adhimukticaryāvihāra</s>)? Here, whatever <s>Bodhisattva</s>-conduct belongs to the <s>Bodhisattva</s> from the first generation of the mind (<s>cittotpāda</s>) onward, while his intention is not yet pure—this is called his abode of aspiration-practice. There, the <s>Bodhisattva</s> abiding in the lineage-abode exists merely at the level of being a cause for all the other eleven <s>Bodhisattva</s>-abodes and for the <s>Tathāgata</s>-abode, through the embracing of the cause. But none of those other <s>Bodhisattva</s>-abodes have been commenced by him, nor attained, nor purified. How much less the <s>Tathāgata</s>-abode! But by the <s>Bodhisattva</s> abiding in the aspiration-practice-abode, all <s>Bodhisattva</s>-abodes and the <s>Tathāgata</s>-abode have been commenced

body.text: no tu pratilabdhā na viśodhitāḥ / sa eva tvadhimukticaryāvihāraḥ pratilabdho bhavati / tasyaiva cāyaṃ viśuddhaye pratipannaḥ / adhimukticaryāvihāre pariśuddhe pramuditavihāraṃ pūrvārabdhameva pratilabhate / tasyaiva ca viśuddhaye pratipanno bhavati / pramudita vihāre pariśuddhe 'dhiśīlavihāraṃ pūrvārabdhameva pratilabhate / tasyaiva ca viśuddhaye pratipanno bhavati / evaṃ vistareṇa yāvatparamaḥ paraniṣpanno bodhisattvavihāro veditavyaḥ / parame pariniṣpanne bodhisattvavihāre pariśuddhe 'nantaraṃ pūrvārabdhasya tātathāgatasya vihārasya sakṛtpratilambho viśuddhiśca veditavyā / idaṃ tāthāgatavihāre bodhisattvavihārebhyo viśeṣaṇaṃ veditavyam /
body.translated_text: but not yet attained, not yet purified. That very aspiration-practice-abode, however, has been attained. And he has entered upon the path toward its purification. When the aspiration-practice-abode is purified, he attains the Joyful abode (<s>pramuditavihāra</s>), which has already been commenced. And he enters upon the path toward its purification. When the Joyful abode is purified, he attains the abode of higher morality (<s>adhiśīlavihāra</s>), which has already been commenced. And he enters upon the path toward its purification. Thus, in detail, up to the supreme, fully accomplished <s>Bodhisattva</s>-abode should be understood. When the supreme, fully accomplished <s>Bodhisattva</s>-abode is purified, immediately afterward, the <s>Tathāgata</s>-abode that has been previously commenced is attained and purified all at once. This should be understood as the distinguishing feature of the <s>Tathāgata</s>-abode from the <s>Bodhisattva</s>-abodes.

body.text: tatra katamo bodhisattvasya pramuditavihāraḥ / yaḥ śuddhāśayasya bodhisattvasya vihāraḥ / tatra katamo bodhisattvasyādhiśīlavihāraḥ / yo 'dhyāśayaśuddhinidānena prakṛtiśīlena saṃyuktastasya vihāraḥ / tatra katamo bodhisattvasyādhicittavihāraḥ / yo 'dhiśīlavihāra viśuddhinidānailaukikadhyānasamādhisamāpattibhirvihāraḥ / tatra katamo bodhisattvasya bodhipakṣyapratisaṃyukto 'dhiprajñavihāraḥ / yo laukikaṃ jñānaviśuddhisanniśrayabhūtaṃ samādhiṃ niśrṛtya satyāvabodhāya samyak smṛtyupasthānādīnāṃ saptatriṃśatāṃ bodhipakṣyāṇāṃ dharmāṇāṃ pravicayavihāraḥ /
body.translated_text: There, what is the <s>Bodhisattva</s>'s Joyful abode (<s>pramuditavihāra</s>)? It is the abode of the <s>Bodhisattva</s> whose intention is pure. There, what is the <s>Bodhisattva</s>'s abode of higher morality (<s>adhiśīlavihāra</s>)? It is the abode of one who, through the purification of superior intention as its cause, is endowed with natural morality. There, what is the <s>Bodhisattva</s>'s abode of higher mind (<s>adhicittavihāra</s>)? It is the abode with supramundane <s>dhyānas</s>, concentrations (<s>samādhi</s>), and attainments (<s>samāpatti</s>), having the purification of the abode of higher morality as its cause. There, what is the <s>Bodhisattva</s>'s abode of higher wisdom connected with the factors of awakening (<s>bodhipakṣya</s>)? It is the abode of investigation of the thirty-seven factors conducive to awakening—beginning with the right foundations of mindfulness (<s>smṛtyupasthāna</s>)—for the purpose of the realization of the truths, relying on concentration (<s>samādhi</s>) that has supramundane knowledge-purification as its basis.

body.text: tatra katamo bodhisattvasya satyapratisaṃyukto 'dhiprajñavihāraḥ / yo bodhipakṣyapravicayaṃ niśritya yathāvatsatyāvabodhavihāraḥ / tatra katamo bodhisattvasya pratītyasamutpādapravṛttinivṛttipratisaṃyukto 'dhiprajñavihāraḥ / yastameva satyāvabodha[madhi]patiṃ kṛtvā tadajñānāt sahetukaduḥkhapravṛti / pravicayaprabhāvitastajjñānācca sahetukaduḥkhanirodhapravicayaprabhāvito vihāraḥ /
body.translated_text: There, what is the <s>Bodhisattva</s>'s abode of higher wisdom connected with the truths (<s>satya</s>)? It is the abode of realization of the truths as they truly are, relying on the investigation of the factors of awakening. There, what is the <s>Bodhisattva</s>'s abode of higher wisdom connected with the arising and cessation of dependent origination (<s>pratītyasamutpāda</s>)? It is the abode produced by the investigation of the arising of suffering together with its causes through ignorance of that [truth], and the investigation of the cessation of suffering together with its causes through knowledge of that [truth]—making that very realization of the truths the governing [factor].

body.text: tatra katamo bodhisattvānāṃ sābhisaṃskāraḥ sābhogo nirnimitto vihāraḥ / yastameva trividhamapyadhiprajñavihāramadhipatiṃ kṛtvā 'bhisaṃskāreṇābhogena niśchidranirantaraḥ sarvadharmeṣu tathatā-nirvikalpaprajñābhāvanā sahagato vihāraḥ /
body.translated_text: There, what is the <s>Bodhisattvas</s>' signless abode with volition and effort (<s>sābhisaṃskāra sābhoga nirnimitta vihāra</s>)? It is the abode that, making that very threefold abode of higher wisdom the governing [factor], through volition and effort, uninterrupted and without gap, is accompanied by the cultivation of wisdom that is non-conceptual with regard to the <s>tathatā</s> (suchness) of all <s>dharmas</s>.

body.text: tatra katamo bodhisattvānāṃ anabhisaṃskāro 'nābhogo nirnimitto vihāraḥ /
body.translated_text: There, what is the <s>Bodhisattvas</s>' signless abode without volition and without effort (<s>anabhisaṃskāra anābhoga nirnimitta vihāra</s>)?

body.text: yastasyaiva pūrvakasya nirnimittasya vihārasya bhāvanā-bāhulyāt svarasenaiva niśchidranirantara-vāhirmārgānugato vihāraḥ /
body.translated_text: It is the abode that, through the abundance of cultivation of that very former signless abode, flows spontaneously by its own momentum, uninterrupted and without gap, following the path.

body.text: tatra katamo bodhisattvānāṃ pravisaṃvidvihāraḥ / yastameva supariśuddhaṃ niścalaṃ prajñāsamādhiṃ niśritya mahāmativaipulyamanuprāptasya pareṣāṃ dharmasamākhyānānuttaryamārabhya dharmāṇāṃ paryāyārtha-nirvacanaprabhedapravicayavihāraḥ /
body.translated_text: There, what is the <s>Bodhisattvas</s>' abode of analytical knowledge (<s>pratisaṃvidvihāra</s>)? It is the abode of investigating the classifications, meanings, etymologies, and analyses of <s>dharmas</s> through various discourses and expositions—having attained the vast extent of great wisdom—relying on that very well-purified and unshakable concentration of wisdom, beginning with the unsurpassed skill of expounding the <s>Dharma</s> to others.

body.text: tatra katamo bodhisattvasya paramo vihāraḥ / yatra sthito bodhisattvo bodhisattvamārganiṣṭhāgato 'nuttarāyāṃ samyaksaṃbodhau mahādharmābhiṣekaprāpta ekajātipratibaddho vā bhavati caramabhaviko vā / yasya vihārasyānantaraṃ saṃhitamevānuttarāṃ samyaksaṃbodhimabhisaṃbudhya sarvabuddhakāryaṃ karoti / tatrādhimukticaryāvihāre [bodhisattvo] bodhisattvabhāvanāyāṃ parīttakārī bhavati cchidrakārī aniyatakārī punarlābhaparihāṇitaḥ / pramuditavihāre bodhisattvastasyāmeva bodhisattvabhāvanāyāṃ vipulakārī bhavatyacchidrakārī niyatakārī yathāpratilabdhāparihāṇitaḥ / yathā pramuditavihāre evaṃ yāvat triṣvadhiprajñavihāreṣu / pratharma nirnimittaṃ vihāramupādāya yāvatparamādbodhisattvavihārādbodhisattvo bodhisattvabhāvanāyāṃ apramāṇakārī bhavatyacchidrakārī niyatakārī ca / tatrādhimukticaryāvihāre bodhisattva-nirnimittabhāvanāyāḥ samārambho veditavyaḥ / pramuditavihāre 'ghiśīlādhicittādhiprajñavihāreṣu ca tasyā bodhisattva-nirnimittabhāvanāyāḥ pratilambho veditavyaḥ / prathame 'nimittavihāre samudāgamo dvitīye 'nimittavihāre bodhisattva-nirnimittabhāvanāyāḥ pariśuddhirveditavyā / pratisaṃvidvihāre parame ca vihāre tasyā eva bodhisattva-nirnimitta-bhāvanāyāḥ phalapratyanubhāvanā veditavyā /
body.translated_text: There, what is the <s>Bodhisattva</s>'s supreme abode (<s>paramo vihāra</s>)? It is that wherein the <s>Bodhisattva</s>, having reached the culmination of the <s>Bodhisattva</s> path, has obtained the great <s>Dharma</s>-consecration (<s>mahādharmābhiṣeka</s>) toward unsurpassed perfect awakening, and is either bound by a single birth (<s>ekajātipratibaddha</s>) or is in his final existence (<s>caramabhavika</s>). Immediately following that abode, he fully awakens to unsurpassed perfect awakening directly and performs all the deeds of a <s>Buddha</s>. There, on the aspiration-conduct stage (<s>adhimukticaryāvihāra</s>), the <s>Bodhisattva</s> is one of limited practice in the <s>Bodhisattva</s> cultivation, of intermittent practice, of undetermined practice, and subject to alternation of gain and loss. On the Joyful stage (<s>pramuditavihāra</s>), the <s>Bodhisattva</s>, in that same <s>Bodhisattva</s> cultivation, becomes one of extensive practice, of uninterrupted practice, of determined practice, and one who does not decline from what has been obtained. As on the Joyful stage, so up to the three Higher Wisdom stages (<s>adhiprajñāvihāra</s>). Beginning from the first signless stage up to the supreme <s>Bodhisattva</s> stage, the <s>Bodhisattva</s> becomes one of immeasurable practice in the <s>Bodhisattva</s> cultivation, of uninterrupted and determined practice. There, on the aspiration-conduct stage, the commencement of the <s>Bodhisattva</s>'s signless cultivation (<s>nirnimittabhāvanā</s>) should be understood. On the Joyful stage and on the higher moral conduct, higher mind, and higher wisdom stages, the attainment of that <s>Bodhisattva</s> signless cultivation should be understood. On the first signless stage, the full accomplishment [should be understood]. On the second signless stage, the purification of the <s>Bodhisattva</s>'s signless cultivation should be understood. On the analytical knowledge stage (<s>pratisaṃvidvihāra</s>) and on the supreme stage, the experiencing of the fruit of that same <s>Bodhisattva</s> signless cultivation should be understood.

body.text: adhimukticaryāvihāre vartamānasya bodhisattvasya ke ākārāḥ kāni liṃgāni kāni nimittāni bhavanti / adhimukticaryā-vihāre vartamāno bodhisattvaḥ pratisaṃkhyānabaliko bhavati / bodhisattvakṛtyaprayogeṣu pratisaṃkhyāya prajñayā prayujyate / no tu prakṛtyā tanmayatayā / dṛḍhāyāḥ sthirāyāḥ avivartayā bodhisattvabhāvanāyāḥ alābhī bhavati / yathā bhāvanāyā evaṃ bhāvanāphalasya vividhānāṃ pratisaṃvidabhijñāvimokṣasamādhisamāpattīnām /
body.translated_text: What are the characteristics, marks, and signs of a <s>Bodhisattva</s> abiding on the aspiration-conduct stage (<s>adhimukticaryāvihāra</s>)? The <s>Bodhisattva</s> abiding on the aspiration-conduct stage is one whose [practice] relies on the power of analytical reflection (<s>pratisaṃkhyānabala</s>). He applies himself to the tasks of a <s>Bodhisattva</s> through deliberate reflection with wisdom, not by natural absorption. He has not obtained firm, stable, irreversible <s>Bodhisattva</s> cultivation. Just as of the cultivation, so of its fruit — the various analytical knowledges (<s>pratisaṃvid</s>), superknowledges (<s>abhijñā</s>), liberations (<s>vimokṣa</s>), <s>samādhis</s>, and attainments (<s>samāpatti</s>).

body.text: pañca ca bhayānyasamatikrānto bhavati / ajīvikābhayamaślokabhayaṃ maraṇabhayaṃ durgatibhayaṃ pariṣadśāradyabhayaṃ ca / pratisaṃkhyāya ca sattvārtheṣu prayujyate na prakṛtyanukampā-prematayā / ekadā ca sattveṣu mithyāpi pratipadyate kāyena vācā manasā / ekadā viṣayeṣvapyadhyavasito bhavati / ekadā āgṛhīta-pariṣkāratāyāmapi saṃdṛśyate / śraddhāgāmī ca bhavati pareṣāṃ buddhabodhisattvānām / no tu pratyātmaṃ tattvajño bhavati yaduta tathāgataṃ vā ārabhya dharmaṃ vā saṃghaṃ vā tattvārthaṃ vā buddhabodhisattvaprabhāvaṃ vā hetuṃ vā phalaṃ vā prāptavyaṃ vā 'rthaṃ prāptyupāyaṃ vā gocaraṃ vā / parīttena ca śrutamayacintāmayena jñānena samanvāgato bhavati nāpramāṇena / tadapi cāsyaikadā saṃpramuṣyate / saṃpramoṣadharmo ca bhavati / duḥkhayā ca dhandhābhijñayā bodhisattva-pratipadā samanvāgato bhavati / na ca tīvracchando bhavati mahābodhau / nottaptavīryo na gambhīrasusanniviṣṭaprasādaḥ / triṣu ca sthāneṣu muṣita-smṛtirbhavati / viṣayeṣu manāpāmanāpeṣu rūpaśabdagandharasaspraṣṭavyadharmeṣvekadā viparyastacittatāyāḥ / upapattau tatra tatrātmabhāvāntare pratyājātasya pūrvakātmabhāvavismaraṇāt / uddiṣṭānāmudgṛhītānāṃ dharmāṇāṃ cirakṛtacirabhāṣitasya caikadā vismaraṇāt / evameṣu triṣu sthāneṣu muṣitasmṛtirbhavati / ekadā ca medhāvī bhavati dharmāṇāmudgrahaṇadhāraṇārthapraveśasamarthaḥ / ekadā na tathā / ekadā smṛtimān bhavati / ekadā muṣitasmṛtijātīyaḥ / na ca sattvānāṃ yathāvadvinayopāyābhijño bhavati / nāpyātmano buddhadharmābhinirhāropāyābhijñaḥ / haṭhena ca pareṣāṃ dharmaṃ deśayati / avavādānuśāsanīṃ vā pravartayati / sā cāsya haṭhena pravartitā na yathābhūtamājñāya / ekadā ca vandhyā bhavatyekadā cāvandhyā / rātrikṣiptānāmiva śarāṇāṃ yadṛcchāsiddhitāmupādāya / ekadā ca cittamapyutpāditaṃ mahābodhādutsṛjati / ekadā ca bodhisattvaśīlasaṃvarasamādānān nivartate notsahate vā / ekadā sattvārthakriyāprayukto 'pi khedamantarā kṛtvā tasmātsattvārthakriyāprayogāt pratinivartate / āśayataścātmanaḥ sukhakāmo bhavati pratisaṃkhyāya ca parasukhakāmaḥ / bodhisattvaskhaliteṣu ca parijñābahulo bhavati / no tu parijñāya parijñāyāśeṣa-prahāṇavān punaḥ punaḥ skhalitādhyācāratayā / ekadā neyaśca bhavatyasmādbodhisattvapiṭakadharmavinayāt /
body.translated_text: He has not transcended the five fears: the fear of loss of livelihood, the fear of loss of reputation, the fear of death, the fear of bad rebirth, and the fear of timidity before assemblies. He applies himself to the welfare of beings through analytical reflection, not through natural compassion and love. And sometimes he acts wrongly toward beings — in body, speech, and mind. Sometimes he is attached to sense-objects. Sometimes he is seen to be [overly] attached to personal possessions. He is one who follows on faith in other <s>Buddhas</s> and <s>Bodhisattvas</s>, but he is not himself a knower of reality — that is, regarding the <s>Tathāgata</s>, the <s>Dharma</s>, the <s>Saṃgha</s>, the true meaning, the power of <s>Buddhas</s> and <s>Bodhisattvas</s>, cause, fruit, the goal to be attained, the means to its attainment, or the range [of practice]. He possesses only a limited measure of knowledge born of hearing and reflection, not immeasurable. And even that sometimes slips from his memory — he is subject to forgetfulness. He is endowed with a <s>Bodhisattva</s> practice that is difficult, slow, and of dull superknowledge. He is not intensely desirous of great awakening, nor of refined vigor, nor of deep and well-established faith. And in three areas he is of confused mindfulness: regarding sense-objects — pleasant and unpleasant forms, sounds, smells, tastes, tangibles, and <s>dharmas</s> — sometimes his mind is perverted; regarding rebirth, from forgetting prior existences when reborn in each successive bodily existence; and from sometimes forgetting <s>dharmas</s> that were taught, grasped, and spoken or done long ago. Thus in these three areas he is of confused mindfulness. Sometimes he is intelligent — capable of grasping, retaining, and penetrating the meaning of <s>dharmas</s>; sometimes not so. Sometimes he is mindful; sometimes he is of the confused-mindfulness type. He is not skilled in the means of disciplining beings as they truly are. Nor is he skilled in the means of accomplishing <s>Buddha</s>-qualities in himself. He teaches the <s>Dharma</s> to others forcibly, and delivers instruction and admonition forcibly. And that which he delivers forcibly, not having understood as it truly is — sometimes it is fruitless, sometimes fruitful — like arrows shot in the dark, by mere chance. And sometimes he even abandons the mind that was generated toward great awakening. Sometimes he turns away from the undertaking of the <s>Bodhisattva</s> moral restraint, or he cannot bear it. Sometimes, even while engaged in welfare-activity for beings, he becomes weary midway and turns back from that welfare-activity. In intention, he is desirous of his own happiness; only through analytical reflection is he desirous of others' happiness. And regarding <s>Bodhisattva</s> stumblings, he is rich in recognition [of them], but even having recognized them, he does not completely abandon them — due to repeated stumbling and transgression. And sometimes he can be led astray from this <s>Bodhisattva</s>-piṭaka, <s>Dharma</s>, and <s>Vinaya</s>.

body.text: ekadā gambhīrāmudārāṃ dharmadeśanāṃ śrutvā utvrasyati / bhavati cāsya cetaso vikampitatvaṃ vimatiḥ sandehaśca / sarveṇa ca sarvaṃ mahākaruṇāsamudācāravivarjito bhavati sattveṣu / alpena ca hitasukhopasaṃhāreṇa sattveṣu pratyupasthito bhavati / na vipulena nāprameyeṇa ca sarvāsu paripūrṇāsu yathānirdiṣṭāsu bodhisattvaśikṣāsu śikṣate / na ca sarvaiḥ paripūrṇairyathānirdiṣṭairbodhisattvaliṅgaiḥ samanvāgato bhavati / na ca sarveṣu yathānirdiṣṭeṣu bodhipakṣaprayogeṣu paripūrṇeṣu saṃdṛśyate / dūre cānuttarāyāṃ samyaksaṃbodherātmānaṃ pratyeti / na ca tathā nirvāṇe 'syādhyāśayaḥ sanniviṣṭo bhavati yathā saṃsārasaṃsṛtau / uttaptairacalaiśca kuśalairbodhipakṣyairdharmairasamanvāgato bhavati / itīmānyevaṃbhāgīyāni liṅgāni nimittānīme ākārā adhimukticaryāvihāre vartamānasya bodhisattvasya veditavyāḥ / adhimukticaryāvihāre mṛddhyāṃ kṣāntyāṃ vartamānasya bodhisattvasyaiṣāṃ yathā nirdiṣṭānāmākāraliṅga-nimittānāmadhimātratā veditavyā / madhyāyāṃ kṣāntau vartamānasya [madhyatā] veditavyā / adhimātrāyāṃ kṣāntau vartamānasya bodhisattvasyaiṣāmākāraliṅganimittānāṃ mṛdutā tanutvaṃ veditavyam / adhimātrāyāmeva kṣāntau vartamānasyaiṣāmākāraliṅganimittānāmaśeṣaprahāṇāmanantarañca pramuditavihārapraveśo bodhisattvasya veditavyaḥ pratilambhayogena / tasyāsya pramuditavihāravihāriṇa ete [sarva]dharmāḥ sarvena sarvaṃ na bhavanti ye 'dhimukticaryāvihāra-vihāriṇa ākhyātāḥ / etadviparyayeṇa ca sarve śuklapakṣyā dharmāḥ saṃvidyante / yairayaṃ samanvāgato bodhisattvaḥ śuddhāśaya ityucyate / kiñcāpyadhimukticaryāvihāre 'pi vartamānasya bodhisattvasya mṛdumadhyādhimātrayogenottarottarā śuddhiradhimokṣasyāsti / na tvasau adhyāśayaśuddhirityucyate / tat kasya hetoḥ / tathā hi so 'dhimokṣa ebhiranekavidhairupakleśairupakliṣṭaḥ pravartate / pramuditavihārasthitasya tu bodhisattvasya sarveṣāmeṣāmadhimokṣopakleśānāṃ prahāṇānnirūpakleśaḥ śuddho 'dhimokṣaḥ pravartate /
body.translated_text: Sometimes, having heard a profound and lofty <s>Dharma</s>-teaching, he becomes frightened. There arises wavering of mind, doubt, and uncertainty in him. He is entirely devoid of the practice of great compassion (<s>mahākaruṇā</s>) toward beings. He stands ready with only a small measure of benefit and happiness for beings, not with a vast and immeasurable one. He does not train in all the <s>Bodhisattva</s> trainings as prescribed, [practiced] in their fullness. He is not endowed with all the <s>Bodhisattva</s> marks as prescribed in their fullness. He is not seen to be complete in all the prescribed practices conducive to awakening (<s>bodhipakṣa</s>) in their fullness. He considers himself far from unsurpassed perfect awakening. His superior intention toward <s>nirvāṇa</s> is not as deeply settled as [his attachment to] wandering in <s>saṃsāra</s>. He is not endowed with refined, immovable, wholesome <s>dharmas</s> conducive to awakening. Such are the characteristics, marks, and signs of a <s>Bodhisattva</s> abiding on the aspiration-conduct stage. For the <s>Bodhisattva</s> abiding on the mild patience (<s>mṛdu kṣānti</s>) of the aspiration-conduct stage, the intensity of these described characteristics, marks, and signs should be understood. For one abiding on the middling patience, their middlingness should be understood. For the <s>Bodhisattva</s> abiding on the intense patience, the mildness and thinness of these characteristics, marks, and signs should be understood. For one abiding on the intense patience itself, immediately after the complete abandonment of these characteristics, marks, and signs, the <s>Bodhisattva</s>'s entry into the Joyful stage (<s>pramuditavihāra</s>) should be understood, through the mode of attainment. For that <s>Bodhisattva</s> abiding on the Joyful stage, all those <s>dharmas</s> that were described for one abiding on the aspiration-conduct stage do not exist at all in any way. And all the bright-side <s>dharmas</s>, opposite to those, are found [in him]. Endowed with these, the <s>Bodhisattva</s> is called 'one of pure intention' (<s>śuddhāśaya</s>). Although there is progressively higher purification of the aspiration for the <s>Bodhisattva</s> abiding on the aspiration-conduct stage as well, through mild, middling, and intense modes, that is not called 'purity of superior intention' (<s>adhyāśayaśuddhi</s>). For what reason? Because that aspiration operates as defiled by these manifold defilements. But for the <s>Bodhisattva</s> established on the Joyful stage, through the abandonment of all these defilements of aspiration, the aspiration operates as undefiled and pure.

body.text: tatrapramuditavihāre vartamānasya bodhisattvasya ke ākārāḥ kāni liṅgāni kāni nimittāni veditavyāni / iha bodhisattvo 'dhimukticaryāvihārāt pramuditavihāramanupraveśana-pūrvakañca bodhisattvapraṇidhānamanuttarāyāṃ samyaksaṃbodhau asupratividdhabodhya supratividdhabodhyupāyaṃ yadbhūyasā parapratyayagāsuniścitaṃ
body.translated_text: There, what are the characteristics, marks, and signs to be understood for a <s>Bodhisattva</s> abiding on the Joyful stage (<s>pramuditavihāra</s>)? Here, the <s>Bodhisattva</s>, preceding the entry from the aspiration-conduct stage into the Joyful stage, [had] a <s>Bodhisattva</s> aspiration toward unsurpassed perfect awakening that was not well-penetrated in awakening though well-penetrated in the means to awakening, for the most part dependent on others, and not well-determined.

body.text: prahāyānyadabhinavaṃ ṣaḍbhirākāraiḥ su[vi]niścitaṃ pratyātmaṃ bhāvānāmayaṃ bodhisattvapraṇidhānamutpādayati / sarvaṃ tadanyaśulkapraṇidhāna-samatikrāntamatulyamasādhāraṇaphalam / laukikaṃ ca tatsarva[loka]viṣaya-samatikrāntaṃ ca / sarvasattvaduḥkhaparitrāṇānugatatvāt sarvaśrāvakapratyekabuddhāsādhāraṇam / ekakṣaṇa[mātraṃ] samutpanne api tasmin praṇidhāne dharmaprakṛtiḥ sā tādṛśī yā 'prameyaśulkadharmeṣṭaphalā bhavati bodhisattvānām / nirvikārañca tatpraṇidhāna[ma]kṣayam / nāsya pratilabdhasya kenacitparyāyeṇa parihāṇiranyathābhāvo vā upalabhyate / viśeṣabhāgīyañca tadaparāntakoṭīpatitam / mahābodhiniṣṭhaṃ tat /
body.translated_text: Having abandoned that, he generates a new, different <s>Bodhisattva</s> aspiration that is well-determined in six aspects, personal, born of cultivation. All of it surpasses all other bright aspirations, is unequaled, and bears uncommon fruit. It is mundane, yet transcends the domain of the entire world. Because it follows the protection of all beings from suffering, it is uncommon to all <s>Śrāvakas</s> and <s>Pratyekabuddhas</s>. Even when that aspiration arises for a single moment, the nature of <s>dharmas</s> (<s>dharmaprakṛti</s>) is such that it bears the fruit of immeasurable bright, desirable <s>dharmas</s> for <s>Bodhisattvas</s>. And that aspiration is unchanging and inexhaustible. No decline or alteration is found in it through any means once it has been attained. It is conducive to distinction and directed toward the final limit. It culminates in great awakening.

body.text: punaretatsuviniścitaṃ bodhisattvapraṇidhānaṃ cittotpāde ityucyate / sa punareṣa cittotpādo bodhisattvasya samāsataścaturbhirākārairveditavyaḥ / katamaiścaturbhiḥ / ādita eva tāvatkīdṛśānāṃ bodhisattvānāṃ taccittamutpadyate / kiñcālambyotpadyate / kīdṛśañca kiṃ lakṣaṇaṃ kenātmanā utpadyate / utpanne ca tasmiścitte ko 'nuśaṃso bhavati / ityebhiścaturbhirākāraiḥ sa cittotpādo veditavyaḥ / tatrādhimukticaryāvihāriṇāṃ sarvākārasūpacitakuśalamūlānāṃ samāsataḥ samyagbodhisattvacaryāniryātānāṃ bodhisattvānāṃ taccittamutpadyate / āyatyāṃ samyagāśu sarvabodhisambhāraparipūriṃ sarvabodhisattva-sattvārthakriyāparipūrimanuttarasamyaksaṃbodhi sarvākāra-sarvabuddhadharmaparipūriṃ buddhakāryakriyāparipūriṃ ca samāsataḥ ālambanīkṛtya tadbodhisattvānāñcittamutpadyate / samyagāśu ca sarvākārasarvabodhisaṃbhārānukūlaṃ sarvasattveṣu sarvākārabodhisattvakṛtyānukūlamanuttara-samyaksaṃbodhisvayaṃbhūjñānapratilambhānukūlaṃ sarvākārabuddhakṛtyakaraṇānukūlaṃ taccittamutpadyate / tasya ca cittasyotpādādbodhisattvo 'tikrānto bhavati bālabodhisattvapṛthagjanabhūmim / avakrānto bhavati bodhisattvaniyāmam / jāto bhavati tathāgatakule / tathāgatasyaurasaḥ putro bhavati / niyataṃ saṃbodhiparāyaṇaḥ tathāgatavaṃśaniyato bhavati / sa ca tathābhūto 'vetyaprasādaprāptaḥ prāmodyabahulo bhavati / asaṃrambhāvihiṃsākrodhabahulaḥ
body.translated_text: Furthermore, this well-determined <s>Bodhisattva</s> aspiration is called 'the generation of the [awakening-]mind' (<s>cittotpāda</s>). That generation of mind of the <s>Bodhisattva</s>, in brief, should be understood through four aspects. Which four? First, in what kind of <s>Bodhisattvas</s> does that mind arise? And what is its object? Of what kind is it, what is its characteristic, and by what nature does it arise? And when that mind has arisen, what is the benefit? Through these four aspects, that generation of mind should be understood. There, that mind arises in <s>Bodhisattvas</s> who, abiding on the aspiration-conduct stage, have accumulated wholesome roots in all their aspects, and who have, in brief, emerged into correct <s>Bodhisattva</s> conduct. Taking as its object, in brief, the future swift and complete fulfillment of all accumulations for awakening, the complete fulfillment of all <s>Bodhisattva</s> welfare-activity for beings, the complete fulfillment of unsurpassed perfect awakening and all <s>Buddha</s>-qualities in all their aspects, and the complete fulfillment of the deeds of a <s>Buddha</s> — that mind arises in those <s>Bodhisattvas</s>. And that mind arises as conducive to the swift and complete fulfillment of all accumulations for awakening in all their aspects, conducive to all <s>Bodhisattva</s> duties toward all beings in all their aspects, conducive to the attainment of the self-arisen knowledge (<s>svayaṃbhūjñāna</s>) of unsurpassed perfect awakening, and conducive to the performance of all <s>Buddha</s>-deeds in all their aspects. And from the arising of that mind, the <s>Bodhisattva</s> has transcended the stage of a beginning <s>Bodhisattva</s> who is an ordinary person (<s>pṛthagjana</s>). He has entered the <s>Bodhisattva</s>'s assured course (<s>niyāma</s>). He is born into the family of the <s>Tathāgata</s>. He becomes a true son of the <s>Tathāgata</s>. He is definitely destined for awakening and determined [to continue] the lineage of the <s>Tathāgata</s>. And being thus, having attained irreversible confidence, he is abundant in delight (<s>prāmodya</s>). He is abundant in non-hostility, non-violence, and freedom from anger.

body.text: pareṣāṃ sarvākārāṃ bodhisattva-sattvārthakriyāṃ sarvākārāṃ bodhisaṃbhāraparipūriṃ sarvākārāṃ bodhiṃ buddhadharmāṃśca buddhakṛtyānuṣṭhānaṃ ca śuddhenādhyāśayenālambanīkurvan adhimucyamāno 'vataran etaddharmāśu-samudāgamo 'nukūlatāñcātmanaḥ sampaśyan pratyavagacchan prāmodyabahulo bhavati / kuśalenodāreṇa naiṣkramyopasaṃhitena nirāmiṣeṇāpratisamena kāyacittānugrāhakeṇa prāmodyena uttaptairacalairasmi kuśalairdharmaiḥ samanvāgataḥ / āsannībhūtaścāsmyanuttarāyāḥ samyaksambodheḥ / viśuddhaśca me ādhyāśayo mahābodhau / sarvāṇi ca me bhayānyapagatāni / iti ato 'pi prāmodyabahulo bhavati / tathā hyasya [suvi]niścitotpāditacittasya bodhisattvasya pañca bhayāni prahīṇāni bhavanti / suparibhāvitanairātmyajñānasyātmasaṃjñā tāvan na pravartate / kutaḥ punarasya ātma[sneho] vā upakaraṇasneho vā bhaviṣyati / ato 'sya jīvikābhayaṃ na bhavati / na ca pareṣamantikātkiñcitpratikāṃkṣati / evaṃkāmaśca bhavati / mayaivaiṣāṃ sattvānāṃ sarvārthā upasaṃhartavyā iti / ato 'sya aślokabhayaṃ na bhavati / ātmadṛṣṭivigamāccāsyātma[vigama]saṃjñā na pravartate / ato 'sya maraṇabhayaṃ na bhavati / maraṇāt me ūrdhvamāyatyāṃ niyataṃ buddhabodhisattvaiḥ samavadhānaṃ bhaviṣyatīti evaṃ niścito bhavati / ato 'sya durgatibhayaṃ na bhavati / ātmanaśca sarvaloke na paśyatyāśayena kañcitsamasamam / kutaḥ punaruttarataramiti / ato 'sya pariṣacchāradyabhayaṃ na bhavati / sa evaṃ sarva bhayāpagataḥ sarvagambhīṃranirdeśatrāsāpagataḥ sarvocchrayamānastaṃbhāpagataḥ sarvaparāpakāravipratipattiṣu dveṣāpagataḥ sarvalokāmiṣa harṣāpagataḥ akliṣṭatvādanupahatena uttaptatvādaprakṛtenāśayena sarvakuśaladharmasamudāgamāya dṛṣṭe ca dharme sarvākāraṃ bodhisattvavīryamārabhate śraddhādhipateyaṃ pūrvaṅgamāṃ kṛtvā / āyatyāñca yāni tāni pūrvanirdiṣṭāni bodhipakṣyapaṭale daśamahāpraṇidhānāni tānyasmin pramuditavihāre 'bhinirhṛtyāśaya-śuddhitāmupādāya agrayasattvadakṣiṇīyaśāstṛdharmasvāmipūjāyai mahāpraṇidhānaṃ tatpraṇīta-[sad]-dharmasandhāraṇāya dvitīyamanupūrvasaddharmapravartanāya tṛtīyaṃ tadanukūla-bodhisattvacaryācaraṇatāyai caturthaṃ tadbhājanasattvaparipācanatāyai
body.translated_text: making the object of aspiration, with pure superior intention, the complete <s>Bodhisattva</s>-activity for the welfare of beings of others in all its aspects, the complete fulfillment of the accumulation for awakening in all its aspects, awakening in all its aspects, and the <s>Buddha</s>-qualities and the performance of <s>Buddha</s>-deeds—entering therein, seeing and understanding in himself the swift attainment of these <s>dharmas</s> and his aptitude for them—he becomes full of joy (<s>prāmodya</s>). [He reflects:] 'With wholesome, noble, renunciation-connected, non-material, incomparable joy that sustains body and mind, I am endowed with ardent, unshakable wholesome <s>dharmas</s>. I have come near to unsurpassed perfect awakening. My superior intention toward great awakening is purified. And all my fears have departed.' Thus he becomes even more full of joy. For indeed, for this <s>Bodhisattva</s> who has generated the mind with firm resolve, five fears have been abandoned. Since the knowledge of non-self has been well cultivated, the notion of self does not arise for him; how much less will there be attachment to self or attachment to possessions? Therefore he has no fear regarding livelihood. And he expects nothing from others; rather, his desire is: 'It is I alone who must bring about all the welfare of these beings.' Therefore he has no fear of ill-repute. Since the view of self has departed, the notion of self-annihilation does not arise for him; therefore he has no fear of death. He has the firm conviction: 'After death, in the future, I shall certainly encounter <s>Buddhas</s> and <s>Bodhisattvas</s>.' Therefore he has no fear of bad destinies. And in the entire world, he sees no one equal to himself in intention, let alone superior; therefore he has no fear of being disconcerted before assemblies. Thus, free from all fears, free from alarm at all profound expositions, free from all haughty pride and rigidity, free from hatred in all instances of harm and wrongdoing by others, free from delight in all worldly bait—with an intention that is unimpaired because unafflicted and extraordinary because ardent, for the attainment of all wholesome <s>dharmas</s> in this present life, he undertakes the <s>Bodhisattva</s>'s energy in all its aspects, making the predominance of faith the forerunner. And for the future, those ten great vows (<s>mahāpraṇidhāna</s>) previously described in the Chapter on Factors Conducive to Awakening—bringing them forth in this Joyful Abiding (<s>pramuditavihāra</s>), taking as basis the purity of intention: the first great vow is for the worship of the foremost beings, those worthy of offerings, the Teacher, the Lord of <s>Dharma</s>; the second for the preservation of that excellent true <s>Dharma</s>; the third for the gradual setting in motion of the true <s>Dharma</s>; the fourth for conducting the <s>Bodhisattva</s>-practice in accordance with it;

body.text: pañcamaṃ buddhakṣetreṣūpasaṃkramya tathāgatadarśanaparyupāsanasaddharmaśravaṇatāyai ṣaṣṭhaṃ svabuddhakṣetra-pariśodhanatāyai saptamaṃ sarvajātiṣu buddhabodhisattvāvirahitatāyai bodhisattvaiśca sahaikāśayaprayogitāyai aṣṭamaṃ sarvasattvārthakriyāmoghatāyai navamamanuttarasamyaksambodhyabhisaṃbudhyanatāyai buddhakṛtyakaraṇatāyai ca daśamaṃ mahāpraṇidhānabhinirharati pāramparyeṇa ca sattvadhātvanupacchedavallokadharmānupacchedavadeṣāmeva [me] mahāpraṇidhānānāṃ janmani janmani yavadbodhiparyantagamanādavigamaścāsaṃpramoṣaścāvisayogaśca syāditi samyak cittaṃ praṇidadhāti / pūrvakaṃ praṇidhātavye 'rthe praṇidhānaṃ paścimakaṃ praṇidhānaṃ veditavyam / etānyeva ca mahāpraṇidhānāni pramukhāni kṛtvā tasya bodhisattvasya daśapraṇidhānāsaṃkhyeyaśatasahasrāṇyutpadyante samyak praṇidhānānām /
body.translated_text: the fifth for the ripening of those beings who are vessels for it; the sixth for going to <s>Buddha</s>-fields, seeing the <s>Tathāgatas</s>, attending upon them, and hearing the true <s>Dharma</s>; the seventh for the purification of his own <s>Buddha</s>-field; the eighth for being never separated from <s>Buddhas</s> and <s>Bodhisattvas</s> in all births, for acting in unison of intention with <s>Bodhisattvas</s>; the ninth for the unfailing activity for the welfare of all beings; the tenth great vow he brings forth for awakening to unsurpassed perfect awakening and performing the <s>Buddha</s>-deeds. And in succession, just as the realm of beings is uninterrupted and as the <s>dharmas</s> of the world are uninterrupted, he properly directs his mind [thus:] 'May there be no loss, no forgetting, and no separation from these very great vows of mine, from birth to birth, until the final attainment of awakening.' The earlier vow is to be understood as the vow concerning what is to be vowed; the later vow [concerning their continuity] is to be known as the vow itself. And taking these very great vows as the foremost, there arise for that <s>Bodhisattva</s> innumerable hundreds of thousands of tens of millions of proper vows.

body.text: tasyaivamāyatyāñca praṇidhānavataḥ dṛṣṭe ca dharme ārabdhavīryasya daśavihārapariśodhanā dharmāḥ pramuditavihārapariśuddhaye saṃvartante / sarvabuddhadharmānabhiśraddadhāti / pratītyasamutpādayogena kevalaṃ sattvānāṃ duḥkhaskandhasamudāgamaṃ paśyataḥ karuṇā / mayaite sattvā asmātkevalād duḥkhaskandhādvimocayitavyā iti saṃpaśyato maitrī / sarvaduḥkhaparitrāṇābhiprāyasyātmanirapekṣatā / tannirapekṣasya sattveṣvādhyātmikabāhyavastuparityāgaḥ / parataśca teṣāmeva sattvānāmarthe laukika-lokottaradharmaparigaveṣaṇo 'khedaḥ / akhinnasya ca sarvaśāstrajñānasamudāgamaviśuddhitaḥ śāstrajñatā / śāsrajñasya hīnamadhyaviśiṣṭeṣu sattveṣu yathāyogānurūpapratipattito lokajñatā / teṣveva prayogeṣu kālavelāmātrādicaryāmārabhya hrī-vyapatrāpyatā / teṣveva ca prayogeṣvapratyudāvartanatayā dhṛtibalādhānatā / lāmasatkārapratipattibhyāñca tathāgatapūjopasthānatā / ime daśa dharmā vihārapariśuddhaye saṃvartante / yaduta śraddhā karuṇāmaitrītyāgaḥ akhedaḥ śāstrajñatā lokajñatā hrīvyapatrāpyatā dhṛtibalādhānatā tathāgatapūjopasthānatā ca /
body.translated_text: For him who thus has vows for the future and who has undertaken energy in the present life, ten <s>dharmas</s> for the purification of the abiding conduce to the purification of the Joyful Abiding (<s>pramuditavihāra</s>). He has faith in all <s>Buddha</s>-<s>dharmas</s>. By the method of dependent origination (<s>pratītyasamutpāda</s>), seeing the arising of the entire mass of suffering of beings, there is compassion (<s>karuṇā</s>). Seeing that 'I must liberate these beings from this entire mass of suffering,' there is loving-kindness (<s>maitrī</s>). For one whose intention is the complete rescue from all suffering, there is disregard for self. For one disregarding self, there is the relinquishment of both internal and external possessions for the welfare of those very beings. And for others, there is untiringness in seeking both worldly and supramundane <s>dharmas</s> for the welfare of those very beings. For one who is untiring, through the purified attainment of knowledge of all treatises, there is knowledge of treatises (<s>śāstrajñatā</s>). For one who knows the treatises, through practice suited and appropriate to inferior, middling, and superior beings, there is knowledge of the world (<s>lokajñatā</s>). In those very endeavors, beginning with the conduct of proper timing and occasion, there is moral shame and scrupulousness (<s>hrī-vyapatrāpya</s>). In those very endeavors, through not turning back, there is the sustaining of firmness and strength (<s>dhṛtibala</s>). And through abundant worship and service to the <s>Tathāgata</s>, there is attendance upon the <s>Tathāgata</s> in worship. These ten <s>dharmas</s> conduce to the purification of the abiding, namely: faith, compassion-and-loving-kindness, generosity, untiringness, knowledge of treatises, knowledge of the world, moral shame and scrupulousness, sustaining of firmness and strength, and attendance upon the <s>Tathāgata</s> in worship.

body.text: sa ca bodhisattva etāṃśca dharmāṃ samādāya vartate bahalīkaroti / tadanyeṣāñca navānāmadhiśīlādīnāṃ bodhisattvavihārāṇāṃ sarvākāramārgaguṇadoṣān paryeṣate buddhabodhisattvānāmantikāt / tadabhijñāśca sukhāvipranaṣṭamārgaḥ sūdgṛhītākārapratilambhaniṣyandanimittaḥ / svayañca sarvavihārānākramya mahābodhimadhigacchati mahāsattvasārthañca saṃsārakāntāramārgāduttārayati / yairākāraiḥ praveśati ta ākārāḥ yaḥ praveśaḥ sa pratilambhaḥ / praviṣṭasya yā [mahā]phalānuśaṃsaniṣpattiḥ samudāgamaśca sa niṣyando veditavyaḥ / tasyāsminvihāre vyavasthitasya dvābhyāṃ kāraṇābhyāṃ bahavo buddhā ābhāsamāgacchanti audārikadarśanasya / ye ca tena śrutā bhavanti bodhisattvapaṭike / ye ca cetasā 'dhimuktā bhavanti / santi daśasu dikṣu nānā-nāmasu lokadhātuṣu nānā-nāmānastathāgatā iti / tānaudārikaprasādasahagatena cetasā darśanāyāyācate / tasya ca tathābhūtasya ṛdhyatyeva / sā āyācanā idamekaṃ kāraṇam / evañca cittaṃ praṇidadhāti / tatra buddhotpādastatra me janma bhavediti / tasya tathābhūtasya ṛdhyatyeva tatpraṇidhānam / sa evamaudārikaprasādadarśanatayā praṇidhānabalādhānatayā ca tāṃstathāgatān dṛṣṭvā sarvākārāṃ pūjāṃ sukhopadhānatāmupasaṃharati yathāśaktyā yathābalaṃ saṃghasammānanāṃ ca karoti / teṣāṃ ca tathāgatānāmantikāddharmaṃ śṛṇoti udgṛhaṇāti dhārayati / dharmānudharmapratipattyā ca sampādayati / tāni ca sarvāṇi kuśalamūlāni mahābodhau pariṇāmayati / caturbhiśca saṃgrahavastubhiḥ sattvānparipācayati / tasyaibhistribhirviśuddhikāraṇaistāni kuśalamūlāni [yad] bhūyasyā mātrāyā viśudhyanti tathāgatadharmasaṃghapūjā-parigraha[ṇa]tayā saṃgrahavastubhiḥ sattvaparipācanatayā kuśalamūlānāṃ bodhipariṇamanatayā ca yāvadanekāni kalpakoṭīniyutaśatasahasrāṇi / tadyathā suvarṇaṃ prakṛtisthitaṃ yathā yathāgnau prakṣipyate dakṣeṇa karmāreṇa tathā tathā viśuddhataratāṃ gacchati / evamevāsyāśayaśuddhasya bodhisattvasya tāni kuśalamūlāni taiviṃśuddhikāraṇairviśuddhitaratāṃ gacchanti / tatrasthaścāsāvupapattito yadbhūyasā cakravartī bhavati janmani
body.translated_text: And that <s>Bodhisattva</s>, having taken up these <s>dharmas</s> and making them habitual, seeks from <s>Buddhas</s> and <s>Bodhisattvas</s> the qualities and faults of the path in all its aspects of the other nine abodes beginning with higher morality. Having direct knowledge of them, with the path unimpaired and well-established, with the fruit-result of well-grasped aspects—he himself traverses all the abodes and attains great awakening, and ferries the caravan of great beings across the wilderness of <s>saṃsāra</s>. The aspects by which he enters—those are the aspects; that entry itself is the attainment. The ripening of great fruits and benefits and the attainment of one who has entered—that is to be known as the fruit-result. While established in this abode, <s>Buddhas</s> come into his presence for two reasons, due to his extensive vision. Whatever he has heard in the <s>Bodhisattvapiṭaka</s> and whatever he has mentally aspired to—[knowing] 'There are <s>Tathāgatas</s> of various names in various world-realms in the ten directions'—he requests with a mind accompanied by intense faith to see them. And for one of such nature, that request succeeds. This is one reason. And he directs his mind thus: 'Where <s>Buddhas</s> arise, may I be born there.' And for one of such nature, that vow succeeds. Thus, through extensive faithful vision and through the sustaining power of vows, having seen those <s>Tathāgatas</s>, he renders all forms of worship and the provision of happiness to the best of his ability, and he also performs the honoring of the <s>Saṃgha</s>. And from those <s>Tathāgatas</s> he hears the <s>Dharma</s>, takes it up, and retains it; and he fulfills it through practice in accordance with the <s>Dharma</s>. And he dedicates all those wholesome roots toward great awakening. And through the four means of gathering (<s>saṃgrahavastu</s>) he ripens beings. For him, those wholesome roots become increasingly purified by three causes of purification: through the embracing of worship of the <s>Tathāgata</s>, <s>Dharma</s>, and <s>Saṃgha</s>; through the ripening of beings by the means of gathering; and through the dedication of wholesome roots toward awakening—for many hundreds of thousands of tens of millions of <s>kalpas</s>. Just as gold in its natural state becomes increasingly pure the more it is cast into fire by a skilled goldsmith, so too the wholesome roots of this <s>Bodhisattva</s> of purified intention become increasingly pure through those purification causes. And while established therein, by rebirth he mostly becomes a wheel-turning king (<s>Cakravartin</s>), from birth to birth,

body.text: janmani jambudvīpeśvaraḥ / sarvamātsaryamalāpagataḥ prabhuḥ sattvānāṃ mātsaryavinayanatāyai / yacca kiñciccaturbhiḥ saṃgrahavastubhiḥ karmārabhyate tatsarvamavirahitaṃ ratnasarvākārabodhisamudāgama-manaskāraiḥ / kaścidahaṃ sarvasattvānāmagryaḥ sarvārthapratiśaraṇo bhaveyamiti / ākāṃkṣamāṇaśca tadrūpaṃ vīryamārabhate yatsarvagṛhakalatrabhogānutsṛjya tathāgataśāsane pravrajitvā ekakṣaṇalavamuhūrtena śataṃ bodhisattvasamādhīnāṃ samāpadyate / tathāgataśataṃ nānābuddhakṣetreṣu divyena cakṣuṣā paśyati / teṣāṃ ca nirmitādhiṣṭhānaṃ bodhisattvādhiṣṭhāñca jānāti / lokadhātuśataṃ ca kampayati / tathā kāyenākrāmate / ābhayā spharitvā pareṣāmupadarśayati / vineyasattvaśataṃ nirmitaśatena paripācayati / kalpaśatamapyākāṃkṣamāṇaḥ sthānamadhitiṣṭhati / kalpaśataṃ ca pūrvāntāparāntato jñānadarśanena praviśati / [dharmamukhaśataṃ ca] pravicinoti skandhadhātvāyatanādikānāṃ dharmamukhānām / kāyaśataṃ ca nirmimīte / kāyañca kāyaṃ bodhisattvaśataparivāramādarśayati ataḥparaṃ praṇidhānabalenāpramāṇā prabhāvavikurvaṇā bodhisattvānāṃ veditavyā asmin pramuditavihāre sthitānām / praṇidhānabalikā hi te praṇidhānaviśeṣairvikurvanti / teṣāṃ samyak praṇidhānāṃ na sukarāṃ saṃkhyā kartu yāvatkalpakoṭīniyutaśatasahasrairapi / evamayaṃ bodhisattvānāṃ pramuditavihāraḥ suviniścita[taḥ] caturākāraḥ cittotpādataḥ samyak praṇidhānavīryārambhābhinirhārataḥ vihārapariśodhanatastadanyavihāravyutpattitaḥ kuśalamūlapariśodhanataḥ upapattitaḥ prabhāvataśca samāsanirdeśato veditavyaḥ / vistaranirdeśa[taḥ] punaryathāsūtrameva daśabhūmike pramuditabhūminirdeśamārabhya / yāśca daśabhūmike sūtre daśa bodhisattvabhūmayaḥ ta iha bodhisattvapiṭake mātṛkānirdeśa-daśa-bodhisattvavihārā yathākramaṃ pramuditavihāramupādāya yāvatparamavihārādveditavyāḥ / tatra bodhisattvānāṃ parigrahārthena bhūmirityucyate / upabhogavāsārthena punarvihāra ityucyate /
body.translated_text: sovereign of <s>Jambudvīpa</s>, free from all stain of miserliness, powerful in subduing the miserliness of beings. Whatever activity he undertakes through the four means of gathering, all of it is accompanied by mental attention directed toward the jewel and the attainment of awakening in all its aspects. [He thinks:] 'May I become the foremost of all beings, the refuge for all purposes.' And aspiring thus, he undertakes the appropriate energy so that, having relinquished all household, spouse, and possessions, having gone forth in the <s>Tathāgata</s>'s teaching, in a single instant, moment, or <s>muhūrta</s> he enters a hundred <s>Bodhisattva</s> <s>samādhis</s>; with the divine eye he sees a hundred <s>Tathāgatas</s> in various <s>Buddha</s>-fields; he knows their miraculous blessings and the blessings of <s>Bodhisattvas</s>; he shakes a hundred world-realms; likewise he traverses them with his body; pervading with radiance, he displays [himself] to others; with a hundred emanations he ripens a hundred beings to be trained; if he wishes, he abides even for a hundred <s>kalpas</s>; he enters a hundred <s>kalpas</s> into the past and future with knowledge-and-vision; he investigates a hundred <s>dharma</s>-gates, the <s>dharma</s>-gates of aggregates, elements, sense-bases, and so forth; he creates a hundred bodies; and he displays each body with a retinue of a hundred <s>Bodhisattvas</s>. Beyond this, through the power of vows, the <s>Bodhisattvas</s>' immeasurable displays of power and miraculous transformations are to be known for those established in this Joyful Abiding. For they are empowered by vows and transform through distinctions of vows. It is not easy to enumerate their proper vows, even in hundreds of thousands of tens of millions of <s>kalpa</s>-<s>koṭis</s>. Thus this Joyful Abiding (<s>pramuditavihāra</s>) of <s>Bodhisattvas</s> is to be understood, when firmly established, as fourfold in summary: from the standpoint of mind-generation; from the standpoint of the carrying out of proper vows and undertaking of energy; from the standpoint of purifying the abiding; from the standpoint of mastery of the other abodes; from the standpoint of purifying wholesome roots; from the standpoint of rebirth; and from the standpoint of powers. For the detailed exposition, it is as in the <s>sūtra</s> itself, beginning with the exposition of the Joyful Stage (<s>Pramuditabhūmi</s>) in the <s>Daśabhūmika</s>. The ten <s>Bodhisattva</s> stages in the <s>Daśabhūmika Sūtra</s> are to be understood here in the <s>Bodhisattvapiṭaka</s>'s <s>mātṛkā</s>-exposition as the ten <s>Bodhisattva</s> abodes in sequence, beginning with the Joyful Abiding up to the Supreme Abiding. Therein, 'stage' (<s>bhūmi</s>) is used in the sense of reception by the <s>Bodhisattvas</s>, while 'abiding' (<s>vihāra</s>) is used in the sense of enjoyment and dwelling.

body.text: tatra katame bodhisattvānāmadhiśīlavihārasya ākārāḥ kāni liṅgāni kāni nimittani veditavyāni / iha bodhisattvena pūrvameva pramuditavihāre daśākāreṇa
body.translated_text: Therein, what are the aspects, what are the marks, and what are the signs to be known of the <s>Bodhisattvas</s>' Abiding in Higher Morality (<s>adhiśīlavihāra</s>)? Here, by the <s>Bodhisattva</s>, already previously in the Joyful Abiding, with ten aspects,

body.text: cittāśayenāśayaśuddhiḥ pratilabdhā bhavati / sarvācāryagurudakṣiṇīyāvisaṃvādanā[dhyā]śayaḥ / sahadhārmikabodhisattvasauratyasukhasaṃvāsāśayaḥ / sarvakleśopakleśamārakarmābhibhava-svacittavaśavartanāśayaḥ / sarvasaṃskāreṣu doṣāśayaḥ nirvāṇe 'nuśaṃsāśayaḥ / kuśalānāṃ bodhipakṣyāṇāṃ dharmāṇāṃ bhāvanāsātatyāśayaḥ / teṣāmeva ca bhāvanānukūlatayā prāvivikyāśayaḥ / sarvalaukāmiṣasamucchrayalābhasatkāranirapekṣāśayaḥ / hīnayānamapahāya mahāyānādhigamāśayaḥ sarvasattvasarvārthakaraṇāśayaśca / itīme daśa samyagāśayāstasmiṃścitte pravṛttā bhavanti / yairasyāśayaḥ śuddha ityucyate / eṣāmeva cāśayānāmadhimātratvātparipūrṇatvāt dvitīyamadhiśīlavihāraṃ bodhisattvaḥ praviśatyākramate / so 'dhiśīlavihāre prakṛtiśīlī bhavati / svalpamapi mithyākarmapathasaṃgṛhītadauḥśīlyaṃ na samudācarati / prāgeva madhyamadhimātraṃ vā / daśasu ca paripūrṇeṣu [kuśaleṣu] karmapatheṣu prakṛtyā saṃdṛśyate / sa evaṃ prakṛtiśīlī prajñayā kliṣṭākliṣṭānāṃ karmapathānāṃ durgatisugatiyāneṣu karmasamudācāre hetuphalasamudāgamavyavasthānaṃ yathābhūtaṃ prajānāti / vipākaniṣyandaphala[ta]śca tāni karmāṇi yathābhūtaṃ prajānāti / sa svayaṃ cākuśalakarmaprahāṇe kuśalakarmasamādāne saṃdṛśyate / parāṃśca tatraiva samādāpayitukāmo bhavati samādāpayati ca viṣamakarmasamācāradoṣaduṣṭañca sattvadhātuṃ sarvamaviśeṣeṇa sampattivipattigataṃ paramārthato duḥkhitaṃ vyasanasthaṃ vicitrairvyasanākārairanukampamāno 'nukampāvaipulyamanuprāptaḥ pratyavekṣate / tasyāsmin adhiśīlavihāre vyavasthitasya buddhadarśanaṃ kuśalamūlaviśuddhiḥ pūrvavadveditavyā / tatrāyaṃ viśeṣaḥ / tadyathā tadeva suvarṇaṃ kuśalena karmakāreṇa kāsīsaṃ grakṣiptaṃ bhūyasyā mātrayā viśuddhataraṃ bhavatyagnau prakṣipyamāṇam / evamasya bodhisattvasya sā kuśalamūlaviśuddhirveditavyā / asmiṃśca vihāre śuddhacittāśayaniṣpattipraveśata upapatti[ta]ścāturdvīpakaścakravartī bhavati / yadbhūyasā bāhulyena ca dauḥśīlyādakuśalebhyaḥ karmapathebhyaḥ sattvān vyāvartayati / kuśaleṣu ca karmapatheṣu samādāpayati / prabhāvo 'pyasya pūrvakād daśaguṇo veditavyaḥ / ityevaṃ bodhisattvānāmadhiśīlavihāraḥ / prakṛtiśīlataśca sarvākāradauḥśīlyamalāpakarṣataśca sarvakarmapathasarvākārahetuphalajñānaprativedhataśca śubhe karmaṇī parasamādāpanakāmaścānukampāvaipulyapratilambhataśca
body.translated_text: the purity of intention has been attained through the mental intention. [He has] the intention of not deceiving all teachers, preceptors, and those worthy of offerings. The intention of dwelling gently and harmoniously with fellow <s>Bodhisattva</s> practitioners. The intention of mastering one's own mind so as to overcome all afflictions, secondary afflictions, and the works of <s>Māra</s>. The intention of seeing danger in all conditioned things. The intention of seeing benefit in <s>Nirvāṇa</s>. The intention of continuous cultivation of wholesome <s>dharmas</s> conducive to awakening. And the intention of seclusion, in conformity with the cultivation of those very [dharmas]. The intention of disregard for all worldly gains, honors, and eminences. The intention of abandoning the <s>Hīnayāna</s> and attaining the <s>Mahāyāna</s>. And the intention of acting for the welfare of all beings in all their purposes. These ten right intentions operate in that mind, by which his intention is called 'pure.' And from the intensity and completeness of these very intentions, the <s>Bodhisattva</s> enters and ascends to the second stage, the higher-moral-conduct stage (<s>adhiśīlavihāra</s>). Established in the higher-moral-conduct stage, he becomes one of natural morality. He does not engage in even a slight immorality embraced by the wrong courses of action, much less moderate or intense [immorality]. And he is naturally seen as established in the ten wholesome courses of action in their completeness. Being thus naturally moral, through wisdom he truly knows the establishment of the cause-and-fruit relationship in the practice of afflicted and non-afflicted courses of action [leading to] the unfortunate destinies, fortunate destinies, and vehicles. And he truly knows those actions through their ripening-fruit and outflow-fruit. He himself is seen abandoning unwholesome action and undertaking wholesome action. And he desires to lead others to the same, and does lead them. And perceiving the entire realm of beings—without exception, whether in prosperity or adversity—as ultimately suffering and in misery, through various modes of misery, due to the wrong practice of crooked action, he obtains the fullness of compassion and contemplates [them] with compassion. For this [<s>Bodhisattva</s>] established in this higher-moral-conduct stage, the seeing of <s>Buddhas</s> and the purification of wholesome roots should be understood as before. And here is the distinction: just as that very gold, cast by a skilled goldsmith into <s>kāsīsa</s> (copper sulfate solution), becomes even more purified to a greater degree when placed in fire—so should the purification of this <s>Bodhisattva</s>'s wholesome roots be understood. And in this stage, from the entry into the accomplishment of the pure mental intention, his rebirth is as a <s>cakravartin</s> (universal monarch) of the four continents. For the most part and abundantly, he turns beings away from immorality and the unwholesome courses of action and establishes them in the wholesome courses of action. And his power should be understood as tenfold compared to the previous [stage]. Thus is the <s>Bodhisattvas</s>' higher-moral-conduct stage. It should be understood through the summary teaching: from natural morality, from the removal of all stains of immorality in all its aspects, from the penetrative knowledge of the cause-and-fruit relationship in all courses of action in all their aspects, from the desire to lead others to engage in wholesome action, from the attainment of the fullness of compassion,

body.text: sattvadhātukarmajaduḥkhavyasanālocanataśca kuśalamūlaviśuddhitaśca upapattitaśca prabhāvataśca samāsanirdeśato veditavyaḥ / vistaranirdeśataḥ punaryathā sūtrameva yathā daśabhūmike vimalāyāṃ bhūmau dauḥśīlyamalāpagatatvāt vimalā bhūmirityucyate / dauḥśīlyamalāpagatatvāt evādhiśīlavihāra iti / yā tatra vimalā bhūmiḥ sehādhiśīlavihāro veditavyaḥ /
body.translated_text: from the contemplation of the suffering and misery of the realm of beings born of action, from the purification of wholesome roots, from the [type of] rebirth, and from the [degree of] power. For the detailed teaching, it is just as in the <s>sūtra</s>—namely, as in the <s>Daśabhūmika</s>, in the <s>Vimalā</s> (Stainless) stage. Because [this stage] is free from the stain of immorality, it is called the <s>Vimalā</s> stage. Because it is free from the stain of immorality, it is also called the higher-moral-conduct stage. The <s>Vimalā</s> stage described there should here be understood as the higher-moral-conduct stage.

body.text: tatra katame bodhisattvānāmākārāḥ kāni liṅgāni kāni nimittāni adhicittavihārasya / iha bodhisattvena pūrvamevādhiśīlavihāre te daśa śuddhāśayā manasikṛtā bhavanti juṣṭāḥ pratividdhāḥ / daśabhiraparairākāraisteṣāṃ cittāśayamanasikārāṇāmadhimātratvāt paripūrṇatvādadhiśīlavihāraṃ samatikramyādhicittavihāramanupraviśati / śuddho me daśabhirākāraiścittāśaya iti manasikāreṇa / abhavyaścāhaṃ tasmād daśākārāttchuddhāśayātparihāṇāyeti manasikāreṇa / sarvāsravasāsraveṣu me dharmeṣu cittaṃ na praskandati pratikūlatāyāṃ ca santiṣṭhata iti manasikāreṇa / tatpratipakṣabhāvanāyāṃ ca me vijñānaṃ saṃsthitamiti manasikāreṇa / abhavyaścāhamasmātpratipakṣātpunaḥ parihāṇāyeti manasikāreṇa / abhavyaścāhamevaṃ dṛḍhapratipakṣastaiḥ sarvāsravasāsravairdharmaiḥ sarvamāraiścābhibhavitumiti manasikāreṇa / asaṃlīnaṃ ca me mānasaṃ pravartate sarvabuddhadharmeṣviti manasikāreṇa / sarvaduṣkaracaryāsu ca me nāsti vyatheti manasikāreṇa / adhimuktaṃ ca me mahāyāne cittamekāntena na tadanyahīnayāneṣviti manasikāreṇa / sarvasattvārthakriyābhiratañca me cittamiti manasikāreṇa / ebhirdaśabhiścittāśayamanasikāraiḥ praviśati /
body.translated_text: There, what are the aspects, marks, and signs of the <s>Bodhisattvas</s>' higher-mind stage (<s>adhicittavihāra</s>)? Here, the <s>Bodhisattva</s> has already, in the previous higher-moral-conduct stage, attended to, cultivated, and penetrated those ten pure intentions. Through the intensity and completeness of ten further aspects of those mental-intention reflections, he transcends the higher-moral-conduct stage and enters the higher-mind stage. [He enters] through the reflection: 'My mental intention is pure in ten aspects.' Through the reflection: 'I am incapable of decline from that tenfold pure intention.' Through the reflection: 'My mind does not rush toward, and stands opposed to, all <s>dharmas</s> with and without <s>āsravas</s> (defilements).' Through the reflection: 'My consciousness is established in the cultivation of their antidote.' Through the reflection: 'I am incapable of decline from this antidote.' Through the reflection: 'Being thus firm in the antidote, I am incapable of being overpowered by all <s>dharmas</s> with and without <s>āsravas</s> and by all <s>Māras</s>.' Through the reflection: 'My mind proceeds unslackened toward all <s>Buddha</s>-<s>dharmas</s>.' Through the reflection: 'There is no distress for me in all difficult practices.' Through the reflection: 'My mind is exclusively devoted to the <s>Mahāyāna</s>, not to any other lesser vehicles.' And through the reflection: 'My mind delights in acting for the welfare of all beings.' Through these ten mental-intention reflections he enters.

body.text: adhicittavihārasthito bodhisattvaḥ sarvasaṃskārānādīnavākārairvicitrairvidūṣayati / tebhyaśca mānasamudvejayati / buddhajñāne cānuśaṃsadarśī bhavati vicitrairanuśaṃsākāraiḥ / tatra ca spṛhājāto bhavati ghanarasena cchandena / sattvadhātuṃ duḥkhitaṃ vyavalokayati vicitrairduḥkhākāraiḥ / teṣu ca sattveṣupekṣācitto bhavatyarthapratiśaraṇacittaḥ / sarvasaṃskāreṣvapramattaḥ / bodhāyottaptavīryaḥ / sattveṣu vipulakaruṇāśayaḥ / teṣāṃ sattvānāmatyantaduḥkhavimokṣopāyaṃ sarvakleśānāvaraṇajñānameva paśyati /
body.translated_text: The <s>Bodhisattva</s> established in the higher-mind stage regards all conditioned things as defective through various modes of danger. And he generates mental urgency from them. And he becomes one who sees benefit in <s>Buddha</s>-knowledge through various modes of benefit. And he develops aspiration for it with a dense, intense desire. He surveys the realm of beings as suffering through various modes of suffering. And toward those beings he becomes one of equanimous mind, with a mind taking refuge in purpose. He is heedful in all conditioned things. He is of ardent vigor toward awakening. He is of vast compassionate disposition toward beings. He sees that the means for the ultimate liberation of those beings from suffering is nothing other than the knowledge free from all affliction-obscurations.

body.text: tasya ca vimokṣasya samudāgamāya dharmadhātau sarvavikalpapracāra-saṃlkeśotpattipratipakṣaṃ prajñāṃ paśyati / tasya ca jñānālokasya niṣpattaye samyaksaṃbodhiṃ paśyati / tañca dhyānasamādhisamāpattinirhāraṃ bodhisattvapiṭakaśravaṇapūrvakaṃ śravaṇanidānaṃ paśyati / dṛṣṭvā [ca] mahatā vīryārambheṇa śrutaparyeṣṭimāpadyate / saddharmaśravaṇahetornāsti taddraviṇaṃ pariṣkāramādhyātmika-vāhyaṃ vastu yanna parityajati / nāsti sā guruparicaryā yānnābhyupagacchati / nāsti sā santatiryānnābhyupagacchati / nāsti sā kāyotpīḍā yānnābhyupagacchati / sa prītataro bhavatyeka catuṣpadagāthāśravaṇena na tvevaṃ trisāhasrapūrṇapratimena mahāratnarāśinā / prītataro bhavatyekadharmapadaśravaṇena samyaksaṃbuddhopanītena bodhisattvacaryāpariśodhakena na sarvaśakratva[-māratva-]brahmatva-lokapālatva-cakravartitva-samucchrayapratilambhaiḥ / sa cedenaṃ kaścidevaṃ vadet / evamahamidaṃ [dharmapadaṃ] samyaksaṃbuddhopanītaṃ sarvabodhisattvacaryāpariśodhakaṃ te 'nuśrāvayiṣyāmi sa cenmahatyāmagnikhadāyāmātmānaṃ prakṣipasi mahāntañca duḥkhopakramaṃ saṃpratīcchasīti / śrutvāsyaivaṃ bhavet / utsahāmyahamasya dharmapadasyārthe pūrvavat trisāhasramahāsāhasrapratimāyāmāpyagnikhadāyāṃ brahmalokādātmānamutsraṣṭuṃ prāgeva pratyavarāyām / nārakaduḥkhasaṃvāsairapyasmābhirbuddhadharmāḥ paryeṣitavyāḥ prāgeva prākṛtairduḥkhopakramairiti / evaṃrūpeṇa vīryārambheṇa dharmān paryeṣyaivaṃ yoniśo manasikaroti / yathā dharmānnudharmapratipattiṃ buddhadharmānugatāṃ na vyañjanasvaramātraviśaddhimiti viditvā tadeva śrutaṃ niśritya dharmanimittāni samyagālambanīkurvan viviktaṃ kāmairvistareṇa prathamaṃ dvitīyaṃ tṛtīyaṃ caturthañca dhyānaṃ laukikaṃ catasra ārūpyasamāpattīrlaukikīścatvāryapramāṇāni pañca cābhijñā upasaṃpadya viharati / sa tairbahulaṃ vihṛtya tāni dhyānāni samādhīn samāpattīḥ vyāvartayitvā praṇidhānavaśena kāmadhātau yatra sattvārthaṃ bodhipakṣadharmaparipūriṃ ca paśyati tatropapadyate / na tvevāsya tadvaśenopapattirbhavati / tasya kāmavītarāgatvātkāmabandhanāni prahīṇāni bhavanti dhyānasamādhisamāpattivyāvartanatvād
body.translated_text: And he sees that the wisdom which is the antidote to the arising of all defilement from the operation of all conceptual proliferation in the <s>dharmadhātu</s> [is necessary] for the accomplishment of that liberation. And he sees that perfect awakening (<s>samyaksaṃbodhi</s>) [is necessary] for the completion of that knowledge-light. And he sees that the accomplishment of that <s>dhyāna</s>, <s>samādhi</s>, and <s>samāpatti</s> is preceded by hearing the <s>Bodhisattva</s>-piṭaka and caused by hearing [it]. Having seen this, with great vigorous exertion he reaches the seeking of learning. For the sake of hearing the true <s>Dharma</s>, there is no wealth, equipment, or internal or external possession that he does not relinquish. There is no service of a teacher that he does not undertake. There is no stream [of suffering] that he does not enter. There is no bodily affliction that he does not endure. He becomes more delighted by hearing a single four-line verse than by a great heap of jewels filling the three-thousand [world-system]. He becomes more delighted by hearing a single <s>dharma</s>-word brought by the perfectly awakened <s>Buddha</s>, one that purifies <s>Bodhisattva</s>-conduct, than by obtaining the position of all <s>Śakras</s>, [<s>Māras</s>,] <s>Brahmās</s>, world-protectors, and <s>cakravartins</s>. If someone were to say to him: 'I will cause you to hear this <s>dharma</s>-word brought by the perfectly awakened <s>Buddha</s>, which purifies all <s>Bodhisattva</s>-conduct, if you cast yourself into a great fire-pit and accept a great ordeal of suffering'—upon hearing this, his thought would be: 'I am willing, for the sake of this <s>dharma</s>-word, to cast myself as before from the <s>Brahma</s>-world into a fire-pit the size of the three-thousand great-thousand [world-system], much less an inferior one. <s>Buddha</s>-<s>dharmas</s> should be sought by us even through dwelling in the sufferings of the <s>naraka</s> realms, much less through ordinary ordeals of suffering.' With such vigorous exertion he seeks the <s>Dharma</s> and wisely attends thus: 'Practice in conformity with the <s>Dharma</s>, following the <s>Buddha</s>-<s>dharmas</s>—not merely the purification of words and sounds.' Knowing this, relying on that very learning, correctly taking the <s>dharma</s>-signs as objects, secluded from sensual desires, in detail, he attains and dwells in the first, second, third, and fourth mundane <s>dhyānas</s>, the four formless attainments, the four immeasurables, and the five superknowledges (<s>abhijñā</s>). Having dwelt in them abundantly, he turns away from those <s>dhyānas</s>, <s>samādhis</s>, and attainments, and by the power of aspiration, is reborn in the desire realm (<s>kāmadhātu</s>) wherever he perceives the welfare of beings and the fulfillment of the factors conducive to awakening. Yet his rebirth does not occur through the power of [those attainments]. Because of his freedom from desire for sensual pleasures, his fetters of sensual desire are abandoned. Because of turning away from <s>dhyānas</s>, <s>samādhis</s>, and attainments,

body.text: bhavabandhanāni / adhimukticaryā-bhūmāvevāsya pūrvameva dharmatathatādhimokṣād dṛṣṭikṛtabandhanāni prahīṇāni bhavanti / mithyārāgadveṣamohāścāsyātyantaṃ na pravartante / tasya buddhadarśanaṃ vistareṇa kuśalamūlaviśuddhiḥ pūrvavadveditavyā / tatrāyaṃ viśeṣaḥ / tadyathā tadeva suvarṇakuśalasya karmārasya hastagataṃ prakṣīṇamalakaṣāyamapi samadharaṇamavatiṣṭhate tulyamānam / evamasya sā kuśala mūlaviśuddhirveditavyā / upapattitaśca śakro bhavati devendro yadbhūyasā / kuśalaḥ sattvānāṃ kāmarāgavinivartanatāyai / prabhāve 'pi yatra pūrvake vihāre sahasramākhyātaṃ tatreha śatasahasraṃ veditavyam / ayaṃ bodhisattvānāmadhicittavihāraścittamanaskāra-pariniṣpa[tti]praveśataśca saṃsārasattvadhātumahābodhisamyak-prativedha[ta]śca sattvaduḥkhavimokṣopāya-samyak-paryeṣaṇataśca mahāgauravadharmaparyeṣaṇataśca dharmānudharmapratipatti-laukikadhyānasamādhisamāpattyabhijñābhinirhāra-vihārataśca tadvyāvartanaṃ praṇidhāya yatra kāmopapattitaśca kuśalamūlaviśuddhitaścopapattitaśca prabhāvataśca samāsanirdeśato veditavyaḥ / vistaranirdeśaḥ punaryathāsūtraṃ tadyathā daśabhūmike prabhākaryāṃ bhūmau / śrutākāradharmālokāvabhāsa-samādhyālokāvabhāsa-prabhāvitatvādasyā bhūmeḥ prabhākarītyucyate / adhyātmaṃ cittaviśuddhimupādāya sā prabhā saṃbhavati tasmātsa vihāraḥ adhicitta ityucyate / yenārthena prabhākarī bhūmiḥ tenaivārthenādhicittavihāro veditavyaḥ /
body.translated_text: his fetters of existence [are abandoned]. Already previously, in the aspiration-conduct stage (<s>adhimukticaryābhūmi</s>), his fetters made by [wrong] views have been abandoned through his aspiration toward the suchness of <s>dharmas</s> (<s>dharmatathatā</s>). And wrong desire, hatred, and delusion do not at all operate in him. His seeing of <s>Buddhas</s> and the purification of wholesome roots in detail should be understood as before. And here is the distinction: just as that very gold, in the hand of a skilled goldsmith, having had its impurities and dross removed, remains stable and even in weight—so should the purification of this [<s>Bodhisattva</s>'s] wholesome roots be understood. And from the [standpoint of] rebirth, he for the most part becomes <s>Śakra</s>, the lord of the gods. He is skilled in turning beings away from sensual desire. And regarding power, where in the previous stage a thousand was stated, here a hundred thousand should be understood. This is the <s>Bodhisattvas</s>' higher-mind stage. It should be understood through the summary teaching: from the entry into the accomplishment of the mental-intention reflections, from the correct penetration of <s>saṃsāra</s>, the realm of beings, and great awakening, from the correct seeking of the means for the liberation of beings from suffering, from the seeking of the <s>Dharma</s> with great reverence, from the dwelling in the practice in conformity with the <s>Dharma</s> and the accomplishment of mundane <s>dhyānas</s>, <s>samādhis</s>, attainments, and superknowledges, from turning away from them and being reborn by aspiration in the desire realm, from the purification of wholesome roots, from the [type of] rebirth, and from the [degree of] power. For the detailed teaching, it is just as in the <s>sūtra</s>—namely, as in the <s>Daśabhūmika</s>, in the <s>Prabhākarī</s> (Radiant) stage. Because this stage is illuminated by the light of learning, the light of the aspects of <s>Dharma</s>, and the light of <s>samādhi</s>, it is called <s>Prabhākarī</s>. Because the radiance arises internally from the purification of mind, that stage is called the higher-mind [stage]. The meaning by which it is called the <s>Prabhākarī</s> stage is the same meaning by which the higher-mind stage should be understood.

body.text: tatra katamo bodhisattvānāṃ bodhipakṣyapratisaṃyukto 'dhiprajñavihāraḥ / iha bodhisattvena pūrvamevādhicittavihāre daśa dharmālokapraveśāḥ śrutaparyeṣṭimadhipattiṃ kṛtvā pratilabdhā bhavanti / yeṣāmadhimātratvātparipūrṇatvādadhicittavihāramatikramya prathamamadhiprajñavihāraṃ praviśati / [te] punardaśa dharmālokapraveśā granthato yathā sūtrameva veditavyaḥ / ye ca prajñapyante yatra ca prajñapyante yena ca prajñapyante te ca yatsamāḥ paramārthaḥ yasya ca saṃkleśa-vyavadānaśca saṃkliśyante viśuddhante ca yatpratiyusaṃktena saṃkleśena saṃkliśyante yayā cānuttarayā viśuddhyā
body.translated_text: There, what is the <s>Bodhisattvas</s>' abode of higher wisdom connected with the factors of awakening (<s>bodhipakṣyapratisaṃyukta adhiprajñavihāra</s>)? Here, the <s>Bodhisattva</s>, already in the prior abode of higher mind, has obtained the ten entries into the light of <s>Dharma</s> (<s>dharmālokapraveśa</s>), making hearing and investigation the governing [factors]. Through the abundance and fullness of these, one surpasses the abode of higher mind and enters the first abode of higher wisdom. The ten entries into the light of <s>Dharma</s> should be understood textually just as in the <s>sūtra</s>. [In summary:] those that are designated, where they are designated, by what they are designated, and that with which they are equal — the ultimate reality; and [the nature] of whose defilement and purification they become defiled and purified, and by which connected defilement they become defiled, and by which unsurpassed purification

body.text: viśudhyante / ityayaṃ samāsārthasteṣāṃ dharmālokanirdeśānāṃ veditavyaḥ / sa tasmin vihāre vyavasthitaḥ / abhedyāśayatā pūrvaṅgamairyathāsūtrameva daśākāreṇa jñānaparipākena [jñāna-]paripācakairdharmaiḥ samanvāgataḥ saṃvṛtto bhavati tathāgatakule tadātmaka-dharmapratilambhāt / sarvākārāṃ bodhisattvāpekṣāmadhipatiṃ kṛtvā smṛtyupasthānapramukhān saptatriṃśadbodhipakṣyān dharmān bhāvayanti yathāsūtrameva / tasya tāndharmānupāyaparigraheṇa bhāvayataḥ satkāyadṛṣṭiḥ susūkṣmāpyasya skandhadhātvāyatanānyabhiniveśaḥ sarveñjitāni cātyantāsamudācārataḥ prahīyante / teṣāṃ prahāṇād yāni tathāgata-vivarṇitāni karmāṇi tāni sarveṇa sarvaṃ nādhyācarati / yāni punastathāgata-varṇitāni tāni sarvāpyanuvartante yathāvat / tathābhūtaśca bhūyasā mātrayā snigdhamṛdukarmaṇyacittaśca bhavati tathā citrākārasuviśuddhacittaśca / kṛtajñakṛtaveditādibhistadāśayānuguṇairvicitraiḥ śukla-dharmaiḥ samanvāgato bhavati / uttari ca bhūmipariśodhakāni karmāṇi samanveṣamāṇo mahāvīryārambhaprāpto bhavati / tasya tannidānamāśayādhyāśayādhimuktidhātuḥ paripūryate / tannidānaṃ cāsaṃhāryo bhavati avikampyaḥ sarvatīrthyamāraśāsanapratyarthikabhūtaiḥ / pūrvavacca buddhadarśanaṃ vistareṇa kuśalamūlaviśuddhirveditavyā / tatrāyaṃ viśeṣaḥ / tadyathā tadeva suvarṇakuśalena karmakāreṇālaṃkāravidhikṛtamasaṃhāryaṃ bhavatyakṛtābharaṇairjātarupaiḥ / evamasya bodhisattvasya tāni kuśalamūlānyasaṃhāryāṇi bhavanti tadanyabālavihārasthitairbodhisattvakuśalamūlaiḥ / tadyathā ca maṇiratnamuktālokamasaṃhāryaṃ bhavati tadanyairmaṇibhiḥ / sarvavātodakavṛṣṭibhiścānācchedyaprabhaṃ bhavati / evamayaṃ bodhisattvo 'saṃhāryo bhavati sarvaśrāvakapratyekabuddhaiḥ / anācchedyaprajñālokaśca bhavati sarvamārapratyarthikaiḥ / upapattitaśca suyāmo bhavati devarājaḥ / kuśalaḥ sattvānāṃ satkāyadṛṣṭivinivartanatāyai / prabhāve ca yatra pūrvavihāre śatasahasraguṇaṃ samākhyātaṃ tatrāsmin koṭisamākhyātaṃ veditavyam / ayaṃ bodhisattvānāṃ bodhipakṣyādhiprajñavihāraḥ / dharmālokapraveśaniṣpattiṃ pratilābhataśca jñānaparipācanataśca bodhipakṣyadharmaniṣevaṇataśca satkāyadṛṣṭyādi-sarvābhiniveśeñjitaprahāṇataśca pratiṣiddhānujñātakarmavivarjana-niṣevaṇataśca tannidānaṃ cittamārdavataśca tadanukūlaguṇasamṛddhitaśca
body.translated_text: they become purified — this should be understood as the summary meaning of those teachings on the light of <s>Dharma</s>. One established in that abode, preceded by an invincible intention (<s>abhedyāśayatā</s>), becomes endowed with <s>dharmas</s> that bring about the maturation of knowledge in ten aspects, just as in the <s>sūtra</s>. One has become [a member] of the <s>Tathāgata</s> family, through the attainment of <s>dharmas</s> that are of the same nature as that [family]. Making the <s>Bodhisattva</s>'s aspiration in all aspects the governing [factor], one cultivates the thirty-seven <s>dharmas</s> conducive to awakening (<s>bodhipakṣya dharma</s>), beginning with the right foundations of mindfulness (<s>smṛtyupasthāna</s>), just as in the <s>sūtra</s>. For one cultivating those <s>dharmas</s> with the embrace of skillful means, the view of the composite self (<s>satkāyadṛṣṭi</s>), even the most subtle, one's clinging to the aggregates, elements, and sense-bases (<s>skandha-dhātu-āyatana</s>), and all wavering — are abandoned through their absolute non-occurrence. Through their abandonment, whatever actions are censured by the <s>Tathāgata</s>, one does not engage in them in any way whatsoever. And whatever actions are praised by the <s>Tathāgata</s>, one follows all of them properly. And being of such a nature, to a far greater degree one's mind becomes moist, soft, and workable, and likewise of variegated form and supremely purified. One becomes endowed with various wholesome <s>dharmas</s> that accord with that intention, such as gratitude, appreciation, and the like. And seeking actions that further purify the stages, one attains the undertaking of great vigor. Through that as cause, one's disposition of intention, superior intention, and conviction (<s>āśaya-adhyāśaya-adhimuktidhātu</s>) becomes fulfilled. And through that as cause, one becomes unassailable and unshakable by all opponents who are <s>tīrthikas</s>, <s>Māras</s>, or adversaries of the teaching. And as before, the seeing of <s>Buddhas</s> and the purification of wholesome roots should be understood in detail. The distinction here is as follows: just as that very gold, when fashioned into ornaments by a skilled goldsmith, becomes unmatched by unworked nuggets of gold, so the wholesome roots of this <s>Bodhisattva</s> become unmatched by the wholesome roots of <s>Bodhisattvas</s> established in other, lower abodes. And just as the radiance of a jewel-gem is unmatched by other gems, and its light is uninterrupted by all winds and rain-storms, so this <s>Bodhisattva</s> becomes unmatched by all <s>Śrāvakas</s> and <s>Pratyekabuddhas</s>, and the light of one's wisdom is uncut by all adversaries who are <s>Māras</s>. And by rebirth one becomes <s>Suyāma</s>, king of the gods, skilled in turning beings away from the view of the composite self (<s>satkāyadṛṣṭi</s>). And regarding power, where in the previous abode it was declared as a hundredfold increase, here it should be understood as declared in terms of <s>koṭis</s> (ten-millions). This is the <s>Bodhisattvas</s>' abode of higher wisdom connected with the factors of awakening — to be understood in summary through the attainment of the entries into the light of <s>Dharma</s>, through the maturation of knowledge, through the cultivation of the <s>dharmas</s> conducive to awakening, through the abandonment of the view of the composite self and all clinging and wavering, through the avoidance and practice of prohibited and permitted actions, through the softness of mind arising from that cause, through the fulfillment of qualities in accord with that

body.text: bhūmipariśodhaka-karmaparyeṣṭimārabhya mahāvīryārambhataśca tannidānamāśayādhyāśayādhimuktiviśodhanataśca tannidānaṃ sarvaśāsanapratyarthikāsaṃhāryataśca kuśalamūlaviśuddhitaścopapattitaśca prabhāvataśca samāsanirdeśato veditavyaḥ / vistaranirdeśaḥ punastadyathādaśabhūmike 'rciṣmatī bhūminirdeśe bodhipakṣyā dharmāstasyāṃ bhūmau jñānārcibhūtāḥ samyagdharmadeśanā prajñāvabhāsakarakālokānām / tasmātsā bhūmirarciṣmatītyucyate / saiva ceha bodhipakṣyāprajñāvabhāsakara-dhiprajñavihāra ityucyate /
body.translated_text: , through the undertaking of great vigor beginning with the search for actions that purify the stages, through the purification of the disposition of intention, superior intention, and conviction arising from that cause, through being unassailable by all adversaries of the teaching arising from that cause, through the purification of wholesome roots, through rebirth, and through power — to be understood in summary. The detailed teaching, moreover, is as in the <s>Daśabhūmika</s>, in the exposition of the <s>Arciṣmatī</s> (Radiant) stage. The <s>dharmas</s> conducive to awakening on that stage become flames of knowledge, [producing] the radiance and light of right <s>Dharma</s>-teaching and wisdom. Therefore that stage is called <s>Arciṣmatī</s> (Radiant). And this very same [stage] is here called the abode of higher wisdom connected with the factors of awakening, the radiance and light of wisdom.

body.text: tatra katamo bodhisattvānāṃ satyapratisaṃyukto dvitīyo 'dhiprajñavihāraḥ / iha bodhisattvaḥ pūrvake 'dhiprajñavihāre [yā] daśa viśuddhāśayasamatāḥ pratilabdhāḥ tāsāmadhimātrātvāt paripūrṇatvāt dvitīyamadhiprajñavihāraṃ praviśati / daśa viśuddhāśayasamatā yathāsūtraṃ granthato veditavyāḥ / asamaiśca buddhairbuddhāḥ samāḥ / tadanyasattvadhātusamatikrāntāḥ / yaiśca dharmairyathā samāḥ / ityayaṃ samāsārtho viśuddhāśayasamatānāṃ veditavyaḥ / so 'sminvihāre vyavasthitaḥ / bhūyo jñānavaiśeṣikatāṃ prārthayamānaḥ catvāryasatyāni daśabhirākārairyathābhūtaṃ prajānāti / granthato yathāsūtrameva sarvaṃ veditavyam / parasaṃjñāpanatāṃ [pratyātmajñānatāṃ] tadubhayādhiṣṭhānatāṃ cārabhya yacca deśyate / sūtravinayamātṛkāmārabhya yena ca deśyate / pratyupannaduḥkhātmakatāṃ hetu[ta]ścānāgataduḥkhaprabhāvatāṃ hetukṣayāt [tat]kṣayānutpāda[na]tāṃ tatprahāṇopāyaniṣevaṇatāṃ cārabhya yathā deśyate / ityayaṃ samāsārthastasya daśākārasya caturāryasatyajñānasya veditavyaḥ / sa evaṃ satyakuśalaḥ sarvañca saṃskāragataṃ prajñayā samyag vidūṣayati / sattvadhātau ca karūṇāśayaṃ vivardhayati / pūrvāntāparāntataśca bālasattvamithyāpratipattiṃ samyak pratividhyati / teṣāñca vimokṣāya mahāpuṇyajñānasambhāraparigrahe cittaṃ praṇidhatte / tadgatāśayaṃ ca samudānayati / smṛtimatigatipramukhaiḥ prabhūtairvicitrairguṇaiḥ samṛddhaśca / anya manasikārāpagataḥ / citraiḥ paripācanopāyai sattvān paripācayati / yāni ca sattvānugrāhakāni laukikāni lipiśāstramudrāgaṇanādīni yathāsūtrameva śilpakarmaṃsthānāni tāni sarvāṇyābhinirharati sattvakaruṇa[ta]yā /
body.translated_text: There, what is the <s>Bodhisattvas</s>' second abode of higher wisdom connected with the truths (<s>satyapratisaṃyukta adhiprajñavihāra</s>)? Here, the <s>Bodhisattva</s>, having obtained the ten equalities of purified intention (<s>viśuddhāśayasamatā</s>) in the previous abode of higher wisdom — through their abundance and fullness — enters the second abode of higher wisdom. The ten equalities of purified intention should be understood textually just as in the <s>sūtra</s>. <s>Buddhas</s> are equal to the unequaled <s>Buddhas</s>, having surpassed the rest of the realm of beings. And the <s>dharmas</s> by which they are thus equal — this should be understood as the summary meaning of the equalities of purified intention.
