One established in this abode, seeking further distinction in knowledge, truly knows the four noble truths in ten aspects. Everything should be understood textually just as in the <s>sūtra</s>. With reference to the capacity for making others understand, for personal knowledge, and for the establishment of both — and what is taught; with reference to <s>sūtra</s>, <s>vinaya</s>, and <s>mātṛkā</s> — and by which it is taught; with reference to the nature of present suffering being of the nature of self, and through cause the nature of future suffering's arising, and through the destruction of cause the nature of its destruction and non-arising, and through the cultivation of the means for its abandonment — and how it is taught — this should be understood as the summary meaning of the ten-aspected knowledge of the four noble truths. One thus skilled in the truths, with wisdom one thoroughly exposes the faults of everything belonging to conditioned existence. And one increases the disposition of compassion toward the realm of beings. And one correctly penetrates the wrong practice of childish beings regarding the past and the future. And for their liberation, one resolves the mind upon the embrace of the great accumulations of merit and knowledge. And one brings about an intention directed toward that. And one is enriched with abundant and varied qualities, beginning with mindfulness, intelligence, and insight. And free from other preoccupations, one matures beings through various means of maturation. And whatever worldly arts and sciences that benefit beings — writing, science, seals, calculation, and the like — just as in the <s>sūtra</s>, all those crafts and applied sciences one brings to completion, out of compassion for beings

body.text: anupūrveṇa yāvat bodhipratiṣṭhāpanārthaṃ laukikavyavahārānukūlatayā dāridrya-nāśopāyatayā dhātuvaiṣamyamanuṣyāmanuṣyopasaṃhṛtopadravapraśamanatayā 'navadyakrīḍārativastūpasaṃhārato dharmarativyāvartanatayā sannivāsopakaraṇārthināmalpakṛcchreṇa sannivāsopakaraṇopasaṃharaṇatayā rājacaurādyupadravaparitrāṇatayā sthānāsthānaprayogānujñāpratiṣedhanatayā maṅgalyāmaṅgalyavastvādānatyāgasanniyojanatayā dṛṣṭe dharme parasparānabhidrohasamparāyāviparītābhyudayamārgopadeśanatayā / ityayaṃ teṣāṃ sattvānugrāhakānāṃ śilpakarmasthānānāṃ samāsārtho veditavyaḥ / sarvamanyatpūrvavat / tatrāyaṃ viśeṣaḥ / tadyathā tadeva svarṇakuśalena karmakāreṇa musāragalva-mṛṣṭaṃ pratyarpitamatulyatayā 'saṃhāryaṃ bhavati tadanyaiḥ suvarṇaiḥ / evamayaṃ bodhisattvo 'saṃhāryo bhavati sarvaśrāvakapratyekabuddhaiḥ tadanyabhūmisthitaiśca bodhisattvaiḥ / tadyathā candrasūryanakṣatrāṇāmābhā asaṃhāryā ca bhavati sarva vātamaṇḍalaiḥ / [sarva]vātavāhā sādhāraṇā ca bhavati / evamevāsya bodhisattvasya sā prajñā asaṃhāryā bhavati sarvaśrāvakapratyekabuddhaiḥ / laukikakriyā sādhāraṇā ca bhavati / upapattitaḥ saṃtuṣito bhavati devarājaḥ / kuśalaḥ sarvatīrthyavinivartanatāyai / prabhāvaśca koṭīśatasahasrasaṃkhyā nirdeśato veditavyaḥ / ayaṃ bodhisattvānāṃ satyapratisaṃyukto 'dhiprajñavihāraḥ / śuddhāśayasamatā-niṣpatti-praveśataśca upāyasatyavyavacāraṇā-prativivardhanataśca sarvasaṃskāravidūṣaṇataśca kārūṇyavivardhanataśca tadarthaṃ puṇyajñānasaṃbhāropacayapraṇidhānaprayogataśca smṛtimatigatyādiguṇavivṛddhitaścānanyamanasikāra-sarvākāra-sattvaparipācanābhiyogataśca laukikaśilpābhinirhārataśca kuśalamūlaviśuddhitaścopapattitaśca prabhāvataśca samāsanirdeśato veditavyaḥ / vistaranirdeśataḥ punastadyathā daśabhūmike sudurjayāyāṃ bhūmau sattveṣu niścayajñānaṃ sudurjayam / tacceha paridīpitam / tasmātsā bhumiḥ sudurjayetyucyate / tenaiva cārthena satyapratisaṃyukto 'dhiprajñavihāro draṣṭavyaḥ /
body.translated_text: — progressively up to the establishment in awakening, through conformity to worldly conventions, as a means for the destruction of poverty, for the pacification of calamities caused by elemental imbalance and by humans and non-humans, for providing blameless recreation and amusement and for turning [beings] toward delight in the <s>Dharma</s>, for providing dwellings and requisites with little difficulty to those who desire dwellings and requisites, for protection from calamities of kings, thieves, and the like, for prescribing and prohibiting the application of what is appropriate and inappropriate, for directing the adoption and relinquishing of auspicious and inauspicious objects, and for teaching the path to mutual non-hostility in this present life and non-perverted prosperity in the future. This should be understood as the summary meaning of those crafts and applied sciences that benefit beings. Everything else is as before. The distinction here is as follows: just as that very gold, when polished with coral by a skilled goldsmith, becomes unmatched by other unpolished gold, so this <s>Bodhisattva</s> becomes unmatched by all <s>Śrāvakas</s>, <s>Pratyekabuddhas</s>, and <s>Bodhisattvas</s> established on other stages. And just as the radiance of the moon, sun, and stars is unassailable by all wind-circles, and yet the course of those winds is shared [with them], so the wisdom of this <s>Bodhisattva</s> is unassailable by all <s>Śrāvakas</s> and <s>Pratyekabuddhas</s>, and yet his worldly activities are shared [with ordinary beings]. By rebirth one becomes <s>Saṃtuṣita</s>, king of the gods, skilled in turning away all <s>tīrthikas</s>. And one's power should be understood as described in terms of hundreds of thousands of <s>koṭis</s>. This is the <s>Bodhisattvas</s>' abode of higher wisdom connected with the truths — to be understood in summary through the attainment and entry into the equalities of purified intention, through the advancement in the investigation of the truths by skillful means, through the thorough exposure of the faults of all conditioned things, through the increase of compassion, through the endeavor of accumulating merit and knowledge for that purpose through aspiration and practice, through the growth of qualities such as mindfulness, intelligence, and insight, through the engagement in all-aspected maturation of beings without other preoccupation, through the accomplishment of worldly arts, through the purification of wholesome roots, through rebirth, and through power — to be understood in summary. The detailed teaching, moreover, is as in the <s>Daśabhūmika</s>, on the <s>Sudurjayā</s> (Difficult to Conquer) stage. The definitive knowledge regarding beings on that stage is difficult to conquer. And that is illuminated here. Therefore that stage is called <s>Sudurjayā</s>. And by that very meaning, the abode of higher wisdom connected with the truths should be seen.

body.text: tatra katamo bodhisattvānāṃ pratītyasamutpādapratisaṃyukto 'dhiprajñavihāraḥ / iha bodhisattvena pūrvameva satyapratisaṃyukte adhiprajñavihāre daśa dharmasamatāḥ pratilabdhaḥ
body.translated_text: There, what is the <s>Bodhisattvas</s>' abode of higher wisdom connected with dependent origination (<s>pratītyasamutpādapratisaṃyukta adhiprajñavihāra</s>)? Here, the <s>Bodhisattva</s>, already in the previous abode of higher wisdom connected with the truths, has obtained the ten equalities of <s>dharmas</s> (<s>dharmasamatā</s>)

body.text: bhavanti / yathāsūtraṃ granthatastā veditavyāḥ / tāsāmadhimatratvātparipūrṇatvādidaṃ vihāramanupraviśati / sarvadharmeṣu pāramārthikasya sataḥ svabhāvasya nirnimittasamatayā abhilāpābhisaṃskārapratibhāsasyālakṣaṇasamatayā tasyaivālakṣaṇatvāt svayamajātasamatayā hetuto 'nutpannasamatā svayaṃ hetu[ta]ścānuptannatvādatyantamādiśāntasamatayā vidyamāna[sya] vastugrāhakasya jñānasya niṣprapañcasamatayā ādānatyāgābhisaṃskāravigamasamatayā ca tasyaiva kleśaduḥkhasaṃkleśa-visaṃyogād viviktasamatayā vikalpitasya jñeyasvabhāvasya māyānirmitopamasamatayā nirvikalpajñānagocarasya svabhāvasya bhāvābhāvādvayasamatayā / ityayaṃ tāsāṃ daśānāṃ dharmasamatānāmarthavibhāgo veditavyaḥ / so 'sminvihāre sthitaḥ sattveṣu saṃvṛddhakaruṇo bodhau tīvracchandābhilāṣajātaḥ / lokānāṃ saṃbhavañca vibhavañca sarvākārayā pratītyasamutpāda-samyagvyavacāraṇatayā vyavacārayati prajānāti / pratītyasamutpādajñānasanniśritaṃ cāsya vimokṣamukhatrayamājātaṃ bhavati śūnyamanimittamapraṇihitam / tato nidānaṃ cāsyātma-para-kāraka-vedakabhāvābhāvasaṃjñā na pravartante / sa evaṃ paramārthakuśalaḥ sattvasāpekṣaḥ yoniśaḥ pratividhyati kleśasaṃyogāt / pratyayasāmagryācca saṃskṛtaṃ prakṛtidurbalamātmātmīyavirahitamanekadoṣaduṣṭaṃ pravartate na vinā kleśasaṃyogapratyayasāmagrīm / tena mayā kleśasaṃyogapratyayasāmagrīṃ ca vikalīkartavyā cātmarakṣārtham / na ca sarveṇa sarvaṃ saṃskṛtaṃ vyupaśamayitavyaṃ sattvānugrahārtham / tasyaivaṃ jñānakārūṇyānugatasyāsmin vihāre 'saṅgajñānābhimukho nāma prajñāpāramitāvihāraḥ abhisaṃmukhī bhavati / yenāyaṃ sarvalokikacaryāsvaśaktaścarati / sa ca vihāro yā tīkṣṇā saptamyāṃ bhūmau prāyogikacaryāparyantagatā bodhisattvakṣāntiḥ tayānulomikyā kṣāntyā saṃgṛhīto veditavyaḥ / so 'saṅgajñānābhimukha-prajñāpāramitā-vihārābhimukhyād bodhyāhārakāṃśca pratyayānāharati / laukikānāñca saṃskṛtasaṃvāse na saṃvasati / praśame ca śāntadarśī bhavati / na ca tatrāvatiṣṭhate / tasyaivamupāya-prajñājñānānugata-syāvatāra-śūnyatāsamādhipramukhāni daśa samādhimukhaśatasahasrāṇyāmukhī bhavati / yathā śūnyatāsamādhiḥ evamapraṇihitānimittasamādhayo veditavyāḥ /
body.translated_text: they are. They should be understood textually as in the <s>sūtras</s>. Through the intensity and completeness of these [equalities], one enters this abode. [The ten equalities are:] the equality of signlessness (<s>nirnimittasamatā</s>) of the ultimate, existent intrinsic nature of all <s>dharmas</s>; the equality of characteristiclessness (<s>alakṣaṇasamatā</s>) of the appearance of conceptual construction through verbal designation; the equality of self-unborn (<s>svayamajātasamatā</s>) because of that very characteristiclessness; the equality of unproduced from causes (<s>anutpannasamatā</s>) because of being both self-unborn and unproduced from causes; the equality of primordially quiescent (<s>ādiśāntasamatā</s>) because of being ultimately [unproduced]; the equality of non-proliferation (<s>niṣprapañcasamatā</s>) of the existing knowledge that apprehends objects; the equality of the cessation of the construction of grasping and releasing (<s>ādānatyāgābhisaṃskāravigamasamatā</s>); the equality of seclusion (<s>viviktasamatā</s>) due to the separation from the defilement of afflictions and suffering; the equality of being like an illusion or magical creation (<s>māyānirmitopamasamatā</s>) of the conceptually constructed intrinsic nature of the knowable; and the equality of the non-duality of existence and non-existence (<s>bhāvābhāvādvayasamatā</s>) of the intrinsic nature that is the domain of non-conceptual knowledge. This should be understood as the analysis of the meaning of these ten equalities of <s>dharmas</s>. Established in this abode, with compassion toward beings greatly increased, with intense desire and longing for awakening arisen, he investigates and knows the arising and dissolution of the worlds through the correct comprehensive examination of dependent origination (<s>pratītyasamutpāda</s>) in all aspects. And relying on the knowledge of dependent origination, the three doors of liberation (<s>vimokṣamukha</s>) arise for him: emptiness (<s>śūnya</s>), signlessness (<s>animitta</s>), and wishlessness (<s>apraṇihita</s>). From that cause, perceptions of self, other, agent, and experiencer as existent or non-existent do not arise in him. Thus skilled in ultimate reality, with concern for beings, he correctly penetrates [the following]: through the conjunction of defilements and the assemblage of conditions, the conditioned arises—inherently weak, devoid of self and what belongs to self, corrupted by manifold faults—and does not arise without the conjunction of defilements and the assemblage of conditions. 'Therefore, I must undo the conjunction of defilements and the assemblage of conditions for the purpose of protecting myself. Yet I must not completely pacify all that is conditioned, for the sake of assisting beings.' For him, thus accompanied by knowledge and compassion, in this abode, the abode of the perfection of wisdom (<s>prajñāpāramitāvihāra</s>) called 'facing unobstructed knowledge' (<s>asaṅgajñānābhimukha</s>) becomes proximate. Through this, he becomes able to engage in all worldly activities. And that abode should be understood as comprised by the conforming patience (<s>ānulomikī kṣānti</s>)—the keen <s>Bodhisattva</s>-patience on the seventh stage (<s>bhūmi</s>) that has reached the culmination of preparatory practice. Through facing the abode of the perfection of wisdom facing unobstructed knowledge, he gathers the conditions that nourish awakening. And he does not dwell in the company of the conditioned that belongs to the worldly. And he sees peace in quiescence. Yet he does not rest in that. For him, thus accompanied by the knowledge of skill in means and wisdom, one hundred thousand groups of ten concentrations (<s>samādhimukha</s>) become accessible, headed by the emptiness concentration (<s>śūnyatāsamādhi</s>). Just as the emptiness concentration, so the wishless and signless concentrations should be understood.

body.text: teṣāmāmukhībhavādabhedyāśayaśca bhavati / sarvākārācchāsanādasaṃhāryaśca bhavati sarvamāratīrthyaśāsanapratyarthikaiḥ śeṣaṃ pūrvavat / tatrāyaṃ viśeṣaḥ / tadyathā tadeva suvarṇaṃ kuśalena karmakāreṇa vaidūryamaṇiratnamuṣṭaṃ pratyarpitamasaṃhāryaṃ bhavati tadanyaiḥ sarvajātarūpaiḥ evamasya bodhisattvasya tāni kuśalamūlāni viśuddhatarāṇi bhavantyasaṃhāryāṇi pūrvavat / tadyathā candraprabhā sattvāśrayāṃśca prahalādayatyanācchedyaprabhā ca bhavati catasṛbhirvātamaṇḍalikābhiḥ / evamasya bodhisattvasya sā prajñābhā sarvasattvakleśaparidāhañca praśamayati / anācchedyā ca bhavati sarvamārapratyarthikaiḥ / sunirmitaśca bhavati devarājaḥ / kuśalaḥ sattvānāṃ sarvābhimānavinivartanatāyai / prabhāvo 'pi koṭīśatasahasraṃ saṃkhyānirdeśato draṣṭavyaḥ / ayaṃ pratītyasamutpādapratisaṃyukto 'dhiprajñavihāraḥ / dharmasamatā-pariniṣpattipraveśataśca pratītyasamutpādāvabodhavimokṣamukhasambhavataśca sarvamithyāsaṃjñāsamudācārataśca upāyasaṃsāraparigrahataśca asaṅgajñānābhimukha-prajñāpāramitāvihārābhimukhataśca apramāṇa-samādhipratilambhataśca abhedyāśayapratilambhataśca śāsanādāsaṃhāryataśca kuśalamūlaviśuddhita upapattitaḥ prabhāvataśca samāsanirdeśato veditavyaḥ / vistara[nirdaśata]stadyathā 'bhimukhyāṃ bhūmau / asaṅgajñānābhimukhasya prajñāpāramitāvihārasyābhimukhyādabhimukhītyucyate / tanaivārthenāyaṃ vihāro veditavyaḥ /
body.translated_text: Through the accessibility of those [concentrations], his intention becomes indestructible. And he becomes unshakable by all opponents—including all <s>Māra</s>-adherents, heretics, and adversaries of the teaching—in all aspects. The remainder is as before. Here there is a distinction: Just as that very gold, when set with a <s>vaiḍūrya</s> jewel-gem by a skilled craftsman, becomes unsurpassable by all other types of gold—even so, the wholesome roots of this <s>Bodhisattva</s> become more purified and unsurpassable, as before. Just as the radiance of the moon both soothes beings in their bodily basis and is uninterruptible by the four groups of winds—even so, the radiance of wisdom of this <s>Bodhisattva</s> pacifies the burning of afflictions of all beings and is uninterruptible by all <s>Māra</s>-adversaries. And the god-king <s>Sunirmita</s> comes into being. He is skilled in removing all the conceit of beings. His power should be seen as amounting to one hundred <s>koṭīs</s> (ten billions) in terms of numerical designation. This is the abode of higher wisdom connected with dependent origination. Through the entry into the completion of the equalities of <s>dharmas</s>, through the arising of the three doors of liberation from the comprehension of dependent origination, through the cessation of all false conceptual habits, through the embrace of <s>saṃsāra</s> through skillful means, through facing the abode of the perfection of wisdom facing unobstructed knowledge, through the attainment of immeasurable concentrations, through the attainment of an indestructible intention, through being unshakable from the teaching, through the purification of wholesome roots, through rebirth, and through power—it should be understood in summary. The detailed [exposition is] as in the sixth stage (<s>Abhimukhī bhūmi</s>). Because of facing the abode of the perfection of wisdom facing unobstructed knowledge (<s>asaṅgajñānābhimukha</s>), it is called <s>Abhimukhī</s> ('Facing'). This abode should be understood by that very meaning.

body.text: tatra katamo bodhisattvānāṃ sābhisaṃskāraḥ sābhogo nirnimitto vihāraḥ / iha bodhisattvenānantare 'dhiprajñavihāre daśopāyena prajñayā cābhinirhṛtāḥ sarvasattvāsādhāraṇā laukikāḥ sarvalokāsādhāraṇāśca mārgāntarārambhaviśeṣāḥ pratilabdhā bhavanti / yeṣāmadhimātratvātparipūrṇatvātsaptamaṃ vihāramanupraviśati / teṣāṃ yathāsūtrameva granthavistaro veditavyaḥ / laukikasampattisaṃvartakaṃ puṇyaparigraha mārabhya sattveṣu hitasukhāśayamārabhya bodhāya puṇyasambhārabodhipakṣya-dharmottarotkarṣamārabhya śrāvakāsādhāraṇatāmārabhya pratyekabuddhāsādhāraṇatāmārabhya sattvadharmadhātumārabhya lokadhātumārabhya tathāgatakāyavākcittajñānamāramya / ityathaṃ teṣāmupāyaprajñābhinihṛtānāṃ mārgāntarāṇāmārambhaviśeṣāṇāmadhikārārthaḥ samāsato veditavyaḥ / sa ebhiryukto 'pramāṇamasaṃkhyeyaṃ tathāgataviṣayaṃ pratividhyati / tatsamutthānāya
body.translated_text: There, what is the <s>Bodhisattvas</s>' signless abode with volition and effort (<s>sābhisaṃskāra sābhoga nirnimitta vihāra</s>)? Here, the <s>Bodhisattva</s>, in the immediately preceding abode of higher wisdom, through the tenfold means and wisdom, has attained the commencement of distinctive path-stages that are extraordinary among all beings and extraordinary among all worlds. Through the intensity and completeness of those [attainments], one enters the seventh abode. Their detailed textual expansion should be understood as in the <s>sūtras</s>. Beginning with the embracing of merit that brings about worldly accomplishment, beginning with the intention of benefit and happiness toward beings, beginning with the progressive elevation of factors conducive to awakening as an accumulation of merit for awakening, beginning with [qualities] not shared with <s>Śrāvakas</s>, beginning with [qualities] not shared with <s>Pratyekabuddhas</s>, beginning with the realm of beings and the realm of <s>dharmas</s>, beginning with the realm of worlds, and beginning with the knowledge of the body, speech, mind, and wisdom of the <s>Tathāgata</s>—thus should be understood in summary the scope and purpose of these distinctive path-stages that have been accomplished through means and wisdom. Endowed with these, he penetrates the immeasurable, incalculable domain of the <s>Tathāgata</s>. For the purpose of actualizing that

body.text: cānābhoganirnimittākalpāvikalpanatayā 'pramāṇabuddhiviṣaya-samutthānaṃ paśyan nirantaraṃ niścchidraṃ prayujyate sarveryāpatha-cāravihāramanasikāreṣu / nāsya sarvāvasthāgatasya mārgaviprayukto bhavati / tasya cittakṣaṇe daśapāramitāḥ pramukhāḥ sarve bodhipakṣyā dharmāḥ paripūryante viśeṣeṇa / anyeṣu tu vihāreṣu na tathā / prathame pramuditavihāre praṇidhānādhyālambanatayā dvitīye cittadauḥśīlyamalāpakarṣaṇatayā tṛtīye praṇidhānavivardhanadharmālokapratilābhatayā caturthe mārgāvatāraṇatayā pañcabhe laukikakriyāvatāraṇa yā ṣaṣṭhe gambhīrapraveśanatayā / āsmin punaḥ saptame vihāre sarvabuddhadharmasamutthāpanatayā bodhaṅgāni paripūryante bodhisattvaprāyogikacaryāparipūrisaṃgrahādasya vihārasya jñānābhijñācaryāviśuddhāṣṭamavihārākramaṇācca / tathā hi sa bodhisattvo 'sya vihārasyānantaramaṣṭamaṃ viśuddhaṃ vihāraṃ praviśati / sa ca vihāra ekāntaviśuddhaḥ / ime tu sapta vihārā vyāmiśrāḥ / viśuddhavihārapūrvaṅgamatvādasaṃkliṣṭaḥ / tadasaṃprāptatvātsaṃkliṣṭacayapatitā vaktavyāḥ / tasmādasmin vihāre sarve rāgādipramukhāḥ kleśāḥ prahīyante / sa ca na saṃkleśo na niḥkleśo veditavyaḥ asamudācārād buddhajñānābhilāṣācca / tathābhūtasyāsyādhyāśayapariśuddhamapramāṇaṃ kāya vāḍabhanaskarma pravartate / sa yāni tathāgatavivarṇitāni karmāṇi pūrvavat tasya pañcamavihārābhinihṛtāni laukikāni śilpajñānānīha paripūryante ācāryasammataśca bhavati trisāhasramahāsāhasre sthāpayitvā ūrdhvavihārasthān bodhisattvāṃstathāgatāṃśca / na kaścidasyāśayaprayogābhyāṃ samo bhavati / sarve ca dhyānādayo bodhipakṣyā dharmā āmukhī bhavanti / bhāvanākārābhimukhatayā nottariyākārasthānataḥ / tadyathā āmukhī bhavanti / bhāvanākārābhimukhatayā nottariyākārasthānataḥ / tadyathā aṣṭhame vihāre / sa tathā prayuktaḥ suniścitaviṣayasamādhipramukhāni daśa samādhiśatasahasrāṇyabhinirharati bodhisattvasamādhīnām / teṣāñca lābhātsamatikrānto bhavati śrāvakapratyekabuddhasamādhiviṣayam / sa evaṃ sarvakleśaviviktena durvijñeyena sarvavikalpapracārāpagatena kāyavāṅmanaskarmaṇā viharati / na cottariviśeṣaparimārgaṇābhiyogamutsṛjati sattvāpekṣayā / bodhiparipūrṇārthaṃ tasyāpramāṇaṃ sarvanimittāpagataṃ kāyavāṅmanaskarma pravartate supariśodhitamanutpattikadharmakṣāntyāvabhāsitam /
body.translated_text: and through the non-conceptualizing, effortless, signless mode of non-conceptualization—seeing the actualization in the domain of immeasurable wisdom—he applies himself without interruption and without gap in all postures, conduct, abiding, and mental attention. In no state whatsoever is he dissociated from the path. In each moment of his mind, the ten <s>pāramitās</s>, foremost among all factors conducive to awakening, are fulfilled in a distinctive way. But in the other abodes, not so. In the first Joyful abode, through taking aspiration as object; in the second, through the removal of the stain of mental misconduct; in the third, through the increase of aspiration and the attainment of the light of <s>Dharma</s>; in the fourth, through the entry into the path; in the fifth, through the entry into worldly activities; in the sixth, through deep penetration. But in this seventh abode, through the actualization of all <s>Buddha</s>-qualities, the factors of awakening (<s>bodhyaṅgas</s>) are fulfilled—through the completion of the <s>Bodhisattva</s>'s preparatory practice as comprised in this abode, and through the entry into the eighth abode of purified wisdom and higher knowledge. For indeed, this <s>Bodhisattva</s>, immediately after this abode, enters the eighth, purified abode. That abode is exclusively pure. But these seven abodes are mixed. Because they have the pure abode as their preliminary, they are undefiled. Because they have not yet attained it, they should be said to fall on the side of defilement. Therefore, in this abode, all afflictions headed by desire and the rest are abandoned. Yet it should be understood as neither defiled nor free from defilement—because of the non-occurrence [of afflictions] and because of the aspiration for <s>Buddha</s>-knowledge. For one who has become thus, whose superior intention is purified, immeasurable action of body, speech, and mind proceeds. Whatever actions have been censured by the <s>Tathāgata</s>, as before—his worldly sciences and arts that have been accomplished in the fifth abode are here brought to fulfillment. And he becomes acknowledged as a master in the three-thousand-fold great thousand world-system, except for <s>Bodhisattvas</s> established in higher abodes and <s>Tathāgatas</s>. No one equals him in intention and endeavor. And all the <s>dhyānas</s> and other factors conducive to awakening become accessible—becoming accessible through facing the mode of cultivation, not from the standpoint of the supreme mode. That is, they become accessible as in the eighth abode, through facing the mode of cultivation, not from the standpoint of the supreme mode. Thus engaged, he brings forth one hundred thousand groups of ten concentrations, headed by the concentration of well-ascertained domain (<s>suniścitaviṣayasamādhi</s>). And through the attainment of these, he surpasses the domain of <s>Śrāvaka</s> and <s>Pratyekabuddha</s> concentrations. Thus he abides with action of body, speech, and mind that is secluded from all afflictions, difficult to comprehend, and freed from the operation of all conceptual proliferations. Yet he does not abandon the endeavor of seeking further distinction, out of concern for beings and for the purpose of completing awakening. His immeasurable action of body, speech, and mind proceeds—freed from all signs, well-purified, and illuminated by the patience of non-arising (<s>anutpattikadharmakṣānti</s>).

body.text: asminvihāre svabuddhiviṣayatayā sarvaśrāvakapratyekabuddhaviṣayasamatikrāntāstadanyeṣu tu ṣaṭṣu buddhadharmādhyālambanatayā ṣaṣṭhe ca vihāre bodhisattvo nirodhaṃ samāpadyate / asmiṃstu pratikṣaṇaṃ samāpadyate / idañcāsyātyadbhutaṃ karmācintyam / yad bhūtakoṭivihāreṇa ca viharati na ca nirodhaṃ sākṣātkaroti / sa tamevopāyajñānābhinihāramadhipatiṃ kṛtvā sarvasattvāsādhāraṇāṃ bodhisattvacaryāñcarati laukikapratibhāsāñcātanmayīṃ ca yathāsūtrameva / tasya tu piṇḍārthaḥ / puṇyakriyāmārabhya kaḍatrapariṣatparigrahamabhinirvṛttiviśeṣaprārthanā-samārambhaṃ vimokṣatrayavihāratāṃ hīnayānādhimuktopāyavinayanatāṃ kāmaparibhogaṃ kāmaviśeṣaprārthanāṃ tīrthikavyāvartanatāṃ paracittānuvartanatāṃ mahājanakāyānuvartanatāṃ cārabhya śeṣaṃ pūrvavat / tatrāyaṃ viśeṣaḥ / tadyathā tadeva suvarṇaṃ kuśalena karmakāreṇa sarvamaṇiratnamṛṣṭuṃ pratyarpitamatyarthaṃ bhrājate / asaṃhāryañca bhavati tadanyairjāmbūdvīpakairābharaṇaiḥ / evamasya tāni kuśalamūlāni viśuddhatarāṇyasaṃhāryāṇi bhavanti sarvaśrāvakapratyekabuddhakuśalamūlaistadanyaiśca nikṛṣṭataravihārasthairbodhisattvakuśalamūlaiḥ / tadyathā sūryābhā jambūdvīpe yadbhūyasā snehaśca pariśoṣayati / asaṃhāryā ca bhavati sa ca tadanyaprabhābhiḥ / evamasya bodhisattvasya prajñābhā sattvānāṃ sarvakleśaviṣāṇi ca śoṣayati / asaṃhāryā ca bhavati pūrvavat śrāvakādijñānaprabhābhiḥ / vaśavartī ca bhavati devarājaḥ / kuśalaḥ śrāvakapratyekabuddhābhisamayopasaṃhāreṣu / prabhāvaḥ koṭīśatasahasrasaṃkhyānirdeśato veditavyaḥ / ayaṃ sābhogo nirnimitto vihāraḥ upāyaprajñābhinihṛtamārgāntarārambhaviśeṣaniṣpattipraveśataśca tathāgataviṣayasamutthāna-prativedha-nirantaraprayogataśca pratikṣaṇaṃ sarvabodhipakṣyadharmasamudāgamataśca kliṣṭākliṣṭa-vyavasthānataśca prayogikacaryāparipūrisaṃgrahataśca āśayaśuddhikarmapravṛttim adhikṛtya sarvalaukikaśilpakarmādiparipūraṇataśca aprameyaśrāvakapratyekabuddhāsādhāraṇasamādhi-pratilambhataśca pratikṣaṇanirodhasamāpattitaśca sarvasattvāsādhāraṇalokacaryācaraṇataśca kuśalamūlaviśuddhitaśca upapattitaḥ prabhāvataśca samāsa-nirdeśato veditavyaḥ /
body.translated_text: On this stage, through being within the range of one's own understanding, [the <s>Bodhisattva</s>] has transcended the domain of all <s>Śrāvakas</s> and <s>Pratyekabuddhas</s>. On the other [lower] six [stages], the transcendence is through taking <s>Buddha</s>-qualities as their object. And on the sixth stage, the <s>Bodhisattva</s> enters cessation (<s>nirodha</s>) [with effort]. But on this stage, he enters [cessation] at every moment. And this is his extraordinary and inconceivable deed: that he abides in the abode of the ultimate limit of reality (<s>bhūtakoṭi</s>) yet does not directly realize cessation. Making that very projection of knowledge through skillful means his governing [principle], he carries on the <s>Bodhisattva</s> conduct that is uncommon to all beings, and [engages in] worldly appearances that are not [merely] constituted by them, exactly as taught in the <s>sūtras</s>. The summary meaning of this [stage] is as follows. Beginning with meritorious action, encompassing the gathering of assemblies worthy of reverence, the aspiration for and commencement of distinguished attainments, the abiding in the three liberations, the disciplining through skillful means of those inclined to the inferior vehicle, the enjoyment of sensual pleasures, the aspiration for distinguished sensual pleasures, the turning away of non-Buddhist ascetics, the adaptation to others' minds, and the adaptation to the great multitude — the rest is as before. Here, this is the distinction: Just as that very gold, when given to a skilled goldsmith for polishing all jewel-gems, shines exceedingly, and becomes unsurpassable by any other ornaments of <s>Jambudvīpa</s> — so his wholesome roots become more purified and unsurpassable by the wholesome roots of all <s>Śrāvakas</s> and <s>Pratyekabuddhas</s>, and by the wholesome roots of <s>Bodhisattvas</s> established on lower stages. Just as the radiance of the sun in <s>Jambudvīpa</s> for the most part dries up moisture and is unsurpassable by any other radiance — so the radiance of this <s>Bodhisattva</s>'s wisdom dries up all the poisons of afflictions in beings and is unsurpassable, as before, by the radiance of the knowledge of <s>Śrāvakas</s> and others. He becomes a sovereign god-king. He is skilled in the presentations leading to the realization of <s>Śrāvakas</s> and <s>Pratyekabuddhas</s>. His power should be understood as indicated by hundreds of thousands of <s>koṭīs</s>. This is the signless abode with effort (<s>sābhoga nirnimitta vihāra</s>). It should be understood in summary from the standpoint of: entry into the accomplishment of the distinct commencement of an alternative path projected by skillful means and wisdom; uninterrupted application toward the arising and penetration of the <s>Tathāgata</s>'s domain; the accomplishment of all <s>dharmas</s> conducive to awakening at every moment; the determination of defiled and undefiled [states]; the encompassing of the completion of preparatory conduct; activity proceeding from the purity of intention, including the completion of all worldly crafts and arts; the attainment of immeasurable <s>samādhis</s> uncommon to <s>Śrāvakas</s> and <s>Pratyekabuddhas</s>; entering the attainment of cessation at every moment; carrying on worldly conduct uncommon to all beings; purification of wholesome roots; and rebirth and power.

body.text: vistarataḥ pūrvavat / tadyathā dūraṃgamāyāṃ bhūmau / bodhisattva-prāyogikacaryā-paripūrisaṃgṛhītatvāt dūraṃgametyucyate / tenaiva cārthena vihāro veditavyaḥ /
body.translated_text: In detail, as before — namely, as on the <s>Dūraṃgamā</s> (Far-Reaching) stage. Because it encompasses the completion of the <s>Bodhisattva</s>'s preparatory conduct, it is called 'Far-Reaching.' And by that same meaning, this abode should be understood.

body.text: tatra katamo bodhisattvānām anābhogo nirnimitto vihāraḥ / iha bodhisattvena prathame 'nantare vihāre daśākāraṃ sarvadharmaparamārthāvatārajñānaṃ pratilabdhaṃ bhavati / triṣu adhveṣu yathāyogam ādyanutpannatāmajanmatāmalakṣaṇatām ārabhya tadanyahetubhāvāsambhavāvināśatāñcārabhya paramārthato nirabhilāpyasvabhāve vastunyabhilāpābhisaṃskārapratibhāsasya svabhāvasya lakṣaṇena hetubhāvena cāvidyamānasya tasyaiva saṃkleśātmanāpravṛttitāñcānivṛttitāñcārabhya tadajñānamithyābhiniveśahetukāñca tasminvidyamāne vastuni nirabhilāpye ādau madhye paryavasāne sarvakālasaṃkleśasamatāṃ cārabhya tathatā-samyakpraveśanirvikalpasamatayā ca tatsaṃkleśāpanayanamārabhya / ityasya jñānasya daśākārasyādhimātratvātparipūrṇatvādimamaṣṭamaṃ pariśuddhaṃ vihāramavatarati /
body.translated_text: There, what is the <s>Bodhisattvas</s>' effortless signless abode (<s>anābhoga nirnimitta vihāra</s>)? Here, the <s>Bodhisattva</s>, on the first signless stage immediately [following], has obtained the tenfold knowledge of entry into the ultimate reality of all <s>dharmas</s>. [This tenfold knowledge operates] in the three periods of time as appropriate: beginning with primordial non-arising, unborn-ness, and characteristiclessness; beginning with the impossibility of the causal existence of anything other [than the inexpressible]; and beginning with, in an entity whose own-nature is ultimately inexpressible (<s>nirabhilāpyasvabhāva</s>), the fact that the own-nature of the appearance of verbal fabrication (<s>abhilāpābhisaṃskārapratibhāsa</s>) does not exist by way of its characteristic or causal status — and that very [appearance], though non-existent, neither operates as the nature of defilement nor ceases [to appear]; beginning with the equality of defilement at all times — in the beginning, middle, and end — with respect to that [inexpressible] entity, on account of the ignorance and false clinging that cause it; and beginning with the removal of that defilement through the non-conceptual equality of correct entry into suchness (<s>tathatā</s>). Through the intensity and fullness of this tenfold knowledge, he descends into this eighth, purified abode.

body.text: ihasthaścānutpattikeṣu dharmeṣu paramāṃ bodhisattvakṣāntiṃ suviśuddhāṃ labhate / sā punaḥ katamā / catasṛbhiḥ paryeṣaṇābhirayaṃ bodhisattvaḥ sarvadhamān paryeṣya yadā caturbhireva yathābhūtaparijñānaiḥ parijānāti / tadā sarvamithyāvikalpābhiniveśeṣvapanīteṣu sarvadharmāṇāṃ dṛṣṭe ca dharme sarvasaṃlkeśānutpattyanukūlatāṃ paśyati / samparāye ca sarveṇa sarvaṃ niravaśeṣato 'nutpatiṃ paśyati teṣāmeva pūrvamithyāvikalpābhiniveśahetusamutpannānāṃ dharmāṇām / tāḥ punaḥ catasraḥ paryeṣaṇā yathāpūrvaṃ nirdiṣṭāstattvārthapaṭale / catvāri ca yathābhūtaparijñānāni tānyadhimukticaryāvihāramupādāya yāvatsābhoganirnirmittādvihārān na suviśuddhāni bhavanti / asmiṃstu vihāre pariśuddhāni bhavanti / tasmāt sa bodhisattvaḥ anutpattikeṣu dharmeṣu kṣānti-pratilabdha ityucyate / sa tasyāḥ kṣānterlābhād gambhīraṃ bodhisattvavihāramanuprāpto bhavati / tasya ye pūrvake nirnimitte vihāre catvāro 'pakṣālāste prahīṇā bhavanti / yaḥ sābhogābhisaṃskāraḥ sa prahīṇo bhavati / uttari ca viśuddhavihāre autsukyaṃ prahīṇaṃ bhavati / sarvākārasattvārthakriyāśaktāvautsukyaṃ
body.translated_text: And established here, he obtains the supreme, well-purified <s>Bodhisattva</s> patience regarding unborn <s>dharmas</s> (<s>anutpattikadharma-kṣānti</s>). What then is that [patience]? When this <s>Bodhisattva</s>, having investigated all <s>dharmas</s> through the four investigations and having comprehended them through the four true comprehensions as they really are — then, when all false conceptual clingings have been removed, he sees, with respect to all <s>dharmas</s>, their conformity with the non-arising of all defilement in the present life, and in the future he sees the complete, total, and unrestricted non-arising of those very <s>dharmas</s> that had previously arisen from the causes of false conceptual clinging. Those four investigations are as previously described in the Chapter on the True Nature of Reality (<s>Tattvārthapaṭala</s>). And the four true comprehensions — those, from the aspiration-conduct stage up to the signless stage with effort, are not well-purified. But on this stage, they become purified. Therefore, that <s>Bodhisattva</s> is called 'one who has obtained patience regarding unborn <s>dharmas</s>.' Through the attainment of that patience, he has reached a profound <s>Bodhisattva</s> abode. The four faults (<s>apakṣāla</s>) that existed on his former signless stages are abandoned: the deliberate fabrication (<s>sābhogābhisaṃskāra</s>) is abandoned; furthermore, on the higher purified stage, eagerness is abandoned; eagerness regarding the ability to act for the welfare of all beings in all aspects

body.text: prahīṇaṃ bhavati / sūkṣmasaṃjñā-samudācāraśca prahīṇo bhavati / tasmāt sa vihāraḥ suviśuddha ityucyate /
body.translated_text: is abandoned; and the occurrence of subtle conceptualization is abandoned. Therefore that abode is called 'supremely purified.'

body.text: tasya ca tasmin gambhīre vihāre 'bhiratasya tasmin dharmamukhasrotasi tathāgata-saṃcodanā-samādāpanā-abhinirhāramukha-jñānābhijñā-karmopasaṃhāro 'prameyaḥ / tathā saṃcoditasya cāpramāṇakāyavibhaktijñānābhinirhāro daśavaśitā-prāptiśca yathāsūtrameva vistareṇa veditavyāḥ / vaśitāprāptaḥ sa tāvadākāṃkṣati tāvattiṣṭhati / yena vā dhyānavimokṣādicittavihāreṇākāṃkṣati tena viharati / saṃkalpamātreṇaivāsya sarvabhojanādi-pariṣkārasampad bhavati / sarvaśilpakarmasthāneṣu cāsya yathākāmapracāratā bhavati / sarvopapattisaṃvartanīyeṣu ca karmasu sarvopapattyāyataneṣu cāsya kāmakāmopapattitā bhavati / yathepsitañca sarvarddhikāryaṃ karoti / sarvapraṇidhānāni cāsya yathākāmaṃ samṛdhyanti / yad yadeva vastu yathādhimucyate tattathaiva bhavati nānyathā / yañca jñeyaṃ jñātukāmo bhavati tadapi jānīte yathāvat / nāmakāyapadakāyavyañjanakāyānāñca nikāmalābhī bhavati / sarvadharmasamyakvyavasthānakuśalaḥ / evaṃ vaśitāprāptasya bodhisattvasyātaḥ pareṇa vaśitāprāptakṛto 'nuśaṃso vistareṇa yathāsūtrameva veditavyaḥ / audārikañca buddhadarśanaṃ vihāya satatasamitamavirahito bhavati buddhadarśanena / śeṣakuśalamūlaviśuddhiryathāsūtraṃ veditavyā / maharghasuvarṇadṛṣṭāntena [ābhādṛṣṭāntena] ca / upapattiḥ prabhāvaviśeṣaścāpyasya bodhisattvasyāsminvihāre yathāsūtrameva veditavyaḥ / ayamanābhogo nirnimitto vihāraḥ / paramārthavatārajñānaniṣpattipraveśataśca anutpattikadharmakṣāntilābhataśca sarvāpakṣālāpagata-gambhīra-bodhisattvavihāraprāptitaśca dharmamukhasrotasi buddhairaprameyābhinirhāramukhajñānābhijñākarmopasaṃhārataśca apramāṇakāyavibhaktijñānapraveśataśca vaśitāprāptitaśca vaśitānuśaṃsapratyanubhavanataśca kuśalamūlaviśuddhita upapattiḥ prabhāvataśca samāsanirdeśato veditavyaḥ / vistareṇa nirdeśato yathāsūtraṃ tadyathā 'calāyāṃ bhūmau / pūrvakābhisaṃskārāpagamādanābhogāniścalavāhimārgasamārūḍhaṃ
body.translated_text: And for him, delighting in that profound abode, abiding in that stream of <s>Dharma</s>-gates, the <s>Tathāgatas</s>' urging, encouragement, and presentation of the gateway of knowledge, superknowledge (<s>abhijñā</s>), and action is immeasurable. And for him, thus urged, the projection of knowledge for the manifestation of immeasurable bodies and the attainment of the ten masteries (<s>daśavaśitā</s>) should be understood in detail exactly as in the <s>sūtras</s>. Having attained mastery, he remains as long as he wishes. He abides in whatever mental state of <s>dhyāna</s>, liberation, and the rest he wishes. By mere intention alone, he obtains the complete provision of all food and other requisites. And in all fields of craft and art, he moves at will. And regarding all <s>karmas</s> that lead to rebirth and in all stations of rebirth, he is reborn wherever he wishes, at will. He performs whatever supernatural deed he desires. All his aspirations succeed according to his wish. Whatever object he resolves upon in whatever way, that very thing becomes just so and not otherwise. Whatever knowable thing he wishes to know, he knows it as it truly is. He obtains word-groups (<s>nāmakāya</s>), sentence-groups (<s>padakāya</s>), and syllable-groups (<s>vyañjanakāya</s>) at will. He is skilled in the correct establishment of all <s>dharmas</s>. Thus, for the <s>Bodhisattva</s> who has attained mastery, the benefits arising from that mastery should be understood in detail exactly as in the <s>sūtras</s>. And having left behind the coarse vision of <s>Buddhas</s>, he becomes constantly and continuously uninterrupted in the vision of <s>Buddhas</s>. The remaining purification of wholesome roots should be understood as in the <s>sūtras</s>, as well as by the simile of the finest gold [and] by the simile of radiance. And the rebirth and special power of this <s>Bodhisattva</s> on this stage should be understood exactly as in the <s>sūtras</s>. This is the effortless signless abode (<s>anābhoga nirnimitta vihāra</s>). It should be understood in summary from the standpoint of: entry into the accomplishment of the knowledge of ultimate entry; the attainment of patience regarding unborn <s>dharmas</s>; the reaching of the profound <s>Bodhisattva</s> abode from which all faults have departed; by the <s>Buddhas</s>' immeasurable presentation of gateways of knowledge, superknowledge, and action within the stream of <s>Dharma</s>-gates; entry into the knowledge of immeasurable body-manifestation; the attainment of mastery; the experience of the benefits of mastery; purification of wholesome roots; and rebirth and power. In detail, it should be understood as in the <s>sūtras</s> — namely, as on the <s>Acalā</s> (Immovable) stage. Because the prior fabrications have departed and the mind on that stage operates having mounted the effortless, non-wavering path-vehicle,

body.text: taccittaṃ tasyāṃ bhūmau pravartate / tasmāt sā bhūmiracaletyucyate / tenaiva cārthenāyaṃ vihāro draṣṭavyaḥ /
body.translated_text: that stage is called <s>Acalā</s> (Immovable). And by that very meaning, this abode should be viewed.

body.text: tatra katamo bodhisattvānāṃ pratisaṃvidvihāraḥ / iha bodhisattvastenāpi vihāreṇa gambhīreṇāsaṃtuṣṭa uttarijñānaviśeṣatāmanugacchan yaiśca dharmajñānābhisaṃskāraiḥ pareṣāṃ dharmaḥ sarvākāro bodhisattvena deśayitavyo yacca dharmākhyānakṛtyaṃ tatsarvaṃ yathābhūtaṃ prajānāti tatredaṃ dharmasamākhyānakṛtyam / gahanopavicāreṣu ye ca saṃkliśyante viśudhyante ca / yena ca saṃkliśyante yena ca viśudhyante / yacca saṃkleśavyavadānam / yā ca tasyānaikāntikatā / yā ca tasyaikāntikatā / yā ca tasyaikāntikatā 'naikāntikatā / tasya yathābhūtajñānam / evañca dharma-deśanākuśalasya deśanākṛtyakuśalasya ca yat sarvākāramahādharma-bhāṇakatvam aprameyadhāraṇīprāptasya sarvasvarāṅgavibhaktikuśalasyākṣayapratibhānasya / yādṛśyā dharmadhāraṇodgrahaṇaśaktyā samanvāgatasya / yayā bodhisattvapratisaṃvidabhinihṛtayā vācā / yadṛśe dharmāsane niṣaṇṇasya / yatra yeṣu ca dharma deśayataḥ yāvadbhirmukhaiḥ yayā sattva-vijñāpana santoṣaṇa-kṛtyasaṃniyojana-śaktyā samanvāgatasya / tat sarvaṃ yathāsūtrameva vistaranirdeśato veditavyam / kuśalamūlaviśuddhyupapattiprabhāvaviśeṣo 'pi yathāsūtrameva veditavyaḥ / ayaṃ bodhisattvānāṃ pratisaṃvidvihāraḥ śāntavimokṣasantuṣṭipraveśataśca dharmasamākhyānābhisaṃskārajñānataśca tatkṛtyajñānataśca acintyamahādharmabhāṇakatvapratilambhataścakaśalamūlaviśuddhita upapattitaḥ prabhāvataśca samāsanirdeśato veditavyaḥ / vistaranirdeśataḥ punaḥ yathāsūtrameva / tadyathā sādhumatyāṃ bhūmau / sarvasattvānāṃ hitasukhāśayapariśuddhyā bodhisattvapratisaṃvinmatyā dharmasamākhyānādhikāratvāt sā bhūmiḥ sādhumatītyucyate / tenaiva cārthenāyamapi vihāro draṣṭavyaḥ /
body.translated_text: There, what is the <s>Bodhisattvas</s>' Analytical Knowledge abode (<s>pratisaṃvidvihāra</s>)? Here, the <s>Bodhisattva</s>, not satisfied even with that profound abode, pursuing ever higher distinction of knowledge, truly understands all that is to be understood regarding the <s>Dharma</s>-teaching activities — by what verbal fabrications of <s>Dharma</s>-knowledge the <s>Bodhisattva</s> should teach the <s>Dharma</s> in all its aspects to others, and what the function of <s>Dharma</s>-proclamation is. Here, this is the function of <s>Dharma</s>-proclamation: those who are defiled and those who are purified in the thickets of investigation; and by what they are defiled, and by what they are purified; and what defilement and purification are; and its non-finality; and its finality; and its combined finality and non-finality; and the true knowledge thereof. And thus, for one who is skilled in <s>Dharma</s>-teaching and skilled in the function of teaching, [there is] the status of being a great <s>Dharma</s>-preacher in all aspects, having obtained immeasurable <s>dhāraṇīs</s>, skilled in the articulation of all tones and expressions, of inexhaustible eloquence; endowed with such power of <s>Dharma</s>-retention and mastery as he possesses; and with the speech projected by the <s>Bodhisattva</s>'s analytical knowledges; and seated on such a <s>Dharma</s>-seat; and in such a place and to such [beings] he teaches the <s>Dharma</s>, through so many approaches, and endowed with such power of informing, satisfying, and yoking beings [to the task] — all of that should be understood in detail exactly as in the <s>sūtras</s>. The special distinction of purification of wholesome roots, rebirth, and power should also be understood exactly as in the <s>sūtras</s>. This is the <s>Bodhisattvas</s>' Analytical Knowledge abode. It should be understood in summary from the standpoint of: entry into contentment with the peaceful liberation; knowledge of the verbal fabrications for <s>Dharma</s>-proclamation; knowledge of its function; the attainment of inconceivable great <s>Dharma</s>-preacher status; purification of wholesome roots; rebirth; and power. In detail, it should be understood exactly as in the <s>sūtras</s> — namely, as on the <s>Sādhumatī</s> (Good Intelligence) stage. Because of the purification of the <s>Bodhisattva</s>'s intention of benefit and happiness toward all beings, and because of the authority of <s>Dharma</s>-proclamation through the <s>Bodhisattva</s>'s analytical intelligence, that stage is called <s>Sādhumatī</s>. And by that very meaning, this abode too should be viewed.

body.text: tatra katamo bodhisattvānāṃ paramo vihāraḥ / iha bodhisattvasya pratisaṃvid-vihāre sarvākārapariśuddhe dharmarājatvārhasya dharmābhiṣekasamāsannasya vimalādisamādhi-aprameyapratilambha-tatkṛtyakaraṇataḥ sarvajñajñānaviśeṣābhiṣekapaścimasādhisammukhībhāvācca
body.translated_text: There, what is the <s>Bodhisattvas</s>' supreme abode (<s>paramo vihāra</s>)? Here, when the <s>Bodhisattva</s>'s Analytical Knowledge abode is completely purified in all aspects, [and he is] worthy of <s>Dharma</s>-kingship, approaching the <s>Dharma</s>-consecration — from the attainment of immeasurable <s>samādhis</s> beginning with <s>Vimalā</s> and the performance of their functions, and from the coming face-to-face with the final <s>samādhi</s> of the consecration by omniscient knowledge

body.text: sarvabuddhebhyasyadanurūpāsanakāyaparivārapratilābhinaḥ svaraśmigamanapratyāgamanaiḥ sarvākārasarvajñajñānābhiṣekapratilambhataśca abhiṣiktasya ca sarvavineya-samudānayana-tadvimokṣopāya-buddhakṛtyajñānataśca aprameya-vimokṣa-dhāraṇī abhijñā pratilambhataśca tadādhipateya mahāsmṛtijñā nābhinirhāranirvacanavyavasthānataśca mahābhijñābhinirhārataśca kuśalamūlaviśuddhi-upapattiprabhāvaviśeṣataśca samāsanirdeśataḥ paramo vihāro veditavyaḥ / vistaranirdeśataḥ punaryathāsūtrameva tadyathā dharmameghāyāṃ bodhisattvabhūmau / paripūrṇabodhisattvamārgaḥ suparipūrṇa-bodhisambhāraśca sa bodhisattvaḥ tathāgatā nāmantikāt dharmamedhabhūmyāmatyudārāṃ duḥsahāḥ tadanyaiḥ sarvasattvaiḥ saddharmaṃvṛṣṭi sampratīcchati / mahāmedhabhūtaśca svayamanabhisambuddhabodhi-abhisambuddhabodhiścāprameyānāṃ sattvānāṃ saddharma-vṛṣṭayā nirapamayā kleśarajāṃsi praśamayati / vicitrāṇi ca kuśalamulaśasyāni virohayati vivardhayatī pācayatī tasyāṃ bhūmāvavasthitaḥ / tasmāt sā bhūmirdharmameghetyucyate / tenaiva cārthena paramo vihāro draṣṭavyaḥ /
body.translated_text: from all <s>Buddhas</s>, through obtaining a retinue with a body and seat befitting [him], through the sending forth and return of rays of light, through obtaining the consecration of omniscient knowledge in all its aspects, and—being thus consecrated—through the knowledge of <s>Buddha</s>-deeds for the guidance and liberation of all those to be trained, through obtaining immeasurable liberations, <s>dhāraṇīs</s>, and superknowledges (<s>abhijñā</s>), and through the authoritative establishment and explanation of the great mindfulness-knowledge produced under their governance, and through the production of great superknowledges, and through the distinction in the purification of wholesome roots, [type of] rebirth, and power—through the summary teaching, the supreme abode (<s>paramo vihāra</s>) should be understood. For the detailed teaching, it is just as in the <s>sūtra</s>—namely, as in the <s>Dharmameghā</s> (Cloud of <s>Dharma</s>) <s>Bodhisattva</s>-stage. That <s>Bodhisattva</s>, having completed the <s>Bodhisattva</s> path and having fully perfected the accumulations for awakening, from the <s>Tathāgatas</s>' proximity, on the <s>Dharmameghā</s> stage, receives the rain of the true <s>Dharma</s> that is supremely exalted and unbearable by all other beings. And being himself a great cloud, whether with awakening not yet realized or with awakening already realized, he pacifies the dust of afflictions of immeasurable beings through an incomparable rain of the true <s>Dharma</s>. And he causes the diverse crops of wholesome roots to sprout, grow, and ripen while established on that stage. Therefore that stage is called <s>Dharmameghā</s> (Cloud of <s>Dharma</s>). And by that very meaning, the supreme abode should be understood.

body.text: na ca yānyuttarottareṣu vihāreṣvaṅgāni nirniṣṭāni tāni pūrvakeṣu vihāreṣu sarveṇa sarvaṃ na saṃvidyante / api tu mṛdutvān na saṃkhyāṃ gacchanti / teṣāmeva ca madhyādhimātratvāt [ta]danyottarabhūmipratilābha-niṣpattivyavasthānaṃ veditavyam / ekaikaścātra vihāro 'nekairmahākalpakoṭīśatasahasraistato vā prabhūtataraiḥ pratilabhyate niṣpadyate ca / te tu sarve vihārāstribhirmahākalpāsaṃkhyeyaiḥ samudāgacchanti mahākalpāsaṃkhyeyenādhimukticaryā-vihāraṃ samatikramya pramuditavihāro labhyate / yacca vyāyacchamāno dhrauvyeṇa nāvyāyacchamānaḥ / dvitīyena mahākalpāsaṃkhyeyena pramuditavihāraṃ yāvatsābhogaṃ nirnimittaṃ vihāramatikramyānābhogaṃ nirnimittaṃ pratilabhate / tacca niya meva / tathā hi sa śuddhāśayo bodhisattvo niyataṃ vyāyacchate / tṛtīyena mahākalpāsaṃkhyeyenānābhogañca nirnimittaṃ pratisaṃvidvihārañca samatikramya paramaṃ bodhisattvavihāraṃ pratilabhate /
body.translated_text: Nor is it the case that the factors accomplished in the higher abodes are entirely absent in the earlier abodes. Rather, being mild, they do not come into reckoning. And it should be understood that the establishment and attainment of each successively higher stage occurs through the middling and intense [development] of those very [factors]. Each abode here is attained and accomplished through many hundreds of thousands of <s>koṭis</s> of great <s>kalpas</s>, or even more. All those abodes are completed through three great incalculable <s>kalpas</s> (<s>mahākalpāsaṃkhyeya</s>). By [the first] incalculable great <s>kalpa</s>, having transcended the aspiration-conduct abode (<s>adhimukticaryāvihāra</s>), the Joyful abode (<s>pramuditavihāra</s>) is attained—and that only for one who exerts himself steadily, not for one who does not exert. By the second incalculable great <s>kalpa</s>, having transcended the Joyful abode up through the signless abode with effort (<s>sābhoga nirnimitta vihāra</s>), he attains the signless [abode] without effort (<s>anābhoga nirnimitta</s>). And that is certain, for indeed the <s>Bodhisattva</s> of pure intention certainly exerts himself. By the third incalculable great <s>kalpa</s>, having transcended both the effortless signless [abode] and the analytical-knowledge abode (<s>pratisaṃvidvihāra</s>), he attains the supreme <s>Bodhisattva</s> abode.

body.text: tatra dau kalpāsaṃkhyeyau veditavyau / yo 'pi mahākalpaḥ so 'pi rātrindivasamāsārdhamāsagaṇanāyogena kālāprameyatvādasaṃkhyeya ityucyate / yāpi
body.translated_text: There, the two incalculable <s>kalpas</s> should be understood [as follows]. That which is a great <s>kalpa</s> is also called 'incalculable' (<s>asaṃkhyeya</s>) because the time is immeasurable by the calculation of nights, days, half-months, and months. And that

body.text: teṣāmeva mahākalpānāṃ gaṇanāyogena sarvagaṇanā samatikrāntā saṃkhyā so 'pyasaṃkhyeyaḥ / pūrvakeṇa kalpāsaṃkhyeyena bodhiranalpaiḥ kalpāsaṃkhyeyairadhigamyate / paścimakena punaḥ kalpāsaṃkhyeyena tribhirevanadhikaiḥ / yastvadhimātrādhimātreṇa vīryārambheṇa prayujyate tataḥ kaścidantarakalpān prabhūtān vyāvartayati kaścit yāvanmahākalpān / na tvasaṃkhyeyavyāvṛttiḥ kasyacidastīti veditavyam /
body.translated_text: number of those very great <s>kalpas</s> that transcends all calculation by the method of enumeration—that too is incalculable. By the earlier incalculable <s>kalpa</s>, awakening is attained through not a few incalculable <s>kalpas</s>. But by the later incalculable <s>kalpa</s>, through exactly three and no more. However, one who applies himself with supremely intense vigor can thereby remove many intermediate <s>kalpas</s>, or even up to great <s>kalpas</s>. But the removal of an [entire] incalculable [<s>kalpa</s>] does not occur for anyone—this should be understood.

body.text: ebhiśca dvādaśabhirbodhisattvavihāraistribhirasaṃkhyeyaiḥ kleśāvaraṇapakṣyañca dauṣṭhulyaṃ prahīyate jñeyāvaraṇa-pakṣyañca / tatra triṣu vihāreṣu kleśāvaraṇapakṣyadauṣṭhulyasya prahāṇaṃ veditavyam / pramudite [vihāre] āpāyikakleśapakṣyasya sarveṇa sarvaṃ samudācāratastvadhimātramamyasya sarvakleśapakṣyasya anābhoge nirnimitte vihāre 'nutpattikadharmakṣānti-viśuddhivibandhakleśa pakṣyasya sarveṇa sarvaṃ dauṣṭhulyasya prahāṇaṃ veditavyam / samudācāratastu sarvakleśānām / parame punarvihāre sarvakleśa[sa]vāsanānuśayāvaraṇaprahāṇaṃ veditavyam / tacca tathāgataṃ vihāramanupraviśataḥ jñeyāvaraṇapakṣyamapi dauṣṭhulyaṃ trividhaṃ veditavyam / tvaggataṃphalgugataṃ sāragatañca / tatra tvaggatasya pramuditavihāre prahāṇaṃ bhavati / phalgugatasyānābhoge nirnimitte sāragatasya tathāgate vihāre prahāṇaṃ bhavati / sarvāvaraṇaviśuddhijñānatā ca teṣu triṣu vihāreṣu tasya kleśa-jñeyāvaraṇaprahāṇasya tadanye vihārā yathānukramaṃ saṃbhārabhūtā bhavanti /
body.translated_text: Through these twelve <s>Bodhisattva</s> abodes and three incalculable [<s>kalpas</s>], both the dysfunction (<s>dauṣṭhulya</s>) belonging to the side of affliction-obscuration (<s>kleśāvaraṇa</s>) and that belonging to the side of knowledge-obscuration (<s>jñeyāvaraṇa</s>) are abandoned. There, the abandonment of dysfunction belonging to the side of affliction-obscuration should be understood in three abodes. In the Joyful abode (<s>pramuditavihāra</s>), [the abandonment] of [dysfunction] belonging to the side of afflictions leading to the lower realms entirely and completely, and that of the intense [dysfunction] belonging to the side of all afflictions in terms of active occurrence. In the effortless signless abode (<s>anābhoga nirnimitta vihāra</s>), the abandonment of dysfunction belonging to the side of afflictions that obstruct the purification of <s>anutpattikadharmakṣānti</s> (patient acceptance of the non-arising of <s>dharmas</s>)—entirely and completely—should be understood, though in terms of active occurrence, [the abandonment is] of all afflictions. In the supreme abode, the abandonment of all afflictions together with their latent tendencies (<s>vāsanā</s>), residual impressions (<s>anuśaya</s>), and obscurations should be understood. And that [occurs] upon entering the <s>Tathāgata</s>-abode. The dysfunction belonging to the side of knowledge-obscuration should also be understood as threefold: superficial (<s>tvakgata</s>), intermediate (<s>phalgugata</s>), and deep/essential (<s>sāragata</s>). There, the abandonment of the superficial occurs in the Joyful abode. The abandonment of the intermediate occurs in the effortless signless [abode]. The abandonment of the deep/essential occurs in the <s>Tathāgata</s>-abode. And the knowledge that is the purification from all obscurations [occurs] in those three abodes; the other abodes [besides those three] serve progressively as the accumulation-basis for that abandonment of affliction-obscuration and knowledge-obscuration.

body.text: eṣu trayodaśasu vihāreṣu samāsata ekādaśavidhā viśuddhirveditavyā / prathame gotraviśuddhiḥ / dvitīye śraddhāvimuktiviśuddhiḥ / tṛtīye 'dhyāśayaviśuddhiḥ / caturthe śīlaviśuddhiḥ / pañcame cittaviśuddhiḥ / ṣaṣṭhe saptame 'ṣṭame ca samyak jñānasamārambhaviśuddhiḥ / navame prāyogikacaryā-paripūriviśuddhiḥ / daśame tattvajñānābhinirhāraviśuddhiḥ ekādaśe tadarthasamyak parasamākhyānāya pratirsavidviśuddhiḥ / dvādaśe sarvākārasarvajñeyānupraveśajñānaviśuddhiḥ / trayodaśe tathāgate vihāre savāsana-sarvakleśa-jñeyāvaraṇaviśuddhiḥ /
body.translated_text: In these thirteen abodes, in summary, an elevenfold purification should be understood. In the first, purification of lineage (<s>gotraviśuddhi</s>). In the second, purification of faith-liberation (<s>śraddhāvimuktiviśuddhi</s>). In the third, purification of superior intention (<s>adhyāśayaviśuddhi</s>). In the fourth, purification of morality (<s>śīlaviśuddhi</s>). In the fifth, purification of mind (<s>cittaviśuddhi</s>). In the sixth, seventh, and eighth, purification of the undertaking of right knowledge (<s>samyakjñānasamārambhaviśuddhi</s>). In the ninth, purification of the fulfillment of practical conduct (<s>prāyogikacaryāparipūriviśuddhi</s>). In the tenth, purification of the production of true knowledge (<s>tattvajñānābhinirhāraviśuddhi</s>). In the eleventh, purification of analytical knowledge (<s>pratisaṃvid</s>) for the correct and complete exposition of its meaning to others. In the twelfth, purification of the knowledge that penetrates all knowables in all their aspects (<s>sarvākārasarvajñeyānupraveśajñānaviśuddhi</s>). In the thirteenth, the <s>Tathāgata</s>-abode, purification from all affliction-obscuration and knowledge-obscuration together with their residual impressions (<s>savāsanasarvakleśajñeyāvaraṇaviśuddhi</s>).

body.text: aṣṭābhiśca pūrvanirdiṣṭairmahāyānasaṃgrāhakairdharmaireṣāṃ trayodaśānāṃ vihārāṇāṃ saṃgraho veditavyaḥ / prathamadvitīyayorvihārayoḥ śraddhājātasyādhimuktigatasya
body.translated_text: Through the eight previously described <s>dharmas</s> that comprise the <s>Mahāyāna</s>, the subsumption of these thirteen abodes should be understood. In the first and second abodes, for one in whom faith has arisen and who has entered the stage of aspiration,

body.text: bodhisattvapiṭaka-śravaṇacintanā / tṛtīye vihāre 'dhyāśayopagamanaṃ bhāvanākārapratilābhapūrvakam / tadanyeṣu sarvavihāreṣu yāvat sābhoganirnimittādbhāvanāvāhulyam / tataścordhvaṃ triṣu bodhisattvavihāreṣu pariśuddhacaryā saṃgṛhīteṣu bhāvanāphalaniṣpattiḥ / tathāgate vihāre 'tyanta nairyāṇikatā veditavyā /
body.translated_text: there is the hearing and reflection on the <s>Bodhisattva</s>-piṭaka. In the third abode, the entry into superior intention preceded by the attainment of the mode of cultivation. In all the other abodes up through the signless [abode] with effort, there is the abundance of cultivation. Then, in the three higher <s>Bodhisattva</s> abodes comprised within purified conduct, there is the accomplishment of the fruit of cultivation. In the <s>Tathāgata</s>-abode, ultimate deliverance (<s>nairyāṇikatā</s>) should be understood.

body.text: śrāvakavihāre sādharmyeṇa caiṣāṃ dvādaśānāṃ bodhisattvavihārāṇāmanukramo veditavyaḥ / yathā śrāvakasya svagotravihārastathā 'sya prathamo veditavyaḥ / yathā tasya [samyakatva]nyāmāvakrāntiprayogavihāraḥ evamasya dvitīyaḥ / yathā tasya nyāmāvakrāntivihāraḥ tathāsya tṛtīyo vihāraḥ / yathā tasyāvetyaprasādalābhinaḥ āryakāntādhiśīlavihāra uttari āsravakṣayāya tathāsya caturtho vihāraḥ / yathā tasyādhiśīlaṃ niśrityādhicittaśikṣānirhāravihāraḥ tathāsya pañcamo vihāraḥ / yathā tasya yathā pratilabdhasatyajñānādhipraśikṣāvihāraḥ tathāsya ṣaṣṭha saptamāṣṭamā vihārā veditavyā / yathā tasya suvicārita jñeyasyānimittasamādhiprayogavihāraḥ tathāsyanavamo vihāraḥ / yathā tasya pariniṣpanno nirnimitto vihāraḥ tathāsya daśamo vihāraḥ / yathā tasya vyutthitasya vimuktyāyatanavihāraḥ tathāsyaikādaśo vihāraḥ / yathā tasya sarvākāro 'rhatvavihāraḥ tathāsya dvādaśo vihāro veditavyaḥ /
body.translated_text: The sequence of these twelve <s>Bodhisattva</s> abodes should be understood by analogy with the <s>Śrāvaka</s> abode. Just as the <s>Śrāvaka</s> has his own lineage-abode, so should the first [<s>Bodhisattva</s> abode] be understood. Just as the <s>Śrāvaka</s> has the abode of the preparatory practice for entering the assured course (<s>samyaktvanyāmāvakrāntiprayogavihāra</s>), so should the second be understood. Just as the <s>Śrāvaka</s> has the abode of entry into the assured course (<s>nyāmāvakrāntivihāra</s>), so should the third abode be understood. Just as the <s>Śrāvaka</s>, having obtained irreversible confidence, has the abode of higher morality beloved of the noble ones (<s>āryakānta adhiśīlavihāra</s>) for the further destruction of defilements, so should the fourth abode be understood. Just as the <s>Śrāvaka</s>, relying on higher morality, has the abode of accomplishing the training in higher mind (<s>adhicittaśikṣā</s>), so should the fifth abode be understood. Just as the <s>Śrāvaka</s> has the abode of training in accordance with the knowledge of the truths as attained, so should the sixth, seventh, and eighth abodes be understood. Just as the <s>Śrāvaka</s>, having well investigated the knowable, has the abode of the preparatory practice of signless concentration (<s>ānimittasamādhiprayogavihāra</s>), so should the ninth abode be understood. Just as the <s>Śrāvaka</s> has the fully accomplished signless abode (<s>pariniṣpanna nirnimitta vihāra</s>), so should the tenth abode be understood. Just as the <s>Śrāvaka</s>, having emerged [from concentration], has the abode of the bases of liberation (<s>vimuktyāyatanavihāra</s>), so should the eleventh abode be understood. Just as the <s>Śrāvaka</s> has the abode of <s>Arhatship</s> in all its aspects, so should the twelfth abode be understood.

body.text: iti bodhisattvabhūmāvādhārānudharme yogasthāne caturthaṃ vihārapaṭalam /
body.translated_text: Thus, in the <s>Bodhisattvabhūmi</s>, in the <s>Ādhāra</s> (Foundation) section of the <s>Dharma</s> conforming to the foundation, in the Yoga Division, [this is] the fourth chapter, the <s>Vihāra-paṭala</s> (Chapter on the Abodes).

body.text: samāptañca yogasthānaṃ dvitīyam /
body.translated_text: And the second Yoga Division is completed.

children.translated_text: <s>Ādhāraniṣṭhā Yogasthāna</s> (Yoga Division on the Establishment of the Foundation)

body.text: samāsato bodhisattvānāṃ pañcavidhā upapattiḥ sarvatraṃ sarvavihāreṣu ca sarveṣāñca bodhisattvānāmanavadyā parvasattvahitasukhāya / īti-saṃśamanī tatsabhāgānuvartanī mahattvopapattirādhipatyopapattiścaramā copapattiḥ /
body.translated_text: In summary, the rebirth of <s>Bodhisattvas</s> is fivefold, throughout all abodes and for all <s>Bodhisattvas</s>, blameless and for the benefit and happiness of all beings: calamity-quelling rebirth (<s>ītisaṃśamanī</s>), similar-class-following rebirth (<s>tatsabhāgānuvartinī</s>), greatness-rebirth (<s>mahattvopapattiḥ</s>), sovereignty-rebirth (<s>ādhipatyopapattiḥ</s>), and final rebirth (<s>caramā upapattiḥ</s>).

body.text: tatreti-saṃśamanī upapattiḥ katamā / iha bodhisattvo durbhikṣeṣu kṛcchreṣu mahākāntāreṣu kāleṣu praṇidhāya sattvānāmalpakṛcchreṇa yātrānimittaṃ mahāmatsyādiyoniṣūpapadyate / vipuleṣvātmabhāveṣu yatropapannaḥ kṛtsnaṃ jagatsvamāṃsena santarpayati / vyādhibahuleṣu ca sattveṣu praṇidhāya siddhavidyādhara-mahāvaidyātmabhāvaṃ parigṛhṇāti teṣāṃ vyādhīnāṃ praśamāya / bhṛśa-paracakropadraveṣu ca sattveṣu balavān bhūmipatirbhavati dharmeṇa śamenopāyakauśalyena paracakropadravapraśamanārthaṃ paraspara-viruddheṣu ca sattveṣvādeyavacano bhavati sandhikriyāyai vairāśayaprahāṇāya ca / daṇḍabandhanacitrapīḍāpravṛtteṣu ca prajānāṃ rājasu teṣāmeva sattvopadravāṇāṃ prahāṇāya tadrūpeṣu rājakuleṣūpapadyate / rājā ca dhārmiko bhavati sattvānukampaḥ / ye ca sattvā mithyādṛṣṭayaśca pāpakāriṇaśca kasmiṃściddevāyatane 'dhimuktāḥ teṣāmanukampayā mithyādṛṣṭiduściritaprahāṇāya tasmindevāyatane upapadyate / praṇidhānavaśitābalābhyāñca iyamupapattiranukampā-pūrvikā aprameyā veditavyā vistaranirdeśatastāsu tāsu vicitrāsu yoniṣu tiryagyonyupapanneṣu sattveṣu samāsa-nirdeśastvayamāśayaḥ /
body.translated_text: There, what is the calamity-quelling rebirth? Here, a <s>Bodhisattva</s>, having made aspiration during times of famine, hardship, and great wilderness, takes birth in the wombs of great fish and the like, so that beings may sustain their livelihood with little difficulty. Having taken such vast bodily forms, wherever he is born, he satisfies the entire world with his own flesh. And when beings are afflicted with many diseases, having made aspiration, he takes on the bodily form of an accomplished knowledge-holder (<s>siddhavidyādhara</s>), a great physician, in order to pacify their diseases. And when beings are greatly oppressed by hostile armies, he becomes a powerful lord of the earth, in order to pacify the oppression of hostile armies through righteousness, peacemaking, and skillful means—and for beings who are mutually hostile, he becomes one whose words are heeded, for the purpose of making peace and eliminating the roots of enmity. And when rulers are engaged in inflicting punishments, imprisonment, and torture upon the people, he takes birth in those very royal families for the purpose of eliminating those oppressions of beings. And he becomes a righteous king, compassionate toward beings. And whatever beings are devoted to a certain divine shrine, who hold wrong views and do evil deeds—out of compassion for them, for the purpose of eliminating their wrong views and misconduct, he takes birth in that very divine shrine. Through the power of aspiration and mastery (<s>vaśitā</s>), this rebirth preceded by compassion should be understood as immeasurable. For the detailed teaching, [it should be understood] in those various and diverse births among beings born in the animal realm. This is but the summary teaching of its essential purport.

body.text: tatsabhāgānuvartinī upapattiḥ katamā / iha bodhisattvaḥ praṇidhāya vā vaśitāprāptito vā vicitreṣu tiryagyonyupapanneṣu sattveṣu devanāgayakṣāsurādiṣu cānyonyadrugdha viruddheṣu tathā mithyādṛṣṭikeṣu brāhmaṇeṣu tathā duścaritacāriṣu tat
body.translated_text: What is the similar-class-following rebirth? Here, a <s>Bodhisattva</s>, through aspiration or through the attainment of mastery (<s>vaśitā</s>), among beings born in various animal realms, among <s>devas</s>, <s>nāgas</s>, <s>yakṣas</s>, <s>asuras</s>, and others who are mutually hostile and in conflict, and likewise among <s>brāhmaṇas</s> who hold wrong views, and likewise among those who practice misconduct, that

body.text: ājīveṣu tadabhirateṣu tathākāmeṣvatyarthādhyavasiteṣu kāmādhimukteṣu [sattveṣu] teṣāṃ sattvānāṃ sabhā[gatā]yāmupapadyate prāmukhyena tasya doṣasya vinivartanārtham / sa pramukho bhūtvā yatte sattvāḥ samudācaranti tadasā na samudācaranti / yatte na samudācaranti kuśalaṃ tadasau samudācarati / kuśalasamudācārāya caiṣāṃ dharmaṃ deśayati / te tayā [ca] dharmadeśanayā [tayā] ca visabhāgasamudācāratayā tebhyo doṣebhyastenopāyakauśalyena vinivartante / iyamapyupapattiprameyā pūrvavadveditavyā /
body.translated_text: in those livelihoods, those who delight in them, those deeply absorbed in sensual pleasures and devoted to sensual desires—among those beings, he takes birth in their very class, primarily for the purpose of turning them away from that fault. Having become foremost among them, he does not engage in what those beings engage in. And what they do not engage in—that which is wholesome—he engages in. And he teaches the <s>Dharma</s> for [their] engagement in wholesome conduct. Through that <s>Dharma</s>-teaching and through that dissimilar conduct, those beings turn away from those faults by that skillful means. This rebirth too should be understood as immeasurable, as before.

body.text: tatra mahattvopapattiḥ katamā / iha bodhisattvaḥ prakṛtyaivaupapadyamānaḥ sarvalokaprativiśiṣṭamāyurvarṇakulaiśvaryādi-vipākamabhinirvartayati / tena ca vipākena yathoktaṃ svaparārthapaṭale karma karoti / sāpyupapattirbodhisattvasyāprameyā tāsu tāsu yoniṣu veditavyā /
body.translated_text: There, what is the greatness-rebirth? Here, a <s>Bodhisattva</s>, by his very nature when taking birth, brings about the ripening [of karma] that is distinguished above all the world in lifespan, complexion, family, sovereignty, and so forth. And through that ripening, he performs the work described in the chapter on self-benefit and others' benefit (<s>Svaparārtha-paṭala</s>). This rebirth too of the <s>Bodhisattva</s> should be understood as immeasurable in those various births.

body.text: tatra katamā bodhisattvasyādhipatyopapattiḥ / yā bodhisattvasya prathamaṃ pramuditavihāramupādāya yāvaddaśamādvihārādupapattirvarṇitā sā 'syādhipattyopapattirityucyate / jambūdvīpeśvaratvamupādāya yāvanmaheśvaratvādakaniṣṭhānatikramya sarvopapattyāyatanapraviṣṭaṃ yatra paramavihāraprāptā eva bodhisattvā upapadyante / teṣāṃ hi tat karmādhipatyena nirvṛttam /
body.translated_text: Therein, what is the <s>Bodhisattva</s>'s sovereign rebirth (<s>ādhipatyopapatti</s>)? That rebirth of the <s>Bodhisattva</s> which has been described beginning from the first Joyful Abiding up to the tenth abode—that is called his sovereign rebirth. Beginning from sovereignty over <s>Jambudvīpa</s>, up to the sovereignty of <s>Maheśvara</s>, surpassing the <s>Akaniṣṭha</s> [heaven], having entered the sphere of all rebirths where only <s>Bodhisattvas</s> who have attained the Supreme Abiding are reborn. For that has been accomplished through the sovereignty of their <s>karma</s>.

body.text: tatra caramā bodhisattvopapattiḥ katamā / yasyāmupapattau paripūrṇabodhisambhārī bodhisattvaḥ purohitakule vā rājakule vā upapadyānuttarāñca samyaksaṃbodhimabhisaṃbudhyate / sarvañca buddhakārya karoti / iyamupapattiścaramā paścimametyucyate / ye kecid bodhisattvā atītānāgatapratyutpanneṣvadhvasu śubhāsu bhadrāsu kalyāṇāsu upapattiṣūpapannā upapatsyante upapadyante ca sarve te āsveva pañcasu / nāta uttari nāto bhūyaḥ sthāpayitvā bālabhūmyupapattīḥ / tathā hi vijñairbodhisattvaiḥ upapattaya etāḥ pañcābhipretāḥ / tāḥ khalvetā upapattayo mahābodhiphalāḥ / yā āśritya bodhisattvāḥ kṣipramanuttarāṃ samyaksaṃbodhimabhisaṃbudhyante /
body.translated_text: Therein, what is the final rebirth of the <s>Bodhisattva</s>? That rebirth in which the <s>Bodhisattva</s>, whose accumulation for awakening is complete, is reborn in a priestly family or a royal family and awakens to unsurpassed perfect awakening and performs all <s>Buddha</s>-deeds—this rebirth is called the final, the last. Whatever <s>Bodhisattvas</s> in past, future, or present times have been reborn, will be reborn, or are being reborn in auspicious, fortunate, and beneficial rebirths—all of them are within these five [types of rebirth] alone; there is none higher, none beyond, excepting the rebirths on the ordinary-being stage. For these five rebirths are intended by wise <s>Bodhisattvas</s>. These rebirths indeed have great awakening as their fruit, relying on which <s>Bodhisattvas</s> swiftly awaken to unsurpassed perfect awakening.

body.text: iti bodhisattvabhūmāvādhāre niṣṭhe yogasthāne prathamamapapattipaṭalam /
body.translated_text: Thus, in the <s>Bodhisattvabhūmi</s>, in the Concluding Foundational Stage of Practice (Ādhāre Niṣṭhe Yogasthāna), the first chapter: the Chapter on Rebirth (<s>Upapattipaṭala</s>).

body.text: tatra sarvāsu vihāragatāsu bodhisattvacaryāsu bodhisattvānāṃ samāsataḥ ṣaḍvidhaḥ samyaktvaparigraho veditavyaḥ / sakṛtsarvasattvaparigrahaḥ / adhipatyaparigrahaḥ / upādānaparigrahaḥ / dīrghakālikaḥ / adīrghakālikaḥ / caramaśca parigrahaḥ /
body.translated_text: Therein, in all the <s>Bodhisattva</s>-practices pertaining to the [various] abodes, the proper embrace of beings by <s>Bodhisattvas</s> is to be known, in brief, as sixfold: the all-at-once embrace of all beings; sovereign embrace; adoptive embrace; long-term [embrace]; short-term [embrace]; and final embrace.

body.text: prathama eva cittotpāde bodhisattvena sarvaḥ sattvadhātuḥ kalatrabhāvena parigṛhītaḥ / eṣāṃ mayā yathāśakti yathābalaṃ sarvākārahitasukhopasaṃhāraḥ karaṇīya iti / tathaiva ca karoti / ayaṃ bodhisattvasya sakṛt sarvasattvaparigrahaḥ /
body.translated_text: At the very first generation of the mind [of awakening], the <s>Bodhisattva</s> has embraced the entire realm of beings as his own family, [thinking:] 'I must bring about the provision of welfare and happiness in all its aspects for these [beings], to the best of my ability and power.' And he does so accordingly. This is the <s>Bodhisattva</s>'s all-at-once embrace of all beings.

body.text: svāmibhūtasya mātāpitṛputradāradāsīdāsakarmakarapauruṣeyaparigrahe rājabhūtasya ca rājyajane bodhisattvasyādhipatyaparigrahasaṃjñā / sa ca tasminparigrahe parigrahānurūpayā kriyayā bodhisattvānurūpayā pravartate / mātāpitarañca kuśalamūle sanniyojayati vividhairupāyaiḥ / kālena ca kālaṃ pūjopasthānaṃ karoti / kṛtajñaśca bhavati kṛtavedī / cittānuvartakaśca mātāpitrorbhavati / dharmeṣvartheṣu tadvaśavartī / putradāradāsīdāsādīnāṃ kālena kālaṃ samyagbhaktaprāvaraṇamanuprayacchati / karmāntaiścaināṃ na bādhate / vyatikramañcaiṣāṃ kṣamate / glānānāñca samyakglānopasthānaṃ karoti / kuśale caināṃ sanniyojayati / kālena ca kālaṃ vaiśeṣikeṇa lābhena priyavāditayā copavatsayati na caiṣu dāsadāsīsaṃjñāṃ karoti / ātmavaccaināṃ viśeṣeṇa vā paripālayati / rājyajane punā rājabhūto bodhisattvaḥ adaṇḍenāśastreṇa rājyaṃ kārayati / dharmeṇa bhogānupasaṃharati / anvayāgatañca rājyaṃ paribhuṃkte / na pararāṣṭraṃ sahasā balenākrāmati / yathāśakti ca yathābalaṃ sattvān pāpānnivārayati / pitṛbhūtaśca bhavati prajānām / saṃvibhāgaśīlaśca bhavati parasattvānāmapi prāgeva svabhṛtyānām / anabhidrohī ca bhavati satyavādī ca / vadhabandhanadaṇḍanacchedanatāḍanādi-sattvotpīḍā vivarjitāḥ /
body.translated_text: When the <s>Bodhisattva</s> is a master, the embrace of mother, father, sons, wife, female and male servants, workers, and dependents—and when he is a king, [the embrace of] the people of his kingdom—is called the <s>Bodhisattva</s>'s sovereign embrace. In that embrace he acts with conduct befitting the embrace and befitting a <s>Bodhisattva</s>. He encourages his mother and father in wholesome roots by various means. From time to time he performs worship and attendance upon them. He is grateful and acknowledges kindness. He follows the wishes of his parents and is obedient to them in matters of <s>Dharma</s> and purpose. To sons, wife, female and male servants, and others, he gives proper food and clothing from time to time. He does not oppress them with labor. He bears with their transgressions. He properly attends to those who are sick. He encourages them in what is wholesome. From time to time, with special gifts and with pleasant speech, he endears himself to them; and he does not regard them with the perception of servants. He protects them as he would himself, or even more so. As a king, moreover, the <s>Bodhisattva</s> rules his kingdom without the rod and without the sword. He gathers wealth through righteous means. He enjoys the kingdom inherited from his ancestors. He does not invade another's realm suddenly by force. To the best of his ability and power, he restrains beings from evil. He becomes a father to his subjects. He is disposed to sharing, even with others' dependents, how much more with his own. He is non-treacherous and truthful. He is free from afflictions upon beings such as execution, imprisonment, punishment, amputation, and beating.

body.text: tatra samyaggaṇaparikarṣaṇaṃ bodhisattvasyopādānaparigraha ityucyate / sa dvābhyāṃ kāraṇābhyāṃ samyak pariṣadaṃ parigṛhṇāti / nirāmiṣacittena parigṛhṇāti / samyak ca svārthe prayojayati / na mithyāprayogeṇa vipratipādayati / sarvasmiṃśca parigrahe samacitto bhavati na pakṣapatitaḥ / na ca teṣāmantike dharmamātsaryaṃ karoti na cācāryamuṣṭim / na ca teṣāmantikādupasthānaparicaryāṃ pratyāśaṃsate / kuśalakāmatayā tu svayaṃ kurvatāṃ na nivārayati teṣāmeva-puṇyasambhāropacayanimittam kālaṃ ca prāpya svayamevateṣāmupasthānaparicaryākartā bhavati / avyutpannañcaiṣāmārthaṃ vyutpādayati / vyutpañca paryavadāpayati / utpannotpannañca saṃśayaṃ nāśayati / kaukṛtyañca prativinoda yati / gambhīraṃ cārthapadaṃ prajñayā pratividhya kālena kālaṃ saṃprakāśayati / samaduḥkhasukhī ca tairbhavati / ātmanaścāntikāt teṣāmarthe āmiṣahetoradhikena vyāpāreṇa samanvāgato bhavati / kālena ca kālameṣāṃvyatikrame samyakcodako bhavati / kālena ca nyāyenāvasādakaḥ / vyādhitāṃścaitāṃ vimanaskaṃ vā sarvathā nābhyupekṣate vyādhipraśamāya daurmanasyāpagamāya / hīnāṃścainān rūpasmṛtivīryajñānādibhirna paribhavati / kālena ca kālaṃ teṣāṃ khedamanupraviśya yuktarūpaṃ dharmaṃ deśayati / kālena ca kālameṣāmālambane samyagavavādamanuprayacchati / vimardasahiṣṇuśca bhavatyasaṃkṣobhyaḥ / taiśca saha tulyavṛttasamācāro bhavatyadhiko vā [na] nyūnaḥ / lābhasatkāre ca niṣpṛho bhavati / kāruṇikaśca bhavati / anuddhataścācapalaśca śalīdṛṣṭyācārājīvasampannaśca bhavati / uttānamukhavarṇaśca [bhavati /] vigatabhṛkuṭiḥ peśalo madhurabhāṇī pūrvābhilāpī smitapūrvaṅgamaḥ / satatasamitamabhiyuktaśca bhavati / kuśalapakṣe / pramādakausīdyāpagataḥ / tathaiva pariṣado 'nu śikṣaṇārthamātmaviśeṣatā-gamanatāyai ca / na ca bodhisattvaḥ sarvaṃ kālaṃ pariṣadupādānaṃ karoti / naiva na karoti / na cānyathā karoti /
body.translated_text: Therein, the proper leading of an assembly is called the <s>Bodhisattva</s>'s adoptive embrace. He properly embraces the assembly for two reasons: he embraces with a mind free from material gain, and he properly engages them in their own welfare; he does not mislead them through wrong practice. In all embrace he is even-minded, not taking sides. He does not practice jealousy regarding the <s>Dharma</s> in their presence, nor does he keep a teacher's closed fist. He does not expect attendance and service from them. But out of desire for their wholesome [welfare], he does not prevent them when they themselves wish to act; for the sake of their accumulation of merit, and when the time comes, he himself becomes the performer of attendance and service for them. He instructs them in what they have not yet mastered. He brings those who are instructed to completion. He destroys doubts as they arise. He dispels remorse. Having penetrated with wisdom the profound meaning and content, he illuminates it from time to time. He shares equally in their joys and sorrows. From his own [resources], for their welfare, he is endowed with exceptional dedication even for the sake of material gain. From time to time he is a proper admonisher of their transgressions. And at the right time, he properly humbles them. He never entirely neglects those who are sick or disheartened, [working] for the alleviation of illness and the removal of dejection. He does not despise those who are inferior in form, mindfulness, energy, knowledge, and the like. From time to time, entering into their weariness, he teaches the <s>Dharma</s> in a suitable manner. From time to time he gives them proper instruction on their objects [of practice]. He is patient with friction and unshakable. His conduct and behavior with them is equal or superior, never inferior. He is free from desire for gain and honor. He is compassionate. He is not agitated, not frivolous, and is accomplished in view, conduct, and livelihood. He is open-faced, free from frowning, gentle, sweet-spoken, the first to greet, preceded by a smile. He is constantly and continuously diligent in the wholesome side, free from heedlessness and laziness—and likewise for the sake of training the assembly and for his own attainment of distinction. The <s>Bodhisattva</s> does not engage in the adoption of an assembly at all times, nor does he not engage at all, nor does he engage improperly.

body.text: tatra ye mṛduke paripāke vyavasthitāḥ sattvāste bodhisattvasya dīrghakālikamupādānamityucyante cireṇa kālena viśuiddhibhavyatayā /
body.translated_text: Therein, those beings who are established in mild ripening—they are called the <s>Bodhisattva</s>'s long-term adoption, because of their capacity for purification over a long period of time.

body.text: ye punarmadhye paripāke vyavasthitāste 'dīrghakālikamupādānamityucyante na cireṇa viśuddhibhavyatayā /
body.translated_text: Those who are established in moderate ripening—they are called the short-term adoption, because of their capacity for purification without a long period of time.

body.text: ye punaḥ sattvā adhimātre paripāke vyavasthitāste bodhisattvasya caramamupādānamityucyante tasminneva janmani viśuddhibhavyatayā / ityayaṃ ṣaḍvidhaḥ samyaksattvaparigraho bodhisattvānām / yena parigraheṇātītānāgatapratyutpannā bodhisattvāḥ sattvān parigṛhītavantaḥ parigrahīṣyanti parigṛhṇanti vā / punaḥ nāstyata uttari nāsto bhūyaḥ /
