body.translated_text: Those beings who are established in intense ripening—they are called the <s>Bodhisattva</s>'s final adoption, because of their capacity for purification in that very birth. This is the sixfold proper embrace of beings by <s>Bodhisattvas</s>, by which embrace <s>Bodhisattvas</s> of past, future, and present have embraced, will embrace, and do embrace beings. Beyond this there is none higher, none beyond.

body.text: evañca samyaksattvaparigrahavṛttānāṃ bodhisattvānāṃ dvādaśasambādhasaṃkaṭaprāptayo veditavyāḥ / tāsu ca vicakṣaṇena bodhisattvena bhavitavyam / vyatikramavyavasthiteṣu sattveṣu yudi vā bādhanaṃ yadi vā 'dhyupekṣaṇā bodhisattvasya saṃbādhasaṃkaṭaprāptiḥ kaṭukena ca prayogeṇa sattve samudācāraḥ svasya cāśayasya kleśārakṣāsambādhasaṃkaṭaprāptiḥ / alpake ca deyadharme saṃvidyamāne bahūnāṃ yācakānāṃ sammukhībhāvo yācanāya saṃbādhasaṃkaṭaprāptiḥ / ekātmakasya cāsya bahūnāṃ sattvānāṃ kṛtyeṣu vicitreṣūtpanneṣu sahāyībhāvayācanā saṃbādhasaṃkaṭaprāptiḥ / pramādasthānīyā ca śubhā laukikī samāpattirdevalokotpattiścākarmaṇyacetasaḥ saṃbādhasaṃkaṭaprāptiḥ / sattvārthakriyārthinaśca sattvārthakaraṇāsamarthatā saṃbādhasaṃkaṭaprāptiḥ / mūḍhaśaṭhakhaṭhuṃkeṣu sattveṣu dharmasya deśanā vādhyupekṣaṇā vā saṃbādhasaṃkaṭaprāptiḥ / saṃsāre ca nityakālaṃ doṣadarśanaṃ saṃsārāparityāgaśca saṃbādhasaṃkaṭaprāptiḥ / aviśuddhe 'dhyāśaye muṣitasmṛte maraṇaṃ saṃbādhasaṃkaṭaprāptiḥ / aviśuddhe cādhyāṣaye parairagrasya parama-priyasya vastuno yācanā saṃbādhasaṃkaṭaprāptiḥ nānādhibhinnamatānāṃ nānādhimuktikānāṃ sattvānāṃ saṃjñaptikā adhyupekṣaṇā vā saṃbādhasaṃkaṭaprāptiḥ / ātyantikaścāpramādaḥ karaṇīyaḥ kleśāśca sarveṇa sarvaṃ na prahātavya iti saṃbādhasaṃkaṭaprāptiḥ / evaṃ saṃbādhasaṃkaṭaprāptena bodhisattve kvacidgurulāghavaṃ lakṣayitvā tathaiva prayoktavyam kvacitpudgalapravicayaḥ karaṇīyaḥ / kvaciddhairyamālambya hetuṃ samādāya vartitavyam / samyak praṇidhānāni ca karaṇīyāni / kvaciccittasya prasaro na deyaḥ / kvacittīvraṃ pratisaṃkhyānamupasthāpyākhinnena kṣamena bhavitavyam / kvacid
body.translated_text: For <s>Bodhisattvas</s> engaged in the proper embrace of beings, twelve straits and difficulties are to be known, and in them the discerning <s>Bodhisattva</s> must be skillful. When beings are established in transgression, whether to punish or to overlook—this is a strait and difficulty for the <s>Bodhisattva</s>. Acting harshly toward a being, while guarding his own intention from defilements—this is a strait and difficulty. When there is only a small amount of what can be given, and many petitioners come forward to ask—this is a strait and difficulty. When he is but one person, and the varied needs of many beings arise, and they request his companionship—this is a strait and difficulty. An auspicious worldly attainment that is an occasion for heedlessness, and rebirth among the gods, for one whose mind is not yet workable—this is a strait and difficulty. Desiring to act for the welfare of beings but being unable to do so—this is a strait and difficulty. Teaching the <s>Dharma</s> to beings who are deluded, deceitful, and rigid, or overlooking them—this is a strait and difficulty. Constantly seeing faults in <s>saṃsāra</s>, yet not abandoning <s>saṃsāra</s>—this is a strait and difficulty. Dying when the superior intention is not yet purified and mindfulness is lost—this is a strait and difficulty. When the superior intention is not yet purified, and others request the most valued and cherished possession—this is a strait and difficulty. Instructing beings of differing views and diverse inclinations, or overlooking them—this is a strait and difficulty. Ultimate vigilance must be maintained, yet the defilements must not be entirely abandoned—this is a strait and difficulty. When the <s>Bodhisattva</s> is thus beset by straits and difficulties, he must sometimes observe the weight and lightness [of the situation] and act accordingly; sometimes he must make a discrimination of persons; sometimes, taking hold of steadfastness and adopting a cause, he must proceed; sometimes he must make proper vows; sometimes he must not give the mind free rein; sometimes, having established intense reflection, he must be untiring and patient; sometimes,

body.text: upekṣakeṇa bhavitavyam / kvacidārabdhavīryeṇa ātaptakāriṇā bhavitavyam / kvacidupāyakuśalena bhavitavyam / evaṃ samyak pratipakṣakuśalo bodhisattvaḥ sarvasaṃbādhasaṃkaṭaprāptisammukhībhāve 'pi na viṣīdati samyakcātmānaṃ pariharati /
body.translated_text: he must be equanimous; sometimes he must be one who has undertaken energy and is ardent in action; sometimes he must be skilled in means. Thus the <s>Bodhisattva</s>, skilled in the proper antidotes, even when confronted with all straits and difficulties, does not despair and properly protects himself.

body.text: iti bodhisattvabhūmāvādhāre niṣṭhe yogasthāne parigrahapaṭalaṃ dvitīyam /
body.translated_text: Thus, in the <s>Bodhisattvabhūmi</s>, in the Concluding Foundational Stage of Practice, the second chapter: the Chapter on Embrace (<s>Parigrahapaṭala</s>).

body.text: eṣu yathāvarṇiteṣu trayodaśasu vihāreṣvanugatāḥ sapta bhūmayo veditavyāḥ / ṣaṭ bodhisattvabhūmayaḥ / ekā vyāmiśrā bodhisattva-tāthāgatī-bhūmiḥ / gotrabhūmiḥ / abhimukticaryābhūmiḥ śuddhādhyāśayabhūmiḥ / caryāpratipattibhūmiḥ / niyatā bhūmiḥ / niyatacaryābhūmiḥ / niṣṭhāgamanabhūmiśca itīmāḥ sapta bodhisattvabhūmayaḥ / āsāṃ paścimā vyāmiśrā / tatra gotravihāro 'dhimukticaryāvihāraśca dve bhūmī / pramudito vihāraḥ śuddhādhyāśayā bhūmiḥ / adhiśīlādhicittavihārau trayaścādhiprajñavihārāḥ sābhogaśca nirnimitto vihāraścaryāpratipattibhūmiḥ / anābhogo nirnimitto vihāro niyatā bhūmiḥ / tasyāṃ bhūmau bodhisattvastṛtīyaniyatipātapatito bhavati / pratisaṃvidvihāro niyatacaryābhūmiḥ / paramo vihārastāthāgataśca niṣṭhāgamanabhūmiḥ / tāthāgatasya punarvihārasya bhūmeśca paścānnirdeśo bhaviṣyati buddhadharmapratiṣṭhā paṭale /
body.translated_text: In these thirteen abodes as described, seven stages (<s>bhūmi</s>) are to be understood as pervading them. Six are <s>Bodhisattva</s>-stages; one is a mixed <s>Bodhisattva</s>-and-<s>Tathāgata</s> stage. [They are:] the Lineage Stage (<s>gotrabhūmi</s>); the Stage of Aspiration-Practice (<s>abhimukticaryābhūmi</s>); the Stage of Pure Superior Intention (<s>śuddhādhyāśayabhūmi</s>); the Stage of Practice and Conduct (<s>caryāpratipattibhūmi</s>); the Determined Stage (<s>niyatābhūmi</s>); the Stage of Determined Conduct (<s>niyatacaryābhūmi</s>); and the Stage of Final Completion (<s>niṣṭhāgamanabhūmi</s>). These are the seven <s>Bodhisattva</s>-stages; the last among them is the mixed [stage]. Therein, the Lineage Abiding and the Aspiration-Practice Abiding are two stages. The Joyful Abiding is the Stage of Pure Superior Intention. The Abiding in Higher Morality, the Abiding in Higher Mind, the three Abidings in Higher Wisdom, and the Abiding with Effort and Signlessness constitute the Stage of Practice and Conduct. The Abiding without Effort and with Signlessness is the Determined Stage; in that stage, the <s>Bodhisattva</s> falls into the third determination. The Abiding of Analytical Knowledge is the Stage of Determined Conduct. The Supreme Abiding and the <s>Tathāgata</s> [Abiding] are the Stage of Final Completion. The exposition of the <s>Tathāgata</s> Abiding and Stage will come later, in the Chapter on the Establishment of <s>Buddha</s>-Qualities (<s>Buddhadharmapratiṣṭhāpaṭala</s>).

body.text: tatra bodhisattvaḥ adhimukticaryābhūmeḥ śuddhādhyāśayabhūmimanupraviśan katham apāyānsamatikrāmati / iha bodhisattvo laukikaṃ pariśuddhaṃ dhyānaṃ niśrityādhimukticaryābhūmau susambhṛtabodhi sambhāro daśottareṇa pūrvanirdiṣṭenākāraśatena sattveṣvanukampāṃ bhāvayapyananyamanasikāraḥ / sa bhāvanānvayāt tadrūpaṃ sattveṣvanukampāśayaṃ karuṇāśayaṃ pratilabhate / yenāpāyān sattvānāmarthe 'gārāvasāyogenādhitiṣṭhati / yadi me eṣveva sannivasato 'nuttarā samyaksaṃbodhiḥ samudāgacchati tathāpyahamutsahāmīti sattvānāṃ duḥkhāpanayanahetoḥ / sarvāñca sattvānāmāpāyikaṃ karma tena śuddhenāśayenātmavaipākyamicchati / atyantañca sarvākuśalakarmāsamudācārāya mānaṃ saṃpraṇidhatte / tasya tathā paribhāvitaṃ tallaukikaṃ pariśuddhaṃ dhyānam / āpāyikakleśapakṣyaṃ dauṣṭhalyaṃ āśrayādapakarṣati / acireṇa tasya prahāṇādāśrayo 'sya bodhisattvasya parivartate pāpakasyāpāyikasya karmaṇo 'tyantamakaraṇatāyai apāyāgamanatāyai
body.translated_text: There, how does the <s>Bodhisattva</s>, entering the stage of pure intention (<s>śuddhādhyāśayabhūmi</s>) from the stage of aspiration-conduct (<s>adhimukticaryābhūmi</s>), transcend the bad destinies (<s>apāya</s>)? Here, the <s>Bodhisattva</s>, relying on purified worldly <s>dhyāna</s>, having well-accumulated the provisions for awakening on the aspiration-conduct stage, cultivates compassion toward beings in the hundred and ten aspects previously described, with undivided attention. Through the continuity of cultivation, one obtains such a disposition of compassion and compassionate intention toward beings that, for the sake of beings, one resolves to dwell even in the bad destinies with the determination of a householder: 'Even if my unsurpassed, perfect awakening were to arise while I am dwelling among these very [beings in the bad destinies], even so I would endure it' — for the purpose of removing the suffering of beings. And with that pure intention, one wishes upon oneself the ripening of all the bad-destiny <s>karma</s> of all beings. And one aspires with firm resolve toward the absolute non-occurrence of all unwholesome action. For one who has thus cultivated that purified worldly <s>dhyāna</s>, the propensity (<s>dauṣṭhulya</s>) belonging to the side of afflictions leading to the bad destinies is removed from the basis (<s>āśraya</s>). Before long, through its abandonment, the basis of this <s>Bodhisattva</s> is transformed toward the absolute non-performance of evil bad-destiny <s>karma</s> and toward the non-occurrence of going to the bad destinies

body.text: ca / iyatā bodhisattvaḥ samatikrānto 'pāyagatīḥ sarvā bhavati / samatikrāntaścādhimukticaryābhūmim / praviṣṭaśca śuddhādhyāśayabhūmim /
body.translated_text: . By this much, the <s>Bodhisattva</s> has transcended all the bad destinies. And one has transcended the stage of aspiration-conduct. And one has entered the stage of pure intention.

body.text: ye ca te daśadharmā vihārapaṭale nirdiṣṭā / śraddhādayo vihārapariśodhanāḥ ta ihāpi bhūmiviśodhanā veditavyāḥ / teṣāṃ vipakṣapratipakṣato vyavasthānaṃ veditavyam / samāsārtho 'nukramaśca veditavyaḥ / tatra daśeme / eṣāṃ daśānāṃ bhūmiviśodhanānāṃ dharmāṇāṃ vipakṣabhūtā dharmāḥ / yeṣāṃ pratipakṣeṇaiṣāṃ vyavasthānaṃ bhavati / katame daśa / sarveṇa sarvamanārambhacittotpādanā bodhisattvaśikṣāpadāsamādānam ayaṃ śraddhāvipakṣo dharmaḥ / yasya pratipakṣeṇa śraddhā / sattveṣu vihiṃsācittaṃ karuṇāvipakṣaḥ / yasya pratipakṣeṇa karuṇā / sattveṣu vyāpādo maitrīvipakṣaḥ / yasya pratipakṣeṇa maitrī / bhogajīvikāpekṣā dānavipakṣaḥ / yasya pratipakṣeṇa tyāgaḥ / sattvebhyo 'pakāra-vipratipattilābho bahukartavyatā cākhedavipakṣaḥ / yasya pratipakṣeṇākhedatā / anupāyaprayogaḥ śāstrajñatā-vipakṣaḥ / yasya pratipakṣeṇa śāstrajñatā / asauratyāparacittānuvartanatā lokajñatā-vipakṣaḥ / yasya pratipakṣeṇa lokajñatā / kuśaladharmabhāvanāyāṃ pramādakausīdyaṃ hrīvyapatrāpya-vipakṣaḥ / yasya pratipakṣeṇa hrīvyapatrāpyatā / dīrghakālikaiścitraistīvrairnirantaraiḥ saṃsāraduḥkhairvyavadīraṇatā dhṛtibalādhānatā-vipakṣaḥ / tasya pratipakṣeṇa dhṛtibalādhānatā / śāstari kāṃkṣā vimatirvicikitsā tathāgatapūjopa sthānatāyāḥ vipakṣaḥ / yasya pratipakṣeṇa tathāgatapūjopasthānatā / evaṃ tāvadeṣāṃ vipakṣapratipakṣato vyavasthānaṃ bhavati /
body.translated_text: And those ten <s>dharmas</s> that were described in the Chapter on Abodes (<s>Vihārapaṭala</s>) as purifying the abodes — beginning with faith — should here also be understood as purifying the stages (<s>bhūmiviśodhana</s>). Their establishment through the relationship of adversary and antidote should be understood. Their summary meaning and sequence should be understood. These are the ten. The following are the ten <s>dharmas</s> that are the adversaries of these ten stage-purifying <s>dharmas</s>, through the antidote to which they are established. Which ten? The arising of a mind of complete non-undertaking of all <s>Bodhisattva</s> training-rules — this is the <s>dharma</s> that is the adversary of faith, by the antidote to which there is faith. An intention to harm beings — this is the adversary of compassion (<s>karuṇā</s>), by the antidote to which there is compassion. Ill-will toward beings — this is the adversary of loving-kindness (<s>maitrī</s>), by the antidote to which there is loving-kindness. Attachment to possessions and livelihood — this is the adversary of generosity (<s>dāna</s>), by the antidote to which there is relinquishment (<s>tyāga</s>). Receiving harm and wrong treatment from beings, having many obligations — this is the adversary of unweariness (<s>akheda</s>), by the antidote to which there is unweariness. The application of unskillful means — this is the adversary of knowledge of the treatises (<s>śāstrajñatā</s>), by the antidote to which there is knowledge of the treatises. Harshness and following the minds of others [inappropriately] — this is the adversary of knowledge of the world (<s>lokajñatā</s>), by the antidote to which there is knowledge of the world. Heedlessness and laziness in the cultivation of wholesome <s>dharmas</s> — this is the adversary of moral shame and scrupulousness (<s>hrī-vyapatrāpya</s>), by the antidote to which there is moral shame and scrupulousness. Being worn down by the long-lasting, varied, intense, and uninterrupted sufferings of <s>saṃsāra</s> — this is the adversary of the sustaining of firmness and strength (<s>dhṛtibalādhānatā</s>), by the antidote to which there is the sustaining of firmness and strength. Doubt, uncertainty, and wavering regarding the Teacher — this is the adversary of attendance upon the <s>Tathāgata</s> in worship, by the antidote to which there is attendance upon the <s>Tathāgata</s> in worship. Thus, their establishment through adversary and antidote is so far [described].

body.text: kaḥ punareṣāṃ samāsārthaḥ / samāsena daśabhirebhirdharmairāśayaśuddhiḥ prayogaśuddhiśca paridīpitā / tatra tribhiḥ pūrvakairāśayaśuddhiḥ / avaśiṣṭaiḥ prayogaśuddhirveditavyā / bodhimabhiśraddhadbodhisattvaḥ sattvān duḥkhitān karuṇāyate / karuṇāyamāno mayaite paritrātavyā iti maitrāyate / tathā maitracittasya sarvaparityāgī bhavatyeṣu bhogajīvitanirapekṣaḥ / nirapekṣaścaiṣāmarthe prayujyamāno na parikhidyate / aparikhinnaśca śāstrajño bhavati / śāstrajñaśca yathā loke
body.translated_text: What then is the summary meaning of these? In summary, through these ten <s>dharmas</s>, the purity of intention (<s>āśayaśuddhi</s>) and the purity of practice (<s>prayogaśuddhi</s>) are illuminated. There, through the first three, the purity of intention [is illuminated]. Through the remaining ones, the purity of practice should be understood. The <s>Bodhisattva</s> has faith in awakening; one has compassion toward suffering beings; being compassionate, [one thinks:] 'These beings must be rescued by me,' and thus one develops loving-kindness. Being of such a loving mind, one becomes one who relinquishes everything, disregarding possessions and life for their sake. Being thus disregarding and applying oneself for their welfare, one does not become weary. Being unwearied, one becomes a knower of the treatises. Being a knower of the treatises, one knows how to conduct oneself in the world

body.text: pravartitavyamanena tathā jānāti / evaṃ lokajño bhavati / svayañca kleśasamudācāreṇa jehrīyate vyapatrapate / hrīmānapatrāpī ca kleśāvaśago dhṛtibaladhānaprāpto bhavati / dhṛtibalādhānaprāptaśca samyak prayogādaparihīyamānaḥ kuśalaiśca dharmairvivardhamānaḥ pratipattipūjayā lābhasatkārapūjayā ca tathāgatapūjopasthānaṃ karoti / ityayameṣāṃ daśānāṃ dharmāṇāmanukramasamudāgamo veditavyaḥ / ebhirdaśabhirdharmaiḥ sarvabhūmiviśodhanā bhavati /
body.translated_text: . Thus one becomes a knower of the world. And one feels shame and scrupulousness at the occurrence of one's own afflictions. Being possessed of moral shame and scrupulousness, when overpowered by afflictions, one attains the sustaining of firmness and strength. Having attained the sustaining of firmness and strength, through correct practice, not declining, and increasing in wholesome <s>dharmas</s> — one performs attendance upon the <s>Tathāgata</s> through both the worship of practice and the worship of gain, honor, and offerings. This should be understood as the sequential arising of these ten <s>dharmas</s>. Through these ten <s>dharmas</s>, the purification of all stages occurs.

body.text: iti bodhisattvabhūmāvādhāre niṣṭhe yogasthāne tṛtīyaṃ bhūmipaṭalam /
body.translated_text: Thus, in the <s>Bodhisattvabhūmi</s>, in the Foundation Section (<s>Ādhāra</s>) and Final Section (<s>Niṣṭha</s>) of the Yoga-ground (<s>Yogasthāna</s>), the third chapter, the Chapter on Stages (<s>Bhūmipaṭala</s>).

body.text: adhimukticaryābhūmimupādāya sarvāsu bodhisattvabhūmiṣu bodhisattvānāṃ samāsataścatasraścaryā veditavyāḥ / [katamāścatasraḥ /] pāramitācaryā bodhipakṣyācaryā [abhijñācaryā] sattvaparipākacaryā ca / tatra ṣaṭ ca pūrvanirdiṣṭāḥ pāramitāḥ / upāyakauśalyapāramitā ca praṇidhānapāramitā ca balapāramitā ca jñānapāramitā ca / itīmā daśapāramitā abhisamasya pāramitācaryetyu cyate / tatra dvādaśākāraṃ pūrvanirdiṣṭamupāyakauśalya[mupāyakauśalya-]pāramitā / pañca pūrvanirdiṣṭāni praṇidhānāni praṇidhānapāramitā / daśabalaprayogaviśuddhirbalapāramitā / sarvadharmeṣu yathāvad vyavasthānajñānaṃ jñānapāramitā / tatra paramārthagrahaṇapravṛttā prajñā prajñāpāramitā / saṃvṛtigrahaṇapravṛttā punarjñānapāramitā / ityayamanayorviśeṣaḥ / aparaḥ paryāyaḥ / apramāṇajñānatā upāyakauśalyapāramitā / uttarottarajñānavaiśeṣikatā-prārthanā praṇidhānapāramitā / sarvamārairmārgānācchedyatā balāpāramitā / yathāvaj jñaiyāvabodhatā jñānapāramitā / smṛtyupasthānānyupādāya sarve saptatriṃśadbodhipakṣyā dharmāścatasraśca paryeṣaṇāścatvāri ca yathābhūtaparijñānāni yathāpūrvanirdiṣṭānyabhisamasya bodhisattvānāṃ bodhipakṣyacaryetyucyate / yathā saṃvarṇitāśca ṣaḍbhijñāḥ prabhāvapaṭale bodhisattvānāmabhijñācaryetyucyate / dvau ca pūrvanirdiṣṭāvaprameyau vineyāprameyaśca vinayopāyāprameyaśca [sarvasattvaparipāko yathānirdiṣṭaḥ] sattvaparipākapaṭale bodhisattvasyābhisamasya sattvaparipākacaryetyucyate /
body.translated_text: From the stage of aspiration-conduct onward, on all <s>Bodhisattva</s> stages, in brief, four conducts of <s>Bodhisattvas</s> should be understood. Which four? The conduct of the <s>pāramitās</s> (<s>pāramitācaryā</s>), the conduct of the factors of awakening (<s>bodhipakṣyācaryā</s>), the conduct of superknowledges (<s>abhijñācaryā</s>), and the conduct of maturing beings (<s>sattvaparipākacaryā</s>). There, the six <s>pāramitās</s> previously described, plus the <s>pāramitā</s> of skill in means (<s>upāyakauśalyapāramitā</s>), the <s>pāramitā</s> of aspiration (<s>praṇidhānapāramitā</s>), the <s>pāramitā</s> of strength (<s>balapāramitā</s>), and the <s>pāramitā</s> of knowledge (<s>jñānapāramitā</s>) — these ten <s>pāramitās</s> taken together are called the conduct of the <s>pāramitās</s>. There, the twelvefold skill in means previously described is the <s>pāramitā</s> of skill in means. The five aspirations previously described are the <s>pāramitā</s> of aspiration. The purification of the endeavor toward the ten powers is the <s>pāramitā</s> of strength. The knowledge of the proper establishment of all <s>dharmas</s> as they truly are is the <s>pāramitā</s> of knowledge. There, the wisdom that operates in grasping the ultimate (<s>paramārtha</s>) is the <s>pāramitā</s> of wisdom (<s>prajñāpāramitā</s>). The wisdom that operates in grasping the conventional (<s>saṃvṛti</s>) is the <s>pāramitā</s> of knowledge (<s>jñānapāramitā</s>). This is the distinction between the two. Another way of stating it: immeasurable knowledge is the <s>pāramitā</s> of skill in means. The aspiration for progressively higher distinction in knowledge is the <s>pāramitā</s> of aspiration. Being unassailable on the path by all <s>Māras</s> is the <s>pāramitā</s> of strength. Awakening to the knowable as it truly is — this is the <s>pāramitā</s> of knowledge. Beginning with the foundations of mindfulness, all thirty-seven <s>dharmas</s> conducive to awakening, plus the four quests and the four knowledges of things as they truly are, as previously described — taken together, these are called the <s>Bodhisattvas</s>' conduct of the factors of awakening. The six superknowledges (<s>abhijñā</s>) as described in the Chapter on Power (<s>Prabhāvapaṭala</s>) are called the <s>Bodhisattvas</s>' conduct of superknowledges. The two immeasurables previously described — the immeasurable [number] of those to be trained (<s>vineya</s>) and the immeasurable means of training (<s>vinayopāya</s>) — and the ripening of all beings as described in the Chapter on the Maturation of Beings (<s>Sattvaparipākapaṭala</s>) — taken together, these are called the <s>Bodhisattvas</s>' conduct of maturing beings.

body.text: ābhiścatasṛbhirbodhisattvacaryābhiḥ sarvabodhisattvacaryāṃsaṃgraho veditavyaḥ / tatrāsaṃkhyeyatraya-dīrghakālasamudāgamātsvabhāvaviśuddhiviśeṣāttadanyebhyaḥ sarvalaukikaśrāvakapratyekabuddhakuśalamūlebhyaḥ paramabodhiphalaparigrahāccaite daśa
body.translated_text: Through these four <s>Bodhisattva</s> conducts, the inclusion of all <s>Bodhisattva</s> conduct should be understood. There, through their arising over three incalculable periods of a long time, through the distinction of their purification of intrinsic nature — surpassing all other worldly, <s>Śrāvaka</s>, and <s>Pratyekabuddha</s> wholesome roots — and through the embrace of the supreme fruit of awakening, these ten

body.text: dānādayo dharmāḥ parameṇa kālena samudāgatāḥ paramayā svabhāvaviśuddhyā viśuddhāḥ paramañca phalamanuprayacchanti / iti tasmātpāramitā ityucyante /
body.translated_text: <s>dharmas</s> beginning with generosity (<s>dāna</s>), having arisen over the supreme duration of time, purified by the supreme purification of their intrinsic nature, and yielding the supreme fruit — are therefore called <s>pāramitās</s> (perfections).

body.text: tribhiśca kāraṇaiḥ pāramitānāmanukramavyavasthānaṃ veditavyam / katamaistribhiḥ / pratipakṣataḥ upapattito vipākaphalataśca /
body.translated_text: And the sequential ordering of the <s>pāramitās</s> should be understood through three reasons. Which three? From the standpoint of antidote (<s>pratipakṣa</s>), from the standpoint of arising (<s>upapatti</s>), and from the standpoint of fruit-ripening (<s>vipākaphala</s>).

body.text: tatra mātsaryaṃ duścaritaṃ sattveṣu vairotpīḍanatā kausīdyaṃ vikṣepo mandamomuhatā ca / amī ṣaḍdharmā bodherāvaraṇasthānīyāḥ / eṣāṃ [ṣaṇṇāṃ] dharmāṇāṃ pratipakṣeṇa ṣaṭ pāramitā yathāyogaṃ veditavyāḥ / tadanyāśca pāramitā ābhireva saṃgṛhītāḥ / evaṃ pratipakṣato vyavasthānaṃ bhavati /
body.translated_text: There, miserliness (<s>mātsarya</s>), bad conduct (<s>duścarita</s>), hostility and oppression of beings (<s>vaira-utpīḍanatā</s>), laziness (<s>kausīdya</s>), distraction (<s>vikṣepa</s>), and dullness and confusion (<s>mandamomuhatā</s>) — these six <s>dharmas</s> stand as obstructions to awakening. As the antidote to these six <s>dharmas</s>, the six <s>pāramitās</s> should be understood in their respective correspondence. And the other <s>pāramitās</s> are included by these very [six]. Thus there is the ordering from the standpoint of antidote.

body.text: kathamupapattitaḥ / ihādita eva bhoganirapekṣo bodhisattvaḥ tyaktvā āgārikān kāmān śīlasamādānaṃ karoti / śīlagauravācca paraviheṭhaṃ kṣamate / no tu paraṃ viheṭhayati / samādānataśca kṣāntitaśca viśuddhiśīlo niścalena nirantareṇa kuśalapakṣaprayogeṇa prayujyate / sa tathā vīryeṇāpramattaḥ spṛśati kuśalāñcittasyaikāgratām / sa tathā samāhitacitto yathābhūtaṃ jñeyaṃ jānāti dṛśyaṃ paśyati / evameṣāmevānukrameṇopapattito vyavasthānaṃ veditavyam /
body.translated_text: How from the standpoint of arising? Here, first of all, the <s>Bodhisattva</s>, disregarding possessions, having relinquished household sensual pleasures, undertakes the adoption of moral conduct. And out of regard for morality, one endures harm from others; one does not oneself harm others. Being of purified morality through adoption [of precepts] and through patience, one applies oneself with unwavering and uninterrupted effort in the wholesome course. One thus heedful through vigor touches the one-pointedness of mind in the wholesome. One thus concentrated truly knows the knowable as it is and sees the visible. Thus the ordering of these through their sequential arising should be understood.

body.text: kathaṃ phalavipākataḥ / iha bodhisattvasya dṛṣṭe dharme etān dānādīn kuśalāndharmān samādāya vartamānasya tannidānamāyatyāṃ bāhyataśca bhogasampatpratilambho bhavati dānakṛtaḥ / adhyātmikaśca pañcākāra ātmabhāvasampatpratilambho bhavati tadanyaśīlādi-pāramitākṛtaḥ /
body.translated_text: How from the standpoint of fruit-ripening? Here, for the <s>Bodhisattva</s> who, in the present life, having adopted these wholesome <s>dharmas</s> beginning with generosity, is engaged [in practice] — through that as cause, in the future, externally, there is the attainment of the endowment of material wealth, produced by generosity. And internally, there is the attainment of the fivefold endowment of personal existence (<s>ātmabhāvasampad</s>), produced by the other <s>pāramitās</s> beginning with moral conduct.

body.text: pañcākārā ātmabhāvasampatkatamā / sugatiparyāpanno divyamānuṣyakastadanyasattvāyurādiviśeṣavān / iyaṃ prathamā sampat / sahajā cakuśalamūlaprayoge akhedatā paravyatikramasahiṣṇutā ca paropatāpapriyatā / iyaṃ dvitīyā sampat / sahajā sarvārambheṣu dṛḍhavyavasāyatā / iyaṃ tṛtīyā sampat / sahajā ca mandarajaskasya svacittavaśitā cittakarmaṇyatā sarvārtheṣu kṣiprābhijñatāyai / iyaṃ caturthī sampat / sahajañca mativaipulyaṃ pāṇḍityaṃ
body.translated_text: What is the fivefold endowment of personal existence? One is born in a fortunate destiny, divine or human, or among other beings distinguished by longevity and the like — this is the first endowment. One has an innate unweariness in the endeavor of wholesome roots, a tolerance for the transgressions of others, and a love of not causing distress to others — this is the second endowment. One has an innate firmness of resolve in all undertakings — this is the third endowment. One has innate mastery over one's own mind, with a mind of little defilement, workability of mind, and swift higher knowledge in all matters — this is the fourth endowment. One has innate breadth of intelligence, learning

body.text: vicakṣaṇatā ca sarvārtheṣu / iyaṃ pañcamī sampat itīdaṃ phalavipākakṛtamanyadanukramavyavasthānaṃ ṣaṇṇāṃ pāramitānāṃ veditavyam /
body.translated_text: , and discernment in all matters — this is the fifth endowment. Thus, this is another ordering of the six <s>pāramitās</s> through the standpoint of fruit-ripening.

body.text: tatra catasṛbhiḥ pāramitābhiḥ [saha]sambhāreṇa svabhāvena parivāreṇa rakṣayā ca paripūrṇā bodhisattvānāmadhiśīlaṃ śikṣā veditavyā / dhyānapāramitayā adhicittaṃ śikṣā / prajñāpāramitayā adhi[prajñaṃ] śikṣā / na ca bodhisattvasyottari śikṣāmārga upalabhyate / tribhiḥ ataḥ sarvabodhisattvaśikṣāmārgaṃsaṃgrahātṣaḍeva pāramitā [vyavasthāpitā] / nāta uttari nāto bhūyaḥ /
body.translated_text: There, the training of the <s>Bodhisattvas</s> in higher morality (<s>adhiśīla śikṣā</s>) should be understood as fulfilled through four <s>pāramitās</s>, together with provision, intrinsic nature, accompaniment, and protection. The training in higher mind (<s>adhicitta śikṣā</s>) [is fulfilled] through the <s>pāramitā</s> of meditation (<s>dhyānapāramitā</s>). The training in higher wisdom (<s>adhiprajña śikṣā</s>) [is fulfilled] through the <s>pāramitā</s> of wisdom (<s>prajñāpāramitā</s>). And no further training-path of the <s>Bodhisattva</s> is found beyond these. Since all the <s>Bodhisattva</s> training-paths are included in these three, precisely six <s>pāramitās</s> are established — there is nothing beyond this, nothing more than this.

body.text: catvāri cemāni bodhisattvānāṃ samāsataḥ kṛtyāni / yaireṣāṃ sarvakṛtyasaṃgraho bhavati / bodhāya kuśalābhyāsaḥ / tatpūrvakaśca tattvārthaprativedhaḥ prabhāvasamudāgamaḥ / sattvaparipācanatā ca / etāni ca catvāri kṛtyāni bodhisattvāḥ ābhiścatasṛbhiścaryābhiryathākramaṃ kurvantyanutiṣṭhanti / tasmādapi taduttarā caryā na vyavasthāpyate /
body.translated_text: And these are, in brief, the four functions of <s>Bodhisattvas</s>, by which all their functions are included: the habitual practice of the wholesome for the purpose of awakening; preceded by that, the penetration of the reality of things (<s>tattvārthaprativedha</s>); the attainment of power (<s>prabhāvasamudāgama</s>); and the maturation of beings (<s>sattvaparipācanatā</s>). And <s>Bodhisattvas</s> carry out and accomplish these four functions through these very four conducts in their respective order. Therefore, no further conduct beyond these is established.

body.text: iti bodhisattvabhūmāvādhāre niṣṭhe yogasthāne caturthaṃ caryāpaṭalam /
body.translated_text: Thus, in the <s>Bodhisattvabhūmi</s>, in the Foundation Section (<s>Ādhāra</s>) and Final Section (<s>Niṣṭha</s>) of the Yoga-ground (<s>Yogasthāna</s>), the fourth chapter, the Chapter on Conduct (<s>Caryāpaṭala</s>).

children.translated_text: <s>Lakṣmaṇānuvyañjanapaṭala</s> (Chapter on the Major and Minor Marks)

body.text: tatra tathāgatavihāramārabhya tāthāgatīñca niṣṭhāgamanabhūmiṃ bhagavatāṃ catvāriṃśaduttaramāveṇikaṃ buddhadharmaśataṃ bhavati / dvātriṃśanmahāpuruṣalakṣaṇāni aśītyunuvyañjanāni catasraḥ sarvākārāḥ pariśuddhayaḥ daśa tathāgatabalāni catvāri vaiśāradyāni trīṇi smṛtyupasthānāni trīṇyarakṣāṇi mahāṃkaruṇā 'sammoṣadharmatā vāsanā-samuddhātaḥ sarvākāra-varajñānañca /
body.translated_text: There, beginning with the <s>Tathāgata</s>-abode and the <s>Tathāgata</s>'s culminating stage (<s>niṣṭhāgamanabhūmi</s>), the <s>Bhagavāns</s> have one hundred and forty exclusive <s>Buddha</s>-qualities (<s>āveṇika buddhadharma</s>): the thirty-two marks of a great person (<s>mahāpuruṣalakṣaṇa</s>), the eighty minor marks (<s>anuvyañjana</s>), the four all-aspect purifications (<s>sarvākārapariśuddhi</s>), the ten powers of a <s>Tathāgata</s> (<s>tathāgatabala</s>), the four fearlessnesses (<s>vaiśāradya</s>), the three foundations of mindfulness (<s>smṛtyupasthāna</s>), the three guardings (<s>arakṣa</s>), great compassion (<s>mahākaruṇā</s>), the nature of non-forgetfulness (<s>asammoṣadharmatā</s>), the eradication of latent impressions (<s>vāsanāsamudghāta</s>), and the knowledge of all aspects in their best form (<s>sarvākāravarajñāna</s>).

body.text: dvātriṃśanmahāpuruṣalakṣaṇāni katamāni / supratiṣṭhitapādo mahāpuruṣaḥ samamākramati mahīm / idaṃ mahāpuruṣasya mahāpuruṣalakṣaṇam / adhasthātpādatalayoścakre jāte sahasrāre sanābhike sanemike sarvākāraparipūrṇe / dīrghāṅgulimaṃhāpuruṣaḥ / āyatapādapārṣṇiḥ / mṛdutaruṇapāṇipādaḥ / jālapāṇipādaḥ / ucchaṅgacaraṇaḥ / eṇeyajaṅghaḥ / anavanatakāyaḥ / kośagatavastiguhyaḥ / nyogradhaparimaṇḍalaḥ / vyāmaprabhaḥ / ūrdhvāṅgaromā / ekaikaromā / ekaikamasya romakūpe jātaṃ nīlaṃ kuṇḍalakajātaṃ pradakṣiṇāvartam / kāñcanasannibhatvak / ślakṣṇavatk / ślakṣṇatvāt tvace rajo malasya kāye nāvatiṣṭhate / saptotsadakāyaḥ / saptāsyotsadāḥ / kāye jātāḥ-dvau hastayordvau pādayordvāvasaṃyoreko grīvāyām / siṃhapūrvārdhakāyaḥ / susaṃvṛttaskandhaḥ / citāntarāṃśaḥ / bahadṛjugātraḥ / catvāriṃśatsamadantaḥ / aviraladantaḥ / suśukladantaḥ / siṃhahanuḥ / prabhūta-tanujihvaḥ / prabhūtatvāj jihvāyāḥ mukhājjihavāṃ nirṇāmya sarvamukhamaṇḍalamavacchādayati yāvantakaṃ kleśaparyantam / rasarasāgraprāptaḥ / brahmasvaraḥ / kalaviṅka-manojñabhāṇī / dundubhisvaranirghoṣaḥ / abhinīlanetraḥ / gopakṣmā /
body.translated_text: What are the thirty-two marks of a great person (<s>mahāpuruṣalakṣaṇa</s>)? The great person has well-planted feet—he treads evenly upon the earth. This is a mark of the great person. On the soles of both feet, wheels have appeared, with a thousand spokes, with hubs, with rims, complete in all aspects. The great person has long fingers. He has extended heels. He has soft and tender hands and feet. He has webbed hands and feet. He has raised arches. He has calves like an antelope (<s>eṇeya</s>). He has an unbent body. His male organ is sheathed (<s>kośagatavastiguhya</s>). He is proportioned like a banyan tree (<s>nyagrodha</s>). His radiance extends a fathom (<s>vyāmaprabhā</s>). His body-hair grows upward. Each hair grows singly. In each single hair-pore, a hair grows that is dark blue, curling, turning clockwise. His skin resembles gold. His skin is smooth. Due to the smoothness of his skin, dust and impurity do not remain on his body. His body has seven prominences (<s>saptotsada</s>). His seven prominences are formed on the body—two on the hands, two on the feet, two on the shoulders, and one on the neck. His front body is like a lion's. His shoulders are well-rounded. The space between his shoulders is broad. His limbs are great and straight. He has forty even teeth. He has teeth without gaps. He has brilliantly white teeth. He has a jaw like a lion's. He has a broad and thin tongue. Due to the breadth of his tongue, extending it from his mouth, he covers the entire face up to the boundary of the hairline. He has attained the foremost of tastes. He has a <s>Brahmā</s>-voice. He has a voice as melodious as the <s>kalaviṅka</s> bird. His voice has the resonance of a drum. His eyes are deeply blue. He has eyelashes like a cow's

body.text: uṣṇīṣaśīrṣā / ūrṇā cāsya bhrūvormadhye jātā śvetā śaṃkhanibhā pradakṣiṇāvartā / idaṃ mahāpuruṣasya mahāpuruṣalakṣaṇam /
body.translated_text: He has a protuberance on his head (<s>uṣṇīṣa</s>). And a hair-tuft (<s>ūrṇā</s>) has grown between his brows—white, resembling a conch-shell, turning clockwise. This is a mark of the great person.

body.text: aśītiranuvyañjanāni katamāni / hastapādayorviśatiraṅgulyaḥ saparvāṇaḥ sanakhāḥ / viṃśatiranuvyañjanāni / hastapādayorevāṣṭau talāni / dvayorhastayoścatvāri dvayoḥ pādayoścatvāryaṣṭāvanuvyañjanāni / ṣaḍvidho gulphajānūrusaṃghātaḥ / ṣaḍanuvyañjanāni / ṣaḍvidho bāha-saṃghātaḥ ṣaḍanuvyañjanāni / jaghanam / sīvanī ca / vṛṣṇe 'nuvyañjanadvayaṃ / upastham / dve sphicau anuvyañjanadvayam / trikam / udaram / nābhiḥ / dve pārśve dve kakṣe dvau stanauabhisamasya ṣaḍanuvyañjane bhavanti / uraḥ hṛdayaṃ grīvā pṛṣṭham / ityetyāni adhaḥ kāyagatāni grīvāyāma ūrdhvaṃ sthāpayitvā ṣaṣṭiranuvyañjanāni bhavati / dve dantamāle dve anuvyañjane / tālukam / dvau saparivārau coṣṭau anuvyañjanadvayam / suparipūrṇaṃ kapolam / dve gaṇḍe paripūrṇe susaṃskṛte anuvyañjanadvyam / dvau akṣiparivārāvanuvyañjanadvayam / dve bhruvāvanuvyañjanadvayam / dve nāsikāvile anuvyañjanadvayam / lalāṭam / dve śaṅkhe dvau ca karṇāvanuvyañjana-catuṣṭam / sakeśañca śiro 'nuvyañjanam / ityetāni grīvāyāḥ ūrdhvaṃ kāye viṃśatiranuvyañjanāni bhavanti / pūrvakāni ca ṣaṣṭiḥ paścimakāni ca viṃśatirekadhyamabhisaṃkṣipya aśītiranuvyañjanāni bhavanti / ityetāni lakṣaṇānuvyañjanāni [bhadrāṇi] śuddhāśayabhūmipraviṣṭo bodhisattvo vipākataḥ pratilabhate / tatastūrdhvameṣāṃ śuddhiruttarottarā yāvadbodhimaṇḍaniṣadanād veditavyā / pariśiṣṭānāveṇikān sarvākāra-pariśuddhādīn suviśuddhān paripūrṇān pratilabhate / hīnaistu taiḥ pūrvamapi bodhisattvabhūtaḥ samanvāgato bhavati śuddhādhyāśayabhūmimupādāya / sarvaścāviśeṣeṇa bodhisambhāraḥ sarveṣāṃ lakṣaṇānuvyañjanānāṃ nirvartako bhavati /
body.translated_text: What are the eighty minor marks (<s>anuvyañjana</s>)? On the hands and feet there are twenty fingers, with joints and with nails—twenty minor marks. On the hands and feet there are eight surfaces—four on the two hands and four on the two feet—eight minor marks. There is the sixfold articulation of ankles, knees, and thighs—six minor marks. There is the sixfold articulation of the arms—six minor marks. The hips and the perineum—two minor marks at the reproductive organ. The two buttocks—two minor marks. The lower back. The abdomen. The navel. The two flanks, the two armpits, and the two breasts—combined, they make six minor marks. The chest, the heart, the neck, and the back. Thus, these are the minor marks belonging to the body below—counting upward from the neck, excluding [the head], there are sixty minor marks. The two rows of teeth—two minor marks. The palate. The two lips with their surrounding—two minor marks. The well-rounded cheeks—the two cheeks, full and well-formed—two minor marks. The two surrounds of the eyes—two minor marks. The two eyebrows—two minor marks. The two nostrils—two minor marks. The forehead. The two temples and the two ears—four minor marks. And the head with its hair—one minor mark. Thus, these are the twenty minor marks belonging to the body above the neck. Combining the former sixty and the latter twenty together, there are eighty minor marks. These marks and minor marks—auspicious ones—the <s>Bodhisattva</s> who has entered the stage of pure intention (<s>śuddhāśayabhūmi</s>) obtains as a result of karmic maturation. From that point onward, their progressive purification should be understood, up to sitting at the seat of awakening (<s>bodhimaṇḍa</s>). The remaining exclusive [<s>Buddha</s>-qualities], beginning with the all-aspect purifications, he obtains in their fully pure and complete form. But even earlier, as a <s>Bodhisattva</s>, he is endowed with those in their lesser forms, beginning from the stage of pure intention. And the entire accumulation for awakening, without exception, produces all the marks and minor marks.

body.text: sa punarbodhisambhāro dvividhaḥ / bodherdūraścāsannaśca / tatra dūraḥ / yaḥ pratilabdheṣu vipākato lakṣaṇānuvyañjaneṣu / āsannaḥ / yaḥ pratilabdheṣu tatprathamato vipākato lakṣaṇānuvyañjaneṣu / tato vā uttarottaraviśuddhiviśeṣagateṣu /
body.translated_text: That accumulation for awakening is of two kinds: distant from awakening and proximate to awakening. There, the 'distant' is that which [occurs when] the marks and minor marks have been obtained as the result of karmic maturation [for the first time]. The 'proximate' is that which [occurs when] the marks and minor marks have been obtained as the result of karmic maturation from the very first time, or when they have progressively attained higher purification.

body.text: vicitrakarmābhisaṃskāraphalāni tvetāni lakṣaṇānuvyañjanāni bhagavatā [arthi-]vineyavaśena nirdeśitāni / tatkasya hetoḥ / sattvā vicitre pāpakarmasamudācāre 'bhiratāḥ / apyeva te tasya pāpakasya karmaṇo vipakṣabhūtasya vicitrasya yatprātipakṣikaṃ vicitraṃ kuśalaṃ lakṣaṇānuvyañjananirvartakaṃ karma tasyedaṃ vicitraphalānuśaṃsaṃ śrutvā tasya mahataḥ phalānuśaṃsasya spṛhyamānarūpāratasmācca pāpādvirameyuḥ / tacca kuśalaṃ samādāya varteranniti / yathoktaṃ lakṣaṇasūtre / śīlavratakṣāntityāgeṣu pratiṣṭhitatvātsupratiṣṭhitapādatvaṃ pratilabhate / mātāpitrorupasthānena vicitreṇa vicitrayā ca sattvopadravārakṣayā āgamana-gamanādiparispandamupādāya cakrāṅkapādatāṃ pratilabhate / paravihiṃsāmadattādānañca prahāya gurūṇāṃ cābhivādanavandana-pratyutthānāñjali-sāmīcī-karma kṛtvā pareṣāṃ manastuṣṭipriyabhogāhrasvīkaraṇān nihatamānatvācca dīrghāṅgulitvaṃ mahāpuruṣalakṣaṇaṃ pratilabhate / yaiśca tribhiḥ karmabhiretāni trīṇi mahāpuruṣalakṣaṇāni nirdiṣṭāni taireva sarvaiḥ samastairāyatapādapārṣṇitvaṃ pratilabhate / tatra trayāṇāmapi lakṣaṇānāṃ saṃniśrayatvāt caturbhiḥ saṃgrahavastubhirgurūn saṃgṛhya jālapāṇipādatāṃ pratilabhate / gurūṇāmeva cābhyaṅgodvartana-snānācchādanāni dattvā mṛdutaruṇapāṇipādatāṃ pratilabhate / kuśaladharmāsaṃtuṣṭyā uttarottarān kuśalāndharmānvardha yitvā ucchaṅgacaraṇatāṃ pratilabhate / yathāvaddharmānudgṛhya paryavāpya pareṣāṃ ca deśayitvā dautyañca samyak pareṣāṃ kṛtvā aiṇeyajaṅghatāṃ pratilabhate / anupūrveṇa dharmasamādānena netrīvartamānatvātpāpakaṃ kāyavāṅgamanaḥkarma saṃyamayya / tatrānavanataḥ glāneṣu ca glānopasthānaṃ kṛtvā bhaiṣajyañca dattvā vyādhyanavanatocchrayaṇān mātrāśī ca kāmeṣvanavanataḥ anavanatakāyatāṃ pratilabhate / parairnirvāsitān sattvān dharmeṇa samena saṃhṛtya hrīmānapatrāpī vastrapradaśca koṣagatavastiguhyatāṃ pratilabhate / kāyavāṅmanobhiḥ saṃvṛtātmā pratigraha-bhojane ca mātrajñaḥ glāneṣu bhaiṣajyapradaḥ viṣame karmaṇi pratigraha-paribhogavaiṣamye cāpravṛttatvāt
body.translated_text: These marks and minor marks, being the fruits of variously constructed actions (<s>vicitrakarmābhisaṃskāra</s>), have been taught by the <s>Bhagavān</s> for the sake of those beings who are to be trained with purposeful motivation. For what reason? Beings are inclined to engage in various evil actions. Perhaps, having heard of the various great fruits and benefits of that wholesome action which produces the marks and minor marks—which is the antidote to and the opposite of that evil action—desiring those great fruits and benefits, they would desist from that evil and would undertake and practice that wholesome [action]. As stated in the <s>Lakṣaṇa Sūtra</s>: Through being established in moral conduct, observances, patience, and generosity, he obtains the [mark of] well-planted feet. Through various service to mother and father, and through various protection of beings from calamity—with reference to the movement of coming and going and so forth—he obtains the [mark of] wheel-marks on the feet. Having abandoned violence toward others and taking what is not given, and having performed salutation, homage, rising, hands-joined reverence, and acts of respectful conduct toward elders, and through providing pleasure and agreeable enjoyments to others' minds, and through the destruction of pride—he obtains the mark of long fingers. And through the same three actions by which these three marks of the great person have been described, collectively he obtains the [mark of] extended heels—since those [heels] serve as the support for the three marks. Through gathering elders by means of the four means of attraction (<s>saṃgrahavastu</s>), he obtains webbed hands and feet. Through giving anointing, massage-oil, bathing, and clothing to elders, he obtains soft and tender hands and feet. Through dissatisfaction with wholesome <s>dharmas</s> and by progressively increasing wholesome <s>dharmas</s>, he obtains raised arches. Through properly grasping and mastering <s>dharmas</s>, teaching them to others, and properly performing the duties of a messenger, he obtains calves like an antelope. Through the gradual undertaking of <s>Dharma</s> practice, proceeding as a guide, restraining evil action of body, speech, and mind—not bending down in that, and by caring for the sick, giving medicine, not bending down from illness, being moderate in eating, and not bending down to sensual desires—he obtains an unbent body. Through bringing together by righteous means beings who have been exiled by others, and being endowed with moral shame and moral dread, and being a giver of clothing—he obtains the [mark of] the sheathed male organ. Through being restrained in body, speech, and mind, and being moderate in the receiving and consuming of requisites, giving medicine to the sick, not engaging in uneven receiving and consuming,

body.text: [dhātuvaiṣamyānu]lomanācca nyagrodhaparimaṇḍalatvaṃ pratilabhate / yenaiva ca karmaṇā utsaṅgacaraṇatāṃ pratilabhate tenaivordhvaṅgaromatām / svayaṃ kuśalamīmāṃsakaḥ paṇḍitavijña-sevī sūkṣmārthacintakaḥ gurūṇāṃ sthānaśodhakaḥ utsādakaḥ snāpakaśca ekavihāritvādekamitra-saṃśrayatvātsūkṣmārthapraveśāt tṛṇaparṇādyāvilāpakarṣaṇādāgantukamalāpakarṣaṇācca ekaikaromatāṃ pratilabhate / manojñaprītikarabhojanapānayānavastrālaṅkārādi-kāyapariṣkāraṃ dattvā akrodhanaḥ kāñcanasannibhatvacatāṃ vyāmaprabhatāñca pratilabhate / yenaiva ca karmaṇā ekaikaromatoktā tenaiva sūkṣmaślakṣṇatvacatā veditavyā / prabhūtenotsadena viśadenānnapānena mahājanakāyaṃ saṃtarpayitvā saptotsadakāyatāṃ pratilabhate / sattvānāmutpannotpanneṣu dharmeṣu karaṇīyeṣu prāmukhyenāvasthitaḥ / nāhaṃ mānī na ca niṣṭhuraḥ / ahitāñca sattvānā nivārayitā tāḍitā hitāhite ca sanniyojayitā siṃhapūrvārdhakāyatāṃ pratilabhate siṃhavatsattvārtheṣu parākramaśīlatvāt / anenaiva ca karmaṇā susaṃvṛttaskandhatā citāntarāṃśatā ca veditavyā / yenaiva ca karmaṇā dīrghāṅgulitvaṃ pratilabhate tenaiva bṛhadṛjugātratāṃ pratilabhate / mitrabhedakarīṃ piśunāṃ vācaṃ prahāya bhinnānāñca sattvānāṃ sāmagrīṃ kṛtvā catvāriṃśad dantatāṃ samāviraladantatāñca pratilabhate / kāmāvacarīṃ maitrīṃ bhāvayitvā dharmārthacintakaḥ suśukladantatāṃ pratilabhate / arthimyaḥ sattvebhyo yathābhipretaṃ dhanaṃ samyagvisṛjya siṃhahanutāṃ pratilabhate / svasutavat-sattvānsaṃrakṣya śrāddhaścānukampakaśca bhaiṣajyapradaśca [prasannaśca] rasarasāgratāṃ pratilabhate dharmarasānupradānāddharmarasāsvādanāt pranaṣṭarasaviśodhanācca / pañca śikṣāpadāni prāṇātipātaviratyādīni svayañca samādāya saṃrakṣya parāṃśca teṣveva samādāpayitvā karuṇācittatāmupādāya mahatī dharmasamādāne pratipannatvāduṣṇīṣaśiraskatāñca prabhūta-tanujihvatāṃ ca pratilabhate / satyavāditayā priyavāditayā kāladharmavāditayā ca brahmasvaratāṃ pratilabhate / kṛtsnaṃ jaganmaitreṇa cetasā 'nukampya mātṛvatpitṛvadabhinīlanetratāṃ gopakṣmanetratāñca pratilabhate / guṇavatāṃ tu bhūtasya varṇasya hartāṃ varṇavādī bhruvormadhye ūrṇāṃ pratilabhate śvetāṃ śaṃkhanibhāṃ pradakṣiṇāvartām /
body.translated_text: and through conforming to the balance of bodily elements—he obtains the [mark of] proportions like a banyan tree. And through the same action by which he obtains raised arches, he obtains upward-growing body-hair. Through being an investigator of the wholesome, associating with the learned and wise, reflecting on subtle meanings, sweeping and cleaning the places of elders, anointing and bathing [them], dwelling alone, relying on a single companion, penetrating subtle meanings, removing thorns, leaves, and such impurities, and removing adventitious defilements—he obtains the [mark of] single body-hairs. Through giving delightful and pleasurable food, drink, vehicles, clothing, ornaments, and other bodily embellishments, and through being free from anger—he obtains skin resembling gold and radiance extending a fathom. And through the same action by which the single body-hairs were stated, the subtle and smooth skin should be understood. Through satisfying a great multitude of people with abundant, excellent, and pure food and drink—he obtains a body with seven prominences. Through standing foremost in matters to be done that arise for beings, being free from pride, not being harsh, restraining beings from what is harmful, and yoking them to what is beneficial and salutary—he obtains a front body like a lion's, for he is by nature one who strives in the interests of beings like a lion. And through this same action, well-rounded shoulders and a broad space between the shoulders should be understood. Through the same action by which he obtains long fingers, he obtains great and straight limbs. Through abandoning divisive, slanderous speech and reconciling beings who have been divided—he obtains forty teeth and teeth without gaps. Through cultivating loving-kindness pertaining to the desire realm and reflecting on the <s>Dharma</s> and its meaning—he obtains brilliantly white teeth. Through properly distributing wealth as desired to suppliant beings—he obtains a jaw like a lion's. Through protecting beings as if they were his own children, and through being faithful, compassionate, a giver of medicine, and serene—he obtains the foremost of tastes, through the giving of the taste of <s>Dharma</s>, the savoring of the taste of <s>Dharma</s>, and the purification of lost taste. Through personally undertaking and safeguarding the five precepts beginning with abstention from taking life, and having caused others to undertake those same [precepts], and having undertaken the great <s>Dharma</s>-practice with a mind suffused with compassion—he obtains the protuberance on the head (<s>uṣṇīṣa</s>) and the broad, thin tongue. Through truthful speech, pleasant speech, and timely <s>Dharma</s>-speech—he obtains the <s>Brahmā</s>-voice. Through regarding all the world with a compassionate mind, like a mother and a father—he obtains deeply blue eyes and eyelashes like a cow's. Through being a speaker who praises the genuine virtues of the virtuous—he obtains between the brows the hair-tuft (<s>ūrṇā</s>), white, resembling a conch-shell, turning clockwise.

body.text: sarveṣu ca dvātriṃśatsu mahāpuruṣalakṣaṇeṣvaviśeṣeṇa śīlaṃ kāraṇaṃ pratilambhāya veditavyam / tatkasya hetoḥ / na hi śīlavipanno bodhisattvo manuṣyatvameva tāvadāsādayet kutaḥ punarmahāpuruṣalakṣaṇam / tatroṣṇīṣaśiraskatā anava lokitamūrdhatā caikaṃ mahāpuruṣakṣaṇaṃ veditavye tadvyatirekeṇānupalambhāt / idaṃ tāvadvistareṇa lakṣaṇābhinivṛttyānurūpyeṇa vicitrakarmavyavasthānam /
body.translated_text: And for all thirty-two marks of the great person without exception, moral conduct (<s>śīla</s>) should be understood as the cause of their attainment. For what reason? For a <s>Bodhisattva</s> whose moral conduct has failed would not even attain human birth—how much less the marks of a great person! There, the protuberance on the head (<s>uṣṇīṣa</s>) and the unsurpassed crown of the head should be understood as a single mark of the great person, since they are not found separately. This, then, is the detailed arrangement of the various actions in accordance with the accomplishment of the marks.

body.text: samāsataḥ punaścaturākārayā pakṣadvayagatayā sukṛtakarmāntatayā sarvalakṣaṇābhinirvṛttirveditavyā / tatra niyatakāritayā supratiṣṭhitapādayā nirvartate / nipuṇakāritayā cakracaraṇatā ucchaṅgacaraṇatā jālapāṇipādatā sūkṣmatvacatā citāntarāṃśatā susaṃvṛttaskandhatā vṛhadṛjugātratā prabhūtatanujihvatā ca nirvartate / nityakāritayā dīrghāṅga litvaṃ āyatapādapārṣṇitā anavanatakāyatā nyagrodhaparimaṇḍalatā aviraladantatā ca nirvartate / anavadyakāritayā pariśiṣṭānāṃ lakṣaṇānāmabhinirvṛttiḥ / tatra sattveṣvavyābādhyaprayogānmṛdutaruṇapāṇipādatā ślakṣṇa-sūkṣma-tvacatā ca nirvartate / kramaprayogācca kālaprayogācca kuśale aiṇeyajaṅghatā nirvartate / prāmodyaprītiprabhāsvareṇa cittena kuśalasamācārād vyāma-prabhatā ca kāñcanasannibhatvacatā śukladantatā ūrṇā ca śvetā nirvartate / kīrtiśabdaśloke 'sanniśrayāt praticchanna-kalyāṇatvācca kośagatavastiguhyatā nirvartate / bodhāya kuśalamūlapariṇamanādūrdhvāṅga-romatā catvāriṃśatsamadantatā rasarasāgratā uṣṇīṣaśiraskatā ca nirvartate / kuśale atṛptālīnaprayogāt siṃhapūrvārdhakāyatā siṃhahanutā ca nirvartaṃte / sattveṣu hitacittatayā samadarśanāt samadantatā abhinīlanetratā gopakṣmamā ca nirvartate / hīnenāsantuṣṭiprayogācca brahmasvaratā ca nirvartaṃte / evamanayā caturākārayā sukṛtakarmāntatayā bodhisattvānāmeṣāṃ dvātriṃśatāṃ-mahāpuruṣa lakṣaṇānāṃ pratilambho viśuddhiśca bhavati /
body.translated_text: Furthermore, in brief, through the fourfold well-performed action belonging to both sides [householder and renunciant], the production of all the marks should be understood. There, through definite performance, well-established feet are produced. Through skillful performance, wheel-marked soles, raised insteps, webbed fingers and toes, fine-textured skin, dense and intermediate joints, well-rounded shoulders, a large and straight body, and a long and slender tongue are produced. Through constant performance, long limbs, extended heels, an unbent body, a <s>nyagrodha</s>-like circumference, and evenly-set teeth are produced. Through blameless performance, the remaining marks are produced. There, through the practice of non-harming toward beings, soft and tender hands and feet, and smooth and fine-textured skin are produced. Through gradual and timely application in the wholesome, antelope-like calves are produced. Through the practice of wholesome conduct with a mind radiant with delight and joy, a fathom-wide aura, golden-hued skin, white teeth, and a white <s>ūrṇā</s> (tuft of hair between the brows) are produced. Through non-attachment to fame, renown, and praise, and through concealing one's virtues, the sheathed male organ is produced. Through the dedication of wholesome roots toward awakening, upward-growing body hair, forty even teeth, supremacy of taste, and the <s>uṣṇīṣa</s> (cranial protuberance) are produced. Through insatiable and undistracted application in the wholesome, a lion-like upper body and lion-like jaws are produced. Through the equal regard born of a mind of benevolence toward beings, even teeth, deep-blue eyes, and cow-lash eyelashes are produced. Through dissatisfaction with what is inferior and its earnest practice, the <s>Brahmā</s>-voice is produced. Thus, through this fourfold well-performed action, the <s>Bodhisattvas</s>' attainment and purification of these thirty-two marks of a great person (<s>mahāpuruṣalakṣaṇa</s>) comes about.

body.text: tatra gotrabhūmau bodhisattvānāmetallakṣaṇabījamātre 'vasthānaṃ veditavyam / adhimukticaryābhūmau prāptyupāye vṛttireṣāṃ veditavyā / adhyāśayaśuddhi bhūmau prāptireṣāṃ veditavyā / tadanyāsu taduttarottarāsu bodhisattvabhūmiṣu viśuddhireṣāṃ
body.translated_text: There, on the lineage stage (<s>gotrabhūmi</s>), the <s>Bodhisattvas</s> should be understood as established merely in the seed of these marks. On the aspiration-conduct stage (<s>adhimukticaryābhūmi</s>), the practice of the means for their attainment should be understood. On the stage of purity of intention (<s>adhyāśayaśuddhibhūmi</s>), their attainment should be understood. On the remaining, progressively higher <s>Bodhisattva</s> stages, their purification

body.text: veditavyā tāthāgatyāṃ niṣṭhāgamanabhūmau suviśuddhataiṣāṃ niruttaratā ca veditavyā / tatra rūpitvādeṣāṃ lakṣaṇānāṃ hīnamadhyottamaiśca sattvaiḥ sūpalakṣyatvāt satsu sarveṣveva buddhadharmeṣu mahāpuruṣalakṣaṇeṣvetānyeva mahāpuruṣalakṣaṇāni vyavasthāpitāni / etānyeva ca dvātriṃśanmahāpuruṣalakṣaṇānyāśrayabhāvena dhārayantyānurūpyācca śobhayante tasmādanuvyañjanānītyucyante /
body.translated_text: should be understood. On the <s>Tathāgata</s> stage, the stage of reaching culmination, their supreme purity and unsurpassedness should be understood. There, because these marks are of a material nature and because they are readily discernible by inferior, middling, and superior beings, among all the <s>Buddha</s>-qualities, it is precisely these marks of a great person that are established [as most prominent]. And precisely these thirty-two marks of a great person are borne as the underlying basis, and the secondary marks (<s>anuvyañjana</s>) beautify them in a fitting manner — therefore they are called secondary marks.

body.text: tatra samāsataḥ sarvasattveṣu puṇyasadṛśena puṇyaskandhena tathāgatasyaikaiko romakūpo nirvartate / yāvatsarvaromakūpapraviṣṭaḥ puṇyaskandhaḥ / iyatā puṇyaskandhenaikaikamanuvyañjanagati nirvartate / yāvatsarvānuvyañjanapraviṣṭaḥ puṇyaskandhaḥ / tataḥ śataguṇena puṇyaskandhena tathāgatasyaikaṃ lakṣaṇaṃ nirvartate / yāvatsarvalakṣaṇapraviṣṭaḥ puṇyaskandhaḥ sthāpayitvā ūrṇāmuṣṇīṣañca / tataḥ sahasraguṇena puṇyaskandhenorṇā nirvartate / yāvānūrṇā-praviṣṭaḥ puṇyaskandhaḥ tataḥ śatasahasraguṇena puṇyaskandhena uṣṇīṣaśiraskatā anavalokitamūrdhatā ca nirvartate / yāvānuṣṇīṣapraviṣṭaḥ puṇyaskandhaḥ / tataḥ koṭīśatasahasraguṇena puṇyaskandhena tathāgatasya lakṣaṇānuvyañjanāsaṃgṛhīto 'nyo dharmaśaṃkhyo nāma nirvartate / yena tathāgata ākāṃkṣamāṇaḥ anantāparyantān lokadhātūn svareṇa vijñāpayati / evamaprameyaḥ puṇyasambhāra-samudāgatastathāgataḥ / tathāgatānāmacintyo niruttaraḥ sarvākārasampattiparigṛhīta ātmabhāvo nirvartate /
body.translated_text: There, in brief, each hair-pore of the <s>Tathāgata</s> is produced by a mass of merit equal to [the merit of] all beings combined. As many masses of merit as have gone into all the hair-pores — by that much merit, each secondary mark is produced. As many masses of merit as have gone into all the secondary marks — by a hundredfold greater mass of merit, each one of the <s>Tathāgata</s>'s marks is produced. As many masses of merit as have gone into all the marks — excluding the <s>ūrṇā</s> and the <s>uṣṇīṣa</s> — by a thousandfold greater mass of merit, the <s>ūrṇā</s> is produced. As much merit as has gone into the <s>ūrṇā</s> — by a hundred-thousandfold greater mass of merit, the <s>uṣṇīṣa</s> (cranial protuberance) and the unseen crown of the head are produced. As much merit as has gone into the <s>uṣṇīṣa</s> — by a mass of merit a hundred-thousand-<s>koṭī</s>-fold greater, another quality of the <s>Tathāgata</s> called the <s>Dharma</s>-conch (<s>dharmaśaṅkha</s>) is produced, which is not encompassed by the marks and secondary marks, and by which the <s>Tathāgata</s>, when he wishes, informs infinite and boundless world-systems with his voice. Thus the <s>Tathāgata</s> has arisen from an immeasurable accumulation of merit. The <s>Tathāgatas</s>' inconceivable, unsurpassed, all-aspect-endowed bodily existence is produced.

body.text: teṣāṃ punarlakṣaṇānuvyañjananirvartakānāṃ kuśalānāṃ karmaṇāṃ samāsatastribhiḥ kāraṇeprameyatā veditavyā / kalpāsaṃkhyeyatayā 'bhyāsasamudāgamāt kālāprameyatayāaprameyasattvahitasukhāśayādhipateyatvādāśayā 'prameyatayā aprameyakuśalakarmavaicitryākārāprameyatayā ca / tasmādaprameyapuṇyasambhārasamudāgatastathāgatānāṃ lakṣaṇānuvyañjanādaya ityucyate /
body.translated_text: Furthermore, the immeasurability of the wholesome actions that produce those marks and secondary marks should be understood through three causes in brief: through the immeasurability of time — because of the accomplishment through repeated practice over incalculable <s>kalpas</s>; through the immeasurability of intention — because the governing [factor] is the intention for the benefit and happiness of immeasurable beings; and through the immeasurability of the variety of aspects of immeasurable wholesome actions. Therefore, the marks, secondary marks, and so forth of <s>Tathāgatas</s> are said to have arisen from an immeasurable accumulation of merit.

body.text: iti bodhisattvabhūmāvādhāre niṣṭhe yogasthāne pañcamaṃ lakṣaṇānuvyañjanapaṭalam /
body.translated_text: Thus, in the <s>Bodhisattvabhūmi</s>, in the Foundation Section, Culmination, of the Yoga-ground, the fifth chapter on the Marks and Secondary Marks (<s>Lakṣaṇānuvyañjana-paṭala</s>) [is completed].

body.text: catasraḥ sarvākārāḥ pariśuddhayaḥ katamāḥ / āśrayaśuddhiḥ / ālambanaśuddhiḥ / cittaśuddhiḥ jñānaśuddhiśca /
body.translated_text: What are the four all-aspect purities (<s>pariśuddhi</s>)? Purity of basis (<s>āśrayaśuddhi</s>), purity of object (<s>ālambanaśuddhi</s>), purity of mind (<s>cittaśuddhi</s>), and purity of knowledge (<s>jñānaśuddhi</s>).

body.text: tatrāśrayaviśuddhiḥ katamā / savāsanānāṃ sarvakleśapakṣyāṇāṃ dauṣṭhulyānāmāśrayān niravaśeṣato 'tyantaparamaḥ sve cātmabhāve yathākāmādānasthānacyutivaśavartitā sarvākārā āśrayaśuddhistyucyate /
body.translated_text: There, what is the purity of basis (<s>āśrayaviśuddhi</s>)? The complete, total, and supreme removal from one's own person of all rigidities (<s>dauṣṭhulya</s>) belonging to the side of afflictions together with their latent tendencies (<s>vāsanā</s>), without remainder, and the mastery over taking up and relinquishing bodily existences at will in all aspects — this is called all-aspect purity of basis.

body.text: tatrālambanaviśuddhiḥ katamā / nirvāṇe pariṇāme saṃprakhyāne ca sarvālambaneṣu yā vaśavartitā / iyamucyate sarvākārā ālambanaviśuddhiḥ /
body.translated_text: There, what is the purity of object (<s>ālambanaviśuddhi</s>)? The mastery over all objects — in <s>nirvāṇa</s>, in transformation, and in clear manifestation — this is called all-aspect purity of object.

body.text: tatra cittaviśuddhiḥ katamā / pūrvavatsarvacittadauṣṭhulyāpagamāccitte ca sarvākāra-kuśalamūlopacayātsarvākārā cittaviśuddhirityucyate /
body.translated_text: There, what is the purity of mind (<s>cittaviśuddhi</s>)? As before, through the departure of all mental rigidities, and through the accumulation in the mind of all kinds of wholesome roots in all aspects — this is called all-aspect purity of mind.

body.text: tatra katamā jñānaviśuddhiḥ / pūrvavatsarvāvidyāpakṣyadauṣṭhulyāpagamātsarvatra ca jñeye jñānasyānāvaraṇāt jñānavaśavartitā sarvākārā jñānaviśuddhirityucyate /
body.translated_text: There, what is the purity of knowledge (<s>jñānaviśuddhi</s>)? As before, through the departure of all rigidities belonging to the side of ignorance, and through the unobstructedness of knowledge with respect to all knowables everywhere — the mastery of knowledge in all aspects is called all-aspect purity of knowledge.

body.text: tatra daśa tathāgatabalāni katamāni / sthānāsthānajñānabalaṃ karmasvakajñānabalaṃ dhyānavimokṣasamādhisamāpattijñānabalam indriyaparāparajñānabalaṃ nānā dhātujñānabalaṃ nānādhimuktijñānabalaṃ sarvatragāminīpratipajjñānabalaṃ pūrvanivāsānusmṛtijñānabalaṃ cyutyupapattijñānabalam āsravakṣayajñānabalañca / ityetāni daśa tathāgatabalāni yuthā daśabalasūtre nirdeśato vistareṇa veditavyāni /
body.translated_text: There, what are the ten Powers (<s>bala</s>) of the <s>Tathāgata</s>? The power of knowledge of what is possible and impossible (<s>sthānāsthānajñānabala</s>); the power of knowledge of the [ripening of] one's own actions (<s>karmasvakajñānabala</s>); the power of knowledge of <s>dhyānas</s>, liberations, <s>samādhis</s>, and attainments (<s>dhyāna-vimokṣa-samādhi-samāpattijñānabala</s>); the power of knowledge of the superior and inferior faculties [of beings] (<s>indriyaparāparajñānabala</s>); the power of knowledge of the diverse dispositions [of beings] (<s>nānādhātujñānabala</s>); the power of knowledge of the diverse inclinations [of beings] (<s>nānādhimuktijñānabala</s>); the power of knowledge of the paths leading everywhere (<s>sarvatragāminīpratipajjñānabala</s>); the power of knowledge of the recollection of past lives (<s>pūrvanivāsānusmṛtijñānabala</s>); the power of knowledge of death and rebirth (<s>cyutyupapattijñānabala</s>); and the power of knowledge of the destruction of the outflows (<s>āsravakṣayajñānabala</s>). These are the ten Powers of the <s>Tathāgata</s>, which should be understood in detail as taught in the <s>Daśabala-sūtra</s>.

body.text: tatra
body.translated_text: There, whatever has been spoken, uttered, and proclaimed by him — all of it is true, thus (<s>tathā</s>), not false. Therefore he is called <s>Tathāgata</s> ('Thus-gone' or 'Thus-come'). There, the genuine, correct, non-erroneous cause of a fruit — whether wholesome or unwholesome — is called its 'ground' (<s>sthāna</s>), 'basis' (<s>pratiṣṭhā</s>), 'support' (<s>niśraya</s>), and 'producer' (<s>abhinirvartaka</s>). The erroneous cause of a wholesome or unwholesome fruit — the opposite of that — is called 'non-ground' (<s>asthāna</s>). Knowledge that is free from conceit is called 'as it truly is' (<s>yathābhūtam</s>). (

body.text: yatkiñcidanena bhāṣitaṃ lapitamudāhṛtaṃ sarvaṃ tattathā avitatheti tasmāttathāgata ityucyate / tatra phalasya śubhāśabhasya yo bhūtapravṛttaḥ aviṣamo hetuḥ tadasya sthānaṃ pratiṣṭhā niśrayo 'bhinirvartakaṃ ityucyate / śubhāśubhasyaiva phalasya viṣamaheturetadviparyayeṇāsthānamityucyate / nirabhimānaṃ jñānaṃ yathābhūtamityucyate /

sarvajñānamasaktajñānaṃ śuddhañca tannirabhimānaṃ [jñānaṃ] veditavyam / eṣāñca sarvajñānādīnāṃ padānāṃ pūrvavadvyākaraṇaṃ veditavyaṃ tadyathā paramabodhipaṭale / anupūrvaṃ gaṇanayā prathamam / niruttaratvātsarvākāra-sarvasattvārthakriyāśaktiyuktatvāt sarvamārabalātyantābhibhavācca balamityucyate / yathāvaddhetusamudāgamaparigrahādyathākāmasamudācāravaśavartitā samanvāgata ityucyate / niruttaratvānnirvāṇamudāramityucyate / āryāṣṭāṅgeṇa mārgeṇa labhyatvātsarvopadravabhayāpagatatvāccārṣabhamityucyate / ātmanastadadhigamena pratijñānātpratijānātītyucyate / svayamadhigamya pareṣāmapyanukampayā vistareṇa prakāśanād brāhmacakraṃ pravartayatītyucyate / tatkasya hetoḥ / tathāgatasyaitadadhivacanaṃ yaduta brahmā ityapi śāntaḥ śītībhūta ityapi / tena tatpravartitaṃ tatprathamataḥ tadanyaiḥ punastadanyeṣām / evaṃ pāraṃparyeṇa brahmā preritaṃ sarvasattvanikāye bhramati / tasmād brāhmañcakramitucyate / agraprajñaptipatitasya niruttaraśāstṛsaṃpatparigṛhītasya cātmano vikhyāpanāt tanmārgadeśanayā ca sarvatadanyapāṣaṇḍapratikṣepaṇāt tanmārgavipratyanīkavādiṣu ca pratyupasthiteṣu asaṃkocātsarvaparavādābhibhavāya codāraniruttaravāgabhyudoraṇātpariṣadi samyak siṃhanādaṃ nadatītyucyate / samāsatastvātmahita-pratipattisampat-parahita-[pratipatti-]sva parahitapratipattisampadaścāsādhāraṇam / teṣām uttānā vivṛtā prajñaptā prakāśitā bhavati / aparaḥ samāsārthaparyāyaḥ / prāptavyantaprāptyabhyupāyaḥ / tasya cābhyupāyasya sarvajanyatāyo [yaḥ] kaścidākāṃkṣati devabhūto vā [manuṣyabhūto vā] sarveṇa tena mamaivāntikāllabhya eṣo 'bhyupāya iti / tatra vyādhipraśamanavadudāramārṣabhaṃ sthānaṃ draṣṭavyam / vyādhipraśamanopāyavad brāhmacakrapravartanā draṣṭavyā / sarva[ku]vaidyapratijñā pratikṣepaṇavat svayaṃ ca niyataṃ vyādhipraśamanapratijñānavatpariṣadi samyak siṃhanādaṃ naditaṃ draṣṭavyam /
body.translated_text: Omniscient knowledge (<s>sarvajñāna</s>), unattached knowledge, and pure knowledge — all of that should be understood as free from conceit. And the explanation of all these terms — omniscient knowledge and so forth — should be understood as before, namely as in the Chapter on Supreme Awakening (<s>Paramabodhi-paṭala</s>). [The powers] are sequentially first by enumeration. Because of being unsurpassed, because of being endowed with the capacity for welfare-activity toward all beings in all aspects, and because of the ultimate overcoming of all the forces of <s>Māra</s>, they are called 'powers' (<s>bala</s>). Because of being endowed with mastery of conduct at will, through the possession of causes as they truly are, they are called 'possessed of' [the powers]. Because of being unsurpassed, <s>nirvāṇa</s> is called 'noble' (<s>udāra</s>). Because it is obtained through the Noble Eightfold Path, and because all calamities and fears have departed from it, it is called 'bull-like' (<s>ārṣabha</s>). Because he himself declares his own realization of it, it is said 'he proclaims.' Having realized it himself, and out of compassion revealing it extensively to others, he is said to 'turn the <s>Brahmā</s>-wheel.' For what reason? Because this is the designation of the <s>Tathāgata</s> — namely, '<s>Brahmā</s>,' and also 'the peaceful one,' 'the cooled one.' What is set in motion by him, first by him and then by others to still others — thus, by succession, propelled by <s>Brahmā</s>, it circulates throughout the entire community of beings. Therefore it is called the <s>Brahmā</s>-wheel. Because he proclaims himself as one who has fallen into the foremost designation, endowed with the unsurpassed perfection of teachership, and because through the teaching of that path he refutes all other sectarian systems, and because when opponents of that path present themselves he does not shrink back, and because for the overcoming of all opposing doctrines he raises his noble and unsurpassed voice — he is said to 'rightly roar the lion's roar in the assembly.' In brief, however, the perfection of practice for one's own benefit, the perfection of practice for others' benefit, and the perfection of practice for both one's own and others' benefit — this uncommon [quality] is openly, clearly, designated, and illuminated [by him]. Another summary meaning: the goal to be attained, and the method for its attainment — and the accessibility of that method to everyone: 'Whoever desires it, whether god or human — all of them can obtain this method from me alone.' There, the noble, bull-like position should be seen as analogous to the curing of disease. The turning of the <s>Brahmā</s>-wheel should be seen as analogous to the method of curing disease. The rightly roaring of the lion's roar in the assembly should be seen as analogous to the refutation of all quack doctors' claims and the certain declaration of one's own ability to cure disease.

body.text: yāni karmāṇi kṛtānyupacitāni niruddhāni tānyatītānītyucyante / yāni naiva kṛtāni na niruddhāni nāpi karoti api tu kariṣyatyāyatyāṃ /
body.translated_text: Those actions that have been performed, accumulated, and ceased — those are called 'past.' Those that have neither been performed nor ceased, nor is one [presently] performing them, but will perform them in the future —

body.text: tānyanagatānītyucyante / yāni punaḥ karmāṇi naiva kṛtāni na niruddhānyapi tu kartumeva praṇihito vyavasitaḥ tāni pratyutpannānītyucyante / tāni punaḥprakārabhedena trīṇi kāyakarma vākkarma manaskarma / dharmasamādānāni catvāri yathāpūrvameva nirdiṣṭāni / asti dharmasamādānaṃ pratyutpannasukhamāyatyāṃ duḥkhavipākamiti vistareṇa / tāni punaretāni dṛṣṭadharmasamparāyahitāhitaprayogato yathāyogaṃ veditavyāni / yasmin deśe kriyante tatteṣāṃ sthānamityucyate / yacca sattvasaṃkhyātamasattvasaṃkhyātaṃ vā vastvādhiṣṭhāya kriyante tatteṣāṃ vastu ityucyate / yenākuśalamūlena [kuśalamūlena] vā nidānena kriyante / tatteṣāṃ heturityucyate / yadiṣṭāniṣṭamādīnavānuśaṃsaṃyuktaṃ phalamabhinivartayanti tatteṣāṃ vipāka ityucyate / tadetadabhisamasya sarvakālaṃ sarvaprakāraṃ sarvāvasthāprayogaṃ sarvadeśaṃ sarvādhiṣṭhānaṃ sarvanidānaṃ sarvādīnavānuśaṃsañca sarvākāraṃ tathāgatānāṃ karmajñānaṃ bhavati / nāsti vāta uttari nāto bhūyaḥ /
body.translated_text: those are called 'future.' And those actions that have neither been performed nor ceased, but toward which one is precisely resolved and committed to perform — those are called 'present.' Those, furthermore, by way of classification, are threefold: bodily action, verbal action, and mental action. The four <s>dharma</s>-undertakings are as previously described. There is a <s>dharma</s>-undertaking that is pleasant in the present but bears the fruit of suffering in the future, and so on in detail. Those, moreover, should be understood as relating to benefit and harm in the present life and the future, as appropriate. The place where they are performed — that is called their 'location.' Whatever entity — whether counted as a being or not counted as a being — is the basis upon which they are performed, that is called their 'object.' The unwholesome root or wholesome root that is the cause from which they are performed — that is called their 'cause.' Whatever fruit they produce — connected with the desirable or undesirable, with danger or benefit — that is called their 'ripening.' Having fully comprehended all this — at all times, in all modes, in all conditions of application, in all places, upon all bases, from all causes, and with all dangers and benefits — in all aspects, the <s>Tathāgatas</s>' knowledge of action (<s>karmajñāna</s>) comes about. There is nothing beyond this, nothing more.

body.text: catvāri dhyānāni / aṣṭau vimokṣāḥ / dhyānavimokṣaiḥ karmaṇyacetasaścetovaśiprāptasya yathepsitasyārthasya samṛddhaye yā tasya tadanurūpasya samādheḥ samāpadyanatā tā samādhisamāpattirityucyate / [yathocyate ca /] bhagavāṃstadrūpaṃ samādhi samāpannaṃ / yathā samāhite citte sarvo brahmalokaudāreṇāvabhāsena sphuṭo babhūva / bhāṣitasya cāsya śabdaḥ śrūyate / na cainaṃ kaścitpaścatīti vistaraḥ / evaṃ hi tathāgato yaṃ yamevārthaṃ prasādhayitukāmo lokasādhāraṇaṃ [asādhāraṇaṃ vā] sa tadrūpaṃ samādhiṃ samāpadya laghuladhveva prasādhayati / tatradhyānavimokṣābhyāṃ cittavaśitayā ca cittādhīna-sarvepsitārthasamṛddhiḥ etāvacca sarvadhyāyīnāṃ karaṇīyam / nāta uttari nāto bhūyaḥ / taccaitad dhyāyikaraṇīyaṃ [sarvākāraṃ] tathāgatānāṃ tasmād dhyānavimokṣasamādhisamāpattaya evocyante / eṣāṃ punardhyānādīnāṃ samāsato dvau saṃkleśau / aprāpteṣu caiṣu prāptaye bibandhasaṃkleśaḥ / tadyathā 'nupāyaprayogo nivaraṇānyatamasamudācāraśca / prāpteṣu caiṣu tadbhūmikaṃ kleśaparyavasthānamanuśayo vā / vyavadānaṃ punarvividhamevaitadviparyayeṇa
body.translated_text: The four <s>dhyānas</s> (meditative absorptions). The eight <s>vimokṣas</s> (liberations). For one whose mind has become workable through <s>dhyāna</s> and <s>vimokṣa</s> and who has attained mastery of mind, the ability to enter into a <s>samādhi</s> (concentration) appropriate for the accomplishment of whatever purpose he desires—that is called <s>samādhi</s>-attainment (<s>samādhisamāpatti</s>). [As it is said:] 'The <s>Bhagavān</s> entered such a <s>samādhi</s> that, when his mind was concentrated, the entire <s>Brahmā</s>-world became pervaded with magnificent radiance; and the sound of his speech was heard, yet no one could see him'—and so on in detail. For thus the <s>Tathāgata</s>, whatever purpose he wishes to accomplish, whether common to the world or uncommon, entering into the appropriate <s>samādhi</s>, accomplishes it easily and quickly. Therein, through <s>dhyāna</s> and <s>vimokṣa</s>, and through mastery of mind, the accomplishment of all desired purposes dependent on mind—this much is the task of all meditators; there is none higher, none beyond. And this task of meditators in all its aspects belongs to the <s>Tathāgatas</s>; therefore they are called <s>dhyāna</s>-<s>vimokṣa</s>-<s>samādhi</s>-<s>samāpattis</s>. Furthermore, there are, in brief, two defilements of these <s>dhyānas</s> and so forth: when they have not been attained, there is the defilement of bondage obstructing their attainment—namely, wrong practice and the occurrence of any of the hindrances (<s>nīvaraṇa</s>); when they have been attained, there is the obsession by defilements belonging to that level, or the latent tendencies (<s>anuśaya</s>). The purification, moreover, is to be understood as manifold, being the opposite of these,

body.text: veditavyam / teṣāmeva ca dhyānādīnāṃ vicitrāṇāmabhinirhṛtānāṃ nāmasaṃketena anurūpeṇa yathāyogaṃ vyavasthitirvyavasthānāmityucyate / eṣāmeva ca dhyānādīnāṃ pratilabdhānāmuttari yā bhāvanā-paripūrirnikāmalābhitā 'kṛcchreṇānavarakalābhitā saiṣāṃ viśuddhirityucyate / tatra yathā caiṣāmaprāptiryathā ca prāptiḥ teṣu ca yā ca hīnatā yā ca praṇītatā yaccaiṣāṃ nāma yā cotkarṣaparyantatā tat sarvaṃ prajānāti / tasmādevaṃ niruttaraṃ tathāgatānāṃ dhyānavimokṣasamādhisamāpattijñānabalamityucyante /
body.translated_text: The arrangement of the various <s>dhyānas</s> and so forth that have been brought forth, by appropriate name-conventions as is fitting, is called their establishment (<s>vyavasthāna</s>). The further cultivation-completion, the effortless attainment and the unobstructed attainment of the <s>dhyānas</s> and so forth that have been obtained—that is called their purification (<s>viśuddhi</s>). Therein, how they are not attained and how they are attained, what is inferior and what is excellent among them, what their names are, and what is the limit of their superiority—all that he fully knows. Therefore, thus unsurpassed, they are called the <s>Tathāgatas</s>' knowledge-power of <s>dhyāna</s>, <s>vimokṣa</s>, <s>samādhi</s>, and <s>samāpatti</s>.

body.text: yathā paripākasamudāgamataḥ śraddhādīnāṃ pañcānāmindriyāṇāṃ mṛdumadhyādhimātratā indriya-parāparatetyucyate /
body.translated_text: According to the attainment of ripening, the mildness, middlingness, and intensity of the five faculties (<s>indriya</s>) beginning with faith (<s>śraddhā</s>)—this is called the superiority and inferiority of faculties (<s>indriyaparāparatā</s>).

body.text: paraśraddhāpūrvā dharmavicāraṇā-pūrvā ca mṛdumadhyādhimātrā ruciḥ pratyavagamaḥ nānādhimuktikatetyucyate / nānāgotravyavasthānam / śrāvakapratyekabuddha-tathāgatagotrāṇāṃ rāgādicaritaprabhedanayena ca yāvadaśīti sattvacaritasahasrāṇi nānādhātukatetyucyate /
body.translated_text: Faith-preceded and <s>Dharma</s>-investigation-preceded mild, moderate, and intense inclination, understanding, and diversity of aspirations—this is called the diversity of aspirations (<s>nānādhimuktikā</s>). The establishment of diverse lineages (<s>gotra</s>)—of the <s>Śrāvaka</s>, <s>Pratyekabuddha</s>, and <s>Tathāgata</s> lineages, and by the method of classifying conduct by passion-temperament and so forth, up to eighty thousand types of being-conduct—this is called the diversity of dispositions (<s>nānādhātukā</s>).

body.text: teṣāmevāvatāra-mukhānurūpā pratipat tadyathā rāgacaritānāmaśubhā vistareṇa tadyathā śrāvakabhūmau sarvatragāminī pratipadityucyate / aparaḥ paryāyaḥ / sarvā pañcagatigāminī pratipatsarvatragāminītyucyate / aparaḥ paryāya / parasparaviruddheṣu nānāpakṣāśriteṣvanyonyarucidṛṣṭivipratyanīkavādiṣu pṛthagito bāhyakeṣu śramaṇabrāhmaṇeṣu yā pratipatsarvaprakārairihāmutrānavadyagāminītyucyate / tadyathā kāmasūtrādiṣu /
body.translated_text: The practice suited to their respective gateways of entry—for example, the contemplation of the impure (<s>aśubhā</s>) for those of passion-temperament, as described in detail in the <s>Śrāvakabhūmi</s>—is called the all-pervading path (<s>sarvatragāminī pratipat</s>). Another interpretation: all practice leading to the five destinies is called all-pervading. Another interpretation: among the various outside ascetics and <s>brāhmaṇas</s>, who are mutually opposed, of differing allegiances, adversaries of one another's inclinations and views—that practice which, in all modes, leads to the blameless in this world and the next—is called [all-pervading]; as in the <s>Kāmasūtra</s> and so forth.

body.text: vicitreṣu sattvanikāyeṣu tadyathā pūrveṣu dakṣiṇeṣu uttareṣu paścimeṣu nānā nāmasaṃketavyavasthānabhinneṣu aṣṭāsu vyavahārapadeṣvanugataṃ pūrvakeṣvabhyatītevātmabhāveṣu ṣaḍvidhaṃ samāsataścaritamanusmaratyanekavidhaṃ pūrvenivāse samanusmaran / aṣṭau vyavahārapadāni katamāni / evaṃ nāmā / evaṃ jātyaḥ / evaṃ gotraḥ / evamāhāraḥ / evaṃ sukhaduḥkhapratisaṃvedī / evaṃ dīrghāyuḥ / evaṃ cirasthitikaḥ / evamāyuḥ paryanta iti /
body.translated_text: In the diverse classes of beings—such as those in the eastern, southern, northern, and western [regions], distinguished by various name-conventions and designations—following the eight conventional terms, recollecting in brief six kinds of conduct in former, past self-existences in various ways, he recollects former abodes (<s>pūrvenivāsa</s>). What are the eight conventional terms? 'Of such a name'; 'of such a birth'; 'of such a clan'; 'of such food'; 'experiencing such happiness and suffering'; 'of such long life'; 'of such duration'; and 'of such life-span as the limit.'

body.text: ṣaḍvyavahārapadavyaritāni katamāni / āhvānāya saṃketaḥ kṣatriyādayo varṇā mātāpitaraṃ bhojanapānavidhiḥ sampattivipattiḥ āryurvaicitryañca / tathā hi loke etānyaṣṭau vyavahārapadāni upaniśritya ṣaṭ caritāni pareṣāmātmano vyapadiśanto vyapadiśanti / idaṃ me nāmāsyedaṃ nāmeti / kṣatriyo 'hamayaṃ vā / brāhmaṇo vaiśyaḥ śūdro 'hamayaṃ vā ayaṃ me pitā 'sya va / yathā pitā evaṃ mātā / evaṃ rūpamahamāhāramāharāmi / manthān vā apūpān vā odānakulmāṣān vā pare vā / evaṃ rūpe 'haṃ vyasane sampadi vā varte 'yaṃ vā / evaṃrūpe 'haṃ vayasi vyavasthito nave vā madhye vā vṛddhe vā / ayaṃ vā / ityetāni ṣaḍ[aṣṭa]vyavahāra padānugatāni caritāni bhavanti / nāsti cāta uttari vyavahārapadaṃ taccaritañca / tasmādetāvadevānusmarati / nāto bhūyaḥ / tatra vyavahāracaritāni ākāro vyavahārapadānyuddeśaḥ / tasya cānusmaraṇāt sākāraṃ soddeśamanusmaratītyucyate / tatra divyo vihāro dhyānānītyucyante / tadāśritatvāttasya cakṣuṣastatphalatvāttatparigṛhītatvāddivyañcakṣurityucyate / suparipūrṇa-pariśuddhadhyānaphalatvātsuviśuddhamityucyate / manuṣyāṇāmantato [nāma]vaidharmyādatikrāntamānuṣyakarmityucyate / asti ca kāmāvacarāṇāṃ devānāmupapatti-pratilambhikamapi tāvaddivyañcakṣustannāmasādṛśyānurti / manuṣyāṇāṃ punastadapi nāsti /
body.translated_text: What are the six conducts following the conventional terms? The convention for summoning, the classes beginning with <s>Kṣatriya</s>, mother and father, the manner of food and drink, fortune and misfortune, and the diversity of life-span.
