For in the world, relying on these eight conventional terms, people designate six conducts regarding others and themselves: 'This is my name, that is his name'; 'I am a <s>Kṣatriya</s>, or he is'; 'I am a <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>, a <s>Vaiśya</s>, a <s>Śūdra</s>, or he is'; 'This is my father, or his'; as with the father, so the mother; 'I eat such food—barley-gruel, cakes, rice, porridge, or other things—or others do'; 'I exist in such misfortune or fortune, or he does'; 'I am established in such an age—young, middle, or old—or he is.' These are the six conducts following the eight conventional terms. There is no conventional term beyond these, nor any conduct beyond them; therefore he recollects precisely this much, no more. Therein, the conducts and conventions are the aspect; the conventional terms are the heading. Because he recollects them, it is said he recollects 'with aspect and with heading.' Therein, the divine abiding is called the <s>dhyānas</s>. Because the eye depends on that, because it is its fruit, because it is encompassed by it—it is called the divine eye (<s>divyacakṣus</s>). Because it is the fruit of <s>dhyāna</s> well-completed and well-purified, it is called 'well-purified.' Because it surpasses the lowest [capacity] of humans even in name-differentiation, it is called 'surpassing human action.' Even the desire-realm gods have an innate divine eye at rebirth, which is called 'divine eye' by similarity of name; but humans do not even have that.

body.text: mriyamāṇāḥ sattvāḥ vyayamānā ityucyante / antarābhavasthā upapadyamānā ityucyante / dvābhyāmākārābhyāṃ tamaḥparāyaṇānāmayamevaṃrūpo manomayo 'ntarābhavo nirvartate / tadyathā kṛṣṇasyakutapasya nirbhāsaḥ andhakāratamisrāyā vā rātryāḥ / tasmād durvarṇā ityucyante / ye punardvābhyāmākārābhyāṃ jyotiḥ parāyaṇāsteṣāmayamevaṃrūpo manomayo 'ntarābhavo nirvartate / tadyathā jyotsnayā rātryā vārāṇaseyakasya vā sampannasya vastrasya / tasmātsuvarṇā ityucyante / tatra ye durvarṇāste hīnāḥ / ye survarṇāste praṇītāḥ / ye hīnāste durgatigāminaḥ / ye praṇītāste sugatigāminaḥ / sa samutthānayā śīlavipattyā kāyavāṅma noduścaritena samanvāgatā ityucyante / dvividhayā mithyādarśanadṛṣṭivipattyā samanvāgamāt
body.translated_text: Beings who are dying are said to be 'passing away' (<s>cyavamāna</s>). Those in the intermediate existence state are said to be 'being reborn' (<s>upapadyamāna</s>). For those destined for darkness, this mind-made intermediate existence arises in two aspects—like the appearance of a black woolen cloth, or like a dark, murky night; therefore they are said to be 'of ugly color' (<s>durvarṇa</s>). For those destined for light, this mind-made intermediate existence arises in two aspects—like a moonlit night, or like a fine cloth from <s>Vārāṇasī</s>; therefore they are said to be 'of beautiful color' (<s>suvarṇa</s>). Therein, those of ugly color are inferior; those of beautiful color are excellent. Those who are inferior go to bad destinies; those who are excellent go to good destinies. Those endowed with misconduct of body, speech, and mind arising from moral failure are said to be 'endowed with bodily, verbal, and mental misconduct.' Through being endowed with twofold wrong view and moral failure,

body.text: sarvāpavādikayā tanmatavipakṣāvasthitāryapavādikayā ca mithyādṛṣṭayaḥ āryāṇāmapavādakā ityucyante / tayā mithyādṛṣṭyā mithyāhetuñca phalañcābhiniveśate / tatastatpratyayaṃ mithyākarmābhisaṃskaroti / mithyākarmābhisaṃskurvan yadidaṃ dharmasamādānaṃ pratyutpannasukhamāyatyāṃ duḥkhavipākam / yat vā pratyutpannaduḥkhamāyatyāmapi duḥkhavipākaṃtatsamādatte / tasmānmithyādṛṣṭikarmadharmasamādānahetorityucyate / samanvāgatasyāpi tadanyairanekavidhaiḥ kuśalairdharmaistenaiva durgatigamanāttaddhetostatpratyayamityucyate / nāmarupānyonyaviśleṣāt kāyasya bheda ityucyate / sarvamaraṇānāṃ nihīnaparamatvāt asya parammaraṇādityucyate / narakāṇāṃ saṅkucitāvanatayā 'pāyadurgativinipātā ityucyante / svabhāvaśarīravastuvibhāvanatayā narakā ityucyante / tatrāpayānamityucyante / adharmacaryā viṣamacaryā ca tayā tatra yānaṃ bhavati / tasmādapāyā ityucyante / duḥkhasaṃsparśatvāddīrghakālika vicitra tīvranirantaraduḥkhopabhogasamudgatatvād durgataya ityucyante / adhobhāgāvasthitatvānmahāprapātabhūtatvāt kṛcchakaruṇadīnamahāvipralāpapralāpitvādvinipātā ityucyante / adhimātrasaṃvejakatvānnarakā evocyante / iti yena copapadyante upapannāśca yadupabhuñjate tadupabhogācca punaryadanyat svayaṃkṛtaṃ duḥkhāntaramabhinirvartayanti tadetadābhiḥ saṃjñābhiḥ paridīpitam / etadviparyayeṇa yathāyogaṃ sarvaśuklapakṣo veditavyaḥ / tatrāyaṃ viśeṣaḥ / sucaritapūrvā gatiḥ sugatirityucyate / sukhopabhogaparatvāt svargaloka ityucyate / sarvāsravāṇāmaśeṣānuśayaprahāṇādyattat prātipakṣikamanāsravaṃ cittamanāśravā prajñāparamādhiprajñasaṃgṛhītā āsravāṇāṃ kṣayādanāsravā cetovimuktiḥ prajñāvimuktirityucyate / tāṃ punaścetovimuktiṃ [prajñāvimukti] tasminneva carame bhave pratyātmaṃ ṣaṣṭhābhijñayā darśanamārgasanniśrayeṇa bhāvanāmārga-sanniśrayeṇa cādhigamya svañcādhigamaṃ yathāvatprajānanti / pareṣāṃ cākāṃkṣamāṇānāmārocayanti / tasmād dṛṣṭa eva dharme svayamabhijñayā sākṣātkṛtvopasaṃpadya
body.translated_text: namely, the all-denying [view] and the [view] that denounces the Noble Ones while being established in the contrary position—these wrong views are said to be 'denouncing the Noble Ones.' Through that wrong view, one clings to wrong causes and wrong fruits. Thereby one performs wrong <s>karma</s> conditioned by that. Performing wrong <s>karma</s>—namely, that undertaking of <s>dharmas</s> which is pleasant in the present but has suffering as its future ripening, or that which is painful in the present and also has suffering as its future ripening—one undertakes that. Therefore it is said 'on account of wrong view and <s>karma</s> and <s>dharma</s>-undertaking.' Even though one may be endowed with various other wholesome <s>dharmas</s>, by going to a bad destiny through that very [wrong view], it is said 'on account of that, conditioned by that.' Through the mutual separation of name and form, there is 'the breaking up of the body.' Because it is the lowest of all deaths, it is said 'after death.' Because the hells are contracted and bent down, they are called 'bad destiny, evil course, and downfall' (<s>apāya</s>, <s>durgati</s>, <s>vinipāta</s>). Because one's own natural body and substance are made manifest [in suffering], they are called 'hells' (<s>naraka</s>). They are called 'bad destinations' (<s>apāya</s>) because unrighteous conduct and uneven conduct serve as the vehicle going there. They are called 'evil courses' (<s>durgati</s>) because of painful contact and because they arise with long-lasting, diverse, intense, and uninterrupted experience of suffering. They are called 'downfalls' (<s>vinipāta</s>) because they are situated in the lower regions, because they are great precipices, because one there utters pitiable, wretched, and great lamentations. They are called 'hells' (<s>naraka</s>) specifically because they cause the most intense spiritual urgency. Thus, that by which one is reborn, what one experiences once reborn, and the further suffering one produces through one's own deeds from that experience—all this is illuminated by these designations. By the opposite of this, as appropriate, the entire wholesome side is to be understood. Therein is this distinction: a destiny preceded by good conduct is called a 'good destiny' (<s>sugati</s>). Because of the predominance of pleasant experience, it is called 'the heavenly world' (<s>svargaloka</s>). Through the complete abandonment of all latent tendencies of all <s>āsravas</s> (defilements), that counteractive undefiled mind and undefiled wisdom, encompassed by the supreme higher wisdom, through the destruction of the <s>āsravas</s>—[this] is called 'undefiled liberation of mind' (<s>cetovimukti</s>) and 'liberation through wisdom' (<s>prajñāvimukti</s>). And that liberation of mind and liberation through wisdom, in that very final existence, realizing personally through the sixth <s>abhijñā</s> (superknowledge), relying on the path of seeing and the path of cultivation, they fully know their own realization as it truly is; and to others who wish to know, they declare it. Therefore they are said to 'declare it, having realized it personally through direct knowledge in this very life, having entered upon and abided in it.'

body.text: pravedayantītyucyante / kṣīṇāṃ me jātirityevamādīnāṃ padānāṃ nānākaraṇaṃ veditavyam / tadyathā paryāyasaṃgrahanyām /
body.translated_text: The differentiation of the terms 'Birth is destroyed for me' and so forth is to be understood as in the <s>Paryāyasaṃgrahaṇī</s>.

body.text: uddānam /
body.translated_text: <s>Uddāna</s> (Summary Verse):

children.translated_text: Own-nature and division, exclusivity and equality likewise,
function-and-action, sequence, and distinction—the last should be.

body.text: eṣāṃ punardaśānāṃ tathāgatabalānāṃ svabhāvo veditavyaḥ / prabhedo veditavyaḥ / kaivalyaṃ veditavyam / samatā veditavyā / karmakriyā veditavyā / anukramo veditavyaḥ / viśeṣo veditavyaḥ / ityebhiḥ saptabhirākāraiḥ samāsato daśa tathāgatabalāni veditavyāni /
body.translated_text: The own-nature of these ten powers of the <s>Tathāgata</s> is to be known; their division is to be known; their exclusivity is to be known; their equality is to be known; their function-and-action is to be known; their sequence is to be known; and their distinction is to be known. By these seven aspects, in brief, the ten powers of the <s>Tathāgata</s> are to be understood.

body.text: tatra [katama] eṣāṃ svabhāvaḥ / pañcendriyasvabhāvānyenāti / api tu prajñāyāḥ prādhānyātprajñāsvabhāvānītyucyante / tathā hyucyate / sthānāsthānajñānabalaṃ na tu śraddhābalaṃ vā tadanyadvā balamityucyate / yathā sthānāsthānajñānabalamevamavaśiṣṭāni draṣṭavyāni / tatra ka eṣāṃ prabhedaḥ / samāsatasrividhena prabhedenaiṣāmapramāṇatā veditavyā / kālaprabhedenātītānāgatavartamānādhvapatitasarvajñeyapraveśāt / prakāraprabhedenaikaikasya saṃskṛtasya vastunaḥ svalakṣaṇasāmānyalakṣaṇasarvākārapraveśāt / santānaprabhedena daśasu dikṣu sarvasattvadhātupratyekasarvasantānasarvārthānupraveśāt / evamebhistribhiḥ prabhedaireṣāṃ daśānāṃ tathāgatabalānāmaprameyatā veditavyā / ayameṣāṃ prabhedaḥ / tatra kaivalyameṣāṃ katamat / tathāgatasyaiva etāni daśabalāni kevalānyāveṇikāni / na tu sarvaśrāvakapratyekabuddhānām / idameṣāṃ kaivalyamityucyate / sarvatathāgatānāṃ caitāni balāni samāni nirviśiṣṭāni / iyameṣāṃ samatā vihāraviśeṣastu tathāgatānāmanyonyaṃ bhavedanyena balavihāreṇa anyastathāgatastadvahulavihārī bhavati / anyenānyaḥ /
body.translated_text: There, what is their intrinsic nature? They are of the nature of the five faculties (<s>indriya</s>). However, because of the predominance of wisdom (<s>prajñā</s>), they are called 'of the nature of wisdom.' For thus it is said: 'The power of knowledge of the possible and impossible (<s>sthānāsthānajñānabala</s>)'—it is not called 'the power of faith' or any other power. As with the power of knowledge of the possible and impossible, so the remaining [powers] should be seen. There, what is their differentiation? In summary, their immeasurability should be understood through a threefold differentiation. Through the differentiation of time—because of penetrating all that is knowable falling within the past, future, and present periods. Through the differentiation of mode—because of penetrating all aspects, both the particular characteristics and the general characteristics, of each single conditioned entity. Through the differentiation of continuum—because of penetrating all purposes in each and every continuum of all the realms of beings in the ten directions. Thus, through these three differentiations, the immeasurability of these ten powers of the <s>Tathāgata</s> should be understood. This is their differentiation. There, what is their exclusiveness? These ten powers belong exclusively to the <s>Tathāgata</s> alone—they are exclusive and unshared. They do not belong to any <s>Śrāvakas</s> or <s>Pratyekabuddhas</s>. This is called their exclusiveness. And these powers are equal and undifferentiated among all <s>Tathāgatas</s>. This is their equality. However, there may be a distinction in the abiding of <s>Tathāgatas</s> among themselves: one <s>Tathāgata</s> may abide predominantly in one power, and another in another.

body.text: eṣāṃ daśānāṃ balānāṃ tathāgataḥ kena kiṃ karmaṃ karoti / sthānāsthānajñānabalena tathāgataḥ hetuñca hetutaḥ phalañca phalato yathābhūtaṃ prajānāti / ahetuviṣamahetuvādinaśca
body.translated_text: Of these ten powers, what function does the <s>Tathāgata</s> perform with which [power]? Through the power of knowledge of the possible and impossible (<s>sthānāsthānajñānabala</s>), the <s>Tathāgata</s> truly knows causes as causes and fruits as fruits, as they really are. And he subdues those <s>śramaṇas</s> and <s>brāhmaṇas</s> who propound no cause or unequal cause.

body.text: śramaṇa-brāhmaṇān nigṛhṇāti / karmasvakatājñānabalena tathāgataḥ svayaṃkṛta-phalopabhogatāñca karmaṇāṃ yathābhūtaṃ prajānāti / dānapuṇyakriyāsaṃkrāntivādinaśca śramaṇabrāhmaṇān nigṛhṇāti / dhyānavimokṣasamādhisamāpattijñānabalena tathāgatasribhiśca prātihāryairvineyān samyagavavadati / prativirodhavipakṣapratyanīkavādāvasthitāṃśca śramaṇabrāhmaṇān nigṛhṇāti / indriyaparāparajñānabalena tathāgataḥ sattvānāmindriyamṛdumadhyādhimātratāñca vibhajya yathābhūtaṃ prajānāti / teṣāñca yathārhaṃ yathāyogaṃ dharmadeśanāṃ karoti / nānādhimuktijñānabalena tathāgato mṛdumadhyādhimātra-śubhāśubhādhimuktitāṃ yathābhūtaṃ prajānāti / śubhāñcādhimuktimanubṛṃhayati / aśubhāñca tyājayati / nānādhātujñānabalena tathāgato hīnamadhyepraṇotadhātukatāśca vibhajya yathābhūtaṃ prajānāti / yathendriyān yathāṣayān yathānuśayāṃśca sattvāṃsteṣu teṣvavatāramukheṣvavavādakriyayā samyagyathāyogaṃ saṃniyojayati / tatra yathā tathāgatāḥ śrāvakāṇāṃ teṣu teṣvavatāramukheṣvavavādamanuprayacchanti tathāśrāvakabhūmau sarveṇa sarvaṃ nirantaramākhyātamuttānaṃ vivṛtaṃ prajñaptaṃ prakāśitam / kathañca punastathāgatā bodhisattvamādikarmikaṃ tatprathamakarmikaṃ samādhisambhāraparigrahe 'vasthitañcittasthitikāmaṃ cittasthitaye 'vavadanti / iha tathāgato bodhisattvāsataṃ samādhisambhāragurukamādikarmikaṃ tatprathamakarmikaṃ tatprathamataḥ evamavavadati / ehi tvaṃ kulaputra praviviktaśayanāsanagata ekākī advitīyo yatte mātāpitṛbhyāṃ nāma vyavasthāpitamācāryopādhyāyābhyāṃ vā tadeva nāmādhyātmaṃ manasikuru / evañca punarmanasikuru-asti me [sa] kaścitṣaḍāyatanavinirmukto dharmaḥ svabhāvena pariniṣpannaḥ adhyātmaṃ vā bahirdhā vā ubhayamantareṇa vā vidyate / yatredaṃ nāma
body.translated_text: Through the power of knowledge of the ownership of actions (<s>karmasvakatājñānabala</s>), the <s>Tathāgata</s> truly knows that the fruits to be experienced are those produced by one's own actions. And he subdues those <s>śramaṇas</s> and <s>brāhmaṇas</s> who propound the transference [of merit] from the meritorious actions of giving. Through the power of knowledge of <s>dhyānas</s>, liberations, concentrations, and attainments (<s>dhyānavimokṣasamādhisamāpattijñānabala</s>), the <s>Tathāgata</s> properly instructs those to be trained through the three miracles (<s>prātihārya</s>). And he subdues those <s>śramaṇas</s> and <s>brāhmaṇas</s> who are established in positions of opposition, contradiction, and antagonism. Through the power of knowledge of the superior and inferior faculties (<s>indriyaparāparajñānabala</s>), the <s>Tathāgata</s> truly knows, having distinguished, the mild, middling, and intense [nature of] the faculties of beings. And he gives <s>Dharma</s>-teaching to them as appropriate and fitting. Through the power of knowledge of the diverse inclinations (<s>nānādhimuktijñānabala</s>), the <s>Tathāgata</s> truly knows the mild, middling, and intense nature of wholesome and unwholesome inclinations. He strengthens the wholesome inclinations and causes the abandonment of the unwholesome ones. Through the power of knowledge of the diverse dispositions (<s>nānādhātujñānabala</s>), the <s>Tathāgata</s> truly knows, having distinguished, the inferior, middling, and superior natures of the dispositions. He properly yokes beings, according to their faculties, inclinations, and latent tendencies, to the respective entry-points through the activity of instruction. There, just as <s>Tathāgatas</s> give instruction to <s>Śrāvakas</s> at the respective entry-points, so in the <s>Śrāvakabhūmi</s> it has been completely, without remainder, and in an accessible manner declared, explained, designated, and illuminated. And how do <s>Tathāgatas</s> instruct a <s>Bodhisattva</s> who is a beginner, newly entered, established in the gathering of the requisites for concentration (<s>samādhisambhāra</s>), desiring stability of mind, for the purpose of mental stability? Here, the <s>Tathāgata</s> instructs the <s>Bodhisattva</s> who is a beginner, newly entered, for whom the gathering of requisites for concentration is of paramount importance, as follows: 'Come, son of good family, go to a secluded dwelling-place; alone, without a companion; whatever name has been established for you by your parents, or by your preceptor and teacher—attend to that very name internally. And further attend to it thus: Is there any <s>dharma</s> of mine, existing by its own nature as something fully established, separate from the six sense-bases (<s>ṣaḍāyatana</s>)—whether internal, external, or between both—where this name,

body.text: saṃjñā prajñaptiḥ upacāraḥ pravartate sa tvamevaṃ yoniśo manasikurvaṃstaṃ dharmaṃ nopalapsyase / nānyatra te evaṃ bhaviṣyati / āgantukeṣveṣu dharmeṣviyamāgantukī saṃjñāpravṛtteti / yadā ca te kulaputra tasmin svanāmni āgantukasaṃjñā utpānna bhavati pratilabdhā sa tvaṃ yā te cakṣuṣi cakṣurnāma cakṣuḥsaṃjñā cakṣuḥ-prajñaptistāmadhyātmaṃ yoniśomanasikuru / evañca punarmanasikuru / asmiñcakṣuṣi dvayamupalabhyate / idaṃ ca nāma saṃjñā prajñaptiścakṣuriti / etacca vastumātram / yatredaṃ nāma saṃjñā prajñaptiḥ / nāta uttari nāto bhūyaḥ / tatra yaccakṣuṣi nāma saṃjñā prajñaptistattāvanna cakṣuḥ / yadapi tadvastu yatra cakṣuḥsaṃjñā tadapi svabhāvato na cakṣuḥ / tatkasya hetoḥ / na hi tatra cakṣurnāma cakṣuḥsaṃjñāṃ cakṣuḥprajñaptiṃ vinā kasyacit cakṣurbuddhiḥ pravartate / sa cedetadvastu tenātmanā pariniṣpannaṃ syāt / yena nāmnā 'bhilapyate na tatra punastadapekṣā cakṣurityevaṃ buddhiḥ pravartate / nānyatra prakṛtyaivāśruto 'parikalpita-nāmakānāmapi tasmin vastuni cakṣuriti buddhiḥ pravartate / na ca punaḥ pravartamānā upalabhyate tasmādidamapi cakṣurnāma cakṣuḥsaṃjñā cakṣuḥprajñaptiḥ āgantuke dharme saṃjñā āgantukī / evaṃ te 'dhyātmametaccakṣuryoniśo manasikurvataścakṣuḥsaṃjñāyāmapyāgantukasaṃjñā utpannā bhaviṣyati pratilabdhā / yathā cakṣuṣyevaṃ śrotraghrāṇajihvākāyeṣu vistareṇa yāvaddṛṣṭaśrutamatavijñāteṣu prāpteṣu paryeṣiteṣu manasā 'nuvitarkiteṣvanuvicāriteṣu samāsataḥ sarvadharmasaṃjñāsvāgantukasaṃjñā utpannā bhaviṣyati pratilabdhā / evaṃ [te] svātmani yā saṃjñā [avasthā] tasyā vibhavāya prayogamārgaḥ samyak parigṛhīto bhaviṣyati / vistareṇa yāvatsarvadharmeṣu yā saṃjñā tasyā vibhavāya prayogamārgaḥ samyak parigṛhīto bhaviṣyati / sa tvamevaṃ sarvajñeya-suvicāritayā buddhyā evaṃ te sarvadharmasaṃjñāsvāgantukasaṃjñayā sarvadharmeṣu sarvaprapañcasaṃjñāmapanīyāpanīya nirvikāreṇa cetasā nirnimittenārthamātragrahaṇapravṛttenāsmin vastuni bahalaṃ vihara / [evaṃ te] tathāgatajñāna-viśuddhisamādhigotrāccittasyaikāgratā pratilabdhā bhaviṣyati / sa tvaṃ sacedaśubhāṃ manasikaroṣi enaṃ manasikāraṃ mā riñciṣyasi / sa cenmaitrī midaṃpratyayatā pratītyasamutpādaṃ dhātuprabhedamānāpānasmṛtiṃ prathamaṃ dhyānaṃ vistareṇa yāvannaivasaṃjñānāsaṃjñāyanamapramāṇa-bodhisattva dhyānābhijñā-samādhisamāpattīrmanasikaroṣi / etameva manasikāraṃ mā riñciṣyasi / evaṃ te 'yaṃ bodhisattva manaskāro 'nupūrveṇa yāvadanuttarāyai samyaksambodhaye niryāsyatīti / iyaṃ sarvatragāminī bodhisattvānāṃ pratipadveditavyā / atīte 'pyadhvani tathāgatā
body.translated_text: conception, designation, and convention operates? You, attending properly in this way, will not find that <s>dharma</s>. And nothing else will occur to you except this: In these adventitious <s>dharmas</s>, this adventitious conception operates. And when, son of good family, the adventitious conception regarding your own name has arisen in you and been obtained—then you should attend internally and properly to whatever perception of the eye as 'eye,' whatever eye-conception, whatever eye-designation, in your eye. And further attend to it thus: In this eye, two things are found—this name, conception, and designation 'eye,' and this mere entity where the name, conception, and designation [operates]. There is nothing beyond this, nothing more. There, what is the name, conception, and designation in the eye—that much is not the eye. And that entity where the eye-conception [occurs]—that too is not the eye by its own nature. For what reason? For in that [entity], no one's eye-awareness operates without the name 'eye,' the eye-conception, and the eye-designation. And if that entity were established by that very nature by which it is designated verbally, then eye-awareness would operate without reference to that, thinking merely 'eye.' But apart from that, even for one who is unlearned and for whom names have not been constructed, eye-awareness does not operate regarding that entity. And even when it does operate, it is not found [to have independent existence]. Therefore, this too—the name 'eye,' the eye-conception, the eye-designation—is an adventitious conception in an adventitious <s>dharma</s>. Thus, as you attend properly and internally to this eye, the adventitious conception regarding the eye-perception too will arise and be obtained. Just as with the eye, so with the ear, nose, tongue, body—in detail up to what is seen, heard, thought, and cognized, what is obtained, sought, and mentally examined and investigated—in summary, the adventitious conception regarding all perceptions of all <s>dharmas</s> will arise and be obtained. Thus, the preparatory path for the disappearance of the conception regarding your own self will be properly grasped. In detail, up to the preparatory path for the disappearance of the conception regarding all <s>dharmas</s> will be properly grasped. And you, with a mind well-examined regarding all that is knowable, with this adventitious conception regarding all <s>dharmas</s>—having removed and removed the conception of all conceptual proliferation regarding all <s>dharmas</s>—with an unperturbed mind, signless, operating with the mere apprehension of the entity—abide abundantly in this entity. Thus, stability of mind, belonging to the <s>Tathāgata</s>'s knowledge-purification-concentration lineage, will be obtained by you. And if you attend to the impure (<s>aśubha</s>), do not abandon this [previous] mental attention. And if you attend to loving-kindness (<s>maitrī</s>), conditionality (<s>idaṃpratyayatā</s>), dependent origination (<s>pratītyasamutpāda</s>), the analysis of elements (<s>dhātuprabhedaḥ</s>), mindfulness of breathing (<s>ānāpānasmṛti</s>), the first <s>dhyāna</s>, in detail up to the sphere of neither perception nor non-perception, the immeasurable <s>Bodhisattva</s> <s>dhyānas</s>, superknowledges, concentrations, and attainments—do not abandon this very mental attention. Thus, this <s>Bodhisattva</s> mental attention of yours will, in due course, lead to the unsurpassed, perfect awakening.' This should be understood as the universal path for <s>Bodhisattvas</s>. In the past period too, <s>Tathāgatas</s>

body.text: bodhisattvamādikarmakamevamevāvavaditavantaḥ / anāgate 'pyadhvanyevamevavadiṣyanti / pratyutpanne 'pyadhvanyevamevavadanti / śrāvako 'pi cānena manaskāreṇa prayujyamānaḥ kṣiprābhijñataraḥ syād dharmābhisamayāya yadi śaknuyādetaṃ manasikāraṃ yathāvatprativeddhum / sarvatrāgaminī pratipat jñānabalena tathāgataḥ sarvaduḥkha-nairyāṇikīmanairyāṇikīṃ ca pratipadaṃ yathābhūtaṃ prajānāti / anairyāṇikīṃ ca pratipadaṃ varjayitvā nairyāṇikīmupasaṃharati / pūrve nivāsānusmṛtijñānabalena tathāgataḥ pūrvānte itivṛttakāṃśca jātakāṃśca smṛtvā cittasaṃvegāya cittaprasādāya vineyānāṃ deśayati / śāśvatavādinaśca śramaṇabrāhmaṇān nigṛhṇāti / cyutyupapādajñānabalena tathāgataḥ śrāvakaṃ cābhyatītakālagatamupapattau vyākaroti / ucchedavādinaśca śramaṇabrāhmaṇān nigṛhṇāti / āsravakṣayajñānabalena tathāgataḥ sve ca vimokṣe niṣkāṃkṣo bhavati nirvicikitsaḥ / arhattvābhimāninaśca śramaṇabrāhmaṇān nigṛhṇāti / idaṃ tāvattathāgatasya daśānāṃ [balānāṃ] karma veditavyam /
body.translated_text: have instructed beginner <s>Bodhisattvas</s> in just this way. In the future period too, they will instruct in just this way. In the present period too, they instruct in just this way. Even a <s>Śrāvaka</s>, when applying himself with this mental attention, would be quicker in higher knowledge for the comprehension of the <s>Dharma</s>—if he is able to properly penetrate this mental attention. Through the power of knowledge of the path leading everywhere (<s>sarvatragāminī pratipaj jñānabala</s>), the <s>Tathāgata</s> truly knows the path leading out of all suffering and the path that does not lead out. And avoiding the path that does not lead out, he provides the one that leads out. Through the power of knowledge of the recollection of former abodes (<s>pūrvenivāsānusmṛtijñānabala</s>), the <s>Tathāgata</s>, recollecting events and birth-stories (<s>jātakas</s>) of former times, teaches them to those to be trained for the purpose of generating spiritual urgency and faith. And he subdues those <s>śramaṇas</s> and <s>brāhmaṇas</s> who propound eternalism. Through the power of knowledge of death-and-rebirth (<s>cyutyupapādajñānabala</s>), the <s>Tathāgata</s> predicts the future rebirth of <s>Śrāvakas</s> who have passed into the past. And he subdues those <s>śramaṇas</s> and <s>brāhmaṇas</s> who propound annihilationism. Through the power of knowledge of the exhaustion of the defilements (<s>āsravakṣayajñānabala</s>), the <s>Tathāgata</s> is himself free from doubt and uncertainty regarding his own liberation. And he subdues those <s>śramaṇas</s> and <s>brāhmaṇas</s> who presumptuously claim the status of <s>Arhat</s>. This much should be understood as the function of the <s>Tathāgata</s>'s ten powers.

body.text: tatra ka eṣāṃ daśānāṃ tathāgatabalānāmanukramaḥ / sahābhisaṃbodhādanuttarāyāḥ samyaksaṃbodhestathāgataḥ sarvāṇyeva daśa balāni sakṛtpratilabhate / sakṛtpratilabdhānāṃ punareṣāṃ krameṇa sammukhībhāvo bhavati / abhisaṃbuddhamātra eva tathāgato dharmāṇāṃ samyageva hetuphalavyavasthānaṃ sthānāsthānajñāgabalena vyavalokayati / vyavalokya kāmadhātāveva sabhāge dhātāviṣṭaphala-viśeṣārthikānāṃ karmasvakatā-jñānabalenākuśalakarmaparivarjanāṃ kuśalakarmasamudācāratāñca vyapadiśati / laukika-vairāgyakāmānāṃ punaḥ sattvānāṃ dhyānavimokṣasamādhisamāpattijñānabalena laukikavairāgyagamanāya yathāvanmārgapratilābhāyāvavādamanuprayacchati / lokottaravairāgyakāmānāṃ punastadanyaiḥ saptabhisthāgatabalairlokottaravairāgyopagamāya mārgaṃ vyapadiśati / tatra pūrvaṃ tāvallottaravairāgyakāmānāmindriyaṃ vyavalokayatīndriyaparāparajñānabalena / tata indriyapūrvamāśayaṃ vyavalokayati nānādhimuktijñānabalena / tataścāśayapūrvamanuśayaṃ vyavalokayati nānādhātujñānabalena / sa evamindriyāśayānuśayajñaḥ yathāyogamālambanāvatāramukheṣvavatārayati sarvatragāminī pratipaj-jñānabalena / tataścānurūpeṇālambanāvatāramukhaprayogena cittasthitiñca grāhayitvā
body.translated_text: There, what is the sequence of these ten powers of the <s>Tathāgata</s>? Simultaneously with the awakening to the unsurpassed, perfect awakening, the <s>Tathāgata</s> obtains all ten powers at once. But once obtained, their becoming proximate occurs in sequence. Immediately upon full awakening, the <s>Tathāgata</s>, through the power of knowledge of the possible and impossible, surveys the proper establishment of cause and fruit among <s>dharmas</s>. Having surveyed, through the power of knowledge of the ownership of actions, he prescribes for those in the desire realm who desire the fruits of their own actions the avoidance of unwholesome actions and the practice of wholesome actions. For those beings who desire mundane dispassion, through the power of knowledge of <s>dhyānas</s>, liberations, concentrations, and attainments, he provides instruction as appropriate for attaining the path leading to mundane dispassion. For those beings who desire supramundane dispassion, through the remaining seven powers of the <s>Tathāgata</s>, he points out the path to the attainment of supramundane dispassion. There, first, he surveys the faculties of those who desire supramundane dispassion through the power of knowledge of the superior and inferior faculties. Then, preceded by [knowledge of] the faculties, he surveys the inclinations through the power of knowledge of the diverse inclinations. Then, preceded by the inclinations, he surveys the latent tendencies through the power of knowledge of the diverse dispositions. Thus knowing the faculties, inclinations, and latent tendencies, he brings [beings] into the appropriate object-entry-points as fitting, through the power of knowledge of the path leading everywhere. Then, through the appropriate practice of the object-entry-point, having caused stability of mind

body.text: caritāni ca viśodhayitvā satkāyadṛṣṭimūla-śvāśatocchedāntagrāhavivarjitāṃ madhyamāṃ pratipadaṃ vyapadiśati sarvakleśaprahāṇāya pūrvenivāsānusmṛtijñānabalena cyutyupapattijñānabalena ca / tata evaṃ samyak prayuktaḥ śamathopastabdho aprahīṇakleśasamudācārayogākṛte kṛtābhimānināmabhimānaṃ tyājayati āsravakṣayajñānabalena / ayaṃ tāvadeko balānāmanukramaparyāyaḥ /
body.translated_text: and having purified conduct, he points out the middle path—free from the extremes of grasping at eternalism and annihilationism rooted in the view of the personal self (<s>satkāyadṛṣṭi</s>)—for the abandonment of all afflictions, through the power of knowledge of the recollection of former abodes and through the power of knowledge of death-and-rebirth. Then, for one thus properly engaged and supported by calm (<s>śamatha</s>), he causes the abandonment of the presumptuous conceit of those who have not abandoned the occurrence of afflictions yet presume themselves to have done so, through the power of knowledge of the exhaustion of the defilements. This is one sequential mode of the powers.

body.text: aparaḥ paryāyaḥ / iha tathāgato 'nuttarāṃ samyaksambodhibhisaṃbudhya tatprathamataḥ sthānāsthānajñānabalaṃ sammukhīkṛtya pratītyasamutpanneṣu dharmeṣu paramaṃ dharmasthitijñānaṃ vyavacārayati / tacca dharmasthitijñānaṃ niḥśritya karmasvakatājñānabalena gṛhipakṣaṃ vyavalokayati yena yena karmaṇā vicitreṇa teṣāṃ gṛhipakṣāśritānāṃ samudāgamo 'bhūdbhaviṣyati vidyate [ca] / gṛhipakṣaṃ vyavalokya dhyānavimokṣa-samādhisamāpattijñānabalena pravrajitapakṣaṃ vyavalokayati / kimastyasmin kaścid pravrajitapakṣe duḥkhānniḥsṛto duḥkhān niḥsaraṇāya ca mārgasya deśayitā / āhośvit nāstīti / sa nāstīti avagamya nisrāṇamaśaraṇaṃ sarvaṃ lokamavekṣya mahākaruṇāmupādāya buddhacakṣuṣā lokaṃ vyavalokayati / sa vyavalokayannindriyaparāparajñānaṃ sammukhīkṛtya prajānāti / santi sattvā loke jātā [loke] vṛddhā mṛdvindriyā api madhyendriyā api tīkṣṇendriyā apīti / [iti] viditvāsya dharmadeśanāyāṃ cittaṃ krāmati / tataḥ pūrvavatsarvānukramo nānādhimuktyādikānāṃ tadanyeṣāṃ balānāṃ veditavyaḥ / ayaṃ dvitīyo balānāmanukramaparyāyaḥ /
body.translated_text: Another way of ordering: Here, the <s>Tathāgata</s>, having fully awakened to unsurpassed perfect awakening, first of all, bringing forward the power of knowledge of what is possible and impossible (<s>sthānāsthānajñānabala</s>), applies the supreme knowledge of the establishment of <s>dharmas</s> (<s>dharmasthitijñāna</s>) to dependently arisen <s>dharmas</s>. And relying on that knowledge of <s>dharma</s>-establishment, with the power of knowledge of the ownership of <s>karma</s> (<s>karmasvakatājñānabala</s>), one surveys the householder side — by whatever varied <s>karma</s> the arising of those relying on the householder side occurred, will occur, and does occur. Having surveyed the householder side, with the power of knowledge of <s>dhyāna</s>, liberations, concentrations, and attainments (<s>dhyānavimokṣasamādhisamāpattijñānabala</s>), one surveys the renunciant side: 'Is there anyone in this renunciant side who has emerged from suffering and who teaches the path for emergence from suffering? Or is there not?' Having understood that there is not, surveying the entire world as without escape and without refuge, taking up great compassion, one surveys the world with the <s>Buddha</s>-eye. Surveying thus, bringing forward the power of knowledge of the higher and lower [capacities of] faculties (<s>indriyaparāparajñāna</s>), one knows: 'There are beings born in the world, matured in the world — some of mild faculties, some of middling faculties, some of sharp faculties.' Having known this, one's mind turns to the teaching of <s>Dharma</s>. Then, as before, the entire sequence of the remaining powers — regarding diverse inclinations and the like — should be understood. This is the second way of ordering the powers.

body.text: aparaḥ paryāyaḥ / pūrvaṃ tāvattathāgato 'bhisaṃbudhyamātra eva sthānāsthānajñānabalena pratītyasamutpannaṃ dharmadhātuṃ vicārayati / tataḥ karmasvakajñānabalena yeṣu pratītatyasamutpanneṣu dharmeṣu sattvasaṃjñātaṃ sattvadhātuṃ vicārayati / amī sattvā evaṃ rūpasya svayaṃkṛtasya karmaṇa evaṃ rūpaṃ phalaṃ pratyanubhavantīti / dharmadhātuṃ [sattvadhātuṃ] ca yathāvadvyavacārayitvā dhyānavimokṣasamādhisamāpattijñānabalena tāneva sattvān duḥkhavimokṣāya samyak tribhiḥ prātihāryairavavadati / avavadan pūrvaṃvadananukrameṇāvaśiṣṭairvalairindriyādīni jñātvā mārge cāvatārayitvā tān sattvān duḥkhādvimocayati / ayaṃ tṛtīyo balānāma nukramaparyāyaḥ /
body.translated_text: Another way of ordering: First, the <s>Tathāgata</s>, immediately upon awakening, investigates the dependently arisen <s>dharmadhātu</s> (realm of <s>dharmas</s>) with the power of knowledge of what is possible and impossible. Then, with the power of knowledge of the ownership of <s>karma</s>, one investigates the realm of beings (<s>sattvadhātu</s>), which is designated as 'beings' among those dependently arisen <s>dharmas</s> — [knowing:] 'These beings experience such-and-such fruit of such-and-such self-created <s>karma</s>.' And having properly investigated the <s>dharmadhātu</s> and the <s>sattvadhātu</s> as they truly are, with the power of knowledge of <s>dhyāna</s>, liberations, concentrations, and attainments, one properly instructs those very beings for liberation from suffering through the three miracles. While instructing, as before, in sequence with the remaining powers, having known their faculties and the like and having guided them onto the path, one liberates those beings from suffering. This is the third way of ordering the powers.

body.text: tatra sthānāsthānajñānavalasya karmasvakajñānabalasya ca ko viśeṣaḥ / yatkuśalākuśalasya karmaṇa iṣṭāniṣṭaphalaṃ nirvartate idaṃ sthānāsthānajñānabalāt / yatpunarya eva kuśalākuśalaṃ karma karoti sa eva tadiṣṭāniṣṭaphalaṃ pratyanubhavati / idaṃ karmasvakajñānabalāt / yattāvadya eva dhyānavimokṣādīnāṃ samāpattyā tasyaiva te bhavanti / nānyasya / idaṃ karmasvakajñānabalāt / yatpunastāneva dhyānādīnāśritya vineyāṃsribhiḥ prātihāryairavavadati / idaṃ dhyānavimokṣa[samādhi]samāpattijñānabalāt / yat tāvacchraddhā-disahajena saṃprayuktaṃ cittaṃ pragṛhṇāti / idaṃ dhyānavimokṣasamādhisamāpattijñānabalāt / yatpunastānyevendriyāṇi mṛdumadhyādhimātrādiprabhedena vibhajati / idamindriyaparāparajñānabalāt / yattāvadindriyapūrva teṣu teṣu dharmeṣvāśayaṃ gṛhṇāti / idamindriyaparāparajñānabalāt / yatpunastamevāśayaṃ nānā vibhajati idaṃ nānādhimuktijñānabalāt /
body.translated_text: There, what is the distinction between the power of knowledge of what is possible and impossible and the power of knowledge of the ownership of <s>karma</s>? That wholesome and unwholesome <s>karma</s> produces desirable and undesirable fruit — this is from the power of knowledge of what is possible and impossible. But that the very one who performs wholesome and unwholesome <s>karma</s> is the very one who experiences the desirable and undesirable fruit — this is from the power of knowledge of the ownership of <s>karma</s>. That the <s>dhyānas</s>, liberations, and the like belong to the very one who has accomplished them, and not to another — this is from the power of knowledge of the ownership of <s>karma</s>. But that, relying on those very <s>dhyānas</s> and the like, one instructs those to be trained through the three miracles — this is from the power of knowledge of <s>dhyāna</s>, liberations, concentrations, and attainments. That one grasps the mind conjoined with faith and the like — this is from the power of knowledge of <s>dhyāna</s>, liberations, concentrations, and attainments. But that one distinguishes those very faculties according to their divisions of mild, middling, and intense — this is from the power of knowledge of the higher and lower faculties. That, on the basis of the faculties, one grasps the disposition toward these and those <s>dharmas</s> — this is from the power of knowledge of the higher and lower faculties. But that one diversely distinguishes that very disposition — this is from the power of knowledge of diverse inclinations (<s>nānādhimuktijñānabala</s>).

body.text: tasya punarāśayasya samāsataḥ ṣaḍbhirākārairvibhāgo veditavyaḥ / anairyāṇika āśayaḥ / tadyathā pṛthaṅ maheśvara-nārāyaṇa-brahmalokādyadhimuktānām / nairyāṇika āśayaḥ tadyathā triṣu yāneṣvadhimuktānām / śuddhidūra āśayaḥ / tadyathā mṛdumadhyaparipākavyavasthitānām / viśuddhisamāsanna āśayaḥ / tadyathā 'dhimātraparipākavyavasthitānām / dṛṣṭe eva dharme nirvāṇaprāptyāśayaḥ / tadyathā śrāvakayānena nirvāṇaprāptyadhimuktānām / āyatyāṃ nirvāṇaprāptyāśayaḥ / tadyathā mahāyānena nirvāṇaprāptyadhimuktānām / yattāvadadhimuktisamutthāpitaṃ tadupamaṃ bījaṃ gṛhṇāti / idaṃ nānādhimuktijñānabalāt / yatpunastadeva bījaṃ bibhajyānekaprakāraṃ gṛhṇāti / idaṃ nānādhātujñānabalāt / sa punardhātupravibhāgaḥ samāsataścatuṣprakāro veditavyaḥ / prakṛtisthaṃ bījaṃ pūrvābhyāsasamutthitaṃ bījaṃ viśodhyaṃ bījam / tadyathā parinirvāṇadharmakāṇām / aviśodhyañca bījam / tadyathā parinirvāṇadharmakāṇām / yattāvadyathā dhātvanurūpaṃ pratipadamavatāraṃ prajānāti / idaṃ nānādhātujñānabalāt / yatpunastāmeva pratipadaṃ sarvaiḥ prakāraiḥ pravibhajati / iyaṃ pratipatsaṃkleśāyeyaṃ vyavadānāyeyamatyantavyavadānāyeyaṃ nātyantavyavadānāyeti /
body.translated_text: That disposition, moreover, should be understood in brief through a sixfold division. The disposition not leading to escape (<s>anairyāṇika āśaya</s>) — as in those inclined toward <s>Maheśvara</s>, <s>Nārāyaṇa</s>, the <s>Brahma</s>-world, and the like. The disposition leading to escape (<s>nairyāṇika āśaya</s>) — as in those inclined toward the three vehicles. The disposition far from purification (<s>śuddhidūra āśaya</s>) — as in those established in mild and middling maturation. The disposition near to purification (<s>viśuddhisamāsanna āśaya</s>) — as in those established in intense maturation. The disposition toward the attainment of <s>Nirvāṇa</s> in this very life — as in those inclined toward the attainment of <s>Nirvāṇa</s> through the <s>Śrāvaka</s> vehicle. The disposition toward the attainment of <s>Nirvāṇa</s> in the future — as in those inclined toward the attainment of <s>Nirvāṇa</s> through the <s>Mahāyāna</s>. That one grasps the seed produced by inclination, corresponding to it — this is from the power of knowledge of diverse inclinations. But that one distinguishes that very seed as manifold — this is from the power of knowledge of diverse elements (<s>nānādhātujñānabala</s>). That division of elements, moreover, should be understood in brief as fourfold: the naturally abiding seed; the seed arisen from prior habituation; the seed that can be purified — as in those who have the nature to attain <s>parinirvāṇa</s>; and the seed that cannot be purified — as in those who do not have the nature to attain <s>parinirvāṇa</s>. That one knows the course and entry [into practice] in accordance with the [respective] element — this is from the power of knowledge of diverse elements. But that one distinguishes that very course in all its aspects — 'this course is for defilement, this is for purification, this is for ultimate purification, and this is not for ultimate purification'

body.text: idaṃ sarvatragāminī pratipajjñānabalāt / yattāvatpūrvāntamanusmaran sarvagatihetuṃ pūrvāntasahagatāṃ yathābhūtaṃ prajānāti / idaṃ sarvatragāminī pratipajjñānabalāt / yatpunaḥ pravibhajya vyavahārapadānugataṃ pūrvavat ṣaḍvidhaṃ caritaṃ prajānāti / idaṃ pūrve nivāsānusmṛtijñānabalāt / yattāvatpūrvāntamārabhya sattvānāṃ cyutyupapādaṃ prajānāti / idaṃ pūrve nivāsānusmṛtijñānabalāt / yatpunaparāntikaṃ sattvānāṃ cyutyupapādaṃ paśyati / idaṃ cyutyupapattijñānabalāt / yattāvadapariniṣṭhita-svakārthānāṃ sattvānāmaparānte upapattiṃ pratisandhiṃ prajānāti / idaṃ cyutyupapattijñānabalāt / yatpunaḥ pariniṣṭhitasvakārthānāṃ suvimuktacittānāṃ dṛṣṭadharmanirvāṇaprāptiṃ prajānāti / idamāsravakṣayajñānabalāt / ayameṣāṃ daśānāṃ tathāgatabalānāmanyonyaṃ viśeṣaścāviśeṣaśca veditavyaḥ /
body.translated_text: — this is from the power of knowledge of the course leading everywhere (<s>sarvatragāminī pratipajjñānabala</s>). That one, recollecting the past, truly knows the cause of all destinies together with the past — this is from the power of knowledge of the course leading everywhere. But that one distinguishes in detail and knows the sixfold conduct following conventional designations, as before — this is from the power of knowledge of recollection of former abodes (<s>pūrvenivāsānusmṛtijñānabala</s>). That one knows the death and rebirth of beings from the past onward — this is from the power of knowledge of recollection of former abodes. But that one sees the death and rebirth of beings in the future — this is from the power of knowledge of death and rebirth (<s>cyutyupapattijñānabala</s>). That one knows the rebirth and connection (<s>pratisandhi</s>) in the future of those beings whose own purpose is not yet fulfilled — this is from the power of knowledge of death and rebirth. But that one knows the attainment of <s>Nirvāṇa</s> in this very life of those whose own purpose is fulfilled and whose minds are well-liberated — this is from the power of knowledge of the destruction of the defilements (<s>āsravakṣayajñānabala</s>). This should be understood as the mutual distinction and non-distinction of these ten powers of the <s>Tathāgata</s>.

body.text: catvāri vaiśāradyāni granthato yathāsūtrameva veditavyāni / tatra catvāryetāni sthānāni tathāgataiḥ pariṣadi pratijñātavyāni bhavanti / śrāvakāsādhāraṇo jñeyāvaraṇavimokṣātsarvākārasarvadharmābhisaṃbodhaḥ / idaṃ prathamaṃ sthānam / śrāvakasādhāraṇaśca kleśāvaraṇavimokṣaḥ / idaṃ dvitīyaṃ sthānam / vimokṣakāmānāṃ ca sattvānāṃ duḥkhasamatikramāya nairyāṇiko mārgaḥ / idaṃ tṛtīyaṃ sthānam / tasyaiva ca mārgasya prāptivibandhabhūtā ye āntarāyikā dharmāḥ parivarjayitavyāḥ / idaṃ caturthaṃ sthānam / yathārthapratijñaśca tathāgataḥ eṣu caturṣu sthāneṣu / ataḥ pratijñāviguṇāṃ dvayoḥ pūrvayoḥ sthānayoḥ kāyavāṅmanaśceṣṭāṃ pratijñāviguṇāṃ ca dvayoḥ paścimayoḥ sthānayoḥ pūrvāparavirodhatāmayuktipatitāñcāpareṣāṃ divyadṛśāṃ cādivyadṛśāñca paracittavidāmaparicittavidāṃ ca pratijñānasthānapratipakṣeṇa saṃcodanāyāṃ nimittabhūtāmasamanupaśyan yenaitāni sthānāni viśārado 'līnacitto nirāśaṅko nirbhīḥ pratijānāti / etāvacca śāstrā pratijñātavyam yaduta paripūrṇā svahitapratipattiḥ parahitapratipattiśca / tatra pūrvakābhyāṃ dvābhyāṃ sthānābhyāṃ paripūrṇā svahitapratipattiḥ pratijñātā bhavati / paścimakābhyāṃ [sthānābhyāṃ] paripūrṇā parihitapratipattiḥ pratijñātā bhavati / tatrātmanaḥ sarvadharmābhisaṃbodhātsamyaksaṃbuddhatvaṃ tathāgato mahāyānasaṃprasthitān bodhisattvānadhikṛtya pratijānīte / sarvāstravakṣayaṃ punaḥ
body.translated_text: The four confidences (<s>vaiśāradya</s>) should be understood textually just as in the <s>sūtra</s>. There, these four grounds are to be proclaimed by the <s>Tathāgata</s> in the assembly: The awakening to all <s>dharmas</s> in all aspects, not shared with <s>Śrāvakas</s>, resulting from liberation from the obscuration of the knowable (<s>jñeyāvaraṇa</s>) — this is the first ground. The liberation from the obscuration of afflictions (<s>kleśāvaraṇa</s>), shared with <s>Śrāvakas</s> — this is the second ground. The path leading to escape for those beings who desire liberation, for the transcendence of suffering — this is the third ground. The obstacles that are obstructive <s>dharmas</s> to be avoided, which obstruct the attainment of that very path — this is the fourth ground. And the <s>Tathāgata</s> proclaims what is true in these four grounds. Therefore, not seeing — in the bodily, verbal, and mental conduct of others — any ground for challenge as a counter-argument to his proclamation regarding the first two grounds, nor any mutual contradiction or logical fallacy regarding the latter two grounds, whether from those with divine sight or without, from those who know others' minds or do not — one proclaims these grounds with confidence, with unflinching mind, without apprehension, and without fear. And this much is to be proclaimed by the Teacher: namely, the complete accomplishment of the practice for one's own welfare and the practice for others' welfare. There, through the first two grounds, the complete accomplishment of the practice for one's own welfare is proclaimed. Through the latter two grounds, the complete accomplishment of the practice for others' welfare is proclaimed. There, by virtue of his own awakening to all <s>dharmas</s>, the <s>Tathāgata</s> proclaims his state of being a perfectly awakened one, with reference to <s>Bodhisattvas</s> who have set forth in the <s>Mahāyāna</s>. And the complete destruction of all defilements

body.text: śrāvakapratyekabuddhayānasaṃprasthitān sattvānadhikṛtya pratijānīte / mārgaṃ nairyāṇikaṃ dharmānāntarāyikāṃstadubhayānadhikṛtya pratijānīte / evametatsūtrapadaṃ tathāgatena deśitam / yo vā me bodhisattvānāṃ śrāvakāṇāñca nairyāṇiko mārgo deśita iti vistaraḥ / sa ca bodhisattvāpadeśaḥ saṃgītikāraiḥ śrāvakapiṭakādhikārādapanītaḥ / bodhisattvapiṭake punarbodhisattvopadeśa eva kevalaḥ paṭhyate /
body.translated_text: he proclaims with reference to beings who have set forth in the <s>Śrāvaka</s> and <s>Pratyekabuddha</s> vehicles. The path leading to escape and the obstructive <s>dharmas</s> he proclaims with reference to both. Thus this <s>sūtra</s>-passage was taught by the <s>Tathāgata</s>: 'The path leading to escape that I have taught for <s>Bodhisattvas</s> and for <s>Śrāvakas</s>' — and so on in detail. And that designation regarding <s>Bodhisattvas</s> was removed by the compilers of the canon from the domain of the <s>Śrāvaka Piṭaka</s>. But in the <s>Bodhisattva Piṭaka</s>, the instruction regarding <s>Bodhisattvas</s> alone is recited.

body.text: trīṇi smṛtyupasthānāni granthato yathāsūtrameva veditavyāni / dīrgharātraṃ tathāgata evaṃ kāmaḥ kaccinmayā sudeśite dharme vineyāḥ pratipattau yathāvadavatiṣṭeranniti / tasya ca dīrgharātraṃ tatkāmasya dharmasvāmino gaṇaparikarṣakasya tasyāḥ prārthitāyāḥ sampattibhyāmasaṃkleśasribhiḥ smṛtyupasthānaiḥ samāsataḥ prabhāvyate /
body.translated_text: The three foundations of mindfulness (<s>smṛtyupasthāna</s>) should be understood textually just as in the <s>sūtra</s>. For a long time, the <s>Tathāgata</s> has had this desire: 'If only those to be trained, in the <s>Dharma</s> well-taught by me, would properly abide in the practice!' And for that one who has long desired thus, who is the Lord of <s>Dharma</s>, who is the leader of the assembly, the non-defilement with regard to those desired attainments is illuminated, in brief, through the three foundations of mindfulness.

body.text: tāni punaretāni pariṣattrayaprabhedāt trīṇi vyavasthāpyante / tisraḥ pariṣadā katamāḥ / ekāntena samyak pratipadyante sarva eva / iyamekā pariṣat / ekāntena mithyā pratipadyante sarva eva / iyaṃ dvitīyā pariṣat / tṛtīyā punaḥ pariṣadyāsyāṃ tadekatyāḥ samyak pratipadyante tadekatyā mithyā pratipadyante /
body.translated_text: These [three foundations of mindfulness] are established as three because of the threefold division of the assembly. What are the three assemblies? [The assembly in which] absolutely all practice correctly, without exception — this is one assembly. [The assembly in which] absolutely all practice wrongly, without exception — this is the second assembly. And the third assembly is one in which some practice correctly and some practice wrongly.

body.text: trīṇyarakṣyāṇi yathāsūtrameva granthato veditavyāni / samāsataḥ sarvākārakukṛtapraticchādanatā-prahāṇam / etattathāgatasya tribhirarakṣyaiḥ paridīpitam yadapi tadarthato 'pi kiñcidavyākṛtaṃ kukṛtamātrakaṃ bhavati kadācitkarhicitsmṛtipramoṣāt / tadapi tathāgatasya sarveṇa sarva nāsti / atastathāgato yathā pratijñātastathā svabhāvaḥ / śrāvakān nigṛhya nigṛhya bravīti / prasahya prasahya tadekatyānavasādayati / tadekatyān pravāsayati / api tu niṣṭhuraṃ pratipadyate nāsya teṣvanurakṣā utpadyate / mā haiva me śrāvakāḥ saṃvāsānvayādapariśuddhakāyavāṅmanaḥ-samudācāratāṃ viditvā tena vastunā 'nāttamanaskā anabhirāddhyāścodayiṣyanti / pareṣāṃ vā ākhyāsyantīti /
body.translated_text: The three things not needing guarding (<s>arakṣya</s>) should be understood textually just as in the <s>sūtra</s>. In brief, the abandonment of all concealment of wrongdoing — this is what is illuminated through the three things not needing guarding of the <s>Tathāgata</s>. For even that which, in terms of its purpose, may be merely a minor indeterminate wrongdoing arising occasionally from a lapse of mindfulness — even that does not at all exist for the <s>Tathāgata</s>. Therefore the <s>Tathāgata</s> is of the same nature as he proclaims. He admonishes <s>Śrāvakas</s> repeatedly; he forcefully humbles some; he banishes some. He even acts sternly — yet no thought of guarding arises in him [of the kind]: 'Lest my <s>Śrāvakas</s>, having learned of my impure conduct of body, speech, and mind through close association, might become displeased and discontented on account of that matter and reproach me, or tell others.'

body.text: tatra tathāgatānāṃ mahākaruṇā sarvākārā yathā pūrvanirdiṣṭā pūjāsevāpramāṇapaṭale veditavyā / sā punarapramāṇā niruttarā tāthāgatī veditavyā / tatra tathāgatasyānuṣṭeyaṃ yacca bhavati [yatra ca bhavati] yathā ca bhavati yadā ca bhavati tatra tasya tathā tadā samyaganuṣṭhānādiyaṃ tathāgatasyāsammoṣadharmatetyucyate / iti yā ca tatra tathāgatasya sarvakṛtyeṣu sarvadeśeṣu sarvakṛtyopāyeṣu sarvakāleṣu smṛtyasaṃpramoṣatā sadopasthitasmṛtitā / iyamatrāsammoṣa-dharmatā draṣṭavyā /
body.translated_text: There, the great compassion (<s>mahākaruṇā</s>) of the <s>Tathāgatas</s>, in all its aspects as previously described, should be understood as in the Chapter on Worship, Service, and the Immeasurables (<s>Pūjāsevāpramāṇapaṭala</s>). And it should be understood as immeasurable, unsurpassed, and belonging to the <s>Tathāgata</s>. There, whatever is to be accomplished by the <s>Tathāgata</s>, wherever it is to be accomplished, however it is to be accomplished, and whenever it is to be accomplished — through his correct accomplishment thereof at the right time, in the right place, in the right manner — this is called the <s>Tathāgata</s>'s nature of non-forgetfulness (<s>asammoṣadharmatā</s>). Thus, the <s>Tathāgata</s>'s non-lapse of mindfulness in all tasks, in all places, in all means for tasks, and at all times — his ever-present mindfulness — this should be seen here as the nature of non-forgetfulness.

body.text: tatra yā tathāgatasya spandite vā prekṣite vā kathite vā vihāre vā kleśasadbhāvasadṛśaṃ ceṣṭā 'samudācāra-pracāratā / ayaṃ tathāgatasya vāsanāsamudghāta ityucyate / arhatāṃ punaḥ prahīṇakleśānāmapi kleśasadbhāvasadṛśī ceṣṭā spandita-prekṣita-kathita-vihṛteṣu bhavatyeva /
body.translated_text: There, whatever conduct of the <s>Tathāgata</s> in his movements, glances, speech, or abiding resembles the presence of afflictions but is not the occurrence of their active manifestation—this is called the <s>Tathāgata</s>'s eradication of residual impressions (<s>vāsanāsamudghāta</s>). But for <s>Arhats</s>, even though their afflictions have been abandoned, conduct resembling the presence of afflictions does indeed occur in their movements, glances, speech, and abiding.

body.text: samāsatastathāgatena dharmāṇāṃ trayo rāśayo 'bhisaṃbuddhāḥ / katame trayaḥ / arthopasaṃhitā dharmā anarthopasaṃhitā naivārthopasaṃhitāḥ nānarthopasaṃhitāḥ / tatra yattathāgatasyānarthopasaṃhiteṣu naivārthopasaṃhita-nānarthopasaṃhiteṣu sarvadharmeṣu jñānam / idaṃ tathāgatasya sarvākārajñānamityucyate / tatra yattathāgatasyārthopasaṃhiteṣu sarvadharmeṣu jñānam / idaṃ tathāgatasya varajñānamityucyate / tatra yacca sarvākāraṃ jñānaṃ yacca varajñānaṃ tadaikadhyamabhisaṃkṣipya sarvākāravarajñānamityucyate /
body.translated_text: In summary, the <s>Tathāgata</s> has fully awakened to three heaps of <s>dharmas</s>. Which three? <s>Dharmas</s> connected with benefit, <s>dharmas</s> connected with harm, and <s>dharmas</s> connected with neither benefit nor harm. There, the <s>Tathāgata</s>'s knowledge of all <s>dharmas</s> connected with harm and those connected with neither benefit nor harm—this is called the <s>Tathāgata</s>'s omniscient knowledge (<s>sarvākārajñāna</s>). There, the <s>Tathāgata</s>'s knowledge of all <s>dharmas</s> connected with benefit—this is called the <s>Tathāgata</s>'s supreme knowledge (<s>varajñāna</s>). There, the omniscient knowledge and the supreme knowledge, when combined together, are called 'omniscient supreme knowledge' (<s>sarvākāravarajñāna</s>).

body.text: tadetadabhisamasya sarvañcatvāriṃśaduttaramāveṇikaṃ buddhadharmaśataṃ bhavati / tatra lakṣaṇānuvyañjanānyanena bodhisattvabhūtena carame bhave supariśuddhāni pratilabdhāni bhavanti / yadā tu bodhimaṇḍe niṣīdati suparipūrṇa-bodhisaṃbhāramārgo bodhisattvaḥ paścime bhave tadāsāvanācāryakaṃ saptatriṃśataṃ bodhipakṣyān dharmān bhāvayannekakṣaṇānāvaraṇajñānadaṃ nāma samādhiṃ pratilabhate śaikṣyabhūtasya bodhisattvasya vajropamasamādhi-saṃgṛhītam / tasyānantaraṃ dvitīye kṣaṇe pariśiṣṭānāṃ daśabalādīnāṃ buddhadharmāṇāṃ sarvākāra-varajñāna-paryavasānānāṃ suviśuddhatāṃ niruttaratāṃ sakṛtpratilabhate / teṣāñca lābhāt sarvasmin jñeye 'saktamanāvaraṇaṃ suviśuddhaṃ nirmalaṃ jñānaṃ pravartate ābhogamātra-pratibaddham / paripūrṇasaṃkalpaśca bhavati / tathā paripūrṇamanorathaḥ samatikrānto bodhisattvacaryā bodhisattvabhūmim / tathāgatacaryāṃ tathāgatabhūmimavakrānto
body.translated_text: Having fully awakened to this, there are one hundred and forty exclusive <s>Buddha</s>-<s>dharmas</s>. There, the marks and secondary marks have been obtained in supreme purity by this being who is a <s>Bodhisattva</s> in his final existence. But when the <s>Bodhisattva</s>, having fully completed the path and the accumulations for awakening, sits at the seat of awakening (<s>bodhimaṇḍa</s>) in his last existence, then, without a teacher, cultivating the thirty-seven factors conducive to awakening (<s>bodhipakṣya dharmas</s>), he attains in a single moment the concentration called 'unobstructed knowledge' (<s>anāvaraṇajñāna samādhi</s>), which belongs to the <s>Bodhisattva</s> on the training stage and is comprised within the diamond-like concentration (<s>vajropamasamādhi</s>). Immediately after that, in the second moment, he attains all at once the supreme purity and unsurpassedness of the remaining <s>Buddha</s>-<s>dharmas</s> beginning with the ten powers (<s>daśabala</s>), culminating in omniscient supreme knowledge. And from obtaining those, with respect to all that is knowable, unattached, unobstructed, supremely pure, and stainless knowledge operates—bound only by the mere application of attention. And his resolve becomes fulfilled. Likewise, his aspirations become fulfilled. Having transcended <s>Bodhisattva</s>-conduct and the <s>Bodhisattva</s>-stage, he has entered upon <s>Tathāgata</s>-conduct and the <s>Tathāgata</s>-stage

body.text:
bhavati / sāragatasya ca jñeyāvaraṇapakṣyasya dauṣṭhulyasya niravaśeṣaṃ prahāṇādasyāśrayaḥ parivṛtto bhavati / sā cāsya niruttarā āśrayaparivṛttiḥ / anyāḥ sarvāḥ paramavihārāvasānā bodhisattvānāmāśrayaparivṛttayaḥ sottarā eva veditavyāḥ /
tatra niṣṭhāgamana-bhūmisthitasya ca bodhisattvasya [tathāgatasya ca kathaṃ jñānaviśeṣo 'vagantavyo jñānāntaram / iha niṣṭhāgamana-bhūmisthitasya bodhisattvasya] pelavapaṭāntaritaṃ yathācakṣuṣmato rūpadarśanam / evaṃ tasya sarvasmin jñeye jñānaṃ veditavyam / yathā punarna kenacidantaritam / evaṃ tathāgatasya jñānaṃ draṣṭavyam / tadyathā sarvākāraraṃga-paripūrṇaṃ citrakarma paścimayā suviśuddhayā raṃgalekhayā 'pariśodhitam / evaṃ tasya bodhisattvasya jñānaṃ draṣṭavyam / yathā suviśodhitamevaṃ tathāgatasya jñānaṃ draṣṭavyam / tadyathā cakṣuṣmataḥ puruṣasya mandatamaskaṃ rūpadarśanam / evaṃ bodhisattvasya pūrvavat / yathā sarvākārāpagatatamaskamevaṃ tathāgatasya jñānaṃ draṣṭavyam / tadyathā cakṣuṣmata ārādrūpadarśanam evaṃ evaṃ bodhisattvasya pūrvavat yathā āsanne evaṃ tathāgatasya pūrvavat / yathā mṛdutaimirikasya rūpadarśanam evaṃ bodhisattvasya pūrvavat yathā suviśuddha-cakṣuṣaḥ evaṃ tathāgatasya pūrvavat / yathā garbhagatasyātmabhāva evaṃ niṣṭhāgamanabhūmisthito bodhisattvo draṣṭavyaḥ / yathopapattibhave jātasyātmabhāva evaṃ tathāgato draṣṭavyaḥ / yathārhataḥ svapnāntaragatasya cittapracārastathā niṣṭhāgamana-bhūmisthitasya bodhisattvasya draṣṭavyaḥ / yathā tasyaiva prativibuddhasya cittapracāra evaṃ tathāgatasya draṣṭavyaḥ / tadyathā pradīpasyāviśuddhasya svabhāvaḥ tathā niṣṭhāgamana-bhūmisthitasya bodhisattvasya jñānasvabhāvo draṣṭavyaḥ / yathā suviśuddhasya pradīpasya svabhāvaḥ evaṃ tathāgatasya jñānasvabhāvo draṣṭavyaḥ / ato mahajjñānāntaramātmabhāvāntaraṃ cintāntaraṃ tathāgataniṣṭhāgamanabhūmisthita-bodhisattvayorveditavyam /
body.translated_text:
. And through the complete, remainderless abandonment of the deep/essential dysfunction belonging to the side of knowledge-obscuration, his basis (<s>āśraya</s>) is transformed. And that transformation of his basis is unsurpassed. All other transformations of basis of <s>Bodhisattvas</s>, up to the supreme abode, should be understood as surpassable.
There, how should the distinction of knowledge between the <s>Bodhisattva</s> established on the culmination-stage (<s>niṣṭhāgamanabhūmi</s>) and the <s>Tathāgata</s> be understood—what is the difference in knowledge? Here, the knowledge of the <s>Bodhisattva</s> established on the culmination-stage with respect to all that is knowable should be understood as like the vision of forms by one with eyes, [but] obstructed by a thin, fine cloth. But the knowledge of the <s>Tathāgata</s> should be seen as if obstructed by nothing at all. Just as a painting filled with pigments of all kinds in all its aspects, [but] not yet finished with the final clear, pure coat of color—so should the knowledge of that <s>Bodhisattva</s> be seen. As if well-finished [with that final coat]—so should the knowledge of the <s>Tathāgata</s> be seen. Just as the vision of forms by a person with eyes in dim darkness—so should the <s>Bodhisattva</s>'s [knowledge] be as before. As if with all darkness completely gone in all aspects—so should the <s>Tathāgata</s>'s knowledge be seen. Just as the vision of forms at a distance by one with eyes—so should the <s>Bodhisattva</s>'s [knowledge] be as before. As if nearby—so should the <s>Tathāgata</s>'s [knowledge] be as before. Just as the vision of forms by one with mild eye-disease—so should the <s>Bodhisattva</s>'s [knowledge] be as before. As if with perfectly clear vision—so should the <s>Tathāgata</s>'s [knowledge] be as before. Just as the bodily existence of one still in the womb—so should the <s>Bodhisattva</s> established on the culmination-stage be seen. Just as the bodily existence of one born in the birth-existence—so should the <s>Tathāgata</s> be seen. Just as the mental activity of an <s>Arhat</s> within a dream—so should [the mental activity] of the <s>Bodhisattva</s> established on the culmination-stage be seen. Just as the mental activity of that same [<s>Arhat</s>] when awakened—so should the <s>Tathāgata</s>'s [mental activity] be seen. Just as the nature of an impure lamp—so should the nature of knowledge of the <s>Bodhisattva</s> established on the culmination-stage be seen. Just as the nature of a perfectly pure lamp—so should the nature of knowledge of the <s>Tathāgata</s> be seen. Thus, the great difference in knowledge, the difference in bodily existence, and the difference in thought between the <s>Tathāgata</s> and the <s>Bodhisattva</s> established on the culmination-stage should be understood.

body.text: evamabhisaṃbuddho bodhistathāgato daśasu dikṣu sarvabuddhakṣetre sarvabuddhakāryaṃ karoti / tatra buddhakāryaṃ katamat / samāsato daśemāni tathāgatasya tathāgatakṛtyāni tathāgatakaraṇīyāni / ekaikañca tathāgatakṛtyamapramāṇānāṃ sattvānāmarthakārakaṃ bhavati / nāstyata uttari nāstyato bhūyaḥ / katamāni daśa / sve mahāpuruṣabhāve
body.translated_text: Having thus fully awakened to awakening, the <s>Tathāgata</s> performs all <s>Buddha</s>-deeds in all <s>Buddha</s>-fields in the ten directions. There, what are the <s>Buddha</s>-deeds? In summary, these are the ten <s>Tathāgata</s>-duties, the <s>Tathāgata</s>-tasks. And each <s>Tathāgata</s>-duty serves the welfare of immeasurable beings. There is nothing beyond this, nothing more. What are the ten? In his own person as a great being

body.text: ādita eva cittaprasādakārakamahāpuruṣa[bhāva]saṃpratyayajananā prathamaṃ tathā[gata]kṛtyaṃ tacca lakṣaṇānuvyañjanaiḥ sampādayati / sarvasattvānāṃ sarvākārāvavādaprayogatathāgatakṛtyaṃ [yat] catasrabhiḥ sarvākārapariśuddhibhiḥ sampādayati / [idaṃ] dvitīyaṃ tathāgatakṛtyam / sarvasattvakāryakaraṇasāmarthyaṃ sarvasaṃśayacchedanasāmarthyañca tṛtīyaṃ tathāgatakṛtyam / yattathāgato daśabhirtāthāgatabalaiḥ sampādayati tathā hi tathāgato daśabhiḥ pūrvanirdiṣṭairvalaiḥ sarvasattvānāṃ sarvārthasampādanaṃ prati samartho bhavati / ye cainaṃ tathāgatabalānyārabhya praśnaṃ pṛcchanti yathā yāni tathāgatena jñātāni dṛṣṭāni viditāni vijñātāni tathā tāni tathāgatasteṣāṃ praśnaṃ pṛṣṭo vyākaroti / sarvaparapravavādanigrahaḥ svavādavyavasthāpanā tathāgatasya caturthaṃ kṛtyam / yattathāgato vaiśāradyaiḥ sampādayati tathāgatājñāyāṃ sthiteṣvasyiteṣu ca vineyeṣvasaṃkliṣṭacittatā pañcamaṃ tathāgatakṛtyam / yattathāgataḥ smṛtyupasthānaiḥ sampādayati yathāvādi tathākāritā ṣaṣṭhaṃ tathāgatakṛtyam / yattathāgataḥ arakṣyaiḥ sampādayati buddhacakṣuṣā rātrindivaṃ sarvalokavyavalokanā saptamaṃ tathāgatakṛtyam / yattathāgato mahākaruṇayā sampādayati / sarvasattvasarvakṛtyāvihārāṇi aṣṭamaṃ tathāgatakṛtyam / yattathāgato 'sammoṣadharmatayā sampādayati tathāgatasyācāravihārasya yathāvadanuvartanā adhitiṣṭhanā navamaṃ tathāgatakṛtyam / yattathāgato vāsanāsamuddhātena sampādayati ye dharmā anarthopasaṃhitā ye ca naivārthopasaṃhitānānārthopasaṃhitāstānabhinirvarjya ye ca dharmā arthopasaṃhitāsteṣāṃ samākhyānaṃ vivaraṇā uttānīkarme daśamaṃ tathāgatakṛtyam / yattathāgataḥ sarvākāravarajñānena sampādayati evaṃ hi tathāgato 'nenāveṇikena catvāriṃśaduttareṇa buddhadharmaśatena daśatathāgata kṛtyāni kurvan sarvabuddhakāryaṃ karoti / vistaravibhāgataḥ punarasyaiva buddhakāryasya na sukarāsaṃkhyāṃ kartuṃ yāvatkalpakoṭīniyutaśatasahasrairapi /
body.translated_text: , the first <s>Tathāgata</s>-duty is generating confidence and trust in his own great-person nature, from the very beginning producing mental clarity [in beings]—and this he accomplishes through the marks and secondary marks. The <s>Tathāgata</s>-duty of providing all beings with instruction of all kinds in all aspects—[this] he accomplishes through the four all-aspect purities. This is the second <s>Tathāgata</s>-duty. The ability to accomplish all tasks for all beings and the ability to cut through all doubts—this is the third <s>Tathāgata</s>-duty, which the <s>Tathāgata</s> accomplishes through the ten <s>Tathāgata</s> powers. For thus the <s>Tathāgata</s>, through the ten previously described powers, is capable of accomplishing all purposes for all beings. And to those who question him regarding the <s>Tathāgata</s> powers—concerning what has been known, seen, understood, and realized by the <s>Tathāgata</s>—the <s>Tathāgata</s>, when questioned, answers accordingly. The overcoming of all opposing doctrines and the establishment of his own doctrine—this is the <s>Tathāgata</s>'s fourth duty, which the <s>Tathāgata</s> accomplishes through the [four] fearlessnesses (<s>vaiśāradya</s>). With respect to those to be trained who abide in the <s>Tathāgata</s>'s instruction and those who have departed [from it], maintaining an undefiled mind—this is the fifth <s>Tathāgata</s>-duty, which the <s>Tathāgata</s> accomplishes through the [three] foundations of mindfulness (<s>smṛtyupasthāna</s>). Being true to his word in conduct—this is the sixth <s>Tathāgata</s>-duty, which the <s>Tathāgata</s> accomplishes through the [three] things needing no guarding (<s>arakṣya</s>). Surveying the entire world day and night with the <s>Buddha</s>-eye—this is the seventh <s>Tathāgata</s>-duty, which the <s>Tathāgata</s> accomplishes through great compassion (<s>mahākaruṇā</s>). Never resting from all duties toward all beings—this is the eighth <s>Tathāgata</s>-duty, which the <s>Tathāgata</s> accomplishes through the quality of unforgetting (<s>asammoṣadharmatā</s>). The proper continuation and superintendence of the <s>Tathāgata</s>'s manner of conduct and abiding as it truly is—this is the ninth <s>Tathāgata</s>-duty, which the <s>Tathāgata</s> accomplishes through the eradication of residual impressions (<s>vāsanāsamudghāta</s>). Avoiding those <s>dharmas</s> that are connected with harm and those connected with neither benefit nor harm, and declaring, explaining, making accessible, and illuminating those <s>dharmas</s> that are connected with benefit—this is the tenth <s>Tathāgata</s>-duty, which the <s>Tathāgata</s> accomplishes through omniscient supreme knowledge (<s>sarvākāravarajñāna</s>). Thus indeed the <s>Tathāgata</s>, through this exclusive set of one hundred and forty <s>Buddha</s>-<s>dharmas</s>, performs the ten <s>Tathāgata</s>-duties, [thereby] performing all <s>Buddha</s>-deeds. But the detailed classification of this very <s>Buddha</s>-activity is not easy to enumerate, even in hundreds of thousands of tens of millions of <s>kalpa</s>-<s>koṭis</s>.

body.text: ayaṃ sa tathāgato vihārastathāgatī bhūmiḥ pratiṣṭhetyucyate / tatkasya hetoḥ / etāmāśrityaitāṃ pratiṣṭhāya yasyāḥ spṛhayamāṇarūpā bodhisattvā bodhisattvaśikṣāsu śikṣante adhigamyāpi ca tāṃ pratiṣṭhāmetāmevāśrityaitāṃ pratiṣṭhāya sarvasattvānāṃ sarvārthān sāmpādayati / tasmātpratiṣṭhetyucyate /
body.translated_text: This <s>Tathāgata</s>-abode, this <s>Tathāgata</s>-stage, is called 'Establishment' (<s>pratiṣṭhā</s>). For what reason? Because it is relying on this, established upon this [ground], that <s>Bodhisattvas</s> train in the <s>Bodhisattva</s>-trainings in the manner of those who aspire to it. And even having attained it, it is relying on this very Establishment, established upon this Establishment, that he accomplishes all purposes for all beings. Therefore it is called 'Establishment.'

body.text: sarve caite buddhadharmā atyarthaṃ parārthakriyānukūlāḥ parārthakriyāprabhāvitāśca tathāgatānām / [na] tathā śrāvakapratyekabuddhānām / tasmāttasyaiva te āveṇikā ityucyante / santi ca te buddhadharmā ye sarveṇa sarvaṃ śrāvakapratyekabuddheṣu nopalabhyante / tadyathā mahākaruṇā 'sammoṣadharmatā vāsanāsamuddhātaḥ sarvākāravarajñānam / ye 'pi copalabhyante te 'pi na sarvākāraparipūrṇāḥ / tathāgatasya tu sarve copalabhyante sarvākāraparipūrṇāścātikrāntatarāśca praṇītatarāśca / tasmātte tasyāveṇikā ityucyante / kaivalyārthaścāveṇikārtho veditavyaḥ /
body.translated_text: And all these <s>Buddha</s>-<s>dharmas</s> are supremely conducive to activity for others' welfare and are empowered by activity for others' welfare, for the <s>Tathāgatas</s>. [They are] not so for <s>Śrāvakas</s> and <s>Pratyekabuddhas</s>. Therefore they are called 'exclusive' (<s>āveṇika</s>) to him alone. And there are <s>Buddha</s>-<s>dharmas</s> that are entirely and completely not found in <s>Śrāvakas</s> and <s>Pratyekabuddhas</s>—namely, great compassion (<s>mahākaruṇā</s>), the quality of unforgetting (<s>asammoṣadharmatā</s>), the eradication of residual impressions (<s>vāsanāsamudghāta</s>), and omniscient supreme knowledge (<s>sarvākāravarajñāna</s>). And those that are found [in them] are not complete in all aspects. But for the <s>Tathāgata</s>, all [<s>Buddha</s>-<s>dharmas</s>] are found, complete in all aspects, and moreover surpassingly superior and sublime. Therefore they are called 'exclusive' to him. And the meaning of 'exclusive' (<s>āveṇika</s>) should be understood as 'uniqueness' (<s>kaivalya</s>).

body.text: ityayaṃ paripūrṇo bodhisattvānāṃ śikṣāmārgaḥ / śikṣāmārgaphalañca prakāśitam / sarvabodhisattva-śikṣāmārgasya śikṣāmārgaphalasya ca tarvākārasya nirdeśāya adhiṣṭhānabhūtam sā khalviyaṃ bodhisattvabhūmirbodhisattvapiṭakamātṛketyapyucyate / mahāyānasaṃgraha ityapyucyate / [praṇāśā-]praṇāśapathavivaraṇamityucyate / anāvaraṇajñānaviśuddhi mūlamityapyucyate / yaḥ kaścit sadevamānuṣā[surā]llokāddevabhūto vā [manuṣyabhūto vā] śramaṇo vā brāhmaṇo vāsyāṃ bodhisattvabhūmau dṛḍhāmadhimuktimutpādyemāṃ śroṣyatyudgrahīṣyati dhārayiṣyati bhāvanākāreṇa vā prayokṣyate pareṣāṃ vā vistareṇa prakāśayiṣyatyantato lekhayitvā dhārayiṣyati pūjāsatkārañca prayokṣyate / tasya samāsato yāvān puṇyaskandho bhagavatā sarvabodhisattvapiṭake saṃgṛhītasya sūtrāntasya śravaṇādikarmaṇa ākhyāta uttāno vivṛtaḥ prajñaptaḥ prakāśitaḥ tāvānasya puṇyaskandhaḥ pratyāśaṃsitavyaḥ / tatkasya hetoḥ / tathā hyasyāṃ bodhisattvabhūmau sarvasya bodhisattvapiṭakasyoddeśanirdeśamukhāni saṃgṛhītānyākhyātāni / yāvaccāsyāṃ [bodhisattva]bhūmau yo dharmavinayo vistareṇa prakāśitaḥ sa bahulamuddeśasvādhyāya-dharmānudharmapratipattitaḥ sthāsyati pṛthuvṛddhivaipulyatāñca gamiṣyati na tāvatsaddharmapratirūpakāḥ pracurā bhaviṣyanti saddharmāntarddhānāya / yataśca punaḥ saddharmapratirūpakāḥ pracurā bhaviṣyanti tataścāyaṃ saddharmo bhūtārthopasaṃhito tasya tadantardhānaṃ bhaviṣyati /
body.translated_text: Thus, this complete training-path of <s>Bodhisattvas</s> and its fruit have been illuminated. For the exposition of all aspects of the entire <s>Bodhisattva</s> training-path and its fruit, this indeed is the foundation—this <s>Bodhisattvabhūmi</s>, which is also called the <s>Bodhisattvapiṭaka</s> <s>Mātṛkā</s> (Matrix of the <s>Bodhisattva</s> Collection). It is also called the Compendium of the <s>Mahāyāna</s> (<s>Mahāyānasaṃgraha</s>). It is called the Elucidation of the Path of Non-Destruction. It is also called the Root of the Purification of Unobstructed Knowledge. Whoever from this world with its <s>devas</s>, humans, and <s>asuras</s>—whether a <s>deva</s>, a human, an ascetic, or a <s>brāhmaṇa</s>—generates firm faith in this <s>Bodhisattvabhūmi</s> and will hear it, take it up, retain it, apply himself to it through the mode of cultivation, or will extensively illuminate it for others, or even will retain it after having it copied, and will engage in worship and honor of it—for him, in summary, whatever mass of merit has been declared, made clear, revealed, designated, and illuminated by the <s>Bhagavān</s> for the hearing and other activities regarding the <s>sūtras</s> comprised in the entire <s>Bodhisattva</s>-piṭaka, that much mass of merit should be expected for him. For what reason? Because in this <s>Bodhisattvabhūmi</s>, the summaries and detailed expositions of the entire <s>Bodhisattva</s>-piṭaka have been comprised and declared. And as long as the <s>Dharma</s> and <s>Vinaya</s> extensively illuminated in this <s>Bodhisattvabhūmi</s> will remain through abundant recitation, self-study, and practice in conformity with the <s>Dharma</s>, and will grow in breadth, expansion, and fullness—so long will counterfeits of the true <s>Dharma</s> not become prevalent for the disappearance of the true <s>Dharma</s>. But from the time when counterfeits of the true <s>Dharma</s> become prevalent, then this true <s>Dharma</s>, connected with genuine meaning, will disappear.

body.text: iti bodhisattvabhūmāvādhāre niṣṭhe yogasthāne ṣaṣṭhaṃ pratiṣṭhāpaṭalam /
body.translated_text: Thus, in the <s>Bodhisattvabhūmi</s>, in the Foundation Section, Culmination, of the Yoga Division, [this is] the sixth chapter, the <s>Pratiṣṭhā-paṭala</s> (Chapter on Establishment).

body.text: // samāptā ca bodhisattvabhūmiḥ //
body.translated_text: The <s>Bodhisattvabhūmi</s> is completed.

body.text: // kṛtiriyamācāryāryāsaṅgapādānām //
body.translated_text: This is the work of the master, the noble <s>Asaṅga</s>.

children.text: ye dharmā hetuprabhavā hetuṃ teṣāntathāgato hyavadat /
children.translated_text: Those <s>dharmas</s> that arise from a cause—the <s>Tathāgata</s> has declared their cause.

children.text: teṣāñca yo nirodha evaṃ vādī mahāśramaṇaḥ //
children.translated_text: And their cessation—thus speaks the Great Ascetic (<s>Mahāśramaṇa</s>).
